docs.text: CLC 400200 1 高級華語二 Mandarin Advance II 任課教師 Instructor 傅聖芳 Sheng-Fang Fu 上課地點 Classroom 綜二館 110 教室 General Building II, Room 110 課程時間 Time 每週一 15:30~18:20 Mondays 15:30~18:20 教師連絡方式 Contact information fusf@gapp.nthu.edu.tw 適合程度 Target learner 本課程為針對母語非華語的國際學生所設計，選材 自真實語篇。涵蓋社會、科技、經濟、政治、文 化、環境等多元主題，拓展學生對不同語體、領域 的語言認知與運用。上完課後，華語程度約可達到 CEFR C1 (ACTFL Superior) 的程度。本課程適合學 習時數超過 700 小時，具備 4000 個詞彙量的學習 者。 This course is designed for international students whose native language is not Chinese. It uses authentic language materials covering diverse topics such as society, technology, economics, politics, culture, and the environment. It aims to expand students' language awareness and usage across different registers and domains. After completing the course, students' Chinese proficiency level is expected to reach approximately CEFR C1 (ACTFL Superior). This course is suitable for learners who have studied for over 700 hours and have a vocabulary of 4000 words. 指定教材 Textbook 《當代中文課程》第六冊 1-5 課 A Course in Contemporary Chinese Book 6, Linking Publishing. Lesson 1-5. 總授課時數 Total hours 共 48 個小時 48 hours 教學內容 Content 1. 本課程主要為閱讀篇章，從而擴展談論的話 題。 CLC 400200 2 This course primarily focuses on reading passages to expand the range of topics for discussion. 2. 內容主題涵蓋教育面向、科技人文、語言文化 等層面。 The content covers aspects such as education, technology and humanities, language and culture. 3. 學生能談論學歷技能、科技與藝術人文、語言 交流等議題。 The students can discuss topics such as academic qualifications, skills, technology and the arts, humanities, and language communication. 授課方式 Teaching methods 師生、生生討論、任務活動、角色扮演、學生報告 Lectures, class activities, group discussion, task-based learning 成績考核 Grading Policy 出席 Attendance: 10 % 課堂參與 Class Participation : 15 % 功課 Assignments : 15% 小考 Quizzes: 10% 期中考 Midterm : 20 % 期末考 Final Exam : 30% 課程進度表 （視教學需要調整） Course Schedule (this schedule is subject to change) 週 Week 進度 Progress 1-2 第一課 職校教育 L1 Vocational School Education 3-5 第二課 科技生活 L2 Technology Life 6-8 第三課 舞蹈藝術 L3 Dance Art 9 期中考 Midterm 10-12 第四課 做人心法 L4 The Way to Behave 13-15 第五課 國際語言 L5 International Language 16 期末考 Final Exam 備註 Remarks 本課程無涉及 AI This course does not involve the use of AI. 修課規定 Course Policies CLC 400200 3 1. 請尊重老師及同學，共同維護友善且良好的學習 環境。Students are expected to respect the instructor and their classmates and contribute to a friendly and positive learning environment. 2. 作業須於規定期限內繳交；逾期超過兩天者，該 作業不予計分。All assignments must be submitted by the specified deadline. Assignments submitted more than two days late will not receive credit. 3. 請準時到課。遲到二十分鐘（含）以內不扣分； 遲到超過二十分鐘者視為曠課，並扣除該節課出席 成績。Students are expected to arrive on time. Arriving within 20 minutes after the start of class will not result in a penalty. Arriving more than 20 minutes late will be considered an unexcused absence, and the attendance score for that class session will be deducted. 4. 課程相關公告、作業繳交期限及考試資訊，請以 課堂公告及教學平台公告為準。 Course announcements, assignment deadlines, and examination information will be communicated through class announcements and the course learning platform. Students are responsible for checking these announcements regularly. 請假與考試相關規定 Attendance, Leave, and Examination Policies 1. 因故無法出席課程者，請事先來信告知原因，並 於請假系統完成請假程序。若因突發狀況無法事先 請假，請於缺課後三日內補辦請假手續並來信說 明；未依規定辦理者，該次缺席視為曠課。 Students who are unable to attend class should notify the instructor in advance and complete the leave request procedure through the university leave system. In cases of emergency, students must submit the leave request and notify the instructor within three days after the absence. Absences without proper notification and leave procedures will be considered unexcused absences. 2. 連續請病假三天（含）以上者，須檢附醫師診斷 證明並主動通知授課教師。 Students who take sick leave for three consecutive days or longer must provide a medical certificate and notify the instructor. 3. 因公假無法出席課程者，請事先來信告知缺課時 CLC 400200 4 間，並自行補足缺課期間之學習內容。Students who are absent due to official university business must inform the instructor in advance and are responsible for making up any missed course content. 4. 經核准之事假累計三次（含）以內不扣分；超過 三次者，每增加一次事假，將扣除部分出席成績。 Approved personal leave of up to three occasions will not affect the attendance grade. Additional approved personal leave beyond this limit may result in deductions from the attendance grade. 5. 期中與期末筆試、口試須依規定時間參加。除不 可抗力因素外，不受理提前或延後考試申請。 Midterm and final written and oral examinations must be taken at the scheduled time. Requests for early or make-up examinations will not be approved except in cases of force majeure or other unavoidable circumstances. 6. 考試如有作弊行為，該次考試成績以零分計算。 Any form of academic dishonesty or cheating during examinations will result in a score of zero for the examination concerned.

It uses authentic language materials covering diverse topics such as society, technology, economics, politics, culture, and the environment. After completing the course, students' Chinese proficiency level is expected to reach approximately CEFR C1 (ACTFL Superior). Please make sure to comply with it.

docs.name: 商用華語一
docs.text: 商用華語一 Business Chinese I 任課教師 Instructor 歐喜強 Ou, Xiqiang (Tulun) 上課地點 Classroom GEN II 綜二 104 課程時間 Time TaTbTc 18:30-21:20 教師連絡方式 Contact Information ouxiqiang@mx.nthu.edu.tw 適合程度 Target Learner 建議學完「中級華語」，學習時數達到 280-360 個小時、累積華語詞彙量 約 1,200 個。 Business Chinese (I) is recommended for students who have taken Mandarin Intermediate (I), or have learned 280-360 hours of Mandarin before (need to know at least 1,200 Chinese words, familiar with pinyin system and basic sentence structures). 指定教材 Textbooks 國立清華大學華語中心 編 《商用華語：一本設身處地式的商務華語教材》（1-7 課） https://play.google.com/store/books/details?id=0F0BEAAAQBAJ 總授課時數 Total Hours 共 48 個小時 48 hours in total 教學內容 Content 本課程目標為幫助國際學生學習及體驗職場或商業情境的中文，內容包含 如何找工作、面試、應聘、上班族日常開會、出差及辦公環境、商務表單 填寫等。為了配合大多正式的商務情境需要，課程除了口語的練習之外， 亦涵蓋書面語的應用文書練習，如開會通知、議程、公告文書等。進度預 定為每兩週一課。 This course is designed to assist international students learn and experience Mandarin in workplace or business contexts. The course content includes topics such as job searching, interviews, employment procedures, office meetings, business trips, work environments, and completing business sheets/forms. In addition to spoken language practice, the course also covers formal written skills to meet the demands of more formal business situations, such as meeting notices, agendas, and official announcements. The course is structured to cover one lesson every two weeks. 授課方式 Teaching Method 老師講授、師生互動、小組討論、活動練習、任務型教學 Lectures, class activities, group discussion, task-based learning 成績考核 Grading Policy 出席、課堂參與 Attendance & Class Participation 30% 含每週課後議題討論 Includes weekly after-class discussions online. 功課、隨堂測驗 Assignments & Quizzes 30% 含語法作業、每課測驗及小組報告 Includes grammar assignments, quizzes for each lesson, and group presentations. 期中報告 Midterm Presentation 20% 期末考（或報告） Final Exam/Reports 20% 課程進度表 Course Schedule 將依教學需要調整 This schedule is subject to change. 週 Week 進度 Progress 1-2 第一課 求職 L1 Job Hunting 3-4 第二課 面試 L2 Job Interview 5-6 第三課 應聘 L3 Job Offer 7-8 第四課 辦公環境 L4 Office Environment 9 期中報告 Midterm Presentation 小組報告：辦公環境設計與招聘 Group Presentation: Office Design/Recruitment 10-11 第五課 參加會議 L5 Attending a Meeting 12-13 第六課 商務表單 L6 Business Sheets 14-15 第七課 商務出差 L7 Taking a Business Trip 16 期末考試/報告 Final Exam/Presentation 作業說明 Assignments 1. 公告、作業繳交、同儕評分等，都利用本校 eLearn 平臺： https://elearn.nthu.edu.tw/ Announcements, assignment submissions, peer assessments, and other course-related activities will all be managed through NTHU’s eLearn platform: https://elearn.nthu.edu.tw/ 2. 每位同學都需要完成以下指定作業： All students are required to complete the following assignments, (1) 每週課後議題討論：預計 14 次，請以個人思考、反思為主， 可以使用軟體或工具輔助，但是必須完全了解自己寫的內 容和文字。 Weekly after-class reflections: A total of 14 posters are expected. Please focus on personal thoughts and reflections. Students may use online tools to assist, but must fully understand all the content and language the submitted. (2) （課前）每課錄音練習：共 7 課，自己錄或找同學一起錄音 都可以，請先預習對話，發音錯誤或太多停頓都會扣分。 Pre-class recording practice: There are 7 lessons in total. Students may record individually or with classmates. Please preview the dialogues in advance, or the points will be deducted for mispronunciations and frequent pauses. (3) （課後）每課語法作業練習：共 7 課，完成後掃描或拍照上 傳，也可以打字繳交（需為完整的一句話）。 After-class grammar exercises: There are 7 lessons in total. Students may submit the assignments by scanning, taking photos, or typing (complete sentences are required). 3. 每課上完後，隔週安排一次隨堂小考（筆試），以當課的詞彙、語 法和應用活動為主，請以藍筆、黑筆書寫，並準備紅筆即時檢討 修正。 The written quizzes will be held after each lesson, focusing on the vocabulary, grammar, and situated activities covered in class. Students are required to write with a blue or black pen, and prepare a red pen for in-class corrections and reviews. 4. 學生可以使用生成式 AI 進行議題發想、文句潤飾或結構參考等， 但是學生必須熟讀生成式 AI 所提供的文字並進行必要的改寫。 若經課堂討論發現學生不理解生成式 AI 所提供的內容，教師有 權重新針對該作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。修讀本課程之學 生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。 Students may use generative AI for idea generation, text refinement, or structural reference. However, students must thoroughly read and make necessary revisions to the text provided by the generative AI. If, during class discussions or proof checking, it is found that a student does not understand the content provided by the generative AI, the teacher reserves the right to re-evaluate or not grade the assignment or presentation. It uses several SoC designs, such as computer chip sets, cell phone IC, multimedia ICs, wireless communication ICs, information appliances and interface ICs, as examples to illustrate the top-down IC design flow, Intellectual Property(IP), system platform design and their market applications. The computer chip sets cover personal computer architectures, memory and peripheral I/O interface chip design. The cell phone IC covers heterogeneous multi-processor (HMP). The wireless communication includes CDMA, OFDM and LTE 4G chip designs. The multimedia ICs covers audio, still image, and video ICs. docs.text: Circuits and Electronics I (108 (spring)電路與電子學一 邱瀞德教授 (3 units) (Undergraduate students) 一、課程說明(Course Description) This course is intended for undergraduates in the computer science and other engineering department. In this course, we focus on two main topics, electronics and circuits. To give students better understanding of the models and circuits of the electronics devices, we will introduce the basic concepts of electric circuits first. It starts from the definition of current, voltage, power and energy. Then it covers the basic circuit components including resister, capacitor, and inductor. We also discuss the basic circuit analysis, such as nodal analysis of resistive circuits, transients in electrical circuits and sinusoidal steady-state circuit behavior. For electronics section, we will present the diode and MOS field-effect transistor. We will use simple models to describe these electronic devices and their I-V characteristics. Since the majority of electronic circuits today are designed as integrated circuits (ICs), we will discuss how to analyze and design the basic elements of integrated circuits with the emphasis on digital logic designs. 二、指定用書(Text Books) Part I: Circuits "Electrical Engineering, Principles and Applications", by Allan R. Hambley, fourth edition, (ISBN: 0-13-206692-0), Pearson, Prentice Hall. Part II” Electronics "Electronic Circuit analysis and Design", by Donald A. Neamen, (ISBN:007-125443-9), McGraw Hill. 三、參考書籍(References) 四、教學方式(Teaching Method) Lecture and discussion. 五、教學進度(Syllabus) Part I: ➢ CH1 Introduction ➢ CH2 Resistive Circuit ➢ CH3 Capacitor and Inductor ➢ CH4 Transient ➢ CH5 Steady State Sinusoidal Analysis ➢ CH6 Frequency Response Part II: ➢ Ch 1: Semiconductor materials ➢ Ch2: Diode ➢ Ch3: MOS field-effect transistor ➢ Ch4: Basic MOSFET Amplifiers simple models to describe these electronic devices I-V characteristics analyze and design the basic elements of integrated circuits with the emphasis on digital logic designs 六、成績考核(Evaluation) HW: 20% In-class participation : 5% Exam I: (25%) Exam II: (25%) Exam III: (25%) 七、可連結之網頁位址 https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw

docs.text: 英文課名: Introduction to Game Programming 中文課名: 遊戲程式設計 一、課程說明(Course Description) Game development is a hot topic in the modern entertainment industry. In this course, we will introduce a popular game engine, Unity3D. In the first half of the course, we will present various components in Unity3D that are fundamental for the beginner of game development. The remaining lectures will cover advanced topics necessary for producing games with large-scale, high quality, and rich interactivity. Every student is requested to participate in a team-project with the capacity of up to 4 persons. Each team will present a complete and original game at the end of the semester. Those outstanding works will be recommended to join a domestic game competition. 二、指定用書(Text Books) NA 三、參考書籍(References) l 人氣遊戲這樣做！Unity3D 遊戲設計實例講堂 第二版 四、教學方式(Teaching Method) l Self-study the online video lectures at home. l Doing practices and quizzes in the course l Joining the discussion session after the quiz. 五、教學進度(Syllabus) l Unity3D 引擎基本介紹 l 用 C# 撰寫 Unity script l 控制物理引擎與物件 transformation l 創建地圖(地形、植被、風、水、天空)與使用粒子特效 l 音效設計與 Unity GUI l 動畫系統、動畫曲線、key frame、finite state machine、blend tree 及匯入動畫 l Unity2D 引擎介紹 l 建立多人網路連線 l 如何提升遊戲效能 l 使用 Navigation 六、成績考核(Evaluation) l Assignments: 30% l In-Class Quiz: 20% l Final Project: 50% 七、AI 使用規則 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出。

docs.text: 英文課名: Introduction to Graphics Programming and its Applications 中文課名: 繪圖程式設計與應用 一、課程說明(Course Description) This course will introduce the fundamental of computer graphics and how to develop 3D applications using a powerful graphics APIs, named OpenGL. OpenGL has been designed to be a cross-platform Graphics API running on PCs and mobile devices. Although OpenGL ES (OpenGL for Embedded System) is widely adopted as the standard Graphics API for mobile devices, it is actually consisting of well-defined subsets of desktop version. In this course, we will lead you to go through the whole rendering pipeline, particularly focus on those programmable stages (or Shaders). Detailed APIs specification will be elaborated with the sample applications to help understand the physical meaning behind the functions. 二、指定用書(Text Books) NA 三、參考書籍(References) 1. OpenGL Programming Guide: The Official Guide to Learning OpenGL, Version 3.0 and 3.1, 7th Edition, by Dave Shreiner and the Khronos OpenGL ARB Working Group, 2009. 2. OpenGL Super Bible: Comprehensive Tutorial and Reference, 5th Edition, by Richard S. Wright, Nicholas Haemel, Graham Sellers, and Benjamin Lipchak, 2010. 3. OpenGL ES 2.0 Programming Guide, by Aaftab Munshi, Dan Ginsburg, and Dave Shreiner, 2009. 4. OpenGL Shading Language, 3rd Edition, by Randi J. Rost and Bill Licea-Kane, 2009. 5. Beginning OpenGL Game Programming, 2nd Edition, by Luke Benstead, 2009. 6. Fundamentals of Computer Graphics, 3rd Edition, by Peter Shirley and Steve Marschnes, 2009. 7. Real-Time Rendering, 3rd Edition, by Tomas Akenine-Möller, Eric Haines, and Naty Hoffman, 2008. 8. Interactive Computer Graphics: A Top-Down Approach Using OpenGL, 5th Edition, by Edward Angel, 2009 9. OpenGL official website. http://www.opengl.org/ 10. OpenGL ES official website. http://www.khronos.org/opengles/ 11. NVIDIA Developer’s Websites. http://developer.nvidia.com/page/home.html 12. AMD Developer’s Websites. http://developer.amd.com/Pages/default.aspx 四、教學方式(Teaching Method) Lectures. 五、教學進度(Syllabus) l Transformations (1 week) n 3D Space, Math, Projection l OpenGL Overview (3 weeks) n Rendering Pipeline n OpenGL Object (Buffer, Texture, Uniform) l Vertex Shader Stage (2 weeks) n Basic Concept n Drawing Commands l Fragment Shader Stage (1 week) n Basic Concept n Frame Buffers l Mesh Rendering (1 week) n Vertex Skinning l Fundamental of Shading (1 week) n Basic Concept n Shading Models (Blinn-Phong, Normal Mapping, Environment Mapping, Cell Shading) l Tessellation Shader Stage + Geometry Shader Stage (1 week) l Rendering Techniques (1 week) n Shadow, SSAO l WebGL (2 weeks) 六、成績考核(Evaluation) Assignments: 30% In-Class Quiz: 25% Final Project: 45% 七、AI 使用規則 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出。

docs.text: CSR 5303 Design Automation (2) EDA Tool Development for Custom Design, DRC/LVS, RC, 3DIC, + Spice Simulation, Waveform Viewing, OPC 李炯霆 (JT Li) Fall, 2026 About This DA (2) Course • We will discuss the major aspects in developing CAD tools for custom design, design rule checking (DRC), layout-versus-schematic (LVS), RC extraction, 3DIC layout • Based on the engineering efforts I led throughout my career. And more on finFet. • Also we are fortunate to have experts coming to discuss how to develop Spice simulator, waveform viewing and OPC • Working together to help you learning the practical aspects of EDA tools • How does design rule checking work? • What is layout versus schematic? Why layout density matters? • Important things to watch in analog layout; how about using FinFet? • How is the look-up-table created in cap extraction? • When watching videos, we can think about how those functionalities were implemented? • … • We design some projects for you to understand more • This course is to broaden your EDA knowledge beyond digital design Course Info • Time and place: Monday (from 2:20pm to 5:20pm) @____ • I will cover custom design, DRC/LVS, RC, 3DIC layout, … • Jack Yao (founder of Sandwork, ex-Scientist@Synopsys) will teach 3 sessions of Spice simulation and waveform viewing (likely 1 session remote) • HsuTing Huang will teach a session of how OPC and litho hot spot detection are developed • Welcome to reach out to me (via school email addr.) even off campus Reference Books Design of Analog CMOS Integrated Circuits, Second Edition Design of Analog CMOS IC by B. Razavi CMOS VLSI Design: A Circuits and Systems Perspective Neil H.E. Weste, David Harris, 4th edition And its web supplements https://pages.hmc.edu/harris/cmosvlsi/4e/index.html CMOS IC Layout - Concepts, Methodologies, and Tools by Dan Clein (1) Areas To Be Covered • Design rule checking (DRC) and layout versus schematic (LVS) • Layout Boolean geometry (polygons, custom shapes); how to develop rules • Double patterning, how to fix, cut poly, cut metal, density, … • Custom design • Design entry, PDK, device layout, custom layout, device matching, custom routing, … • Interactive design editing, asynchronous GUI programming, event driven, … • Verification • Parasitic extraction, IR/EM, P2P resistance, least resistive path • 3DIC • Chiplets -> design planning, wiring, dummy shapes, (electrical performance, …) (2) Spice Simulation, Waveform Viewing (By Jack Yao) • Simulator types: Spice, FastSpice, FasterSpice, AMS • Applications: verification, characterization, statistical • Automation: parametric, optimization, sensitivity • Analog simulation types: OP, transient, AC, HB • Spice fundamentals: KCL, KVL, Linear, Nonlinear, device modeling, • Algorithms: • From KCL/KVL to a linear system, matrix stamping, Newton-Raphson, OP, AC • Time domain simulation: • Companion models for energy-storing caps/inductors, numerical integration (forward, backward Euler, …) and orders (for stability) • Truncation errors, simulation tuning, harmonic balancing, … • Interactive waveform visualization, batch post processing • Raster vs. cartesian space, performance (remote display, refresh rate), storage, … (3) Lithography OPC And Hot Spot Detection (by HsuTing Huang) • Basics in developing OPC and hot spot detection Grading • Project-1: BPV (10%) (programming) • To exercise how to create an abstract view (blockages, pins, vias) for digital APR. A simple test case is given. Welcome to use Boost’s Boolean geometry APIs. • Project-2: DRC (10%) (programming) • Develop a checker for end-of-line, spacing, width. Display errors. • Project-3: CCM (25%) (tool flow) • We know device matching using common centroid method (CCM) is necessary. • Let’s use ADFP (TSMC 16nm PDK) to verify if indeed CCM is better. • Want you to expose to FinFet design Project oriented (80%) + participation (20%); then curve • Project-4: Qt & GDS (15%) (programming) • Enhance a program (which parses a GDS file and invokes Qt to display some hard coded shapes) by adding new shapes. • Understand the event queue and point out which procedures capture the cursor point to do query. • Parser and Qt codes are provided. • Project-5: flip-chip placement (10%) (report) • It is an ICCAD contest case. Write down your thoughts about how to do it. • Project-6: die-to-die routing (10%) (report) • Write down your thoughts about how to route a D2D wiring problem with shielding (based on a generic case from foundry-T) Please don’t miss invited speakers’ sessions. Otherwise, you will lose 4 participation points for each missing session.

docs.text: 課程簡述 (Brief course description) According to the course of “Essentials of Intelligent System Design Flow I” in spring semester, we set up system-level design methodology for chip(let) based 3D-IC and advanced packaging full flow (IC-Package-System) design, simulation including signal integrity and power integrity, E/T (Electrical/Thermal) co-analysis, and sign-off methodology. In this course, entitled “Essentials of Intelligent System Design Flow II”, we would focus on IC/Chip(let)-level design methodology including Full-Custom IC design flow such as analog and RF ICs design and Cell-based digital IC design flow such as physical synthesis, physical implementation, and multi-core silicon sign-off etc. Students can get the essential components of the challenges of latest IC/Chip(let)-level circuit design, advanced layout, simulation, synthesis, and silicon signoff. In addition, HLS (high-level synthesis) design flow based on generative artificial intelligence, which converts specifications into RTL, will also be included in this course. 教學方式 (Teaching Method) Lectures 教學大綱 (Syllabus) This course will include 6 major topics and provide students with essential capabilities to understand the challenges and requirement in each design phases for full custom IC and cell- based IC design methodologies, respectively. There are consist of 1. Overall System Level Design Planning – From IC to System 2. Custom IC, Analog and RF Design – Circuit Design, layout, and Verification 3. Digital Design and Sign-off – Logic Synthesis and Test 4. Digital Design and Sign-off – Physical Implementation 5. Digital Design and Sign-off – Silicon Sign-off 6. Digital Design and Sign-off – High Level Synthesis from Spec. to RTL 成績考核(Evaluation) • Attendance 30% • In-class activity 4% • Exam1 33% • Exam2 33% Schedule Detail Week Date Topics Hours Date and Speaker Teaching Method Instructor Lecture Exam 1 9/10 Overall System Level Design Planning – From IC to System 3 9/10 (Wilbert Chen, Sr. Manager) PowerPoint IC and Package design 2 10/1 Custom IC, Analog and RF Design -- Circuit Design, layout, and Verification 3 10/1 (Wilbert Chen, Sr. Manager) PowerPoint Analog, RF and Mixed Signal design, layout, and verification 3 11/5 Digital IC Design and Sign-off – Logic Synthesis and Test 2 11/5 (Chen-Yin Wu, Sr. Engineer) PowerPoint Digital IC Design Logic Synthesis 3 11/5 Midterm Examination 1 11/5 Multi- Selection 4 11/19 Digital IC Design and Sign-off – Physical Implementation 3 11/19 (Steven Lin, Director) PowerPoint Digital IC Design Physical Implementation 5 12/3 Digital IC Design and Sign-off – Silicon Sign-off (STA and EM-IR) 3 12/3 (Jason Huang, Director) PowerPoint Digital IC Sign-off and Verification 6 12/17 Digital IC Architecture Exploration – High Level Synthesis 2 12/17 (Edward Yeh, Sr. Manager) PowerPoint Digital IC Architecture Exploration 6 12/17 Final Examination 1 12/17 Multi- Selection TOTAL 16 2

docs.text: 課程資訊 (Course Information) 科號 Course Number 11510CTM 210100 學分 Credit 1 人數限制 Class Size 36 中文名稱 Course Title E-News 自媒體的多重宇宙課程 英文名稱 Course English Title Journalism Multi-Media Program on E-News Practices 任課教師 Instructor 周岐原 上課時間 Time Mn 上課教室 Room TSMC 台積 431 提醒您：請遵守智慧財產權，勿使用非法影印教科書 Please respect the intellectual property rights, do not use illegal copies of textbooks. 此科目對應之系 所課程規畫所欲 培養之核心能力 Core capability to be cultivated by this course  媒體素養與傳播實務  文字採訪撰寫與編輯能力  跨領域整合時，缺一不可的創作與商業思維  個人品牌與自媒體經營的核心能力與韌性 課程簡述 (Brief course description) 為提供跨領域學習，增進科管院學生遊刃於科技、財經專業知識與大眾傳媒之能力，將透過本 X-Class 課程培 養新聞編輯採訪技能，以科管院所發行之 E-news 線上刊物為實作媒體，提升學生媒體素養及培養新聞報導之 文字採訪撰寫編輯與視覺設計企劃編排能力。本課程由科管院兼任講師周岐原擔任 E-news 編輯團隊指導老 師。課程安排將在本學期利用 16 小時上課時數，進行實體與線上課程；本課程為一學分選修之 X-Class，全程 錄製影音檔案供衝堂學生課後自主學習，衝堂學生課堂中若需與教師討論，則另行安排時段線上進行。為便利 學生選課，本課程將於上下學期重複開課，同樣以 E-News 為實作刊物，課程教學內容則將有所不同；歡迎有 志學習大眾傳播新聞編採之同學上下學期均來選修，單獨選修亦可。 課程大綱 (Syllabus) Course keywords: X-class, E-news, 大眾媒體, 自媒體, 新聞, 編輯, 危機處理, 企劃, 媒體經營, youtube, podcast, Instagram, tiktok, 採訪, 寫作, 訪談, 主持, 電子報, 出版, 著作, 一、課程目標 ● 結合新聞編輯採訪相關理論與實務，提升學生媒體專業知能。 ● 統整大眾傳播理論與實務，強化產學交流，協助學生就業準備。 ● 藉由客座講師的講授與新聞界先進的分享，瞭解個人品牌發展的創作與商業營運狀況。 ● 經由科管院 E-News 電子報編輯採訪及實作，學生從做中學，累積實務經驗。 二、教學方式 (一) 教室實體授課。 (二) 線上遠距教學。 (三) 新聞媒體業界人士分享與機構參訪。 (四) 科管院 E-News 電子報專題企畫、採訪撰文與美術編輯實作。 三、課程進度 (9/7 開學、12/28 開始放寒假) 第一週 9/7: 第二週 9/14: 第三週 9/21: 第四週 9/28: 不上課 第五週 10/5: 第六週 10/12: 第七週 10/19: 第八週 10/26: 不上課 第九週 11/2: 第十週 11/9: 第十一週 11/16: 第十二週 11/23: 第十三週 11/30: 第十四週 12/7: 第十五週 12/14: 第十六週: 12/21: 不上課（期末考試開始） 四、參考書籍 五、課程評量 (一)E-News 文章專欄或美術編輯實作成績 70% (二)課堂紀律與師生互動狀況 30% ●使用 AI 的聲明：禁止使用。 根據本校公布之「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採取禁止使用，以下為相 關的監管機制： ◎修讀本門課程之學生應注意本門課不得繳交使用生成式人工智慧所產出的作業、報告或個人心 得。若經查核發現，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。 ◎修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。

docs.name: 企業導師與職涯發展(一)
docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 學分 Credit 0.5 人數限制 Class Size 0 中文名稱 Course Title 企業導師與職涯發展(一) 英文名稱 Course English Title Mentor Program and Career Development 任課教師 Instructor 洪淳琦 上課時間 Time SaturdayN（週六 1210-1310） 上課教室 Room 台積館 104 教室 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters 以科技管理學院「企業導師領航計畫」為主軸，藉由本課程推動「企業導師領航計畫」，讓本院學生提早認知 職涯發展，此課程中由本院及本校傑出企業家校友擔任導師，提供經驗交流及傳承，引領本院大二以上學生 了解產業趨勢及就業市場，培養未來競爭力。具體而言，本課程的導師來自高科技、金融、證券、投資、生 物科技、製造、文創、法律各領域，藉由導師們豐富實務經歷、產業專業、職場生存法則，讓參與課程的同 學不斷檢視自己的職涯規劃並調整學習方向。 請輸入課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」至少 5 個, 每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文, 以半形逗點分隔 (必填) Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 職涯發展、企業導師、就業、競爭力、校友 career development, mentor, jobs, competency, alumni 課程大綱 Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本微學分課程結合『科管院企業導師領航計畫』，並由唐迎華導師協助課程規畫及開設，本課程旨在將參與 計劃的學生之學習歷程，做系統化並完整紀錄。 課程內容依照『科管院企業導師領航計畫』進行，本計畫邀請多位傑出熱心校友擔任企業導師，目前參與本 計畫的導師共有 17 位，每位導師至多帶領 3 位學生，為期一學年執行職涯發展探討。 課程內容及活動方式將根據導師專長領域與學生需求彈性調整，課程內容可能涵蓋導師授課、企業參訪或邀 請專家演講，詳細內容視各位導師而訂，本課程的目的為讓修課學生儘早了解職涯發展的重要性。 ● 指定用書(Text Books) 由企業導師指定。 ● 參考書籍(References) 由企業導師推薦。 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 1. 修課對象: 本課程限定科管院大二以上學生選課修讀，包含其他學院雙主修學生(不包含輔系、雙專長)。 2. 修課期間: 本課程為一學年課程，分為上下學期各 0.5 微學分，一學年計一學分。 11510CTM 210200 3. 課程要求: 1.) 【報名配對制】 I. 本課程採報名配對制，透過填寫報名表單的方式，經執委會根據導師志願序與其他綜合表現，將 學生與企業導師分組配對，且以加簽方式選課。未配對成功者無法選修本課程。 II. 報名前須參加課程說明會：開學第一週 9/7 中午 12:00~13:00 於台積館一樓孫運璿演講廳舉辦。因 衝堂無法參加者，須補看課程說明影片。課程說明影片連結於會後提供。 III. 課程說明會報名網址：https://forms.gle/f3cse2DzZx9EjEVf9 IV. 報名表單網址：https://forms.gle/2NCWrdEXeRuJfL8x5 (9/10 23:59 前完成) V. 9/16 email 通知配對結果。 VI. 配對成功者，須在 9/18 完成加簽選課。 2.) 【必出席之團體活動】 I. 導師生相見歡(日期暫定)：9/21 18:00~21:00，只接受衝堂請假，本活動無法補課。 II. 企業參訪：暫定學期第三週參訪。只接受衝堂請假，請假者補看指定影片補課。無論實體參訪或 補看影片，活動結束後三天內完成個人心得報告，一人一篇 300 字內。 III. 以上兩項團體活動缺席者學分不通過。 3.) 【必出席之小組活動】 I. 每學期至少兩次小組活動，由各組導師生共同討論訂定；例如：職涯座談、演講、展覽、履歷面 試加強、參與導師公司會議或計畫、一日實習、執行專案等。 II. 小組活動結束後三天內完成小組心得報告，一組一篇 300 字內。缺席者須看指定影片補課。 ● 成績考核(Evaluation) 企業導師根據學生出席狀況及表現，核給通過或不通過。授課教師有最終成績審核權利。宜注意如學生未滿 足上述每學期兩次全體活動(衝堂者有補課機制)、小組活動兩次之要求，本課程將不予通過。 ●『科管院企業導師領航計畫』導師名單: https://career-ctm.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/406-1380-293944,r4772.php?Lang=zh-tw ●『科管院企業導師領航計畫』宣傳影片: https://youtu.be/5fN_rW1Lo3I 日期皆暫定

docs.name: 跨境科技創業實作
docs.text: National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 科號 Course Number 11510CTM 501000 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Size of Limit 14（限參與 ABPC 競賽學 生） 中文名稱 Course Title 跨境科技創業實作 英文名稱 Course English Title Cross-Border Tech Entrepreneurship Practicum 任課教師 Instructor 郭孟倫、賴怡君 教師聯絡方式 Contact Information tonny@gapp.nthu.edu.tw 上課時間 Time Monday 17:30~20:20 M9MaMb 上課教室 Room TSMC Building 223 先修科目 Prerequisite(s) 無 課程目標 Course Objectives This course is designed in conjunction with the Asia Business Plan Competition (ABPC 2026). The objectives are: 1. To select and train students with a passion for and potential in entrepreneurship, equipping them with fundamental knowledge and skills in entrepreneurial management. 2. To experience cross-border entrepreneurship in practice by participating in ABPC and forming cross-cultural teams with students from Hong Kong, Singapore, and China. 3. To guide students through the complete entrepreneurial process, from business opportunity analysis and business model design to prototype validation and investor pitching. 本課程為配合亞洲商業計劃競賽（Asia Business Plan Competition, ABPC 2026）所開 設，其目的為： 1. 篩選對創業有熱情、有潛力之學生加以培訓，使其具備創業管理之基礎知識與技 能。 2. 透過參與 ABPC，與香港、新加坡、中國學生組成跨文化團隊，體驗跨境創業實 務。 3. 指導學生完成從商業機會分析分析、商業模式設計、原型驗證到投資人簡報之完整 創業流程。 課程說明 Course Description The Asia Business Plan Competition (ABPC) is co-organized by our college, the National University of Singapore (NUS) School of Computing, and the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST) Dual Degree Program in Technology and Management. This year marks the third edition, hosted by HKUST, with the theme "Smart Robotics for Better Living and Work". The event will take place from June 15 to 25, 2026, at the HKUST Guangzhou campus. This year's partners also include the HKUST(GZ) Redbird Startup Program. The total participation scale is 48 students, organized into 8 cross-university and cross-cultural teams. This course adopts a three-phase wrap-around design: pre-departure training (Spring semester), on-site field practicum (10 days), and post-return reflection and synthesis (Summer National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus to early Fall semester), totaling approximately 90 hours of practical work. Enrollment is restricted to students who have passed the college's selection process and are participating in the ABPC. 亞洲商業計劃競賽（ABPC）由本院、新加坡國立大學運算學院、香港科技大學科技及 管理學雙學位學程共同舉辦。本年度為第三屆，由 HKUST 主辦，主題為 Smart Robotics for Better Living and Work，活動期間為 2026 年 6 月 15 日至 25 日，地點 為 HKUST 廣州校區。本屆夥伴另增列 HKUST(GZ) Redbird Startup Program，總參與 規模 48 名學生，編組為 8 個跨校跨文化團隊。 本課程採三段式 wrap-around 設計：行前訓練（春季學期）、現場移地實作（10 天）、 返國後反思綜合（暑期至秋季初），實作總時數約 90 小時。修習對象限定為通過院遴 選並參加 ABPC 之學生。 請輸入課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」至少 5 個, 每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文, 以半形逗 點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) Entrepreneurship, Lean Startup, Business Model, Design Thinking, Cross-cultural Teams. 創業, 精實創業, 商業模式, 設計思考, 跨文化團隊 指定用書 Textbooks This course does not specify a single textbook; the following three are core readings: 本課程不指定單一教科書；以下三本為核心讀物： 1. Ries, E. (2011). The lean startup. Crown Business. 2. Osterwalder, A., & Pigneur, Y. (2010). Business model generation. Wiley. 3. Brown, T. (2008). Design thinking. Harvard Business Review, 86(6), 84–92. 參考書籍 References 1. Blank, S., & Dorf, B. (2020). The startup owner’s manual. Wiley. 2. Duarte, N. (2010). Resonate: Present visual stories that transform audiences. Wiley. 3. Sharkey, A., & Sharkey, N. (2012). Granny and the robots: Ethical issues in robot care for the elderly. Ethics and Information Technology, 14(1), 27–40. 教學方式 Teaching Approach This course adopts a three-phase wrap-around design:  Pre-departure Training (Spring semester): Focuses on Lean Startup, Business Model Canvas, and Design Thinking as core methodologies, supplemented by an introduction to the smart robotics industry and preparatory courses for cross-cultural teamwork.  On-site Field Practicum (June 15 to 25 at HKUST Guangzhou campus): Students are assigned to cross-university, cross-cultural teams. They will fully participate in 4 Master Workshops, 3 robotics company visits (UBTECH, iFLYTEK, PuduTech, Geek+, etc.), 5 rounds of mentor reviews, and finally deliver an investor pitch at the Investor Pitch Competition.  Post-return Reflection and Synthesis (Summer to early Fall semester): Complete a reflection journal, re-evaluate business model feasibility (putting the proposal back into the context of Taiwan and Southeast Asian markets), and hold a public final presentation at the beginning of the Fall semester. Selection Method: Due to the overseas field practicum, the enrollment quota is subject to the host's limitations and is restricted to students who pass the college's selection. The selection criteria include a personal resume, proof of English proficiency (CEFR B2 or equivalent), a 1- page idea pitch, and an interview. National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 本課程採三段式 wrap-around 設計： 1. 行前訓練（春季學期）：以精實創業、商業模式畫布、設計思考為核心方法論，搭配 智慧機器人產業導讀與跨文化團隊合作預備課程。 2. 現場移地實作（6 月 15 日至 25 日於 HKUST 廣州校區）：學生編入跨校跨文化 團隊，全程參與 4 場 Master Workshops、3 場機器人企業參訪（UBTECH、 iFLYTEK、PuduTech、Geek+ 等）、5 輪 mentor reviews，最終於 Investor Pitch Competition 進行投資人簡報。 3. 返國後反思綜合（暑期至秋季學期初）：完成反思日誌、商業模式可行性再評估（將 提案放回台灣與東南亞市場脈絡），並於秋季學期初舉辦公開成果發表會。 遴選方式：本課程因涉及境外移地，名額受主辦方配額限制，限通過院遴選之學生修 習。遴選項目包含個人簡歷、英語能力證明（CEFR B2 或同等）、1 頁 idea pitch 與面 試。 評分標準 Grading Grading 1. Pre-departure assignments (Reading notes, Business Model Canvas, Interviews, Mock Pitch): 20% 2. HKUST mentor reviews (accumulative over 5 rounds): 30% 3. ABPC Investor Pitch (including presentation, 1-pager, and on-site Q&A): 30% 4. Post-return reflection journal: 10% 5. Public final presentation: 10% Grading will be jointly evaluated by our university's instructors (accounting for 55%) and the HKUST mentor team (accounting for 45%). The university's instructors reserve the right to determine the final grades. 1. 行前作業（讀書筆記、商業模式畫布、訪談、模擬簡報） 20% 2. HKUST mentor reviews（5 輪累計） 30% 3. ABPC 投資人簡報（含簡報、1-pager、現場答辯） 30% 4. 返國後反思日誌 10% 5. 公開成果發表 10% 評分由本校授課教師（合計 55%）與 HKUST 業師團（合計 45%）共同評定，本校教 師保留最終成績之決定權。 教學進度 Course Schedule Phase 1: Pre-departure Training (Spring Semester)  Pre-departure preparation: Course orientation, ABPC event briefing, smart robotics industry landscape  Lean Startup, Business Model Canvas, and Design Thinking methodologies  Customer discovery, cross-cultural teamwork preparation  Robot ethics, validation methods Phase 2: On-site Field Practicum (June 15 to 25 at HKUST Guangzhou campus)  Day 1-2: Arrival, Opening, X-culture Teaming Workshop  Day 3-4: Ideation Workshop, Robotics company visits, Mentor Review #1  Day 5-7: Validation Workshop, Mentor Review #2-3, Free Exploration Day  Day 8-9: Pitching Workshop, Mentor Review #4-5  Day 10: Investor Pitch Competition, Award Dinner  Day 11: Return journey National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus Phase 3: Post-return Reflection and Synthesis (Summer to early Fall semester)  Summer: Individual debriefing, reflection journal, business model feasibility re- evaluation  Fall: Public final presentation Phase 1 行前訓練（春季學期）  行前準備：課程定位、ABPC 賽事說明、智慧機器人產業地景  精實創業、商業模式畫布、設計思考方法論  客戶探索、跨文化團隊合作預備  機器人倫理、驗證方法 Phase 2 現場移地實作（6 月 15 日至 25 日於 HKUST 廣州校區） Day 1-2：抵達、開幕、X-culture Teaming Workshop Day 3-4：構想工作坊、機器人企業參訪、Mentor Review #1 Day 5-7：驗證工作坊、Mentor Review #2-3、自由探索日 Day 8-9：簡報工作坊、Mentor Review #4-5 Day 10：投資人簡報競賽、頒獎晚宴 Day 11：返程 Phase 3 返國後反思綜合（暑期至秋季學期初）  暑期：個別 debrief、反思日誌、商業模式可行性再評估  秋季公開成果發表會 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則 (Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI)：(2)有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output (2) Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output This course allows students to use generative AI (such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) as assistants for idea generation, market research, and language polishing. All deliverables must include an AI Use Statement disclosing the tools used, the purpose, and the extent of human revision. The core paragraphs of the reflection journal must not be ghostwritten by AI, and interview subjects and market data must not be fabricated by AI. 本課程允許學生使用生成式 AI（如 ChatGPT、Claude、Gemini）作為構想發想、市場 研究與語言潤飾之輔助。所有交付產出須附 AI Use Statement，揭露使用工具、用途與 人類修訂幅度。反思日誌核心段落不得由 AI 代寫，訪談對象與市場資料不得以 AI 偽造。 課程相關連接 Course Related Links  Steve Blank, How to Build a Startup: https://www.udacity.com/course/how-to-build-a- startup--ep245  Strategyzer Business Model Canvas: https://www.strategyzer.com/library/the-business- model-canvas

docs.text: National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 科號 Course Number 11510CTM520100 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Size of Limit 18 人 中文名稱 Course Title ESG 永續投資與綠色金融創新 英文名稱 Course English Title ESG Sustainable Investment and Financial Innovation 任課教師 Instructor 俞明德 Min-Teh Yu 教師聯絡方式 Contact Information 教師: mtyu@mx.nthu.edu.tw Office hours: Fri. 0830-10:00; 13:00-14:10 TSMC Bldg.: 710 上課時間 Time F6F7F8 (14:15 – 17:00) 上課教室 Room 台積 833 先修科目 Prerequisite(s) 本課程對應之學習目標與核心能力 Aligned Learning Goals and Learning Objectives 1. Equip students with professional writing and reading ability. 2. Equip students with fundamental concepts of financial management. 3. Link students with financial management to real business decisions. 課程目標 Course Objectives 1. 培養學生了解國內外 ESG 永續投資與金融創新之發展趨勢。 2. 使學生掌握當前 ESG 相關議題及企業在永續投資與金融創新領域之現況。 3. 透過議題討論與分組報告，培養學生理論分析與實務應用能力，提升學習成效。 課程說明 Course Description 近年來在疫情、氣候變遷及全球永續發展趨勢影響下，ESG 已成為國際金融市場與企 業治理的重要議題。根據 World Economic Forum, WEF 之全球風險報告指出，環境與氣 候風險已成為全球重要風險之一，各國政府、企業及金融機構逐漸重視綠色金融與永續 投資發展，並積極推動相關金融商品與投資策略。許多國際金融機構與基金亦遵循 Principles for Responsible Investment, PRI，將 ESG 納入投資決策。 本課程從理論與實務面進行深入探討全球與台灣 ESG 永續投資與綠色金融市場之發 展趨勢，並融入 CFA 永續投資相關教材內容及產業專家之實務分享。透過議題分析及企 業案例分享，介紹國內外永續金融的重要理論架構與實務運作，使學生掌握 ESG 投資最 新趨勢、永續金融創新商品發展，以及如何運用金融科技進行投資標的篩選與資產配置 分析。本課程並透過議題討論與小組報告，培養學生對 ESG 永續投資與金融創新的分析 能力與國際視野。 請輸入課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」至少 5 個, 每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文, 以半形逗 點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus ESG 永續投資 ESG Investing, 永續金融 Sustainable Finance, 綠色金融 Green Finance, 金融科技 FinTech, 永續投資策略 Sustainable Investment Strategies, 金融創新 Financial Innovation 指定用書 Textbooks Class notes, PowerPoint slides, and assigned readings 參考書籍 References 《永續投資與綠色金融創新》永續金融與影響力投資學院出版 由證基會會贈書，於加退選結束，確認修課人數後提供名單 教學方式 Teaching Approach Lectures and group discussions. 評分標準 Grading Class Participation 70% (全勤 70 分，缺席一次減 3 分，請假減 1 分) Final Research Report 30% (PPT presentation; 任何一場或多場演講的心得分享或是任何 一篇相關主題的學術論文閱讀分享; 有報告>= 15 分) 教學進度 Course Schedule The actual schedule may be adjusted based on course progress. 授課內容 Topic(s) 1 CFA 永續投資說明與考試經驗分享&國內永續金融證照說明 09/11 2 臺灣永續金融政策法規與市場發展趨勢 /法銀巴黎投顧黃智偉副總 09/18 3 中秋節放假 09/25 4 國際永續金融政策與投資市場發展趨勢 /Deloitte 林志煒副總 10/02 5 國慶日補假 10/09 6 永續投資策略、商品創新與實踐方法 /政治大學王儷玲教授 10/16 7 國際淨零減碳與碳交易 /臺北大學李堅明教授 10/23 8 永續投資典範實務經驗分享 /東方匯理投信劉佳雨基金經理 10/30 9 永續投資之盡職治理與議合 /法銀巴黎投顧黃智偉副總 11/06 10 氣候治理：低碳轉型與韌性調適連結企業經營 /臺灣師範大學葉欣誠 教授 11/13 11 證基會職涯發展博覽會活動 (on site or online) 11/20 12 永續投資之研究評估、資產配置建構與優化 /東吳大學李宜熹副教授 11/27 13 期末報告 12/04 14 企業永續數位轉型與綠色金融科技創新 /政治大學謝明華教授 12/11 15 永續投資與綠色金融未來發展 /政治大學王儷玲教授 12/18 16 行憲紀念日放假 12/25 AI 使用規則 (use of the AI) (1)完全開放使用且無須註明 Unrestricted use with no disclosure required (2)有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output (3)禁止使用，請註明相關的監管機制 Prohibited use; please specify relevant oversight (4)本課程無涉及 AI 使用 Not applicable National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 課程相關連接 Course Related Links 1. 本課程證基會提供用書，請助教於加退選結束後提供名單，以利書籍寄送，上課以 講師簡報為主，簡報會放置在 雲端連結 https://reurl.cc/L2RDN4 提供下載 2. 有參與此課程的同學證基會頒發研習證明，因此需要同學資料進行帳號建檔後才能 登入下載，屆時提供修課名單還請包含 姓名、年級系所、身分證字號、連絡電話、 email，若無需要研習證明的同學可不提供，再請助教們協助蒐集，學期結束時請同 學們可到證基會網站自行下載證明。 3. 本課程為鼓勵同學將提供獎學金，期末報告第一名組別可獲得 3000 元獎學金及優 異獎狀，期末報告方式不限，老師們可於評比後決選出第一名組別並提供同學名 單。（再請老師們於期末報告結束後一周內提供名單以利獎狀製作寄送） 4. 有關獎學金需要請同學們簽收領取單據，相關文件將會和獎狀一同寄送，請助教們 於同學完成簽收後將單據寄回至 臺北市中正區南海路 3 號 9 樓。 5. 預計會於 12/18(五) 頒發獎狀及獎學金，還請老師們協助頒發並一同合影。

docs.name: 跨領域學術英文分析與學習
docs.nameEn: Interdisciplinary Academic English Analysis and Learning
docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科 號 組別 學分 2 人數限制 40 科目中文名稱 跨領域學術英文分析 與學習 教室 生科 113 室 科目英文名稱 Interdisciplinary Academic English Analysis and Learning 任 課 教 師 湯學成 上 課 時 間 Ma Mb 請勾選 此科目對應之系所課程規畫所欲培養之核心 能力 Core capability to be cultivated by this course 權重（百分比） Percentage √ 自我瞭解與溝通表達 Self-awareness, expressions & communication 20% √ 邏輯推理與批判思考能力 Logical reasoning & critical thinking 20% √ 科學思維與反思 Scientific thinking & reflection 20% √ 藝術與人文涵養 Aesthetic & humanistic literacy 10% √ 資訊科技與媒體素養 Information technology & media literacy 20% √ 多元觀點與社會實踐 Diverse views & social practices 10% 一、課程說明： 「跨領域學術英文分析與學習 」為協助大學部學生銜接研究所學習 而設計，適合大二至大四、已開始接觸專題研究或對未來研究發展有興 趣之學生修習。隨著研究歷程的推進，學生在學術文獻閱讀、研究理解 與學術寫作表達方面，對英文能力的需求日益提升。本課程旨在系統性 地培養學生之學術英文閱讀與分析能力，協助其建立紮實基礎，以利未 來研究所階段之學習與研究發展。 本課程選用教材涵蓋多元學術領域，透過跨領域學術文本的閱讀、 解析與比較，引導學生理解不同學科之研究取向、論證邏輯與共通的學 術論述結構。藉由此一學習歷程，學生不僅能有效提升學術英文理解與 表達能力，亦能在語文學習的同時，逐步拓展其跨領域學術視野，培養 理解不同研究文化與思維方式的能力。 在全球化與跨國科研合作日益頻繁的趨勢下，具備良好的學術英文 閱讀、分析與溝通能力，已成為清華大學學生及臺灣未來科研人才不可 或缺的核心素養。本課程期望協助學生及早建立跨領域學術英文能力， 使其在未來參與國際學術交流、研究合作與科學溝通時，能清楚表達研 究理念、理解多元學術觀點，並在國際舞台上展現清華大學與臺灣科研 社群的學術實力與影響力。 二、指定用書： 本課程主要教材為 Academic Writing for Graduate Students（第三版）， 作者為 Swales 與 Feak，將依大學部學生之知識背景與學習階段，調整 教學深度與引導學習重點。 三、參考書籍： 將依照課堂同學的知識背景提供適合之參考文獻。 四、教學方式： 本課程以課堂講授與討論並行。教師將於課堂中系統性講解學術英 文寫作與分析相關主題，課程內容涵蓋以下單元： Unit 1: An Approach to Academic Writing； Unit 2: General-Specific Text； Unit 3: Problem, Process, and Solution； Unit 4: Data Commentary； Unit 5: Constructing a Research Paper。 課堂中將引導學生參與文本分析與討論，並透過作業練習強化學 習成效；學生之學習成果亦將透過考試方式進行評量。本課程設有期 中考與期末考，以綜合評估學生對課程內容之熟悉程度、理解與應用 能力。 五、課程進度： Unit 1: An Approach to Academic Writing (Week 1-3)； Understanding academic discourse communities; purposes and audience in academic writing; characteristics of academic style. Unit 2: General-Specific Text (Week 4-5)； Text organization patterns; topic generalization and specification; paragraph development and coherence. Unit 3: Problem, Process, and Solution (Week 6-8)； Problem identification and framing; process description; solution articulation and logical flow. Midterm Exam. (Week 9) Unit 4: Data Commentary (Week 10-12)； Describing trends and patterns; interpreting figures and tables; language for reporting data. Unit 5: Constructing a Research Paper (Week 13-15)； Creating a research space; citation and tense; negative opening in introduction; purpose statement and tense; data commentary; location statements; special verb agreement; making comparisons. Final Exam. (Week 16) 六、成績考核 Midterm Exam (45%), Final Exam (45%), Homework + Participation of Discussion + Attendance (10%) 七、學生於本課程使用 AI 的聲明 本課程鼓勵學生在透明與負責的原則下，使用 AI 工具進行課業協 作。學生在課堂作業應簡要說明如何使用生成式 AI 如文句潤飾或結構 參考等內容。

docs.name: 癌症生物學導論
docs.text: 1 Cancer Biology 101 (癌症生物學導論) Instructor: Chun-Chao Wang (王群超) Email: ccwang@life.nthu.edu.tw Phone: +886-3-516-2589 (office) https://chunchaowang.wixsite.com/wanglab Office Location: Life Science Building I, Room 527 Office Hours: By appointment Course Description: If you want to understand how cancer starts and spreads, this course is for you. This course is also a useful introduction to cancer biology for undergraduate students from diverse backgrounds. Some biology knowledge will be helpful but not required. We'll talk about the origins of cancer and the genetic and cellular basis for cancer. The factors that have been implicated in triggering cancers and research directions for cancer therapy will also be covered. Primary Resources: The Biology of Cancer, Third Edition, by Robert A. Weinberg Recent publications investigating human cancer Course Structure: This is a lecture-based course on cancer biology. In addition to two exams, students are required to present a scientific review paper both in class and on YouTube. Active participation in class discussion is expected. Exams: 1st exam: Covers Ch. 01-05 2nd exam: Covers Ch. 06-10 Student Group Presentation Guidelines Overview Each group will select one review paper from the provided list to present. The presentation consists of two parts: • Lightning Talk: A 3-minute recorded video. • Oral Presentation: A 35-minute live presentation. Presenter Responsibilities A. Before Your Presentation: • Record your 3-minute lightning talk and upload it to YouTube. Example Lightning Talks https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLd8bBKy1dyo2Z52CGlZl58gt6q4p7QD X-&si=0E8Jf8HYHY8zVGq3 2 • Submit your final presentation slides to eeclass at least 3 days prior to your presentation date. • Grade all YouTube questions submitted by the audience, categorizing them into four tiers (e.g., Top 10%, Good 40%, Average 40%, Needs Improvement 10%). • Answer the top 10% of YouTube questions during the live presentation. • Prepare questions for the audience. You will use a random name picker during your session to select an audience member to answer a question. Random Name Picker: https://tw.piliapp.com/random/wheel/ B. After Your Presentation: • Rank the live answers given by audience members. Audience Responsibilities A. Before Each Presentation: • Submit one question for each group in the comments of their YouTube lightning talk. • Deadline: 4 days before the group's live presentation. • Upload a screenshot of your submitted YouTube comment to eeclass to receive credit. B. During Each Presentation: • Be prepared to be randomly selected to answer a question live from the presenters. Note: Members of a presenting group are exempt from audience duties for their own presentation. Grading Breakdown Exams (60%) • 1st exam: 30% • 2nd exam: 30% Group Presentation (30%) • Lightning Talk Video: 5% • Oral Presentation: 25% Participation (20%) • YouTube Questions: 10% • In-Class Q&A Response: 10% Extra Credit (Up to 1%) • Students will receive +0.5% if their YouTube question is selected for the top 10% and they ask it live during the presentation. Total possible score is 111%, though the final grade is capped at 100%.

docs.text: 第 1 頁，共 3 頁 科目課程簡介課目名稱： (中文) 人體解剖學虛擬實作 (英文) 3D Organon Virtual Reality (VR) Human Anatomy 授課老師：張壯榮、彭明德、莊永仁、李佳霖 學分數： 1 學分上 課時間：Wed. 13:20-14:10 or 14:20-15:10 教室: 生二220 修課資格：大學部二年級以上 (需修習過人體生理與解剖學) 課程目標： 大體解剖學實驗一直是解剖學的重要教學方式，但並非所有學校皆具備相關的軟硬體設備與師 資（包括大體老師）。此外，對部分學生而言，實驗課程可能造成相當大的心理壓力。近年來， 隨著電腦科技的進步，以及新教學方法與教材的研發，虛擬實境（Virtual Reality, VR）解剖學 教材逐漸被應用，以補充或部分取代傳統的大體解剖學實驗。 授課方式: 本課程採用解剖學虛擬實境設備與教材進行教學，具備以下功能：可觀察人體局部構造（如頭 部、胸部、腹部等），即局部解剖學。可單獨觀察各系統（如呼吸、循環、消化、神經等）， 即系統解剖學。可搜尋並定位特定器官構造。提供不同角度的切面，並可放大以觀察細節。可 組合多個切面以了解器官構造的走向、相對位置與關係。互動式解剖功能（器官構造可移除、 放回、旋轉等）。可對器官構造進行著色與標記。可與同部位的 X 光、MRI 或 CT 影像進行比 對。內含器官構造的文字說明、影片與動畫。 關鍵字: Anatomy解剖學, Physiology生理學, Virtual Reality (VR) 虛擬實境, Clinical Perspective 臨床觀 點, Organ Function 器官功能 授課進度表 Date Chapter and Topics Teacher 1 9/09 助教時間/ The Skeletal System Dr. CR Chang 2 9/16 The Skeletal System Dr. CR Chang 3 9/23 The Urinary System Dr. CR Chang 4 9/30 The Muscular System Dr. MD Perng 5 10/07 Special Senses Dr. MD Perng 6 10/14 The Endocrine System Dr. MD Perng 7 10/21 Midterm Exam I 8 10/28 The Cardiovascular-Heart Dr. YJ Chuang 第 2 頁，共 3 頁 9 11/04 The Cardiovascular-Brain Dr. YJ Chuang 10 11/11 全校運動大會(停課一天) 11 11/18 The Cardiovascular-Liver Dr. YJ Chuang 12 11/25 Midterm Exam II 13 12/02 The Nervous System Dr. JL Lee 14 12/09 The Nervous System Dr. JL Lee 15 12/16 The Digestive System The Reproductive Dr. JL Lee 16 12/23 Final Exam 縮短為 16 周教學說明：扣除開始的準備周及微調整體實作時間，調整為 16 周。

docs.text: - 1 - 115 人體生理與解剖學 11510DMS 370300 (Human Anatomy & Physiology) COURSE IDENTIFICATION LS Bldg. II R105: Human Anatomy & Physiology Lecture: Mon 15:30-18:20 (M7M8M9) Lecturers: Prof. Chuang-Rung Chang, Prof. Ming-Der Perng, Prof. Yung-Jen Chuang, Prof. Jia-Lin Lee COURSE DESCRIPTION: Human Anatomy and Physiology is designed for majors in the Department of Medical Science. This course covers both the anatomy and physiology of the human body, including cell structure and function as well as fundamental concepts of A&P. Emphasis is placed on the cellular level and the following systems: integumentary, muscular, nervous, endocrine, cardiovascular, lymphatic, respiratory, digestive, urinary, and reproductive. Course Outcomes: Students will be able to 1. Recognize and understand anatomical and physiological terminology 2. Know major organic and inorganic chemicals as they relate to the human body 3. Describe cellular structure and cellular activity 4. Discuss anatomical and physiological features of Integumentary, Muscular, Nervous, Endocrine, Cardiovascular, Lymphatic, Respiratory, Digestive, Urinary and Reproductive systems. 5. Apply the concept of homeostasis to human physiological activity 6. Evaluate select pathological conditions as they relate to normal functioning of the above-named systems TEXTBOOK: Essential of Human Anatomy and Physiology 12th edition by Elaine N. Mariem, Pearson Education. ISBN: 978-1-292-21611-9 Author(s): Elaine N. Marieb, PhD, Professor, Holyoke Community College • The best-selling Essentials of Human Anatomy and Physiology continues to set the standard for one-semester A&P texts. With her hallmark clear and friendly writing style and meaningful analogies, Elaine Marieb emphasizes the relevance of anatomy & physiology to students’ lives and future careers. The book continues to offer just the right balance of anatomy, physiology, and clinical coverage to make the content complete, but not overwhelming. New clinical photos in the - 2 - Homeostatic Imbalance feature help students visualize diseases and disorders, and new integrated Concept Links help students make connections across topics and body systems. A new, more modern design makes the book more accessible than ever, and new specific references to Mastering A&P direct students to study tools and resources that reinforce their understanding of chapter concepts. ATTENDANCE: Students are expected to attend all lectures punctually. Repeated lateness may result in a deduction of points. Absences or excuses must be communicated in advance and in accordance with University regulations to be considered valid. Lecturers may be contacted by email. docs.text: 1 11510DMS 370500 醫學遺傳學 Medical Genetics 任課教師: 廖品超、周裕珽 Time: T3T4 (星期二 10:10-12:00) Room: LSII R217 生命科學二館 217 教室 一、課程說明(Course Description) In addition to the basic introduction of human genetics, the most updated scientific and technical advances in human genetics will be included. The class will cover the basic genetic rules with emphasis on medical applications. The lectures will include genetic testing, screening, approaches to therapy, personalized medicine, disease models, comparative genomics, model organisms, and epigenetics. 二、指定用書 Human Heredity Principles and Issues. 10th/9th ed. docs.nameEn: Medical Measurement in the Application of Music Healthcare
docs.text: 課 程 名 稱 生理量測與音樂健康照護 開課教師 授課對象 學分數 授課時數(h) 開授系所 蘇美如 戚居暘 大學、研究所 選修、2 學分 32 醫學科學系 授課時間、地點 週四 10:10-12:00 生科二館 217 課程說明 本課程以「音樂、健康科技與表演藝術醫學」為核心，帶領學生從實 證醫學基礎出發，學習如何將音樂介入、健康照護與生理量測應用於 高齡者照護與表演藝術健康促進。課程前半部介紹實證醫學、學術海 報製作、音樂健康照護、音樂介入成效評估，以及表演藝術醫學的基 本概念與研究典範；後半部則進一步探討常用生理量測技術，包括 IMU、關節活動度、姿勢動作分析、表面肌電圖與肌肉負荷分析，並延 伸至智慧健康照護系統、生理訊號資料應用、多模態資料與 AI 輔助照 護系統設計。課程採講授、案例討論、分組主題分享與期末海報競賽 並行，培養學生跨領域整合、實證分析、研究表達與健康科技應用能 力，期望學生能以音樂與科技為媒介，提出具創新性與實務價值的健 康促進方案。 成績評量 評分項目：出席率 20%、提問 10%、期末個人延伸報告 20% 創意構想生醫專題海報競賽 50%，評分項目：創造力、跨域力、學理 性、Slogan 學生使用 AI 的規則：有條件開放 本課程鼓勵學生在透明與負責的原則下，適度使用 AI 工具進行課業協作。學生應在作 業或報告的標題頁註腳或引用文獻部分簡要說明 AI 工具的使用情況，並遵循學校的相 關指引。如未明確標註，教師有權重新評分或不予計分。 周次/日期 講題 授課老師 (1)09/10 課程介紹 清大音樂科技與健康研究中心蘇郁惠 主任；清大醫科系戚居暘助理教授 (2)09/17 實證醫學基礎 清大醫科系戚居暘助理教授 (3)09/24 學術海報製作與實證醫學應用 清大醫科系戚居暘助理教授 (4)10/1 高齡者音樂健康照護 清大醫科系戚居暘助理教授、清大音 樂科技與健康研究中心蘇郁惠主任 (6) 10/8 音樂與健康科技整合概論 清大音樂科技與健康研究中心蘇郁惠 主任 (5)10/15 音樂介入成效評估之生理量測 清大醫科系戚居暘助理教授、 中原大學醫工系蘇美如主任 (7)10/22 表演藝術醫學概論 清大音樂科技與健康研究中心蘇郁惠 主任、清大醫科系戚居暘助理教授 (8)10/29 表演藝術醫學研究暨典範機構 清大醫科系戚居暘助理教授、清大音 樂科技與健康研究中心蘇郁惠主任 (9)11/5 表演藝術醫學常採之生理量測 清大醫科系戚居暘助理教授、 中原大學醫工系蘇美如主任 (10) 11/12 期中分組主題分享 各組推派一位組員報告 (11)11/19 IMU、ROM 與姿勢動作分析 中原大學醫工系蘇美如主任 (12)11/26 sEMG 與肌肉負荷分析 中原大學醫工系蘇美如主任 (13)12/3 智慧健康照護系統與生理訊號資料應用 中原大學醫工系蘇美如主任 (14)12/10 多模態資料、AI 與智慧照護系統設計 中原大學醫工系蘇美如主任 (15)12/17 期末分組海報競賽（一） 蘇郁惠、蘇美如、戚居暘 (16)12/24 期末分組海報競賽（二） 蘇郁惠、蘇美如、戚居暘

docs.text: 工程導論課程大綱 一、本課程前兩週為工學院大一學生之共通課程，隨後進入四大主題課程（每主 題各為期三週），由不同學系教師分別講授。 二、工程導論課程之授課教師如下： ◼ 化學工程學系－楊東翰老師 ◼ 動力機械工程學系－李昇憲老師 ◼ 材料科學與工程學系－許瑋麟老師 ◼ 工業工程與工程管理學系－洪一峯老師 三、成績考核： ◼ 各主題課程各佔總成績之 25%，合計為 100%。 ◼ 各主題課程之成績評量方式略有不同，請參閱各授課教師之課程大綱以 了解詳細規定。 國立清華大學課程大綱－化工系 楊東翰教授 課程簡述 化學反應工程原理：解說莫耳均衡、轉化率與反應器大小的決定、速率定律與化學計量、恆溫反 應器的設計等。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」 莫耳均衡 Mole Balance, 轉化率 Conversion, 反應器設計 Reactor Design, 速率定律 Rate Law, 化學計量 Stoichiometry, 恆溫反應器 Isothermal Reactor. 課程大綱 ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程介紹化學反應工程之基本原理，內容涵蓋莫耳衡算、轉化率與反應器大小之決定、速率定 律、化學計量關係，以及恆溫反應器之設計。課程將說明如何依據反應動力學、進料組成與操作 條件，建立批次式反應器、連續攪拌槽反應器與管流式反應器之設計方程式，並進一步評估轉化 率、反應速率與反應器體積之間的關聯，使學生具備分析與設計基礎化學反應器之能力。 ● 指定用書(Text Books)：無。 ● 參考書籍(References)：無。 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method)：投影片說明 ● 教學進度(Syllabus)：上課說明 ● 成績考核(Evaluation)：課程最後一堂課安排考試（100%），佔總成績 25% ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) (1) 本課程無涉及 AI 使用 Not applicable 可參考下列網頁範例 See the following web page for examples. https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248357.php?Lang=zh-tw 國立清華大學課程大綱－動機系 李昇憲教授 課程簡述 動力機械工程涵蓋四個基礎專業領域：熱流與能源、機電控制、固力與微奈米，以及設計製造。 機械工程技術的應用範圍廣泛，包含光機電、生醫、動力、能源、微奈米科技等。本課程將介紹 機械工程的專業與應用，以及討論近年快速興起的微機電、半導體、機器人、以及人工智慧等主 題與機械工程的相關性。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」 機械工程(Mechanical Engineering)，光機電系統(Opto-mechatronic systems)，微機電 (Microelectromechanical Systems, MEMS)，半導體(Semiconductor)，機器人(Robotics)， 人工智慧(Artificial Intelligence) 課程大綱 ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程將介紹動力機械工程的專業與應用，以及討論近年快速興起的微機電、半導體、機器人、 以及人工智慧等主題與機械工程的相關性。 ● 指定用書(Text Books)：無 ● 參考書籍(References)：課程投影片 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method)：課堂講授 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 1. Power Mechanical Engineering: Fields, Scales and Applications 2. Introduction to MEMS and Sensors 3. Introduction to Robotics ● 成績考核(Evaluation)：課堂小考（100%），佔總成績 25% ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 本課程無涉及 AI 使用 Not applicable 可參考下列網頁範例 See the following web page for examples. https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248357.php?Lang=zh-tw 國立清華大學課程大綱－材料系 許瑋麟教授 課程簡述 本課程介紹材料科學與材料工程之基本概念與核心精神，說明材料結構、性質與製程三者間的 關聯性，並探討材料科技在能源、環境永續及高科技產業中的重要角色。課程內容涵蓋晶體結 構、微結構、機械與物理性質，以及熔煉、鍛造、軋延與熱處理等傳統材料製程。此外，也將 介紹現代先進材料技術，包括積層製造、熱噴塗與半導體乾蝕刻等製程，並說明其於航太、能 源、生醫植入物與半導體產業中的實際應用，使學生了解材料科學對現代科技發展與高階產業 的重要影響。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」 材料科學與工程、材料結構與性質、積層製造、熱噴塗技術、半導體乾蝕刻技術 Materials Science and Engineering、Material Structure and Properties、Additive Manufacturing 、Thermal Spray Technology、Semiconductor Dry Etching 課程大綱 ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程首先介紹材料科學與材料工程的關聯性、材料科學與工程與在科技與產業上的角色、能 源及環境永續發展的關係。接著介紹材料科學與材料工程的基礎：材料科學工程學習材料之結 構、性質與製程，並研究三者之間的關聯性。材料結構包括晶體結構與微結構，材料性質涵蓋 機械性質、物理性質與化學性質，材料製程則包括熔煉、鍛造、軋延、熱處理等傳統製程。第 三部分則進一步介紹數種現代工業中重要材料技術與實際應用情形: 如積層製造技術 (如選擇性 雷射熔融與電子束熔融等)、以及熱噴塗技術 (如電漿噴塗與高速氧燃燒噴塗) 等進階製程。這 些技術能應用於國防與航太元件、能源轉換裝置、生醫植入物與高溫防護塗層等領域，展示了 現代材料技術如何支援高階產業發展並因應極端環境需求。最後介紹半導體材料相關製程，以 晶圓代工產業之乾蝕刻製程為例，體現材料科學對現代科技發展的深遠影響。 ● 指定用書(Text Books) ● 參考書籍(References)： Materials, 3rd Edition, Engineering, Science, Processing and Design, eBook ISBN: 9780080982816 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method)：投影片上課 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 1. 材料的重要性 (Importance of Materials in human society) 2. 材料科學與工程基礎 (The basics of Materials Science & Engineering) 3. 進階材料技術應用 (Applications of Advanced Materials Technology) ● 成績考核(Evaluation)：每堂課後繳交課程筆記與心得學習單（100%），佔總成績 25% ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 本課程無涉及 AI 使用 Not applicable 可參考下列網頁範例 See the following web page for examples. https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248357.php?Lang=zh-tw 國立清華大學課程大綱－工工系 洪一峯教授 課程大綱 ● 課程說明(Course Description)： ※ 最佳化與工業工程 簡介介紹工業工程部分的技術，包含生產管理概念、作業研究、線性規劃及整規劃之建模技 術，並利用套裝軟體求解數學規劃模型。 ● 指定用書(Text Books) ： None ● 參考書籍(References) ： Frederick S. Hillier and Gerald J. Lieberman, Introduction to Operations Research, 11-th edition McGraw Hill, New York 2021. ● 教學方式(Teaching Method)： 課堂講授（class lectures） ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 1. 作業研究 2. 線性規劃 3. 整數規劃 4. 生產管理 ● 成績考核(Evaluation) 課堂學習心得（15%）、數學規劃軟體專案作業（50%）、最後一堂課結束前小考（35%）， 佔總成績 25%

Introduction to Robotics ● 成績考核(Evaluation)：課堂小考（100%），佔總成績 25% ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 本課程無涉及 AI 使用 Not applicable 可參考下列網頁範例 See the following web page for examples. https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248357.php?Lang=zh-tw 國立清華大學課程大綱－材料系 許瑋麟教授 課程簡述 本課程介紹材料科學與材料工程之基本概念與核心精神，說明材料結構、性質與製程三者間的 關聯性，並探討材料科技在能源、環境永續及高科技產業中的重要角色。課程內容涵蓋晶體結 構、微結構、機械與物理性質，以及熔煉、鍛造、軋延與熱處理等傳統材料製程。此外，也將 介紹現代先進材料技術，包括積層製造、熱噴塗與半導體乾蝕刻等製程，並說明其於航太、能 源、生醫植入物與半導體產業中的實際應用，使學生了解材料科學對現代科技發展與高階產業 的重要影響。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」 材料科學與工程、材料結構與性質、積層製造、熱噴塗技術、半導體乾蝕刻技術 Materials Science and Engineering、Material Structure and Properties、Additive Manufacturing 、Thermal Spray Technology、Semiconductor Dry Etching 課程大綱 ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程首先介紹材料科學與材料工程的關聯性、材料科學與工程與在科技與產業上的角色、能 源及環境永續發展的關係。接著介紹材料科學與材料工程的基礎：材料科學工程學習材料之結 構、性質與製程，並研究三者之間的關聯性。材料結構包括晶體結構與微結構，材料性質涵蓋 機械性質、物理性質與化學性質，材料製程則包括熔煉、鍛造、軋延、熱處理等傳統製程。第 三部分則進一步介紹數種現代工業中重要材料技術與實際應用情形: 如積層製造技術 (如選擇性 雷射熔融與電子束熔融等)、以及熱噴塗技術 (如電漿噴塗與高速氧燃燒噴塗) 等進階製程。這 些技術能應用於國防與航太元件、能源轉換裝置、生醫植入物與高溫防護塗層等領域，展示了 現代材料技術如何支援高階產業發展並因應極端環境需求。最後介紹半導體材料相關製程，以 晶圓代工產業之乾蝕刻製程為例，體現材料科學對現代科技發展的深遠影響。 ● 指定用書(Text Books) ● 參考書籍(References)： Materials, 3rd Edition, Engineering, Science, Processing and Design, eBook ISBN: 9780080982816 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method)：投影片上課 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 1. 材料的重要性 (Importance of Materials in human society) 2. 材料科學與工程基礎 (The basics of Materials Science & Engineering) 3. 進階材料技術應用 (Applications of Advanced Materials Technology) ● 成績考核(Evaluation)：每堂課後繳交課程筆記與心得學習單（100%），佔總成績 25% ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 本課程無涉及 AI 使用 Not applicable 可參考下列網頁範例 See the following web page for examples. https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248357.php?Lang=zh-tw 國立清華大學課程大綱－工工系 洪一峯教授 課程大綱 ● 課程說明(Course Description)： ※ 最佳化與工業工程 簡介介紹工業工程部分的技術，包含生產管理概念、作業研究、線性規劃及整規劃之建模技 術，並利用套裝軟體求解數學規劃模型。 ● 指定用書(Text Books) ： None ● 參考書籍(References) ： Frederick S. docs.name: 書報討論
docs.text: E500100 Seminar Course No.: E500100 Course Title: 書報討論 Seminar Credit: 1 Time: T5T6 (Tuesdays, 13:20~15:10) Classroom: R215, Engineering Building 1 Instructor: 黃智永教授 Chih-Yung Huang <cyhuang@pme.nthu.edu.tw> Office: R619, Engineering Building 1 TA: TBA Course Description: This is an interdisciplinary course with a series of lectures by guest speakers (professors, scholars, and experts) from research fields related to engineering. This course is designed to provide students with ideas and thoughts on diverse cutting edge research. This course aims to help students develop their own strategic thinking, explore and expand their research interests. Grading Policy: Students should attend the class on time, listen to the lectures attentively, and participate in in- class discussions. Students are required to submit thoughts/weekly feedbacks after the class and also give one oral presentation on the scheduled time-slot about subjects of their own choice or related to their majors/research/studies. Extra points could be earned during the Q & A session, especially when actively joining in discussions or asking questions after the lectures.  Attendance 30% (twice, one before the class begins, the other after the class ends)  Thoughts/Weekly Feedbacks 30%  Oral Presentation 40%  Extra Points: QA and discussions in class Syllabus: Schedule of lectures will be provided in the first class.

docs.text: 「東亞與現代世界的形成」研究生國際博士班學程 (TIGP) International Ph.D. Program in East Asia in the Making of Modern World 上課時間：2026 年 9 月 週三 14:00-17:00 上課地點：臺灣史研究所 817 室（待確認） 一、課程基本資料 (Course Information) 課程代碼 11510EAMW 600100 授課老師 Instructor(s) 曾品滄、林玉茹、林文凱 課程名稱 Course Title 臺灣海洋史專題 Seminar on Taiwan Maritime History 必/ 選修 選修 總學分數 3 每週授課時數 3 授課語言 Language of Instruction (Chinese and/or English) 中文 先修課程 無 課程簡介 Course Description 中文： 臺灣是一個海島，由海洋展開的內外連結應是社會經濟發展根基。本課程的 安排是按照主題區分，從臺灣的海洋環境結構、國家與海岸治理、漁業發展、漁 村共同體、商業網絡、宗教信仰、飲食文化、洋行、商人、米糖經濟、帝國學知、 對外貿易、冷戰與工業發展等十五個課題，進行緣起或貫時性討論。本課程的主 要教學目標是透過臺灣海洋史相關研究和史料的閱讀和分析，引起同學對海洋史 保持關懷與興趣，並能理解臺灣以海洋為中心之發展歷程，而能進一步作過去與 現在的對話。其次，透過對於過去歷史現象的理解，培養分析、判斷能力，啟迪 智慧。第三，透過專題論文的閱讀和相關史料的解析，以及共同討論，培養獨立 研究的能力。 English： Taiwan is an island, and the internal and external connections unfolded through the ocean constitute the foundation of its socioeconomic development. This course is organized thematically and comprises fifteen topics, including Taiwan’s marine environmental structure, state and coastal governance, the development of fisheries, fishing village communities, commercial networks, religious beliefs, food culture, foreign trading firms, merchants, the rice and sugar economy, imperial knowledge, trade, the Cold War and industrial development. Each topic is examined through discussions of its origins and diachronic development. The primary objective of this course is to engage students with Taiwan’s maritime history by reading and analyzing relevant scholarly research and historical sources, thereby fostering sustained interest in and critical concern for maritime history. Through this process, students will gain an understanding of Taiwan’s development as a society centered on the sea and will be encouraged to engage in a dialogue between the past and the present. A secondary objective is to cultivate students’ analytical and evaluative abilities through an informed understanding of historical phenomena, thereby sharpening critical judgment and intellectual insight. Finally, through the reading of specialized research articles, the analysis of related historical materials, and collective discussion, the course aims to develop students’ capacity for independent research. 課程要求與評分標準 Course Requirements and Grading Policy 本課程的教學評量以學生每次上課報告、書面文 獻解讀以及參與討論情況，作為依據。評比分配 如下：報告占 40%，文獻解讀 30%，參與討論 30 ％。由三位老師分別打分數再平均得出。 AI 使用規則 本課程鼓勵學生在透明與負責任的原則下，適度 使用 AI 工具進行課業協作。學生可使用 AI 蒐集 資料及構思問題，但應遵守學術倫理規範。AI 可 能引用他人的作品，直接使用若無適當引註，可 能有侵權疑慮。將 AI 生成的內容假裝是自己撰寫 的，是學術造假行為。另外，在課程討論時，不 可使用 AI 工具。如經查核未標註 AI 工具的使用 情況，教師或學校有權重新評分或不予計分。 二、教學大綱 教學進度與主題（說明每週進度） 【授課方式：16 週】 Weekly Schedule (16 weeks) week1 導論介紹 林玉茹 week2 臺灣的海洋：從南方到北方 曾品滄 week3 國家與海岸治理 曾品滄 week4 捕撈漁業的擴展：從沿岸到遠洋 曾品滄 week5 養殖漁業的發展：塭與塘 曾品滄 week6 海岸的村落共同體 曾品滄 week7 由福建到全球：商業網絡的擴張 林玉茹 week8 海洋與宗教信仰的普及 林玉茹 week9 海產與飲食文化 林玉茹 week10 開港的衝擊：洋行來襲 林玉茹 week11 跨政權下國際商人的出現 林玉茹 week12 晚清開港前後米穀出口的演變 林文凱 week13 日治時期米糖經濟與對外貿易 林文凱 week14 日本帝國學知的擴展：臺灣、福建、滿洲 林文凱 week15 二戰前後對外經貿結構的嬗變 林文凱 week16 國際冷戰體系與戰後工業發展 林文凱 參考書目 Textbooks/ Readings Diamond, Norma. docs.text: 經濟學原理一 課程大綱 Instructor: 余朝恩 Email: chaoenyu@mx.nthu.edu.tw 本門課程簡介經濟學的基本原理。經濟學不是一門教人自私的社會科學，而 是研究個人、廠商和組織如何做選擇的社會科學。 本課程主要介紹理性消費者和廠商決策的最適化，以及市場如何運作和達成 均衡的原理。本課程也將介紹在不同市場結構下，廠商的訂價和合作競爭等 決策行為。最後，本課程將分析政府在經濟社會運作中可以和應該扮演的角 色（或者不扮演）。鑑於近年來各國對公平、正義的呼聲日益高漲，本課程 也將針對部分大眾對於經濟學的迷思進行答辯和剖析。本門課程也將以數理 套裝軟體和 Python 程式設計展示經濟分析常用的繪圖和運算。 評分方式： 兩次期中考(各佔總成績 26%)，一次期末考(佔總成績 28%); 課堂 小考佔 10%，作業佔 10%，缺交缺考扣分。 教科書： Hubbard and O'Brien (2022), Economics, Pearson Education Limited, 8th edition (滄海圖書) 考試規則： (1) 考試時禁止使用手機。 (2) 請同學務必參加考試。考試時應按時進入試場，遲到逾 20 分 鐘者不得入場，遲到或缺席者以「缺考」處理。 (3) 遇國定假日放假於期中考日(10 月 12 日和 11 月 23 日)補課。 生成式 AI 倫理聲明 基於透明與負責任原則，本課程鼓勵學生利用 AI 進行協作或互學，以提升課程產出品質。 本課程採取「有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出」。學生須於課堂作業 或報告中的「標題頁註腳」或「引用文獻後」，簡要說明 AI 用於議題發想、文句潤飾、結 構參考等方式。若經查核使用卻未依規定標明，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新評分或不 予計分。教師若於教材或學習資料使用 AI，也應於投影片或口頭適當標注。修讀本課程之 學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。

docs.text: 1 11510ECON100102 Principles of Economics I Instructor: Prof. Hui-chen Wang (王惠貞) Fall 2026 (115上) Office: 台積館 810 Classroom: TSMC (台積館) 224 Office Hours: TBA Lecture Time: R5R6R7 (150 minutes on Thu 13:20-16:20) Email: huichenwang@mx.nthu.edu.tw Principles of Economics (I) Syllabus (Preliminary) Course Description This course offers an introduction to microeconomic theories and applications. We will discuss the basic economic concepts and theories concerning market functions and the choices of individual decision makers, including people and firms. This course is offered in English. Learning Objectives After successful completion of this course, students will be able to (1) define and discuss the key economic concepts including the basic principles of rational choices, (2) identify and analyze the fundamental microeconomic issues using verbal, graphical and simple mathematical techniques, and (3) apply economic thinking to daily decisions and events. Course Requirements and Policies Examinations There will be an in-class midterm exam and a final exam. The exams are not strictly cumulative; however, previously tested concepts may be covered in the final exam to the extent that they are the bases of a current topic. The format of the examinations will be a combination of multiple-choice questions and short written problems. The midterm and final exam dates will be announced in the first class meeting. All students must take the exams at their scheduled times. Make-up exam policy: No make-up exam will be given for the midterm exam. The weight for a missed midterm exam, if excused, will be reallocated to the final exam. Make- up exam for the final exam will only be given under unexpected, extremely unusual and justifiable circumstances. Students who miss an exam due to an unexpected emergency should inform professor Wang within 24 hours from the missed exam and provide official documentation for the absence within one week. Pop quizzes: Short, unannounced quizzes will be given throughout the semester. For each student, the lowest score of all quizzes given in the semester will be excluded from the calculation of quiz average. It is important to note that NO makeup quiz may be given for any reason since the one quiz waiver (indicated above) already takes into account the occasional illness or unexpected personal situations that may prevent you from taking a quiz. However, under extremely unusual and justifiable circumstances 2 (official documentation required), extra quiz waivers may be granted on a case- by-case basis, at professor Wang’s discretion. Homework assignments: Problem sets will be assigned throughout the course. Your homework will not be graded; however, all students are expected to complete all assignments in a timely manner for effective learning and preparation of the tests. Attendance and Participation: Students are required to attend the lectures regularly. Participation in class discussion is expected and appreciated. You will be held responsible for all assignments, tests, and any announcement made in class, even in your absence. Your attendance and participation may affect your overall course grades on the margin. Grading Course letter grades will be assigned based on the weighted sums of the graded components of your performance: Midterm exam: 40 % Final exam: 45 % Quizzes: 15% The grades are not negotiable. No individual request for extra credit work will be taken. Textbook (tentative) Glenn P. Hubbard and Anthony P. O'Brien (2022), Economics: Global Edition 8/e. Pearson. (ISBN-13: 978-1292430645) Our class discussion and test coverage may include some material not from this textbook. Class Communication and Resources TA Office hours: In addition to Professor Wang’s office hours (see header), there will be weekly office hours held by one of our teaching assistants. The time and location of the TA office hours will be announced separately on eeclass (see next). eeclass: In addition to in-class communication, email and office hours, we will utilize the eeclass digital course tool maintained by the university. Class announcements, lecture slides (student version), homework assignments, answer keys, grades and other course-related material will be posted. You are expected to check your email as well as your eeclass account regularly to remain up to date. Note: The posted version of the lecture slides will be incomplete by design with spaces to be filled out in class. You are expected to download or print out the slides in advance and bring them to the class. Keep in mind that the lecture slides will not remove the need for your class attendance and note taking efforts Regulation on AI Usage The usage of AI is irrelevant in this course since student learning will be assessed in class by closed-book tests. 3 Tentative Course Outline Topics Textbook Chapters 1. Introduction 2. How Market Works: Demand and Supply; Market Equilibrium; Economic Efficiency and Government Intervention 3. Consumer Choices: Budget, utility, and consumer’s demand 4. Production Theory: Output and cost 5. Market Structure and Profit Maximization: Perfect Competition; Monopoly and Price discrimination; Monopolistic Competition and Oligopoly (if time permits) 1-2 3, 4 10 11 12 15 13-14

docs.text: ECON100103 經濟學原理一 課程大綱 Instructor: 李翎帆 Office: 台積館 703 Email: lilf@mx.nthu.edu.tw Office Hours: 週二 12:00-13:30 經濟學是研究理性個人如何做選擇的社會科學。本課程主要介紹消費者與廠商如何做決策。在消 費者理論方面，本課程將探討影響消費者購買行為之因素與其決策準則。在生產者理論方面，將 介紹在不同市場結構下，廠商的生產與定價決策行為。此外，也將分析政府在經濟社會裡所扮演 之角色。 主要用書: M. Parkin, Economics, 14th edition (雙葉書廊) 評分方式 : 本學期總成績由一次期中考試(50%)和一次期末考試(50%)評定，時間如下： 期中考: 2026/11/09。 期末考: 2026/12/21。 請同學們特別注意期末總成績不會進行調分。 考試規則 : (1) 考試時禁止使用手機。 (2) 請同學務必參加考試 ，考試當天缺席者以 〝缺考 〞處理。 若遇不可抗拒之因素需 請事假 ，於考試前向授課教師申請補考，無法事後申請補考。 課程相關連結 : 清華大學 https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw/ 授課內容 : 1. 經濟學基本概念 (Ch.1, ch.2) 2. 供需均衡與彈性 (Ch.3) ➢ 分析在完全競爭市場下，商品 (或服務) 的價格如何決定 3. 價格彈性(ch.4) ➢ 價格變動與消費數量之間的關係 4. 效率與平等(ch.5) ➢如何分配資源 5. 市場機能與政府干預 (Ch.6) ➢市場管制 ➢最低工資 6. 消費者決策 (ch.8, ch.9) ➢效用和需求 ➢消費者在既有的資源(財富)下，如何選擇市場上個別商品的消費量 7. 生產者決策 (ch.10, ch.11) ➢ 介紹廠商生產理論與成本分析 8. 競爭與獨佔 (ch.12, ch.13) ➢ 介紹在不同市場結構下廠商的訂價決策行為 9. 外部性與公共財 (ch.16, ch.17) ➢ 分析在市場經濟發生缺陷時(市場失靈)，政府可以介入市場提升社會福利 ➢ 分析政府設立關稅對一國福利之影響

docs.text: 經濟學原理一 Fall 2026 教師: 唐震宏 E-mail: jhtang@mx.nthu.edu.tw Office: TSMC727 有關加簽的常見問題 1. 如果有加簽需求的同學，請在加簽期間登入學校系統提出要求。 2. 教室有容量限制，我能加簽的名額等於教室容量減去已選課人數。如果有加簽需求的 人數超過可加簽人數，原則上以大四同學優先，再來依序是大三、大二、大一。若同 一順位要求加簽人數超過空位 (例如有 N 個空位，但有 N+1 位大四同學要加簽)，則 以亂數抽籤決定。 課程概述 本課程目的在介紹經濟學的基本分析工具與核心議題。內容以市場機制之運作為主軸， 包括經濟學的基本概念，如機會成本、比較利益、專業分工，以及個體經濟學的議題，如 供給與需求、市場均衡、消費者行為、生產者行為、和產業組織等。 課程目標 本課預期能協助同學 (1) 瞭解經濟學基本原理；(2) 應用經濟理論分析經濟問題。 參考用書 1. Mankiw, N.G. (2024), Principles of Economics, 10th Edition, Cengage Asian Edition. 授課方式 1. 授課以教師講解為主，歡迎同學隨時發問並提出意見。 2. The lectures are taught in Chinese (Mandarin). Students who have diffi- culties in understanding Chinese are advised not to take this course. 1 3. 上課投影片會在上課前公布在 eeclass: http://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw。投影片的內 容是演講的重點與綱要，但不可能是文理清晰邏輯通順的文章。建議同學上課時記下 重要的邏輯推論及實例，或是準備一本課本，方便日後複習。 4. 如果你常來聽課，遇到聽不懂的地方，或是不會答的題，我有責任，也很樂意回答你 的問題，讓你明白。但有些同學平常不來上課，自己看課本講義又看不懂 (或是不想 費神)，然後考前發 email 給我問問題，或是考前才來課堂上，利用下課來問一大堆我 早已反覆講過多次的內容，把我當成函授學校或是私人家教。占用我的時間，也排擠 掉其他同學發問的時間，甚至影響到正常上課。這對我或是對其他同學，應該都是不 公平吧？所以如果你有缺課，又想補上進度，請你自己想辦法。 5. 考試命題範圍以上課投影片為準，所有在課堂上講解過的內容都包含在內。大致上與 課本一致，但會有所增減。 放假與上課時間 • 放假：9/25 (中秋）、10/9 (雙十)、12/25（行憲）。 • 上課：九月 (11、18)、十月 (2、16、23、30)、十一月 (6、13、20、27)、十二月 (4、 11、18)。 成績計算、考試時間、及相關規定 1. 期中考 50%，期末考 50%。 2. 期中及期末考時間：10/30、12/18，3:30–5:20pm。 3. 上述考試時間若無法出席參加考試，請依本校請假辦法辦理。任何事假歉難同意，且 無法給予補考。公假需出示本校派遣單位核發之公假單，喪假需請家長、監護人、或 直系尊親屬來信 (電郵) 代為請假，病假需請校醫或醫院開立證明，否則視同無假缺 考。因懷孕、分娩或為撫育三歲以下幼兒而核准之事病假及產假視同病假。 4. 考試以中文或英文出題，可以中文或英文回答。如果你自認中/英文不好，請自己加 強中/英文閱讀能力。 2 課程進度 • 經濟學簡介 • 供給與需求 • 市場均衡 • 價格彈性 • 效用與消費者的選擇 • 期中考 • 生產者決策的基礎 • 競爭市場的供給線 • 市場機能與經濟效率 • 獨占 • 不完全競爭市場 • 要素市場 • 期末考 3

Chou swchou@mx.nthu.edu.tw. edu Tel: 03-5162032 Textbook Title: Principles of Economics (Free Textbook) Copyright year: 2016 ISBN-13: 9781946135162 Publisher: University of Minnesota Libraries Publishing Link: https://open.umn.edu/opentextbooks/textbooks/ principles-of-economics?utm_source=chatgpt.com Grading (NEW!): • Three Assignments, totally 15% of final grade • Three Quizs, tallly 45% of final grade • Final exam 40% of final grades Communication: We will only use the eLearn system. Please do not use other system to contact the instructor. Page 1 of 5 Appendix: Explanation for the Three Assignments 15% of Final Grade Over the course of the semester, you will complete three assignments, each tied to an assigned textbook chapter. These assignments are designed to develop your ability to read carefully, think independently, and engage critically with both economic concepts and AI- generated responses. What You Will Do For each assignment, you will submit two questions that emerged from your serious engage- ment with the assigned chapter. These are not questions you look up — they are questions you arrive at after reading, thinking, and getting genuinely stuck. Each question must be written in English and structured around the following six elements: 0. Textbook Anchor Identify the specific concept, argument, or passage in the assigned chapter that your question grows out of. Be precise — name the concept and where it appears. 1. Foundation Explain what you understood before you got stuck. A good question shows what you do know, not just what you don’t. 2. Stuck Point Describe exactly where your understanding broke down. The more specific, the better. 3. Argued Uncertainty Explain why this particular thing is hard to understand. What did you try? Why didn’t it resolve? This is not the same as saying “I don’t get it” — you need to make a case for your confusion. 4. Curiosity Source Tell me why you actually want to know the answer to this question. Where does the curiosity come from — a real-world observation, a personal experience, a logical tension you noticed, something you couldn’t explain to someone else? 5. AI Response and Your Evaluation Pose your question to any AI model of your choice and include its response. Then evaluate: were you satisfied with the answer? If yes, explain what made it adequate. If no, explain specifically what it missed, where it fell short, or what it left unresolved. What Makes a Good Question — and What Doesn’t Your questions should be about ideas, logic, and reasoning — not technical procedures or mathematical derivations. Economics at this level is fundamentally about building models to understand how people, firms, and societies make decisions under constraints. A model is a deliberate simplification of reality — that is not a flaw, it is the point. Pointing out that a model is unrealistic Page 2 of 5 is therefore not a good question. Every model is unrealistic by design. The most interesting questions are about the model’s internal logic — whether it is consis- tent, where its reasoning leads, what it can and cannot explain on its own terms, and under what conditions its conclusions hold or break down. You are NOT looking for: • “How do I calculate price elasticity?” — this is a procedure question • “I don’t understand the algebra in Figure 3.2” — this is a technical stumbling block • “The model assumes people are rational but real people aren’t — so is the model wrong?” — this misunderstands what a model is for. Of course it simplifies reality. That is not a puzzle worth asking about. You ARE looking for: • “The model says a price ceiling below equilibrium creates a shortage — but it also assumes supply and demand curves stay fixed. If sellers respond to a persistent shortage by exiting the market, wouldn’t the supply curve shift and change the pre- diction? Does the model account for that, or is it only meant to describe the short run?” • “Consumer surplus is measured as the area above the price line and below the demand curve — but that assumes every consumer actually buys at the market price. If some consumers would have paid more and didn’t have to, why does the model treat that as a social gain rather than just a transfer they didn’t receive?” The test is simple: if your question could be resolved by re-reading the chapter, redoing the math, or simply observing that the real world is more complicated than the model — it is not a good question. On Word Limit There is none. You are expected to figure out the appropriate length yourself. A question that is too short probably lacks depth. A question that is too long probably lacks focus. Finding the right length is part of the assignment. Grading Submitted Assignment Each of the three assignments is worth up to 3% of your final grade, for a combined maximum of 9%. Your two questions are graded as a pair. A strong submission can earn full marks. A weak or inadequate submission can earn zero. The quality of both questions matters — a strong first question does not compensate for a weak second one. Page 3 of 5 Debrief Bonus After each submission deadline, approximately 12 questions will be selected for in-class discussion, and students will be randomly called upon to discuss their questions live. If your submission is selected, you have the opportunity to earn bonus points based on your oral performance: Oral Performance Bonus Points High pass +2% Pass +1% No pass +0% The debrief is bonus only — it cannot reduce your grade. The same student may be selected across multiple rounds, and each selection is an independent opportunity to earn bonus points. Total Possible Grade Source Maximum 3 submitted assignments × 3% 9% 3 debrief bonuses × 2% 6% Grand Total 15% In-Class Debrief You do not know in advance whether your submission will be selected or whether you will be called upon. Therefore, every submission must be one you can genuinely defend and discuss. When called upon, you will be asked to walk the class through how you arrived at your question, what you made of the AI’s answer, and how you thought about it. The in-class debrief must be conducted in English. Schedule Assignment Chapter Submission Deadline Assignment 1 TBA TBA Assignment 2 TBA TBA Assignment 3 TBA TBA A Note on Academic Integrity You are encouraged to use AI as a thinking partner and as a source of answers — that is part of the assignment. However, using AI to generate your questions defeats the entire purpose. Page 4 of 5 The questions must come from your own reading and your own thinking. The in-class debrief exists partly to verify this. Submit only questions that are genuinely yours. Additionally, your questions must go beyond what has already been covered in lectures. Questions that simply revisit or repackage concepts already explained in class are not acceptable. The assignment is designed to push you into territory the lectures have not yet mapped — into the gaps, tensions, and implications that your own reading opens up. If your question could be answered by recalling something already said in class, it is not the right kind of question. In short, your questions must come from your own reading, your own thinking, and your own curiosity — not from lectures, not from AI, and not from simply repeating what you already heard.
