docs.text: Microeconomics (I) ECON 206102 Syllabus Fall 2026 Instructor: Stephen Jui-Hsien Chou Email: jhchou@mx.nthu.edu.tw Time: W3W4F3F4 Location: TSMC 104 Textbook: Microeconomics: Theory and Applications with Calculus (5th Edition), Jeffrey M. Perloff (2020). Course Description: This course is offered in English and is the first part of a one-year course in Microeconomics required for students in the Economics program. Knowledge of calculus is expected, as it will be used frequently to solve economic problems. The course begins with an introduction to supply and demand, followed by an analysis of how consumers make choices among different goods. After developing the basic framework of consumer theory, we examine the demand curve and its properties in a more rigorous manner. We also discuss how consumer welfare can be measured and explore the implications for public policy. In the second half of the course, we turn to the behavior of firms and study how firms make production decisions in both the short run and the long run. Similar to the consumer’s problem of maximizing utility, firms seek to minimize their costs, and we examine the properties of cost functions in detail. We then introduce one of the most important models of market structure, perfect competition, and analyze how firms and consumers interact in a competitive market. Finally, we extend our analysis from individual markets to a general equilibrium framework and discuss the welfare properties of a competitive economy. Grading Policy: There will be one midterm exam and one final exam for this course. Together, the two exams will account for 100% of the course grade. The exam with the higher score will account for 55%, while the exam with the lower score will account for 45%. The final exam will cover only the material from the chapters taught after the midterm exam. The two exams are scheduled as follows: Midterm Exam: Nov. 6 Week 9 Final Exam: Dec. 18 Week 15 T.A. Office Hours: Additional office hours will be held by the T.A.(s) for this course. The times and locations will be announced on eeClass. Class Communication: Important class announcements, lecture slides, and other course-related materials will be posted on eeClass. If you wish to contact me and expect a reply, please email me directly.

docs.text: 1 Microeconomics I Course Syllabus Fall 2023 W7W8W9 Classroom: TSMC (台積館) Room 224 Prerequisite: Principles of Economics(I) 經濟學原理一 Knowledge of calculus is required Method of Instruction: Lecture/Discussion Learning Objective: Our graduates will understand basic economic theories. Learning Goal: Our students will understand the basic knowledge of behaviors of individual economic agents, such as consumers and firms. Course Description: This is a two-semester course. Economics is the study of human behavior. To understand how people can cooperate in social orders, and why they often cannot, we need to have a framework for understanding human action and its consequences. Economics provides one such framework. Microeconomics has been applied to issues ranging from those expected in economics, such as what determines the price of consumer Instructor: Crystal Wong (黃賀寶) Office: TSMC (台積館) Room 704 Email: wonghopo817@gmail.com by appointment Teaching Assistants: TBA 2 goods, to such things as how people vote, how much education they acquire, and how many children they have. This course offers an introduction to the theory and methods of microeconomics. In the first semester, we will cover topics include the simple demand and supply framework, consumer choice and demand under constrained maximization; price and output determination of the firm, and the perfect competition model. Course Website: courses materials are available on our course website in the eeclass system (eeclass 數位學習平台). Required Text: Microeconomics with Calculus, Jeffrey M. docs.text: 1 Cost and Managerial Accounting(I) 成本與管理會計(I) College of Technology Management, National Tsing Hua University (FALL 2026) Instructor: 沈瑜峰 Shen Yu-Feng Office Hour: By appointment E-mail: shenyf@mx.nthu.edu.tw Class time: 12:10-15:00, Wednesdays, WnW5W6 Classroom: TSMC 台積 Course Objective: The goal of cost and managerial accounting is to acquaint students of management with the fundamental tools of management accounting, but also to promote their understanding of the dramatic ways in which the field is changing. The emphasis throughout the course is on using accounting information in managing an organization. In this course, the traditional tools of managerial accounting, like product costing, budgeting, and performance evaluation, will be augmented and updated with contemporary approaches such as activity- based costing, customer profitability analysis, value-chain analysis, target costing, balanced scorecard, and strategic cost management. Prerequisite: Accounting(I)、(II)。 Topics Cost Concepts for Decision-Makers 1 Managerial Accounting 2 Job Order Costing 3 Process Costing 4 Activity-Based Costing Decision-Making Concepts 5 Cost-Volume-Profit 6 Cost-Volume-Profit Analysis: Additional Issues 2 7 Incremental Analysis 8 Pricing Planning and Control Concepts 9 Budgetary Planning 10 Budgetary Control and Responsibility Accounting 11 Standard Costs and Balanced Scorecard 12 Planning for Capital Investments Performance Evaluation Concepts 13 Statement of Cash Flows 14 Financial Analysis: The Big Picture Required Materials: Weygandt, J. J., Kimmel, P. D., Kieso, D. E., & Aly, I. M. (2024). Managerial accounting: Tools for business decision-making 9/e IA . John Wiley & Sons.

docs.text: 1 Financial Reporting： Theory and Practices College of Technology Management, National Tsing Hua University (Fall 2026) Instructor: 沈瑜峰 Shen Yu-Feng Office Hour: By appointment E-mail: shenyf@mx.nthu.edu.tw Class time: 15:30-18:20, Wednesdays, W7W8W9 Classroom: TSMC 台積 Course Objective: This course is designed to provide a strong conceptual, analytical and procedural foundation for the study of financial reporting and practice. The historical development of accounting thought and the role of financial accounting in today’s economy are investigated. Socioeconomic, political, legal, and ethical influences on financial reporting are considered. Discussions include procedures to record, summarize, and report results of business events; content and presentation of financial statements and specific reporting issues related to cash and receivable. An overview of financial statement analysis is also presented. International issues are addressed as appropriate. The aims and objectives of the course are to: • stimulate theoretical enquiry into financial accounting issues • develop the student’s knowledge and understanding of financial accounting • prepare students for further academic study in accounting and related areas • enable students in the pursuit of a professional accountancy qualification • equip students for employment in areas where an understanding of accounting issues and tools is helpful. Prerequisite: Accounting(I)、(II)。 Topics Module 1 Theory and Conceptual Framework Module 2 Depreciation Policy and Analysis and Interpretation of Statements of Changes in Financial Position Module 3 Accounting Information And Disclosure 2 Module 4 Financial Accounting and Reporting Standards Module 5 Corporate Reporting and Accounting for Multinational Corporations Module 6 Contemporary Issues in Accounting Required Materials: Higson, A. W. (2002). Corporate financial reporting: Theory & practice. Supplementary Reading: Lee, T. A. (2007). Financial reporting and corporate governance. John Wiley & Sons. Ding, Y., Lebas, M. docs.text: 11510ECON316100 Public Finance (I) Instructor: Prof. Hui-chen Wang (王惠貞) Fall 2026 (115上) Office: 台積館810 Classroom: TSMC (台積館) 103 Email: huichenwang@mx.nthu.edu.tw Lecture Time: W7W8W9 (150 minutes on Wed 15:30-18:20) Office Hours: TBA Public Finance (I) 財政學一 Syllabus (Preliminary) Course Description This is the first course in the two-semester undergraduate sequence of Public Finance. Public Finance is the branch of economics that studies the role of the public sector in the economy, and the approach is primarily based on microeconomics. In this semester, we will have a focus on the expenditure side of public finance. The course will begin with an introduction to the public sector and basic economic tools, followed by the economic reasons and outcomes of government interventions. We will then look at what the public sector actually does using examples from the expenditure policies in the United States and in Taiwan, and how it affects individual decision-making and welfare. This course is offered in English. Learning Objectives After successful completion of this course, students will be able to (1) define and discuss the key economic concepts pertinent to the public sector, (2) analyze the fundamental issues in public finance using microeconomic theories and tools, (3) have a basic understanding of the important public expenditure policies in the world, and (4) apply economic thinking to the issues in the public expenditure policies in Taiwan. Prerequisite Principles of Economics I and II. Reference Text Teaching material will be primarily drawn from the following textbooks: Hyman, David N. (2021), Public Finance: A Contemporary Application of Theory to Policy, 12th Edition. Cengage. (ISBN-13: 978-0357442159.) Rosen, Harvey S. and Ted Gayer. (2014). Public Finance. 10th global edition. McGraw-Hill/Irwin. ISBN-13: 978-0077154691 Some material that is not in the textbooks may be presented in the lectures. Course Requirements and Policies Examinations There will be two in-class examinations: one midterm exam and one final exam. The exams are not strictly cumulative; however, previously tested concepts may be covered in a later exam to the extent that they are the basis of a current topic. The midterm and final exam dates will be announced in the first class meeting. 2 All students must take the exams at their scheduled times. Make-up exam policy: No make-up exam will be given for the midterm exam. The weight for a missed midterm exam, if excused, will be reallocated to the final exam. Make-up exam for the final exam may be given under unexpected, extremely unusual and justifiable circumstances. Students who miss an exam due to an unexpected emergency should inform professor Wang within 24 hours from the missed exam and provide official documentation for the absence within a week. Pop Quizzes: Four short quizzes will be given in the semester. These quizzes will not be pre-announced. For each student, only the highest three quiz scores of the four will count towards the course grade calculation. NO makeup quiz may be given for any reason. However, under extremely unusual and justifiable circumstances (official documentation required), additional quiz waiver(s) may be granted on a case-by-case basis, at professor Wang’s discretion. Homework assignments: Problem sets will be assigned throughout the course. Your homework will not be collected nor graded; however, all students are expected to complete all assignments in a timely manner for effective learning and preparation of the tests. Attendance and Participation: Students are required to attend the lectures regularly. Participation in class discussion is expected and appreciated. You will be held responsible for all assignments, tests, and any announcement made in class, even in your absence. Your attendance and participation may affect your overall course grades on the margin. In addition, we reserve the right to impose penalty in terms of course grades if high frequency of unexcused absences is observed for a student. docs.name: 數理經濟學一
docs.text: 數理經濟學一 Fall 2026 Friday 12:30–15:20 @ TSMC 205 教師: 唐震宏 E-mail: jhtang@mx.nthu.edu.tw Office: TSMC727 課程介紹 數理經濟學是什麼？ 數理經濟學是一門經濟學的分支，其目的在為經濟分析提供嚴謹的架 構，尤其當經濟理論過於複雜而超過口語或圖形的表達範圍時，數理經濟學提供分析 的工具。除了在經濟理論的發展中發揮了關鍵的作用，數理經濟學也普遍應用於經濟 學的各個領域，提供數學工具對經濟現象進行建模及分析，進而發展出明確且可檢驗 的理論假說。 本門課的目標是什麼？用到那些數學工具？ 經濟系的同學在大二的個體經濟學都上過微 積分和個經，對微積分、靜態優化等應該都不陌生。本門課將建立在這個基礎上，介 紹經濟學常用的數學工具，如線性代數、多變數微積分、凸性規劃等，及其在個體經 濟學的應用。 數理經濟學有什麼用？ • 幫助學習及深入瞭解經濟理論：學習使用代數等數學工具的輔助，以及使用抽象 簡潔的數學表達，有助理解複雜的經濟理論，提高學習效率，並為未來學習更進 階的經濟理論奠定基礎。 • 提高分析和解決問題的能力：數理經濟學可以幫助學生將複雜多變的經濟問題 化繁為簡，並應用適當的模型進行分析，進而培養解決問題的能力。 • 培養跨領域的數學技能：數理經濟學需要使用微積分、線性代數、微分方程、最 優化理論等數學工具，而數學是科學之母，這些數學工具也都普遍應用在大數據 分析、機器學習、和人工智能等其他領域。尤其現在人工智能的時代已經來臨， 學習人工智能已不再是理工科系的專利。經濟主修的同學熟練應用數學工具可 以培養數學技能，除了提高經濟理論的學習效率，也有助於渉獵其他領域。 1 數理經濟學適合那些同學選修？ 選不選修數理經濟學要根據同學自身的興趣、職業規劃和 學術需求等因素來考慮。如果同學對數學和統計比較感興趣，且想將這些技能應用於 經濟學分析中，那麼選修數理經濟學會是一個不錯的選擇。這些技能可以幫助同學更 深入地理解經濟學理論和應用，並提高升學或就業競爭力。 但如果同學對數學和統計沒有太大的興趣，或者想在其他領域發展自己的職業生涯， 那麼選修數理經濟學可能不是必需的。同學可以根據自己的興趣和職業規劃選擇相應 的選修課程，以發揮自己的潛力。 課程目標 本課程預期能協助同學瞭解及學習 1. 如何應用數學工具有效學習經濟理論 2. 如何應用數學工具模型化並解決經濟問題 參考用書 • Chiang, A.C. and K. Wainwright (2004). Fundamental Methods of Mathematical Eco- nomics, 4th Ed. • Simon, C.P. and L. Blume (1994). Mathematics for Economists, Norton. 放假與上課時間 • 放假：9/25 (中秋）、10/9 (雙十)、12/25（行憲）。 • 上課：九月 (11、18)、十月 (2、16、23、30)、十一月 (6、13、20、27)、十二月 (4、 11、18)。 成績計算與考試時間 • 期中考 50 %、期末考 50%。 • 期中及期末考時間：10/30、12/18，12:30–15:20。 2 課程進度 1. Linear algebra (S & B, Chs.6–11) 2. Linear economic models (C & W, Chs.4, 5) 3. Calculus of several variables (S & B, Chs.12–14) 4. Implicit functions (S & B, Ch.15) 5. Comparative-static analysis (C & W, Chs.6, 7, 8) 6. Homogeneous and concave functions (S & B, Chs.20, 21) 7. Static optimization (C & W, Chs.9, 11, 12, 13; S & B, Chs.16–19, 22) 3

docs.text: 1 Applied Microeconometrics and Data Analysis 應用個體計量與資料分析 Syllabus Fall 2026 Lecture time: Thursdays 12:10 pm – 3:10 pm Classroom: TSMC 206 Instructor: Hsin-Yuan (Jeff) Hsieh Office hours: TBD Course description: This course introduces some of the most widely used econometric methods in the economics literature, including linear and nonlinear models, multinomial choice models, semiparametric methods, and simulation-based methods. You will learn to apply these techniques using R, a free and open-source statistical programming language, working with real-world economic data. As British mathematician Clive Humby famously remarked, “data is the new oil.” In an increasingly data-driven world, the ability to clean raw data, analyze it, extract meaningful insights, and communicate results effectively has become essential for economic analysis. In addition to core econometric tools, the course introduces fundamental R programming and data manipulation skills, along with general programming concepts that carry over to other languages such as Python or Julia. While we will review statistical and econometric ideas, the primary focus is on practical skills: data handling, estimation, and building reproducible workflows. Therefore, the emphasis is on applying econometric methods rather than their technical theoretical foundations. Language: This course is offered in English. Class discussions and oral presentations may be conducted in either English or Mandarin, though English is strongly encouraged. Your choice of language will not affect your final grade. Requirement: This course is intended for third-year undergraduate students and above who have a basic background in statistics and econometrics. Graduate students without prior experience in statistical programming are also welcome. While knowledge of linear algebra is not required, it can be helpful, as working in R often involves matrix operations. The necessary mathematical tools will be introduced in the first part of the semester. Students are expected to be comfortable using a computer and a standard operating system (such as Windows or macOS). If you are concerned about your level of computer proficiency, please contact the instructor as early as possible. It is recommended that you bring your laptop to class, as we will often work through coding exercises together. 2 Grading: Each week includes a short coding assignment for practice. You will also complete a final project on a topic of your choice, which will be presented in class and submitted electronically after the final exam period. There are no exams in this course. 20% weekly assignments 30% participation 50% final project (10% proposal, 20% oral presentation) AI policy: AI can be a powerful tool for writing and coding. You are encouraged to use it in your final project for brainstorming, coding support, and proofreading. However, its use in weekly assignments is strongly discouraged, as it limits hands-on learning. Because AI can make mistakes, it is important to get your hands dirty and develop the ability to evaluate whether its output is correct. Through regular practice, you will learn to read, understand, and assess AI-generated code. To ensure the reproducibility of your final project and to avoid potential issues with AI- generated results, you are required to submit a copy of your original data. Textbooks: Wickham, H., & Grolemund, G. (2017). R for data science (Vol. 2). Sebastopol: O'Reilly. Heiss, F. (2016). Using R for introductory econometrics. Düsseldorf, Germany: Florian Heiss. (Advanced) Cameron, A. C., & Trivedi, P. K. (2005). Microeconometrics: methods and applications. Cambridge university press. Topics: Part I (Weeks 1–3): Preparation In this part of the course, you will learn the mathematical tools and foundational R programming skills that are essential for the rest of the semester. Tentative topics: 1. Course introduction, math review 2. R and RStudio basics, data import, cleaning, wrangling, reshaping, and visualization 3. Conditional operators, for/while loops, creating functions 4. Microeconomic data structure 3 Part II (weeks 4-10): Econometric Modeling In this part of the course, we will introduce various econometric methods commonly used in empirical economic research. Your final project may build on one or more of these topics. Tentative topics: 1. Linear models, including OLS, WLS, quantile regression, and IV 2. Maximum likelihood, nonlinear least squares, and generalized method of moments 3. Systems of equations and seemingly unrelated regression 4. Multinomial logit/probit, nested logit 5. Semiparametric methods Week 11: In-class presentation of your final project proposal, including research question, methodology, and data description. Part III (weeks 12-14) Advanced Topics: By this point in the course, you should be comfortable with the core R programming workflow. We will introduce two advanced applications that require integrating and extending the skills learned in earlier weeks. Tentative topics: 1. Monte Carlo simulation, finite-sample and asymptotic properties of estimators 2. Numerical optimization 3. Bootstrap methods 4. Random parameter models Week 15-16: Final project oral presentations.

docs.text: 1 ECON412100 國際經濟學一(International Economics (I)) 課程大綱 (temporary) Instructor: 李 宜 助教: TBA Office: 台積館 812 Email: ylee@mx.nthu.edu.tw Office: Office Hours: 週一 12pm-1pm Office hour: 在全球化的潮流下，近 30 年來世界各國紛紛降低貿易障礙，加速商品貿易的流量。 此外，國際間生產分工的方式，已從過去產品之間的分工，逐漸轉為生產同一種商品 在不同製程上的分工。在貿易自由化與國際分工的趨勢下，加速商品、人才與資金的 跨國移動，提升國家與國家間生產活動的關聯性。透過國際貿易，各國可專注於本國 較具生產優勢的商品，在國際市場換取本國生產成本較高的商品，進而提升本國的生 產效率與福利。雖然自由貿易可提升一國福利，但同時也可能對一國所得分配造成不 均度惡化。因此，各國政府在制定貿易相關政策時多受到許多爭議。 本課程主要介紹當前國際貿易理論模型，分析國家間為何會進行貿易，以及自由貿易 與貿易政策(如:關稅)下對一國福利的影響，期望學生未來能對國貿相關議題有初步認 識及相關分析能力。 主要用書: International Economics Theory and Policy, by Paul Krugman, Maurice Obstfeld and Marc Melitz (KOM) [華泰書局代理] 評分方式: 本學期成績評定內容涵蓋： (1) 作業: 本課程將依照授課進度不定期發放作業，學生由 6 人組成小組， 每組繳交一份作業。作業需於指定日期(時段)繳交，逾期不收。 (2) 期中考: TBA (3) 期末考: TBA 學期總成績計算方式如下: A =﹝作業(30%)，期中考(35%)，期末考(35%)﹞ B =﹝作業(30%)，期中考(25%)，期末考(45%)﹞ 學期總成績將取 A 與 B 兩者中較高者(Max{A,B})。 考試規則: (1) 考試時禁止使用手機。 (2) 請同學務必參加考試，考試當天缺席者以〝缺考〞處理。若遇 不可抗拒之因素需請事假，需於考試前向授課教師請假申請補考。 2 授課大綱: 1. Introduction 2. 李嘉圖模型 (KOM: Ch.3) ➢ 以國家間生產技術的差異解釋國家間貿易形成的原因 3. 特定要素模型 (KOM: Ch.4) ➢ 分析自由貿易在短期間對一國不同生產要素擁有者所得之影響(如:雇 主 vs 勞工) ➢ 分析勞工的跨國移動(如:外國白領人才、藍領勞工、移民)在短期與長 期下對一國所得分配的影響 4. HO 模型 (KOM: Ch.5) ➢ 以國家間生產資源分佈差異解釋國家間貿易形成的原因 ➢ 分析自由貿易在長期下對一國不同生產要素擁有者所得之影響 ➢ 分析勞工的跨國移動(如:外國白領人才、藍領勞工、移民)在長期下對 一國所得分配的影響 5. 經濟成長與國際貿易 (KOM, Ch.6) ➢ 當國家生產技術進步或生產資源增加，對一國貿易條件與福利之影響 6. 外部規模經濟與國際貿易 (KOM: Ch.7) 7. 內部規模經濟、不完全競爭與貿易 (KOM: Ch.8) ➢ 解釋產業內貿易發生的原因 ➢ 解釋個別廠商出口決策與對外投資(國際分工)的行為 ➢ 分析廠商國際分工對勞動市場的影響(FT: Ch. 7) 8. 貿易政策 (KOM: Ch.9) ➢ 關稅的經濟效果-大國 v.s. 小國 ➢ 關稅與配額比較: 完全競爭市場 v.s. 不完全競爭市場 ➢ 出口補貼、傾銷與其他非關稅貿易政策工具 9. 貿易干預的理論基礎 (KOM: Ch.10,11,12) ➢ 介紹政府限制貿易的理由與工具

docs.text: ECON 504200 Machine learning and econometrics: concepts and procedures (機器學習與計量經濟: 概念與程序) National Tsing Hua University 1st semester, 2026-2027 Time: 3:30pm - 6:20pm, every Tuesday (T7T8T9) Venue: TSMC 832 Office hours: By appointment Instructor: CY (Chor-yiu) SIN (Office: CTM-804, Email: cysin@mx.nthu.edu.tw, Phone: 03-516-2134) Course description: Since the publication of Varian (2014), people have been believing that machine learning uses data to predict some variable as a function of other variables, while econometrics use statistical methods for prediction, inference, and causal modeling of economic relationships. However, nowadays some tend to believe that machine learning is the new generation nonparametric statistical and econometric methods, branded as machine learning (Chernozhukov et al. 2017). While academically rigorous theorems are much appreciated, they are not the focus of this course. Instead, this course starts with basic concepts of machine learning and econometrics; and ends with procedural computer codes. Students are required to be familiar with at least one software such as Python, R or C++. This course discusses the basic concepts with examples in economics and management. Hands-on exercises with the software “Python”. Course topics: Part~(1) Preliminaries which include (1a) Linear algebra (1b) Mathematical analysis (1c) Probability and statistics (1d) Machine learning introduction (1e) Linear regression (1f) Logistic regression (1g) Overfitting problem Part~(2) Basic machine learning (2a) Evaluating a learning algorithm (2b) Decision tree (2c) Clustering: K-means (2d) Recommender system (2e) Reinforcement learning: Q-learning Part~(3) Basic deep learning (3a) Neural networks and deep learning (3b) Hyperparameter tuning, regularization and optimization (3c) Structuring machine learning projects (3d) Convolutional neural networks (3e) Sequence models Textbooks and references: (1) Chernozhukov, V., Chetverikov, D., Demirer, M., Duflo, E., Hansen, C., Newey, W., 2017. Double/debiased/Neyman machine learning of treatment effects. American Economic Review: Papers and Proceedings 107, 261-265. (2) James, G., Witten, D., Hastie, T., Tibshirani, R., Taylor, J., 2023. An introduction to statistical learning with applications in Python. New York, U.S.: Springer Science+Business Media (https://www.statlearning.com/) (3) Varian, H.R., 2014. Big data: new tricks for econometrics. The Journal of Economic Perspectives 28, 3-27. (4) https://github.com/chtunsw/ai_notes (5) https://github.com/julianyulu/Machine-Learning-Notes Assessment: Attendance and class discussions and class presentations 30%, mid-term oral examination 20%, final project 30%, final closed-book written examination 20%. docs.text: 1 Family Economics Spring 2023 M7M8M9 Classroom: TSMC(台積館) Room 428 Course Description: This course focuses on research on family and demographic economics. Students will be introduced to a wide range of research topics related to family and demographic economics and learn to develop the ability to conduct research in this field. The study of families and households is an important research area given the increasingly complex organization of families, which have produced substantial effects on behavior of households and welfare of children as well as spouses. We will focus on the theoretical modeling and empirical investigation of how individuals sort into families (cohabitation, marriage and divorce) and of the major economic outcomes determined in a family context (such as spousal time allocation, labor supply (particularly the changing role of women in the labor force), fertility, consumption, investments in children and intergenerational transfers. Of particular importance are the various classes of household models and their testable implications on family decisions. We will also investigate family laws and policies from the economic perspective and draw insights from research studies in sociology and demography on the family. Method of Instruction: Lecture/Discussion Course Website and Communication: Courses materials are available on our course website in the eeclass system (eeclass 數位學習 平台). Readings, usually academic articles, will be assigned throughout this course. Students are expected to participate in the discussion of papers covered in each topic. The links for the papers and selected articles and lectures notes will be posted on the course website. So please make sure to regularly check the course website. docs.text: 1 Political Economy: Theories and Applications (Graduate) 政治經濟理論與應用 Class time: R567 13:20-16:20 Class location: Instructor: Pi-Han Christine Tsai Office: TSMC Building 717 Online office hour: by appointment Email: pihantsai@mx.nthu.edu.tw 1. Course Description： This course introduces students to major themes in political economy, with a focus on how political institutions, market mechanisms, state capacity, interest groups, public values, and distributional conflicts influence economic policy and development outcomes. Rather than treating policies as purely technical solutions, the course asks why certain policies are adopted, who benefits from them, who bears their costs, and why seemingly efficient or fair policies often fail in practice. The first half of the course introduces core analytical tools in political economy, including institutions, collective action, voting, redistribution, political incentives, and state capacity. The second half applies these tools to contemporary debates on market society, inequality, meritocracy, populism, and AI governance. 2. Course Objectives This course introduces students to core concepts, analytical frameworks, and empirical research in political economy. Students will learn to use political economy tools to analyze how institutions, incentives, distributional conflicts, and public values shape policy choices and development outcomes. Through academic paper presentations, book discussions, and a final policy report, students will develop the ability to critically evaluate real-world policy issues from both analytical and normative perspectives. 3. Grading Policy Class Participation 10% Academic Paper Presentation 20% Student-led discussion 30% Final Report 40% 4. Course Requirements (1) Class Participation (10%): Active and meaningful participation in class discussions is essential and valued. (2) Academic Paper Presentation (20%): Each student will give one in-class presentation on an academic paper related to the weekly topic. The presentation should explain the paper’s research question, political economy mechanism, evidence or empirical strategy, main findings, limitations, and broader implications for public policy. 2 (3) Student-led discussion (30%): Each student will select one topic from Weeks 10–14 and lead a class discussion based on the relevant book(s) from the required book list. The presentation should identify the book’s central argument, critically evaluate its perspective, and connect its arguments to a contemporary public policy issue. Students should prepare discussion questions and facilitate class participation. (4) Final Report (40%): Students are required to write a report analyzing a public policy issue from a political economy perspective. The report should introduce the policy issue and its context, identify the key actors involved, compare their incentives and interests, evaluate the existing policy response, and propose a more effective and feasible policy alternative. Students will first present a preliminary version of their analysis in the midterm proposal workshop. They are then required to conduct a small survey or interview to assess the feasibility and public acceptability of their proposal. Based on the survey or interview results, students should reevaluate and, if necessary, revise their recommendation. The goal is not only to propose an ideal policy, but also to understand why good policies are often difficult to implement in practice. The final report should be no more than 10 pages, including figures, tables, and references. * Ethics Statement on Generative Artificial Intelligence: Conditionally open Students must briefly explain how generative AI was used, such as for topic ideation, sentence refinement, or structural reference. This explanation should be included either in a footnote on the title page or after the references in their assignments or reports. 5. Tentative Course Schedule 1. 9/10 Introduction: What is political economy? 2. 9/17 Institutions and economic development 3. 9/24 The logic of collective action 4. 10/1 Political Economy of Environmental Policy 5. 10/8 Median Voter Theorem: Electoral Competition 6. 10/15 Voting, Redistribution, and Collective Choice 7. 10/22 Political Business and Budget Cycle 8. 10/29 Bureaucrats, Politicians, and State Capacity 9. 11/5 Midterm policy proposal workshop 10. 11/12 Market, Morality, and the Political Economy of Policy Choice 11. 11/19 Inequality, Poverty, and Redistribution 12. 11/26 Meritocracy, Elitism, and the Reproduction of Inequality 13. 12/3 Globalization, Populism and Democratic Backlash 14. 12/10 AI Governance and the Future of Political Economy 15. 12/17 Final Presentation 16. 12/24 Course Wrap-up: What does Political Economy Teach us?

Lin Contact Information:  O¢ ce: CTMñ712  E-mail: slin@mx.nthu.edu.tw  Tel: 03-574-2729 Time and Location: Friday 9 to noon; CTM 732 Course Webpage: http://mx.nthu.edu.tw/~slin/ Secretary: TBA, E-mail: TBA Course Description: This doctoral-level course examines the interactions between health, education, and labor market outcomes from both theoretical and empirical perspectives. The course integrates insights from health economics, labor economics, and the economics of education to analyze how human capital investments in schooling and health jointly shape productivity, labor supply, earnings, and inequality across the life cycle. We begin with theoretical foundations, including the human capital framework, health production models, and life-cycle labor supply decisions. The course then explores key empirical questions such as the causal e§ects of education on health, the role of health in labor market participation and productivity, and the intergenerational transmission of health and human capital. Particular attention is given to modern empirical strategies used to identify causal relationships, including natural experiments, instrumental variables, regression discontinuity designs, di§erence-in-di§erences, and randomized controlled trials. Students will engage with frontier research in the literature and examine policy-relevant topics such as health insurance and labor supply, early-life health shocks, education reforms, workplace health policies, and aging and retirement behavior. Emphasis will be placed on the interpretation and replication of empirical studies, as well as the design of new research projects using large-scale administrative or survey data. ECON 7077 Fall 2026 By the end of the course, students will develop a deep understanding of the theoretical mechanisms linking health, education, and labor markets and will acquire the empirical tools needed to conduct rigorous research in these areas. Hopefully, each student will end up with a draft paper that is close to being ready for submission. Learning Objectives: By the end of the course, students should be able to: 1. Understand core theoretical models linking health, education, and labor supply. 2. Critically evaluate empirical research in health, education, and labor economics. 3. docs.nameEn: Partial Differential Equations and Complex Variables
docs.text: 偏微分方程與複變函數−課程大綱 (10510 EE 202002, Partial Differential Equations and Complex Variables) 一、課程說明(Course Description) 本課程銜接常微分方程，涵蓋偏微分方程及 複變數函數兩者，提供修習其他工程或物 理學科所需之數學基礎。修完本科目 可對偏微分方程之物理意義、基本解法與複變函 數之理論、應用等有一概括性 之認識，有助於修習電磁學、近代物理、控制系統、電力工程等課程。本科目 需具有大一微積分、常微分方程(Ordinary Differential Equations) 及傅氏/拉氏 (Fourier/Laplace)變換之基礎。 二、教科書(Text Books) E. Kreyszig, Advanced Engineering Mathematics, 9th Ed., John Wiley & Sons, Inc., 2006. 三、參考書籍(References): n/a 四、教學方式(Teaching Method) 課堂講授(中文授課) 五、教學進度(Syllabus) 1.偏微分方程簡介;一維波動方程式之物理模型 2.解偏微分方程的方法:分離變數法、本徵函數展開法、積分轉換法 3.二維波動方程式:直角座標、極座標 4.Laplace 方程式:直角座標、極座標、球座標;正交函數展開 5.複變函數簡介:解析函數(Analytic functions)、Cauchy-Riemann 方程組 6.複變函數之路徑積分、Cauchy 積分定理 7.Taylor 級數、Laurent 級數、留數(Residue)積分法 8.複變之應用:以留數積分法計算實變函數積分，解二維 Laplace 方程式 六、成績考核(Evaluation) 1.兩次 Quiz(分別為 25%, 30%)，期末考(涵蓋全學期範圍 45%)作業僅為練習 用，不計分。 2.按照上述權重算出原始總分，之後還會根據分數分佈進行調分 3.調分二原則：(1) 只調高不調低 (2) 調分後大小關係不變 七、學生使用 AI 的規則 學生可自由使用 AI 學習，無任何限制。但是學生必須了解 AI 對於數學科目 的學習給出的答案正確率較低，學生必須能夠具備不靠 AI 分辨錯誤的能力。 八、可連結之網頁位址 （於 eLearn）

Overview: This course offers a rigorous and foundational journey through one of the most elegant and widely applied branches of mathematics. Using Linear Algebra by Stephen H. Friedberg, Arnold J. Insel, and Lawrence E. Spence as our primary text, we will explore the theory and applications of vector spaces, linear transformations, matrices, and inner product spaces with a level of depth suited for serious study in mathematics, physics, computer science, and engineering. This course emphasizes both conceptual understanding and abstract reasoning. We will not only learn how to perform computations with matrices and vectors but also delve into the theoretical structure that underpins these operations. By the end of the course, you will have a solid grasp of the fundamental concepts of linear algebra, such as • Vector spaces and subspaces • Linear independence, bases, and dimension • Linear transformations and their matrix representations • Eigenvalues, eigenvectors, and diagonalization • Inner product spaces and orthogonality Our classes are built around structured handouts, and your active participation is expected. Topics include advances in photonics and optoelectronic technologies, scientific breakthroughs, industrial perspectives, career development, and mental well-being. docs.text: 1 11510EE 423000 Design and Fabrication Laboratory of Compound Semiconductor Transistors (化合半導體電晶體設計與晶圓製程實驗) Course Description & Objective: Through this course, students will experience the complete device development cycle of gallium nitride (GaN) high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs), from design and simulation to fabrication and electrical characterization. Students will use TCAD tools to analyze and optimize transistor structures, develop device layouts, participate in fabrication processes, and perform electrical measurements and data analysis. Under the guidance of the instructor, teaching assistants, and technical staff, students will gain hands-on exposure to semiconductor process flows, fabrication equipment, and characterization techniques. Students will be expected to independently refine and optimize their device designs through iterative simulation and layout development. By designing, fabricating, and evaluating compound semiconductor devices, students will develop a deeper understanding of the relationships among material properties, device architecture, fabrication processes, and electrical performance. This hands-on experience will provide practical skills in semiconductor device development while offering valuable insights into emerging technologies for power electronics, RF systems, and next-generation compound semiconductor applications. Teaching Method: Lectures offered in Chinese The instructor will provide lectures on TCAD simulation, layout design, semiconductor fabrication, and device physics. Students will independently conduct TCAD-based design optimization and process/device split studies. Teaching assistants will guide students through fabrication processes and support device characterization, including DC and RF measurements. Students are expected to analyze measurement results, compare them with simulation predictions, and summarize their findings in technical reports for each module. Course Time: Official W7W8W9 Laboratory and fabrication activities may occasionally require extended processing time beyond the regular class period. In such cases, students may be required to participate in evening sessions, potentially between 7:30 PM and 9:00 PM, depending on process requirements and equipment availability. 2 Course Content: 有三週的星期五上午安排至台灣半導體研究中心(TSRI)作實驗 一、 課程說明與修課須知 本課程分為兩大部分：元件模擬與 Layout 設計以及元件製作與量測實 作。課程將提供 GaN-on-Si 試片，由學生自行完成 TCAD 模擬、Layout 設計 優化、製程參與及元件量測分析等工作，體驗從設計到製作驗證之完整半導體 元件開發流程。由於課程內容涵蓋多項實作與專題工作，所需投入時間較一般 課程為高，請同學於選課前依據自身課業負擔與研究規劃審慎評估。 二、 授課與分組方式 實驗課上課方式將採用五人一組、全班分成四組，每組預計將安排一位助 教全程協助實驗進行。由於課程實作內容繁多，將會衍生額外的助教與實驗時 間。我們將會在課程開始後調查大家可行的空檔，實際的額外實驗時間將由各 組助教與學生共同討論決定。 三、 課程進度與實務備註 關於 Layout 設計調整： 本課程會使用 Maskless Aligner 為 Lithograph 設備。屆時學生可依照各自的模擬結果，在此設計規範內進行 Layout 調整。Unit Topics Week 1 Gallium nitride high electron mobility transistor structure, operation principle and process flow 1 2 TCAD Simulation -1 2 3 TCAD Simulation - 2 3 4 Fabrication Lab. Safety Course (TSRI) 4 5 Layout Introduction Design 5 6 Presentation of Device Design (TCAD and Simulation) 6 7 Fabrication 1 1st Passivation –ALD + PECVD) (TSRI) 7 8 Fabrication 2 (S/D Contacts) –Lithography and Ohmic Open 8 9 Fabrication 3 (S/D Contacts) –Wet Cleaning & Metal Disposition and Patterning 9 10 Fabrication 4 (S/D Contacts & Isolation) – RTA Process and Implantation (TSRI) 10 11 Fabrication 5 (Interconnection) –Pad Metal Formation 11 12 Fabrication 6 MOCVD Introduction (TSRI) 12 13 Fabrication 7 (Interface State Measurement) CV Measurement Analysis 13 14 Fabrication 8 (2nd Passivation + Gate Open) – PECVD, Litho. for gate pass. opening 14 15 Fabrication 9 (Gate Metal Formation) –Metal Deposition and Patterning 15 16 Fabrication 10 Bonus for T-Gate Formation and Measurement 16 17 Final Presentation 17 3 Grading: 1. Simulation and layout report: (20%) 2. Lab. Report.: (50%) (10 Short Fabrication Reports) • A short report of each lab. including lab procedures, findings, and key summary 3. Final Report and Presentation: (30%) 4. Cheating: Any form of cheating results in a final score below 60 (fail). 教科書： (1) Gaudenzio Meneghesso, Matteo Meneghini, Enrico Zanoni, “Gallium Nitride-enabled High Frequency and High Efficiency Power Conversion”, 2018, Springer. (2) Fabrizio Roccaforte, Mike Leszczynski, “First Nitride Semiconductor Technology: Power Electronics and Optoelectronic Devices”, 3 August 2020, Wiley-VCH. 參考書： (1) Nirmal, D., Ajayan, J., “Modeling of AlGaN/GaN High Electron Mobility Transistors”, 2025, Springer. (2) Doering, Robert, Nishi, Yoshio, “Handbook of semiconductor manufacturing technology”, 2008, CRC Press.

docs.text: EE5219: Design and Application of Phase-Locked Loop Instructor: Pen-Jui Peng Office: R803, Delta Building E-mail: pjpeng@ee.nthu.edu.tw Course Description: This course introduces the design and analysis of the phase-locked loop (PLL). It covers the phase domain analysis and modeling of the loop, building blocks, phase noise evaluation of the PLL. It also includes the applications of the PLL, especially the clock and data recovery (CDR) design for the wireline receiver. Course Description Talk Like a Pro: Effective Presentation Skills is an interactive online course hosted on Future Learn that develops strategic presentation and public speaking skills for academic and professional contexts. The course adopts a step-based microlearning design integrating short video lectures, guided reflection, embedded quizzes, and discussion-based activities. Learners explore how to analyze audience and purpose, structure compelling content, enhance delivery techniques, manage Q&A sessions, and build a confident speaker mindset. Through task- based assignments and peer interaction, participants apply key concepts to their own presentation topics, progressively refining both content and delivery. By the end of the course, learners will have developed practical tools to design, deliver, and evaluate presentations with clarity, engagement, and professional impact. Access to FutureLearn Courses with NTHU License National Tsing Hua University provides students with free access to selected courses on FutureLearn Campus through the university license. ⚠️ Important: If you log in using a personal email or through the regular FutureLearn website, you may NOT receive the NTHU license benefits, and some course content or features may be restricted. Login Instructions Step 1 First, log in through the NTHU Campus portal: NTHU FutureLearn Campus Portal. It is recommended to use your NTHU Google account or university email. Step 2 After logging in, search for the course you would like to take. Step 3 Click “Join Course” Step 4 Make sure to select: “FutureLearn Campus (Get free upgrade)” ⚠️ Do NOT choose the regular paid option. Step 5 You will then successfully join the course with: ✅ Full course access for free ✅ Unlimited access duration ✅ FutureLearn upgraded features. Fall 2026 2/3 1. Add the course “Talk Lik a Pro: Effective Presentation Skills” to your course list. https://www.futurelearn.com/courses/talk-like-a-pro-effective-presentation-skills 2. Complete steps and tasks of the course on Future Learn platform. 3. Synchronous sessions (SS) are conducted through Google Meet on at 13:20 p.m. (GMT +8) Thursday, October 1, October 8, October 22, and November 5, 2026 (GMT+8) of the Fall semester, 2026. Google Meet Link @ https://meet.google.com/cmi-dyrw-hbk 4. Use of AI: Conditionally open. Regarding transparency and responsibility, you can choose to use AI for collaboration and mutual learning to enhance the quality of your work. If you do, you must briefly explain how generative AI was used. ⚫ Assessment (The grading follows a pass/fail (satisfactory/unsatisfactory) system.) 1. Platform Engagement and Step Completion (50%) Completion of weekly learning steps, including videos, quizzes, and embedded activities. 2. Participation (20%) Active and thoughtful contributions to discussion in all four live sessions, demonstrating reflection on presentation strategies and peer interaction. 3. Final Presentation Project (30%) Submission of a recorded presentation, following 3MT format, demonstrating integration of course concepts, clarity of message, audience awareness, and effective delivery strategies. Tentative weekly schedule Week Topic Assignment, Quiz/Exam or In-class interaction 1 10/1 Foundations of effective presentations Learners analyze audience expectations and define clear presentation objectives. Activities include audience profiling, purpose statements, and identifying key messages. Draft an audience analysis and a concise presentation purpose statement. SSI 2 10/8 Organizing compelling content Learners explore logical structures, persuasive frameworks, and storytelling techniques. Emphasis is placed on crafting strong openings, coherent body organization, and impactful conclusions. Develop a structured presentation outline with introduction, main points, and conclusion. SSII 3 10/15 Verbal and non-verbal communication Topics include voice control, pacing, body language, eye contact, and slide design principles. Learners reflect on delivery strengths and areas for improvement. Create a delivery improvement plan. 4 Analyzing exemplary presentations Write a short analysis of a selected Fall 2026 3/3 10/22 Learners examine effective presentation models to identify rhetorical strategies, engagement techniques, and persuasive elements. presentation, identifying strategies that can be applied to their own talk. SSIII 5 10/29 Handling interaction professionally Learners practice strategies for responding to questions, managing challenging situations, and maintaining composure during discussions. Prepare and script responses to potential audience questions related to their presentation topic. [Submission of final presentation] 6 11/5 Managing anxiety and building confidence This week addresses mindset, rehearsal strategies, and performance preparation. Learners integrate content, structure, and delivery skills into a cohesive presentation plan. Submit a final presentation outline or recorded presentation demonstrating integrated application of course concepts. SSIV References Alley, M. (2013). The Craft of Scientific Presentations: Critical Steps to Succeed and Critical Errors to Avoid. New York: Springer-Verlag. Gallo, C. (2014). Talk like TED: The 9 public speaking secrets of the world’s top minds. New York, St. Martin’s Griffin. Hey, B. (2024). Mastering Scientific Presentations: Unlocking Your Communication Skills. Springer Wiesbaden. Zanders, E. & Macleod, L. (2018). Presentation Skills for Scientists: A Practical Guide. Cambridge, Cambridge University Press.

docs.name: 策略性人力資源管理
docs.text: 1 Strategic Human Resource Management Instructor Information Instructor George S. Benson, Ph.D. Office Number COB 209 Office Telephone Number 817-272-3412 Email Address benson@uta.edu Faculty Profile https://www.uta.edu/profiles/george-benson Office Hours By Appointment via Teams Course Information Description of Course Content This is an applied course that examines how modern corporations use human resource management (HRM) to enhance organizational capabilities and achieve strategic objectives. Through the assigned readings, case discussion and various class exercises we will examine how the acquisition, deployment, assessment and retention of an organization’s workforce impacts productivity and firm performance in various contexts. Readings will cover the theory and research on strategic HRM as well as the various parts of a typical HR system. Some of the topics we will discuss include HR planning, recruitment, methods of selection, job design, and implementation of performance management processes. Cases will then be used to focus on specific strategic issues faced by companies including talent management, selecting for cultural fit, incentive pay, and organizational culture. No prior knowledge of HR is assumed and there are no prerequisites for this course. The approach of the course will be practical guidance for making staffing and management decisions in organizations based on explanatory theory and scientific research. In addition to learning the theory and topics of human resource management through readings and classroom lecture, this course cover the skills required for HR planning, selection, and conducting performance evaluations. The course material is not only useful for working in human resource departments, but for all managers who hire, train, and evaluate employees. 2 Student Learning Outcomes 1. Recognize the practices that comprise human resource management in modern corporations: a) Work design b) HR Planning c) Recruiting and selection d) Performance Management e) Total Rewards 2. Apply concepts and approaches to align HRM systems with business strategy. 3. Evaluate the role of HR in developing and maintaining organizational culture. 4. Discuss an analytics driven approach to developing HR practices. Required Textbooks and Other Course Materials Jeffrey A. Mello, Strategic Human Resource Management, 5th edition (Cengage Learning). Harvard Publishing Cases 1. Talent Recruitment at frog design Shanghai (#411040) 2. Box: The Evolution of Management Practices in a Startup (#HR43) Follow this link: https://hbsp.harvard.edu/import/785425 Required Readings in Canvas 1. Wright (2008). Human Resource Strategy: Adapting to the Age of Globalization. Alexandria, VA: Society for Human Resource Management. 2. Porter (2008). The Five Forces That Shape Strategy. Harvard Business Review, 86:1. 3. Bartlett & Ghoshal (2002). Building Competitive Advantage Through People. Sloan Management Review, 43:2. 4. Capelli and Tavis (2019). HR Goes Agile, Harvard Business Review, 96:2. 5. Ton (2012). Why good jobs are good for retailers. Harvard Business Review. 6. Donovan & Benko (2016). “AT&T’s Talent Overhaul,” Harvard Business Review. 7. Stahl et al. (2012). “Six Principles of Effective Talent Management,” MIT Sloan Management Review. 8. Nisen, M. (2015). Why GE had to kill its annual performance reviews after more than three decades. http://qz.com/428813/ge-performance-review-strategy-shift/ 9. Schaerer, M. & Swaab, R. Are You Sugarcoating Your Feedback Without Realizing It? Harvard Business Review Online. https://hbr.org/2019/10/are-you-sugarcoating-your-feedback-without- realizing-it? 10. Pfeffer (1998). Six Dangerous Myths About Pay. Harvard Business Review. 11. Huselid, Becker & Beatty (2005). “A players” or “A positions”? Harvard Business. 12. Davenport, Harris, Shapiro (2010). Competing on Talent Analytics. Harvard Business Review. 13. Chatman & Cha (2003). Leading by leveraging culture. California Management Review 45:4. 14. Porath (2016). Creating a More Humane Workplace Where Employees and Businesses Thrive. Society for Human Resource Management. 3 Grading Information GRADING A grade of A (90%), B (80%), C (70%), D (60%), or F (<60%) will be earned based on: Group Assignments HR And Strategy Example 10% Job Design Example 10% Total Rewards Example 10% Organizational Culture Scavenger Hunt 10% frog Design Selection Case 15% Box: The Evolution of Management at a Start-Up Case 15% Peer Evaluation 10% Individual Paper 20% Total 100% GROUP ASSIGNMENTS (80%) You will work in groups do a number of assignments and exercises. These will be done as a group and every group member will receive the same grade. Group members will be asked to rate teammates on group participation at the end of the class. Peer evaluation is 10% of the total grade. HR And Strategy Example (10%) Groups will give an example of how HR practices match or mismatch the strategy at an organization you are familiar with. Describe the organization and its strategy using the language from Mello Chapter 3. Then give an example of how a specific HR practice (job design, recruiting, selection, training, compensation, or performance appraisal) either supports that strategy by encouraging specific employee behaviors or works against the intended strategy by encouraging the wrong behaviors. Job Design Example (10%) Groups will give an example of an organization that you are familiar with that uses either a high involvement work design or a control-oriented work design. Describe the organization, the strategy and the nature of the work. If high involvement work designs such as those described in The Good Jobs Strategy lead to superior performance, why don’t all organizations use high involvement work design? Total Rewards Example (10%) Groups will give an example from an organization you are familiar with about a way in which total rewards practices demonstrate one of the myths from Jeff Pfeffer "Six Dangerous Myths About Pay". What would you recommend to change to improve this practice based on the concepts we have covered in this module. OR Give an example from an organization you are familiar with about a way in which total rewards practices has overcome one of these myths. Why is this practice effective total rewards based on the concepts we have covered? 4 Organizational Culture Scavenger Hunt (10%) This assignment requires you to do a "Scavenger Hunt" for organizational culture artifacts. Artifacts are representations or manifestations of culture - symbols or practices that reinforce organizational values. Then discuss how these artifacts work to reinforce company culture. What values are they intended to promote? How do they work to guide employee behavior? The scavenger hunt asks you to find: 1. Mission Statement 2. Founding Story 3. Story / Legend 4. Language – Shorthand / Lingo / Terminology 5. Visual or Graphic Identity / Logo 6. Ritual or Ceremony 7. Physical space 8. HR Practices: Recruiting 9. HR Practices: Socialization / Training 10. HR Practices: Rewards frog Design Selection Case (15%) This case requires you to develop rubrics for assessing job candidates for fit of job requirements and organizational culture. The case involves a very unique design firm called frog and requires you to select between two finalists for a job. Assess the candidates for the jobs of Associate Creative Director and Business Development Director against (1) the job requirements in Exhibit 6 and (2) the archetypes as detailed in Exhibit 7. (Hint: Make a spreadsheet). Resumes for the four finalist are in Canvas. This case can be accessed through Harvard Publishing. 1. Make recommendations for hiring decisions among the finalists. Who did you recommend and why? What factors did you weigh most heavily for each of the jobs? 2. How can hiring managers balance job-related skills and cultural fit when assessing candidates? Box: The Evolution of Management at a Start Up Case (15%) Each group will read and analyze the case “Box: The Evolution of Management Practice in a Start- up.” The case analysis should be approximately 6-8 pages in length double-spaced and presented in a narrative form with headings and sub-headings. Case questions are provided to guide your analysis. You will be graded on your response to each of these but the paper does not have to be written in question and answer format. Apply the concepts that we have covered over and give your assessment of the issues at Box and how HR matches company strategy as Box has grown and matured. Case write-ups will be graded based on your substantive response to each of the discussion questions. 1. Give a short overview of Box. 2. Describe Box’s strategy. How does Box compete? 3. Describe the culture at Box. What are its basic values and operating principles? 4. How is Box’s culture evolving as it grows and matures? 5. How do Box HR practices fit with the corporate strategy and culture? Asses the evolution of HR practices as the company has grown and matured. 6. What are the biggest HR challenges that Box faces with growth? Make some HR practice recommendations. 5 INDIVIDUAL PAPER (20%) This paper requires you to analyze a significant HRM issue in a large organization. The paper can be done in one of two ways: 1) identify an HRM problem and recommend a solution, or 2) detail how the organizational has already responded to a HRM issue and critique that response. Research should include interviewing relevant employees including an HR manager. All assessment should be based on the principles covered in the course and consistent with business strategy. The paper should include the following: Background information: You should begin with a basic description of the organization, the mission, strategy and relevant company history. Attach to your completed paper information on your source materials. This should include information on personal interviews conducted. Description of the issue and how it was handled: Summarize the issue which you have identified. Provide a short history of events including how the issue came about and what the organization did to address the issue. Assess the effectiveness of the HR practices in this situation and indicate the shared roles of HR department and line managers. Obtain copies of forms/documents such as job descriptions, employee selection tests, performance evaluation forms, organizational career management or succession plan, exit interview schedule, and any other item that helps to explain the issue. Your assessment: Give either recommendation for future action or your critique of the organization’s previous actions using the concepts discussed in class. Include reasons why the organization was successful or unsuccessful in dealing with the issue as well as specific recommendations for what managers could have done differently. Particular emphasis should be given to the alignment or misalignment of company strategy and the HR practices examined. The report should be approximately 6-8 pages, excluding exhibits, and presented in a narrative form with headings and sub-headings. The report will be evaluated primarily in terms of content, but 20 percent of the report score will be allocated to organization, compositional quality (style, spelling, grammar, and syntax), and appearance (typed or word-processed, headings and sub-headings, etc.) If two of you work for the same business organization, you can work together to obtain information. However, each of you must prepare a different individual HR report.

docs.text: 國立清華大學工業工程與工程管理學系張國浩林東盈©2026 115 學年度第 1 學期 11510 AIMS Fellows EMIM5002 大數據與決策分析 Big Data and Decision Analysis 任課教授：張國浩 教授 (Professor Kuo-Hao Chang, Ph.D.) E-Mail: chang@mx.nthu.edu.tw 辦公室：清華大學工程一館 713 室 Tel: 03-5742337 林東盈 教授 (Professor Dung-Yin Lin, Ph.D.) E-Mail: dylin@ie.nthu.edu.tw 辦公室：清華大學工程一館 814 室 Tel: 03-5742694 課程助教：洪紹庭 (h34101127@gs.ncku.edu.tw) 上課時間：每週五(Friday) 18:30~21:20 (2025/09/05 ~ 2025/12/19) 上課教室：綜四 223 一、課程說明 (Course Description) 學習有系統地分析策略決策問題、架構目標、評估方案的預期結果和可能的風 險、探討決策方案的執行，並應用數位決策與大數據分析技術並結合模擬分析，從巨 量資訊找出問題，並提出解決方案，透過大數據輔助決策，從問題架構、資料收集、 資訊整理、決策分析乃至決策輔助的完整思維過程，提供系統化、數位化之決策依據 與實行策略。除介紹大數據、作業研究與決策分析方法和工具外，並利用演講、個案 討論、上機實做和實證案例研究，培養策略性決策思維及應用資料挖礦解決相關問 題，進而提升大數據分析和數位決策能力。 二、課程大綱(Agenda) 週次 日期 單元主題及參考資料 授課教授 附註 1 9/11 大數據與決策分析簡介 林東盈 2 9/18 運輸與指派問題概念 林東盈 3 9/25 中秋節停課一次 林東盈 4 10/2 運輸與指派實務案例分析與應 用 林東盈 5 10/9 國慶連假停課一次 林東盈 6 10/16 生產排程問題概念 林東盈 7 10/23 生產排程問題案例分析與應用 林東盈 8 10/30 期中報告 林東盈 國立清華大學工業工程與工程管理學系張國浩林東盈©2026 115 學年度第 1 學期 9 11/6 Decision Analysis (1) 張國浩 助教:洪紹庭 課堂練習並繳交作業 10 11/13 Decision Analysis (2) 張國浩 課堂練習並繳交作業 & Case study 11 11/20 Simulation (1) & A refresher on Probability and Statistics 張國浩 課堂練習並繳交作業 &專題報告 1 (一組) 12 11/27 Simulation (2) (3) 張國浩 課堂練習並繳交作業 &專題報告 2 (兩組) 13 12/4 Stochastic Optimization: Introduction 張國浩 課堂練習並繳交作業 &專題報告 3 (兩組) 14 12/11 Stochastic Optimization: Direct Search Method 張國浩 課堂練習並繳交作業 15 12/18 Stochastic Optimization: Stochastic Approximation 張國浩 課堂練習並繳交作業 16 12/25 Online presentation & discussion 張國浩 線上報告 三、成績考核 (Evaluation) 1. 課堂練習與作業 15% (個人) 2. 軟體實做 15% (2 人一組為原則，上課完成) 3. Case study 10% (4 人一組為原則，每人報告兩次) 4. 期中報告 50% (4 人一組為原則) 5. 期末報告 10% (4 人一組為原則) 四、課程網頁資源(Resources) 講義及案例的原始論文和相關資料：https://elearn.nthu.edu.tw/

docs.name: 跨領域研究方法
docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 11510EMIM501700 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size AIMS Fellows 中文名稱 Course Title 跨領域研究方法 英文名稱 Course English Title Interdisciplinary Research Methods 任課教師 Instructor 曾元琦 上課時間 Time RaRbRc 上課教室 Room 旺宏 3A 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) 本課程旨在引導學生掌握進行跨領域研究所需的核心方法與學術寫作能力，涵蓋從研究設 計、資料蒐集到成果撰寫的完整研究流程，並透過實作經驗逐步深化理解與應用。學生將 學習如何依據具體問題與情境背景，選擇與整合適切的研究策略，提出具備實證基礎的創 新解方。課程前半段聚焦於研究設計與方法論建構，內容涵蓋研究問題的界定、資料蒐集 與分析策略、跨領域合作的實務挑戰，以及研究倫理與學術責任。透過案例分析與小組討 論，學生將培養實務敏感度，並強化與異質專業背景研究者協作的能力。後半段則專注於 科技論文撰寫技巧，依序涵蓋文獻綜述撰寫、研究方法與結果呈現、討論與結論發展，進 一步延伸至標題設計與摘要撰寫。課程將寫作視為研究思維發展與深化的關鍵歷程，透過 書寫的過程，學生將學習如何釐清問題意識、反思研究決策、修正論述方向，進而強化其 跨領域整合與溝通能力。學生將透過漸進式的寫作演練與回饋修正，有系統地提升論文的 結構邏輯、語言表達與學術溝通力，最終能完整表達其研究成果，並與相關領域進行有效 交流。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 研究方法, 跨領域合作, 研究設計, 研究溝通, 研究成果展示 Research Methods, Cross-disciplinary Collaboration, Research Design, Research Communication, Research Presentation 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程旨在引導學生掌握進行跨領域研究所需的核心方法與學術寫作能力，涵蓋從研究設 計、資料蒐集到成果撰寫的完整研究流程，並透過實作經驗逐步深化理解與應用。學生將 學習如何依據具體問題與情境背景，選擇與整合適切的研究策略，提出具備實證基礎的創 新解方。課程前半段聚焦於研究設計與方法論建構，內容涵蓋研究問題的界定、資料蒐集 與分析策略、跨領域合作的實務挑戰，以及研究倫理與學術責任。透過案例分析與小組討 論，學生將培養實務敏感度，並強化與異質專業背景研究者協作的能力。後半段則專注於 科技論文撰寫技巧，依序涵蓋文獻綜述撰寫、研究方法與結果呈現、討論與結論發展，進 一步延伸至標題設計與摘要撰寫。課程將寫作視為研究思維發展與深化的關鍵歷程，透過 書寫的過程，學生將學習如何釐清問題意識、反思研究決策、修正論述方向，進而強化其 跨領域整合與溝通能力。學生將透過漸進式的寫作演練與回饋修正，有系統地提升論文的 結構邏輯、語言表達與學術溝通力，最終能完整表達其研究成果，並與相關領域進行有效 交流。 ● 指定用書(Text Books) Wallwork, Adrian. English for writing research papers. Springer Nature, 2023. (清大圖書館電子書 https://link-springer-com.nthulib-oc.nthu.edu.tw/book/10.1007/978-3-031-31072-0) ● 參考書籍(References) Research Papers in ACM digital library; IEEE Xplore; IJHCS; Related SCI/SSCI Journals ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 本課程採多元教學方式進行，以理論與實作並重，強調學習過程中的思辨與應用能力： • 講義授課：系統性介紹研究方法與論文寫作相關理論基礎。 • 文獻導讀與分享：閱讀與分析關鍵研究方法文獻，並由學生進行簡報與反思討論。 • 實務專家經驗分享：邀請具跨領域研究實務經驗的專家學者進行現身說法與案例講 解。 • 小組討論與研究專案演練：透過實際研究設計與模擬練習，深化跨領域整合與合作 能力。 • 論文撰寫練習與回饋：分階段進行科技論文各部分的撰寫練習，搭配師生個別回饋 與同儕互評。 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) • 課程導論與跨領域研究導引 • 研究問題的界定與提問技巧 • 研究方法概論與分類 • 資料蒐集與分析方法（一）：訪談與觀察 • 資料蒐集與分析方法（二）：問卷與實驗設計 • 跨領域研究的挑戰與協作 • 研究倫理與學術責任 • 研究設計工作坊與初步提案分享 • 文獻綜述與資料整理技巧 • 論文撰寫架構與標題、摘要設計 • 撰寫研究方法與研究結果章節 • 撰寫討論與結論章節 • 學術表達與邏輯建構 • 初稿發表與同儕回饋 • 完稿修訂與成果呈現 • 成果發表與課程總結 ● 成績考核(Evaluation) • 相關研究方法閱讀報告 (個人) 20% • 相關研究方法課堂分享 (小組) 20% • 研究方法應用實作與發表 (小組) 30% • 專案報告 (小組) 20% • 課程參與 (個人) 10% ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 本課程鼓勵學生在透明與負責的原則下，適度使用 AI 工具進行課業協作。學生應在作業或 報告的標題頁註腳或引用文獻部分簡要說明 AI 工具的使用情況，並遵循學校的相關指引。 如未明確標註，教師有權重新評分或不予計分。 ● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website) https://mx.nthu.edu.tw/~yc.tseng/zh-tw.html

docs.name: 財經個案研究
docs.text: National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 科號 Course Number EMM 600300 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Size of Limit - 中文名稱 Course Title 財經個案研究 英文名稱 Course English Title Finance and Economic Cases Analysis 任課教師 Instructor 余士迪、蔡子晧 教師聯絡方式 Contact Information thtsai@mx.nthu.edu.tw 上課時間 Time 待定 上課教室 Room 待定 先修科目 Prerequisite(s) 無 本課程對應之學習目標與核心能力 Aligned Learning Goals and Learning Objectives ■ 以堅實理論為基礎，理解財金體系運作機制，應用財金分析技術，實際解決財金問 題。 (20%) To understand the mechanism of the finance system through solid theoretical foundation and to apply quantitative financial analysis to solve real-world financial issues. (20%) ■ 具備厚實財金基礎知識，包括財務管理與公司理財、衍生性商品訂價與風險管理 (20%) To learn the knowledge of financial management, corporate finance, financial derivatives, and risk management. (20%) ■ 具備創新管理，開發新領域的能力 (20%) To acquire the ability to innovate, integrate, and develop new research areas. (20%) ■ 培養跨領域工作的能力 (20%) To develop the ability to work across different disciplines. (20%) ■ 具備團隊合作的精神，有效溝通的能力，以及人文素養與國際觀。 (20%) To develop teamwork spirit, to acquire the ability to communicate effectively, and to have broad knowledge across humanities, social science and natural science with international perspective. (20%) 課程目標 Course Objectives 以財務管理重要決策為主軸，並以公司整體觀點為架構，思考各項財務決策與公司策略 的關係，從而思考公司價值創造的財務規劃與政策。尤其是以許多重要個案為基礎，思 考如何將所學財務決策觀念導入於實際的案例中，本課程希望以演講、課堂討論、及個 案教學方式，幫助學生將學理知識與實務運用結合一體，俾達到學以致用之效果。站在 National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 財務長與公司整體觀點，思考各項財務決策對公司價值的影響。 課程說明 Course Description 針對企業個案進行分析討論，協助同學了解企業個案分析之方法。 進行方式,模擬練習、評論與企業個案分析。學生有機會深入研究實際企業個案，應用 經濟學工具進行深度分析，了解商業決策的複雜性。 透過對實例的討論，學生將學會 如何從經濟學角度全面評估企業策略。 這門課程旨在培養學生在實際商業環境中運用 經濟學原理進行深度分析的能力，使他們能夠更全面、更深入地理解並應對現代企業面 臨的各種挑戰。 以資本預算、投資與購併、企業價值評估與公司治理三個範疇，思考如何創造公司價值 並顧及利害關係人的權益。本課程將以課堂討論及個案教學方式，幫助學生將財務決策 觀念導入於實際企業經營中，達到學以致用，提升自身價值與企業價值。包含三部分： 一、回顧與建立財管知識，並運用這些知識進行公司理財決策。（投資決策、融資決策 與股利決策） 二、運用財管與公司理財的知識，分析解讀財務個案。 三、提升計算能力，解決財務問題。計算IRR、NPV、Beta與進行資本預算等。上課方式 先導讀個案，介紹財務觀念與解決方法，最後討論個案與制訂決策。 指定用書 Textbooks 上課教材以教師講義與投影片為主。 參考書籍 References Ross, S.A., R.W. Westerfield, J.F. Jaffe and B.D. Jordan, Corporate Finance, 11th ed., McGraw-Hill, 2016. (華泰代理) 教學方式 Teaching Approach The course is based on lectures. You can download the lectures from eeClass https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw/ Lectures will be distributed on the website several days before the class. 評分標準 Grading Homework and Quiz 50% Class participation 50% National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 教學進度 Course Schedule 編號 主題/講師 授課內容 1 效率市場假說/余士迪 事件究研法: 挑戰者號太空梭災難 1986 Reading: Maloney, M. & Mulherin, H. (2003). The complexity of price discovery in an efficient market: the stock market reaction to the Challenger crash. Journal of Corporate Finance, 9, p453- 479 2 因子模式/余士迪 因子模式: 單因子、三因子、四因子模式？ Reading: 顧廣平(2005) ， 「單因子、三因子或四因子模式？」 ， Review of Securities & Futures Markets ， 17:2, 101-146 Fama, Eugene and Kenneth French, 1992. The cross- of Financial Economics 33, 3–56. 3 事件研究法/余士迪 PROGRAM Evaluation vs. 事件研究法 Efficient Market Hypothesis Hsiao, Cheng, H. Steve Ching and Shui Ki Wan (2012). “A Panel Data Approach for Program Evaluation: Measuring the Benefits of Political and Economic Integration of Hong Kong with Mainland China,” Journal of Applied Econometrics, Vol. 27(5), August 2012, pp. 705–740. 4 股票評價/余士迪 投資前的計算:股票評價 Reading: Investments (第 18 章), 12th Edition by Zvi Bodie and Alex Kane and Alan Marcus 5 行為財務學/余士迪 行為財務學 1. 周賓凰、池祥萱、周冠男、龔怡霖，2002.07。「行為財務 學：文獻回顧與展望」，證券市場發展季刊，第 14 卷第 2 期，1-46。 2. 王韻怡、池祥萱、周冠男, 2016.03。「行為財務學文獻回顧 與展望：台灣市場之研究」，經濟論文叢刊 44:1，頁 1-55。 6 資本預算/蔡子晧 資本預算 + 個案 1(台灣高鐵) 7 資本預算/蔡子晧 情境分析與決策樹 + 個案 2 8 投資與購併/蔡子晧 購併 + 個案 1（日月光併購矽品） 9 投資與購併/蔡子晧 購併 + 個案 2

docs.text: 工程圖學 課程目標 : 本課程旨在培養學生具備工程圖學之基本理論與實務能力，使學生能理解工程圖在機械 設計與製造過程中的重要角色。透過工程圖學基礎概念、投影原理及視圖表達方法之介紹， 使學生建立正確的空間概念與圖面判讀能力，並能運用正投影視圖、剖視圖與輔助視圖等方 式表達機械零件之形狀與結構。 課程同時導入「Creo」電腦輔助設計軟體，讓學生學習基本草圖繪製、三維建模、特徵 建立及組立設計等操作技能，使學生能將傳統工程圖學概念與數位設計工具相結合，提升產 品設計與建模能力。 此外，透過實物測繪、徒手繪圖及工程圖練習，使學生能由實體觀察轉換為工程圖表 達，並培養圖面標註與工程圖溝通能力。藉由期末專題與成果報告，使學生整合課程所學， 完成零件建模、組立配置與工程圖繪製之完整流程，進而建立基礎機械設計與工程製圖能 力，為後續機械設計與產品開發相關課程奠定基礎。 課程大綱 週次 主題內容 (對應章節) Creo 實作重點 回家手繪作業 W01 工程圖學概論與電腦 整合平台 (Ch 1, 2) 學生分組與定專題 軟體環境介紹與設定。 他班期末專題演示。 草圖：直線、圓、圓弧、修剪、圓角。 單斜三視圖 - 1 手繪練習 15 題。 W02 幾何形體與平面幾 何作圖(Ch 3) 投影幾何學 (Ch 4) 草圖：矩形、偏移、尺寸標註。 課堂練習 : 3 題草圖。 單斜三視圖 – 2 手繪練習 15 題。 W03 正投影視圖 (Ch 5) 草圖：鏡射、多邊形、橢圓。 特徵 : 伸長、除料、圓角。 課堂練習 : 1 題草圖，2 題特徵。 復斜三視圖 – 1 手繪練習 15 題。 W04 尺寸標註(Ch 8) 特徵 :薄殼、旋轉、旋轉除料。 課堂練習 : 3 題特徵。 復斜三視圖 – 2 手繪練習 15 題。 W05 實物測繪與徒手畫 (Ch 10) 特徵 : 旋轉、旋轉除料。 課堂練習 : 3 題特徵。 圓弧三視圖 – 1 手繪練習 15 題。 W06 公差與配合（11） 曲線、疊層拉伸 : 課堂練習 : 3 題特徵。 圓弧三視圖 – 2 手繪練習 15 題。 W07 立體圖：等角、斜投 影與透視（10） 基準面、掃出 課堂練習 : 3 題特徵。 立體圖 – 1 手繪練習 15 題。 W08 期中考 : 筆試 期中考 : 上機考試 立體圖 – 2 手繪練習 15 題。 工程圖學 W09 表面織構的標注 （12） 組合件 課堂練習 : 3 題組合件。 立體圖（橢圓板）–3 手繪練習 15 題。 W10 機械螺紋與扣件 （13） 組合件、組合件爆炸、爆炸動畫 課堂練習 : 3 題組合件。 立體圖（橢圓板）–4 手繪練習 15 題。 W11 輔助視圖 (Ch 6) 簡易工程圖 : 零件、組合件工程圖 課堂練習 : 3 題。 輔助視圖 – 1 手繪練習 – 12 題 W12 軸 承（14） 簡易動畫 課堂練習 : 6 題。 輔助視圖 – 2 手繪練習 – 12 題 W13 剖視圖（7） 特徵應用 課堂練習 : 6 題特徵。 剖視圖 – 1 手繪練習 – 20 題 W14 產品開發與工程製 圖（15） 特徵應用 課堂練習 : 6 題特徵。 剖視圖 – 2 手繪練習 – 20 題 W15 期末考 : 筆試 期末考 : 上機考試 W16 期末報告 學生進行期末作品展示與報告 評量方式: 期中考、期末考:各 20％ 專題:每週上傳進度 15％，期末報告 25％ 回家作業:20％ 選用書籍/講義: 軟體:自編教材 理論:最新 CNS 工程圖學 3 版，高立出版社，作(編/譯)者: 陳朝光 審閱／賴元隆‧黃維富 修訂。出版年份:2024。ISBN: 9789863783985 。

docs.text: 1 INTRODUCTION TO WESTERN LITERATURE Instructor: Chien-heng Wu COURSE DESCRIPTION This course introduces the first-year student of literature to some of the major concepts, themes, as well as some of the most famous narratives, characters, and literary forms of the western literary tradition. The aim of such a course is to provide students the basic tools, concepts, and reading knowledge for more advanced study of western literature in upper-level courses beyond their first year at the university. While such a course does not offer a comprehensive coverage of all the major texts of western literature, it conceptualizes the western literary tradition as a series of debates and issues for discussion. We will analyze the literary texts in their historical, cultural, and political contexts, and we will examine the significance of these texts for the western literary tradition. COURSE OBJECTIVE 1. Introduce students to the masterpieces of Western literature from its inception to the 16th century. 2. Develop students’ appreciation for values and ideals that have come to shape societies and cultures in the West. 3. Cultivate students’ analytic skills (e.g. textual and contextual analysis). docs.text: 1 閱讀與寫作一(上) Reading & Writing (1) Fall 2026 Instructor: Huifen Lin Office: C630 Class time/location: T34 10:00 - 12:00 / Computer Lab 2, Computer center Office Hours: by appointment Email: huifennthu@gmail.com Office Phone: 03-5715131 (Ext.) 34382 Course goal: This course equips students with the skills needed to write multi-paragraph compositions in academic settings. We will introduce and practice pre-writing techniques along with the fundamentals of essay writing. This will be achieved by involving students in various in-class and post-class activities and assignments. The course will place particular emphasis on planning body paragraphs, crafting compelling introductions and conclusions, making appropriate word choices, and constructing effective sentences. Additionally, the course will incorporate AI into various writing tasks to enhance students' writing development by allowing them to seek and utilize feedback from the AI, ensuring a more informed and refined writing process. Course objectives: Upon completing the course, students will: 1. Possess a comprehensive understanding of the foundational steps involved in academic essay writing. 2. Develop metacognitive skills (controlling and monitoring one’s own learning) by integrating the AI tool, throughout various stages of the writing process. 3. Practice how to incorporate AI-generated text into their own essays ethically. Course material: Wyrick, J. (2017). Steps to writing well (Cengage Learning; 13th edition). The textbook is required for taking this class. It is students’ responsibility to get a copy of the text. Earlier edition of the text is not allowed in class. 2 Grading Policy A. Attendance and Participation (10%) Attendance will be checked at random intervals throughout the semester. You must notify the instructor at least one day in advance for anticipated absences. For unexpected emergencies, please inform the instructor within one week. Accumulating three absences (excused or unexcused) will result in a grade of zero for this category. B. In-Class Writing Assessments – AI Prohibited (40%) To evaluate your individual writing proficiency, two major exams will be conducted in class without the assistance of digital tools or artificial intelligence. • Midterm Exam (20%): You will compose a 5-paragraph essay (approx. 1,000 words) based on provided readings. This exam assesses your mastery of Prewriting (Ch. 1), Thesis Statements (Ch. 2), Body Paragraphs (Ch. 3), and Beginnings/Endings (Ch. 4). • Final Exam (20%): This assessment focuses on technical precision. It evaluates your ability to construct Effective Sentences (Ch. 6) and apply Word Logic (Ch. 7) to improve clarity and style. C. AI-Integrated Process-oriented Writing Tasks (30%) Several pre-class and in-class writing tasks will be used to practice your metacognitive skills— controlling and monitoring your own learning by interacting with AI tools. • Chapter Q&A (14%): Prior to each class, you will read the designated chapter, generate one or two specific questions and use ChatGPT to explore responses. You must record these interactions in the provided form and be ready to share them in class. • Draft Revision Portfolio (16%): You will maintain a portfolio documenting the sequential revision of your draft. You must document your prompts and reflect on how AI feedback specifically helped you refine your work. The breakdown for evaluation is as follows: Thesis statement (1%); Body paragraph 1, 2 and 3 (3% each); Beginning/Introduction (3%); Ending/Conclusion (3%) D. Peer Feedback (10%) Writing is a social process. You will participate in two formal peer-review sessions. Both your classmates and the instructor will evaluate the quality and specificity of the feedback you provide. • Session 1 (Content): Focusing on the strength of the thesis, supporting evidence, and logical organization. • Session 2 (Language): Focusing on sentence variety, word choice, and grammatical clarity. E. Final Revised Essay (10%) This is the final "polished" version of the essay you have worked on all semester. • Integration: Your final grade will reflect how effectively you integrated feedback from three sources: the instructor, your peers, and AI tools. • Final Submission: The essay must demonstrate a clear progression from your initial pre-test draft to a refined academic composition. 3 Schedule Week Date Topic Content 1 9/8 Introduction Artificial Intelligence: Benefits and pitfalls 2 9/15 Writing Pretest 3 9/22 AI prompt engineering 4 9/29 Chapter 1: Prewriting Read Chapter 1 (pp. 3-30) 5 10/6 Chapter 2: The thesis statement Read Chapter 2 (pp. 31-47) 6 10/13 Chapter 3: The body paragraphs Read Chapter 3 (pp. 48-80) 7 10/20 Chapter 3 (Cont.) 8 10/27 Chapter 4: Beginnings and endings Read Chapter 4 (pp. 81-94) 9 11/3 Midterm exam 10 11/10 Chapter 5: Drafting and Revising Read Chapter 5 (pp. 95-128) 11 11/17 Peer review session 1: Content 12 11/24 Chapter 6: Effective sentence Read Chapter 6 (pp. 129-157) 13 12/1 Chapter 6 (Cont.) 14 12/8 Chapter 7: Word logic Read Chapter 7 (pp. 158-181) 15 12/15 Peer review session 2: Language 16 12/22 Final exam
