docs.text: 國立清華大學清華學院國際學士班課程大綱【甲組-華語與專業學科】 科號 Course Number 教 101 中文名稱 Course Title <生命教育> 英文名稱 Course English Title < Life Education> 任課教師 Instructor 陳淑娟 顏秀芬 上課時間 Time 週三 13:20-15:10 一、課程之教學目標 從全人教育的人與自己、人與他人、人與環境、人與宇宙四個面向，為此生命教育課程架構。 期能達成 1. 增進對於個人生命的探索、認識與價值的重視。 2. 立志效學典範、楷定生命方向、探索生命意義。 3. 提升學習者主動關懷周遭生命、建立良好人際關係,涵養積極因應未來生活挑戰之態度。 4. 透由實踐利他的服務過程，創造生命價值，對生命充滿希望與熱誠。 5. 透由正念的練習, 開展平靜、安定、專注、善良、感恩的心，提升專注力與情緒管理。 二、教學方法 教師講述、影片教學、分組討論、分組報告 三、教學進度 周次 日期 課程名稱 備註 1 9/9 總說: 耶魯大學關於快樂的研究 課綱程與評量 課程與評量 發幸福存摺 2 9/16 正念簡介、覺知呼吸、身體掃描 課程核心: 活在當下(專注力與覺察力) 3 9/23 感恩心是幸福的籌碼 課程核心:幫助他人+感恩 前測 4 9/30 感恩禮讚 課程核心:幫助他人+感恩 感恩小測驗 5 10/7 科技的的真相 - 網路電子科技可以帶給我們快樂嗎? 課程核心:與人社交 6 10/14 吃葡萄乾+身心出走、留白的幸福、打開五感– 沒有網路 電子科技 我快樂嗎? 課程核心: 活在當下+感恩 7 10/21 我的生命故事 – 高蘭欣學姊/陳淑娟老師 課程核心: 活在當下+感恩 8 10/28 期中報告：感恩禮讚 課程核心: 活在當下+感恩+幫助他人+與人社交 交幸福存摺、我想認識你 9 11/04 正念溝通 課程核心: 活在當下(專注力與覺察力)+與人社交 10 10/11 運動會 11 11/18 正念聆聽 (非暴力溝通) 課程核心: 活在當下(專注力與覺察力)+與人社交 12 11/25 壓力的因應：有覺察地回應 VS 慣性反應 課程核心: 活在當下+與人社交 13 12/2 復原力+尋找資源 課程核心: 活在當下(專注力與覺察力)+與人社交+感恩 14 12/9 如何面對比較忌妒與批評 課程核心: 活在當下(專注力與覺察力)+與人社交+感恩 15 12/16 課程總結、分享與提問 後測/製作總結表單 16 12/23 期末報告：讓自己幸福快樂的三個方法: 我的實踐與分享 課程核心: 活在當下+與人社交+感恩+幫助別人 評量： 一、平時成績: 25% 1. 出席 15% (缺席一次，每次扣學期總成績 1 分) 2. 課程參與度 10% (老師評量 5%+同學自評 5%) 二、口頭報告 : 40 % 1. 期中報告 (感恩禮讚) 20% 2. 期末報告 (讓自己幸福快樂的三個方法: 我的實踐與分享) 25 % 三 、平常作業: 35% 1. 我想認識你 10% (10/21 繳交) 課程核心: 活在當下+與人社交+感恩+幫助別人 2. 幸福快樂 111 10% ( 10/21 繳交) 課程核心: 活在當下+與人社交+感恩+幫助別人 3. 期末學習心得 10% (12/15 繳交) 四 、加分 (1) 整學期都出席 加總分 2% (2) 遵守手機使用規範 加總分 2% 手機規範：上課請將手機收在包包，若有緊急事件要用手機聯絡，請同學至教室外使用手機，用 完再回教室上課。 四、參考資料 五、成績考核 教學評量： 一、平時成績: 25% 1. 出席 15% (缺席一次，每次扣學期總成績 1 分) 2. 課程參與度 10% (老師評量 5%+同學自評 5%) 二、口頭報告 : 45 % 1. 期中報告(感恩禮讚) 20% 2. 期末報告 (讓自己幸福快樂的三個方法: 我的實踐與分享) 25 % 三 、平常作業: 30% 1. 我想認識你 10% 2. 幸福快樂 111 10% 3. 期末學習心得回饋 10% 四、加分 (1) 整學期都出席 加總分 2% (2) 遵守手機使用規範 加總分 2% 作業說明: (一) 期中報告: 20% 形式：透過多媒體方式呈現 報告時間：每人 10-12 分鐘 【感恩禮讚】報告個人這學期做的一件令父母歡喜的事情或者訪問父母的生命故事。 (二) 期末報告: 25% 形式：透過多媒體方式呈現並繳交實踐紀錄 報告時間：每人 10-12 分鐘 【讓自己幸福快樂的三個方法: 我的實踐與分享】 (1) 每天主動與一人互動(必選) (2) 減少使用手機/社群媒體(必選) (3) 自訂讓自己幸福快樂的方法 (三) 平常作業: 30% 【幸福快樂 111】發送幸福存摺，每天記錄 1 件自己的善行+1 件感恩的事+1 件別人的優點， 連續四周。 10% (期中考前繳交) 【我想認識你】認識全班同學及五位台灣學生(記下名字+學號+系級)，各訪問他們 3 個深度問 題，並簡要記下他們的回答，請從以下三個問題中挑選 1-2 個，其他問題可自行提問 如: (1)在你告別式上，你希望別人怎麼懷念你? (2)你生命中曾經遇過的重大挫折或失敗，你是 如何面對及克服的? (3)您覺得生命中最值得追求的是甚麼? 為什麼? (健康、財富、地位、自 由 、家庭/人際關係 快樂….) 10% ( 11/25 繳交) 【期末學習心得回饋】:我這學期的學習成果總結 10% (12/08 繳交) 加分 1. 整學期都出席 加總分 2% 2. 遵守手機使用規範 加分 2% 使用 AI 聲明選項 有條件開放: 本課程「期中個人感恩實踐報告」和「讓自己幸福快樂的三個方法: 我的實踐與分享」及「期末學 習心得回饋」，禁止使用生成式 AI 工具進行撰寫。 其他平時作業學生可在透明與負責任的原則下，適度使用 AI 工具進行課業協作。但學生應在課堂作業或報告 的標題頁註腳或引用文獻後，說明如何使用生成式 AI 進行議題發想、文句潤飾或結構參考等內容。 如經查核未標註 AI 工具的使用情況，教師或學校有權重新評分或不予計分。

docs.name: 國際禮儀與跨國溝通
docs.text: 1 National Tsing Hua University (NTHU) Course Title: International Etiquette and Cross-Cultural Communication Course Description: 1. This course is primarily initiated to help NTHU students acquire knowledge and understanding of international etiquette in terms of its norms and practices. 2. Major teaching emphasis will be developing "2Cs": Culture & Career. Culturally speaking, students will be taught to create a basic global perspective & cross-cultural sensitivity, and, on the career front, to familiarize themselves with tips on job interviews & international business meetings /travels. 3. In addition to lectures/discussions, videos & field trips will be introduced, depending on availability, to enable students to learn in a fun & friendly environment. Teaching Objectives: To help students possess top-notch manners & social skills, which come from quality etiquette guidance and will make them stand out from any peers personally & professionally. Teaching Syllabus: 1. Basic etiquette in clothing, Food, Housing, Transportation, Education & Entertainment. 2. The difference and competition between Western Christian civilization and Eastern Buddhist culture. 3. Etiquette models of Asian and Western countries. 4. Survival tips for job interviews. 5. Cultivation and practice of Sense of Humor. 6. Etiquette in the international business world. Teaching Methods: Lecture, Discussions, Appreciation, Simulation, Visit Evaluation: Study Assignments (20%), Class Attendance and Discussions (including in classroom and online) (40%), Individual Reports (including oral and written) (20%) and Group Reports (20%). docs.text: 國立清華大學清華學院國際學士班課程大綱 科號 Course Number 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Size of Limit 30 中文名稱 Course Title 大學生活規劃與設計 英文名稱 Course English Title College Life Planning and Design 任課教師 Instructor 林佩錡 Lin, Pei-chih 上課時間 Time 上課教室 Room 提醒您：請遵守智慧財產權，勿使用非法影印教科書 Please respect the intellectual property rights, do not use illegal copies of textbooks. 使用 AI 聲明：有條件開放 AI Usage Declaration: Conditional Use Permitted 課程簡述 (Brief course description) 課程簡述 這門課會帶領學生使用「設計思考」的方法，來探索並改善自己的大學生活。學生會先了解自己的 學習和生活需求，然後一起討論在校園生活中遇到的挑戰和機會。課程中會有小組討論、拼圖式閱 讀活動、校園導覽和來賓演講，幫助學生認識資源並制定可行的計畫。最後，學生會完成一個小組 專題，設計並展示自己理想的大學生活圖像，使用像是「美好時光日記」和「人生旅程計畫」等工 具。這門課強調自我反思、合作學習，以及把知識和技能應用在真實生活中。 學習目標 修完這門課後，學生將能夠： 1. 使用設計思考的方法，了解自己的學習和生活需求。 2. 使用設計思考工具（例如：美好時光日記、人生旅程計畫），規劃個人化的大學生活。 3. 了解校園資源，並說明如何有效使用這些資源來幫助學習和生活。 4. 在多元小組中一起想出解決方法，並透過圖像和口頭報告來評估成果。 5. 透過作業和同儕回饋等活動，反思自己的成長和學習成果。 注意事項  本課程使用 Zuvio 平台進行簽到、課堂活動、小測驗和作業繳交。請記得定期登入，完成相 關任務。  如果需要請假，請使用「學生請假系統」。  所有學生在使用 AI 工具時，必須遵守 GenAI 使用規範（等級 0–3）。如果違規，該次作業 將以零分計算。 選課前須知  請一定要參加第一週的課程，老師會說明課程的重點、進度和成績計算方式。  不管你第一週有沒有正式加選這門課，如果第一週沒有來上課，會影響你的出席、參與和作業 成績。 指定閱讀  比爾‧柏內特, 戴夫‧埃文斯（2016）。 做自己的生命設計師：史丹佛最夯的生涯規畫課，用 「設計思考」重擬問題，打造全新生命藍圖。大塊文化。  艾琳．路佩登（2017）。 圖解設計故事學：好設計，觸發愉悅、渴望、驚喜和信任感！用講故 事的技術，把設計思考作成一部好劇本。商周出版。 評分方式（以開學第一堂課公告為主） 出席率， 課堂參與+小考， 作業， 期中討論， 期末報告， *分數配比可能會因學生學習狀 況而整體調整 課程進度表（以開學第一堂課公告為主） 週次 主題 作業／備註 1 認識彼此 2 人生羅盤 3 AI的使用與影響 4 時間與精力管理 作業：好時光日誌 5 發掘問題 作業：看見校園中的問題 6 心智圖與原型 7 訪談目的與技巧 8 身心健康與壓力調適 9 自我探索(奧德賽、原型) 10 設計人生(期中小組檢視) 11 探索校園 12 對失敗免疫 13 設計夢幻工作 14 選擇幸福 15 期末成果分享 16 人生影展 作業：寫給「未來的自己」 作業：「新生的建議信」 *課程進度可能因實際狀況調整，例如外部講師時間配合 課程關鍵字：大學適應,設計思考,職涯發展,生涯規劃,學習適應

Students will begin by understanding their personal learning and living needs, then collaboratively identify challenges and opportunities in their campus experience. Through team-based and problem-based learning, students will engage in activities such as group discussions, Jigsaw reading, campus tours, and guest lectures to explore resources and develop actionable plans. The course culminates in a final group project where students design and exhibit a visual representation of their ideal university life, using tools like the Good Time Journal and Odyssey Plan. This course emphasizes self-reflection, collaboration, and real-world application of knowledge and skills. Learning Objectives By the end of this course, students will be able to: 1. Identify personal learning and living needs by applying design thinking frameworks. 2. Apply design thinking tools (e.g., Good Time Journal, Odyssey Plan) to develop a personalized university life plan. 3. Understand campus resources and explain how to use them effectively for academic and personal development. 4. Create solutions collaboratively in diverse teams and evaluate them through visual and oral presentations. 5. Evaluate personal growth and learning through structured reflection activities such as assignments and peer feedback. Note: 1. This course uses the Zuvio platform for check-ins, in-class activities, quizzes, and submitting assignments. Please remember to log in regularly to complete tasks. 2. docs.text: Forms in Nature I. Abstract This course explores the rich and varied forms found in nature, alongside the mathematical and physical ideas that illuminate them. We begin with the repeated patterns in space, structures, and crystals. From there, we investigate archetypal patterns including symmetry, waves, spirals, fractals, and music, the repeated patterns in time. Each topic is paired with hands-on activities, enabling students to experience the intersection of beauty and science through direct engagement with the natural world. II. Introduction Our journey begins by investigating natural forms—from the geometric order of crystals to the spirals found in shells and galaxies. Alongside these visual and structural patterns, we study the mathematical and physical frameworks that reveal their underlying logic: crystallography, Fourier analysis, and fractal geometry. The course emphasizes experiential learning, integrating artistic practice with scientific exploration. Activities such as pendulum drawing, modeling celestial motion, making “flowers” of music highlight the unity between nature, mathematics, and art. III. References The references are listed as below 1. What Is Mathematics? An Elementary Approach to Ideas and Methods 2nd Edition ISBN-10 0195105192 2. Understanding Physics, Cassidy, Holton, and Rutherford, ISBN 1-4757-7698-5 (e-book) 3. Geometry of Grief: Reflections on Mathematics, Loss, and Life, Michael Frame (2021), ISBN-10 022680092X IV. Syllabus Week 1: Introduction and Overview (9/7) Overview of the course Syllabus and evaluation What we are going to do? Week 2: Symmetry (9/14) Reflection Translation, glide Rotation Hands-on activity: Identifying symmetry groups Week 3: Crystals (9/21) Crystals patterns: cubes, honeycomb Unit cell, lattice structures Hands-on activity: Drawing and Making crystals Week 4: Holiday: Teacher’s Day (9/28) Week 5: Inversion (10/5) Crystallography and diffraction Fourier transformation Symmetry modeling and crystal patterns Hands-on activity: Drawing Diffractions Week 6: Fractals (10/12) Koch curve, Sierpinski triangle, Cantor cubes Natural fractals: ferns, trees, lightning Fractal dimension: concept and examples Hands-on activity: Drawing fractals and estimate dimension Week 7: Spirals (10/19) Logarithmic spirals Shells, galaxies, whirlpools, pinecones Hands-on activity: Drawing Spirals Week 8: Holliday (10/26) Week 9: Mid-term examination (11/2) Week 10: Fibonacci and Phyllotaxis (11/9) Fibonacci sequence Golden spirals Sun flowers, Pinecone Hands-on activity: Finding Fibonacci in pinecone Week 11: Fractals in Time: Music (11/16) Waves, frequency and wavelength twelve-tone equal temperament Hands-on activity: Making Pan flutes Week 12: Campus Tour (11/23) Looking for natural forms: leaves, veins, branches, spirals Self-similarity in nature Hands-on activity: Drawing and analyzing forms Week 13: Music as Forms (11/30) Vine of music Music of trees Music of flowers Hands-on activity: Making flowers of music Week 14: Rhythm and Waves (12/7) Pendulum and Coriolis forces Hands-on activity: Pendulum drawing Hands-on activity: Making trees of music Week 15: Wave-like Structures (12/14) Zebra stripes, fish patterns, sand dunes Moire pattern and Turing pattern Self-organization and emergence Hands-on activity: Drawing fractals Week 16: Final Examination and Course Reflection (12/21) V. Evaluation 1. Initial attendance: 4% Students who want to take this course are required to attend for the first two weeks. 2. Participation (Week 3-16 except Week 4, 8, 9, 16): 10% 3. Midterm Examination: 25% 4. Final Examination: 25% 5. Hand-on activities: 36% Students are required to participate in the hands-on activities or in-class activities, and write reports afterwards. 6. An A+ indicates that the students achieve all goals beyond expectation. Students with two unexcused absences will not receive a grade of A+. VI. Grading Policy for Attendance This policy is designed to promote fairness, responsibility, and clarity throughout the semester. Attendance and participation are essential to the course experience. For consistency, attendance is graded separately from hands-on activities and presentations. Unexcused absences will strictly result in a score of zero for all missed components, with no make-up opportunities allowed. For the students with approved excused absences (valid documentation provided), all late submissions and make-up assessments (including questions for today, discussion on eLearn, and hands-on activity reports) will be strictly capped and graded at 70% of the original score. 1. Initial Attendance (Week 1-2) (4%) The first two weeks are for orientation and course adjustment. 1. Each week counts for 2% of the final grade. 2. Absence results in zero attendance points, regardless of whether or not you are officially registered. 2. Regular Weeks (Week 3-16 except Week 4, 8, 9, and 16; Total 10%) 1. Attendance counts for 0.4% of the final grade each week. 2. Weekly coursework consists of “questions for today” (0.3%) and “discussion on eLearn” (0.3%), which together count for 0.6% of the final grade each week. 3. Unexcused absences will result in a score of zero for attendance (0.4%), questions for today (0.3%), discussion on eLearn (0.3%), and hands-on activities conducted that week. 4. Students with excused absences (valid documentation for illness, bereavement, or official leave) are eligible to submit “questions for today”, “discussion on eLearn”, and the corresponding reports or assignments for the hands-on activities on time. However, these submissions will be capped or graded at 70% of the original score. 3. Examination (Midterm 25%, Final 25%) 1. Absence from any exam results in a score of zero. 2. Students with an excused absence (valid documentation for illness, bereavement, or official leave) may request a make-up exam. 3. To ensure academic integrity, all make-up exams will be capped at 70% of the original score. 4. It is the student’s responsibility to contact the TA in advance to schedule the make-up exam. VII. The use of AI is conditionally open. You may use AI to check the grammar of your reports, but NOT for writing or generating articles. VIII. The content above may be subject to change based on actual circumstances. Updated information will be announced in class or on e-Learn.

docs.text: Programming Implementation Lab Hands-on Companion Lab for Introduction to Programming I (IBP 105100) (Fall 2026) Instructor: Carlos Argueta Contact info: Classroom: Class time: Wednesday 12:10-15:10 Course Purpose This practical lab accompanies the formal Introduction to Programming I course. It was created to ensure that students develop genuine, independent coding ability rather than relying on AI-generated solutions. Each session mirrors the topic taught in the regular course and consists of a brief live-coding demonstration followed by progressively challenging programming exercises completed during class. Students learn to write code by hand, read error messages, test systematically, and debug using their own knowledge. AI may be used only when the instructor explicitly permits it and only as a support tool after an independent attempt; students must always be able to explain, modify, and debug their own code. Course Objectives A. Build independent programming fluency: By the end of this lab, students will be able to 1. Write small Python programs from a blank file without copying AI-generated code. 2. Translate a problem statement into variables, expressions, control flow, functions, and data structures. 3. Develop solutions incrementally and verify them with meaningful test cases. B. Strengthen debugging and problem-solving skills: By the end of this lab, students will be able to 1. Read tracebacks and distinguish syntax, runtime, and logic errors. 2. Use tracing, print-based inspection, assertions, and small test cases to locate defects. 3. Explain why a program works and revise it when requirements change. C. Use AI responsibly without losing core skills: By the end of this lab, students will be able to 1. Attempt and document a solution independently before consulting AI or other references. 2. Evaluate AI suggestions critically instead of accepting generated code without verification. 3. Use programming knowledge to test, debug, and improve code suggested by tools. Course Materials and Tools 1. Python 3, a text editor or IDE, terminal access, and the course online judge or submission system. 2. Instructor-provided task sheets, starter files when appropriate, and selected Python documentation. Course Requirements and Grading Weekly in-class coding performance 60% Practical coding checkpoint 1 15% Practical coding checkpoint 2 15% Final supervised implementation 10% Independent coding and explanation are required in every session. No take-home homework is assigned; all graded work is completed during class. Unauthorized AI-generated solutions receive no credit for the affected task. Course Schedule Week Topic Object ives In-Class Mini-Programs Week 1 Introduction to Programming & Environment Setup AB 1. Hello, Lab! - Create and run a Python program that prints a personalized welcome message. 2. Profile Card - Store basic personal information in variables and display it in a neatly formatted block. 3. Command-Line Calculator - Read two numbers and print their sum, difference, product, and quotient. 4. Unit Converter Starter - Convert a user- entered distance between kilometers and miles. 5. Broken Setup Rescue - Diagnose and repair a short program containing path, indentation, and syntax mistakes. Week 2 Data Types, Variables, and Memory Concepts AB 1. Variable Type Explorer - Create values of several Python types and report each value and its type. 2. Shopping Receipt - Calculate subtotal, tax, and final price from item price and quantity. 3. Time Breakdown - Convert a number of seconds into hours, minutes, and remaining seconds. 4. Digit Analyzer - Extract and report the digits of a three-digit integer using arithmetic. 5. Value Swap and Trace - Swap two variables without losing data and explain each value change step by step. Week 3 Conditional Statements & Control Flow AB 1. Positive, Negative, or Zero - Classify an entered number using a basic if-elif-else structure. 2. Letter Grade Converter - Convert a numeric score into an A-F letter grade using ordered conditions. 3. Ticket Price Calculator - Determine admission price from age, student status, and discount rules. 4. Triangle Classifier - Validate three side lengths and classify the triangle as equilateral, isosceles, or scalene. 5. Progressive Tax Estimator - Calculate tax using multiple income brackets and explain which conditions were applied. Week 4 Loop Structures & Control AB 1. Countdown Timer - Use a while loop to count down from a user-selected number. 2. Multiplication Table - Use a for loop to print the multiplication table for an entered integer. 3. Sentinel Sum - Repeatedly accept numbers and calculate the total until the user enters a stop value. 4. Menu-Driven Assistant - Display a repeating menu, perform the selected action, and exit only when Quit is chosen. 5. Number Guessing Game - Implement a bounded guessing game with hints, attempt counting, and input validation. Week 5 Functions & Variable Scope ABC 1. Temperature Converter - Write reusable functions to convert between Celsius and Fahrenheit. 2. Geometry Toolkit - Create separate functions for the area and perimeter of common shapes. 3. Password Strength Checker - Build a function that returns a strength category based on several password rules. 4. Statistics Helper - Write functions that calculate minimum, maximum, mean, and range without built-in shortcuts. 5. Scoped Bank Account - Use parameters, return values, and carefully controlled state to simulate deposits and withdrawals. Week 6 Sequences & Mappings AB 1. List Score Summary - Store scores in a list and report count, minimum, maximum, and average. 2. Unique Word Collector - Use a set to find distinct words entered by the user. 3. Phone Book Dictionary - Add, search, update, and remove contacts in a dictionary. 4. Inventory Counter - Count repeated product names and display quantities using a mapping. 5. Student Record Manager - Maintain nested student records and produce a sorted summary by average score. Week 7 Practical Coding Checkpoint 1 ABC 1. Foundations Sprint - Complete a short variables and arithmetic problem from a blank file. 2. Decision Challenge - Implement a multi- branch business rule using conditionals. 3. Loop Debugging Trial - Repair and complete a loop-based program with a hidden logic error. 4. Function Construction - Design and test a function that satisfies a given input-output specification. 5. Collection Integration - Solve a small problem that combines lists or dictionaries with control flow. Week 8 String Manipulation & Regular Expressions AB 1. Text Statistics - Count characters, words, spaces, vowels, and digits in a line of text. 2. Palindrome Inspector - Normalize a phrase and determine whether it is a palindrome. 3. Username Generator - Create valid usernames from names while enforcing formatting rules. 4. Email Pattern Validator - Use a regular expression to check whether input resembles a valid email address. 5. Log Line Parser - Extract date, level, source, and message fields from structured log lines using regex groups. Week 9 Recursion & Divide and Conquer AB 1. Recursive Countdown - Print a countdown using a recursive function and a clear base case. 2. Factorial by Recursion - Compute factorial recursively and reject invalid inputs. 3. Recursive Digit Sum - Find the sum of an integer’s digits without loops. 4. Binary Search - Implement recursive binary search on a sorted list and trace each search interval. 5. Nested List Total - Recursively calculate the sum of values stored in arbitrarily nested lists. Week 10 File I/O & Exception Handling ABC 1. File Line Counter - Read a text file and report its number of lines, words, and characters. 2. Safe Number Reader - Handle invalid numeric input with try-except and repeat until valid data is entered. 3. Grade File Processor - Read scores from a file, skip malformed rows, and write a summary report. 4. CSV Expense Analyzer - Parse an expense file and calculate totals by category with useful error messages. 5. Resilient File Copier - Copy a file while handling missing files, permission errors, and safe resource cleanup. Week 11 Modules, Packages, and Python Standard ABC 1. Random Password Maker - Use the random and string modules to generate passwords Library under selected rules. 2. Calendar Reporter - Use datetime and calendar to display useful information about a chosen date. 3. Statistics Module Comparison - Compare manually computed statistics with results from Python’s statistics module. 4. Reusable Utility Module - Move related functions into a custom module and import them into a main program. 5. Command-Line Package Tool - Organize a small multi-file program as a package with a clear entry point. Week 12 Object-Oriented Programming I AB 1. Rectangle Class - Create a class with attributes and methods for area, perimeter, and display. 2. BankAccount Class - Model deposits, withdrawals, and balance checks with validation. 3. Student Class - Store student data and calculate a grade average through instance methods. 4. Library Book Tracker - Represent books and their loan status using multiple interacting objects. 5. Shopping Cart Model - Build Product and Cart classes that calculate totals and manage item quantities. Week 13 Object-Oriented Programming II ABC 1. Shape Inheritance - Create a base Shape class and specialized subclasses with overridden area methods. 2. Employee Payroll - Use inheritance to calculate pay differently for salaried and hourly employees. 3. Comparable Products - Implement an operator overload that compares products by price or rating. 4. Polymorphic Notification System - Send messages through several notification subclasses using one common interface. 5. Mini Role-Playing Battle - Design interacting character classes with inheritance, encapsulation, and polymorphic actions. Week 14 Scientific Computing & Visualization AB 1. Array Arithmetic - Use NumPy arrays to perform vectorized calculations on a small dataset. 2. Temperature Data Summary - Load measurements and compute descriptive statistics with NumPy. 3. Function Plotter - Plot a mathematical function over a selected interval with labeled axes. 4. Survey Bar Chart - Convert category counts into a clear bar chart and interpret the result. 5. Data Cleaning Dashboard - Clean a small numeric dataset and create two appropriate visual summaries. Week 15 Practical Coding Checkpoint 2 ABC 1. String and Regex Sprint - Transform text and extract required patterns under time limits. 2. Recursive Reasoning - Complete or repair a recursive function and identify its base and recursive cases. 3. Robust File Processor - Read imperfect data, handle exceptions, and produce a correct output file. 4. Module and OOP Build - Create a small multi-file object-oriented solution from a specification. 5. Debug-and-Explain Challenge - Diagnose an unfamiliar program, repair it, and verbally justify each correction. Week 16 Final Project Implementation ABC 1. Requirements Breakdown - Convert the final program specification into inputs, outputs, functions, classes, and test cases. 2. Minimum Viable Program - Implement the smallest complete working version before adding optional features. 3. Feature Integration - Combine control flow, data structures, functions, files, or classes into one coherent program. 4. Testing and Debugging Pass - Create edge cases, repair defects, and document the evidence that the program works. 5. Live Modification Demo - Demonstrate the program and implement a small instructor- requested change without AI assistance. Weekly In-Class Coding Performance 60% Most instructional sessions include five mini-programs arranged from introductory to more challenging. Students submit working code before the end of class. Credit is based on correctness, completion, code clarity, testing, and the ability to explain or debug the submitted solution. Practical Coding Checkpoint 1 15% A supervised, no-AI assessment covering foundational Python, variables, conditionals, loops, functions, and basic collections. Students solve several short programs during the scheduled session. Practical Coding Checkpoint 2 15% A supervised, no-AI assessment covering strings, regular expressions, recursion, files, exceptions, modules, and object-oriented programming. Final Supervised Implementation 10% Students complete and demonstrate a small integrated program during class. The instructor may ask students to explain design choices, modify requirements, or debug a deliberately introduced error. AI and Academic Integrity Policy Unless the instructor explicitly authorizes AI for a specific activity, students may not use generative AI, code-completion agents, or AI-produced solutions during graded lab work. Permitted Support Students may use their own notes, instructor examples, official documentation, and non-AI debugging tools as announced for each session. Required Demonstration of Understanding 1. Students must be able to explain their code, predict its behavior, create test cases, and repair errors without relying on AI. 2. Code that a student cannot explain or modify may be treated as non-original work and may receive reduced or no credit. Attendance and Make-up Work Because grading occurs during each lab session, attendance is essential. Make-up work is available only according to the institution’s approved absence policy.

docs.text: First-Year Exploration Course First Year Seminar: Exploratory Studies Fall 2026 Instructor: Carlos Argueta Contact info: kid.a.rgueta@gmail.com Classroom: Delta Building 102 Class time: Tuesday 13:20-15:10 Course Purpose This course is designed to help first-year students at National Tsing Hua University make a smooth academic and personal transition from their previous schools to NTHU. By encouraging participation in university coursework and extracurricular life, the course aims to foster a sense of belonging to the university, help students develop and apply critical- thinking skills to adjust successfully to campus life, and support them in discovering purpose, meaning, and direction in life. Course Learning Objectives A. Support Academic Success: Through this course, students will be able to 1. Apply appropriate strategies to adjust their approaches to coursework and learning. 2. Use effective time-management methods. 3. Become familiar with flexible academic pathways relevant to their studies. B. Understand and Connect with NTHU: Through this course, students will be able to 1. Use appropriate campus resources and participate in opportunities that support learning inside and outside the classroom. 2. Build positive relationships with classmates, faculty members, and administrative staff. 3. Understand the history and traditions of National Tsing Hua University. C. Promote Personal Development, Well-Being, and Social Responsibility: Through this course, students will be able to 1. Develop their own values and identities; understand how these values and identities shape their perspectives; and build relationships with people who hold similar or different viewpoints. 2. Develop strategies that promote health and understand how physical and mental well-being affect academic and personal success. 3. Plan their own careers and gain an understanding of possible future career directions. Course Reading Materials 1. Freshman Orientation Camp Handbook, Office of Student Affairs 2. It Is Good to Stay Just the Way You Are (Hidehiro Inagaki, 2024/10/09) Course Requirements and Grading Class Participation and Discussion 15% Faculty Visit and Reflection Paper 10% Campus Activity Chi-Ying Chang of the Center for General Education and teaching assistants Week 11 Interpersonal Relationships and Multiculturalis m C Relationships with classmates/roommates, intimate relationships, docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 11510IBP 201400 組別 學分 2 人數限制 40 上課時間 M3M4 教室 教育館 115 科目中文名稱 中華文化概論 科目英文名稱 Introduction to Chinese Culture 任課教師 游騰達 一、課程說明 (一) 課程宗旨 本課程旨在經由老師的帶領，引導學生認識中國歷史發展的進程，以及掌握中 華文化之特色與精神內涵。 (二) 課程目標 1、認識中國的歷史，以及歷朝各代的文化特點。 2、學習閱讀短篇教材（講義）。 3、認識古代中華文化對當代華人社會與文化的影響與意義。 二、指定用書 教師自編講義 三、參考書籍 (一) 中國文化史 王仲孚：《中國文化史》，臺北：五南圖書出版公司，2009 年。 王若葉：《用年表讀通中國文化史》，臺北：商周出版社，2019 年。 余秋雨：《中國文化課》，北京：中國青年出版社，2019 年。 甘懷真，簡杏如等編：《中國文化史（全）》，臺北：三民書局出版公司， 2016 年。 李貴豐編：《中國文化史》，臺北：中華電視出版股份有限公司，2015 年。 葛兆光：《古代中國文化講義》，臺北：三民書局出版公司，2005 年。 杜正勝主編：《中國文化史》，臺北：三民書局出版公司，2006 年。 吳方：《圖說中國文化史》，北京：生活‧讀書‧新知三聯書店‧2019 年。 許倬雲：《中國人的精神生活》，新北：聯經出版社，2017 年。 許倬雲：《萬古江河：中國歷史文化的轉折與展開》，臺北：英文漢聲出版 公司，2006 年。 華林甫主編：《中華文明地圖》，北京：中國地圖出版社，2018 年。 張崑將等編：《中國文化史》，臺北：五南圖書出版公司，2006 年。 錢穆：《中國文化史導論》，臺北：臺灣商務印書館出版公司，2013 年。 孫機：《中國古代物質文化》，臺北：華品文創出版公司，2017 年。 (二) 華人社會與文化 何修仁：《華人社會與文化》，臺北：新學林出版公司，2013 年。 黃苕冠：《華人社會與文化講義》，臺北：新學林出版公司，2009 年。 方麗娜：《華人社會與文化》，臺北：正中書局出版公司，2009 年。 賴明德、何淑貞、丁原基、林振興：《華人社會與文化》，臺北：文鶴出版 公司，2009 年。 劉國平：《華人社會與文化——文化思想篇》，臺北：新學林出版公司， 2016 年。 陳雅芳：《華人社會與文化》，臺北：五南圖書出版公司，2019 年。 (三) 其他 邢義田：《立體的歷史：從圖像看古代中國與域外文化》，臺北：三民書 局，2016 年。 佟洵、王雲松主編：《看得到的中國史》，臺北：大是文化，2019 年。 林柏亭主編：《大觀：北宋汝窯特展》，臺北：故宮博物院，2007 年。 上海博物館編：《幽藍神采：元代靑花瓷器特集》，上海：上海書畫出版 社，2012 年。 童文娥主編：《繪苑璚瑤─清院本清明上河圖》，臺北：故宮博物院，2010 年。 那志良：《清明上河圖》，臺北：故宮博物院，1993 年。 四、教學方式 1、主題式課程講授、 2、「素養導向」教學法 3、分組報告、 4、自主學習 五、教學進度 週 次 課 程 內 容 備註 第 1 週 09/07 課程說明 第 2 週 09/14 中國文化起源與傳說時代：堯舜、夏、商 第 3 週 09/21 百家爭鳴的時代：周（西周、東周-春秋、戰國） 第 4 週 09/28 教師節（停課一次） 第 5 週 10/05 秦漢帝國的生活與信仰：秦、兩漢 第 6 週 10/12 魏晉的玄學與玄風：魏晉南北朝 第 7 週 10/19 唐代的士風與多民族世界：隋、唐 第 8 週 10/26 光復節（補假‧停課一次） 第 9 週 11/02 期中考 第 10 週 11/09 文藝美學與個性伸展：宋(1) 第 11 週 11/16 文藝美學與個性伸展：宋(2) 第 12 週 11/23 征服王朝與文化碰撞：元 第 13 週 11/30 城市發展與庶民文化：明(1) 第 14 週 12/07 城市發展與庶民文化：明(2) 第 15 週 12/14 近世中國的國際世界：清 第 16 週 12/21 期末考 六、成績考核 1、課堂參與 20％：出席率 2、書面作業 30％：作業 (1) [日常中的文化風景] 15％ 作業 (2) [報告] 15％ 3、期中測驗 20％：紙筆測驗 4、期末測驗 30％：紙筆測驗 七、備註 有條件開放 AI 協作、共學，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出

docs.text: 科號 Course Number 11510IBP 201701／11510IBP 201702 中⽂名稱 Course Title 聽⼒與⼜說（⼆） 英⽂名稱 Course English Title Listening and Speaking II 任課教師 Instructor 李羿妏 上課時間 Time T7T8／R7R8 上課教室 Classroom 教102 課程簡述 Brief Course Description 本課程以已具備中⾼級華語能⼒之學⽣為對象，約相當於 CEFR B2 程度。課程⽬標在於 培養學⽣在⼤學、⽣活、社會與跨⽂化情境中進⾏有效聽解與⼜語表達的能⼒。課程內容 將結合教師⾃編教材、華語教材選⽂、新聞影⾳、訪談、短講、圖表與真實語料，訓練學 ⽣聽懂較長篇幅的⼜語材料，掌握主旨、細節、⽴場與語氣，並能進⾏摘要、敘事、討 論、評論、訪談、協商、辯論與⼜頭發表。 指定⽤書 Textbooks ⾃編講義 教學⽅式 Teaching Methods 教師講授、⼩組討論、個別練習、任務型教學 教學進度 Course Schedule （依教學需要可能調整或修改） 週 內容 1 課程說明、聽⼒測驗（前測） 2-3 單元⼀：個⼈經驗 4-5 單元⼆：意⾒表達 6-7 單元三：新聞時事 8 期中考 9-10 單元四：資料解讀 11-12 單元五：問題分析 13-14 單元六：討論協商 15 聽⼒測驗（後測） 16 期末考 成績考核 Evaluation 出席與課堂參與 30% 需寫信給⽼師請假，缺席三次，出席分數為0分。 平時⼜說任務 30% 期中考 20% 期末⼜試 20% AI使⽤規則 AI Usage Policy 禁⽌在作業或練習中使⽤AI，如經發現學⽣使⽤⽣成式 AI，教師有權重新評分或不予計分。 115上 國立清華大學 清華學院國際學士班 課程大綱

docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱-大學部 科號 IEEM5311 必/選修 必修 組別 00 上課時間 W3W4F3 教室 104 人數限制 60 科目學分說明 總學分數 各專業所佔學分比例分配 (合計須為 3) 3 數學 基礎科學 工程專業 授課小時數 理論 設計 3/每週 1 0 2 0 科目中文名稱 機率論 科目英文名稱 Probability Theory 任課教師 陳雨欣 (Yu-Hsin Chen) 授課語言 □中文 ▓英文 檔修科目 建議先修 此科目對應之系 所核心能力(請勾 選並填入比例，比 例合計為 100%) Core capabilities to be cultivated by this course ▓ 工工專業與系統分析能力 IE profession and systems analysis skills 70% ▓ 獨立研究及解決問題的實作能力 Capability of independent research and problem solving 20% □ 領導、溝通與團隊合作能力 Leadership and coordination abilities % □ 自我充實能力 Capability of self-development and enrichment % ▓ 國際觀視野、國際化互動與表達能力 Global interaction and communication skills 10% 一、課程說明 This course introduces foundational concepts in probability and statistics with an emphasis on their practical application in industrial engineering. Students will develop a conceptual understanding of probabilistic models and statistical techniques, alongside hands-on experience in applying these methods to analyze real-world engineering problems. 請提供至少五個課程關鍵字：隨機變數(Random Variable), 期望值(Mathematical Expectation), 機率分配(Probability Distribution), 動差(Moments), 動差生成函數 (Moment-Generating Function) 二、指定用書 Walpole, R.E., Myers, R.H., Myers, S. L. and Ye, Keying (2016). Probability and Statistics For Engineers and Scientists. (9th edition). Global Edition, Pearson Education. 三、參考書籍 1. Johnson, R. A. (2011). Ch 3: Random Variables and Probability Distributions. Ch 4: Mathematical Expectations. Ch 5: Some Discrete Probability Distributions. Ch 6: Some Continuous Probability Distributions. Ch 7: Functions of Random Variables. docs.text: 2026/9 Page 1 of 4 IEEM2810 ENGINEERING ECONOMICS Syllabus, Fall 2026 (Lecture in English) INSTRUCTOR: Professor Amy J.C. Trappey, trappey@ie.nthu.edu.tw, 818 Engineering Building I. Office Hour: Monday morning and Wednesday afternoon or by appointment. TEACHING ASSISTANTS: TA office is in Lab-726 (Engineering Building I); Tel: 03-5715131 x33970 or x33961. TA office hours: Monday and Tuesday (10:00 ~ 14:30) or by appointments. CLASS SESSIONS: Mondays, 3:30-6:20 pm; on-campus lectures will be held in Lecture Room 107, Engineering Building I. Seating assignment will be announced. Lecture (Prof): 1~ 2 hrs; problem solving exercise (TA): 0.5 hr; and homework (self-exercise): 0.5 hr. COURSE OVERVIEW: In this course, we will learn the critical knowledge of engineering economics, e.g., interest rates, annuities, equivalent values, taxes, exchange rates, depreciation, investment risks, and the associating computing techniques for evaluating engineering projects and their alternative solutions. With the familiarity of these concepts and approaches, one can conduct engineering economic analyses and compare alternatives during the engineering decision making process. Specifically, students will learn fundamental models and methods (e.g., Present Worth, Future Worth, Annual Worth, Internal Rate of Return, and External Rate of Return) for engineering economic analyses. Both the deterministic analysis (Replacement Analysis, Benefit-Cost Ratio Analysis, Break-even Analysis Sensitivity Analysis) and the probabilistic analysis (Risk Analysis) will be covered in the lectures. COURSE OBJECTIVES: Students should clearly learn the definitions and methods of important economic concepts and be able to do the computational practices by hand and by software (e.g., EXCEL). Many engineering and financial problems will be introduced and practiced during the lecture sessions and also given as homework assignments. Students must understand all of the examples and complete your weekly homework assignments diligently on time. COURSE MATERIALS: Page 2 of 4  Textbook: William G. Sullivan, Elin M. Wicks, C. Patrick Koelling, Engineering Economy, the latest (international) edition, Pearson/Prentice Hall (17/18th Edition). GRADING WEIGHT (TOTAL 100 POINTS): Homework/assignments/class-participations 20 points; Midterm exam 40 points; Final exam 40 points. HOMEWORK POLICIES: - The due date of each homework will be ONE week (at 15:30 on Monday) after the homework assigned. - No late homework is accepted. Homework turned in late will not be graded and receive NO credit. LEARNING POLICIES/RULES: - The course emphasizes the cultivation and training of highly professional engineers with the highest ethical standard. All homework assignments must be done by your own efforts. Plagiarism and cheating on homework and exams are prohibited and, if found, can result in a no-passing grades. - Students should follow the course’s weekly schedule. Suggest reading the chapter prior Monday lecture. The homework assignments must be completed and uploaded to eeClass homework folder before the deadline (i.e., the following Monday before 15:30). EXAMS WILL BE HELD IN LECTURE ROOM 107: Midterm exam: 2026/11/2 Final exam: 2026/12/21 - You are allowed to bring an engineering calculator, a dictionary, and only one A4-size formula/notes sheet to the exams. - No mobile phones, laptops and other electronic devices are allowed in the exams. - Discussing/chatting during the exams is prohibited. - Seats will be assigned and announced at the exams. You must sit accordingly. docs.text: 國立清華大學簡禎富©2026 115 學年度第 1 學期 1 11510 IEEM439100 智慧製造專題 Special Topic for Smart Manufacturing 任課教授(Professor)： 簡禎富講座教授 (工程一館 922 室) E-Mail: cfchien@mx.nthu.edu.tw 盧映宇秘書：Tel: 03-5742648 / E-Mail: dalab@ie.nthu.edu.tw 助教(TA)： 上課時間：2026/9/7~2026/12/25 每週五 (Thursday) 13:20 ~ 16:20 上課教室：綜合四館 R223 室 清華臻鼎講堂 (全家便利店樓上) 一、課程說明 (Course Description) 本課程針對智慧製造重要議題和技術，每一學期選擇重要產業領域作為基礎，透過個案 研究、工廠參觀、業師演講、以及小組專題，讓大學部高年級學生系統系瞭解產業結構、製 造模式與智能化技術的實際應用，學習整合所學工業工程與管理知識和智慧製造產業用技術 的整合。舉例而言，若以印刷電路板產業為主軸，將透過實例和參觀介紹印刷電路板產業， 探討智慧製造的問題需求、技術工具與各種解決方案，透過業師經驗分享與產業實際案例， 作為一方面從印刷電路板價值鏈介紹生產過程各個階段的製程、設備和產業領域知識為基礎， 使學生知道如何應用技術和方法來提昇生產力、品質和彈性決策，以滿足智慧製造的需要； 另一方面，透過課堂講授內容和實務分享，引導小組專題研究，討論台灣各個產業智慧製造 的實務問題。 二、課程大綱(Agenda) 週次 日期 課程進度/內容 (暫定) 講 員 1 9/10 大數據技術及製造領域應用 吳家駒協理 2 9/17 產業分析研究方法 陳家樂經理 3 9/24 主題授課暨先豐工廠參觀 @觀音先豐廠 陳峯興資深協理 4 10/1 智慧製造趨勢與應用 束文龍協理 5 10/8 PCB 產品創新力 何明展協理 6 10/15 智慧供應鏈管理 范振璋資深經理 7 10/22 PCB 智能工廠智動化應用 黎進財協理 8 10/29 Mini LED 產品及智能製造介紹 徐耿璋資深經理 9 11/5 PCB 智慧製造(淺談過去與未來) 鄭建聰資深協理 10 11/12 FCBGA 載板的智能製造與未來展望 賴學翰資深經理 11 11/19 電路板產業在供應鏈價值與第三方機構的重要性 李明旺協理 12 11/26 PCB 領域先進製程知識介紹與發展(半導體產品) 陳貽和資深協理 13 12/3 車用 PCB 製程技術及車載應用 張喻/陳弘倫/黃志鵬 14 12/10 以研發為核心之小量產工廠 呂明錞經理 15 12/17 用精益規劃打造智能工廠 許再豐資深協理 16 12/24 解讀智慧製造 鄭建聰資深協理 三、作業 (Homework) 國立清華大學簡禎富©2026 115 學年度第 1 學期 2 分組作業，每組約 3 – 4 人，輪流於每週演講製作課程筆記和記錄，並提供完整書面報 告。 四、書籍及參考文獻 (Text Book and References) 指定用書：智慧工廠-迎戰資訊科技變革、工廠管理的轉型策略(經濟新潮社) 參考文獻：簡禎富、施義成、林振銘、陳瑞坤（2005），半導體製造技術與管理，清華大學 出版社。 五、成績考核 (Evaluation) 作業：PCB 製程單元記錄與完整書面報告(分組/含同學互評成績) 30% 期中專題個人 ppt 報告：近五年 PCB 論文 35% 期末專題分組：PCB 智慧製造專題報告 35% 課程出席與參與(抽點個人論文口頭報告) extra 10% 六、課程網頁資源(Resources) 1. 個案參考論文及講義等相關資料下載：http://DALab.ie.nthu.edu.tw 2. 紫式決策 FB 與即時資訊：https://www.facebook.com/groups/UNISON.DALab/ 3. The course features a curated lineup of distinguished guest speakers from both academia and industry, offering students unique insights into real-world challenges and emerging technological trends. To maximize engagement and professional development, this course operates in an interactive seminar format. Students are expected to take an active role in their learning. Students must: 1) Attend all guest presentations, maintain detailed notes, and actively participate in Q&A sessions with speakers. 2) Synthesize insights from the presentations and literature into comprehensive, detailed technical reports. 3) Conduct independent reviews of literature relevant to the presentation topics to contextualize the speaker’s work. docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱-研究所 科號 IEEM 必/選修 選修 組別 00 上課時間 待定 教室 待定 人數限制 60 科目學分說明 總學分數 各專業所佔學分比例分配 (合計須為 3) 3 數學 基礎科學 工程專業 授課小時數 理論 設計 3/每週 1 2 科目中文名稱 統計學習 科目英文名稱 Statistical Learning 任課教師 張國浩 授課語言 ■中文 □英文 檔修科目 建議先修 Engineering Statistics、 Stochastic Processes 此科目對應之系 所核心能力(請勾 選並填入比例， 比例合計為 100%) Core capabilities to be cultivated by this course ■ 工工專業與系統分析能力 IE profession and systems analysis skills 50 % ■ 獨立研究及解決問題的實作能力 Capability of independent research and problem solving 50 % □ 領導、溝通與團隊合作能力 Leadership and coordination abilities % □ 自我充實能力 Capability of self-development and enrichment % □ 國際觀視野、國際化互動與表達能力 Global interaction and communication skills % 一、課程說明 This course aims to provide a comprehensive introduction to statistical learning—a discipline that lies at the intersection of statistics, machine learning, and data science. Students will explore both the theoretical foundations and practical applications of modern learning algorithms, gaining the skills to analyze complex datasets and build predictive models. Emphasis is placed on understanding the tradeoffs between model complexity and prediction accuracy, developing robust methods for high-dimensional data analysis, and implementing state-of-the-art techniques in a programming environment (Python). Student Learning Objectives: ⚫ Fundamental Concepts: Understand key ideas such as bias-variance tradeoff, model complexity, overfitting, and the principles behind various learning algorithms. ⚫ Methodological Proficiency: Gain hands-on experience with linear models, regularization methods (e.g., ridge, lasso), nonparametric techniques, ensemble methods, and modern high-dimensional approaches. ⚫ Theoretical Insight: Develop an appreciation for the theoretical guarantees underlying statistical learning methods, including non-asymptotic performance bounds and sparsity principles. ⚫ Practical Application: Apply statistical models to real-world data, evaluate model performance using cross-validation and other techniques, and critically assess the assumptions and limitations of different methods. 二、指定用書 Introduction to Statistical Learning with Python by Gareth James, Daniela Witten, Trevor Hastie, and Robert Tibshirani (2023) 三、參考書籍 四、教學軟體 Python 五、教學方式 The course combines lectures, hands-on laboratory sessions, assignments and project- based learning. Students will work with statistical software to implement and experiment with different learning methods, thereby bridging the gap between theory and practice. 六、教學進度 Week Video Assignment 1 Introduction 2 Statistical learning #1 3 Linear regression #2 4 Classification #3 5 Resampling method #4 6 Linear model selection and regularization #5 7 Moving beyond linearity 8 Tree-based methods (1) #6 9 Tree-based methods (2) #7 10 Support vector machines (1) #8 11 Support vector machines (2) #9 12 Deep learning #10 13 Survival analysis and censored data #11 14 Unsupervised learning #12 15 Multiple testing #13 16 Final exam 七、成績考核 □小考 □期中考 ■期末考 ■作業 ■書面報告 ■口頭報告 □實作成品 □口試 □其他，請說明: (若有其他評分方式亦可於下方補充說明) Grade Element Weighting Final exam 30% Assignment 40% Project 30% Assignment Each week, students will be assigned hands-on programming tasks that directly relate to the concepts and algorithms covered in lectures. These assignments are designed to reinforce theoretical understanding through practical application, requiring students to independently implement models, run experiments, and analyze data using Python. By leveraging libraries such as NumPy, pandas, and scikit-learn, students will explore real- world datasets and develop solutions that mirror industry practices. The weekly assignments not only build technical proficiency but also encourage critical thinking and problem-solving skills, ensuring that each student actively engages with the course material and gains valuable experience in statistical learning. Project For final project, teams of 3-4 students will collaborate to select a topic that interests them and apply the statistical learning methods covered throughout the course. Teams are expected to design and execute a comprehensive analysis, including relevant numerical experiments that demonstrate the practical implementation and effectiveness of these methods on real or simulated datasets. This project is intended to synthesize theoretical knowledge with hands-on experience, culminating in a 20-minute presentation where each team will share their findings, discuss challenges encountered, and illustrate how the chosen techniques can be applied to solve complex data analysis problems. 八、核心能力達 成指標 請依據前項「本科目所對應之核心能力」所勾選之能力項目，填寫核心能力達成 指標(即會依據什麼指標來衡量學生修習該核心能力的程度)。 例：本門課對應的核心能力有 1 和 2，即須填寫核心能力 1 和 2 的衡量指標。 核心能力 1：工工專業與系統分析能力 核心能力 達成指標 熟悉統計學習的相關理論與演算法 核心能力 2：獨立研究及解決問題的實作能力 核心能力 達成指標 應用統計學習的理論與演算法處理相關的實務問題之能力 核心能力 3：領導、溝通與團隊合作能力 核心能力 達成指標 核心能力 4：自我充實能力 核心能力 達成指標 核心能力 5：國際觀視野、國際化互動與表達能力 核心能力 達成指標

docs.text: Soft Computing Course Syllabus National Tsing Hua University | Graduate Course Syllabus Soft Computing 柔性演算課程大綱 Graduate-Level Course Syllabus I. Course Description / 課程說明 This graduate-level course introduces the fundamental theories, computational models, and advanced applications of soft computing and artificial intelligence (AI). The course focuses on solving complex, large-scale, nonlinear, and uncertainty-intensive problems using fuzzy logic, evolutionary computation, swarm intelligence, deep learning, hybrid intelligent systems, and uncertainty analysis. Students will study representative and emerging soft computing methodologies, critically review recent peer-reviewed journal papers, and implement selected algorithms using modern computational tools. Special emphasis will be placed on heuristic optimization, Simplified Swarm Optimization (SSO), deep learning models, hybrid AI frameworks, and applications in reliability engineering, smart manufacturing, digital twins, autonomous systems, and decision-making under uncertainty. II. Textbooks and Software Tools / 指定用書與軟體工具  Course handouts, lecture slides, and selected journal papers.  Selected papers from leading peer-reviewed journals, including IEEE Transactions, Reliability Engineering & System Safety, Applied Soft Computing, Expert Systems with Applications, and related journals.  WEKA 3.9+ for data mining and machine learning demonstrations.  Python for algorithm implementation.  PyTorch or TensorFlow for deep learning implementation.  Additional open-source packages may be introduced according to project needs. III. References / 參考資料 Classic and contemporary research papers in soft computing, artificial intelligence, optimization, reliability engineering, and intelligent systems will be assigned throughout the semester. Representative journals include:  IEEE Transactions on Cybernetics  IEEE Transactions on Reliability  IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems  Reliability Engineering & System Safety  Applied Soft Computing  Expert Systems with Applications  Information Sciences Soft Computing Course Syllabus National Tsing Hua University | Graduate Course Syllabus IV. Course Learning Outcomes / 課程學習目標 1. Explain the theoretical foundations and major paradigms of soft computing and artificial intelligence. 2. Implement selected soft computing algorithms, including fuzzy logic systems, evolutionary algorithms, swarm intelligence, and deep learning models. 3. Analyze the strengths, limitations, and computational complexity of representative soft computing methods. 4. Critically review recent journal papers and identify research gaps in soft computing and AI. 5. Design hybrid intelligent frameworks for solving complex engineering and decision-making problems under uncertainty. 6. Develop a research proposal, technical report, or term paper with the potential to be extended into an international journal submission. V. Teaching Method / 教學方式 This course is designed for Ph.D. students and advanced Master's students. The teaching approach combines lectures, paper reading, algorithmic demonstrations, group discussions, brainstorming sessions, and research-oriented project development. Students are expected to actively participate in class discussions, present selected papers, and propose novel algorithmic ideas or hybrid computational frameworks. Guest lectures by collaborating scholars, industry experts, or research partners may be arranged to introduce advanced topics and real-world applications. VI. Weekly Schedule / 教學進度 Week 1: Introduction to Soft Computing and Artificial Intelligence  Overview of soft computing, artificial intelligence, and computational intelligence.  Comparison between hard computing and soft computing approaches.  Applications of soft computing in complex engineering systems. Week 2: Fuzzy Logic Systems  Fuzzy sets, crisp sets, membership functions, and linguistic variables.  Fuzzy rules, fuzzification, inference mechanisms, and defuzzification.  Fuzzy logic controllers and engineering applications. Weeks 3-5: Swarm Intelligence and Heuristic Optimization  Introduction to swarm intelligence and metaheuristic optimization.  Particle Swarm Optimization, Ant Colony Optimization, and related methods.  Core algorithm focus: Simplified Swarm Optimization (SSO).  Applications of SSO in reliability engineering, machine learning, and engineering optimization.  Algorithmic complexity, benchmarking, and implementation examples. Soft Computing Course Syllabus National Tsing Hua University | Graduate Course Syllabus Week 6: Evolutionary Computation  Genetic Algorithms: encoding, selection, crossover, mutation, and fitness evaluation.  Evolution Strategies and Genetic Programming.  Applications of evolutionary computation in large-scale search and optimization problems. Week 7: Convolutional Neural Networks  Convolutional layers, activation functions, pooling layers, and fully connected layers.  Representative CNN architectures, including LeNet, ResNet, and EfficientNet.  Applications in image classification, defect detection, and engineering pattern recognition.  Framework-based implementation examples using Python. Week 8: Long Short-Term Memory Networks  Recurrent neural networks and the vanishing gradient problem.  LSTM cells, gates, memory states, and sequence learning.  Applications in time-series forecasting, reliability tracking, and predictive maintenance.  Case studies and implementation examples. Week 9: Transformer Models  Self-attention, multi-head attention, and positional encoding.  Encoder-decoder architecture and representative Transformer variants.  Applications in natural language processing, sequential data analysis, and engineering data modeling.  Discussion of large language models and their relevance to research workflows. Weeks 10-11: Hybrid Soft Computing and AI Techniques  Neuro-fuzzy systems and adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference systems.  Fuzzy evolutionary algorithms and co-evolutionary models.  Integration of swarm intelligence with machine learning and deep learning.  Hybrid frameworks for optimization, prediction, classification, and reliability analysis. Weeks 12-13: Uncertainty Analysis in Soft Computing and AI  Types of uncertainty in complex system modeling, including aleatory and epistemic uncertainty.  Representation, propagation, and quantification of uncertainty.  Robustness, reliability, and sensitivity analysis in AI-based models.  Applications in network reliability, resilience, and decision-making under uncertainty. Week 14: Advanced Topics and Research Trends  Deep reinforcement learning and its integration with soft computing.  Explainable AI, interpretable models, and trustworthy AI.  Scalability, computational efficiency, and hardware acceleration.  Emerging topics in digital twins, autonomous systems, and intelligent manufacturing. Soft Computing Course Syllabus National Tsing Hua University | Graduate Course Syllabus Week 15: Real-World Case Studies and Industry Applications  Applications in smart manufacturing, semiconductor systems, digital twins, autonomous mobile robots, and reliability engineering.  Discussion of practical benefits, implementation challenges, ethical considerations, and deployment limitations.  Student-led case study discussions. Week 16: Final Review and Term Project Presentations  Comprehensive review of core concepts and major algorithms.  Discussion of future research directions in soft computing and AI.  Final project presentations and research proposal discussions. VII. Grading and Assessment / 評量方式 Assessment Item Weight Description Assignments and Problem Sets 30% Algorithm implementation, theoretical exercises, short technical reports, and computational experiments. Midterm Project or Literature Review 30% Critical review and oral presentation of selected high- impact journal papers, or a practical implementation checkpoint. Final Project or Research Paper 40% Development of a novel algorithmic framework, empirical study, research proposal, or term paper aimed at international journal standards. VIII. docs.text: SUBJECT OUTLINE IEEM525000 人機互動 Human-Computer Interaction Delivery Autumn 2026 Credit points 3 Result type Grade Subject Coordinator and Teaching Staff Dr. Chun-Hsiang (Michael) Chuang Email: ch.chuang@ie.nthu.edu.tw Course description: This course introduces students to the essential concepts and theoretical underpinnings of human-computer interaction (HCI), an interdisciplinary domain that bridges areas such as cognitive science, neurocognitive systems, computer technology, ergonomics, and engineering design. Students will examine both theoretical and practical aspects of how people interact with digital systems, focusing on perceptual and cognitive processes that inform the development and assessment of user interfaces. Core subjects include interface architecture, usability analysis, accessible design, and the use of multiple input and output modalities, such as tactile, visual, spoken language, and auditory feedback. The course also covers advanced topics like brain- computer interfaces and immersive virtual environments. In addition to traditional lectures, learners will participate in a series of individual and group projects where they will design, implement, and assess interactive technologies by integrating course concepts with supplementary research and user-centered methodologies. docs.text: 1 IEEM 554600 Sustainable Engineering and Management 永續工程與管理 Instructor: Ming-Chuan Chiu, 邱銘傳 Ph.D. E-mail: mcchiu@ie.nthu.edu.tw Office Phone: (03)574-2699 FAX: (03)572-2204 Office Location: 923 ENG I Office Hours: Wed 10:00-11:59 am and by appointment Class Times: W789 Class Location: Eng I 901 Class TA: 張芷瑄 chihsuan@gapp.nthu.edu.tw,石文德 aa29960939@gmail.com Office: 913 ENG I TA Office hour: Monday afternoon at 913 Ext:33949 Class Web: eeclass (https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw/course/22208) FB 社團: www.facebook.com/groups/1544856802791801 Course Objective Carbon neutrality and sustainability have become a global trend and had a great impact on design, manufacturing, service, supply chains, corporate governance, etc. This course provides students the basic knowledge about these issues and enables them to develop preliminary skills of applications for industries. 永續環保理念已成國際趨勢，在設計、生產、服務、供應鏈、公司治理等多方面的永續議題也受到重 視。本課程目標為使學生對這些永續內容具備基礎知識，在管理面與工程面介紹現今重要議題與未來發 展趨勢，並提供相關實踐作法(Best Practice)，協學生進而發展初步的應用技能與產業接軌能力。 Textbook 永續工程與管理, 中國工業工程學會, 2022, 前程文化 Grade Construction: You will be evaluated based on a broad spectrum of assignments. Your grade will be determined in the following fashion: ● Final Projects – 20% ● Examinations – 40% ⮚ Midterm 20% ⮚ Final Exam 20% 2 ● Assignments/Homework – 30% ● Class Participation – 10% Grading Policy: The major lesson to be learned in this course is that it is ok to make mistakes. If you feel frustrated that something isn’t working out, don’t worry! Design projects will be evaluated on the basis of effort and how well you followed the design process, and not whether the “correct” result was obtained. When it comes time to put together final grade, the following grade cutoffs will be applied. %Range 100 – 90 89 – 85 84 – 80 79 – 77 76 – 73 72 – 70 69 – 60 59 – 50 49 – 1 Letter A+ A A- B+ B B- C D E Class Policies The following are some ground rules to help us progress steadily through the semester: 1. Attendance is mandatory for all class periods. Because this class meets for 1.5~2 hours each session, significant material is covered each class session. You need to be present to learn and contribute to your team's success. Course grade will be dropped to the next lower grade (such as from A - to B+) for every three classes missed Also, the course grade will be dropped to the next lower grade if there is a pattern of tardiness. Missing class due to family vacation is not an excused absence. If possible, send the e-mail to me (mcchiu@ie.nthu.edu.tw) before class if you are sick or injured and will not be attending class. 2. If you have an excused absence that results in missing a quiz or other major assignment, you must discuss this with me prior to the quiz. 3. Late assignments (i.e., those not turned in at the beginning of the class period they are due) are graded out of 80%. Assignments turned in late will be graded, but with a 20% grade reduction for every week beyond the due date. 4. The instructor will discuss any exam or assignment grade within 48 hours (excluding weekends and holidays) of its return, after which time the discussion is closed. 5. The Design and Computer labs cannot be made up if they are unique and involve team work. 6. Students are responsible for any missed handout and homework assignment for any unexcused missed class. 7. Changes to assignments will be announced in class and supersede what is on the syllabus (the syllabus may be updated periodically without prior notice, please check iLMS weekly for updates). If you miss a class for an excused absence, it is your responsibility to ensure that you have the proper assignment. 8. Teams are expected to address team member problems (such as missed meetings or not completing work). However, do not let a small team issue or problem develop into a major conflict. Contact the class instructor to help address and correct the problem early! 3 9. Excellent team work can improve your project grade by as much as 2% per design project. Poor teamwork can lower your course grade by the same amount. A project grade is determined for each project, and team peer evaluations will be used to determine your final score for that project. Students earning high peer evaluation scores will see a project grade boost, and students earning a low peer evaluation scores will see a grade decrease. 10. Cell phones are to be turned off or in silent mode when in class. No IM and newspaper during the class. docs.text: 課程資訊 及 課程大綱 課程名稱 (中文) 密碼學設計與分析 課程名稱 (英文) Cryptography Design and Analysis 授課教師 陳昱圻 上課時間 M234 （非同步課程） (如果要連續 3 小時上課，請一併提供理由。) 開課年級 研究所 學分數 3 人數限制 90 先修科目 無 課程簡述 Brief Course Description (required) Cryptography is a science used to design algorithms and formulate protocols for achieving security requirements, e.g. privacy, authentication, and data integrity. Recently, with the vigorous development of electronic communication and e-commerce, the importance of cryptography has gone beyond its historical military use. Cryptography provides technology to achieve security, for example: it allows us to successfully use credit cards for online transactions without revealing the card number to others. Over the past 25 years, cryptography has transformed from a technology developed for a specific purpose to a science with a solid theoretical foundation. This course will also teach the following directions of cryptography. 1. Definition: Cryptographic requirements (also known as cryptographic concepts) are formally defined to quantify the so-called security. 2. Cryptographic design and security proof: Cryptographic scheme design will be introduced, and its the security can be guaranteed by some difficult assumptions. 3. Theoretical basis: Cryptography schemes are all based on difficult assumptions. 4. Advanced topics (including post- quantum cryptography). (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters / 最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 關鍵字 Cryptography 密 碼 學 , Security definition 安 全 性 定 義 , Security analysis 安 全 性 分 析 , Cryptographic design 密 碼 學 設 計 , Post- quantum cryptography 後量子密碼學 請輸入課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」至少 5 個, 每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文, 以半形逗點分隔 (必填) Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 課程大綱 Detailed Course Syllabus 一、課程說明(Course Description) 密碼學是一門用來設計演算法和訂定協議的科學，目的為如何在 不安全的環境中達到安全的需求，如：隱私、認證、以及資料的完 整性。近期，在電子通訊和電子商務的蓬勃發展下，密碼學的重要 性已遠超越它在歷史上的軍事用途，而已經充滿在我們的生活當 中。非常重要的是密碼學提供了實現安全的技術，例如：它讓我們 可以成功使用信用卡於線上交易，同時又不洩漏卡號給其他人。 由過去 25 年來的進展，密碼學已經從一個為了達成特定目的所開 發的技術轉變成一門富有嚴謹理論基礎的科學。 二、指定用書(Text Books) Katz, Jonathan, and Yehuda Lindell. Introduction to modern cryptography. Chapman and Hall/CRC, 2014. 三、參考書籍(References) 自編教材 四、教學方式(Teaching Method) 非同步遠距授課 五、教學進度(Syllabus) 1. Intro to Crypto 密碼學簡介 2. Perfect Secrecy 完美秘密 3. Private Key Encryption 私密金鑰加密法 4. Message Authentication Code 訊息認證碼 5. Hash Functions 雜湊函數 6. Public Key Encryption 公開金鑰加密法 7. Digital Signatures 數位簽章 8. Other Advanced Topics 其他進階主題 六、成績考核(Evaluation) 平時小考、期中考、期末考 70% 小組報告 30% 七、可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website) https://hackmd.io/@wycchen/1132_Crypto_NTHU 核心能力 Core capability 請勾選 此科目對應之系所課程規畫所欲培養之核心能力 Core capability to be cultivated by this course 權重（百分比） Percentage 具有設計與操作實驗以及分析、解釋數據的能力。 To be able to design and perform experimentation as well as analyze and explain the experiment data. % v 具有發現問題、定義問題、並設計程式以解決問題的能 力。 To have the ability to discover problems, define them, and design computer programs to solve problems. 30% v 具有資訊、數學及科學的基礎知識。 To have fundamental knowledge of computer science, mathematics, and science. 30% v 具有分析、設計、開發、整合、測試、與評估資訊系統、 元件、或演算法的能力。 To be able to analyze, design, develop, integrate, test, and evaluate systems, components, and algorithms of computer science. 30% 具有良好的溝通技巧與跨領域團隊合作的能力。 To have good communication skills and be able to cooperate with others in interdisciplinary teams. % v 瞭解與資訊相關之產業脈動與最新的資訊科技進展。 To understand the most recent technological and industrial advancements regarding computer science. 10% 瞭解資訊科技對於全球性社會、經濟、文化等層面的影響 與責任。 To understand the social, economical, cultural effects of computer science and related technologies on the global level. % 瞭解國際視野及終身學習的重要性。 To understand the importance of international view as well as lifelong education. % 尊重學術、工程倫理、及智慧財產權。 To respect academics, engineering ethics, and intellectual property. %

docs.text: National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 科號 Course Number 11510IMBA400200 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Size of Limit 25 中文名稱 Course Title 企業家精神與創業管理 英文名稱 Course English Title Entrepreneurship and New Venture 任課教師 Instructor Yu-Wei Hsu 許祐維, Hung-Wen Chen 陳鴻文 教師聯絡方式 Contact Information Email: yhsu.edu@gmail.com 上課時間 Time F2F3F4 上課教室 Room R903 (@TSMC Building) 先修科目 Prerequisite(s) 本課程對應之學習目標與核心能力 Aligned Learning Goals and Learning Objectives Entrepreneurial mindset- ideas origination, opportunity realization, economic thinking, risk taking and be passionate. Business Plan- to work in a team to put together a sound Business Plan. Leadership- Build up observation skills to provide sound feedbacks and challenges on others’ views and business proposals. 課程目標 Course Objectives To understand the essential mindset and mental models of a successful entrepreneur- a startup entrepreneur or a corporate entrepreneur. To learn and practice the necessary tools in starting up a business- the entrepreneurial process, business planning, Business Plan, etc. To build up strong interactive capability in business group discussion- to provide useful feedbacks, to challenge ideas and to help driving others to be successful. 課程說明 Course Description This course is useful for students who are especially interested to run a startup company. We will discuss entrepreneurship from the essential mindset and mental models through to key useful tools in starting up a company. Even though you may not plan or expect to run a startup, this course could help you build up the key competence to be a corporate entrepreneur who realize career advancement through entrepreneurial mindset and with competence in related tools. Participants are expected to get actively engaged in class discussions, to provide feedbacks at the end of each lecture, to work in groups on Business Plan and to provide feedbacks on others’ Business Plan presentations. No mid term nor final term exam is designed while we emphasize on the Business Plan preparation and reviews that stress on interactive participations. Additionally, considering Business Plan that involves the utilizing of AI assisted tools or services is encouraged with condition. Policy on use of AI:(2) Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output. Group discussion could be case study discussion or continuously working through a part of the group Business Plan in accordance with the weekly topic. Also, Site Visit or Invited Speech will be arranged as shown in the Course Schedule. - Time will be given for reflection at the end of selected sessions for the participants to provide feedbacks and summarize key learning in a concise manner. 評分標準 Grading Class participation and group discussions: 25% Lecture reflection: 25% - By the end of selected lectures (or within given days), a feedback form is to be submitted with feedbacks and key learning. Individual Report: 20% - After the arranged events which may consist of Invited Speech or Site Visit, each member will have to submit an individual report as requested. Business Plan Group Reports: 30% - At the designated weeks, Business Plan is to be presented by each group. - At the end of the course, each group is to submit such Business Plan. - Individual contribution and performance will be considered as well. docs.text: National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus Course Number: IMBA400600 Course Title: Financial accounting 2027 (Fall 2026) Instructor: Hsieh, Chih-Cheng Contact Info: chih-cheng.hsieh@pwc.com Time: 9:10~12:00 (Monday) Classroom: TSMC Building Room 428 COURSE DESCRIPTION The global accounting environment has been evolving around greater transparency and comparability through continuous amendments to existing guidance and challenges emerge in different areas, e.g. continuing development of ESG, cloud computing and respective variations and fluctuations of global and domestic economics. The two main-stream financial reporting frameworks (International Financial Reporting Standard (“IFRS”) and Generally Accepted Accounting Principle in the United States (“US GAAP” or “GAAP”) have been working on enhancing respective guidance on accounting treatments and disclosures in respect to the abovementioned topics, as well as continuously working on aligning newly announced “co-developed” guidance, though discrepancies still exist. However, new accounting guidance was continuously being discussed and communicated to minimize potential discrepancies. The Taiwanese-IFRS (“T-IFRS”) has caught up with the global trend since 2018. Continuing the trend, the course is designed to educate students on these matters: 1. provides students with a basic understanding of accounting (primarily IFRS); 2. provides high level understanding of accounting principles when reviewing financial statements based upon IFRS; and 3. analyses various factors and methods that would be adopted in identifying the financial statements at risk. COURSE OBJECTIVES 1. To introduce students to understand information / underlying implication from a company’s financial statements. 2. To introduce students to analyze the accounting transactions on financial reports and business decision. 3. To orient students to organize the operating, investing, and financing activities of a company. TEACHING METHOD Instructor-led discussion, case study, team presentation, and etc. TEXTBOOKS Earl K. Stice, James D. Stice, W. Steve Albrecht, Monte R. Swain, Rong-Ruey Duh, Audrey Wenhsin Hsu --- Financial Accounting IFRS 4th Edition COURSE REQUIREMENTS AND GRADING POLICY 1. Participation – group presentation and question-raising: 30% 2. Group case – group presentation: 50% 3. Group case – write-up of ratio analysis for case company: 20% COURSE OUTLINE Fall 2026 Week Format Date TOPIC/ACTIVITY Week 1 Classroom 09/07 Introduction Week 2 Classroom 09/14 Ch.1 – Accounting Information: Users and Uses Ch.2 – Financial Statements: An Overview Week 3 Classroom 09/21 Ch.3 – The Accounting Cycle: The Mechanics of Accounting Ch.4 – Completing the Accounting Cycle Week 4 NA 09/28 Teacher’s Day Week 5 Classroom 10/05 Ch.5 – Internal Control: Ensuring the Integrity of Financial Information Ch.6 – Cash Week 6 Classroom 10/12 Ch.7 – Receivables Week 7 Classroom 10/19 Ch.8 – Inventory and the Cost Sales Ch.9 – Completing the Operating Cycle Week 8 NA 10/26 Taiwan Retrocession Day (make-up day for 10/25) Week 9 Classroom 11/02 Ch.10 – Investments: Property, Plant and Equipment and Intangible Assets Week 10 Classroom 11/09 Ch.11 – Financing: Long-Term Liabilities Ch.12 – Financing: Equity Week 11 NA 11/16 Class off Week 12 Virtual 11/23 Ch.13 – Investments: Debt and Equity Securities Week 13 Virtual 11/30 Ch.14 – Statement of Cash Flows (class starting at 10:00) Week 14 Classroom 12/07 Ch.15 – Analyzing Financial Statements Week 15 Classroom 12/14 Group Case Study (full day) Week 16 NA 12/21 Final Write-Up / Examination 1. The 16-week schedule was made through combining multiple chapters (two in most cases) into one session. 2. Courses from Week 9 might subject to change (some might subject to full day course). However, all courses will be held on Monday.

Students shall be prepared to face and alerted with all these upcoming challenges. National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 課程說明 Course Description This course is intended to be an organizational behavior and management course for the technology management student and International MBA student. Students will gain a general overview of the types and patterns and innovation and transformation, open innovation, timing of entry and challenges of sustaining transformation, along with theories, concepts and skills relevant to managing new product development effectively in today’s global environment. Students will be challenged to integrate knowledge they have gained from other business core courses and apply their accumulated knowledge to business case studies. The first part of the course focuses on the industry dynamics of technological innovation, including technological trajectories, competitive shifts, and innovation-driven disruption. Students will learn how organizations formulate and execute technological innovation strategies, addressing issues such as capability development, resource allocation, and organizational alignment. The second part of the course emphasizes innovation-driven transformation across industries. Through case discussions and applied analysis, students will explore how innovation reshapes major sectors, including the semiconductor and financial industries, as well as broader transformations related to digitalization and ESG/decarbonization. A field trip will provide exposure to real-world innovation practices. Throughout the course, students will develop the ability to analyze technological change, evaluate innovation strategies, and assess industry transformation. Assignments include an individual midterm report and a final presentation that integrates course concepts with real-world industry analysis. Students will engage in case study and business analysis for new product development as well as business transformation, and they will be frequently asked to conduct group discussion and present their findings to the class. 指定用書 Textbooks Melissa A. docs.name: 華語教學之跨文化溝通
docs.nameEn: Cross-cultural Communication for Teaching Chinese as a Second Language
docs.text: 《華語教學之跨文化溝通》 授課教師：宋怡南 ynsung@gmail.com 時間地點：12:10-15:10 GEN II 綜二 二、課程內容與學習 語言與文化的關係密切，跨文化溝通知識及能力屬華語教學專業知能之 一。華語教師必須充分了解語言與本國文化之間的連結，在生活中與自我經驗 中觀察文化，進而能適當的將之展現在教學中；另一方面，教師在面對來自世 界各地不同背景的學生，必須有足夠的文化敏感度，對各國文化及其相關影響 抱持尊重的態度，進而幫助學生從其母語文化出發，認識目標語的文化，結合 跨文化交際知能，獲得完整之語言溝通能力。 本課程《華語教學之跨文化溝通》由理論與實務出發，首先界定語言與文 化的關係及其定義，介紹語言與文化的研究方法，綜合探討華語教學中合適的 文化範圍。其次在語言交際和跨文化溝通的目的和基礎上，探討語言與文化接 觸與衝擊，經由各種語言現象所反映的文化背景，理解背後不同文化的交際模 式和核心價值。同時選取五類於跨文化溝通中具代表性及差異性的語言主題， 如：借字、禮節語言、禁忌語和委婉語等，通過與不同文化之受訪者對談，真 實觀察跨文化交際衝突和適應過程。最後由本學期探討主題出發，規劃具備華 語教學效能之主題文化課程單元。 三、課程要求 （一）閱讀與討論 課前閱讀教材並於班上積極參與討論，有助於在短時間內 取得最大收穫。請妥善規劃每次出席，課堂參與度將是學期成績的重要參考。 （二）跨文化個案訪談 分組後找到本學期五次文化主題訪談的對象，對象請 鎖定在臺學華語的外籍人士，國籍不拘，華裔背景請排除。 【訪談對象介紹】配合投影片介紹訪談對象：本人華語學習背景所來自國 家/鄰近地區的歷史宗教政治文化背景母語特色華語在該國的發展狀況對 臺灣文化的印象。 【五次訪談與分享】根據大綱上所列主題進行訪談，應輪流分工，於課上口頭 分享後繳交一份 4 頁的訪談書面報告 ※訪談請依照各週規劃之主題，依次完成。每次訪談均需全組到齊，盡量採 實體形式以利觀察跨文化溝通，不可合併主題訪談。書面報告均須附上分工 狀況與全組合照。 （三）華語教學主題文化課程單元設計 根據本學期訪談及探討的主題出 發，練習規劃不同主題之文化課程單元，報告包含海報票選與課堂講述兩部 分，期末前有一次主題簡報。 評量項目（總分 100％）  出席與閱讀討論（個人） 20%  訪談對象介紹（分組） 10%  個案採訪報告（分組） 40% （共 5 次，每次 8%）  期末主題文化課程設計（分組） 30% （簡報佔 5%） 四、每週進度（暫訂） 週 授 課 主 題 活 動 內 容 一 課程介紹與主題討論 語言學習與文化衝突經驗 二 語言與文化的關係 民族價值核心與文化對比 三 語言與文化的研究方法 活動：訪談注意事項 四 跨文化交際理論與實務 序曲：訪談對象介紹 1 五 從造詞心理、親屬稱謂看文化 序曲：訪談對象介紹 2 六 先人的智慧：各類熟語探討 活動：訪談行前討論 七 文化接觸之一：借字 第 1 次訪談與分享 八 文化接觸之二：混合語 第 2 次訪談與分享 九 誰最有禮貌：禮節語言的運用 第 3 次訪談與分享 十 語言的力量：咒罵語、髒話 活動：教學現場的文化議題 1 十一 佛曰不可說：禁忌語與委婉語 第 4 次訪談與分享 十二 男女大不同：性別語言 活動：教學現場的文化議題 2 十三 非語言符號：動作、表情、服飾… 期末主題文化課程簡報 十四 語言教學與文化課程設計 終曲：第 5 次訪談與分享 十五 ～期末主題文化課程單元設計報告與回饋～ 十六 ～期末主題文化課程單元設計報告與回饋～ 五、課程閱讀清單 課程主題指定閱讀文獻，已公告於本課程平台上。請按照進度完成閱讀與 筆記，帶至課堂上討論。

docs.name: 書報討論：專業華語
docs.text: 1 書報討論：專業華語 Seminar: Chinese for Specific Purposes 一、教師資訊 授課教師：李明懿 . 電子信箱：myli@cc.ncu.edu.tw 二、課程資訊 上課時間： 週二晚間 18:30 --- 19:30 a.m. 上課地點：綜二 205 三、課程說明 本課程限碩二以上準備寫畢業論文學生選修。 課程旨在引導學生進行專業華語教學相關研究和論文寫作。學生將透過此課 程瞭解專業華語教學研究和實務之現況和展望， 並透過系統性與階段性的學習 指導，協助學生進行學位論文寫作。本課程有三大學習目標： (1) 確立論文問題意識與研究方法。 (2) 培養華語教學學術研究能力。 (3) 培養論證架構的能力與論文寫作能力。 四、教學方式 上課以報告和討論的方式進行。由學生報告最近所研讀的文獻，及論文書 寫進度，出席同學需要輪流提問以及評論。上課前之週末需將論文進度或所讀 的文獻摘要寄給任課老師。 五、成績考核 課堂報告與討論：30% 摘要或論文進度：30% 自主研究： 40% 六、學生使用 AI 的聲明 根據本校公布之佈的「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門 課程採取有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於作業或報告，說明如下： 2 學生須於課堂作業或報告中的「標題頁註腳」或「引用文獻後」說明如何 使用生成式 AI 進行議題發想、文句潤飾或結構參考等使用方式，並在教師要 求下提供與生成式 AI 之對話內容。 學生不得使用 AI 工具生成論文的文字內容。若經查核使用卻無在作業或 報告中標明，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不 予計分。 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。 (以下書目和資源由陳淑芬教授提供) 七、論文撰寫相關書籍 上野千鶴子著，涂紋鳳譯，《如何做好研究論文？成為知識生產者，從提問到輸 出的18個步驟》，臺北：三采，2021。 安伯托．艾可（Umberto Eco）著，倪安宇譯，《如何撰寫畢業論文：給人文學科 研究生的建議》，臺北：時報，2019。 何德華，《華語教學研究方法與論文寫作》，臺北：正中書局出版，2009。 吳鄭重：《研究研究論論文：研究歷程之科P解密與論文寫作SOP大公開》，臺北： 遠流出版，2016。 孟樊，《論文寫作方法與格式》，新北市：威仕曼文化，2012。 美國現代語言協會編著，《MLA 論文寫作手冊，第9版》，臺北：書林出版有限 公司，2022。 張可婷譯，Diana Ridley 著，《一步步教您做文獻回顧》，新北：韋伯文化，2010。 畢恆達，《教授為什麼沒告訴我？——論文寫作的枕邊書》，臺北：學富文化事 業，2005。 陳信助，《研究方法易上手》，臺北：學富文化，2020。 彭明輝，《研究生完全求生手冊：方法、秘訣、潛規則》，臺北：聯經，2017。 葉至誠，《研究方法與論文寫作》，臺北：商鼎文化，2011。 蔡柏盈，《從字句到結構：學術論文寫作指引》，臺北：臺灣大學出版中心，2015。 顏志龍，《傻瓜也會寫論文（量化+質化增訂版）： 社會科學學位論文寫作指南》， 臺北：五南圖書，2018。 露辛妲・貝克(Lucinda Becker)著，王敏雯譯，《報告力：報告寫得好，輕鬆搞定 所有人！寫好報告與論文的 6 堂必修課》，新北市：木馬文化，2016。 Brown, J. docs.text: 1 漢語語言學 （115學年度第一學期） 一、教師資訊： 授課教師：陳淑芬 電子信箱：chensf@gapp.nthu.edu.tw 辦 公 室：綜二館 A607 聯絡電話：35167 二、課程資訊： 上課時間： 週一下午 3:30 --- 6:20 p.m. 上課地點：綜二 204 Office Hours: 週一早上 10-12、週五下午 2-4, or by appointment （請來信預約） 三、課程說明： 本課程介紹漢語語言學的基本概念、理論與分析方法，內容涵蓋語音、音韻、 構詞、詞彙、句法、語意、篇章、語用及漢字教學等領域。透過對漢語結構與語言 現象的系統分析，培養學生理解漢語運作機制及人類語言本質的能力，並將語言學 知識應用於漢語作為第二語言／外語之教學與研究。修習本課程後，學生將具備分 析與解釋漢語語言現象的能力，能有效回應教學現場所面臨的語言問題，提升華語 教學的專業素養與實務能力。 四、課堂用書： 1. 舒兆民，2021，《現代漢語語言學概要》，台北：新學林。 2. 自編講義（請見閱讀清單）。 五、參考資料： Chao, Yuen Ren (1968). A Grammar of Spoken Chinese. Berkeley: University of California Press. Li, Charles N. & Sandra Thompson. (1981). Mandarin Chinese: A Functional Reference Grammar. University of California Press.（黃宣範譯，《漢語語法》） Lin, Yen-Hui. (2007). The Sounds of Chinese. New York: Cambridge University. Sun, Chao-Fen. (2006). Chinese: A Linguistic Introduction. Cambridge University Press. 李子瑄、曹逢甫（2009）。《漢語語言學》，台北：正中書局。 邵敬敏（2001）。《當代漢語通論》，上海：上海教育出版社。 胡裕樹（1992）。《現代漢語》，臺北：新文豐出版社。 黃伯榮、廖序東 主編（2002）。《現代漢語》，北京：高等教育出版社。 趙元任著、丁邦新譯（2002）。《中國話的文法》，香港：中文大學出版社。 劉月華、潘文娛、故韡（2004）。《實用現代漢語語法》，北京：商務印書館。 鄧守信（2009）。《對外漢語教學語法》，台北：文鶴出版有限公司。 盧福波（2011）。《對外漢語教學實用語法》，北京：語言學院出版社。 錢乃榮（2002）。《現代漢語概論》，台北：師大書苑。 2 六、課程助教： 許晨希 sylviahsunthu@gapp.nthu.edu.tw 七、課程進度：(暫訂，會隨教學需要而做調整) 週次 日期 教學內容 閱讀章節 作業/課堂練習 1 09/07 課程總體說明 漢語語言學簡介 第一章； 程祥徽、田小琳 (2015) 2 09/14 語言的類型特徵 第二章；胡裕樹 (2002) 3 09/21 漢語語音 I 4 09/28 教師節放假 5 10/5 漢語語音 II 第三章 黃伯榮、廖序東 (2002) 現代漢語音節表分析 6 10/12 漢語音韻 第四章；邵敬敏 (2007) 小考 7 10/19 漢語構詞與詞彙 I 第五章；湯廷池 (2014) 8 10/26 台灣光復節補假 9 11/2 漢語構詞與詞彙 II 鄧守信 (2009a) 國語教學中心 (2017) 華語課本複合詞分析 10 11/9 語料庫介紹 北京語言大學 BCC 語料 庫、COCT 國教院語料庫、 TOCFL 學習者語料庫和 HSK 動態作文語料庫 小考 11 11/16 漢語語意學、語義 /構詞和句法的關係 石毓智 (2007a) 石毓智 (2007b) 近義詞分析 短語的結構和功能類型 12 11/23 漢語句法 I 第六章；陸儉明 (1980) 楊玉玲、吳中偉 (2013a) 楊玉玲、吳中偉 (2013b) 句子層次分析 13 11/30 漢語句法 II 鄧守信 (2009b) 鄧守信 (2009c) 歧義分析 14 12/7 漢語篇章結構、 漢語語用 第七章；陳俊光 (2010) 15 12/14 期末考 + 漢字 第八章；裘錫圭 (2012)； 黃沛榮 (1996) 16 12/21 期末研究報告 3 八、成績考核： 1. 課堂參與（5%）：出席率、課堂提問、小組討論貢獻度 2. 兩次小考（20％） 3. 兩次作業（20%） 4. 期末考 （25%） 5. 期末研究報告 + DDL 學習單設計 （30%） 九、學生使用 AI 的聲明： 本課程遵循本校「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，採取有條 件開放的方式使用生成式 AI 工具。學生在作業及期末研究報告的文章構思、議題 發想、文獻蒐集與回顧等階段，可以適度利用生成式 AI（如 ChatGPT 等）作為輔 助，以提升資料整理與內容架構的效率與完整性。然而，正式報告與作業的內容必 須由學生親自撰寫，不得直接複製生成式 AI 產出的文字。期末研究報告則不得使 用任何生成式 AI 工具參與撰寫，確保學術誠信與個人原創性。 若學生於作業或報告的前期構思、資料蒐集或文句潤飾等階段有使用生成式 AI， 須於正式報告的標題頁註腳或參考文獻之後，簡要說明所使用的生成式 AI 名稱、 協助範圍，以及 AI 產出與個人原創內容的比例。若經查核發現學生未依規定註明 使用 AI，或正式內容直接來自生成式 AI，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新評分或 不予計分。 修讀本課程即視為同意並遵守以上 AI 使用規範與倫理聲明。 4 閱讀清單 一、緒論 程祥徽、田小琳著（2015）。〈緒論〉。《現代漢語》修訂版。臺北市：書林出版社。 胡裕樹主編（2002）。〈緒論〉。《現代漢語（增訂本）》。香港：三聯書店。 二、漢語語音與音韻 黃伯榮、廖序東 主編（2002）。〈第二章 語音〉。《現代漢語》。北京：高等教育出版社。 敬敏主編（2007）。〈附錄二：國際音標簡表〉、〈附錄三：普通話聲韻配合總表〉。《現代漢語 通論》（第二版）。上海：教育出版社。 三、漢語詞彙 湯廷池編著、徐淑慎編修（2014）。〈華語的「字」、「詞」、「語」與「語素」〉。《華語詞法研 究入門（上）》。臺北市：致良出版社。 鄧守信（2009a）。〈第十三章：漢語詞類的教學語法〉。《對外漢語教學語法》。臺北市：文 鶴出版社。 陸儉明（1980）。〈關於漢語虛詞教學〉。《語言教學與研究》 4: 69 - docs.name: 書報討論：華語教學與語言學研究專題
docs.nameEn: Seminar: Special Topics in Teaching Chinese as a Foreign Language and Linguistic Research
docs.text: 1 書報討論：華語教學與語言學研究專題 一、教師資訊： 授課教師：陳淑芬 . 電子信箱：chensf@gapp.nthu.edu.tw 辦 公 室：綜二館 A607 聯絡電話：35167 二、課程資訊： 上課時間： 週五早上 10:10 --- 1:00 p.m. 上課地點：綜二館 608 Office Hours: 週一早上 10-12、週五下午 2-4, or by appointment 三、課程說明： 本課程旨在引導學生利用漢語語言學理論，應用在華語教學相關領域，瞭解 當代語言學理論的發展，培養學生口語表達能力及回答問題能力，並協助學生進 行學位論文寫作。 本課程有三大學習目標： (1) 探索並決定碩士/博士論文方向。 (2) 加強對華語教學與漢語語言學文獻的理解能力。 (3) 培養論證架構的能力與論文寫作能力。 四、參考資料： 華語教學、漢語語言學、認知語言學、語言與文化等領域相關論文與書籍。 五、教學方式 上課以報告和討論的方式進行。由學生上台報告最近所研讀國別化教材相關 的文獻，及論文書寫進度，出席同學需要輪流提問以及評論。上課前兩日需將 全文寄給評論的同學和任課老師。 六、成績考核： 課堂報告 + 書面報告：50% 提問與同儕評論：20% 期末報告： 30% 2 七、學生使用 AI 的聲明： 根據本校公布之佈的「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」， 本門課程採取有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於作業或報告，說明如 下： 學生可於課堂作業或報告中的「標題頁註腳」或「引用文獻後」簡要說明 如何使用生成式 AI 進行議題發想、文句潤飾或結構參考等使用方式。然而， 學生不得使用生成式 AI 工具撰寫期末研究報告。若經查核使用卻無在作業 或報告中標明，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或 不予計分。 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。 備註： 限修習過「漢語語言學」和「華語文教材教法」之學生選修，請簡要說明個人研 究主題、興趣、曾經修習課程、修課動機等，由授課教師同意後加簽。 3 論文撰寫相關書籍： 上野千鶴子著，涂紋鳳譯，《如何做好研究論文？成為知識生產者，從提問到輸 出的18個步驟》，臺北：三采，2021。 安伯托．艾可（Umberto Eco）著，倪安宇譯，《如何撰寫畢業論文：給人文學科 研究生的建議》，臺北：時報，2019。 何德華，《華語教學研究方法與論文寫作》，臺北：正中書局出版，2009。 吳鄭重，《研究研究論論文：研究歷程之科P解密與論文寫作SOP大公開》，臺北： 遠流出版，2016。 孟樊，《論文寫作方法與格式》，新北市：威仕曼文化，2012。 美國現代語言協會編著，《MLA 論文寫作手冊，第9版》，臺北：書林出版有限 公司，2022。 張可婷譯，Diana Ridley 著，《一步步教您做文獻回顧》，新北：韋伯文化，2010。 畢恆達，《教授為什麼沒告訴我？——論文寫作的枕邊書》，臺北：學富文化事 業，2005。 陳信助，《研究方法易上手》，臺北：學富文化，2020。 彭明輝，《研究生完全求生手冊：方法、秘訣、潛規則》，臺北：聯經，2017。 葉至誠，《研究方法與論文寫作》，臺北：商鼎文化，2011。 蔡柏盈，《從字句到結構：學術論文寫作指引》，臺北：臺灣大學出版中心，2015。 顏志龍，《傻瓜也會寫論文（量化+質化增訂版）： 社會科學學位論文寫作指南》， 臺北：五南圖書，2018。 參考資源： 1. 學校授權資源（可至清大圖書館---資料庫檢索/期刊檢索中檢索所需工具） A. 愛如生的《中國基本古籍庫》、《中國方志庫》、《歷代別集庫》、《譜 牒庫》、《典海平台》 B. 讀秀 C.
