docs.name: 立方衛星設計與實作
docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 11510IOSE500300 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 15 中文名稱 Course Title 立方衛星設計與實作 英文名稱 Course English Title Cubesat Design and Practice 任課教師 Instructor 羅之愷 Lo, Chi-Kai 上課時間 Time T2T3T4 上課教室 Room ENG I 工一 212 ／容量 24 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 本課程深入探討立方衛星（CubeSat）任務的設計、分析和操作的工程原理和實際操作。學生將探索這些小型 衛星帶來的獨特挑戰和機會，涵蓋從任務規劃和需求定義到次系統設計、整合、測試和在軌運行等主題。該課 程重點在將理論知識應用於實際場合，並培養小型衛星技術領域所需的技能。 This course provides a deep dive into the engineering principles and practical considerations for designing, analyzing, and operating CubeSat missions. Students will explore the unique challenges and opportunities presented by these small satellites, covering topics from mission planning and requirements definition to subsystem design, integration, testing, and on-orbit operations. Emphasis will be placed on applying theoretical knowledge to real-world scenarios and developing the skills necessary to contribute to the rapidly evolving field of small satellite technology. 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) Satellite(衛星), Cubesat (立方衛星), Micro-Sat(微衛星), Mission Analysis(任務分析) , Payload(酬載), Launch Vehicle Adapter(發射火箭接合器), System Design and Integration(系統設計整合) 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明 修完本課程後，學生將能夠： • 了解立方體衛星技術和應用的歷史、現狀和未來趨勢。 • 定義任務目標並將其轉換為立方體衛星任務的要求。 • 分析立方體衛星的各個次系統（結構、動力、姿態確定與控制、推進、通訊、酬載、熱管理、資料處理） 及其相互依賴關係。 • 了解整合和測試立方體衛星系統所涉及的挑戰和解決方案。 • 評估影響立方體衛星設計和運作的環境因素（太空環境、發射載重）。 • 使用並操作衛星任務設計分析軟體 (ANSYS-STK) • 分析任務預算（動力、質量、鏈路預算）並評估任務可行性。 • 參與立方衛星的實際組裝，整合，測試程序。 Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to: • Understand the history, current state, and future trends of CubeSat technology and applications. • Define mission objectives and translate them into requirements for a CubeSat mission. • Analyze the various subsystems of a CubeSat (structure, power, attitude determination and control, propulsion, communication, payload, thermal management, data handling) and their interdependencies. • Understand the challenges and methodologies involved in integrating and testing CubeSat systems. • Evaluate the environmental factors affecting CubeSat design and operation (space environment, launch loads). • Familiarize with the System Tools Kit (ANSYS-STK) for mission design and analysis • Analyze mission budgets (power, mass, link) and assess mission feasibility. • Participate in the actual assemble, integration, and test of a Cubesat ● 指定用書(Text Books) • CubeSat Handbook: From Mission Design to Operations ● 參考書籍 • A Guide to CubeSat Mission and Bus Design by Frances Zhu • Spacecraft Systems Engineering 4th Edition by Peter Fortescue (Editor) • Various research papers and technical articles on Cubesat Design. ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 課堂學習，電腦軟體操作，立方衛星實體組裝測試 Classroom presentation, Software operation, Cubesat assembly, integration, and testing. ● 教學進度(Syllabus) Week 1: Introduction to CubeSats • History and evolution of small satellites and CubeSats. • Motivations for using CubeSats (science, education, commercial applications). • Overview of the CubeSat standard and its variations (U-sizes). • Advantages and limitations of CubeSat platforms. • Current trends and future directions in CubeSat technology. • Case studies of successful CubeSat missions. Week 2: CubeSat System Architecture • Space systems engineering overview • CubeSat mission design and requirements analysis • System trade-offs and constraints (mass, power, cost, volume) • CubeSat reference architectures • Common CubeSat platforms and their configurations Week 3: Systems Engineering • Program Phases. • Role of Systems Engineers. • Requirements • Project Management • Decision Analysis • Risk Management Week 4: Mission Planning and Requirements Definition • Defining mission objectives and stakeholders. • Identifying mission requirements (scientific, operational, programmatic). • Developing concept of operations (CONOPS). • Orbit selection and analysis (LEO, SSO, etc.). • Mission lifetime considerations. • Regulatory aspects (spectrum allocation, debris mitigation). • Introduction to mission budgeting (mass, power, link). • Systems Tool Kit (STK) Labs Week 5: Structure and Mechanisms • Structural design principles for CubeSats. • Material selection and analysis (strength, stiffness, thermal properties). • Deployment mechanisms (antennas, solar panels, payloads). • Launch environment and load analysis. • Structural testing and verification. Week 6: Thermal Management and Environmental Considerations • Space environmental effects on CubeSat hardware (radiation, vacuum) • Space environment thermal considerations (solar radiation, Earth albedo, infrared). • Thermal design principles (passive and active control). • Thermal analysis and modeling. • Material selection for thermal properties. Week 7: Power System • Power generation (solar cells, batteries). • Power storage and management. • Power distribution and regulation. • Power budgeting and analysis. • Efficiency considerations. Week 8: Attitude Determination and Control System (ADCS) • Attitude determination sensors (magnetometers, sun sensors, star trackers, gyroscopes). • Attitude control actuators (reaction wheels, magnetorquers, thrusters). • Control algorithms and strategies. • Pointing requirements and accuracy. Week 9: Mid Term Exam Week 10: Propulsion System • Need for propulsion (orbit maintenance, maneuvering, deorbit). • Different types of small satellite propulsion systems (chemical, electric). • Thrust and delta-V calculations. • Propellant management. Week 11: Communication System • Link budget analysis (uplink and downlink). • Antenna design and selection. • Transceiver selection and characteristics. • Modulation and coding schemes. • Ground station considerations. Week 12: Payload and Data Handling • Types of CubeSat payloads (scientific instruments, imagers, communication systems). • Payload integration considerations. • Onboard data handling (processing, storage, downlink). • Command and telemetry systems. • Payload requirements and mission objectives • Instrumentation for CubeSat missions Week 13: Software Systems and Data Handling • CubeSat onboard software (operating systems, real-time systems) • Data collection, processing, and storage • Fault tolerance and recovery techniques • Software development tools and methodologies • CubeSat mission operations and ground control systems Week 14: Integration, Testing, and Operations • Assembly, integration, and Test (AI&T) process. • Environmental testing (thermal vacuum, vibration, shock). • Functional testing and performance verification. • Ground segment design and operations planning. • On-orbit operations and anomaly resolution. • Decommissioning and disposal. Week 15: CubeSat Launch and Deployment • Launch vehicle options (rideshare, dedicated CubeSat launches) • Deployment mechanisms (P-POD, others) • Post-deployment operations and initial communication • Orbit insertion and mission commissioning Week 16: Future of CubeSats and Emerging Trends ● 成績考核(Evaluation) • Homework Assignments (30%): Regular assignments to reinforce concepts learned in lectures. • Midterm Exam (20%): Covers the fundamental principles and concepts from the first half of the course. • Final Project (40%): Evaluation of the team's design report and presentation. • Participation and Class Discussions (10%): Based on engagement in discussions, peer feedback, and contribution to group activities. ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) (1) 完全開放使用且無須註明 Unrestricted use with no disclosure required (2) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output (3) 禁止使用，請註明相關的監管機制 Prohibited use; please specify relevant oversight (4) 本課程無涉及 AI 使用 Not applicable

docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 15 中文名稱 Course Title 衛星系統導論 英文名稱 Course English Title Introduction to Spacecraft Systems 任課教師 Instructor 林新發 (Shin-Fa Lin) 上課時間 Time 上課教室 Room 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) 本課程介紹太空系統工程方法論，並探討太空飛行器(spacecraft)之設計流程與主要次系統。內容涵蓋任務目標、 操作概念、需求分析、軌道設計、太空環境、系統架構等系統工程流程，並介紹太空飛行器主要次系統，包括通訊、 資料處理、電力、姿態控制、結構、熱控、推進等，以及酬載設計與系統整合。學生將以分組方式完成一組 LEO CubeSat 之概念設計，包括任務需求、架構選擇、次系統初步設計與 Budget 分析，並於學期末進行概念設計審 查與初步設計審查，以建立完整的系統整合與設計權衡的能力 This course introduces the methodology of space systems engineering and explores the design process and major subsystems of spacecraft. The content covers the systems engineering process, including mission objectives, operational concepts, requirements analysis, orbit design, space environment, and system architecture. It also introduces the major subsystems of a spacecraft, including communication, data handling, power, attitude control, structure, thermal control and propulsion, as well of payload design and system integration. Students will work in groups to complete a conceptual design of a LEO CubeSat, including mission requirements, architecture selection, preliminary subsystem design, and budget analysis. At the end of the semester, a conceptual design review and a preliminary design review will be conducted to establish overall system integration and design trade-off analysis capabilities. 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) Space Systems Engineering(太空系統工程), Spacecraft(太空飛行器), LEO (低地軌道), CubeSat(立方衛星), Conceptual design(概念設計) 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) 修習此課程後，學生能夠： --建立以太空系統工程（SE）為基礎之任務與系統設計能力 --理解太空環境特性與其對太空飛行器設計之影響 --學習 CubeSat 主要次系統設計原理 --能進行軌道、通聯、功率與質量初步估算 --完成 CubeSat 概念設計並進行初步設計審查簡報 Upon successful completion of this course, the students will be able to: --Develop mission and system design capabilities based on systems engineering (SE) --Understand the space environment and its impact on spacecraft design --Learn key subsystems of CubeSats --Perform basic orbit, link, power, and mass budgeting --Complete a CubeSat conceptual design and present it in a PDR format ● 指定用書(Text Books) “Space Mission Analysis and Design (SMAD)” by Wertz and Larson “Spacecraft Systems Engineering” by Fortescue, Swinerd and Stark “Space Vehicle Design” by Griffin and French ● 參考書籍(References) NASA/SP-2007-6105 Rev.2: NASA Systems Engineering Handbook NPR 7123.1: Systems Engineering Processes and Requirements ECSS-E-ST-10: Space Engineering – System Engineering General Requirements CubeSat Design Specification ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) ● 教學進度(Syllabus) ● 成績考核(Evaluation) ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) (1) 完全開放使用且無須註明 Unrestricted use with no disclosure required (2) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 無 中文名稱 Course Title 太空動力與熱系統 英文名稱 Course English Title Space Power & Thermal Systems 任課教師 Instructor 胡相宸 上課時間 Time 上課教室 Room 工一 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 This course offers a systems-level treatment of space power and thermal systems, covering power generation, energy storage, conditioning, distribution, and thermal integration for satellites, crewed spacecraft, space stations, launch vehicles, and planetary surface infrastructures. Emphasis is placed on physics-based design, radiation and thermal survivability, space power system and engine, and fault- tolerant Power Management and Distribution (PMAD) architectures for extreme environments. 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) Space Power Systems, Space Thermal Control, Photovoltaic Degradation and Radiation Effects, Nuclear Fission Space Power, Closed Brayton Cycle (CBC), Radioisotope Power Systems (RPS), Energy Storage Systems, Human-Rated Power Systems, Environmental Control and Life Support Systems (ECLSS) 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) Core topics include photovoltaic energy conversion under ionizing radiation, radioisotope and nuclear fission power systems with dynamic energy conversion—with particular emphasis on closed Brayton cycle engines—as well as electrochemical energy storage, regenerative fuel cells, and spacecraft thermal control systems. Dedicated attention is given to human-rated power system design, including integration with Environmental Control and Life Support Systems (ECLSS) and contingency-driven operational prioritization. The course integrates fundamental theory, heritage and modern space systems, and emerging technologies, providing a comprehensive foundation for future lunar, Martian, and deep-space missions. Upon successful completion, students will be able to:  Analyze space mission power requirements across orbital and planetary regimes.  Design and size solar, nuclear, and hybrid power systems under radiation and thermal constraints.  Integrate power and thermal management into spacecraft and habitat system designs.  Critically assess emerging space power technologies for future missions. This course is suitable for master's and doctoral students, as well as advanced undergraduates (junior or senior year) who have completed an introductory course in thermodynamics, dynamics, and fluid mechanics. ● 指定用書(Text Books) None ● 參考書籍(References) 1. Neil Gollhardt, Brian Buchholz, Kimberly Peppi, Steve Hu, C.L. Chen and Bruce Beihoff, Parametric Design Study of an Evaporator/Chill Plate, Rockwell Automation Power Technology Seminar, 1999. 6. Steve H. Hu, Fracture Control /Rack Flow Control Assembly, 97-69367, AlliedSignal Aerospace, February 1998. 7. Steve H. C. Hu and Steve Kuei, Three-Way Mixing Valve for Internal Thermal Control System, 97- 69351, AlliedSignal Aerospace, August 1997. 8. Steve H. C. Hu and H. Badani, Rack Flow Control Assembly for Internal Thermal Control System, 97- 69352, AlliedSignal Aerospace, December 1997. 9. Steve H. C. Hu and Wei-Shing Chaing , Air Blower for Carbon Dioxide Removal Assembly, 92- 65102-3, Revision 2, AlliedSignal Aerospace, June 1997. ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) Lecture Notes & Class ppt ● 教學進度(Syllabus) Syllabus 課程大綱 Lecture Contents 1 Fundamentals & Environment –Physics of Space –Mission Loading –Orbital Mechanics for Power 2 Solar Power Generation –PV Science –Survivability 3 Nuclear & Radioisotope Systems –Static Conversion –Fission Systems –Dynamic Cycles 4 Satellite Power Units (SPU) –Power Conditioning & Distribution Units –SmallSat/CubeSat Power Systems 5 International Space Station (ISS) Power Systems –Large-Scale Generation –Energy Storage Evolution 6 Environmental Control & Life Support Systems (ECLSS) Power Integration –Atmospheric Control –Thermal–Power Coupling 7 Launch Vehicle & Propulsion Power –Auxiliary Power Units (APUs) –Launch Environment Effects 8 Energy Storage Systems –Battery Management Systems –Fuel Cells 9 Power Management & Distribution (PMAD) –Power Electronics –Fault Protection 10 Space Thermal Management (STMS) –Radiative Transfer –Hardware 11 Closed Brayton Cycle (CBC) for Nuclear Power –Turbomachinery in Microgravity –Thermal Integration 12 Advanced Concepts & Future Trends –Wireless Power Transmission –Planetary Surface Power –Electrodynamic Systems ● 成績考核(Evaluation) Grading Policy Mid-term 20% Final 20% Homework 20% Term-paper, and Presentation 40% ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) (1) 完全開放使用且無須註明 Unrestricted use with no disclosure required (2) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; docs.text: 1 授課學期 115 學年度 第 1 學期 開課單位 □ 跨院國際博士班學位學程 □ 跨院國際碩士學位學程 課程名稱(中文) 華語作為第二語言/外語的測評 (20 字以內) 課程名稱(英文) Assessing Chinese as a Second or Foreign Language 授課教師 王海丹 學分數 1 授課教室 □校本部______ □南大_________ 上課時間 2026 年 9 月 11(五)、 13(日)、18(五)、20(日) 授課語言 □英文 □中文 人數限制 無 課程限制 無 課程簡述 本課程聚焦語言測試在華語作為第二語言/外語教學與課程體系中 的關鍵功能，通過系統教導第二語言測評的核心概念、方法，結 合前沿文獻並實踐案例，深入探討測評工具的設計、實施及結果 解釋，強調其在華語第二語言测评的應用價值。課程旨在培養學 生具有科學評估促進教學，改進與學習成效提升的能力。完成課 程後，學生將能夠設計或分析不同類型語言測評任務，制定評量 表，進行诸如口語能力面試，並掌握該領域的最新研究動態。 中文暨英文關鍵 字（五組） 華語、第二語言/外語、測試、評估、程度與能力 CSL, CFL, testing, assessment, proficiency & competence 課程大綱 Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程圍繞著語言測試在華語作為二語教學與課程發展中的核心 作用，介紹華語作為二語/外語的測試所包含的基本概念、方法與 理論基礎，通過綜述華語測試研究的代表性成果，幫助學生理解 二語測試如何科學的提升教學品質、學習成效與計畫發展。 完成此學分的課程後，學生將能掌握華語二語測試的基本原則與 方法、了解華語二語測試領域的最新研究進展同時，能夠具備針 對不同教學情境設計單項與綜合語言測試，撰寫測試題目的能 力，並在一定程度上能够評析測試題目優劣，或製定與課程學習 目標相匹配的評價量表。 2 ● 指定用書(Text Books) – 無單一課本，但提供某課本選章內容 ● 參考書籍(References) – 見所附英文教學大綱之後部分 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) – 教師課堂講授、思考型提問、小組或全體討論結合 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 第一天: 4 小時 – (課程簡介、彼此認識、相關興趣主題) – 二語測試基本概念及原則、 – 評試類型 (e.g. NRT & CRT) 及在二語題目中的功用 第二天: 4 小時 – 出具有效的能力測評題目 – 測評分數的解讀、評量題目的改進 – 華語評測研究與實務綜述(TOCFL/HSK/ACTFL/AP/IB) – 當今華測方方面面（一） o 字彙、聽說讀寫 o 其它方面能力測評 (e.g. 漢字、文法、語用能力測評) 第三天: 4 小時 – 當今華測方方面面（二） o 其它方面能力測評 (e.g. 文化、技術輔助的華語能力測評) – 其他方面 o 教學綜合展現測評 (Integrated Performance Assessment) 第四天: 4 小時 - 总结：有效提升課堂測評的 15 中方法 – 學生期末報告 ● 成績考核 (Evaluation) – 課堂出席率 (30%) – 課堂討論 (30%) – 期末報告 (40%); 選課者據個人興趣及就讀班級(碩士或博士 計畫)可從以下建議中選擇，或跟教師課下討論後決定 o 依個人先前所教課程出具考題(例如聽/說/讀/寫，或文 化、交際能力)等等，並依據課程所涵蓋理念解釋所出考 題的道理 o 依據課程所涵蓋基本概念或原則評估所熟悉的華語測試 題(單項或全套)或課程考題 o 依據課程所涵蓋基本概念或原則，評估現有華語外語/二 語教學大綱中關於課程測評華語能力的語言論述與程度 標準間的對應 ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則 (Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 3 本課程無涉及 AI 使用 Not applicable Assessing Chinese as a Second/Foreign Language Prerequisites: Introduction to Chinese linguistics; or instructor’s consent Course Description and Instructional Goals Language testing plays an important role in language teaching and curriculum development. The design, implementation, and utilization of language testing are essential to language classes and a strong program. A well-designed and valid test will benefit both learners and teachers, and eventually enhance the quality of teaching, student learning, and language programs in general. In this course, participants will explore the basic concepts, techniques, and theoretical issues in the field of second language testing through reading and examining recent and representative literatures and research. The application of general testing principles and theories on teaching Chinese as a second or foreign language will be a primary focus of this course. Student Learning Outcomes (SLOs) In completing this course, students will 1. become familiar with the design and methods of Chinese language testing; 2. develop the basic skills of incorporating appropriate testing techniques to different types of CSL/CFL assessment; 3. be able to design and create Chinese language tests to serve various testing needs in language classes. 4. be able to analyze Chinese test items (and write critiques); 5. be able to create both single skill and multiple-skill test items; 6. be able to create assessment rubrics based on certain criteria or student learning outcomes; 7. become familiar with the procedures of and be able to conduct classroom Chinese oral proficiency interview 8. become familiar with the recent research on Chinese language testing Grading Course grade will be based on these followings Attendance …………………………………….…...……………………30% Participation in class discussion…………………………………….…... 30% Final project…………………………………….…...……………………40% *Creation and/or revision of test items %Writing a short analysis or critique of a Chinese test or a subsection of a test Note: Test items creation or revision, e.g. the creation/revision of CHN(101-402) test/quiz(e.g. listening/speaking task/reading/writing Section, etc.), including A short statement of purposes: why, or what motivated you to create this test (section), existing problem, etc. Demonstration: test format, why it’s reasonably designed (rationales) a rubric or grading suggestions %A critique revision of an existing Chinese language course syllabus L/S/R/W 4 section with reference to an official guidelines: What is the issue of the current/existing statement in that course syllabus; to what extent does the narrative passage align well with the guideline details it aims for; Why do you suggest such changes References Bourgerie, D.S., Cox, T.L., & Riep, S.L. (2022). Does text entry method make a difference on Chinese writing test scores? Chinese as a Second Language 57(3) 270-297 Brown, J. D., & Trace, J. (2017). docs.text: Page 1 Intensive 1-Credit Seminar: Comparative Education, Conflict and Peace National Tsing Hua University September 2026 Instructor Email Office Hours & Location Dr. Kevin Kester kkester@snu.ac.kr or kevinajkester@gmail.com General Information The global community has set as a goal to get all children into schools by 2030, and to provide them quality education, yet war and violent conflict around the world remains the greatest barrier to achieving this goal. This course will examine the policies and practices that local, national and international educators and agencies adopt to resolve conflict and build peace in and through education. The course will examine the following questions: How does conflict affect education? How does education affect conflict? What role do international educational actors play in mitigating or perpetuating conflict in diverse contexts? And what theories, methods, and pedagogies could support the transformation from conflict to peace in society via education? The course will explore the diversity of interpretations of education for peacebuilding and education in emergencies in different forms across the globe. Case studies from Afghanistan, China/Taiwan, Cyprus, Korea, Sierra Leone, and Somalia/Somaliland will be examined, with additional optional cases from Jordan, Lebanon, Nepal, Palestine, and Ukraine. Teaching Methods This course involves student-directed learning and lecturer-student supervisions. Students are expected to complete readings outside of class and to bring questions to class for discussion. Each class will be facilitated as follows: a 30-minute group discussion on the assigned course reading(s) at the beginning of class followed by a whole-class discussion and Q&A for up to three hours. The final hour will be a set of practical exercises on teaching peace and conflict. Students will also complete individual reflections on readings before class. The focus is on greater teacher-student and student-student interaction to enhance students’ knowledge and skills in comparative education, conflict and peace studies. Course Goals and Learning Outcomes In this course, students will: • Examine the impact of conflict on education in diverse contexts; • Study the impact of education on conflict and peacebuilding; • Compare education, conflict and peacebuilding in different regions, cultures, and communities; • Explore various methods, pedagogies, and practices of conflict transformation through education; • Assess the contributions of this literature to the comparative educational field, as well as the comparative education literature to international understandings of issues of peace and conflict; • Learn practical exercises for teaching peace and conflict. Course Requirements & Grading Students are expected to attend and actively participate in all class meetings and complete all readings and assignments carefully and thoughtfully. Component Weight Attendance & Active Participation in Class 20% Response Papers (4 x 20 pts each) 80% Page 2 The professor will introduce the expected assignments and due dates for the course the first week. In consultation with students the final assessment procedure may change. This will be decided in a participatory democratic way. Evaluations In this course, there will be two key evaluations: attendance/participation and written reflections: Attendance & Active Participation (20%) – Class attendance and participation is an expected component of the course. Participation in class and preparation for sessions will be further reflected in the daily response papers. As such, 20% of the course grade has been allotted to attendance and participation. Response Papers (80%) – Participation in class and preparation for sessions will be reflected in the class discussions and preparation of response papers. As such, 80% of the course grade has been allotted to response papers (80; 4 x 20 pts each). In preparation for class, students will read and summarize the selected chapter(s) for reading for each session. Students will complete 4 response papers during the term. The response paper must be given to the instructor as a word doc at the beginning of each session. Late assignments will not be accepted. The length of the paper should be 500-750 words but strictly no more. In the response paper, students must include: 1. Description of the central argument(s) developed in the papers (6 pts); 2. Explanation of how the argument(s) relate(s) to or differs from the argument(s) presented in previous readings (7 pts); 3. The student’s response to the argument(s) (7 pts) The paper will be assessed on the following criteria: • Grasp of the central argument(s) • Understanding of how readings relate to each other • Originality of the response • Writing effectiveness (clarity, logic and coherence) When submitting the paper, make sure to include the following info in the word file: Student’s full name, CECP 2026, Response paper Session X. Course Materials Course Texts All students are expected to read passages from the course texts, as listed in the schedule below. Readings marked REQ are required while all others are optional. The full set of readings is available at the Google Drive link. Course discussions and response papers will be developed around these readings: Required: • Readings are available in this Google Drive Additional recommended books: • Karen Mundy and Sarah Dryden-Peterson (2011). Educating Children in Conflict Zones. New York: TC Columbia. • Elisabeth King (2013). From Classrooms to Conflict in Rwanda. Cambridge, UK: Cambridge University Press. • Michalinos Zembylas, Constadina Charalambous and Panayiota Charalambous (2016). Peace Education in a Conflict-Affected Society: An Ethnographic Journey. Cambridge, UK: Cambridge University Press. • Hilary Cremin and Terrence Bevington (2017). Positive Peace in Schools. London: Routledge. • Kevin Kester (2020). The United Nations and Higher Education: Peacebuilding, Social Justice and Global Cooperation for the 21st Century. Leeds, UK: Emerald. • Tejendra Pherali (2022). Conflict, Education and Peace in Nepal. London: Bloomsbury. Page 3 • Oliver Ramsbotham, Tom Woodhouse and Hugh Miall (2024). Contemporary Conflict Resolution, Fifth Edition. UK: Polity. Course Expectations & Guidelines 1. Academic Integrity Students are expected to produce their own work and, when using the work of others, include clear citations. Failure to properly cite or attribute the work of others will impact your grade, including a partial loss of points on particular projects or a failure of the class. 2. Student Special Needs If a student has a condition that impacts their classroom learning (such as a hearing disability), they should discuss special arrangements with the professor. A note from the departmental office may be required. 3. Attendance and Class Participation It is the student’s responsibility to attend class, and to inform their department in the event of excused absences. Students should come to class having read the required readings and be prepared to participate in discussion and activities. Active participation is integral to collaborative learning in the course. 4. Student Use of Mobile Devices in the Classroom In general, mobile phones should NOT be used in this course. Occasionally, the instructor may allow students to use mobile devices for research purposes, provided they are not used excessively or disruptively, but for the most part mobile devices should be turned off during class. This is to facilitate better engagement and learning during the course. 5. Additional Course Policies This course is based around your responsible preparation and use of class time, both for lectures and small and large group projects. It is assumed at the outset that you will use this time well. If you need extra assistance, please speak with the professor. Some Useful Journals and Websites for Global Education and Peace Debates • Asia Pacific Education Review: https://link.springer.com/journal/12564 • Asia Pacific Journal of Education: https://www.tandfonline.com/journals/cape20 • Compare: http://www.tandfonline.com/toc/ccom20/current • Comparative Education: http://www.tandfonline.com/toc/cced20/current • Comparative Education Review: http://www.journals.uchicago.edu/toc/cer/current • Current Issues in Comparative Education: https://www.tc.columbia.edu/cice/ • Discourse: Studies in the Cultural Politics of Education: http://www.tandfonline.com/toc/cdis20/current • Educational Philosophy and Theory: http://www.tandfonline.com/toc/rept20/current • Globalisation, Societies and Education: http://www.tandfonline.com/toc/cgse20/current • Journal on Education in Emergencies: https://inee.org/evidence/journal • Journal of Peace Education: http://www.tandfonline.com/loi/cjpe20 • Journal of Peace Research: https://journals.sagepub.com/home/JPR • Journal of Transformative Education: https://journals.sagepub.com/home/jtd • International Education Journal: Comparative Perspectives: https://openjournals.library.sydney.edu.au/IEJ/index • International Journal of Educational Development: https://www.journals.elsevier.com/international-journal-of-educational-development • International Review of Education: https://link.springer.com/journal/11159 • Peace Review: https://www.tandfonline.com/journals/cper20 • Prospects: https://link.springer.com/journal/11125 Page 4 Course Schedule Session Focus Class activities and details, daily goals November 14 Introduction to Course: Comparative Education and Peace Introductions, review course syllabus; teambuilding; introductory lecture and ideas Required reading: 1. (2026), Healing the Scars of War (China/Taiwan, Cyprus, Korea, and Somalia/Somaliland) Optional reading: 15. Roozbeh Shirazi (2011), When Projects of ‘Empowerment’ Don’t Liberate (Jordan) 16. Tejendra Pherali (2016), School Leadership During Violent Conflict (Nepal) 17. Zeena Zakharia (2017), Locating Critical Peace Education (Lebanon) 18. Hilary Cremin et al. (2018), Transrational Page 5 Peacebuilding Education to Reduce Epistemic Violence (United Nations university) 19. Mona Jebril (2023), Between Construction and Destruction (Gaza) 20. Olena Polovko & Sergei Glotov (2026), ‘The War Illuminates Everything’ (Ukraine) 21. Yann-Ru Ho (2026), Moving Beyond Militarization (Taiwan) The instructor reserves the right to modify this schedule based on new information, extenuating circumstances, or student performance. Students will be informed before any changes, and due consideration will be given to grades and participation. Instructor’s Bio Kevin Kester is Associate Professor of Comparative International Education and Peace/Development Studies, and Director of the Education, Conflict and Peace Lab, at Seoul National University. His research interests lie in the sociology and politics of education with a focus on the intersectional fields of comparative education, education and conflict, higher education, peace education, and global citizenship education. He is especially interested in critical theoretical perspectives on research and practice drawing on poststructural, postmodern, decolonial, and posthumanist thought. He completed his PhD and postdoc at the University of Cambridge and holds a PGCE from Columbia University, MA in Education and International Development from the University of Toronto, MA in Peace and Conflict Studies from the United Nations, and a postgraduate certificate in Global Affairs from NYU. His most recent (co-)authored books/special issues include International Handbook on Peace Education (forthcoming, Routledge); Conflict, Peace and Teaching in Higher Education (2026, Routledge); A Modern Guide to Education in East Asia: Globalization and Local Intersections (2026, Edward Elgar); Revisiting 'Asia as Method' in Education Research (2023, Springer); Common Curriculum Guide for Peace Education in Northeast Asia (2023, UNESCO-APCEIU); and The United Nations and Higher Education: Peacebuilding, Social Justice, and Global Cooperation for the 21st Century (2020, Emerald). He is recipient of the 2024 Professor Noam Chomsky Shining Star Research Award and the 2022 Unju Prize for Research Excellence. Kevin is originally from Kentucky, USA, where he received the commission of Kentucky Colonel – the highest civilian honor bestowed by the Governor of Kentucky – in 2020. He is Editor of Asia Pacific Education Review, Executive Editor of Teaching in Higher Education, and Associate Editor of Journal of International Cooperation in Education.

A task-based and application-oriented approach to professional communication is adopted. Each session is structured around a real-world business scenario commonly encountered in technology-driven and global workplace contexts. Students will engage in a sequence of guided tasks that move from input to output. Initial exposure to key language forms and communication strategies is followed by analysis of authentic materials (e.g., emails, reports, business cases), after which students apply these elements in structured tasks. These tasks culminate in the production of professional communication outputs such as emails, reports, proposals, and presentations. Collaborative learning is implemented through small task-force groups, where students work together to develop and refine their outputs. Instructor feedback is provided throughout the process to support clarity, organization, and strategic communication. communication contexts Week 13 12/4 Professional Report Writing — Structuring reports with clarity, coherence, and purpose Week 14 12/11 Case Study (Technology Context) — Analyzing and responding to real-world industry scenarios Week 15 12/18 Final Project Presentation — Integrated professional communication task Week 16 12/25 Holiday (No Class) National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 課程相關規定 Course Requirements & Rules The following course requirements are subject to change without prior notice. 1. Class attendance, lesson preparation and active class participation are required.  As you are all present whenever the instructor takes the roll, you will get 60% in this category Attendance and Participation. 經常性點名，全勤者可得「出席與參與」項目中的 60%成 績。  Each skip will cost 2 points from the category Attendance and Participation (up to 15 points in the final grade). 未假不到課（翹課），每 次從「出席與參與」成績（占學期成績 15 分）扣 2 分。  If you are absent in case of UNCONTROLLABLE situations (e.g. illness, emergency, important occasions, etc.), please apply for a leave on the Student Leave System on Academic Information System of National Tsing Hua University or on the iNTHU app (from the Office of Student Affair website), with clear leave information, including leave type, leave period, and reasons (must be clear and valid enough for the teacher’s approval). As the reasons or the documents are not clear, valid or sufficient enough, the teacher may deny the application. 遇不可抗力情形需請假者，請於本校校務資訊系統上的 學生請假系統或下載 iNTHU APP，填寫資料（請假類別、請假日期、請假事由）。請假事 由須合理並敘述清楚，提供老師是否准假之參考。請假單上的理由或所附證明文件不清楚或 不充分時，該次請假申請得不予核准。  Please observe the information you are expected to offer for each of the following leave types:  When requesting sick leave, please specify in the reason column the significant symptoms affecting your ability to attend class, as well as any medical consultation or medication taken. Only those who provide a doctor's certificate of diagnosis are eligible to submit makeup assignments. Medical receipts or prescription slips are not considered official proof of sick leave. 請病假時，請於理由欄位說明影響上課之顯著症狀，就醫或服藥等處 置。只有提出請假當日的醫生診斷證明者才能補交作業，就醫收據或藥單都不算病假正式證 明。  For personal leave, please describe the uncontrollable event and how it makes you absent from the class. 請事假時，請於理由欄位敘明事件，並說明該事件如何致使你無法前來上 課。  No leave application will be approved on the dates of presentations, peer evaluations, and midterm/final exams. Please care for your health and reserve the time for these important class activities. 報告、同儕互評、期中／期末考當日不得請假。請注意身心健康並為這些 重要課程活動預留時間。  There will be NO make-up exams or presentations unless you apply for leave with valid and official reasons for your absence beforehand. 無合理且正式的缺課原因，將不予補考 或補行報告。  You are expected to apply for leave before the class you are absent from. Any overdue leave NTHU 學生請假 Q&A National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus application must be made within 7 days from the last day of absence. 請假已事先申請為原 則。逾期請假申請必須於 7 日內補請。未能於規定期間申請者，均以曠課論。  Being late for more than 10 minutes (with no valid excuses) is treated as absence from that hour. Being late for more than 30 minutes is treated as absence from the whole class. 無故遲 到逾 10 分鐘，以該小時未到課紀錄。遲到逾 30 分鐘，視為該次上課未到課。  No points will be deducted for your ATTENDANCE as long as your approved leave is no more than 6 hours. However, you may lose points for your PARTICIPATION or in-class practices scheduled on the date of your absence. 核准的請假時數未逾 6 小時，不扣出席成 績。惟當日如有上課練習或小組活動，請假者無法參與或完成，將無法獲得該次練習或該項評 量成績。換言之，缺課仍可能影響「參與」與「作業」等成績。  If you skip class for more than 8 hours, your course withdrawal may NOT be approved, and you will get 0 credits for this course. 無故不到課逾 8 小時者，將不予同意其停修申請，亦無 法取得本課程學分。 2.  Absence or leave cannot be used as an excuse for failing to complete in-class exercises, missing assignment deadlines, or being unaware of the homework for that session.缺席與請假不 得作為未能完成當日上課練習、無法及時繳交作業或不知道該次課後作業之藉口。 3.  Assignments are expected to be completed and submitted by the due date. No late submission will be accepted or graded unless the instructor approves or grants your application for extension of submission. 作業請按時繳交（或上傳）。未獲教師同意可延遲繳交者或超過寬限 期，其遲交作業不批改、不計分。  Frequent late submissions with no valid excuses or under controllable circumstances will NOT be accepted or graded since the third late assignment. 無合理原因或非為不可抗力情形的 慣性遲交作業，第三份起將不予批改與計分。 4. Plagiarism on assignments and cheating on the exam is absolutely unacceptable. If someone is found plagiarizing or cheating, it means he/she will get a zero point for that assignment or exam. 嚴禁抄襲與作弊。抄襲與作弊者，學期成績以不及格處理。情節重大時，將提報至相關單位依校 規處理。 5. AI-assisted reports and assignments are allowed in limited instances: AI can be used to prepare for reports and assignments by brainstorming and tentative revision, but students must show how AI helps them reach the result. 僅限使用生成式 AI 於作業或報告之準備（如腦力激盪與初步修訂 等），學生須註明 AI 如何用於協作其作業或報告。 6. Penalty for no or poor participation in pair or group work Students are expected to take part in pair or group activities. Failure to engage in these activities (due to you absence or lateness) will lead to reductions in grades awarded. Sometimes the reduction may be suggested by other group members; in other circumstances, the instructor may reduce the grade awarded without reference to other group members. 學生負有參與雙人或小組 活動之義務。如因個人遲到或缺席導致小組活動無法順利進行，請假或缺席者該次活動成績將以 扣分或甚至 0 分計算。 National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 7.  Mobile devices are only used for educational purposes relevant to the subject or tasks in the classroom setting with the permission of or at the request of the instructor. Using mobile devices for studying other subjects or entertaining purposes is absolutely prohibited. Students who violate the regulation will be considered absent from the class or asked to leave the classroom. 行動裝置僅限於學習活動，使用須獲得老師同意或遵照老師指示。嚴禁使用行 動裝置研習其他課程或娛樂使用。違反規定者，以「未到課」處置，亦得請違規者離開教室。  During class students are not to be seen with a cell phone in hand or on the desk. Mobile phones are expected to be turned off or switched to a silent mode. 課程進行時，請關閉行動電 話或轉為靜音模式。未獲教師指示或許可，不得於上課時間使用或放置於桌上。 8. The syllabus, handouts, and returned assignments should be kept at least until the end of this semester for later reference or the final exam. 課程相關各項文件請妥為保存至學期結束。

docs.name: 跨域探索課程：科管院學士班
docs.text: National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 科號 Course Number IPMT100500 學分 Credit 1 人數限制 Size of Limit 20 中文名稱 Course Title 跨域探索課程：科管院學士班 英文名稱 Course English Title Interdisciplinary Exploration in IPMT 任課教師 Instructor 郭孟倫 教師聯絡方式 Contact Information tonny@gapp.nthu.edu.tw 上課時間 Time M5M6 上課教室 Room 台積 223 先修科目 Prerequisite(s) 無 本課程對應之學習目標與核心能力 Aligned Learning Goals and Learning Objectives 運用專業管理與科技知識的能力。 Our students will master the knowledge of technology and professional management. 10% 整合與活用第一專長及第二專長的專業知識能力，並具備跨領域規劃、領導 與執行團隊合作的能力。 Our students will be able to integrate expertise from their double specialty and thus plan, execute and lead in an interdisciplinary team setting. 20% 具備中文及英文閱讀寫作商業報告與商業口頭簡報能力。 Our students will be able to read and produce professional business documents as well as deliver a professional oral presentation in English and in Chinese. (30%) 20% 認識產業的國際發展趨勢，瞭解管理與科技對環境、社會及全球的影響，並 培養自我學習成長的能力。 Our students will develop the ability of self-learning by comprehending the international development trend of the industry and by comprehending the impact of management and technology made on the environment, the society and the world. 20% 理解專業倫理及社會責任的能力。 Our students will be equipped with understandings of professional ethics and social responsibility. 30% 課程目標 Course Objectives 本課程旨在幫助科管院學士班新生順利適應大學生活，並建立跨領域學習的思維與習 慣。課程目標分為三大面向： A 協助學業成功：透過本課程，學生將能 1. 應用適當的學習策略，調整跨領域課程的學習方式 2. 運用有效的時間管理方法，平衡多元課程負擔 3. 熟悉科管院學士班的彈性學制與跨域選課規劃 B 認識清華並與科管院建立連結：透過本課程，學生將能 1. 使用適當的校園與學院資源，參與有助於跨領域學習的機會 2. 與同學、師長及業界人士建立正向的人際網絡 3. 瞭解科管院學士班的特色定位與清華的歷史傳統 National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus C 促進個人發展、幸福和社會責任：透過本課程，學生將能 1. 建立自己的價值觀和身份認同，理解跨領域背景如何形塑個人獨特觀點 2. 發展促進身心健康的策略，建立可持續的學習與生活節奏 3. 進行自我生涯規劃，對科技管理相關的多元職涯方向有所認識 課程說明 Course Description 本課程為科管院學士班一學分選修課程，採密集授課方式，每週上課 2 小時，共計 8 週。課程設計以清華大學探索學習中心（ExAlt）新生探索系列課程為基礎，針對科 管院學士班學生的跨領域學習需求進行濃縮與調整。 科管院學士班學生具有獨特的跨域學習背景，需要同時涉獵科技與管理兩大領域， 包含第一專長（經濟、計財、法律、管理）與第二專長（全校不同學程任選）。本課程 除了涵蓋自我探索、設計人生、學習策略、校園資源認識等核心主題外，特別加入跨域 思維培養、科技管理產業趨勢認識、以及跨領域專題實作等內容，幫助本班學生在大學 初期即建立清晰的跨域學習藍圖。 課程採用互動式教學模式，每堂課包含 Check-in、短講、活動實作、總結與 Check-out 等環節，強調體驗式學習與同儕互動。每週搭配 2–3 篇 Harvard Business Review 文章作為職涯閱讀參考，培養商管思維與國際視野。 請輸入課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」至少 5 個, 每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文, 以半形 逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 跨域探索, 自我探索, 設計人生, 生涯規劃, 學習策略, 時間管理, 校園資源,表達溝通 指定用書 Textbooks 1. 學務處新生領航營新生手冊 2. 科管院學士班學生手冊（含彈性學制與跨域選課說明） 參考書籍 References 1. 《做自己的生命設計師》（Designing Your Life），Bill Burnett & Dave Evans 著 2. 《保持原來的樣子就很好了》，稻垣榮洋 著（2024） 3. 《跨能致勝》（Range: Why Generalists Triumph in a Specialized World），David Epstein 著 4. Harvard Business Review 指定文章（詳見各週教學進度） 教學方式 Teaching Approach 1. 互動式短講：每堂課安排 2 段主題短講（各 15–20 分鐘），介紹核心概念 2. 體驗式活動：運用 EYP 工具（九宮格、way-finding-map、生涯卡、奧德賽計畫等） 進行自我探索與生涯設計 3. 分組討論與合作學習：透過小組活動促進同儕互動與跨域對話 4. Show and Tell：每週安排學生進行以物件為導向的故事分享與公眾短講 5. HBR 閱讀與討論：每週指定 2–3 篇 Harvard Business Review 文章，課前閱讀、課 堂討論 6. 課外實作任務：包含拜訪教授、校園探索、參加活動等延伸學習 7. 期末跨域專題：以小組方式針對科管院學生面臨的真實問題進行研究與提案 National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 評分標準 Grading 作業 比例 內容 課堂參與及討論 20% 出席、分組討論、Show and Tell 短講、HBR 文章討論 自我探索與設計人生作業 15% 完成 EYP 工具作業：way-finding-map、奧德賽計畫等 拜訪教授心得 10% 邀請一位科管院或相關領域教授交流，撰寫 500 字心得 探索校園與跨域活動紀錄 10% 參加校內跨領域活動 1 次+探索校園特色地點 1 處 期中反思分享 15% 個人報告：分享開學以來的挑戰、收穫與跨域學習心 得，每人 5 分鐘 期末跨域專題 30% 小組專題：針對科管院學士班或清大學生面臨的問題， 進行研究並提出解決方案 教學進度 Course Schedule 週次 主題 教學活動 1 9/7 認識彼此與自我探索 § 相見歡：認識學校、清大跨域學制、認識科管 院學士班 § 破冰活動與建立心理安全感 § EYP 工具：九宮格、way-finding-map § 瞭解自我特質：MBTI 人格測試簡介 2 9/14 設計人生與跨域思維 § EYP 工具：生涯卡、奧德賽計畫 1.0 & 2.0 § 跨域思維導論：T 型人才素養 § 示範 Show and Tell 3 9/21 學習策略、AI 素養 與時間管理 § 有效學習法：做筆記、寫作業、準備考試策略 § 科管院跨域課程選課策略 § 學術倫理、著作權與 AIEYP 素養 § 時間管理與習慣養成 6 10/12 人際互動與跨域溝通 § 人際關係經營：同學/室友/師生關係 § 多元共融與跨文化溝通 § 簡報製作技巧與短講練習 § 期末專題題案說明 7 10/19 生涯探索與職涯規劃 § 科管院學長姊經驗分享（科技業、管顧、新創） § 跨域職涯：實習、工讀、專題、出國交換 § 履歷撰寫技巧：CV 格式、自我介紹 9 11/2 身心健康與壓力調適 § 正念體驗 § 身心健康與壓力調適策略 10 11/9 期中反思與狀況分享 § 學習成效檢核：回顧前十週歷程 § 分享校園資源使用經驗 § 同儕回饋與互助討論 § 專題提案 10 11/9 探索校園 15:30-17:20 § 清華走讀 (自由參加) 15 12/14 期末成果分享 § 小組期末跨域專題成果發表 § 個人學期反思：給下一屆科管院新生的 3 分鐘 National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 影片 § 課程回顧與未來展望 § 課程回饋問卷 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則 (Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) (2) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 本課程允許學生在以下條件下使用生成式 AI 工具： • 可使用 AI 工具輔助資料蒐集、文獻整理與腦力激盪 • 所有作業與報告的核心觀點與反思內容須為學生本人撰寫 • 使用 AI 輔助產出時，須於作業中標註使用方式與範圍 • 期末專題鼓勵探索 AI 工具在跨域問題解決中的應用，但須說明 AI 扮演的角色 課程相關連接 Course Related Links 清華大學探索學習中心（ExAlt）：https://exalt.nthu.edu.tw/ Harvard Business Review：https://hbr.org/ 科管院學士班網站：https://ipmt.site.nthu.edu.tw

Key presentation concepts and presentation skills will be introduced and reinforced. 課程目標 Course Objectives By the end of this course, students will be able to: 1. build understanding of their audience before their presentation. 2. create and outline structed presentation. 3. deliver their presentations clearly and concisely. 4. redefine their delivery style. 5. end their presentation with a strong and impressive conclusion. 6. demonstrate awareness of cultural and communicative conventions in global world. Learning about the audience - Methods of background information research - Addressing the audience -Role play -practice exercise 4 Engaging audience -use inclusive language - learn to emphasize -Role play -practice exercise 5 Types of outline -Introducing a new product -Recommending a new policy -Reporting on research -Reporting on feasibility -Creating your own outline 6 Preparing the format - Guidelines for laying out slides -prepare your slides -practice exercise 7 How to use visual aids - Different types of visual aid - Using language with visual aids -Role play -practice exercise Page 4 by Kwong Week Date Tentative course schedule Remarks / activities 8 Enhancing your delivery - Delivery essentials -Appearance -Voice -gestures -language style -Role play -practice exercise 9 Midterm exam (including a listening test + textbook material) 10 Presenting the content Introducing and explaining charts , graphs and pictures -emphasizing significant points Role play -practice exercise 11 Conclusion of presentation -Concluding with a summary -ending with a style Role play -practice exercise 12 Questions & Answer -How to answer questions -Construct your response Role play -practice exercise 13 Informative presentation Examples of informative personation Role play -practice exercise 14 Persuasive Presentation Examples of persuasive presentation Role play -practice exercise 15 Personal Oral Presentation (Informative /Persuasive) Personal Presentation 16 Final Exam (including a listening test+ textbook materials)

Course Credit: 3 Class Time: 15:30-18:20, Tuesday Session Location: TSMC Building 224 TA: 吳玟萱 lunahsuan@gapp.nthu.edu.tw Instructor: Tonny Menglun Kuo, Ph.D. (郭孟倫) Office: Rm. 617, TSMC Building Tel: (03)571-5131 ext. 42248 Email: tonny@gapp.nthu.edu.tw Office Hours: By appointment Prerequisite: Management 課程概述 Course description 科技的觸角，正無聲地探入管理的殿堂，它們的相遇，將譜寫出怎樣的未來序曲？在新 竹這片科技沃土就學的你，是否洞悉科技產業瞬息萬變的前瞻議題？近三年來，有哪些新興 科技被運用在產業中？當科技被應用到不同領域（如：行銷、財務、法律、生產、研發、供 應鏈），管理思維會發生哪些改變？這門課會是你走進這些議題的敲門磚。 本課程在延續科管院對產業前瞻視野的培養之外，新增系統性的研究方法訓練。課程以 研究設計為核心，引導學生掌握質性、量化與混合研究方法的基礎，並將其應用於管理與科 技議題的專題研究中。課程同時將生成式 AI 融入研究歷程的各個階段（文獻檢索、研究設 計、資料分析與學術寫作），培養學生運用 AI 解決問題、並負責任地查核與揭露 AI 使用的 能力。本課程的學生來自不同第一專長（經濟、計量財務、法律、管理等），課堂任務設計 保留領域選擇彈性，鼓勵學生從自身專業背景出發進行研究實作，同時在小組合作中促進跨 領域對話。課程結合新興科技報告、專題演講、企業參訪、履歷撰寫與期末專題海報展，讓 學生在理論與實務之間建立連結，最終完成一份具有研究架構的專題論文與成果海報。 課程目標 Course objectives 上過這門課程後，學生將能夠： 1. 辨別科技產業所面臨的管理議題，並運用研究方法提出系統性的分析策略。 2. 理解質性、量化與混合研究方法的差異，選擇適當的研究取徑進行專題研究。 3. 具備文獻探討、研究設計與學術寫作的基本能力，完成一篇專題論文。 4. 探索近年的新興科技，預想這些科技如何改變我們的未來工作與生活。 5. 透過小組合作與海報發表，培養學術溝通與團隊協作能力。 6. 比較學術與實務上的差異，準備好自己的履歷與職涯定位。 7. 在研究歷程中負責任地運用生成式 AI 輔助文獻檢索、研究設計與資料分析，並對 AI 產 出進行查核、批判與揭露。 成績考核 Evaluation 評分項目 比重 說明 課堂任務 30% 每週課堂實作任務，須於指定時間結束前上傳至教學平台 課堂小考 20% 根據上週的課堂內容，測驗主要核心概念 小組討論匯報 15% 以小組為單位之新興科技報告與論文工作坊進度報告；個人撰寫 之專題演講心得與企業參訪心得計入課堂任務 期末專題成果海報展 15% 邀請不同領域教師與業界專家擔任評審，進行公開評選 期末專題紙本論文 15% 以研究方法為架構撰寫之專題論文，須含完整研究設計 期末反思報告 5% 個人學期總結反思，回顧學習歷程與職涯規劃 備註：本課程有許多互動成分，除非有不可抗力因素外，本課程不接受請假。 2 教學方式 Learning methods 本課程結合不同的學習方式，包含：微型講授、小組討論、課堂任務、個案研究、專題演 講、企業參訪、校友訪談、AI 協作實作、期末海報展。 教學進度 Schedule Overview： ◎課表為預排參考，授課教師有權依進度及學生程度滾動調整內容◎ 週次 日期 主題 作業/備注 第一階段：研究方法與研究設計 1 9/8 課程概述與 研究方法導 論 § 課程介紹與自我介紹；分組（3-4 人一組） § 小組討論：列出 3 個你關心的管理與科技議題 § 課堂任務 1：填寫「研究興趣探索表」，寫下個人感興趣 的研究方向與初步想法，上傳至教學平台 2 9/15 文獻探討與 資料庫檢 索：如何 找、如何讀 一篇論文 § 概念講授：實證論文的結構（IMRaD）與閱讀策略：先讀 摘要、圖表與結論，再讀方法與討論 § 實作：使用學術資料庫（Google Scholar、華藝、Web of Science）與 AI 檢索工具（如 Elicit、Consensus、Semantic Scholar）平行檢索同一主題，比較兩者結果的差異與遺漏 § 幽靈引用查核：各組檢驗一份 AI 生成的參考文獻清單， 辨識哪些文獻不存在或內容遭扭曲，並記錄查核方法 § 練習文獻篩選與整理：每人找出 3 篇與專題相關的期刊論 文 § 課堂任務 2：完成文獻探討矩陣表（Literature Matrix）， 整理 3 篇文獻的作者、年份、研究目的、方法與主要發 現，並註明每篇的檢索來源與查核方式，上傳至教學平台 3 9/22 研究取徑概 論：質性、 量化與混合 方法 § 閱讀摘要分析：各組從第 2 週檢索到的文獻中挑出一篇質 性、一篇量化論文，比較其研究取徑差異 § 小組討論：三種研究取徑的適用情境 § 課堂任務 3：完成研究取徑比較表，比較質性/量化/混合方 法的特徵、優缺點與適用情境，上傳至教學平台 4 9/29 研究緒論與 目的陳述撰 寫 § 拆解範例論文 Introduction 段落結構：研究背景、問題陳 述、研究目的 § 寫作練習：撰寫自己專題的研究背景與問題陳述 § 同儕互評：兩兩交換，給予書面回饋 § 課堂任務 4：繳交緒論初稿（研究背景、問題陳述各一 段；研究目的先以一句話暫擬，待第 8 週研究問題定稿後 修訂），附上同儕回饋紀錄與修訂說明，上傳至教學平台 5 10/6 研究倫理、 學術寫作規 範與 AI 寫 作倫理 (線上) § 案例討論：分析研究倫理爭議案例（如：數據造假、知情 同意不足、以 AI 撰寫文獻探討卻引用不存在的文獻） § AI 與寫作倫理：作者權（APA 與主要期刊皆不接受 AI 列 為作者）、潤飾與代寫的界線、AI 偵測工具的限制、訪談 逐字稿與個人資料不得上傳至公開 AI 工具、查核責任在 作者 3 週次 日期 主題 作業/備注 § APA 格式練習：文內引用（單一作者、兩位作者、三位以 上）、直接引用與參考文獻格式，以及生成式 AI 內容的 引用與揭露格式 § 課堂任務 5：完成「APA 格式練習單」，含 5 題文內引 用改錯與 5 筆參考文獻格式撰寫；並撰寫自己專題的「AI 使用聲明」草稿（工具、用途、查核方式），上傳至教學 平台 6 10/13 理論框架的 建構與應用 § 案例分析：閱讀一篇應用理論框架的管理學論文，標示其 理論如何引導研究設計 § 小組討論：辨別不同理論（如資源基礎觀、創新擴散理 論、TAM）的應用場景 § 課堂任務 6：撰寫「我的理論框架初稿」（300 字），說 明專題擬採用的理論基礎與理由，同儕互評後修訂，上傳 至教學平台 7 10/20 質性與混合 研究方法 (李柏毅老師) § 概念講授：質性研究策略（個案研究、訪談、民族誌）、 混合方法設計類型 § 實作練習：為一個管理情境設計訪談大綱（5–8 題半結構 式訪談問題） § 小組討論：比較質性與量化取徑對同一議題的不同切入角 度 § 課堂任務 7：繳交專題的訪談大綱（5–8 題半結構式訪談 問題），並簡述預計訪談對象與招募方式，上傳至教學平 台 8 10/27 研究問題與 假設設計 § 範例分析：從 3 篇不同類型的論文中辨識其研究問題與假 設的寫法 § 寫作練習：為自己的專題撰寫 1–2 個研究問題（質性）或 研究假設（量化） § 小組討論：互相檢視研究問題的聚焦性與可行性 § 課堂任務 8：繳交「研究問題/假設定稿」，附上修訂歷程 說明（原版→同儕回饋→修訂版），上傳至教學平台 9 11/3 量化研究設 計與 AI 輔 助分析 § 概念講授：實驗設計、調查研究、變數操作化、抽樣方法 § AI 輔助設計：請 AI 針對一個管理議題提出實驗或問卷設 計，各組找出其中的干擾變數、測量效度與抽樣問題並修 正 § 實作練習：設計一份簡易問卷（5 題 Likert 量表），針對 一個管理議題；以 AI 生成模擬資料進行描述統計與視覺 化（R 或 AI 資料分析功能皆可），並討論如何驗證 AI 的 分析結果 § 小組討論：檢視問卷題目的信效度與可行性 § 課堂任務 9：繳交研究方法章節初稿（500 字，含研究設 計、研究對象、資料蒐集方式與分析方法）與量化研究工 具設計練習（研究變數定義、問卷或測量工具草稿、抽樣 4 週次 日期 主題 作業/備注 計畫說明），並註明 AI 參與的部分與查核方式，上傳至 教學平台 第二階段：新興科技趨勢與專題演講 10 11/10 新興產業科 技報告(I)： 技術與產業 落地 § § 新興科技趨勢報告（每組 12 分鐘簡報+ 4 分鐘 Q&A） i. 生成式 AI 應用：從理解到落地 ii. AI 趨勢下我國機器人產業發展之挑戰與機會 iii. 我國矽光子技術發展之探討 iv. 國際電池技術發展現況及我國電池產業發展 v. 我國再生醫療未來發展之挑戰 vi. 綠電時代虛擬電廠供電服務技術與市場機制 § 課堂任務 10：撰寫「新興科技報告回饋與反思」（300 字），分析報告中最具啟發的觀點及其對你專題方向的影 響，上傳至教學平台 11 11/17 專題演講(I) § 演講前準備：各組針對講者背景與產業趨勢準備 3 個提 問 § 演講中紀錄：記錄講者的核心觀點與產業洞見 § 課堂任務 11：撰寫專題演講心得與反思（300 字），連結 演講內容與個人研究主題或職涯規劃，上傳至教學平台 § 課外任務指派：「清華學長姐／產業前輩採訪」與「個人 履歷檔案」初稿，請於第 13 週前完成（詳見作業說明） 12 11/24 新興產業科 技報告 (II)：制 度、資源與 地緣政治 § 新興科技趨勢報告（每組 12 分鐘簡報+ 4 分鐘 Q&A） i. 強化我國碳定價機制與國際關聯性之探討 ii. 臺灣水資源的安全管理與永續發展之探討 iii. 川普能源戰略對油氣市場與氣候治理之影響分析 iv. 川普主義重塑國際地緣政治秩序之探討 v. 國際局勢變遷下之全球金融、貨幣與經貿之挑戰 vi. 臺灣新創生態系之優化策略 vii. 提升女性投入科研和科技產業之策略 § 課堂任務 12：撰寫新興科技報告回饋與反思（300 字）， 聚焦該科技對管理實務的影響與研究潛力，上傳至教學平 台 13 12/1 企業參訪 § 參訪前：蒐集企業背景資料，各組設計 3–5 個高層次提問 § 參訪中：記錄企業運營模式、科技應用與管理挑戰 § 課堂任務 13：繳交企業參訪心得報告（400 字），分析該 企業的科技應用策略並反思對專題研究的啟發；同步繳交 「清華學長姐／產業前輩採訪報告」與「個人履歷檔案」 初稿（詳見作業說明），上傳至教學平台 第三階段：期末專題 14 12/8 論文個別討 論 § 實作：教師與每組學生進行個別論文討論（每組約 5–10 分鐘），聚焦於研究主題明確性、研究問題設定、理論架 構與資料來源可行性 5 週次 日期 主題 作業/備注 § 課堂任務 14：繳交一份約 500 字的論文進度說明，內容包 含：目前研究主題與研究問題、已完成的進度（如文獻整 理、初步架構）、遇到的主要困難、下一階段的具體規劃 （至少 3 項行動）；同步上傳目前版本之研究構想或初稿 （如研究計畫書、文獻整理筆記）至教學平台 15 12/15 專題演講 (II) +論文工作 坊 Jason 學長：現職 Google 客戶經理、22 歲錄取哥大 MBA！分 享：高效成長 x 外商職涯 x 留學申請 專題演講（前半堂）：演講前準備提問、演講中紀錄核心觀點 論文工作坊（後半堂）：各組報告專題進度，交換論文草稿進 行同儕互評；「AI 當審稿人」練習：請 AI 以期刊審稿人身分 評論自己的草稿，再逐條判斷哪些意見有效、哪些為誤判 履歷同儕審閱：兩兩交換履歷與作品集，給予具體建議（詳見 作業說明） 課堂任務 15：繳交專題論文完整草稿（含導論、文獻探討、研 究方法章節），附上同儕回饋紀錄、「AI 審稿人」意見評估表 與專題演講心得，上傳至教學平台 16 12/22 期末專題成 果海報展 § 海報展形式：各組製作學術海報，於公開場地展示 § 邀請不同領域教師與業界專家擔任評審，進行提問與評分 § 各組進行 5 分鐘海報口頭簡報+ 5 分鐘評審提問 § 繳交期末專題紙本論文定稿（含完整研究架構與「AI 使用 聲明」附錄） § 繳交期末反思報告（750 字），回顧學習歷程、最大挑 戰、所學技能、本學期運用 AI 的經驗與省思，以及職涯 應用規劃 § 繳交同儕審閱修訂後的「個人履歷檔案定稿」（中英文各 一份） § 以上皆上傳至教學平台 6 生成式 AI 倫理聲明 Ethical Statement of Generative AI 基於透明與負責任的原則，本課程鼓勵學生利用 AI 進行協作或互學，以提升本門課產出 品質。根據本校公布的「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採取： 「有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出」 學生須於課堂作業或報告中的「標題頁註腳」或「引用文獻後」簡要說明如何使用生成 式 AI 進行議題發想、文句潤飾或結構參考等使用方式。若經查核使用卻無在作業或報告中標 明，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。本門課授課教材 或學習資料若有引用自生成式 AI，教師也將在投影片或口頭標注。本課程各項作業對生成式 AI 的具體規範如下表；期末專題論文須另附「AI 使用聲明」附錄，說明使用之工具、用 途、查核方式與未使用 AI 的部分。 使用類別 具體情境 要求 鼓勵使用 文獻檢索與主題探索、腦力激盪與 研究問題發想、程式除錯與資料視 覺化、語言潤飾與翻譯、模擬審稿 與自我檢核 仍須於作業中簡要揭露；AI 提供 的文獻、數據與引文須回到原始來 源查核後方可使用 有條件使用 （須揭露） 任何進入繳交文件的 AI 生成或改寫 內容：摘要、文獻整理、問卷題 目、訪談大綱、分析結果詮釋、簡 報文字與圖表 於標題頁註腳或參考文獻後說明工 具、用途與查核方式；期末論文另 附「AI 使用聲明」附錄；學生須 能口頭說明所有繳交內容 禁止使用 將訪談錄音、逐字稿、受訪者或企 業之個人資料與未公開資訊上傳至 公開 AI 工具；未經查核即引用 AI 生成的文獻或數據；以 AI 代寫反思 報告、採訪報告等以個人經驗為核 心之作業；課堂小考使用 AI 違反者依本校學術倫理規範處理， 該作業得重新評分或不予計分 AI 產出中的錯誤、捏造文獻、不當引用或資料外洩，一律視為作者本人之責任。教師得 於任何作業繳交後要求學生口頭說明其研究歷程與 AI 使用方式。修讀本課程之學生於選課時 視為同意以上倫理聲明。 作業規範與任務 (教師有權依照進度滾動調整內容) 作業 任務內容 反思鷹架 新興科技趨 勢報告（第 10、12 週） 1. 各組於第 10 或 12 週就分配主題進行 15 分鐘 簡報 + 5 分鐘 Q&A，主題於第 1 週分組後由 教師分配。 2. 內容須涵蓋：科技概況與近三年產業應用、管 理思維的改變、該科技與 AI 的交互影響（AI 如何加速、取代或改變該科技的應用，以及伴 隨的風險）、對管理實務與未來研究的啟示。 3. 資料來源至少包含 2 篇學術文獻與 2 份產業 報告或權威媒體報導，並以 APA 第七版列 出。 § AI 在你們蒐集資 料時，哪一次給 了錯誤或過時的 資訊？你們是怎 麼發現的？ § 這項科技與 AI 結 合後，管理者最 需要重新思考的 是什麼？ 7 作業 任務內容 反思鷹架 4. 簡報末頁附「AI 使用與查核說明」：使用了哪 些工具、用於哪些工作（檢索、摘要、翻譯、 製圖等）、哪些資訊經人工查核並與原始來源 比對。 5. 聽眾填寫同儕回饋表（含資料來源可信度與 AI 使用透明度），作為小組討論匯報成績之參 考。 § 若要把這個主題 發展成專題研 究，可行的研究 問題是什麼？ 清華學長姐/ 產業前輩採 訪（第 13 週 繳交） 1. 選定一位清華校友或理想產業的前輩進行訪 談，訪談請以面對面為主。 2. 請拍攝一張合照（或使用前輩的形象照）。 3. 訪談問題建議包含：選擇工作的動機、目前的 工作內容、工作的魅力與成就感、產業進入門 檻與技能要求、職涯發展路徑、產業挑戰與挫 折經驗、對未來從業者的建議。 4. 訪談錄音與逐字稿含受訪者個資，不得上傳至 公開 AI 工具；如以 AI 協助整理或潤飾內容， 須先去識別化，並取得受訪者同意後於報告中 揭露。 5. 完成圖文並茂的專業報告，發佈於 LinkedIn， 並提交至教學平台。 § 這位前輩的經驗 如何幫助你做職 涯選擇？ § 訪談中哪些建議 最具行動性？ § 這個產業的實際 挑戰與你想像的 有何不同？ 個人履歷檔 案（第 11 週 指派、第 13 週初稿、第 15 週同儕審 閱、第 16 週 定稿） 1. 撰寫中、英文版履歷各一份，履歷需包含基本 資料、教育背景、專業技能、重要經歷、專案 或成果。 2. 準備個人作品集，內容可包括：課堂專案、研 究報告、實習成果或其他能展現能力的作品。 3. 根據目標產業或職位的標準修改履歷與作品 集，確保格式與內容符合國際或台灣產業規 範。可使用 AI 協助潤飾語句或對照職缺要求， 但經歷與成果須真實，且不得上傳他人個資。 4. 第 13 週繳交初稿；第 15 週課堂中找兩位同學 審閱你的履歷與作品集，請他們提供具體建 議。請將他們的建議列點紀錄，一併上傳到教 學平台。 5. 根據同學建議修正檔案，完成履歷與作品集的 第二版。 6. 第 16 週提交更新後版本至教學平台，並同步更 新 LinkedIn 檔案。 § 你的履歷是否清 楚展現核心能 力？ § 是否有空缺的技 能或經歷需要提 前補足？ § 這些建議如何幫 助你更好地展現 專業？ § 哪些部分的修改 最能提升你的履 歷競爭力？ § 你的 LinkedIn 專 業形象是否更清 晰了？ 期末專題海 報展 1. 形式：各組製作一張學術研究海報（建議尺寸 A0 或 90cm × 120cm），內容涵蓋研究背景、 研究問題、研究方法、預期結果或初步發現、 結論與建議。 § 在製作海報的過 程中，你如何決 定哪些研究內容 該保留、哪些該 捨棄？這個取捨 過程讓你對自己 8 作業 任務內容 反思鷹架 2. 評審機制： 邀請不同領域的教師（2–3 位）與 業界專家（1–2 位）組成評審團，依據以下評 量規準進行評分： 評分面向 比重 評分重點 研究設計 30% 研究問題明確性、方法適切 性、理論基礎 海報呈現 20% 視覺設計、資訊架構、圖表 運用 口頭報告 20% 表達清晰度、時間掌控、團 隊合作 回應提問 20% 對評審提問的理解與回應品 質 AI 使用透 明度與資 料查核 10% AI 使用聲明完整、引用文獻 與數據可追溯、能說明查核 過程 的研究有什麼新 的理解？ § 面對不同領域的 評審提問時，你 是否發現自己的 研究有哪些盲點 是在同領域討論 中不容易察覺 的？ § 你的小組如何分 工完成海報？每 位成員的專長背 景在這個過程中 分別發揮了什麼 作用？ § 觀摩其他組的海 報後，有哪些研 究設計或呈現方 式值得你未來借 鏡？ 期末專題紙 本論文規範 格式要求： § 字數：3,000–5,000 字（不含參考文獻與附錄） § 格式：APA 第七版 § 結構：標題頁、摘要、導論（含研究背景、問 題陳述、研究目的）、文獻探討、研究方法、 預期結果或初步發現、結論與建議、參考文 獻、附錄「AI 使用聲明」（使用之工具、用 途、查核方式與未使用 AI 的部分；未使用者亦 須聲明） § 繳交方式： 第 16 週上課前上傳電子檔至教學 平台，並於海報展當天繳交紙本。 § 回顧你從第 1 週 的研究興趣探索 表到最終論文的 歷程，你的研究 主題經歷了哪些 轉變？是什麼促 使你做出這些調 整？ § 在撰寫論文的過 程中，你認為第 一階段學到的哪 一個研究方法概 念對你幫助最 大？為什麼？ § 你的第一專長背 景如何影響了你 選擇的研究取徑 與分析方式？如 果換一個學科視 角，你的研究可 能會有什麼不同 的切入點？ 9 作業 任務內容 反思鷹架 § 同儕互評與「AI 審稿人」收到的 回饋中，哪一條 對你的論文修訂 影響最深？你如 何判斷該意見是 否成立？ 期末反思報 告 § 撰寫期末總結反思報告（750 字）。 § 內容需回答：本學期你印象最深刻的學習經 驗、遇到的最大挑戰與解決過程、學到最多的 技能或知識、本學期運用 AI 的經驗（AI 在哪 些地方幫了你、哪一次誤導了你、你如何發現 與判斷）、如何將本課所學應用於職涯發展。 § 報告需具體、誠懇且有行動計畫。 § 第 16 週上傳至教學平台。 § 哪個作業或活動 最讓你有成就 感？ § SAGE Publications. 陳曉萍、鄭伯壎、沈偉、黃敏萍(2024)。組織與管理研究的實證方法，第四版。台北：華泰 文化。 鈕文英(2023)。質性研究方法與論文寫作，第四版。台北：雙葉書廊。 參考書籍與網址： § 從邊緣到核心：台灣半導體如何成為世界的心臟 § 社會與經濟：信任、權力與制度 § 組織創新五十年：台灣飛利浦的跨世紀轉型 § 數據長與數據驅動型組織：擁抱大數據時代的衝擊 § 為什麼我們這樣對話，那樣生活？：當個超級溝通者，解鎖與他人連結的祕密語言 § 愈忙愈要會表達：讓自己受重用、點子被採用的解說藝術 § 破框思維的技術 § 為什麼對方總是聽不懂？：認知科學為你揭曉溝通的本質與解決方案 § 我全都要：顛覆大腦二選一慣性的進階思維 § 基恩斯的高附加價值經營──卓越管理篇：日本新首富管理世界頂級企業的原則 § AI 時代生存聖經：AI 時代的我們將如何生活、如何工作？ § 慢速工作力：快時代的慢技術，3 大原則擺脫倦怠、鍛造更高成就 § 上位思維：從當上主管到成為領導人，上千位執行長最想告訴你的事 § 隱性潛能：華頓商學院最具影響力教授，突破天賦極限的實證科學 § 目的與獲利：ESG 大師塞拉分的企業永續發展策略 § 晶片戰爭 § 決勝矽紀元 § 萬物藍圖 10 § 重新想像資本主義 § 信義學 § 天下雜誌 https://www.cw.com.tw/ § 數位時代 https://www.bnext.com.tw § 經濟日報 https://money.udn.com § MIT Sloan Management Review https://sloanreview.mit.edu § Harvard Business Review https://hbr.org/ § California Management Review https://cmr.berkeley.edu 本課程對應之學習目標與核心能力： 運用專業管理與科技知識的能力。 Our students will master the knowledge of technology and professional management. 20% 整合與活用第一專長及第二專長的專業知識能力，並具備跨領域規劃、領導與執行 團隊合作的能力。 Our students will be able to integrate expertise from their double specialty and thus plan, execute and lead in an interdisciplinary team setting. 20% 具備中文及英文閱讀寫作商業報告與商業口頭簡報能力。 Our students will be able to read and produce professional business documents as well as deliver a professional oral presentation in English and in Chinese. 20% 認識產業的國際發展趨勢，瞭解管理與科技對環境、社會及全球的影響，並培養自 我學習成長的能力。 Our students will develop the ability of self-learning by comprehending the international development trend of the industry and by comprehending the impact of management and technology made on the environment, the society and the world. 30% 理解專業倫理及社會責任的能力。 Our students will be equipped with understandings of professional ethics and social responsibility. 10%

docs.text: NATIONAL TSING HUA UNIVERSITY College of Technology Management Interdisciplinary Program of Management and Technology Human Resource Management (Offered in English) Fall Semester 2026 Professor: Hua-Wei Hung (hwhung@mx.nthu.edu.tw) Teaching Assistant: Amy Hoang (hoangphuonglinh281107@gmail.com) Time: Monday 14:20-17:00 (W6W7W8) Classroom: TSMC building Room#421 Office hours: Please email to make an appointment Course Objectives: This course explores HR's central, strategic role in making organizations competitive. This course focuses on the concepts and practices of human resource management, namely recruitment and selection of employees, equal opportunity, training and development, performance appraisals, compensation, and benefits issues. A special focus on the increase of globalization and workforce diversity in the high-performance organization is also included. By the end of this course, students should be able to: 1) Describe the functions of HR management. 2) Provide examples of the new management practices that are changing HR management. 3) Illustrate how building employee commitment can be a cornerstone of an employer's HR philosophy. 4) Present the basic processes for: developing job specifications; recruiting, interviewing, and placement of employees; compensation and benefits plans; and conducting performance appraisals. 5) Outline the organization's role in the career management process. 6) Explain employee mobility. 7) Understand the impact of globalization on HR management. Teaching Arrangements: Class sessions may include lectures and small and large discussion groups. We will strive to clarify, supplement, and analyze text materials. You are responsible for all assigned readings and all materials presented in class. You are also responsible for all information disseminated in class and all course requirements, including deadlines. Lectures: Each lecture is about 1.5 hours. Please note that all lectures will be taught in English. Topic Presentation (30 minutes):  Presentation (20 minutes): All students will come up with topics they are interested in related to human resources. Some potential topics include how to write a resume, how to write a cover letter, how to dress professionally, how to prepare for an interview, MBTI, etc.  Each group will present fruitful information on this topic that helps deepen the understanding of this topic, some key indications, managerial inspiration, and/or any other issues that you want to share with the class.  Activity (10 minutes): Each group will prepare a small activity to allow interaction with audiences that is related to your topic, be creative. Case Presentation (30 minutes):  Case presentation (20 minutes): Each group will choose a case to present in class, which should include the content and solution of a specific managerial situation. Please upload your case presentation 10 pm before the day you are presenting, so the group preparing to ask questions will have time to review your material.  Q&A (10 minutes): Other groups must prepare at least three questions to discuss with the presenting group. Guest Speaker Reflection  Students are required to write a reflection (1-2 pages) that captures their personal learning and critical thinking about the talk. Your reflection should go beyond simply summarizing the talk - it should demonstrate engagement with the ideas presented and connect them to your own knowledge, experience, or future aspirations.  In addition, attendance will be taken at the start of the invited talk. You must be present for the entire session to be eligible to submit your reflection, unless you have notified me in advance and received approval for your absence. Midterm Individual Essay:  Think of a company/job that you wish to go to in the future.  Conduct research on the company’s corporate culture. What kind of talent are they looking for? What is the job design and description of the position you want to apply for? What are your interview strategies to highlight your value?  Develop a one-page company overview (be concise and to the point), a one-page cover letter, a two-page statement of purpose, and one page with 3 expected interview questions and how you would respond (scoring depends on depth of response).  Conditional accept: AI only when the AI screenshot report is attached, which will also affect the grading. Final Group Presentation (30 minutes):  Select two companies from the same industry. Analyze the characteristics of their HRM and what they need to do to find the right people (their HRM strategies). Analyze how their HRM strategies are different (what aspects are the same and what is different). What are the current operational strengths and weaknesses and how can they be improved (learn from other companies in the same industry)? Final Group Report:  In addition to an oral presentation, a printed paper report must also be submitted. This report will put your presentation into words and should be between 8 and 14 pages.  If AI is utilized, screenshots of conversations with the AI must be included.  APA format: 12 font Times New Roman, 1/1.5 leading, PDF file.  No plagiarism; shall also attach with the Turnitin report (acceptable similarity percentage: below 15%) (please register in advance through NTHU Library: https://learning.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/412- 1319-7120.php?Lang=en)  Conditional accept: AI only when the AI screenshot report is attached, which will also affect the grading. Assessment:  Class Participation: 10%, Case Presentation: 15%, Topic Presentation: 15%, Guest Speaker Reflection: 5%, Midterm Individual Essay: 30%, Final Group Presentation: 10%, Final Group Report: 15%.  Assessing materials are required to be uploaded on eeclass in advance, with less tolerance for additional adjustment/improvement after the deadline (need to be discussed). Audience Scoring will be conducted in class, with group-based scoring from other groups to value each criterion; Peer Scoring will be managed within a group, and each group member will evaluate teammates’ contributions individually. No roll-call in class, therefore you get your participation by speak-up during class, or you may also share your ideas on eeclass.  Sometimes there will be spontaneous pop-up quizzes. Pop-up quiz: this quiz will cover the materials taught in the previous lectures, the top three students who get the highest score will get cards, which will count towards the participation (1st get three cards, 2nd get two cards, and 3rd get 1 card). Assessment Grading Percentage Assessing Approach Marking criterion Class Participation 10% In-class Speak-up Off-class reflection (on eeclass) • Raise in-depth discussion • Provide interesting viewpoint Guest Speaker Reflection 5% 100% Lecturer Scoring • Attendance required Case Presentation 15% 50% Lecturer Scoring + 50% Audience Scoring * Presentation slide shall be uploaded on eeclass • Fruitful Information • Presentation Fluency • Slide Layout • Persuasiveness • Interesting viewpoint Topic Presentation 15% 50% Lecturer Scoring + 50% Audience Scoring * Presentation slide shall be uploaded on eeclass • Logical analysis and discussion • Presentation Fluency • Slide Layout • Interesting viewpoint • Creative interaction Midterm Individual Essay 30% 100% Lecturer Scoring * Essay shall be uploaded on eeclass • Persuasiveness • Fruitful Information • Interesting ideas • In-Depth analysis Final Group Presentation 10% 70% Lecturer Scoring + 30% Audience Scoring * Presentation slide shall be uploaded on eeclass • Logical analysis and discussion • Presentation Fluency • Slide Layout • Interesting viewpoint Final Group Report 15% 100% Lecturer Scoring * Essay shall be uploaded on eeclass • Persuasiveness • Fruitful Information • Interesting ideas • In-Depth analysis Ethics Statement on Generative Artificial Intelligence: Grounded in the principles of transparency and responsibility, this course encourages students to leverage AI for collaboration and mutual learning to enhance the quality of course outputs. In accordance with the published Guidelines for Collaboration, Co-learning, and Cultivation of Artificial Intelligence Competencies in University Education, this course adopts the following policy: Conditionally open. Students must briefly explain how generative AI was used for topic ideation, sentence refinement, or structural reference in the footnotes of the title page or after the reference in their assignments or reports. If usage is discovered without proper disclosure, instructors, the institution, or relevant units have the right to reevaluate the assignment, report, or withhold scores. The cost center that paid its way. Harvard Business Review, 80(4), 5-12. 04) Michael D. Watkins. (2012). How managers become leaders. Harvard Business Review, 1-15. 05) Roelofsen, E., & Yue, T. (2019). Bad blood on the senior team. Harvard Business Review, 97(1), 145-149. 10) Nofsinger, Mary M., & Betty J. Galbraith. (2000). Streamlining the hiring process. National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus This course focuses on the management and improvement of supply chain processes and performance, providing a comprehensive foundation for students interested in pursuing a career in various sectors, including consulting, operations, marketing, or finance within manufacturing or distribution firms. Throughout the course, we will delve into essential supply chain metrics that are critical for assessing performance and making informed decisions. Students will learn about the primary trade-offs involved in supply chain decision-making, equipping them with the analytical skills necessary to navigate complex scenarios. Basic tools for effective and efficient supply chain management will be introduced, covering key areas such as production planning, inventory control, order fulfillment, and supply chain coordination. In addition to these foundational elements, we will explore advanced topics that are increasingly relevant in today’s global marketplace. This includes global supply chain design, where students will learn how to strategically structure supply chains to optimize efficiency and responsiveness. We will also examine logistics and outsourcing strategies, discussing how companies can leverage external partnerships to enhance their supply chain capabilities. Furthermore, the course will investigate several recent innovations in supply chain management, including the integration of technology and data analytics, which are transforming traditional practices and driving competitive advantage. By the end of this course, students will have gained a robust understanding of the complexities of supply chain management and will be well-prepared to apply their knowledge in real-world settings, ultimately contributing to the success of their future organizations. 請輸入課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」至少 5 個, 每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文, 以半形逗 點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) • 供應鏈(Supply Chain) • 供應鏈管理(Supply Chain Management) • 物流管理(Logistics management) • 管理(Management) • 策略(Strategy) 指定用書 Textbooks Designing and Managing the Supply Chain: Concepts, Strategies and Case Studies (third edition) National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 教學方式 Teaching Approach & 評分標準 Grading The grade in this course will be based on class participation, group case studies and reports, and lecture summaries and comments. • Class Participation and Discussions: 50% • Group Case Reports: 40% o Company Introduction 5 min o Supply Chain Management 25 min o Q&A 5 min o Note: Each team needs to provide the materials of presentation for TA by last Friday.
