docs.text: 1 [Please respect intellectual property rights. Do not infringe copyrights.] IPMT301100 Marketing Management: Service, Technology & Innovation (行銷管理：整合服務、科技與創新) Interdisciplinary Program of Management and Technology (IPMT) College of Technology Management, National Tsing Hua University Course credit: 3 Class Time: 14:20-17:20, Wednesday Session Location: TSMC Building 223 Email: tonny@gapp.nthu.edu.tw Instructor: Tonny Menglun Kuo, Ph.D. (郭孟倫) Office: Rm. 617, TSMC Building Tel: (03)571-5131 ext. 42248 TA: Jesselyn Gracia (蔡艷真) Office Hours: by appointment TA Email: selyngracia@gmail.com Course Description In a world where digital innovation evolves at lightning speed, marketing has become more than just product promotion—it’s about designing experiences, telling compelling stories, and leveraging emerging technologies. This course equips undergraduate students with a solid foundation in marketing strategy, covering essential topics such as STP (Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning), branding, pricing, channel design, and integrated marketing communications (IMC). Beyond the fundamentals, students will explore how service robots and chatbots, generative AI, live commerce, and immersive VR/Web3 technologies are transforming customer engagement. We will read and discuss cutting-edge conceptual papers and strategic frameworks to help shape a forward-thinking blueprint for the ever-evolving world of marketing. Trust-building, responsible use of AI, and sustainability are treated as cross-cutting criteria in project work, helping students understand marketing’s expanding role in both business and society. Through interactive lectures, case studies, weekly quizzes, authentic mini-tasks, hands-on VR building workshops, and a final team project, students will develop strategic thinking and creative agility to solve real-world marketing challenges—and gain the confidence to lead in the marketing landscape of tomorrow. Course Objectives After taking this course, students will be able to: 1. Understand and apply core marketing strategies such as the 4Ps, 7Ps, STP, customer value, and market orientation to develop customer-centric marketing plans. 2. Analyze consumer behavior and interpret marketing research data (qualitative and quantitative) to make evidence-based marketing decisions. 3. Design marketing strategies related to product lifecycle, brand management, pricing, and omnichannel promotion based on customer insights. 4. Evaluate and implement technological tools (e.g., generative AI, chatbots and service robots, VR) to enhance service design, customer experience, and relationship marketing. 5. Critically examine emerging marketing trends such as the metaverse, Web3/NFTs, and live commerce, and propose responsible, sustainable, and value-driven marketing innovations. 2 Class Policies § Attendance Policy: Missing two or more classes will result in an automatic failing grade (F) for this course. If you must be absent due to unavoidable circumstances, please notify me in advance. Excused absences will be considered on a case-by-case basis (e.g., medical leave with official documentation from a hospital). Attendance is therefore a prerequisite for passing rather than a graded component; the Participation and Contribution grade (20%) reflects the quality of in-class engagement, not mere presence. § Punctuality: Being late is disruptive to the learning environment and is therefore strongly discouraged. Please make every effort to arrive on time. § Academic Integrity: Any form of academic dishonesty—such as cheating, misrepresentation, or plagiarism—will result in a failing grade. Be sure to properly cite and acknowledge all sources to avoid unintentional plagiarism. There is zero tolerance for academic misconduct. § Communication: I welcome open communication. If you have questions, concerns, or simply want to talk about your learning, please don’t hesitate to reach out to me at any time. § Let’s enjoy this semester together! Looking forward to a meaningful and engaging journey with you all. Learning Methods The course combines different learning methods: mini lectures, group discussions, case studies, weekly quizzes, authentic mini-tasks, an industry guest lecture, and project-based learning with hands-on VR building (Module III). Grading Participation and Contribution 20% Mini-Tasks 20% Leading discussions on readings assigned 5% Quizzes 20% Midterm Project 15% Final Project 20% Notes on grading components Mini-Tasks: short authentic tasks completed in or right after class in Modules I–II, plus the Weekly Artifacts of Module III (Weeks 13–15). Weekly Artifacts are graded here and are not counted again in the Final Project. Quizzes: short pre-class or in-class quizzes on the assigned chapter in every lecture week (Weeks 2– 9 and 11). The two lowest quiz scores are dropped. Leading discussions on readings: each team leads one discussion of an assigned research reading in Week 9 or Week 11. Readings are posted on the course platform at least two weeks in advance. Midterm Project and Final Project: see the Midterm Team Marketing Project Guidelines and Final Project Guidelines below. 3 Schedule Overview # Date Topic Key Concepts / Deliverables I. Introduction to Marketing & Strategies 1 Sep 9 Introduction to Marketing and Strategic Planning Holistic Marketing, G-STIC Framework, Strategic Business Units (SBUs), BCG Matrix, 5-C Framework, Marketing Philosophy Evolution 2 Sep 16 Consumer Insights & Marketing Research Consumer Decision Journey, Marketing Research Process, Qualtrics, Marketing Metrics, Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM), Brand Strength, CPA/CPC/CPM, Forecasting Market Demand 3 Sep 23 Segmentation, Targeting, and Positioning (STP) Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning, Value Proposition, 3-V Principle (Customer, Collaborator, Company) 4 Sep 30 Branding & Value Proposition Design Brand Image, Brand Elements, Brand Personality, Value Creation 5 Oct 7 Product and Service Strategy Product Mix Decisions (Width, Length, Depth, Consistency), Line Stretching, Service Characteristics (Intangibility, Inseparability, Variability, Perishability), Service Profit Chain, 7Ps of Services Marketing 6 Oct 14 Pricing Strategy Pricing and Revenue Management, Differential Pricing 7 Oct 21 Distribution and Omnichannel Marketing Channel Design Decisions, Channel Conflict, Value Delivery Networks, Logistics & Supply Chain, 3PL, RFID, omnichannel strategy. 8 Oct 28 Integrated Marketing Communication Promotion Mix, PESO Media Model (Paid, Earned, Shared, Owned), Content Marketing, Communication Process, Live Commerce & Influencer Marketing II. Emerging Technologies, Industry Practice & Service Applications 9 Nov 4 Generative AI in Marketing Mind perception, algorithm adaptivity, algorithm predictability/creativity, product outcome range (POR), prompt engineering, MADE framework (mapping, assembling, demonstrating, executing), experimental stimuli, ecological validity, image generation tools 10 Nov 11 Industry Guest Lecture: Brands and Differentiation Guest Speaker: Claudia Lin Founder, WINspiration Brand & Marketing Consultancy | Former Account Director, Ogilvy Taiwan | Former Director of Brand Marketing, TTFB Group Claudia Lin is a brand and marketing professional with over 20 years of experience in brand consulting, integrated marketing communications, and management. She has worked with multinational and local brands across diverse industries, including food and beverage, travel, fashion, finance, and healthcare. As the founder of WINspiration Brand & Marketing Consultancy and a Brand Champion, she specializes in helping organizations identify their distinctive value and translate it into meaningful brand communication. Lecture Topic: How Can Brands Create Meaningful Differentiation? (2 hours) Drawing on real-world industry cases, this session explores how brands identify meaningful differentiation, develop 4 # Date Topic Key Concepts / Deliverables compelling value propositions, and communicate their unique value to the market. Students will be introduced to practical frameworks, including the Brand Lighthouse and PESO Media Model. The third hour is an instructor- led debrief and mini-task in which teams apply the Brand Lighthouse and PESO frameworks to their midterm proposals. 11 Nov 18 Chatbot & Robotics Technology social actors, human–robot interaction (HRI), functional vs. experiential tasks, social presence, persuasion, service robots, warmth & competence, cobotic service teams, power dynamics, leader power perception, human–robot collaboration (HRC) Preparing students for designing tech-enabled service interactions in the VR module. 12 Nov 25 Midterm Project Presentation § Presentation slides III. Immersive Marketing in Metaverse This module adopts a constructionist learning approach where students learn by building shareable VR artifacts. 13 Dec 2 Deconstructing Service Experiences & Intro to VR Microworlds Key concepts: service blueprinting, customer journey mapping, VR microworlds, constructionist learning, Web3/NFTs and digital ownership in the metaverse. Weekly Artifact: § VR Customer Journey Mini-Room (Spatial project) 14 Dec 9 Building the Initial VR Service Environment (Prototype) Key concepts: servicescape design, spatial presence and embodiment, low-code VR prototyping (Spatial), design rationale. Weekly Artifact: § VR Service Space Prototype 1.0 § A one-page design rationale explaining key choices. 15 Dec 16 User Testing (Firsthand Data) + Reflection-on- Action Key concepts: user testing protocols, think-aloud, analysing firsthand data, reflection-on-action. Weekly Artifact: § User Testing Record Sheet § Reflection Memo (1 page) § VR Prototype 2.0 16 Dec 23 Final Presentation & Service Tech Strategy Key concepts: service technology strategy, business case for immersive experiences, pitching to stakeholders. Weekly Artifact: § Final VR Service Environment (Spatial) § Marketing / Service Tech Strategy Deck (3–5 pages) Textbook Albrecht, M. G., Green, M., & Hoffman, L. (2023). Principles of marketing. OpenStax. https://openstax.org/details/books/principles-marketing (This is open textbook. You can have access to the book for free) Kotler, P., Keller, K. L., & Chernev, A. (2022). Marketing management (16th ed., Global ed.). Pearson. 5 Midterm Team Marketing Project Guidelines Instruction The midterm assessment for this course will be conducted through a team-based marketing project. Each team will develop a year-long integrated marketing campaign and propose its own marketing budget, justified by the sales and demand forecast. This campaign may consist of a series of smaller, interrelated activities. The plan should center on the product, service, or brand chosen by the team (to be confirmed with the instructor) and develop a well-rounded and actionable marketing proposal. Content: The report should begin with a comprehensive Situation Analysis, identifying key market demands, focus areas, or problem points. Based on this analysis, students are expected to set marketing objectives and strategies accordingly. A tailored Marketing Mix should be developed to support these goals. Students are encouraged to integrate experiential design, compelling brand storytelling, or emerging technologies to enhance the innovation and impact of their proposal. A financial plan must also be included, with estimations of expected sales, a feasible budget breakdown, and a concise explanation of how the project’s progress will be monitored and evaluated. Required Content: 1. Executive Summary (1 page max) 2. Industry and Environmental Analysis 3. Competitor Analysis 4. Consumer Analysis 5. Current Product Positioning and Target Customer Profile 6. Strategic Objectives or Key Issues to Address 7. Sales and Demand Forecast 8. Overall Marketing Strategy 9. Marketing Mix and Key Action Plan 10. Budget Plan: propose a feasible total marketing budget derived from the sales forecast, with a breakdown by activity and a brief justification 11. Monitoring and Control Mechanisms Format: The written proposal should adopt a formal business presentation format, demonstrating a logical structure with clearly articulated cause-and-effect relationships. The content should be concise, relevant, and directed toward convincing potential stakeholders or supervisors. Although there is no strict page limit, unnecessary content should be avoided. A well-structured proposal is recommended to be completed within 20 pages, with effective use of visuals and charts to strengthen clarity and professionalism. Oral Presentation: Each team will deliver a 15-minute oral presentation in class, which includes 5 minutes for Q&A. The presentation should highlight the logic of the proposal, strategic insights, and feasibility 6 of execution. Teams are advised to rehearse thoroughly and coordinate effectively to demonstrate both collaboration and professionalism in their final delivery. Final Project Guidelines Instruction The final assessment is the team output of Module III. Each team designs a tech-enabled service experience for a chosen brand or service context and builds it as a shareable VR environment on Spatial, iterating from Prototype 1.0 (Week 14) through user testing (Week 15) to the final version (Week 16). The Marketing / Service Tech Strategy Deck (3–5 pages) explains the service concept, the target customer journey, the role of immersive technology in the value proposition, and the business rationale. Deliverables (Dec 23): (1) Final VR Service Environment on Spatial with a shareable link; (2) Marketing / Service Tech Strategy Deck (3–5 pages); (3) a 10-minute team presentation including a live walkthrough of the VR environment, followed by 5 minutes of Q&A. Assessment criteria: quality of the service experience design and its grounding in course concepts (service blueprint, customer journey, servicescape); strategic rationale of the technology- enabled service (deck); evidence of iteration based on user-testing data; presentation quality and teamwork. Weekly Artifacts from Weeks 13–15 are graded as Mini-Tasks and are not double- counted here. Recommended Journals: Given the rapid evolution of topics within service technology, many of our readings delve into recent research issues. We actively encourage students to delve into articles from the suggested top- tier journals as a means of exploring and understanding the most up-to-date advancements in the field of service marketing and technology. § Journal of Service Research § Journal of Interactive Marketing § Computers in Human Behavior § Consumer Psychology Review § Journal of Consumer Research § Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science § International Journal of Hospitality Management § Annals of Tourism Research § Cornell Hospitality Quarterly Ethics Statement on Generative Artificial Intelligence Grounded in the principles of transparency and responsibility, this course encourages students to leverage AI for collaboration and mutual learning to enhance the quality of course outputs. docs.text: 1 NATIONAL TSING HUA UNIVERSITY College of Technology Management Interdisciplinary Program of Management and Technology Innovation Management (Offered in English) Fall Semester 2026 Professor: Hua-Wei Hung (hwhung@mx.nthu.edu.tw) Teaching Assistant: Luke Choe (luke.yeejie@gapp.nthu.edu.tw) Time: Thursday 14:20-17:00 (R6R7R8) Classroom: TSMC building, Room#223 Office hours: Please email to make an appointment Course Objectives: This course covers three main contents and objectives, each crucial for developing a comprehensive understanding of innovation and technology strategies in the modern business landscape. The first objective is to impart the abstract theories and systematic knowledge necessary for understanding innovation and technology strategies. This involves exploring fundamental concepts and frameworks that underpin technological innovation, including but not limited to disruptive innovation theory, technology adoption lifecycle, and strategic management of intellectual property. Students will gain a solid theoretical foundation that will enable them to analyze and develop effective strategies in various technological contexts. Secondly, the course aims to train students' thinking, questioning, and communication abilities through discussions and analyses of practical cases. This hands-on approach will expose students to real-world scenarios, challenging them to apply theoretical knowledge to complex business situations. Through case studies and interactive discussions, students will develop critical thinking skills, learn to ask insightful questions, and enhance their ability to communicate complex ideas effectively. This practical component bridges the gap between theory and application, preparing students for the challenges they may face in their future careers. Finally, the course is designed to cultivate students' team spirit and rapport, as well as their understanding of the relationship between industry practices and management theories. Through group projects and collaborative assignments, students will learn to work effectively in teams, mirroring the collaborative nature of modern business environments. Additionally, the course will emphasize the interconnectedness of academic management theories and real-world industry practices, helping students to develop a holistic view of the business world. This understanding will enable them to navigate the complexities of technological innovation in various organizational contexts and industries. 2 Teaching Arrangements: Class sessions may include lectures and small and large discussion groups. We will strive to clarify, supplement, and analyze text materials. You are responsible for all assigned readings and all materials presented in class. You are also responsible for all information disseminated in class and all course requirements, including deadlines. Lectures: Each lecture is 1 hour. Please note that all lectures will be taught in English. • The lecture will be delivered in a highly interactive way, and speaking up and idea- sharing/discussion are always welcome through lecturing, which is also counted as class participation. Book Review (30 minutes): • Book review sharing (25 minutes): Each group will be assigned to review one book at the beginning of the course, and share their review with the class during the discussion session. Each group will finish the book, and you will present feedback to the class, consisting of book summaries, key insights, managerial inspiration, and/or any other issues you want to share with the class. • Q&A (5 minutes): Other groups must prepare at least three questions to discuss with the presenting group. AI Technology Analysis (30 minutes) • In this group assignment, your team will select a real-world AI innovation—whether a major market breakthrough like ChatGPT and Tesla’s FSD, or a notable corporate failure—and analyze its trajectory through the lens of our course concepts. • The chosen technology can span any industry and may take the form of a revolutionary product, service, internal process, or entirely new business model. Your mission is to investigate the strategic story behind the innovation, evaluating the specific internal and external factors that ultimately determined its market outcome. • By examining these cases, you will apply core innovation management frameworks to understand how competitive advantages are built, sustained, or lost in the rapidly evolving AI landscape. Ultimately, your team will present these findings to the class, extracting actionable strategic lessons that help your peers learn from the innovation's real-world successes and challenges. • Your task is to investigate the story behind the innovation, evaluate the factors that influenced its outcome, and present your findings in a way that helps your classmates learn from its successes and challenges. Midterm Project: • In this assignment, you will write an individual analytical essay (1-2 pages) comparing two companies in the same industry, one representing the traditional incumbent model (“old”) and the other representing the disruptive challenger (“new”). • Your goal is to examine how the disruptive company changed the competitive landscape and challenged the incumbent’s market position, using innovation management concepts from this course. 3 Final Project Presentation: • In this assignment, your group will select two competing companies from the same industry and evaluate their strategic timing in launching a critical innovation. Your objective is to analyze whether pioneering the market provided a sustainable First-Mover Advantage or if it exposed the firm to a costly First-Mover Disadvantage that allowed fast-followers to overtake them. • Your analysis must go beyond a basic historical timeline. You must evaluate their market outcomes by applying core innovation management frameworks from our lectures: • Technology Trajectories & Dominant Design: Did the pioneer successfully establish the industry standard, or did they spend massive R&D costs only for a follower to swoop in and capitalize on a refined "dominant design"? • Complementary Assets: Did the first-mover possess the necessary manufacturing, marketing, and distribution networks to capture the value of their innovation, or did the follower win because they controlled these assets? • Market Vulnerabilities & Free-Rider Effects: Did the first-mover suffer from high customer education costs, regulatory friction, or early technological defects that the second-mover safely avoided and improved upon? • Switching Costs & Buyer Inertia: Did the pioneer build strong brand loyalty and high customer switching costs, or did the fast-follower successfully lower entry barriers to capture the market share? • Your analysis should go beyond identifying differences in emphasis. You should also examine how each company’s CSR priorities influence or align with its innovation strategy. Final Group Report: • In addition to an oral presentation, a printed paper report must also be submitted. This report will put your presentation into words and should be between 8 and 14 pages. • If AI is utilized, screenshots of conversations with the AI must be included. • APA format: 12 font Times New Roman, 1/1.5 leading, PDF file. • No plagiarism; shall also attach with the Turnitin report (acceptable similarity percentage: below 15%) (please register in advance through NTHU Library: https://learning.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/412- 1319-7120.php?Lang=en) • Conditional accept: AI only when the AI screenshot report is attached, which will also affect the grading. 4 Assessment: This course consists (but is not limited to) the following assessments: Class Participation 10%, Book Review 15%, Innovation Case Analysis 15%, Guest Speaker Reflection 5%, Midterm Project 30%, Final Group Presentation 10%, Final Group Report 15%. Assessing materials must be uploaded on eeclass in advance, with less tolerance for additional adjustment/improvement after the deadline (need to be discussed). Audience Scoring will be conducted in class, with group-based scoring from other groups to value each criterion; Peer Scoring will be managed within a group, and each group member will evaluate teammates’ contributions individually. No roll-call in class, random call is included in class participation, once one fails to answer random calls up to four times, they will be failed. Through a modular structure covering six core topics, students will learn to build operational models and derive managerial insights to solve organizational bottlenecks. 課程關鍵字 Course Keywords Operations Decision-Making, Data-Driven Modeling, Risk Simulation, Supply Chain Optimization, Capacity & Inventory Management 指定用書 Textbooks • Meredith, J. R., & Shafer, S. M. (2023). Operations and supply chain management for MBAs. John Wiley & Sons. These lectures build foundational knowledge in operations management, equipping students with the analytical mindset necessary for managing complex operational processes and logistical systems. ▪ Case Study Discussions: From Weeks 3–13, there will be 60-minute case study sessions. Each week, one group will act as the leading group to facilitate the session. Case materials will be provided to the leading group two weeks in advance, and the leading group is responsible for introducing the case context, facilitating class discussion, and synthesizing key insights. The leading group can determine the discussion format for their classmates to follow, but must ensure all 3–5 questions provided in the case materials are thoroughly discussed. ▪ Studio: This course includes a weekly 30-minute Hands-on Studio session to bridge the gap between theory and practice. The program is organized into six core modules, with each module spanning two weeks (Part I + Part II). Teams will use simulation tools to make data-driven decisions on topics such as demand forecasting, risk simulation, inventory optimization, and capacity planning, with simulated data provided by the instructor. For each of the six modules, teams are only required to submit their practice results by 23:59 on the day of the Part (II) session; no submission is required for Part (I). This means there will be a total of six submissions for the studio practices. ▪ Midterm & Final Exam: Since technical modeling and calculations are assessed during the Studios, the exams will primarily consist of analytical questions. You will be expected to demonstrate your understanding of operational logic and your ability to propose strategic solutions based on model outputs. 評分標準 Grading ▪ Class Discussion Participation: 20% ▪ Studio Practice: 20% ▪ Case Study Presentation: 20% ▪ Midterm Exam: 20% ▪ Final Exam: 20% 教學進度 Course Schedule Week Lecture Case Study Discussions Studio Hands-on Session (Part I & II: Sequential) 1 Course Introduction & OM Mindset 2 Introduction to OM & Project Management Group Time: Group formation Project Management (I) 3 Project Scheduling & Risks Case 1 Project Management (II) 4 Forecasting & Business Intelligence Case 2 Forecasting (I) National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 5 Forecasting Accuracy & Tech Trends Case 3 Forecasting (II) 6 Quality Management & Process Monitoring Case 4 Quality Control (I) 7 Six Sigma & Process Capability Case 5 Quality Control (II) 8 Midterm Exam Week 9 Supply Chain Strategy & Location Analysis Case 6 Location & Logistics (I) 10 Logistics Optimization & Transportation Case 7 Location & Logistics (II) 11 Inventory Management Fundamentals Case 8 Inventory Management (I) 12 Supply Chain Inventory & Discount Decisions Case 9 Inventory Management (II) 13 Service Operations & Queuing Theory Case 10 Queuing Theory (I) 14 Capacity Planning & Service Optimization Queuing Theory (II) 15 Group Time: Studio Integration & Final Deadline 16 Final Exam Week Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI (2) Conditionally open: ▪ Students are permitted to use AI tools as learning aids. docs.text: 科號 Course Number 11510IPMT3 01800 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Size of Limit 30 中文名稱 Course Title 領導力與 AI 輔助決策 英文名稱 Course English Title Leadership and Data-Driven Decisions 任課教師 Instructor Gary Hsieh & Matthew Bobea 教師聯絡方式 Contact Information cphsieh@mx.nthu.edu.tw matt.bobea@iss.nthu.edu.tw 上課時間 Time R2R3R4 上課教室 Room TSMC120 先修科目 Prerequisite(s) None 本課程對應之學習目標與核心能力 Aligned Learning Goals and Learning Objectives 目對應之系所課程規畫所欲培養之核心能力 Core capability to be cultivated by this course □ 運用專業管理與科技知識的能力。(20%) Our students will master the knowledge of technology and professional management. (20%) □ 整合與活用第一專長及第二專長的專業知識能力，並具備跨領域規劃、領導與執行團隊 合作的能力。(20%) Our students will be able to integrate expertise from their double specialty and thus plan, execute and lead in an interdisciplinary team setting. (20%) □ 具備英文閱讀寫作商業報告與商業口頭簡報能力。(20%) Our students will be able to read and produce professional business documents as well as deliver a professional oral presentation in English. (20%) □ 認識產業的國際發展趨勢，瞭解管理與科技對環境、社會及全球的影響，並培養自我學習 成長的能力。(20%) Our students will develop the ability of self-learning by comprehending the international development trend of the industry and by comprehending the impact of management and technology made on the environment, the society and the world. (20%) □ 理解專業倫理及社會責任的能力。(20%) Our students will be equipped with understanding of professional ethics and social responsibility. (20%) 課程簡述 (Brief course description) This course explores the intersection of psychological leadership frameworks and data-driven decision making. Students will transition from analyzing the internal dynamics of power, leadership derailers, and distributed team models to mastering modern managerial execution, including forecasting, data storytelling, and the ethical implementation of AI. By synthesizing directional judgment, operational execution, and interpersonal influence, the course prepares students to navigate complex organizations and lead high-performance teams with both emotional intelligence and analytical rigor. 課程目標 Course Objectives Leadership Philosophy & Psychology ● Deconstruct the “Great Man” theory to understand leadership as a developed skill set rather than an inherent personality trait. ● Analyze the “Psychology of Power” and identify common leadership derailers to build self-awareness and professional resilience. ● Evaluate the “Complementary Team” model to demonstrate how distributed leadership and diverse skill sets improve organizational outcomes. Decision & Operational Mastery ● Synthesize directional decision making and operational execution to bridge the gap between intent and day-to-day action. ● Navigate complex organizational structures by applying decision frameworks for leading within and through bureaucracies. ● Master an integrated leadership synthesis process to align interpersonal dynamics with evidence-based decisions and measurable outcomes. Management & Technical Execution ● Utilize quantitative management tools, including forecasting and data visualization, to drive evidence-based decision making. ● Construct compelling narratives through data storytelling to communicate complex information to diverse stakeholders. 課程說明 Course Description This course provides a comprehensive exploration of the dual pillars of modern organizational success: the art of leadership and the discipline of evidence-based decision making. Moving beyond the “Great Man” myth, students will examine leadership through three critical lenses—directional decision making, operational execution, and interpersonal influence—while investigating the psychological underpinnings of power and the common derailers that challenge even seasoned professionals. The curriculum transitions from theoretical frameworks to hands-on practice, equipping students with competencies in data visualization and forecasting, for managerial decisions. By integrating distributed leadership models with practical tools for delegation, team communication, and data storytelling, students will develop a versatile toolkit for navigating complex organizations and leading complementary teams in a rapidly evolving global landscape. 請輸入課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」至少5個, 每個關鍵字至多20個中文, 以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) Leadership, Psychology, Data Driven Decision Making, Analytics 領導, 決策制定, 數據分析, 心理, AI倫理 指定用書 Textbooks Pendleton, D., Furnham, A., & Cowell, J. (2021) Leadership: No More Heroes, Palgrave Macmillan; Third edition, ISBN: 978-3030604363 https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-030-60437-0 Few, S. (2021) Now You See It: An Introduction to Visual Data Sensemaking, Analytics Press; Second edition, ISBN: 978-1938377129 https://www.books.com.tw/products/F017641155 參考書籍 References N/A 教學方式 Teaching Approach This course moves beyond passive theory to prioritize applied mastery through a two-pronged pedagogical strategy: hands-on technical labs and high-fidelity case studies. By bridging the gap between "knowing" and "doing," students develop the pragmatic instincts required for real-world leadership. Case-Based Strategic Analysis: Rather than reviewing abstract concepts, students will dissect real-world organizational dilemmas. Using the "No More Heroes" framework, we will analyze historical and contemporary business cases to identify leadership "derailers" and evaluate how strategic, operational, and interpersonal domains were balanced—or neglected. This approach forces students to inhabit the role of the decision-maker, defending their choices against competing priorities and bureaucratic constraints. Hands-On Technical Workshops: The second half of the course functions as a management laboratory. Students will not just discuss data; they will work directly with it. Through interactive sessions, students will practice team management, data analysis, data visualizations, and story telling. This "learning by doing" ensures that technical fluency and managerial judgment develop as a unified capability, rather than as parallel disciplines that never meet. Strategic Synthesis: The curriculum culminates in a final presentation that requires the integration of both psychological insights and quantitative evidence. Students must demonstrate the ability to lead a complementary team while utilizing data storytelling to justify a strategic pivot. By the conclusion of the term, students will have transitioned from observers to practitioners, equipped with a portfolio of applied skills that are immediately transferable to professional environments. 評分標準 Grading Homework - 56% (14 assignments at 4 points) In Class Assignments - 28% (14 assignments at 2 points) Final Presentation - 16% 教學進度 Course Schedule Part 1 (Instructed by Gary Hsieh): This section explores the psychological core and strategic dimensions of leadership, challenging the traditional "Great Man" myth. Students will examine the internal mechanics of power while learning to balance the three essential domains of professional success: the strategic, the operational, and the interpersonal. By identifying common leadership "derailers" and studying the impact of complementary, distributed leadership, the course prepares students to navigate the complexities of organizational life. As professional landscapes demand more than just technical expertise, this section equips future leaders with the self-awareness and strategic synthesis required to align diverse teams with long-term goals. Part 2 (Instructed by Matthew Bobea): This course provides a comprehensive framework for modern leadership, bridging the gap between high-level management theory and data-driven decision-making. Students will explore the core pillars of effective leadership: delegation, team dynamics, and ethical governance, while gaining hands-on proficiency in the tools used to communicate complex information. As business environments become increasingly reliant on algorithmic processes, this course empowers future managers to lead with both emotional intelligence and quantitative clarity. Week Instructor Course Description 1 Gary & Matt Introduction 2 Gary The myth of the “Great Man” + Decision Mindsets Challenging the assumption that leadership is an innate heroic trait rather than a learnable, multifaceted skill—then translating that insight into how leaders frame decisions, avoid hero-centric bias, and build repeatable judgment under uncertainty. 3 Gary Directional Judgment & Decision Framing Developing the “helicopter vision” required to set direction and make high-stakes decisions: problem framing, defining decision criteria, identifying trade-offs, and communicating decisions amid uncertainty and external constraints. 4 Gary Operational Domain Mastering the "engine room" of leadership by ensuring high-performance standards and efficient resource management. 5 Gary Interpersonal Domain Refining the emotional intelligence and relationship-building skills necessary to inspire and influence others. 6 Gary Psychology of Power Analyzing how power is acquired, maintained, and the psychological impact it has on decision-makers and followers. 7 Gary Leadership Derailers Identifying the personality flaws and "dark side" traits that cause otherwise successful leaders to fail. 8 Gary Distributed Leadership Moving from solo leadership to a model where diverse strengths are leveraged across a balanced, high-functioning team. 9 Gary Leadership Synthesis for Decision Integration Integrating directional judgment, operational execution, and interpersonal influence into a coherent leadership approach—using structured decision processes (assumptions, evidence, stakeholder impacts, and execution plans) to ensure decisions translate into outcomes. 10 Gary Leading Bureaucracies Understanding the mechanics of large-scale organizations and how to maintain agility within rigid institutional structures. 11 Matt Leading with Analytical Thinking: Goals, Data, and Decisions Introduction to defining and operationalizing decision goals as the foundation of data-driven leadership. Students learn how to translate managerial objectives into measurable metrics, followed by principles of visual perception and basic visualization techniques (pivot tables, bar charts, histograms, boxplots, line charts, scatterplots) to align analysis with clearly defined goals. 12 Matt Visualizations and Data Oriented Communication Through team activities, students practice annotating visualizations, exploring data interactively, and communicating insights clearly, culminating in a team presentation of data-driven findings. 13 Matt Communications with Advanced Visualizations Focus on preparing data for effective visualization by restructuring datasets, creating and removing variables, imputation, and merging multiple data sources. Students then apply advanced visualization techniques, including heatmaps, treemaps, and map charts, to uncover deeper patterns, reinforced through a hands-on team activity. 14 Matt Decision Making using Time Series Data Introduction to how leaders interpret and act on time-based data, focusing on trends, seasonality, and evolving patterns in organizational contexts. Students learn time series visualization techniques. 15 Matt Forecasting for Managerial Planning Focus on how forecasting informs planning, resource allocation, and risk management in organizations. Students learn smoothing-based algorithms (moving averages, differencing, and simple exponential smoothing) and apply them in Tableau, with emphasis on interpreting forecasts, understanding limitations, and using predictions to support strategic and operational decisions. 16 Gary & Matt Final Presentation 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則 (Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 有條件開放 Conditionally open Generative AI is integrated into this course as a secondary analytical partner rather than a replacement for student inquiry. Students are encouraged to use AI tools for brainstorming strategic frameworks, drafting initial communication templates, and assisting with complex data processing; however, all final outputs must reflect original human judgment and include a formal disclosure of AI involvement. This hands-on usage is paired with critical ethical evaluation, requiring students to verify AI-generated insights against primary sources and account for algorithmic biases in their decision-making processes. 課程相關連接 Course Related Links N/A

docs.text: 11410IPT 514000 課程綱要表 課程名稱 (中文) 光電子學一 (英文) Photonics I 開課單位 電機系 授課教師 李依珊 課程代碼 IPT 5140 選課性質 ⎕必修■選修 學分數 3 開課年級 碩博 先修科目或先備能力 Prerequisites Electromagnetic theory 課程概述 本課程全面介紹光電子學與光子學的基本原理與實際應用。學生將深入探討光的 行為及其與物質的交互作用、各類光子元件的運作原理，以及這些元件在現代科技 中的整合應用。課程設計旨在為學生建立紮實的理論基礎與實作能力。 This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the fundamental principles and practical applications of optoelectronics and photonics. Students will explore the behavior of light and its interaction with matter, the operation of photonic devices, and the integration of these components in modern technologies. The curriculum is structured to build a strong foundation in both theoretical concepts and practical device operation. 課程目標 在課程結束時，學生將能夠： 1. 理解並應用光的基本性質包含傳播、發射與偵測的物理原理 2. 分析與建模主要光電子與光子元件的性能 3. 設計基礎的光子系統，用於光通訊、感測與訊號處理等應用 4. 解讀並運用各權威教科書所提供的理論架構 By the end of the course, students will be able to: 1. Understand and apply the physics of light propagation, emission, and detection 2. Analyze and model the performance of key optoelectronic and photonic devices 3. Design basic photonic systems for applications such as optical communication, sensing, and signal processing 4. Interpret and apply the theoretical frameworks provided by leading texts in the field 教科書 自編教材 lecture notes 參考書 1. Principles of Photonics, Liu, Jia-Ming, Cambridge University Press. 2. Optoelectronics and Photonics: Principles and Practices, Safa O. Kasap, Prentice Hall, ISBN10: 0201610876. 3. Fundamentals of Photonics, Bahaa E. A. Saleh and Malvin V. Teich, Wiley- Interscience, ISBN-10: 0471358320. 教學要點概述 講義編選 自己編寫 教學方法 ☑講授 ☑討論互動 評量方式 作業 Homework assignment 20% 出席 Attendance 10% 期中考 Midterm 35% 期末考 Final exam 35% 課程綱要 單元主題 單元綱要 (Week 1-4) 1 – Introduction to Photonics 2 - Optical Properties of Materials 3 - Optical Wave Propagation (Week 5-7) 4 - Optical Coupling 5 - Optical Interference 6 - Optical Resonance Midterm (Week 9-13) 7 - Optical Absorption and Emission 8 - Optical Amplification 9 - Laser Oscillation (Week 14-15) 10 - Optical Modulation 11 - Photodetection Optional Review of the Quantum theory Final 生成式人工智慧倫理聲明：禁止使用 經仔細考量後，本課程授課教師認為不宜於此門課程當中使用生成式人工智慧於課堂學習當 中。因本課程的內容於生成式 AI 中尚有諸多錯誤，且容易影響學生對基礎核心知識之判讀。 根據本校公布之佈的「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採取禁止使 用，以下為相關的監管機制 修讀本門課程之學生應注意本門課不得繳交使用生成式人工智慧所產出的作業、報告或個人心 得。若經查核發現，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。 Unit I: Fundamentals of Photonics (Weeks 1–4) Week 1: Introduction to Photonics  What is photonics? Historical development  Overview of applications (telecom, sensors, imaging, quantum)  Basic EM theory of light Week 2: Wave Optics  Maxwell’s equations in dielectric media  Polarization, interference, and diffraction  Complex refractive index and absorption Week 3: Geometrical Optics and Gaussian Beams  Snell’s law, total internal reflection  Paraxial approximation  Gaussian beam propagation and beam quality Week 4: Light-Matter Interaction  Absorption, spontaneous and stimulated emission  Einstein coefficients  Optical gain and cross-sections Unit II: Optical Waveguides and Cavities (Weeks 5–6) Week 5: Optical Waveguides and Fibers  Planar and slab waveguides  Step-index and graded-index fibers  Dispersion, attenuation, and modes Week 6: Optical Resonators  Fabry-Pérot cavities  Quality factor (Q), finesse  Mode structure and losses Unit III: Optoelectronic Devices (Weeks 7–11) Week 7: Semiconductors and Band Structures  Direct vs. indirect bandgap  Effective mass, density of states  Carrier recombination and diffusion Week 8: Light Emitting Diodes (LEDs)  Radiative recombination  Internal and external quantum efficiency  Design considerations and materials (e.g., GaAs, InGaN) Week 9: Semiconductor Lasers  Gain medium and threshold condition  Laser diode structures: Fabry–Pérot, DFB, VCSELs  Temperature and current effects Week 10: Photodetectors  Photoconductors, p-n and p-i-n photodiodes  Avalanche photodiodes (APDs), SPADs  Responsivity, quantum efficiency, noise Week 11: Optical Modulators and Switches  Electro-optic, acousto-optic, and thermo-optic effects  Mach–Zehnder modulators  High-speed modulation Unit IV: Applications and Integration (Weeks 12–14) Week 12: Photonic Integrated Circuits (PICs)  SOI and III-V platforms  Passive and active components  Coupling, splitters, multiplexers Week 13: Photonic Systems and Applications  Fiber optic communications  LIDAR and biomedical sensing  Emerging applications (quantum photonics, neuromorphic) Week 14: Review, Projects, and Future Trends  Student presentations/project demos (optional)  Emerging research topics  Final review and Q&A

docs.text: IPT 514300 Digital Optics Laboratory Objectives: This Course will introduce classical optics in a graduate level. The theories of geometry optics, diffraction, liquid-crystal optics and Fourier Optics will be systematically present. With these basic understandings, students then will get hand-on experience on operating the spatial light modulators (SLM) and developing diverse digital optical systems. Instructor: Chang-Hua Liu Prerequisites: Optics, Electromagnetic theory or Graduate standing Office hours: by appointment (send me an email: chliu@ee.nthu.edu.tw) Textbook: None required. I will post the lecture notes. Supplementary References: E. Hecht, Optics (Addison Wesley) A. Yariv, P. Yeh, Optical waves in Crystals (Wiley) Grades: Homework: 15% Mid-term exam: 25% Labs: 40% Final exam: 20% Course Outline: Lectures will cover the following topics: - Lenses and image formation - ABCD matrices of optical elements and imaging systems - Aberrations - Optical waves in anisotropic dielectric medium (vector nature of waves, representations of a polarization state, Birefringence, Jones calculus and its applications) - Fraunhofer diffraction (Rectangular & circular apertures, Arrays of apertures & diffraction gratings, Fresnel lens, Fourier transformation by a lens) Laboratories (using SLM to realize the following experiments): - Amplitude and phase modulation - Wavefront modulation and control - Diffraction and interference - Fourier optics (dispersion and optical signal processing) - Fourier optics (talbot image and phase shift digital holography) - Field programmable lens

docs.text: 超快光學−課程大綱 (11510 IPT 543000, Ultrafast Optics) 一、課程說明(Course Description) 本課程旨在介紹超短(10-12~10-15 秒)雷射光脈衝之產生、量測、傳播、色散管理及其應 用。此一技術提供的超精密時間解析度可用以觀測前所未知的分子、准粒子短暫動態。 所產生之巨大亮度(>1023 W/cm2)足以突破原子基本引力，實現微米尺度異質材料鍵 合，或驅動物質產生顯著之非線性效應，從而獲得一系列新的(如中紅外光、極紫外光) 同調光譜成份。本課程所需要的背景知識為：傅立葉轉換、電磁平面波，並具備運用 數學軟體(如 Matlab)之能力。 This subject is designed to introduce generation, measurement, propagation, dispersion management and applications of ultrashort (10-12-10-15 sec) laser pulses. The ultrahigh temporal resolution enabled by this technique can trace the fleeting dynamics of molecules or quasi particles. The gigantic peak intensity (up to 1023 W/cm2) can overrun the atomic force, realize micrometer precision bonding between heterogeneous materials, or generate a series of new coherent spectral components (e.g. mid-infrared, extreme ultraviolet) by strong nonlinear interaction with materials. The prerequisites include Fourier transform, electromagnetic plane waves and the ability to conduct numerical simulation with package software (e.g. Matlab). 二、教科書(Text Book) 自編講義(Lecture slides, pdf files will be offered at the beginning of semester.) 三、參考書籍(References) Andrew Weiner, Ultrafast Optics, Wiley, 2009. (ISBN: 978-0-471-41539-8) 四、教學方式(Teaching Method) 開放式課程影片預習、隨堂討論及問答、課堂講授、團隊專題 (OpenCourseWare video preview, discussion and Q&A in class, lectures, group project) 五、教學進度(Syllabus) 1. Introduction and review (6 hours) 2. Active mode-locking (1 hour) 3. Light-matter interaction (5 hours) 4. Passive mode-locking (6 hours) 5. Pulse measurement by correlation techniques (4 hours) 6. Pulse measurement by FROG and SPIDER (4 hours) 7. Dispersion and dispersion management (5 hours) 8. Flexible topics on request (6 hours) 9. Term project in the form of group competition 六、成績考核(Evaluation) 教師考核(20%)，期中考(30%)，期末考(25%)，團隊專題(15%)，作業(10%) Instructor’s assessment(20%), midterm exam(30%), final exam (25%), group projects (15%), homework assignments (10%) 七、可連結之網頁位址(Useful links) 數位學習平台(E-learning)：eeclass.nthu.edu.tw 開放式課程(Open Course Ware)：ocw.nthu.edu.tw/ocw/index.php?page=course&cid=206& 八、生成式人工智慧使用規則(Generative Artificial Intelligence access rules) 本課程同意學生利用人工智慧(AI)進行協作或互學。根據本校公布之「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本課程採取有條件開放，以下說明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出。 學生須於課堂作業或報告中的「標題頁註腳」或「引用文獻後」簡要說明如何使用生 成式 AI 進行議題發想、文句潤飾或結構參考等使用方式。若經查核使用 卻無在作業 或報告中標明，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。 本門課授課教材或學習資料若有引用自生成式 AI，教師也將在投影片或口頭標注。 修讀本課程之學生 於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。

docs.text: Principle and Design of Passive Si Photonics Devices Course Description：This course mainly introduces the principles and applications of passive silicon photonic devices. The course begins with the fundamental theory of optical waveguides and the mechanisms of optical waveguide loss, followed by topics including waveguide mode coupling theory, waveguide mode interference theory, fiber couplers, integrated optical resonators, and literature reading and discussion. The course also incorporates training in professional simulation software and a final project. Through a balanced emphasis on both theory and practice, students are expected to develop a solid understanding of the design and applications of passive silicon photonic devices. docs.text: National Tsing Hua University 11510 EE 561000 Materials Science for Organic Optoelectronics Page 1 of 2 Course syllabus Basic Information: Course title ( 中文): 有機光電材料科學 Course title (English): Materials Science for Organic Optoelectronics Instructor: 大江昌人 (Oh-e, Masahito) (oh-e@ee.nthu.edu.tw) @台達館#838 Language for teaching: English Class time: M5M6W5 Location: DELTA 台達 210 Course Description: This course is constructively prepared for graduates as well as junior and senior undergraduate students. The course content consists of materials science fundamentals required for understanding optoelectronic device technology. Before we explore the fundamentals of optoelectronic devices*, it is prerequisite to have fundamental knowledge of materials and their related areas, as optoelectronic devices are composed of interdisciplinary technologies. This course covers quantum chemistry from atoms to molecules, as well as quantum mechanical frameworks for materials science, including the physics and chemistry of materials, such as photo-physical processes of molecules, light-matter interactions, molecule-molecule interactions, and other materials-related topics. In this course, we do not deal with organic devices themselves. * These topics will be provided in “Organic Optoelectronics: Physics, Materials and Devices” (The course to be offered in the following spring semester); however, the courses in the fall and spring semesters are basically independent. ** Having knowledge of “Modern Physics” or other related courses is not required, but desirable. *** This course is offered in English. Course materials: Available on eeclass, https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw/ References: “Concepts of Modern Physics”, sixth edition, by Arthur Beiser (McGraw-Hill); “Modern Quantum Mechanics”, by J.J. Sakurai (Addison-Wesley Publishing Company); “Organic Electro-Optics and Photonics: Molecules, Polymers and Crystals” by L. R. Dalton (Cambridge Univ. Press); “Optics and Nonlinear Optics of Liquid Crystals”, by Iam-Choon Khoo (World Scientific); “Nonlinear Optics”, by Robert W. Boyd (Academic Press) ···, etc. Teaching Method: A combination of blackboard, handout teaching, and PowerPoint viewgraphs. Report presentation by students. National Tsing Hua University 11510 EE 561000 Materials Science for Organic Optoelectronics Page 2 of 2 Syllabus: Session 1 – 5: Introduction to chemical bonding theory  From atoms to molecules (Computational chemistry)  Valence bond theory  Molecular orbital theory  Quantization of molecular motions  Energy structures Session 6 – 7(8): Perturbation theory  Time-independent  Time-dependent Session 8 – 10: Symmetry of molecules  Symmetry operations and elements  Use of the point group  Group theory Session 11 – 12(13): Metal complexes  Crystal field theory  Ligand field theory Session (13)14 – 15: Photo-physics of molecules  Light-matter interactions  Photo-physical processes  Born-Oppenheimer approximation Session 16: From molecules to materials  Molecule–molecule interactions  Molecular orientation and its related topics …etc. **** The content and plans will be adjusted as needed throughout the course. ***** Exams may be replaced with report work. Grading: Midterm exam (30%), Final exam including a report and presentation (40%), Homework and class attendance and participation (30%) ****** This may be adjusted at the end of the semester. If it is confirmed that generative AI was used for topic generation, text refinement, or structural reference, and this is not mentioned in the assignment or report, the faculty, department, or relevant department reserves the right to re-evaluate the assignment or report or withhold a grade.

Throughout the semester, experts and scholars from diverse fields will be invited to share their latest research findings and professional experiences. Topics include advances in photonics and optoelectronic technologies, scientific breakthroughs, industrial perspectives, career development, and mental well-being. The course aims to help students stay informed about emerging trends while fostering interdisciplinary perspectives and personal growth. - 建議先修課程 (Prerequisite): 無 (None) 二、使用書籍 (Text Books) 無 (None) 三、參考資料 (References) 無 (None) 四、教學方式 (Teaching style) 每週邀請演講 (Weekly invited talk) 五、教學內容 (Course Content) 書報討論課程將於每週五下午 14:20 舉行，邀請講者及演講主題等相關資訊將 公布於 eeclass 線上平台，請同學定期查閱最新公告。 The seminar series will be held every Friday starting at 2:20 PM. Students are encouraged to check the announcements regularly for updates. 六、成績考核 (Evaluation) 出席與課堂參與 Attendance and participation （70%） 11510IPT 591000 問答 Q&A（30%） 七、課程準則 (Policy) 本課程不建議於學習過程中使用生成式人工智慧工具。目前生成式人工智慧 於本課程相關內容中仍可能存在錯誤資訊，且過度依賴其產出可能影響學生對基 礎概念與核心知識的理解與判斷。依據本校公布之「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共 學與素養培養指引」，本課程採取禁止使用之規範。修讀本課程之學生不得提交 由生成式人工智慧產生之作業、報告或個人心得作為課程成果。若經查證發現相 關情形，授課教師、學校或相關單位得依規定重新評分、酌予扣分或不予計分。 學生完成選課程序後，視同已閱讀、理解並同意遵守上述課程規範與學術倫理要 求。 The use of generative AI tools is not permitted in this course. Since generative AI may still produce inaccurate or misleading information related to the course content, excessive reliance on AI-generated outputs may hinder students’ development of a solid understanding of fundamental concepts and core knowledge. In accordance with the University's Guidelines for AI Collaboration, Co-learning, and Literacy Development in Higher Education, this course adopts a no-AI-use policy. Students may not submit assignments, reports, or personal reflections generated by generative AI as course work. If such use is identified, the instructor, the University, or relevant authorities reserve the right to reassess the work, apply grade penalties, or assign no credit. By enrolling in this course, students are deemed to have read, understood, and agreed to comply with the above course policy and academic integrity requirements.

Through class discussions, group meetings, and individual consultations, students will gain a deeper understanding of their learning needs and personal growth potential. Additionally, the course guides students in assessing their progress and reflecting on their experiences through midterm and final reports. docs.text: 1 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 11510IPTH101600 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Class Size 30 中文名稱 Course Title 健康心理學 英文名稱 Course English Title Health Psychology 任課教師 Instructor 常善媚 上課時間 Time 每週三，第 7, 8 堂 上課教室 Room 教育館 101 教室 Course Description(課程簡述) Health psychology is an interdisciplinary field that applies theories and concepts from psychology to the study of human well-being, illness, and healthcare. This course is designed to help students explore how psychology can be used to promote health while gaining insight into themselves, others, and their environment. By learning how psychology can improve health, students can better understand how to support their own well-being and that of others. 健康心理學被定義為一個跨領域的學門，它應用心理學的理論和概念於人類的幸福、疾病和醫療保 健相關研究。本課程幫學生了解如何應用心理學促進健康，同時深入了解自己、他人、與環境。經 學習從心理學的概念來改善健康的方式，學生可以更好地理解如何幫助自己和他人。 Course Objectives (課程目標) 2 By the end of this course, students will be able to: 1. Explore how psychology influences and is applied to health care. 2. Understand the major psychosocial factors that contribute to health behaviors and the development of disease. 3. Learn to apply their knowledge of psychology in the development, implementation, and evaluation of health programs. 4. Students will be able to assess their own health status and formulate their own health goals and health plans. 1. 探討心理學如何影響並應用於醫療保健。 2. 理解影響健康行為及疾病發展的主要心理社會因素。 3. 學習如何將心理學知識應用於健康計畫的制定、實施與評估。 4. 學生將能夠評估自身的健康狀況，並制定個人的健康目標與健康計畫。 Core capability to be cultivated by this course (欲培養之核心能力) 1. Developing social concern and empathy（培養社會關懷與同理心） 2. To adapt to social change（社會變遷因應能力） 3. To practice（生活實踐能力） 4. To think critically（慎思明辨能力） 5. Attendance: 10% 2. Group discussion and participation: 30% 3. Midterm assignment: 25% 4. Attendance ➢ Pre-test: At the beginning of each week of the course, participants must answer five multiple- 6 choice questions related to the content of the weekly preview. ➢ Worksheets: During the two-hour weekly class, participants will complete a worksheet. This worksheet must be turned in before the end of the course. 出席率 ➢ 課前測驗：每週課程開始時，學員需回答五道與當週預習內容相關的選擇題。 ➢ 學習單：在每週兩小時的課程中，學員需完成一份學習單，並於課程結束前提交。 1. Group discussion and participation Your attendance and participation are expected and will be documented. Much of the work in class involves collaboration and discussion, as human knowledge is socially constructed. You should contribute to the group work, raise your hands to share ideas and ask questions, and avoid using digital devices (e.g., cellphones, laptops, iPad, etc.) for reasons irrelevant to the class activities. You should make every effort to attend class and be on time, and you must be in the classroom for the entire time to receive full credit for the attendance. 小組討論與課堂參與 你的出席與參與是必要的，並將被記錄下來。課堂中的許多活動都涉及合作與討論，因為人類 的知識是透過社會互動建構而成的。你應積極參與小組討論，舉手發表意見並提出問題，並避 免使用與課程無關的數位設備（如手機、筆記型電腦、iPad 等）。你應盡力準時到課，並全程 參與課堂活動，才能獲得完整的出席與參與分數。 2. Midterm assignment ➢ Choose a topic from the second through eighth week topics and record a two-minute video. This video must contain two parts: The first part is to introduce your topic and share the main concepts from the course content, i.e., Like a YouTuber; the second part is for you to share your own experiences on the topic, your advice, or your goals and plans. In the video you can choose to show your face or not, but in addition to the sound, the video also contains video/pictures. ➢ You will upload the video to your "YouTube" and set public to share with other participants. (Please #HealthPsyNTHU) ➢ There are three important dates for the Midterm Report: - On 11/1 in class, you must turn in your midterm report topic. - You must upload your video before 11/8 11PM and shard your video address. 7 - Before 11/14 at 11PM you must view everyone's videos and feedback. 期中作業 ➢ 選擇一個主題（從第二週至第八週的課程主題中選擇），並錄製一段 兩分鐘的影片。影 片需包含兩個部分： 第一部分：介紹你的主題，並分享與課程內容相關的核心概念，就像 YouTuber 一樣。 第二部分：分享你個人的相關經驗、建議，或你的目標與計畫。在影片中，你可以選擇是否 露臉，但除了聲音之外，影片還需包含影像或圖片。 ➢ 影片上傳： 請將影片上傳至 YouTube，並設定為公開，以便與其他同學分享。（請標記 #HealthPsyNTHU） ➢ 期中報告的三個重要日期： 11/1（課堂上）：需提交你的期中報告主題。 11/8 晚上 11 點前：需上傳影片並分享影片連結。 11/14 晚上 11 點前：需觀看所有同學的影片並提供回饋。 3. Final presentation and report ➢ The final presentation and report is a group report. The teacher divides the students into groups and lets each group choose the topic on which they want to make a report. The group members are determined by the teacher. Group assignments are determined after all students in the class have been identified. ➢ Each group is free to choose which topics related to health psychology they would like to explore. ➢ The oral presentation will be 20 minutes per group. After the oral report, a PPT file must be submitted. ➢ The content of the report must cite at least two research reports on the topic. ➢ Points will be calculated for the content of the report, detailed understanding of the research findings, and the contribution of each individual in the group. 期末報告與展示 ➢ 期末報告與展示為小組報告，由老師分組，並讓各組選擇報告主題。小組成員將由老師分 配，分組作業會在全班名單確定後進行。 8 ➢ 各組可自由選擇 與 健康心理學 相關的主題進行探討。 ➢ 口頭報告時間：每組報告時間為 20 分鐘。口頭報告結束後，需提交 PPT 檔案。 ➢ 報告內容要求：需引用至少兩篇 與主題相關的研究報告。 ➢ 評分標準：報告內容的完整性、對研究結果的深入理解，以及每位組員的貢獻，都將列入 評分標準。 ● Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI (AI 使用規則) This course allows the conditional use of AI. docs.name: 參與觀察與資料分析
docs.text: 1 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 11510IPTH101700 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 30 中文名稱 Course Title 參與觀察與資料分析 英文名稱 Course English Title Participant Observation and Data Analysis 任課教師 Instructor 常善媚 上課時間 Time 每週二（7, 8, 9 節） 上課教室 Room 教育館 101 教室 課程簡述 (Course Description) 本課程旨在介紹田野研究與參與觀察法的核心概念與實務操作。課程將引導同學學習如何運用參與觀 察與訪談技巧，進入特定場域進行觀察、訪談並撰寫田野筆記。同時，課程將探討如何基於參與觀察 所得資料設計調查問卷，並嘗試分析不同類型的資料（如質性資料、量化數據、政府大型資料、社群 網站爬蟲資料等）。最後，課程將指導同學撰寫研究結果，培養綜合運用多種研究方法進行社會調查 與分析的能力。 This course introduces the fundamental concepts and practical applications of field research and participant observation methods. It guides students in using participant observation and interview techniques to enter specific research settings, conduct observations and interviews, and take field notes. Additionally, the course explores how to design survey questionnaires based on participant observation data and analyze various types of data, including qualitative and quantitative data, large-scale government datasets, and social media web- scraped data. Finally, students will learn how to synthesize and present their research findings, developing skills in integrating multiple research methods for social inquiry and analysis. 2 課程目標 (Course Objectives) 1. 了解田野研究與參與觀察的基本概念。 2. 練習參與觀察的資料蒐集。 3. 就感興趣的主題進行文獻查找與閱讀。 4. 進行所蒐集之質性與量性資料分析。 5. 進行研究結果撰寫的練習。 6. 探討參與觀察可能面臨的倫理議題。 1. understand the basic concepts of field studies and participant observation. 2. collect data through the method of participant observation. 3. conduct literature reviews on the topic of your interest. 4. analyze the quantitative and qualitative data collected. 5. practice writing up the results of the study. 6. explore the potential ethical issues of participant observation 欲培養之核心能力 (Core capability to be cultivated by this course) 1. 培養社會關懷與同理心 （Developing social concern and empathy.） 2. 社會變遷因應能力（To adapt to social change） 3. 生活實踐能力（To practice） 4. 慎思明辨能力（To think critically） 5. 跨領域能力（To cross disciplinary boundaries） 課程內容 (Course Content) ● 關鍵字(Course keywords) 參與觀察, 田野研究, 內容分析, 質性研究, 描述性統計 participant observation, field study, content analysis, qualitative research, descriptive statistics 3 ● 課程大綱 (Detailed Course Syllabus) No Topics Reading Homework 1 課程導讀與介紹 Introduction 2 參與觀察法的特徵與用途 Features and application of participant observation method Ch 1. 反思心得 1 3 參與者角色：既參與、又觀察 As a participant, we engage and observe Ch 2. 反思心得 2 4 田野在哪裡? docs.name: 數位音樂實務與應用
docs.text: 1 國立清華大學 資訊系統與應用研究所 115(1)課程大綱 科號 11510ISA 556000 3 學分 人數上限 45 人 中文課名 數位音樂實務與應用 英文課名 Digital Music Practice and Implementation 開課教師/合作業師 蘇郁惠/林尚德 隸屬學分學程 音樂科技與健康學分學程 課程綱要 本課程由蘇郁惠教授規劃，115 學年合作業師為金曲製作人/金馬配樂家林尚 德。本課程旨在培養學生理解當代流行音樂的創作核心與製作脈絡，並具備基 礎的數位音樂實作能力。將以音樂製作概論為起點，訓練獨立的數位流行音樂 製作能力，逐步帶領學生進入 ： ＊歌詞創作 ＊華語流行音樂暢銷作曲法分析 ＊Billboard 熱門歌曲結構拆解 ＊經典名曲案例研究 學生將透過旋律、節奏、和聲配置與敘事技巧的解析，理解商業音樂的創作邏 輯與趨勢。同時，課程強調理論與實務並行，透過示範與短篇創作練習，使學 生能在課堂中即時應用所學，建立屬於自己的音樂語彙與創作方法，為進入音 樂製作領域奠定重要基礎。 教 學 內 容 及 進 度 各周課表 上 課 內 容 第 1 週 數位音樂導論 第 2 週 當代流行旋律寫作 1 第 3 週 當代流行旋律寫作 2 第 4 週 當代流行旋律寫作 3 第 5 週 當代流行歌詞寫作 1 第 6 週 當代流行歌詞寫作 2 第 7 週 當代流行歌詞寫作 3 第 8 週 期中報告 第 9 週 上架與發行所需之準備 第 10 週 上架與發行後之檢討分析 第 11 週 除了音樂你也需要會這些：版權、自我經營、媒體、經紀人 第 12 週 歌曲創作實戰演練 1 第 13 週 歌曲創作實戰演練 2 第 14 週 數據分析與檢討 第 15 週 綜合討論、本學期課程回顧與延伸 第 16 週 繳交期末作業及期末成發講評 2 教學 活動 ■ 口頭講授 ■ 視聽教學 ■ 上課講義之補充 ■ 分組討論 ■ 實務演練 ■ 放投影機 評量 方式 課堂參與 30% 期中報告 30% 期末呈現 40%

docs.name: 錄音與音樂製作
docs.text: 1 國立清華大學 資訊系統與應用研究所 115(1)課程大綱 科號 11510ISA 556100 3 學分 人數上限 45 人 中文課名 錄音與音樂製作 英文課名 Tonmeister 開課教師/合作業師 蘇郁惠/陳仕桓 隸屬學分學程 音樂科技與健康學分學程 課程綱要 本課程由蘇郁惠教授規劃，115 學年合作業師為金音獎得主混錄音工程 師陳仕桓。本課程為進階音樂製作課程，採遠距同步課程模式，以實作 講解的方式訓練學生對於聽覺與聲音成像的敏銳度，掌握音樂製作基本 技術、錄音實作、plug in 軟硬體、歌曲理論分析、混音處理進程。因應 商業作品標準規格，講課端將使用擁有專業聲學空間的錄音室及其專業 設備，用於分析並處理複雜的聲音特性和細膩的音色表現，輔以收音技 法、軟硬體後製達成音樂畫面成像之藝術。 本課程導入多元音樂類型的 製作專案以及樂手協作，幫助學生了解自己未來在產業的定位以及跨領 域合作的工作方法，除了在最有效的時間內獲得聲音設計的基礎概念， 並培植未來從事音響導演或相關研究之人才。 適合學生 具備數位音樂工作軟體基本操作能力、錄音設備具備基礎了解者 教 學 內 容 及 進 度 各周課表 上課內容 第 1 週 課程內容講解 PROTOOLS 基礎操作教學：介面操作、錄音設備簡介 第 2 週 PROTOOLS 基礎操作教學：剪輯、整理音軌、對整訊號 第 3 週 錄音實作(vocal 錄音)tune 音準、剪輯、歌手現場示範 第 4 週 軟體 EQ、COMP、REVERB 基礎介紹 第 5 週 歌曲曲式分析、音軌編輯 第 6 週 進階混音/母帶處理 1 (民謠類型) 第 7 週 進階混音/母帶處理 2 (爵士類型) 第 8 週 進階混音/母帶處理 3 (各式搖滾類型) 第 9 週 進階混音/母帶處理 4 (電音類型) 第 10 週 進階混音/母帶處理 5 (流行音樂類型) 第 11 週 進階混音/母帶處理 (嘻哈類型) 第 12 週 進階混音/母帶處理 6 (日式音樂類型) 第 13 週 進階混音 / 母帶處理 7 (日式音樂類型) 第 14 週 進階混音/ 母帶處理 8 (SLOW ROCK 台語) 第 15 週 進階混音/ 母帶處理 9 (流行鋼琴弦樂類型台語) 第 16 週 期末分組發表與講評 師生互動方式 教室面授及線上互動：業師講授示範與講評、封閉社群討論 成績評量方式 30% 期中個人作品：30％ DEMO 混音 期末小組作品：40％

docs.name: 互動設計
docs.text: 1 ISA 557900: 互動設計 Interaction Design 教師: 許有真 (ychsu@mx.nthu.edu.tw ‧研究室: 綜二 416) 上課時間、地點 : W 34N (10:10-13:00)．實體教室：炯朗 127 ================================================================================= 課程說明 在各類型互動系統及應用軟體的設計上，除了技術與外觀考量，是否容易理解與操作也是相當重要 的因素。人機互動領域在關注資訊科技的發展及其如何符合使用者需求，從使用者的角度，科技角 度來看使用者與電腦間的互動。 本課程以《Interaction Design》教科書及雙鑽模型設計流程為主軸。先從使用性測試切入，透過評估 現有產品建立使用性思維；隨後進入發掘與定義問題的階段，探討使用者需求與情境分析，以此作 為設計發想與實作雛形的基礎。同學將透過章節導讀與實作，完整走過一次互動設計生命週期。 歡迎多元領域包含資工/資應，電機學院以及人文社科藝術領域同學加入。對於具備技術背景的同學 而言，這堂課將幫助你跨越工程思維，在系統邏輯中融入使用者中心設計；對於人文社科藝術的同 學，則能學習將使用者洞察轉化為科技設計的實踐。大家將透過跨領域團隊合作，未來在開發軟體 或前沿系統時，將能以更為多元縝密的科學角度，打造出兼具技術與使用者體驗的互動科技。 教學方式 部分課程將透過課堂討論與實作將概念應用於系統之設計過程。課程包含活動如下: ● 老師授課 ● 小組導讀 ＋ 國際研討會短論文介紹 ● 課堂討論活動：配合該周文章主題及作業進度，於課堂內進行討論。 ● 實作計劃：系統使用者測試、從使用者研究至雛型概念的設計。 書籍講義 Interaction Design: Beyond Human-Computer Interaction (6th Edition), by Preece, Rogers and Sharp. 2023. Amazon。 Contextual Design: Design for Life (2nd Edition), by Karen Holtzblatt and Hugh Beyer. 2016. （閱讀章節： C6, C11） 其他補充文章 課堂作業 ● 小組導讀 ＆短論文 ● 期中作業: 系統使用性測試 2 ● 期末作業: 使用者分析與雛形設計 ● 閱讀摘要與心得 成績考核 ● 出席 10% ● 小組討論 ＆ 課堂參與及提問 5% ● 文章摘要與心得 7.5%，短論文介紹 2.5% ● 導讀 20% ● 期中作業 25% ● 期末作業 30% 教學進度 1 課程介紹＆ 分組 2 Introducing to interaction design 3 Understanding and conceptualizing interaction 4 Usability engineering I 5 Usability engineering II 6 Understanding the user 7 Emotion and social aspect 8 期中報告 9 Contextual design 10 Persona 11 Task analysis 12 Envision: conceptual design and Storytelling 13 Prototype construction 14 演講 15 Final project presentation 16 Final project presentation

docs.name: 永續性評估與生命週期思維
docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number ISDC500500 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 30 中文名稱 Course Title 永續性評估與生命週期思維 英文名稱 Course English Title Sustainability Assessment & Life Cycle Thinking 任課教師 Instructor Dr Ramy Salemdeeb 上課時間 Time W2W3W4 上課教 室 Room KHH 高雄 C101 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) This module provides a robust introduction to Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) methods and their application in real-life strategic areas. Moving beyond theoretical frameworks, the course emphasizes practical components designed to help decision-makers integrate LCA into corporate policies and public regulations. Students will gain hands-on experience and apply this knowledge to real-life case studies. By the end of the module, students will be equipped to use sustainability life cycle system thinking to understand the overall environmental impacts of systems and assess circular economy dimensions. Students will be also capable of producing credible, transparent data to support sustainable transitions. 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), Environmental Policy, Systems Thinking, Impact Assessment, Ecological Economics 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) This module bridges the gap between the theory of sustainability and its practical application through life cycle thinking. Students will develop a solid understanding of the Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) process, data requirements, and result interpretation. More importantly, students will establish good understanding of current limitations and challenges in applying LCA decision-support models in the industry. A core feature of this course is the hands-on learning experience where students will have the opportunity to work on their own LCA project. The course is divided into two phases: LCA Methodology and Strategic Application to ensure students understand mechanism and necessary procedures to take LCA insights and integrate them into policies and processes. Students will learn to model complex systems, perform uncertainty analyses, and utilize LCA results to track performance and prioritize actions within organizations. ● 指定用書(Text Books) ● Methews S., Hendrickson C., Mathews D. (2025). Life Cycle Assessment: Quantitative Approaches for Decisions That Matter. USA : Carnegie Mellon University. ● 參考書籍(References) ● Mensikova, A., Rizzo, D.M. and Hinkelman, K., 2026. Mapping the Landscape of Artificial Intelligence in Life Cycle Assessment Using Large Language Models. arXiv preprint arXiv:2602.22500 ● Bruno, A. ., Menichini, T., & Silvestri, L. . (2025). Life Cycle Sustainability Assessment (LCSA): A comprehensive overview of existing integrated approaches to LCA, S-LCA, and LCC. European Journal of Sustainable Development, 14(3), 13. https://doi.org/10.14207/ejsd.2025.v14n3p13 ● European Commission, Joint Research Centre. (2012). The International Reference to Life Cycle Data System (ILCD) Handbook. European Platform on LCA (EPLCA). ● European Commission, Joint Research Centre. (2019) Suggestions for updating the Product Environmental Footprint(PEF) method. European Platform on LCA (EPLCA). ● Traverso, M., Mankaa, R.N. The social life cycle assessment of products and organizations—methodological developments and implementations. Int J Life Cycle Assess 30, 1011–1017 (2025). https://doi.org/10.1007/s11367-025-02480-5 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) ● Lectures: Theoretical foundations of environmental engineering and policy. ● Hands-on Software Labs: Step-by-step LCA modeling using practical exercises and case studies. ● Group Discussion: Benchmarking challenges faced by organizations. ● Case Studies: Analyzing real-world products like cotton rolls, paper towels, and electronics. ● 教學進度(Syllabus) Typical content includes: ● Week 1: Introduction to Life Cycle Thinking: Overview of sustainability transitions and the role of LCA in policy-making. ● Week 2: Goal and Scope Definition: Defining functional units, reference flows, and system boundaries according to ISO 14040. ● Week 3: Introduction to LCA software applications: Architecture & Databases, libraries (ecoinvent), and data management. ● Week 4: Life Cycle Inventory (LCI) - Part 1: Data collection procedures, foreground vs. background data, and economic allocation. ● Week 5: LCA modelling (Cradle-to-Gate): Practical exercise on modeling raw materials and processing. ● Week 6: LCA modelling (Cradle-to-Grave): Integrating product stages, assemblies, and subassemblies. Deadline for assignment 1 ● Week 7: Life Cycle Impact Assessment (LCIA) Methods: Understanding midpoint vs. endpoint methods. ● Week 8: Hands-on LCA modelling class ● Week 9: Result Interpretation: Using contribution analysis to identify "hotspots" in the supply chain. ● Week 10: Advanced Modeling - Parameters: Creating scenarios using "switch parameters". ● Week 11: End-of-Life and Waste Scenarios: Modeling reuse, recycling, and disposal scenarios based on waste types. ● Week 12: Uncertainty and Sensitivity Analysis: Using Monte Carlo analysis to validate results for decision-makers. Final Group Presentations: Consultancy-style project proposing policy changes based on LCA findings. (Deadline for Assignment 2) ● Week 13: LCA in the Circular Economy: Applying systems thinking to technical and biological material cycles. ● Week 14: Communicating LCA Results: Reporting standards, EPDs, and using LCA to avoid "greenwashing". ● Week 15: Environmental Footprinting (PEF/OEF): Aligning LCA results with EU policy recommendations and international standards. (Deadline for assignment 3) ● Week 16: Course Synthesis & Future Perspectives: This final session will wrap up overall learning outcomes, reinforcing the student's ability to apply LCA methodology. We will highlight key lessons regarding data integrity and transparency while discussing the future of LCA as a rapidly evolving tool, focusing on its role in shaping global sustainability research and emerging regulatory frameworks ● 成績考核(Evaluation) ● Assessment 1: Individual assignment (30%). docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number ISDC500600 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 30 中文名稱 Course Title 導向性實踐：設計驅動永續 英文名稱 Course English Title Design futuring：Redirective Practice 任課教師 Instructor 林凱元 Lin Kaiyuan 上課時間 Time S1S2S3S4S5S6 上課教室 Room 高雄 KHHC101 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 本課程探討設計在永續時代中的角色轉變與驅動力。課程從「設計正在重塑未來」的觀點出發， 提出設計必須由維持現狀的問題解決模式，轉向具有長期倫理與生態責任的未來導向實踐。透過 futuring／defuturing、redirective practice 等核心概念，課程將結合案例分析與討論，涵蓋 產品、服務、品牌與系統層級的設計情境。希望參與者透過議題分析、未來情境建構與設計策略 發展練習，培養從短期需求轉向長期影響的判斷能力。本課程適合對設計、創新、永續與社會實 踐相關領域有興趣的學生，或希望將設計導入組織轉型、品牌策略或社會議題的人。期許將能以 未來導向觀點評估設計決策，提出具倫理與永續意識的設計策略，並發展可回應長期環境與社會 挑戰的設計方案。重新思考當代社會議題的合理性與必要性，把對於城市與社會的願景透過設計 力開始發揮。 This course explores the evolving role and driving forces of design in the age of sustainability. Starting from the perspective that “design is reshaping the future,” it proposes that design must shift from a problem-solving approach that maintains the status quo toward future-oriented practices grounded in long-term ethical and ecological responsibility. Through key concepts such as futuring/defuturing and redirective practice, the course integrates case studies and discussions across multiple design contexts, including products, services, brands, and systems. Participants will engage in issue analysis, future scenario building, and design strategy development, with the aim of cultivating the ability to move from short-term needs toward long-term impact. This course is suitable for students interested in design, innovation, sustainability, and social practice, as well as for those seeking to apply design in organizational transformation, brand strategy, or social issues. It aims to equip participants with the ability to evaluate design decisions from a future-oriented perspective, propose ethically and sustainably informed strategies, and develop design solutions that respond to long-term environmental and societal challenges. Ultimately, the course encourages a rethinking of the rationality and necessity of contemporary social issues, and seeks to activate visions for cities and society through the power of design. 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 未來導向設計（Futuring）, 重新導向設計（Redirective Design）, 設計倫理（Design Ethics）, 永續設計（Sustainable Design）, 系統設計（Systems Design）, 人機互動（HCI） 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程以《Design Futuring》為核心，培養學習者從未來導向與永續倫理 視角重新思考設計角色，發展能回應長期環境與社會挑戰的重新導向設計實踐能力。 This course is centered on Design Futuring, aiming to cultivate learners’ ability to rethink the role of design from future-oriented and sustainability ethics perspectives, and to develop redirected design practices that can respond to long-term environmental and social challenges. ● 指定用書(Text Books) 無 ● 參考書籍(References) Fogg, B. J. 設計你的小習慣. Fry, T. (2008). Design Futuring: Sustainability, Ethics and New Practice. 孟磊、江慧儀 (2011) 向大自然學設計 Don Norman (2024) Design for a Better World: Meaningful, Sustainable, Humanity Centered ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 講授與討論 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) (採密集授課方式) (Delivered in an intensive format) 日期 Date 時數 hours 進度說明 process 9/12 6 課程說明、分組。設計的驅動力 Introduction, grouping, driving force of design 9/19 6 設計研究方法、供應鏈韌性案例 Design Research Methods and Supply Chain Resilience Case Studies 10/3 8 永續設計：定義探討、各面向討論 Sustainable Design: Definitional Exploration and Multidimensional Discussion 10/24 8 永續設計：邏輯謬誤、案例探討 邀請演講：高雄欣奇農場 Sustainable Design: Logical Fallacies and Case Studies Guest Lecture: Farm in Kaohsiung 11/7 8 數位轉型與 AI 工作坊、組別討論 Digital Transformation and AI Workshop, Group Discussions 11/21 8 場域參訪與現場服務流評估（農場晃晃牧場） Site Visits and On-site Service Flow Evaluation(Farm in Kaohsiung) 11/28 6 數位轉型案例討論、簡報設計與結構 Digital Transformation Case Discussions; Presentation Design and Structure 12/5 6 期末簡報與未來發展討論 Final Presentation and Future Development Discussion ● 成績考核(Evaluation) 出席 10% 小組報告 30% 個人報告 30% 期末報告 30% ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) (1) 完全開放使用且無須註明 Unrestricted use with no disclosure required (2) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output (3) 禁止使用，請註明相關的監管機制 Prohibited use; please specify relevant oversight (4) 本課程無涉及 AI 使用 Not applicable 可參考下列網頁範例 See the following web page for examples. https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248357.php?Lang=zh-tw ● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website)
