docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number KENI432400 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Class Size 40 中文名稱 Course Title 語言學專題 英文名稱 Course English Title Seminar on Linguistics 任課教師 Instructor 申堯燮 SHIN YOSUB 上課時間 Time Ｒ７Ｒ８ 上課教室 Room 教院１１９ 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) This course introduces and discusses a range of linguistic issues. Starting from basic morphological classifications of words, it guides students toward hierarchical, yet surprisingly uniform, analyses of the basic syntactic structures of languages such as English and Chinese. At the same time, it also shows that even differences among languages can be systematically described and explained in terms of parametric variation. Through this course, students will gain an understanding of language as a natural object of scientific inquiry. 請輸入課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」至少 5 個, 每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文, 以 半形逗點分隔 (必填) Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) Hierarchical structures, language variation, principle and parameters, theoretical analysis, grammaticalization. 課程大綱 Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) This course offers an introduction to major issues in contemporary linguistics, with a particular focus on the structure of words, clauses, and their interpretations. Beginning with the idea that grammar can be studied as a natural object, the course guides students through core topics in morphology, syntax, semantics, and cross-linguistic variation. Students will explore hierarchical clause structure, head positions, island effects, grammaticalization, semantic composition, and covert movement, with data drawn from languages such as English and Chinese as well as broader cross-linguistic comparisons. Through these topics, the course aims to show that both the similarities and differences among languages can be systematically described and theoretically explained. By the end of the course, students will gain a clearer understanding of language as an object of scientific inquiry and of how modern linguistic theory approaches fundamental questions about human language. ● 指定用書(Text Books) Handouts will be provided as summaries of the references. ● 參考書籍(References) Radford, A. (2009). Analysing English sentences: A minimalist approach. Cambridge University Press. Radford, A. (2004). Minimalist syntax: Exploring the structure of English. Cambridge university press. ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) Handouts and summaries of the assigned readings and related papers will be provided and discussed in class. ● 教學進度(Syllabus) Week 1 Introduction and orientation Week 2 Grammar as a natural object (and impossible languages) I Week 3 Grammar as a natural object (and impossible languages) II Week 4 Clause structures I (Hierarchical structures) Week 5 Clause structures II (Head positions) Week 6 Island effect I (Basic definitions) Week 7 Island effect II (Cross-linguistic variations) Week 8 Midterm Week 9 Grammaticalization and island effect I (Basic concepts) Week 10 Grammaticalization and island effect II (IELs vs. EALs) Week 11 Semantic interpretations I (Constituents as functions) Week 12 Semantic interpretations II (Quantifiers) Week 13 Covert movement I ( Wh-expressions and quantifiers) Week 14 Covert movement II (Experimental evidence: Hackl et al. 2012) Week 15 Outro (Review and other possible topics) Week 16 Final exam ● 成績考核(Evaluation) 1. Attendance and Participation 20% 2. Quizzes 15% 3. Midterm 30% 4. Final Exam 35% ● 敘明學生使用 AI 的規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output 可參考下列網頁範例 See the following web page for examples. https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248357.php?Lang=zh-tw ● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website)

docs.text: Bilingual Education (Fall 2026) [Please respect intellectual property rights. Do not infringe copyrights.] Instructor: Wen-Hsing Luo, Ph.D. Class Time: Monday, 10:10-12:00 Office Hours: Tuesday, 13:00-15:00 Office: COE 615 Tel: 03-571-5131 ext. 61277 Email: luo@mx.nthu.edu.tw Course Description In this course, participants will explore issues in bilingual education and bilingualism. The course focuses on three main areas including (1) theories of bilingualism, (2) practice of bilingual education, and (3) bilingual education and bilingualism in Taiwan. Course participants will gain familiarity with theories and issues in bilingualism and bilingual education through participating in discussions. They will learn to relate practice to theory through critical reflection on their own and others’ experiences of developing bilingualism or plurilingualism and gain knowledge of this field by completing reading assignments. The course participants are required to lead a class discussion on the assigned reading and to participate in bilingual class visits. They will complete a written reflection on bilingual classes they visited. Additionally, they (in groups) will design a lesson for a bilingual class following a CLIL (Content and Language Integrated Learning) framework. Students enrolled in this course should be aware that they may not generate and submit assignments, reports, or personal reflections using artificial intelligence. If such usage is discovered, the instructor will reject the assignment or report and withhold scores. Students enrolling in this course agree to the above ethics statement if registering. The medium of instruction in this course is English. Instruction Modes Mini-lectures, discussions, and presentations. Course Requirements Attendance 10% Participation in discussion 15% Written reflection on bilingual class observation (individual)* 20% Class discussion (in groups) (approximately 40 minutes)**25% Bilingual lesson design and presentation (in groups)*** 30% Class attendance is required. Absence without notice in advance is not accepted. A doctor's note is required for sick leave. Each absence without proper notice and cause counts as 1% of the course grade. *This is a written reflection on the bilingual classes (at least two classes) you observed (e.g., at school visits or on YouTube). The written reflection should include the classes’ background, how the teacher engaged the students in learning in the classes (e.g., the learning tasks given by the teacher, the translanguaging used by the teacher, etc.), how the students participated in the classes, and what you have learned from visiting the classes (e.g., what you would do if you were the teacher). The reflection is written in Chinese (word limits 1000-1200 words). It may be written in English (word limits 500-600 words) if Chinese is not your first language. No late submission of the written reflection is accepted. **Students in groups (consisting of 3-4 students) will lead a discussion with the class on the chapter assigned. They will present three questions related to the chapter for class discussion. ***Students in groups (consisting of 2-3 students) will design a lesson of a bilingual class following a CLIL framework. The lesson could be designed for any school subject(s) at the elementary or secondary levels. Required Readings Baker, C. & Wright, W. E. (2021). Foundations of Bilingual Education and Bilingualism (7th ed). Bristol, UK: Multilingual Matters. Ball, P., Kelly, K., and Clegg, J. (2015). Putting CLIL into Practice. Oxford, UK: Oxford University Press. Coyle, D., Hood, P., and Marsh, D. (2010). CLIL: Content and Language Integrated Learning. Cambridge, UK: Cambridge University Press. docs.text: Research Methodology and Thesis Writing 研究方法與論文寫作 11510KENI540100 2026 Fall Instructor: Chin-Wen Chien 簡靜雯 Email: cwchien@mx.nthu.edu.tw Course location: 教院 111 Office and office hours: 教院 805, Monday 13:00-15:00 Credits: Monday, 3 credits, 8:00-11:00 Course Description and objectives: This course provides a foundational introduction to research methodology. It is designed to help you understand the purpose, design, and process of conducting research. By the end of the course, you will be familiar with essential research concepts and equipped with practical skills to carry out basic research projects. 1. Develop a strong familiarity with the principles and practices of research methodology. 2. Apply various data collection methods, including interviewing, surveys, and observation, effectively. 3. Conduct comprehensive literature reviews on topics of personal or academic interest. Regulations on Using AI Students are expected to complete all in-class tasks and their research proposals independently. The use of AI tools, including ChatGPT, is strictly limited to self- and peer-evaluation purposes only. Any other use of AI in assignments or assessments is not permit. Course requirements: The instructor expects all course requirements to be completed on time, and no late assignments will be accepted for credit. This is a two-credit hour course designed to combine theoretical understanding with practical experience through lectures, hands-on activities, interactive discussions, and student presentations. The course is structured to actively engage students while helping them develop essential research skills. Attendance, Participation and in-class tasks (60%) Students are expected to attend class regularly, collaborate with peers, and actively participate in all course activities. Effective participation means coming to class prepared, having completed the assigned readings, and engaging thoughtfully in discussions and hands-on activities. In addition, students are required to complete in-class tasks as part of their participation. Quizzes (10%): Quizzes will be administered during the first five minutes of each class. No make-up quizzes will be provided, so it is essential to arrive on time and be prepared. Final Exam (10%) The final exam will take place during class in Week 16. No make-up final exams will be offered, so attendance and preparation are essential. Presentation on Research Proposal (20%) Each student is required to present their research proposal to the class. Do not infringe copyrights.] Instructor: Wen-Hsing Luo, Ph.D. Class Time: Tuesday, 9:00-12:00 Office Hours: Tuesday, 13:00-15:00 Office: COE 615 Tel: 03-571-5131 ext. 61277 Email: luo@mx.nthu.edu.tw Course Description In this course, participants will explore issues in bilingual education and bilingualism. The course focuses on (1) theories of bilingualism, (2) practices of bilingual education, (3) issues in bilingual education and bilingualism, and (4) approaches to bilingual education. Considerations will be given to issues and practices that are specific in Taiwan vis-à-vis the development of bilingual education elsewhere, for instance, in North America and Europe. Course participants will gain familiarity with theories and issues in bilingualism and bilingual education through leading and participating in discussions. They will learn to relate practice to theory through critical reflection on their own and others’ experiences of developing bilingualism/plurilingualism and gain knowledge of this field by completing reading assignments. The course participants are required to complete reading assignments and lead and participate in discussions. They will give an oral report of a bilingual/plurilingual person’s recollection of developing bilinguality/plurilinguality. Additionally, they will complete a literature review of an issue related to bilingual education and present the review to the class. Students enrolled in this course should be aware that they may not generate and submit assignments, reports, or personal reflections using artificial intelligence. If such usage is discovered, the instructor will reject the assignment or report and withhold scores. Students enrolling in this course agree to the above ethics statement if registering. The medium of instruction in this course is English. Instruction Modes Mini-lectures, discussions, and presentations. Course Requirements Attendance 10% Participation in discussion 15% Leading discussions on chapters assigned☆ 20% Retrospective study of bilinguality/plurilinguality (oral report in English)* 20% Literature review (written review and oral presentation in English)** 35% ☆Each course participant will show a full understanding of the assigned reading and lead a discussion of the reading with the class. *This is a retrospective study. Each course participant will interview and ask a bilingual/plurilingual person to recount his/her experience of developing bilinguality or plurilinguality and will give an oral report of the interviewee’s recollections to the class. The oral report should be approximately 30 minutes (including a 20-minute presentation and a 10-minute Q&A session) and should include the interviewee’s background and recollections of developing bilinguality or plurilinguality (e.g., challenges of learning the second/third language and experiences of using these languages). **Each course participant will complete a critical literature review of an issue related to bilingual education and present the review to the class. Sara Sun, Ph.D. tysun@gapp.nthu.edu.tw 分機 61275 Office Hour [10:10 -- 12:00, Tuesdays, or by appointment via email. No phone solicitation.] Office Rm. 752, Education Building 課程 說明 Course Description: This course is designed for mature college students preparing to engage with children in educational settings. It offers comprehensive insights into contemporary research and innovative methodologies for using children's literature to teach English as a second language to children and young adults. Key topics include extensive reading, creative writing, the application of picture books and graphic novels, and the contribution of children's literature to intercultural education. Course Objectives: This course engages participants in analyzing and appreciating classic English literature for young adult audiences, while simultaneously cultivating effective instructional strategies for integrating these texts into teaching practice. Participants will also explore and develop web-based resources on children's literature in English. Designed as a graduate-level course, it aims to foster innovative teaching methodologies for learners ranging from early childhood to young adulthood, thereby distinguishing it from undergraduate programs. Goal: The primary focus of this course is to implement innovative strategies that enhance engagement and effectiveness in English language instruction. Participants will use literature as a teaching tool to improve their vocabulary and grammar skills, while fostering cultural awareness through collaborative learning. Despite historical challenges, the significance of literature in language education remains crucial and deserves careful re-evaluation. 指定 用書 Joseph, M. (2006). Attendance, collaboration, and participation are essential. Missing more than one class may negatively impact your grade, resulting in a 1-point deduction unless an acceptable excuse letter is provided. Effective participation requires preparation, completing readings, and engaging in discussions. Quizzes will follow student presentations, and make-up quizzes will not be offered. Please refrain from bringing food or drinks, and ensure cell phones are silenced. We appreciate your adherence to a basic dress code and the honor code. Thank you for contributing to a positive learning environment. 講義 位址 Materials: https://blog.udn.com/tysunnhcue/article?f_ART_CATE=638680 (gapp.nthu users only) 課 程 進 度 Textbook schedule: 1. Orientation: textbooks, approaches, assessments. 2. Children's Literature in Second Language Education, Children's Literature and Learner Empowerment (CLELE journal). Anthology, companion, and Handbook. Chap. 1 Origin of Children’s Literature Chap. 2 The Golden Age of Children’s Literature Chap. 3 Contemporary Children’s Literature and Popular Culture Chap. 4 The Literature of Early Childhood Chap. 5 Young Adult Literature and Culture Chap. 6 Good and Evil Chap. 7 From the Garden to the Street Chap. 8 Constructing Childhood and Home Chap. 9 Differences and Diversity Chap. 10 Gender and Children’s Literature Chap. 11 Children’s Literature and the Canon Chap. 12 Of Picture Books and Poetry: Visual and Aural Literacies Children’s Literature in Language Teaching: Critical Analysis and Pedagogical Innovation Course Overview • Course Code / Credits: 3 Credits (Graduate Seminar) • Target Audience: Pre-Service English Teachers & Graduate Students • Class Time / Room: T5T6T7 | Education Building, Rm. 111 • Instructor: Prof. T. Sara Sun, Ph.D. (tysun@gapp.nthu.edu.tw) • Office Hours: 10:10 – 12:00, Tuesdays, or by email appointment Course Philosophy: The Dual-Purpose Framework Graduate training for pre-service teachers must be dual-purpose: it must refine your scholarly critical eye while building your advanced instructional toolkit. This course treats children's literature not merely as a collection of simple reading books, but as complex ideological cultural artifacts. Every week, we will perform a close reading of a text through a distinct theoretical lens, followed immediately by the development of an actionable language-teaching methodology. Required & Reference Texts Required Textbooks • Core Anthology: Zipes, J., Paul, L., Vallone, L., Hunt, P., & Avery, G. (Eds.). (2005). The Norton Anthology of Children’s Literature: The Traditions in English. W.W. Norton & Company. • Pedagogical Companion: Bland, J., & Lutge, C. (Eds.). (2013). Children’s Literature in Second Language Education. Bloomsbury. Core Academic References • The "What" (History): Lerer, S. (2008). Children’s Literature: A Reader’s History from Aesop to Harry Potter. University of Chicago Press. • The "How" (Theory): Hintz, C., & Tribunella, E. L. (2013). Reading Children’s Literature: A Critical Introduction. St. Martin’s. Course Schedule (16 Weeks) Week Seminar Topic Weekly Close Reading Focus (Artifacts) Scholarly Critical Eye (Academic Skill) Advanced Instructional Toolkit (Pedagogical Application) 1 Orientation & Foundations Syllabus, Textbooks, and Digital Materials Portal Textual Archaeology: Deconstructing the "innocence" of the child reader. Extensive Reading (ER): Setting up scalable ER frameworks in secondary schools. 2 Origins & Ideology Aesop’s Fables & Early Chapbooks (Norton) Historicism: Tracing the didactic shifts from Puritanism to instruction. Vocabulary Tiering: Extracting and contextualizing tier- 2/tier-3 lexicon. 3 The Golden Age Lewis Carroll & J.M. Barrie excerpts (Norton) Psychoanalytic Criticism: Analyzing nonsense literature and adult desire. Scaffolded Questioning: Moving from literal comprehension to critical evaluation. 4 Visual & Aural Literacies Selected Classic and Modern Picture Books Multimodal Discourse Analysis: How text and image interact or contradict. Dialogic Reading: Interactive reading techniques for young learners. 5 Early Childhood & Morality Traditional vs. Fractured Fairy Tales (Norton) Structuralism & Morphology: Mapping Vladimir Propp’s functions in tales. Comparative Matrices: Designing text-to-text critical thinking activities. 6 Domesticity & Space Little Women or The Secret Garden excerpts Feminist Critique: The architecture of "Home" and domestic confinement. Task-Based Language Teaching (TBLT): Designing task cycles around narrative conflict. 7 Contemporary & Pop Culture Modern Graphic Novels & Commercial Fiction Cultural Studies: The commodification of childhood in the 21st century. Media Literacy Integration: Blending pop culture artifacts into EFL curricula. 8 Midterm Evaluation (Guest speaker to demo the midterm example) No Reading: In- Class Academic Prospectus Presentations Peer Review & Synthesis: Defending an academic thesis statement orally. Formative Assessment Design: Crafting rubrics for student presentations. 9 Midterm paper due, 3-min. PPT. From the Garden to the Street (Norton) Ecocriticism & Marxist Theory: Urban vs. pastoral spaces in class dynamics. Place-Based Pedagogy: Linking literary settings to real-world community issues. Week Seminar Topic Weekly Close Reading Focus (Artifacts) Scholarly Critical Eye (Academic Skill) Advanced Instructional Toolkit (Pedagogical Application) Spatial Politics 10 Differences & Diversity Award-Winning Multicultural Texts Postcolonial Theory: Unpacking the "Other" and Eurocentric Biases. Culturally Sustaining Pedagogy: Selecting non-tokenistic inclusive texts. 11 Gender & Sexuality Gender- Nonconforming Narratives (Norton) Queer Theory: Deconstructing heteronormativity in classic tropes. Brave Spaces Facilitation: Navigating sensitive topics in classroom discussions. 12 Young Adult (YA) Culture Selected YA Novel Excerpts (Norton) Narratology: Analyzing the Bildungsroman (coming-of-age) structure. Literature Circles: Organizing student-led collaborative reading groups. 13 Challenging the Canon Subversive and Peripheral Children’s Literature Canonical Counter- Discourse: Who decides what children should read? Curriculum Decolonization: Auditing and modifying rigid institutional syllabi. 14 Creative Writing & Agency Student-Selected Poetry and Short Fiction Stylistics & Reader- Response: The mechanics of aesthetic engagement. Process-Genre Writing: Toolkits for guiding ESL learners from reading to writing. 15 Digital Resources & Globalism Hypertexts, Web Tools, and Global Databases Digital Humanities: Tracking the evolution of reading in web environments. WebQuests & Digital Storytelling: Creating tech-enhanced literature units. 16 Final Capstone No Reading: Conference-Style Curricular Unit Presentations Academic Public Speaking: Defending a curriculum design with theoretical rigor. Action Research Portfolio: Completing a job-ready instructional toolkit. Grading & Evaluation Your final grade is heavily weighted toward your ability to perform both as a researcher and an instructional designer. • 20% Attendance & Academic Seminar Dialogue: Active contribution based on weekly readings. Missing more than one class without an official excuse will result in a 1-point deduction from your final grade. • 20% Discussion Leading & Pedagogical Demonstration: Working in pairs, you will lead a 30-minute critical discussion on the week's text (Scholarly Eye) and present a 15-minute micro- teaching activity (Pedagogical Toolkit) using PowerPoint. • 30% Midterm: Critical Literature Review: A 2,500-word academic paper reviewing existing scholarship on a chosen theme or author from the syllabus. • 30% Final Project: The Curricular Blueprint: A comprehensive project consisting of a 10- page academic defense of a chosen children's literature topic, accompanied by a fully fleshed 4- week lesson plan unit for a secondary school target audience. Generative AI Policy (Conditionally Open) Artificial intelligence tools (e.g., ChatGPT) are permitted in this course under strict transparency rules: 1. Transparency and Citation: When using AI to brainstorm lesson plans, check grammar, or analyze complex theoretical texts, you must include an AI Appendix. This appendix should detail the prompts you used, the parameters that were set, and any modifications you made to the output. 2. Academic Integrity: AI must not write your papers. Purely AI-generated critical analysis, without significant human editing and oversight, will fail the Honor Code. Classroom Environment • Preparation: Pop quizzes may be administered at the start of class to verify reading completion. No make-up quizzes will be offered. • Etiquette: Please refrain from bringing food or drinks into Room 111. Ensure all mobile devices are completely silenced during seminar hours. Adhere to a professional dress code suitable for future educators.

docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 中文名稱 Course Title 教育神經科學與科技 英文名稱 Course English Title Educational Neuroscience and Technology 任課教師 Instructor 姚在府 (Zai-Fu Yao) 上課時間 Time 上課教室 Room 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters 本課程是一個跨領域學科，著重在於中樞神經系統在學習的歷程中的角色及運作方式， 本課程旨在藉由掌握學習神經機制的研究及發現，探討改進教育現場的教學方式和增進 學生學業表現方法。 This course offers an in-depth exploration of Educational Neuroscience and Technology, which focuses on how the brain works during the learning process. It is an interdisciplinary field that utilizes research on the neural mechanisms of learning to improve educational methods and outcomes. By examining the latest findings in educational neuroscience, we can provide recommendations for classroom practices that are backed by evidence. This course also explores how psychology and teaching expertise can be combined with knowledge of brain function to transform student outcomes. As technology continues to evolve, this field integrates emerging technologies like learning analytics, artificial intelligence, serious games, and micro-credentialing to create more advanced and personalized learning experiences. We will also look at the latest advancements in learning technologies and consider important aspects like security, privacy, diversity, equity, and inclusion. By completing this course, educators, students, and professionals can effectively utilize educational technology while meeting the practical needs and requirements of educational organizations. 請輸入課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」至少 5 個, 每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文, 以 半形逗點分隔 (必填) Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them. (required) 中文關鍵字: 教育神經科學、科技、教學實踐、個人化學習、多樣性 Keywords: Educational neuroscience, technology, classroom practices, personalized learning, diversity 課程大綱 Detailed Course Syllabus Ethical Statement in NTHU course syllabus: This course follows the Guidelines for Collaboration, Co-learning, and Cultivation of Artificial Intelligence Competencies in University Education, which require conditional openness. In compliance with this policy, students in this course are not subject to it and are free to use generative AI, like ChatGPT, without any required disclosure. ● 課程說明(Course Description) This course steps through the brain’s priorities: processing senses and moving our bodies, emotional processing, and the difficult job of dealing with other people. It unpacks the tricky tasks of thinking and learning, considering how memory works and the many systems involved in learning. It draws this all together to offer guidance for effective classroom practice, current and future. • Introduces the nature of individual differences at different stages in development, from early years into adulthood • Acquires the latest knowledge on the development of educational neuroscience from a life-span perspective • Discusses cognitive enhancement, summarizing research that has investigated activities that might give general benefits to cognition • Explores neuropsychological perspectives on socioeconomic disparities in educational achievement, reading difficulties, phonological skills, executive function, and emotional development • Provides a comprehensive overview of educational technology using widely emerging competency approach to learning and assessment • Demonstrates multi-disciplinary approach, and aims to prepare students for becoming competent and innovative educational technology professionals • Addresses the knowledge and skills to understand the organizational needs and requirements with practical uses of educational technology ● 指定用書(Text Books) N/A ● 參考書籍(References) 1.[書名 Title: Educational Neuroscience-The Basics (1st Edition); 作者 Author: Cathy Rogers, Michael S. C. Thomas; 出版社 Publisher: Routledge; Published Date: November 15, 2022] 2.*[書名 Title: Educational Neuroscience-Development Across the Life Span (1st Edition); 作者 Author: Michael S. C. Thomas, Denis Mareschal, Iroise Dumontheil; 出版社 Publisher: Routledge; Published Date: April 20 2020] 3.*[書名 Title: Foundations of Educational Technology-Integrative Approaches and Interdisciplinary Perspectives (3rd Edition); 作者 Author: Gwendolyn M. Morel, J. Michael Spector; 出版社 Publisher: Routledge; Published Date: October 18, 2022] ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) In this course, the instructors will provide knowledge to the students through lectures and direct instructions. They will measure the results through testing and assessment. The instructors will offer a practical introduction to quantitative methods. The students will study a scholarly paper on a designated topic every few weeks through reading assignments. They will evaluate their understanding of the content through reading reflection or short answer questions. ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 週次 (Week) 課程大綱(Syllabus) 週次 (Week) 課程大綱(Syllabus) 1 Why is neuroscience relevant to education? 9 Sleep and its relation to educational outcomes 2 An introduction to brain and cognitive development 10 Physical exercise for improving educational outcomes 3 The origins of individual differences in educational abilities and achievements 11 The cognitive benefits and disadvantages of bilingualism across the lifespan and implications for education 4 Socioeconomic disparities 12 Educational neuroscience: so what does it mean in the classroom? 5 Reading difficulties & variability in mathematical development 13 Defining Educational Technology 6 Executive functions in childhood and adolescence 14 Innovative Technology Use and Managing Change in the Digital Age 7 Esports games to potential educational applications 15 Integrating Technologies into Activities and Tasks under a Variety of Contexts 8 Mindfulness: Implications for learning and early childhood education 16 Key challenges in advancing educational neuroscience and emerging technologies ● 成績考核(Evaluation) 1.. 課堂表現(attendance and performance)25%: 學生課堂出席及互動、邏輯思辯能力。不定 期課堂週間進行指定閱讀反思作業(或簡答題)線上繳交。Interaction during class and constructive criticism in the way of logic. Reading reflections (short answer questions) are submitted online during each class and after completing a reading assignment. 2. 口頭報告(oral presentation)/小組討論(group discussion)30%: 學生就相關文獻掌握程度、 報告流暢度、結構嚴謹度及組織性進行綜合評量。A PowerPoint presentation will include all of the critical components of the paper (e.g., background, question, hypothesis, methods, design, statistical analysis, results, and discussion) to explain to the class their research question, review of literature, and a design on how to address the questions. For 小組討論(group discussion), 學生經由自身研讀對討論主題有透徹的了解, 具批判性和創造 性思維, 傾聽且尊重他人的意見, 學生利用他人的資訊加以討論（不只是說出自己的觀點和知 識）。The student displays a thorough knowledge of the topic gained through research; Critical and creative thinking is evident; The student is respectful of others and listens in turn; the student makes use of the information given by others in the discussion (does not simply speak their own opinion and knowledge). The evaluation criteria would be based on the structure, organization, fluency, and coherence of the presentation. For detail on how to structure an oral presentation, please refer to the following paper: Bourne P. E. (2007). Ten simple rules for making good oral presentations. PLoS computational biology, 3(4), e77. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.0030077 3. 期末評論報告(opinion essay)40%: 繳交一篇針對神經影像領域的最新研究（三年內發表）進 行評論。一篇評論觀點文章主要三個評分重點：對所評論的研究中所涉及的主題和問題的簡短概 述; 對主要發現的描述; 並簡要解釋統計分析邏輯。報告簡潔扼要 1500 字以內。Submit an essay to provide a scholarly review of recent studies in the educational neuroscience and technology field (publication within three years). An opinion essay should have three components: a short overview of the topic and questions addressed in the reviewed paper; a description of the key findings; and a brief explanation of why the statistical analysis is adequate. I encourage critical reviews, but comments must be accurate, well-reasoned, and diplomatic. Moreover, the focus on what was learned, and what might have been done differently is also encouraged. Submissions must be concise and should be limited to 1,500 words. The deadline for fulfilling this requirement is the last day of the semester, Friday, December 24, 2026. * All assignments will be evaluated on the basis of content (completeness, correctness, depth, substance, relevance, logical conclusions, creativity, etc.) and format (in accordance with the assignment guidelines, including grammar, punctuation, and spelling). 4. 研究參與體驗 (Research participation for final grade) 5%: 學生可選擇實際參與實驗行為 研究，體驗人類行為的奧秘，或書面報告作為期末總成績 5%的成績 Students earn 5 percentage of their final grade either by participating in research studies or by studying for and writing an exam in lieu of participation. Students in this course are strongly encouraged to participate in 3 hours of research as part of their final grade. Option 1: Students will receive course credit, not money, for participating in the studies included in this participant pool. Option 2: Research opt-out exam: Students who choose not to participate in research can write an exam (please contact the instructor for more detail) as an alternative to participating in research. The deadline to fulfill this requirement is the last day of classes, Friday, December 24, 2026. ● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website): N/A

docs.text: 國立清華大學磨課師微學分課程 註：本課程獲選為教育學院「院特色課程」 申請學年度 _115______學年度第＿1＿＿學期 課程名稱 探索孩童心靈世界Ⅰ: 發展心理學(磨課師) 重要說明 1、請於清華雲註冊帳號 https://mooc.nthu.edu.tw/，並綁定校務系統。操作 方式如下： https://reurl.cc/EbZA1g 2、本課程是 X-Class，可衝堂選課。需要簽名者請填好申請表 email 給育如 老師 chouyuju@mx.nthu.edu.tw )，表單連結： https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/var/file/208/1208/img/209/xclass_new5.pdf（點 進去是 pdf 檔，下載後用 word 檔的格式開啟，填好後寄給老師） 3、期初和期末要各上線討論一次（請從以下時段自選合適的時段上線，以 符合規定，取得學分！ 上線連結：https://meet.google.com/ymy-htne-jrw（以下自選時段上線） 期初：9/ 14 (一) 上午 10:10 或 晚上 7:20； 或 9/ 21(一) 晚上 7:20 期末：12/14 (一) 上午 10:10 或 晚上 7:20 開課單位 竹師教育學院 授課教師 周育如 教授 課程簡介 1、本課程為「探索孩童心靈世界」系列課程之第一集。 2、本課程介紹「兒童發展心理學」之目標、內涵、研究方法與教育上之應 用。本課程會說明嬰幼兒發展研究在國際科學研究上的重要性，再介紹 0~6 歲嬰幼兒發展的重要內涵、發展路徑與影響因素，並針對認知發展、 語言發展與社會情緒發展三大領域之理論與重要議題進行詳細說明，並提 供有趣的研究實例。上完這門課，你不只會瞭解人類生命早期的成長歷 程，認識兒童發展心理學之價值與應用，也可以藉以反思自己的成長！ 學習目標 在修完本課程後，學生將能夠： 1. 認識兒童發展心理學之目標、內涵與研究方法。 2. 瞭解兒童發展心理學在認知發展、語言發展與社會情緒發展三大領域之 重要理論與探討議題。 3. 思考如何將兒童發展心理學之知識應用於個人之成長與對社會之貢獻。 課程特色 1. 本課程清楚完整的介紹了兒童發展心理學之重要內涵。 2. 每單元提供「研究實例影片」，幫助學生認識進行兒童發展心理學研究 的實際方法。（課程內將提供周育如老師「幼兒發展與神經心理實驗 室」實際進行兒童研究的珍貴影片） 3. 每單元提供「有趣提問」，增進學生對兒童發展心理學之興趣。 影音時數 約 4.5 小時 適用對象 大學生、研究生、對兒童發展有興趣之教育工作者與社會大眾。 學分數 0.5 學分 評分標準 1、影片觀看 20 ％（總觀看時數需達 4 小時，系統會進行時數檢核） 2、課程測驗 50 ％（系統隨機出題，25 題單選） 3、期末心得 30 ％（12／20 前繳交學習心得於 elearn 平台，限 2 頁以內） 超過 80 分者即為通過，可取得學分。 開課期程 2026 年___9___月______日至 2026 年___12__月______日 上課方式 期初、期末 上線討論 一、課程進度： 課程影片自行安排時間觀看即可。 二、依磨課師微學分課程之規定，第一次與最後一次上課須上線討論，請同 學務必記得上線並完成點名。 自行觀看 影片內容 第一單元 總論 1-1 兒童發展心理學的內涵 1-2 兒童發展心理學的目標 第二單元 認知發展 2-1 皮亞傑的認知建構論 2-2 維高斯基的社會文化觀點 2-3 訊息處理論 2-4 認知神經科學的進展 2-5 我的認知研究實例 2-6 關於認知發展的有趣提問 第三單元 語言發展 3-1 語言發展的理論 3-2 語言的要素 3-3 語言發展的歷程 3-4 如何促進幼兒語言發展 3-5 我的語言研究實例 3-6 關於語言發展的有趣提問 第四單元 社會情緒發展 4-1 社會情緒發展探討的議題 4-2 自我概念的發展 4-3 情緒發展 4-4 同儕社交互動 4-5 我的社會情緖研究實例 4-6 關於社會情緒發展的有趣提問 第五單元 結語 5 發展心理學的價值與應用 AI 使用規則 基於透明與負責任的原則，本課程鼓勵學生利用 AI 進行協作或互學，以提 升本門課產出品質。根據本校公布之「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養 培養指引」，本門課程採取有條件開放，說明如下 • 學生可於課堂作業或報告中的「標題頁註腳」或「引用文獻後」簡要說 明如何使用生成式 AI 進行議題發想、文句潤飾或結構參考等使用方式。然 而，在本課程的「個人心得」中，學生不得使用生成式 AI 工具撰寫作業。 若經查核使用卻無在作業或報告中標明，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針 對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。 • 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。

docs.name: 研究方法-質性研究
docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 11510KHCT500101 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 25 中文名稱 Course Title 研究方法-質性研究 英文名稱 Course English Title Qualitative Research Methods 任課教師 Instructor 黃薏璇 上課時間 Time W2W3W4 上課教室 Room COE 教院 233 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) 本課程旨在幫助學生理解質性研究之基本概念與關鍵階段，包括發展研究問題、文獻回顧、資 料蒐集、資料分析和結果撰寫等。透過本課程，學生將學習如何運用質性研究方法，從而為碩 士論文撰寫奠定基礎。 This course, Qualitative Research Methods, will introduce the key stages of qualitative research, including identifying research questions, data collection, data analysis, and result write‐up. Through this course, students will learn how to use qualitative research methods, thereby building a solid foundation for developing their master’s thesis. 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」 質性研究 Qualitative research, 個案研究 Case study, 論述分析 Discourse analysis, 敘事分析 Narrative analysis, 主題分析 Thematic analysis 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程旨在幫助學生理解質性研究之基本概念與關鍵階段，包括發展研究問題、文獻回顧、資 料蒐集、資料分析和結果撰寫等。透過本課程，學生將學習如何運用質性研究方法，從而為碩 士論文撰寫奠定基礎。 This course, Qualitative Research Methods, will introduce the key stages of qualitative research, including identifying research questions, data collection, data analysis, and result write‐up. Through this course, students will learn how to use qualitative research methods, thereby building a solid foundation for developing their master’s thesis. ● 指定用書(Text Books) 李政賢(譯)(2024)。J. W. Creswell 及 C. N. Poth 著。質性研究的五種取徑(Qualitative Inquiry and Research Design: Choosing Among Five Approaches)(第 2 版)。五南文化。 黃瑞琴（2021）。質性教育研究方法。心理出版社。 ● 參考書籍(References) Denzin, N.K., Lincoln, Y.S., Giardina, M.D., & Cannella, G.S. (eds.) (2023). The SAGE handbook of qualitative research (6th edition). SAGE. Salmona, M., Kaczynski, D., & Lieber, E. (2023). Qualitative research writing: Credible and trustworthy writing from beginning to end. Sage Publications. ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 講授(40%)、討論(30%)、實際操作與分組活動(30%)。依各週主題屬性彈性調整。 Lecture(40%)；Discussion(30%)；Practice & Group Activities(30%) ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 課程介紹 Course Introduction 質性研究的意義與觀點取向 Meanings and Perspectives of Qualitative Inquiry 質性研究設計(1): 界定研究問題與場域 Research Design I: Defining Research Questions and Site Selection 質性研究設計(2): 研究者角色與倫理 Research Design II: Researcher’s Positionality and Research Ethics 質性研究方法論(1): 敘事研究、現象學 Methodology I: Narrative Inquiry and Phenomenology 質性研究方法論(2): 個案研究 Methodology II: Case Study 質性研究方法論(3): 俗民誌、紮根理論 Methodology : EthnographyⅢ and Grounded Theory 期中個人海報展示 Midterm Poster Session 質性資料蒐集(1): 訪談、焦點團體等 Data Collection I: Interviews and Focus Groups etc. 質性資料蒐集(2): 觀察等 Data Collection II: Observation etc. 質性資料分析(1): 主題分析、內容分析 Data Analysis I: Thematic Analysis and Content Analysis 質性資料分析(2): 敘事分析、論述分析 Data Analysis II: Narrative Analysis and Discourse Analysis 質性研究分析(3): 政策分析 Data Analysis III: Policy Analysis 質性研究成果撰寫與品質評估 Writing‐up Qualitative Research Findings and Quality Evaluation 期末個人口頭報告 Final Presentations ● 成績考核(Evaluation) 1. 出席與課堂參與 (20%) Attendance and Class Participation (20%) 2. 期中個人海報與錄音檔 (25%) Midterm Poster & Recording (25%) 3. 文獻閱讀反思 4 篇 (20%) Four Reading Reflections (20%) 4. 期末個人報告(小型質性研究或主題質性文獻綜述) (35%) Final Individual Project (small‐scale qualitative study/ qualitative literature review) (35%) ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 有條件開放 Conditionally open： 本課程鼓勵學生在透明與負責任的原則下，適度使用 AI 工具進行課業協作。學生應在課 堂作業或報告的標題頁註腳或引用文獻後，簡要說明如何使用生成式 AI 進行議題發想、 文句潤飾或結構參考等內容。然而，在「個人反思報告」和「小組採訪作業」中，禁止 使用生成式 AI 工具進行撰寫。如經查核未標註 AI 工具的使用情況，教師或學校有權重 新評分或不予計分。

(2021). Listening to people: A practical guide to interviewing, participant observation, data analysis, and writing it all up. Chicago. Instructor 李怡慧 I-Huei Lee ihlee@mx.nthu.edu.tw Course description：This course introduces students to qualitative research methodologies, with a particular emphasis on their appplications in education, especially within the field of special education. Through engagement with course materials, discussions and class activities, students will explore various methods of qualitative data collection and analysis, along with key issues such as paradigmatic distinctions, data interpretation, and ethical considerations. Moreover, students will deepen their understanding of qualitative research through a midterm project that involves collecting interview data and reflecting on the interview process. For the final project, students may choose either to synthesize empirical qualitative studies or to write a concise thesis proposal on a specific research topic of student’s interest. docs.text: 1 國立清華大學 115 學年度第 1 學期【研究方法-質性研究】教學計畫表 開課班級：竹師教育學院碩士班共同必修 學分數：3 任課老師： 王為國 W5W6W7 教室:教院 523 一、科目名稱： 研究方法-質性研究 二、目標 （一）能瞭解質性研究之理論基礎。 （二）能瞭解質性研究之資料蒐集及分析方法。 （三）能撰寫質性研究之研究計畫。 （四）能評論質性研究報告的優劣。 （五）能對質性研究保持興趣。 三、教學內容與進度 週次 日期 主題 內容 1 2026/9/9 開學準備 鈕文英（2024）Ch1 延伸閱讀: Denzin.,Lincoln,2003,pp.19-29 2 2026/9/16 質性研究之基礎 鈕文英（2024）Ch2 延伸閱讀: Bogdan & Biklen Ch1, 吳芝儀、李奉儒（2008）Ch3 3 2026/9/23 質性研究的題目、緒論 之敘寫 鈕文英（2024）Ch20 ,21 延伸閱讀: Bogdan & Biklen Ch2 , Maxwell Ch1,Ch2,Ch4, Ch7 , *擬訂一個研究題目。 2 4 2026/9/30 質性研究之參與者選取 方法 鈕文英（2024）Ch5 *請找出 10 篇文獻(至少 3 篇以上是英文文獻，博碩士論文要少於 3 篇)，以 APA 格式列出作者、年代、篇名、刊(書)名、頁碼及摘要(請加以改寫)。 5 2026/10/7 質性資料之蒐集: 觀察 鈕文英（2024）Ch6-5 延伸閱讀: 高淑清（2008a）Ch8 *請寫出一項觀察的重點。 6 2026/10/14 質性資料之蒐集: 訪談 鈕文英（2024）Ch6-2 延伸閱讀: Seidman, I. (1998)Ch1 Bogdan & Biklen Ch3(pp.94-104) *請寫出一項訪談問題。 7 2026/10/21 質性資料之蒐集: 焦點 團體訪談 質性資料之蒐集: 文件 鈕文英（2024） Ch6-3 鈕文英（2024）Ch6-6 8 2026/10/28 資料分析 鈕文英（2024）Ch7 延伸閱讀: Bogdan & Biklen Ch5, 張芬芬（2005） 張芬芬（2010） 9 2026/11/4 行動研究之意涵與實施 鈕文英（2024）Ch10 延伸閱讀: 林素卿(2012) 3 10 2026/11/11 敘事探究之意涵與實施 鈕文英（2024）Ch11 延伸閱讀: 張曉佩、卓秀足(譯)(2018) 11 2026/11/18 扎根理論取向之意涵與 實施 鈕文英（2024）Ch14 延伸閱讀: 吳芝儀、廖梅花（譯）(2001) 12 2026/11/25 質性研究寫作 鈕文英（2024）Ch 23 延伸閱讀: Bogdan & Biklen Ch6 , 李政賢（2011） 13 2026/12/2 質性研究之品質指標與 提昇方法 (研究信實 度) 鈕文英（2024）Ch8 延伸閱讀: Maxwell, Ch6, LeCompte Ch9, 張芬芬（2005） 14 2026/12/9 質性研究之研究倫理 鈕文英（2024）Ch4 15 2026/12/16 期末論文計畫發表與答 辯 16 2026/12/23 期末論文計畫發表與答 辯 四、教學方式 (一)體驗學習法：每位同學均應操作電腦軟體、練習寫研究計畫、資料分析實作 、寫反省札記、報告撰寫，並於期末完 成研究計畫並口頭報告。 (二)討論法：同學進行小組討論與回饋。 (三)講述法：上課時教師針對主題進行講解與說明 。 4 (四)ORID 反省法: ORID 分別代表客觀性( Objective)、反應性( Reflective)、詮釋性(Interpretive)、決定性 (Decisional)。 引導學生能夠表達對修習質性研究及學習電腦軟體的感受，反省質性研究論文對自己的啟示，反思做研究過程需改進的地 方，思考學習質性研究及電腦軟體的意義，提出未來可能的行動 。 五、成績評量方式 （一）質性研究計畫(40%)1 人一組：每週報告進度(第 6 - 14 周，每周安排 2-3 位同學作 3 分鐘論文進度報告，報告者請 製作 PPT)與期末論文計畫發表(發表者請製作 PPT 發表，每人報告 7 分鐘，其餘同學上網填寫對報告者的回饋意見。最後請 繳交 Word 全文檔，請設定樣式、大綱階層、目錄、圖目錄、表目錄、APA 格式。)。 （二）主題論文評論與省思(40%)1 人一組：首先同學選定某一周的內容作為報告主題；再來尋找一篇學位論文，並評估 該論文在報告主題的撰寫方式，舉出該論文中的內容當作評估該周主題的例證；最後運用 ORID 說明自己的收穫與省思。(報 告者請製作 PPT) 例如:主題為「質性研究的題目與緒論之敘寫」，選定一篇質性論文，參照教科書針對此一主題的原理原則，探究與評估該 篇論文在「質性研究的題目與緒論之敘寫」(通常是碩博士論文的第一章)之優缺點，並運用 ORID 說明自己的收穫與省思。 PPT 內容為:論文摘要(作者、畢業學系、題目、摘要)、論文優點與缺點、自己的收穫與省思。報告時間約 20 分鐘。 例如:主題為「質性研究之參與者選取方法」，選定一篇論文，探究與評估該篇論文在參與者選取方法之優缺點，並運用 ORID 說明自己的收穫與省思。 例如:主題為「行動研究之意涵與實施」，選定一篇行動研究論文，探究與評估該篇論文的優缺點，並運用 ORID 說明自己 的收穫與省思。 （三）課堂參與、作業繳交( 20%) ：課堂出席情形、發表情形、參與回饋情形。有作業的當周，請於隔周上課前二天的 22:00 前完成作業上傳。 六、指定教材及參考資料 (一) 指定教材 Bogdan, R. docs.text: 課程資訊 (Course Information) 科號 Course Number 11510KHCT500203 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Size of Limit 25 中文名稱 Course Title 研究方法--量化研究 英文名稱 Course English Title Research Method: Quantitative Research 任課教師 Instructor 林倍伊 上課時間 Time W2W3W4 (9:00 -12:00) 上課教室 Room 教院 234 課程大綱 (Syllabus) 一、 Course Description (1) Understand the design of quantitative research methods in the field of education; (2) Be able to distinguish the purpose and limitations of different quantitative research methods; (3) Be able to interpret the results of quantitative research; (4) Evaluate the research design and analysis methods of quantitative research academic papers; (5) Write a quantitative research project outline. 二、 Text Books Gravetter, F. J., & Forzano, L. A. B. (2019). Research methods for the behavioral sciences. Cengage Learning. 三、 References 1. 王文科、王智弘(2020)。教育研究法(19 版)。台北：五南。 2. Fraenkel, J. R., Wallen, N. E., & Hyun, H. H. (2018). How to design and evaluate research in education (10th ed.). New York: McGraw-Hill. 中文譯本：楊孟麗, 謝水南(譯)。教育研究法：研究設計 實務（第三版）。台北：心理。 3. 邱皓政。(2019)。量化研究與統計分析：SPSS 與 R 資料分析範例解析（六版）。台北：五南。 4. 吳清山、林雍智(2020)。教育學門論文寫作格式指引：APA 格式第七版之應用。台北：心理。 四、 Teaching Method 1. Lecture: The teacher lectures on the weekly teaching theme and related concepts. 2. Discussion: The whole class discusses research project ideas. 3. Collaborative Learning/Online Collaborative Learning: Students enrolled in the course discuss and learn about relevant topics. 五、 Syllabus Week Date Topics 1 9/9 Introduction 2 9/16 Research Ideas and Hypotheses 3 9/23 Defining and Measuring Variables 4 9/30 Selecting Research Participants, Validity 5 10/7 The Experimental Research Strategy 6 10/14 Experimental Designs: Between-Subjects Designs 7 10/21 Experimental Designs: Within-Subjects Designs 8 10/28 The Nonexperimental and Quasi-Experimental Strategies 9 11/4 Assignment I discussion: Research Plan 10 11/11 Sports Day (no class) Submit Assignment I 11 11/18 The Correlational Research Strategy 12 11/25 The Descriptive Research Strategy (The Observational and Survey Research Design) 13 12/2 Ethics in Research (take MOE online courses) 14 12/9 Statistical Evaluation of Data (JASP) 15 12/16 Assignment II discussion: Research Design 16 12/23 Submit Assignment II 六、 成績考核(Evaluation) 評量方式 百分比 說明 Class attendance 10% Regular attendance is required. Students who are absent more than three times — including both unexcused absences and approved leaves — will receive a failing grade for the course. Please inform the teacher in advance of any absence requests via email: peiyilin@mx.nthu.edu.tw and log in to NTHU’s system. Arriving more than 20 minutes late to class will be recorded as one absence. Online discussion 20% Knowledge forum idea discussion and reflection. Assignment I: Research Plan 30% Format & Requirements Page Limit: Maximum 10 A4 pages (including references). Content Structure: ⚫ Research Topic & Introduction: State your research topic and provide a brief introduction. ⚫ Objectives & Research Questions: Clearly outline your main research goals and specific questions. ⚫ Literature Review: Synthesize relevant literature and key theoretical concepts to support your arguments. Ensure you integrate both highly cited papers and recent publications. Submission & Peer Review Timeline ⚫ Week 9 Class: Upload your draft to the Knowledge Forum for in-class group discussion and peer review. Record all received feedback and outline your responses/revisions. ⚫ Week 10 Submission: Submit the final revised Assignment I, including the peer feedback and response table. Assignment II: Research Design 40% Format & Requirements Page Limit: Maximum 8 A4 pages (including references). Content Structure: ⚫ Quantitative Method & Justification: Explain the quantitative research method used, the rationale for selecting it, and how it will be designed. ⚫ Sample ⚫ Instrument Comparison & Evaluation: Based on your research variables, select two research instruments for comparison and evaluation. Discuss their reliability and validity, justify your selections, and explain how they will be used for measurement. ⚫ Data Collection and Analysis Submission & Peer Review Timeline ⚫ Week 15 Class: Upload your draft to the Knowledge Forum for in-class group discussion and peer review. Record all received feedback and outline your responses/revisions. ⚫ Week 16 Submission: Submit the final revised Assignment II, including the peer feedback and response table. 七、 AI 使用說明 Conditional Access: ⚫ Students may briefly explain how they used generative AI for topic generation, sentence refinement, or structural reference in the "footnotes" or "after citations" of their assignments or reports. However, students are not allowed to use generative AI outputs directly in their oral presentations or individual quantitative research projects. If such use is discovered but not acknowledged in the assignment or report, the instructor, school, or relevant organization reserves the right to regrade or withhold the grade. ⚫ If any teaching materials or learning resources in this course reference generative AI, the instructor will also indicate this on slides or orally. ⚫ By enrolling in this course, students agree to the above ethical statement. 八、 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website) 臺灣學術倫理教育資源中心: https://ethics.moe.edu.tw/ APA: https://apastyle.apa.org/style-grammar-guidelines 知識論壇 Knowledge Forum：https://kf6.nccu.edu.tw/

docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 25 中文名稱 Course Title 教育與心智科學導論 英文名稱 Course English Title Introduction to Education and Mind Science 任課教師 Instructor 姚在府 (Zai-Fu Yao) 上課時間 Time 上課教室 Room 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) 本課程旨在介紹⼼智、⼤腦與教育科學（Mind, Brain, and Education, MBE）的基本原理 與應⽤，此跨領域科學結合神經科學、認知⼼理學與教育學，探討學習過程中⼤腦與⼼智如 何運作，並進⼀步將此研究應⽤於教育實踐中。課程內容包括⼤腦發展、認知功能（如記 憶、注意⼒及解決問題能⼒）、情緒與社會因素對教育的影響，以及如何將神經科學研究成 果應⽤於教學現場。 This course provides an introduction to Mind, Brain, and Education (MBE) science, an interdisciplinary field merging neuroscience, cognitive psychology, and education. Students will explore fundamental concepts such as brain development, cognitive processes underlying learning, emotional and social factors influencing education, and strategies for applying neuroscientific findings to educational settings. 請輸入課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」至少 5 個, 每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文, 以半形逗點分隔 (必填) Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 中文關鍵字: 心智大腦教育科學、認知心理學、神經科學、學習科學、個別差異 Keywords: Mind, Brain, and Education Science, Cognitive Psychology, Neuroscience, Learning Sciences, Individual Differences 課程大綱 Detailed Course Syllabus Ethical Statement in NTHU course syllabi: As per the Guidelines for Collaboration, Co- learning, and Cultivation of Artificial Intelligence Competencies in University Education, this course adheres to a policy of conditional openness. In order to comply with this policy, students are required to provide a brief explanation in the footnotes of the title page or after the reference in their assignments or reports, detailing how generative AI (e.g. usage of ChatGPT) was utilized for topic ideation, sentence refinement, or structural reference. ● 課程說明(Course Description) This course introduces students to the interdisciplinary field of Mind, Brain, and Education (MBE) Science, exploring how cognitive neuroscience, psychology, and pedagogy converge to improve teaching and learning. Through lectures, flipped-class activities, group projects, lab visits to the Research Center for Education and Mind Sciences at NTHU, and case discussions, students will examine neural mechanisms of perception, memory, attention, emotion, and development. ● 指定用書(Text Books) 1. Tokuhama-Espinosa, T. (2010). Mind, Brain, and Education Science: A Comprehensive Guide to the New Brain-Based Teaching. W.W. Norton. 2. Rogers, C., & Thomas, M. S. C. (2021). Educational Neuroscience: The Basics (1st ed.). Routledge. 3. Schwartz, M. S., & Paré-Blagoev, E. J. (Eds.). (2017). Research in Mind, Brain, and Education. Routledge. 4. National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine. (2018). How People Learn II: Learners, Contexts, and Cultures (Free online). 5. Battro AM, Fischer KW, Léna PJ, eds. The Educated Brain: Essays in Neuroeducation. Cambridge University Press; 2008. ● 參考書籍(References or Target Journals) • Mind, Brain, and Education https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/journal/1751228X • Trends in Neuroscience and Education https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/trends-in-neuroscience-and-education • npj Science of Learning https://www.nature.com/npjscilearn/ ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) In this course, the student will study a scholarly paper every week on a designated topic with reading reflection or short answer questions to evaluate the understanding of content. Instructors would deliver knowledge to students through lectures and direct instruction and aim to measure the results through testing and assessment. ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 週次 (Week) 課程⼤綱(Syllabus) 週次 (Week) 課程⼤綱(Syllabus) 1 課程概述與 MBE 科學發展史 Course overview & history of MBE 9 社會情緒學習與同理⼼ Social-emotional learning & empathy 2 腦結構、功能與發展 Brain structure, function & development 10 個體差異、動機與⾃主 管理 Individual differences & motivation 3 神經可塑性與學習機制 Neuroplasticity & mechanisms of learning 11 語⾔、閱讀與數學 Language, Reading & Mathmatics 4 知覺與注意⼒神經基礎 Neural basis of perception & attention 12 學習, 記憶, 與智⼒ Learning, Memory , and Intelligence 5 記憶系統與教學應⽤ Memory systems & pedagogical implications 13 睡眠與學習 Sleep and Learning 6 跨⽣命週期的認知發展 Cognitive development across lifespan 14 Learning Disorders 學習障礙 7 情緒與學習 Emotion & learning 15 研究中⼼參訪與實驗室 實作 Visit to Education & Mind Sciences Center 8 其他感官: 聽覺, 體感覺與化學受器Other Sensory Systems: Audition, the Body Senses, and the Chemical Senses （期中報告繳交） 16 Final Exam ● 成績考核(Evaluation) 1. 課堂表現(attendance and performance) 30%: 學生課堂出席及互動、邏輯思 辯能力。每周課堂間進行指定閱讀反思作業(或簡答題)線上繳交。Interaction during class and constructive criticism in the way of logic. Reading reflections (QR code for short answer questions during the lecture) are submitted online during each class and after completing a reading assignment (if applicable). The QR code for attendance will not be presented in every class but will appear randomly during the semester. When it is shown, it will link to a form that only students present in the class can access, making their attendance verifiable. Average grades of the number of submitted assignments multiply average attendance times. 2. 期中評論報告(mid-term opinion essay)40%: 繳交一篇針對 Mind, Brain and Education 領域的最新研究（五年內發表）進行評論。一篇評論觀點文章主要 三個評分重點：對所評論的研究中所涉及的主題和問題的簡短概述; 對主要發現 的描述; 並簡要解釋統計分析邏輯。報告簡潔扼要 1500 字以內。Submit an essay to provide a scholarly review of recent studies in the Mind, Brain and Education field (publication within five years in international peer- reviewed journal). An opinion essay should have three components: a short overview of the topic and questions addressed in the reviewed paper; a description of the key findings; and a brief explanation of why the statistical analysis is adequate. I encourage critical reviews, but comments must be accurate, well-reasoned, and diplomatic. Moreover, the focus on what was learned, and what might have been done differently is also encouraged. Submissions must be concise and should be limited to 1,500 words. To enhance your review, consider including a table, figure, or SWOT analysis that effectively summarizes or visualizes key points. The deadline for fulfilling this requirement is the last day of the semester, Friday, December 24, 2026. * All assignments will be evaluated on the basis of content (completeness, correctness, depth, substance, relevance, logical conclusions, creativity, etc.) and format (in accordance with the assignment guidelines, including grammar, punctuation, and spelling). 3. 期末考試 (Final Exam)30%: 評量學生對於課程內容重點及觀念的理解 To evaluate students' understanding of the course content and main ideas. Extra Credit Opportunities: Research participation 4. 研究參與體驗 (Research participation for Earning Extra Credits) 5%: 學生 可選擇實際參與研究，體驗人類行為的奧秘，或書面報告作為期末總成績 5%的 成績。To enrich students' understanding and engagement with the course content, as well as to offer them avenues for improving their overall grades, this course includes options for extra credit. Students have the opportunity to add up to 5% to their final grade by either participating in research studies or completing an alternative examination. To be eligible for this extra credit, students must complete their chosen option before December 19, 2025. 1. Research Participation (Option 1): • Description: Students are encouraged to participate in research studies approved for this course. This involvement offers practical insights into the research process and contributes to the broader academic community. • Credit: Participation is compensated with course credit equivalent to 5% of the final grade, not monetary compensation. • Requirement: A total of 3 hours of research participation is required to earn the full extra credit. • Procedure: Details about available studies and sign-up procedures are provided through the course platform or directly by the instructor. 2. Research Opt-Out opinion essay (Option 2): • Description: For students who prefer not to participate in research studies, an alternative opinion essay is available. This essay will cover topics related to the course material and aims to assess the student's understanding and application of key concepts. • Credit: Successful submission of the essay will earn the same extra credit as research participation, adding 5% to the final grade. • Procedure: Students interested in this option must contact the instructor directly for details regarding the exam content, format, and scheduling. • Ex: Submit an essay providing a scholarly review of recent studies in phyiological psychology published within the last five years. Your opinion essay should consist of three parts: a brief overview of the topic and questions addressed in the reviewed paper, a description of the key findings, and a concise explanation of how these findings contribute to the field. While critical reviews are welcome, please ensure that your comments are accurate, well- reasoned, and diplomatic. Additionally, we encourage you to focus on what was learned and what could have been done differently. Please keep your submission concise, limited to 1,500 words. The deadline for fulfilling this requirement is the last day of the semester, Friday, December 19, 2025. Criteria include Structure, organization, fluency, and coherence of presentation. ● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website) N/A

docs.name: 學習與科技專題探究
docs.nameEn: Special Topic on Learning and Technology
docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 11510KIPE101100 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size - 中文名稱 Course Title 學習與科技專題探究 英文名稱 Course English Title Special Topic on Learning and Technology 任課教師 Instructor 游師柔 上課時間 Time M56R5 上課教室 Room COE 教院 223 COE 教院 302 課程簡述(Brief Course Description) 本課程目標為以專題探究歷程，培養學習科技理論概念、實作經驗、發現問題、 解決問題、合作溝通與創造學習科技之教與學的跨領域能力，並具備學習科技開 發技能，運用科技媒體呈現主題式探究成果。 課程大綱 (Syllabus) ●課程關鍵字(Course keywords) 學習科技, 探究式學習, 人工智慧, 擴增實境, 虛擬實境, 問題解決 Learning and Technology, Inquiry-based learning, Artificial intelligence, Augmented reality, Virtual reality, Problem solving ●課程說明(Course Description) 本課程目標為以專題探究歷程，培養學習科技理論概念、實作經驗、發現問題、 解決問題、合作溝通與創造學習科技之教與學的跨領域能力，並具備學習科技開 發技能，運用科技媒體呈現主題式探究成果。本課程以學習科技課程發展相關理 論為基礎，探討學習科技願景、素養導向、學習科技之課程選擇、評鑑策略與課 程設計等知識，並採用結構化步驟，引導學生解析市面教材，奠基實作經驗。延 續實作成果，發想融入學習科技的課程設計作為專題成果，期望學習者能建構應 用學習科技的洞察力，習得探究式思考脈絡、教材開發與反思能力。 ● 指定用書(Text Books) 無。 ● 參考書籍(References) 沈中偉、黃國禎（2012）。科技與學習：理論與實務。心理。 國家教育研究院（2026）。國家教育研究院。https://mlearn.moe.gov.tw/ 張霄亭等（譯）（2012）。S. E. C.-Y., Ye, S.-L., Yu, S.-J., & Chiu, T. K. F. (2023). Educational Psychology, 39(10), 1293-1310. 其他參考資料於課堂發放。 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 課堂講授、電腦實作、課堂討論、合作學習、線上授課。 ● 教學進度(Course Schedule) 週次 課程內容 1 課程介紹 學習科技發展與應用現況 2 學習科技課程理論與模式 3 學習科技之課程選擇與活動設計 4 國定假日放假 學習科技之課程評鑑 5 學習科技之課程設計 教材分析報告與期末報告說明與討論 6 人工智慧/機器學習/AI 使用倫理 7 大數據/學習分析 學習分析實作 8 國定假日放假 教材分析報告 9 教材分析報告 聊天機器人理論 10 聊天機器人應用 11 穿戴式科技、AR 與 VR 12 教室裡的教學科技 13 翻轉教室、體感學習 機器人實作 14 資料蒐集與討論 15 專家分享 專家分享學習單 16 期末報告 ● 成績考核(Evaluation) 1. 課堂參與(10%) 2. 教材分析報告(20%) 3. 學習科技主題報告(20%) 4. 專家分享學習單(15%) 5. 期末報告(35%) ● 與課程相關的網站 (Course-related Website) 無。 根據本校公布之「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採 取有條件開放，說明如下： 學生可於課堂作業或報告中的「標題頁註腳」或「引用文獻後」簡要說明如何使 用生成式 AI 進行簡報製作、資料蒐集、議題發想、文句潤飾或結構參考等使用 方式，作業請體現自身想法，避免過度依賴 AI 學習工具。 若經查核使用卻無在作業或報告中標明，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作 業或報告重新評分或不予計分。 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。

docs.name: 文化資源田野調查實務
docs.text: 國立清華大學竹師教育學院環境與文化資源學系 文化資源田野調查實務 Fieldwork on Cultural Resources 授課對象：竹師教育學院乙組學士班 上課時間︰M3M4 W1W2 授課教師︰榮芳杰 副教授 上課地點︰教院 117 教室 聯絡方式：fj.rong@mx.nthu.edu.tw 03-5715131 # 72827 課程助教：待聘 ※注意，本課程將自暑假期間 8/5 至 8/10 密集在台灣與金門進行 全日教學課程，請選課同學務必確認自己在該區段時間可出席※ 課程說明 本課程為竹師教育學院乙組(永續發展教育組)的移地教學系列課程之一。課程設計的主要 目的在於選擇國內一處場域，帶領學生進入該場域進行各種以文化資源調查為主的田野訓 練。本學期(115 學年度第 1 學期)的移地教學地點為「金門」。課程操作方式為了使學生有 完整的學習成效，我們將會提前在 2026 年 8 月 5 日至 10 日開學前，提早進入田野地點金 門，並且在前往金門之前進行校內的基礎課程。在校內課程結束後才移至田野地點(金門) 進行為期一周的移地教學訓練。最後，本課程會在移地教學期程結束後，回到學校進行最 後的課程成果製作與發表，預計在 2026 年 10 月結束本課程。 本課程主要在於讓學生從觀察文化資源應具備的基礎能力著手，訓練學生對於環境敏感度 的掌握，並且透過台灣本島或其他離島等不同田野地點的踏查訓練，期望學生能夠透過實 際進入田野地點的操作，對於文化資源的應用與詮釋能力有更充足的認識。本課程會把田 野資料分為採集調查和田野訪談口述歷史兩大部分，田野資料分成人、事、地、物四方面， 「人」以族（家）譜、戶政資料、日記為重，「事」以政府檔案和民間文書為主，「地」包 括地名及建置沿革、方志、地圖等等，「物」則涵蓋建築、遺址、石碑、墓碑、古橋、古 道、宅第、石刻等等。本課程主要讓學生了解文化資源類型的田野調查的方法論與實務技 巧。為學生提供機會致力於田野調查研究，並探討案例與資料蒐集。並養成學生對田野調 查的反思與批判能力。 課程目標 1. 讓學生能夠認識田野調查的各種工具與應用 2. 藉由移地教學的現場訓練學生對於文化資源的踏察能力 3. 建立學生進入田野調查前所需要具備的基本知識與觀念 4. 訓練學生熟悉歷史文獻資料的收集與分析能力 5. 訓練學生基本的建築空間測繪能力 課程要求 1. 本課程採理論與實作並重的方式進行，所有修課同學必須在學期內完成各階段所需要 提交的習作，各組並在學期結束時，分別完成大型海報輸出，以及其他書面成果報告 或多媒體成果展示，修課同學必須於 08/05~08/10 前往金門進行為期一周的田野調查課 程訓練，並且負擔個人機票與食宿費用(系上會爭取教育學院補助經費)，其他離島移地 教學工作坊所需相關校外師資演講鐘點費、導覽費、門票費、保險費用等，將由本課 程授課教師爭取其他補助支應。 2. 習作進度將會搭配課程授課進度，使同學能夠透過課堂案例與解說，舉一反三的思考 與修正習作的問題。因此，請同學務必每週準時上課，課堂採不定期點名。 3. 本課程要求與配分比重如下：作業 A︰移地教學金門的工作坊階段性討論報告佔學期總 成績 50%、作業 B︰期末總報告佔 35%、平時成績佔 15%。平時成績的計算方式以出席 率與課堂表現為主。 教學方式 1. 理論講述與討論(50%) 2. 個案分析與作品賞析(50%) 評量方式 1. 表現評量(80%) (說明：學期作業) 2. 上課參與(20%) (說明：出缺席&上課討論) 主要教材 自編講義 參考書目 1. 周婉窈著，《台灣歷史圖說:史前至 1945》 台北市:聯經化出版，1998。 2. 劉益昌，《田野調查曁田野發掘實施報告》臺北市:蘭陽文敎基金會，1996。 3. 劉還月，《常民文化田野調查速記表》臺北市:常民文化出版，1996。 4. 唐偌.里齊作，《大家來作口述歷史》台北：遠流出版社，1997。 5. 日常生活，《女性密碼：女性田野調查日記》臺北市：三民書局，2002。 6. 李欽賢著，《臺灣城市記憶-地圖上消失的街道風景》，臺北：玉山出版社，2004。 7. 楊南郡譯注、伊能嘉矩著，《臺灣踏查日記》(上)(下)，臺北:遠流出版社，1996。 8. 黃卓權，《進出客鄉—鄉土史田野與研究》，臺北市：南天，2008。 9. 唐諾．里齊（Donald A. Ritchie）著，王芝芝譯，《大家來做口述歷史》，臺北市： 南天，1997。 注意事項 1. 有任何課業上的問題，歡迎用 email (fj.rong@mx.nthu.edu.tw)跟老師聯繫。任何一 位同學詢問的信件，我都一定會親自回覆，請務必確認收到老師的回覆信件，以免 因系統誤認為廣告信件而遺漏。 2. 請善用老師每週的晤談時間，提前跟老師約定討論時間。 3. 整學期無故缺課三次，平時成績以零分計算。 課程進度安排 在此基礎上，本學期課程會分為三個學習階段。第一個階段是開學前七週的田野基礎理論 與實務的介紹。這部分包括： (一)田野資料採集調查—人物篇 本節著重私人族（家）譜、日記、官方戶政等資料之介紹。 (二)田野資料採集調查—歷史篇 本節介紹與臺灣歷史有關官方檔案和民官文書，側重於清代和日治時期。 (三)田野資料採集調查—地理篇 本節介紹臺灣地名及建置沿革、方志、地圖等資料。 (四)田野資料採集調查—建築篇 本單元將深入田野地點進行建築普查的工作，並且探索地方特色建築的興建脈絡與 空間特質。 (五)田野訪談口述歷史 本節分成口述歷史的緣起與發展、口述歷史的定義和重要性、口述歷史採集的實務 三大部分。生命地圖與生命故事 以自己為例，實際繪製自己個人生命地圖和撰寫 自己個人生命故事，藉此學習口述歷史實務技巧。 第二個學習階段則是以金門為國內移地教學的基地，在為期一週的田野實地調查過程中， 與金門大學建築系合作，共同針對金門特殊的軍事文化地景進行一系列的課程研習。目 前暫定金門移地教學的工作坊課程主軸包括： 1. 軍事遺產的田野調查練習與觀察 2. 聚落空間的田野調查訓練與紀錄 3. 金門城隍信仰與新竹城隍信仰的比較研究 4. 金門飲食文化的踏察與分析 5. 金門文化資產的活化再利用 6. 其他金門在地相關的文化資源調查與應用 第三個階段則是學期後半段 10-17 週的實作課程，透過這三個學習階段的課程訓練，讓同 學能夠熟悉進入一個陌生的田野地點後，如何尋找相關的文化資源，並且從中尋找資源活 化應用的可能。 周次 日期 單元類型 課程單元主題 備註 08 08/05- 08/10 金門移地教學工作坊(08/05-08/10) 09 09/07 實作課程 開學日/金門田野調查工作坊(一) 10 09/14 實作課程 金門田野調查工作坊(二) 11 09/21 實作課程 金門田野調查工作坊(三) 12 09/28 中秋連假，停課一次 13 10/05 實作課程 金門田野調查工作坊(四) 18 待定 期末總評 田野躍進期末聯展
