docs.text: Language and the Brain 語言與大腦 Instructor: Keng-Yu Lin 林耿育 Contact: linkengyulky@gmail.com Office hours: By appointment Course Description: This course introduces the fundamental principles of language science and their relationship to cognitive neuroscience. Students will gain a foundational understanding of neurolinguistics and develop the skills needed to engage with advanced topics in the field. Prerequisites: Familiar with the fundamental concepts introduced in an introductory linguistics course. Objectives:  Understand the fundamental concepts of language science and cognitive neuroscience  Understand how cognitive neuroscience methods are used to investigate different aspects of language References: Brennan, J. R. (2022). Language and the brain: a slim guide to neurolinguistics. Oxford University Press. Course Materials: There will be no required textbook but suggested references. Course materials will be posted on the course website. All updates and announcements will be shared on the website and followed by an email notification. Students are responsible for regularly checking both their email and the website for important information. Grading:  Exam 1: 25%  Exam 2: 25%  Exam 3: 35%  Course reflection: 10%  Attendance: 5%  Participation in a psycholinguistics/neurolinguistics talk or study (bonus): 2% Grading Policy: The three in-class exams will account for 85% of the total grade. Make-up exams are only permitted with valid, documented excuses. Exam 3 will be cumulative, with approximately 30% of the questions drawn directly from Exam 1 and Exam 2. Students are required to submit a course reflection discussing what they have learned in the course and their main areas of interest. This reflection accounts for 10% of the total grade (1-2 pages, 1.5 spacing, 2.54 cm or 1 inch margins, 12-point Times New Roman). Late submissions will not be accepted after the third day past the deadline, and a penalty of 5% per day will be applied. Please note that internet connection issues or other personal technical problems are not accepted as valid reasons for late homework submissions. Attendance is mandatory and is generally associated with stronger course performance. Students are allowed one absence without penalty; additional absences require valid, documented justification for exemption from penalty if approved. Each absence beyond the first will result in a 5% deduction, and missing half or more of the course will result in a failing grade. Participation in a psycholinguistics or neurolinguistics talk or study may earn bonus points (1% per hour, up to a maximum of 2%). Honesty Policy: Any use of AI tools must be disclosed. When using AI tools, students are responsible for ensuring that they fully understand the material. Any AI-generated references that do not exist will not be accepted and will result in failing the course. docs.name: AI 時代的語用學專題:從結構到價值觀的標註
docs.nameEn: Special Topics in Pragmatics in the Age of AI: Annotation from Structure to Values
docs.text: 1 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 碩博合開 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 20 中文名稱 Course Title AI 時代的語用學專題：從結構到價值觀的標註 英文名稱 Course English Title Special Topics in Pragmatics in the Age of AI: Annotation from Structure to Values 任課教師 Instructor 林書宇、呂菁菁 上課時間 Time 週二 89a 節 (16:30~19:20) 上課教室 Room 課程簡述 (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 在人工智慧持續推進知識生產、語言應用與人際互動型態轉變的時代背景下，語用學的重要性 日益凸顯。相較於僅著重語言形式、句法結構或字面意義的分析，語用學關注的是語言在真實 情境中的使用方式，包括說話者意圖的表達、互動關係的協商、禮貌與面子策略的運作，以及 語言如何結合手勢、語調與其他多模態線索共同建構意義。此一能力不僅是理解人類溝通本質 的關鍵，也正是當前人工智慧系統在面對真實語言情境時最需要補強的重要面向。 本課程即以語用學為核心，結合人工智慧發展所帶來的新興研究需求，系統性引導研究生從言 說行為、合作原則、禮貌策略、面子威脅，到手勢與語音同步、價值觀標註等主題，逐步理解 人類溝通中最細緻且最具解釋力的層面。課程並透過標註工具及相關實作訓練，培養學生將語 用學理論轉化為可操作、可分析、可應用之研究方法的能力，使其不僅能掌握理論基礎，更能 實際參與語料建置、標註分析、語言科技應用與跨領域合作。 透過本課程之規劃，學生將有機會建立面向未來的重要學術基礎，理解語用學如何在 AI 時代 重新展現其核心價值，並進一步培養參與國際研究對話、掌握語言科技發展方向及回應新世代 溝通議題之能力。此課程所體現者，不僅是研究所教育對前沿議題的即時回應，更是高等教育 在人才培育上結合理論深度、方法訓練與未來視野的具體實踐。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」 語用學, 語料標註, 人工智慧, 言談分析, 語言模型 Pragmatics, Annotation, Artificial Intelligence, Discourse Analysis, Language Models Language Models Data 2 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) (1) 教師講授與理論導讀 (2) 指定文獻閱讀與討論 (3) 多模態語料觀察與課堂分析 (4) 工具操作與標註實作 (5) 資料探勘與初步模型分析示範 ● 課程要求(Course Requirements) 本課程歡迎對語言、社會互動、AI、語料分析、多模態研究或語言科技有興趣之碩博士生修 習。修課學生無須預先具備完整程式設計能力，但須願意投入理論閱讀、課堂討論及實作練 習，並配合完成指定之課前準備。 ● 預期學習成果 (Expected Learning Outcomes) (1) 說明語用學在人工智慧與自然語言處理中的理論與應用價值。 (2) 分析真實互動語料中的言說行為、合作原則、禮貌策略、面子威脅及多模態同步現象。 (3) 設計基礎語用學標註架構，並對資料進行初步標註與整理。 (4) 使用工具進行多模態語料的基本對齊與標註操作。 (5) 理解標註一致性與研究品質控制的概念，並能進行初步檢核。 (6) 將語用理論與資料探勘、文字探勘及語言模型之基本方法相互連結。 (7) 對 AI 如何理解人類語言中的情境、互動與價值判斷提出具研究潛力的初步思考。 3 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 每週教學主題 Week 1： 為何 AI 需要語用學？ Week 2： 言說行為理論（Speech Act Theory）與意圖偵測 Week 3： 合作原則（Cooperative Principle）與 AI 的回覆品質 Week 4： 禮貌理論與面子威脅 Week 5： McNeill 手勢分類學及對話中的多模態同步現象 Week 6： 實作演練：「面子威脅程度」標註 Week 7： 標註一致性分析 Week 8： 期中專題報告 Week 9： 課程與資料探勘簡介 Week 10： 資料與資料前處理 Week 11： 資料的相似與相異衡量、資料探索、關聯規則探勘 Week 12： 分群 Week 13： 分類 Week 14： 文字探勘與早期自然語言處理介紹 Week 15： 語言模型 Week 16： 主題探勘 ● 成績考核(Evaluation) (1) 田野語料前處理：20% (2) 多模態標記實作：30% (3) 期中進度報告：20% (4) 期末研究報告：30% ● 指定閱讀(Assigned Readings) (1) Muhammad Umair, Vasanth Sarathy, and Jan Ruiter. 2024. Large Language Models Know What To Say But Not When To Speak. In Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024, pages 15503–15514. (2) Umair, M., Mertens, J. B., Warnke, L., & de Ruiter, J. P. 2024. Can Language Models Trained on Written Monologue Learn to Predict Spoken Dialogue? Cognitive Science, 48(11), e70013. ● 參考資源(References) 1. 清華磨課師（NTHU MOOCs）：2026 TAICA-資料探勘與應用（1–6 月） 2. The Bayes Factor Podcast 3. The Stanford Natural Language Inference (SNLI) Corpus 4. Multimodal Behaviour Modelling in Affective Computing Applications 5. MIT Media Lab 相關研究資源 4 ● 課程說明(Course Description) 近年來，人工智慧在文字處理、語言生成與大型語料學習方面雖有顯著進展，但在真實人類互 動中最關鍵的層面 (例如語境感知、言外之意、禮貌策略、面子協商、價值立場辨識、多模態 線索整合) 仍顯示出高度侷限。傳統自然語言處理若僅依賴去脈絡化文字資料，便難以充分理 解人類語言在社會互動中的複雜運作機制。因此，語用學不僅未因 AI 的發展而失去重要性， 反而在當代更成為連結語言理論與人工智慧應用的關鍵領域。 另一方面，國際上許多重要大學的語言學研究與研究生訓練，早已逐步與 AI、資料科學、語料 建置及自然語言處理密切結合。若語言學的研究與教學仍停留於與資料及技術隔絕的狀態，將 不利於研究生未來參與國際學術社群及跨領域研究合作。國立清華大學作為我國重要的研究型 大學與人文學術重鎮，有責任引導研究生在維持語言學理論深度的同時，具備將理論轉化為資 料、標註系統與分析架構的能力。 本課程即建立於此一理念之上：一方面補足人文與語言背景研究生理解 AI 與資料分析所需的 基礎知識，另一方面深化語言學研究生在語境分析、語料判讀與高品質標註方面的優勢，使其 成為 AI 時代中真正具有專業判準與學術主體性的研究者。 本課程內容主要分為兩大部分，由兩位授課教師分別帶領學生進入不同面向，但最終以整合方 式完成整體學習。 第一部分為語用學理論與標註實作。此部分將從 AI 為何需要語用學出發，介紹言說行為理 論、合作原則、禮貌理論、面子威脅、多模態互動與手勢分類等重要主題，並引導學生實際進 行語用現象的標註設計與分析。學生將學習如何把抽象理論轉化為可操作的資料欄位與標註標 籤，理解高品質語料對 AI 模型的重要性。 第二部分為資料探勘與語言技術基礎。此部分將介紹資料前處理、探索分析、相似度衡量、關 聯規則、分群、分類、文字探勘、主題探勘與語言模型等方法，協助學生建立與語言研究相關 的基礎分析能力。課程設計重點並不在於將研究生訓練為工程技術人員，而在於培養語言學研 究者與資料方法之間的理解與對話能力。 ● 開課教師之教學理念與期待 (Instructor’s Teaching Philosophy and Expectations) 本課程不僅希望學生理解「AI 與語用學有關」，更期待學生真正意識到：在 AI 時代，語言學 者最不可取代的價值，正在於其對語境、互動、意圖、社會關係與價值表達的細緻分析能力。 教師希望藉由本課程，使研究生理解當代最重要的語言資料，已不再只是描述性材料，而是足 以影響模型判斷、回覆品質與社會倫理方向的關鍵資源。 ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI): 完全開放使用且無須註明

docs.text: 1 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 碩博合開 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 20 中文名稱 Course Title 臨床社會語言學 英文名稱 Course English Title Clinical Sociolinguistics 任課教師 Instructor 呂菁菁 上課時間 Time 週四 789 節 (15:30~16:20) 上課教室 Room 課程簡述 (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 本課程內容包括：區域與社會中之語言使用方式變異、語言與性別、雙語與多語主義、語碼轉 換、語言與權力、語言與文化、語言接觸與變遷、語言規劃、方言知覺與語言態度、多語習 得、語音知覺與變異、多語人口的失語症、多語兒童評估設計、讀寫能力之社會文化視角，以 及臨床語境中的口譯與多語溝通議題。課程實作部分包含資料清洗、分層標註、特徵提取與文 化敏感度分析等實作訓練，接軌國際上的『臨床社會語言學』，結合社會語言學、對話分析、臨 床語言研究與多模態數位工具，探討多語社會中語言使用、文化脈絡與認知評估之關聯。期中 與期末專題聚焦於高齡化社會中少數語言使用者與多語長者在臨床溝通與認知篩檢上的語言公 平性問題，並引導學生處理真實田野與自然語音語料中的語碼轉換、語碼混合、停頓、非語言 聲音及多模態行為訊號。學生將學習運用 ELAN、Praat、MediaPipe／OpenPose 等工具進行標 註、對齊與分析，並透過國際標準化資料集與在地化任務，建立兼具理論深度、方法整合與文 化敏感度的研究能力，目標為訓練學生具備數位人文標記之硬實力，回應臺灣高齡化、多語社 會與少數族群語言公平性的現實需求。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」 臨床社會語言學, 多語現象, 語碼轉換, 對話分析, 自然語音語料 Clinical Sociolinguistics, Multilingualism, Code-switching , Conversation Analysis, Naturalistic Speech Data 2 課程大綱 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 教師講授、文獻討論、工具實作、資料分析練習、投入期中專題與期末專題。 ● 課程要求(Course Requirements) 修課學生須能閱讀中英文學術資料，參與課堂討論與實作，並完成期中、期末專題。無須具備 程式設計背景，但須願意接受跨領域方法訓練，並對研究倫理與文化敏感度保持重視。 ● 預期學習成果 (Expected Learning Outcomes) 1. 說明臨床社會語言學之主要理論框架與研究議題。 2. 辨識多語社會中語碼轉換、語碼混合、語言態度與互動權力等現象。 3. 處理真實田野或臨床情境中的非結構化語音與影音資料。 4. 使用 ELAN、Praat 與相關多模態工具進行基本標註與分析。 5. 理解 ADReSS、DementiaBank 等標準化資料集之研究用途與限制。 6. 以文化敏感度為前提，設計並完成小型臨床社會語言學研究專題。 3 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 週次 主題 核心內容 W1 區域與社會因素 地理方言、社會階級對語言產出的影響 W2 語言與性別 性別化言談特徵及其在臨床對話中的意義 W3 雙語與多語現象 全球與個人層次的雙語現象分析 W4 語碼轉換 Code-switching 的社交功能與 Diglossia 概念 W5 語言與權力 診間互動中的權力不對等與話語權控制 W6 語言與文化 文化圖式如何影響溝通風格與理解 W7 語言演變 語言接觸導致的結構性變遷 W8 語言規劃 國家政策、語言復振對臨床服務的影響 W9 方言腔調覺知 社會對口音的刻板印象與語言歧視 W10 社會語言變異的習得 兒童如何學會在不同社交情境切換風格 W11 雙語與多語語言習得 跨語言影響與多語習得的發展歷程 W12 語音知覺、聽障與變異 聽損者處理不同方言變體時的知覺挑戰 W13 使用多語者的失語症 失語症在不同語言間的受損與恢復差異 W14 多語兒童評估設計 文化公平性之標準化與非標準化評估設計 W15 讀寫能力之臨床社會語言學視角 識字發展作為一種社會文化實踐 W16 現實的語言多樣性考量 專業口譯員在語言治療診間的角色與挑戰 ● 成績考核(Evaluation) (1) 田野語料前處理：20% (2) 多模態標記實作：30% (3) 期中進度報告：20% (4) 期末研究報告：30% ● 指定用書(Text Books) Ball, M. J. (2005). Clinical sociolinguistics. Blackwell Pub. ● 參考書籍(References) 1. ELAN 線上資源 2. Praat 官方資源 3. MediaPipe 官方文件 4. Conversation Analysis 相關導論資源 5. Glasgow University Laboratory of Phonetics 相關資源 6. Trinity College Dublin Department of Clinical Speech and Language Studies 相關資源 4 7. Cao, Z., Hidalgo, G., Simon, T., Wei, S.-E., & Sheikh, Y. (2021). OpenPose: Realtime Multi-Person 2D Pose Estimation Using Part Affinity Fields. IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence, 43(1), 172–186. ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程旨在回應當前高齡化社會中，少數族群語言使用者在認知障礙篩檢與臨床溝通上的文化 與語言不對等問題。傳統評估工具多以單語使用者為常模，難以處理台灣多語社會中常見的語 碼混合、語碼轉換與文化脈絡差異，因而可能造成判讀偏差。傳統臨床評估工具多以單語為常 模，忽略了臺灣原住民族長輩頻繁使用的「語碼混合（Code-mixing）」現象。有鑑於此，本課 程引導學生認識國際上臨床社會語言學、對話分析與自然語料研究的前沿發展，並結合數位標 註與行為計算技術，訓練學生面對真實而複雜的非結構化語料。課程亦兼顧臺灣在地需求，特 別關注原住民族語言、地方語言、多語長者與文化公平性評估等議題，使語言學研究不僅與世 界學術趨勢接軌，也回應本土社會的實際需要。 ● 開課教師之教學理念與期待 (Instructor’s Teaching Philosophy and Expectations) 本課程期待研究生不僅掌握社會語言學之理論基礎，更能進一步建立處理真實語料、理解文化 脈絡、整合技術工具與提出研究判讀的能力。課程強調語言是認知、互動與社會文化條件交織 後的實際產物，因此研究者必須具備從真實資料出發的觀察力、分析力與詮釋力。 教師期待學生修畢本課程後，能以更具文化敏感度與方法整合力的方式，理解多語社會中的語 言現象，並逐步具備將語言學專業轉化為長照溝通、臨床評估、語言科技與社會實踐之研究能 力。 ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI): 完全開放使用且無須註明 ● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁 (1) https://archive.mpi.nl/tla/elan (2) https://www.fon.hum.uva.nl/praat/ (3) https://ai.google.dev/edge/mediapipe/solutions/guide?hl=zh-tw (4) https://sheffield.ac.uk/linguistics/home/all-about-linguistics/about-website/branches- linguistics/conversation-analysis (5) https://www.gla.ac.uk/schools/critical/aboutus/resources/gulp/ (6) https://www.tcd.ie/slscs/department-of-clinical-speech-and-language-studies/

Primary aim This one-year course is designed to enhance students’ overall English competence through listening, speaking, and reading activities plus grammar review and vocabulary development. A four-skill coursebook plus a self-access learning project will be integrated to design learning tasks and provide opportunities for students to practice language learning strategies, get exposed to English in any form, and develop their confidence and fluency in the classroom and outside the classroom. After having taken this course, students are expected to consolidate their knowledge of English language and engage themselves more confidently and fluently in authentic communication in everyday settings and even in school settings. 2. Subsidiary aim In this class, students will have the opportunity to 1. review and incorporate grammar points and sentence structures, especially concerning verb tenses, into description and discussion of a variety of topics and issues related to their life 2. build up theme-based vocabulary and academic words for and through reading and listening to conversations, interviews, talks, and lectures 3. practice academic skills such as outlining, summarizing, paraphrasing, and critical thinking through theme-based listening, reading, speaking and writing tasks 4. manage and present information, perspectives, or problem-solving/decision-making in speaking and writing tasks or activities 3. B2 Can understand a clearly structured lecture on a familiar subject, and can take notes on points which strike him/her as important, even though he/she tends to concentrate on the words themselves and therefore to miss some information. [vocabulary range] Control GRAMMATICAL ACCURACY B2+ Good grammatical control. [grammatical accuracy] VOCABULARY CONTROL B2 Lexical accuracy is generally high, though some confusion and incorrect word choice does occur without hindering communication. [vocabulary control] ORTHOGRAPHIC CONTROL B2 Can produce clearly intelligible continuous writing, which follows standard layout and paragraphing conventions. Liu liumeitzu@gapp.nthu.edu.tw N/A N/A 2 Course Aims / Description Primary aim This one-year course aims to enhance students’ overall English competence by developing their listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills. Through interactive activities, grammar review, and vocabulary expansion, students will strengthen their ability to communicate effectively in both everyday and academic contexts. The course incorporates a four-skill coursebook and a self-access learning project to provide structured learning tasks and opportunities for independent practice. Students will also be introduced to essential academic English skills, such as summarizing texts and writing structured essays, as well as practicing note-taking and understanding lectures to improve their ability to engage with academic materials. By the end of the course, students are expected to demonstrate greater confidence and fluency in authentic communication, whether in daily interactions or academic discussions. Subsidiary aim In this class, students will have opportunities to 1. review and practice grammar points and sentence structures to describe and discuss a variety of topics and issues related to their life 2. build up theme-based vocabulary and even academic words for and through reading and listening to conversations, interviews, talks, and lectures 3. practice academic skills such as outlining, summarizing, and critical thinking while listening, reading, speaking, and writing 4. present information, perspectives, or problem-solving in speaking and writing tasks or activities Corresponding CEFR Can-do statements 1. [LISTENING]: Can understand the main ideas of propositionally and linguistically complex speech of both concrete and abstract topics in a standard dialect, including technical discussions in his/her field of specialization. 2. [READING]: Can quickly identify the content and relevance off news items, articles and reports on a wide range of professional topics, deciding whether closer study is worthwhile. 3. [SPOKEN INTERACTION]: Can use the language fluently, accurately and effectively on a wide range of general, academic, vocational or leisure topics, marking clearly the relationships between ideas. 4. [WRITTEN PRODUCTION]: Can write letters conveying degrees of emotion and highlighting the personal significance of events and experiences and commenting on the correspondent’s news and views. 5. [SOCIOLINGUISTIC APPROPRIATENESS]: Can express him/herself confidently, clearly and politely in a formal or informal register, appropriate to the situation and the person(s) concerned. 3 英文核心能力指標 University Student Core Competency Indicators 1. 英語溝通與表達能力 (ability to communicate and express oneself in English) 30% 2. 深度分析與組織思考的能力 (ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English) 20% 3. 英語學習策略與技巧 (knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques) 20% 4. 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 (global views of English and multicultural diversity) 20% 5. 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣與能力 (ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit) 10% Teaching Materials and References Textbook(s) Christina Latham-koenig, Clive Oxenden, and Kate Chomachi.(2021) American English File 4, 3rd Edition. VoiceTube / YouTube / Podcast 4. Online news stories Requirements & Rules: 1.Class attendance and class participation:  Attendance is taken every session throughout the semester. You have a total of three opportunities for leave without penalty. Sick leave, official leave, personal leave, mental health leave (activated on the third time with school-parent concern), and menstrual leave no proof is required. All leave requests should be submitted through the school’s online System。  Four absences (with approved requests) or two absences (without requests) will result in a failing grade.  Through school system: 3 chances.  Without school system: 1 chance Official school competition leave — we’ll discuss this separately. 4  Lateness: Unless an unavoidable reason is provided, a 20% deduction will be applied.  Class Participation: In-class assignments (pair work) and answering questions. 請特別留意，這門課很注重出席率，因此如果經批准的請假累計達到四次以上 (包含四次)， 或是有 2 次沒有來也沒有請假（包含 2 次），這門課程就會不及格。 2. Assignment: No make-up submissions.  In the first week, I’ll open the assignment submission period, which will last until the deadline. You’ll have time to submit. It is your responsibility to ask your classmates what has been covered in the class. 3. A four-skill coursebook plus a self-access learning project will be integrated to design learning tasks and provide opportunities for students to practice language learning strategies, get exposed to English in any form, and develop their confidence and fluency in the classroom and outside the classroom. After having taken this course, students are expected to consolidate their knowledge of English language and engage themselves more confidently and fluently in authentic communication in everyday settings and even in school settings. 2. Subsidiary aim In this class, students will have the opportunity to 1. review and incorporate grammar points and sentence structures, especially concerning verb tenses, into description and discussion of a variety of topics and issues related to their life 2. build up theme-based vocabulary and academic words for and through reading and listening to conversations, interviews, talks, and lectures 3. practice academic skills such as outlining, summarizing, paraphrasing, and critical thinking through theme-based listening, reading, speaking and writing tasks 4. manage and present information, perspectives, or problem-solving/decision-making in speaking and writing tasks or activities 3. What major goals will you have achieved by then?  Example: "Ten years from now, I imagine you will be working as a senior consultant at a global firm. I hope that by 2036, you will have graduated top of our class and will have traveled to at least five diƯerent countries. By the time you watch this video, I hope you will have built a career you love. Don't forget where you started!" The student is absent for more than 5 classes: The student never explains to or discusses with the teacher his/her difficulty in taking care of this subject. 2. Liu liumeitzu@gapp.nthu.edu.tw N/A N/A 2 Course Aims / Description Primary aim This one-year course aims to enhance students’ overall English competence by developing their listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills. Through interactive activities, grammar review, and vocabulary expansion, students will strengthen their ability to communicate effectively in both everyday and academic contexts. The course incorporates a four-skill coursebook and a self-access learning project to provide structured learning tasks and opportunities for independent practice. Students will also be introduced to essential academic English skills, such as summarizing texts and writing structured essays, as well as practicing note-taking and understanding lectures to improve their ability to engage with academic materials. By the end of the course, students are expected to demonstrate greater confidence and fluency in authentic communication, whether in daily interactions or academic discussions. Subsidiary aim In this class, students will have opportunities to 1. review and practice grammar points and sentence structures to describe and discuss a variety of topics and issues related to their life 2. build up theme-based vocabulary and even academic words for and through reading and listening to conversations, interviews, talks, and lectures 3. practice academic skills such as outlining, summarizing, and critical thinking while listening, reading, speaking, and writing 4. present information, perspectives, or problem-solving in speaking and writing tasks or activities Corresponding CEFR Can-do statements 1. [LISTENING]: Can understand the main ideas of propositionally and linguistically complex speech of both concrete and abstract topics in a standard dialect, including technical discussions in his/her field of specialization. 2. [SPOKEN INTERACTION]: Can use the language fluently, accurately and effectively on a wide range of general, academic, vocational or leisure topics, marking clearly the relationships between ideas. 4. [WRITTEN PRODUCTION]: Can write letters conveying degrees of emotion and highlighting the personal significance of events and experiences and commenting on the correspondent’s news and views. 5. [SOCIOLINGUISTIC APPROPRIATENESS]: Can express him/herself confidently, clearly and politely in a formal or informal register, appropriate to the situation and the person(s) concerned. 3 英文核心能力指標 University Student Core Competency Indicators 1. 英語溝通與表達能力 (ability to communicate and express oneself in English) 30% 2. 深度分析與組織思考的能力 (ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English) 20% 3. 英語學習策略與技巧 (knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques) 20% 4. 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 (global views of English and multicultural diversity) 20% 5. 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣與能力 (ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit) 10% Teaching Materials and References Textbook(s) Christina Latham-koenig, Clive Oxenden, and Kate Chomachi.(2021) American English File 4, 3rd Edition. VoiceTube / YouTube / Podcast 4. Online news stories Requirements & Rules: 1.Class attendance and class participation:  Attendance is taken every session throughout the semester. You have a total of three opportunities for leave without penalty. Sick leave, official leave, personal leave, mental health leave (activated on the third time with school-parent concern), and menstrual leave no proof is required. All leave requests should be submitted through the school’s online System。  Four absences (with approved requests) or two absences (without requests) will result in a failing grade.  Through school system: 3 chances.  Without school system: 1 chance  Official school competition leave — we’ll discuss this separately. 4  Lateness: Unless an unavoidable reason is provided, a 20% deduction will be applied.  Class Participation: In-class assignments (pair work) and answering questions. 請特別留意，這門課很注重出席率，因此如果經批准的請假累計達到4次以上 (包含4次)， 或是有 2 次沒有來也沒有請假（包含 2 次），這門課程就會不及格。 2. Primary aim Upper-intermediate English I is an integrated course designed to develop students' four English skills (i.e., listening, speaking, reading, & writing) with an emphasis on speaking and listening. Subsidiary aim In this class, students will have opportunity to 1. listen to authentic English-speaking topics such as English news reports, daily life conversations or English documentary video clips and personal presentation. 2. review and practice grammar points and sentence structures to describe and discuss a variety of topics and issues related to their life 3. build up theme-based vocabulary and even academic words for and through reading and listening to conversations, interviews, talks, and lectures 4. practice academic skills such as outlining, summarizing, critical thinking while listening, reading, speaking and writing 2 revised by KWONG 5. manage and present information, perspectives, or problem-solving in speaking and writing tasks or activities 3. docs.text: 1 National Tsing Hua University Upper-Intermediate English I 中高級英文一 Fall 2026 Course Information Course Number LANG 1010 10 Credits 2 Classroom 教院 223 教室 Class hours ■ Monday □ Tuesday □ Wednesday □ Thursday □ Friday □ 8:00A.M. – 9:50A.M. ■ 10:10A.M. – 12:00P.M. 可選課學生 身分別  前標生 □ 中級生 □ 初級生 Language Level □ A2－A2+（初級） □ B1-B1+（中級）  B2（中高級） Prerequisites 加簽說明 □ 不開放人工加簽。所有學生須由選課系統亂數選課。 ■ 開放人工加簽 3 位學生。學生符合以下條件，得於第 1 週上課 時，向老師提出加簽申請。老師簽署申請表後，申請表送英語教育中心 辦公室。由老師進行線上簽核（校務資訊系統）。 ■ 條件 1：必須於第一週到課 Requirement #1: Attend the first class ■ 條件 2：須有其他時段【中高級英文一】衝堂無法選課之證明（如 選課紀錄或本學期所有科目課程表） Requirement #2: Offer a proof of time conflict with the other courses of the same title so that you MUST be taking this course. ■ 條件 3：自所屬選課階段（大一生：新生選課與第 3 次選課，點選 自己所屬「學院別」班級；所有大學部學生：第 1-3 次選課亂數選 課皆未選上；各次選課，已選上任一【中高級英文一】但自行退選 者，不予人工加簽再次選課） Requirement #3: Offer the history or record of course registration in the previous sessions that you were NOT selected for any class of Upper- Intermediate English I or that you are not qualified for course registration ■ 條件 4：應屆畢業生 Requirement #4: You are supposed to graduate this semester or this school year 提醒：學生修讀英文領域課程，請依本校規劃選課之修業年級選課。如因個人考 量，未對應年級而逕自改於其他修業年級選課之英文領域課程，或指定加簽某特 定課程，英語教育中心與任課教師將礙難配合或處理。 Reminder: Please take the required English courses in accordance with the scheduled 2 curriculum offered by our school. Your personal scheduling or preference of taking courses during your college stay will NOT be a valid excuse for the teacher to take your request for extra course registration into account. Instructor & Contact Information Name Email Office & Tel Office Hour 吳聖鵬 hank.spwu@gmail.com N/A N/A Course Aims / Description Primary aim This year-long course is designed to enhance students’ overall English proficiency by integrating listening, speaking, reading and writing activities with targeted grammar review and vocabulary development. Utilizing a four-skill coursebook plus a self‐ access learning project, the curriculum provides opportunities for students to apply language learning strategies, synthesize complex arguments, and build communicative confidence both inside and outside the classroom. Upon completion of the course, students are expected to have consolidated their linguistic foundation, enabling them to engage fluently and confidently in authentic everyday communication. Furthermore, students will master academic vocabulary and word- formation principles, including the use of prefixes, suffixes and roots. Subsidiary aim In this course students will have opportunities to 1. review and practice grammar points and sentence structures to describe and discuss a variety of topics and issues related to their life 2. build up theme-based vocabulary and even academic words for and through reading and listening to conversations, interviews, talks, and lectures 3. practice academic skills such as outlining, summarizing, critical thinking while listening, reading, speaking and writing 4. manage and present information, perspectives, or problem-solving in speaking and writing tasks or activities Corresponding CEFR Can-do statements 1. Can understand the main ideas of propositionally and linguistically complex speech of both concrete and abstract topics in a standard dialect, including technical discussions in his/her field of specialization. [overall listening comprehension] 2. Can follow the essentials of lectures, talks and reports and other forms of academic/professional presentations which are propositionally and linguistically complex. [listening as a member of a live audience] 3. Can read with a large degree of independence, adapting style and speed of 3 reading to different texts and purposes, and using appropriate reference sources selectively. Has a broad active reading vocabulary, but may experience some difficulty with low-frequency vocabulary. [overall reading comprehension] 4. Can interact with a degree of fluency and spontaneity that makes regular interaction, and sustained relationships with native speakers quite possible without imposing strain on either party. [overall spoken interaction] 5. Can give clear, detailed description and presentations on a wide range of subjects related to his/her field of interest, expanding and supporting ideas with subsidiary points and relevant examples. [overall spoken production] 6. Can write clear, detailed texts on a variety of subjects related to his/her field of interest, synthesizing and evaluating information and arguments from a number of sources. [overall written production] 7. Can pass on detailed information reliably. [propositional precision] 英文核心能力指標 University Student Core Competency Indicators 1. 英語溝通與表達能力 (ability to communicate and express oneself in English) [30%] 2. 深度分析與組織思考的能力 (ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English) [10%] 3. 英語學習策略與技巧 (knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques) [30%] 4. 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 (global views of English and multicultural diversity) [15%] 5. 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣與能力 (ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit) [15%] Teaching Materials and References Textbook(s) Christina Latham-Koenig, Clive Oxenden, and Kate Chomacki. (2021) American English File 4, 3rd Edition. New York: Oxford University Press. ISBN: 978-0-19-490685-2 CEFR Scale □ B1 □ B1-B2 ■ B2 □ B2+ □ C1 Additional Textbook(s) Learning/Resource Platform Teachers may upload the teaching materials such as audio files, lectures slides, assignments, quizzes, and supplementary materials or hyperlinks to the following learning platform: eeclass https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw 4 Grading Scheme 1. Attendance and participation 15% 2. Midterm exam 20% 3. Final Exam 20% 4. assignments 15% 5. quizzes 10% 6. presentations (e.g., briefing, podcast, role plays, skits) 20% Requirements & Rules 1. Class attendance, lesson preparation and active class participation are required. ✓ As you are all present whenever the instructor takes the roll, you will get 60% in this category Attendance and Participation. 經常性點名，全勤者可得「出席與參與」項目中的 60%成績。 ✓ Each skip will cost 2 points from the category Attendance and Participation (up to 15 points in the final grade). 未假不到課（翹課），每 次從「出席與參與」成績（占學期成績 15 分）扣 2 分。 ✓ If you are absent in case of UNCONTROLLABLE situations (e.g. illness, emergency, important occasions, etc.), please apply for a leave on the Student Leave System on Academic Information System of National Tsing Hua University or on the iNTHU app (from the Office of Student Affair website), with clear leave information, including leave type, leave period, and reasons (must be clear and valid enough for the teacher’s approval). As the reasons or the documents are not clear, valid or sufficient enough, the teacher may deny the application. 遇不可抗力情形需請假者，請於本校校務資 訊系統上的學生請假系統或下載 iNTHU APP，填寫資料（請假類別、請假日期、請假事由）。請假 事由須合理並敘述清楚，提供老師是否准假之參考。請假單上的理由或所附證明文件不清楚 或不充分時，該次請假申請得不予核准。 ✓ Please observe the information you are expected to offer for each of the following leave types: ◼ For sick leave, please describe severe symptoms and medical treatments you have been taking in the box “Reason.” 請病假時，請於理由欄位說明影響上課之顯著症狀，就醫或服 藥等處理。 ◼ For personal leave, please describe the uncontrollable event and how it makes you absent from the class. 請事假時，請於理由欄位敘明事件，並說明該事件如何致使你無法前來上 課。 ◼ No leave application will be approved on the dates of presentations, peer evaluations, and midterm/final exams. Please care for your health and reserve the time for these important class activities. 報告、同儕互評、期中／期末考當日不得請假。請注意身心健康 並為這些重要課程活動預留時間。 NTHU 學生請假 Q&A 5 ◼ There will be NO make-up exams or presentations unless you apply for leave with valid and official reasons for your absence beforehand. 無合理且正式的缺課原因，將不予補考 或補行報告。 ✓ You are expected to apply for leave before the class you are absent from. Any overdue leave application must be made within 7 days from the last day of absence. 請假已事先申請為原 則。逾期請假申請必須於 7 日內補請。未能於規定期間申請者，均以曠課論。 ✓ Being late for more than 10 minutes (with no valid excuses) is treated as absence from that hour. Being late for more than 30 minutes is treated as absence from the whole class. 無故 遲到逾 10 分鐘，以該小時未到課紀錄。遲到逾 30 分鐘，視為該次上課未到課。 ✓ No points will be deducted for your ATTENDANCE as long as your approved leave is no more than 6 hours. However, you may lose points for your PARTICIPATION or in-class practices scheduled on the date of your absence. 核准的請假時數未逾 6 小時，不扣出席成績。惟當日 如有上課練習或小組活動，請假者無法參與或完成，將無法獲得該次練習或該項評量成績。換 言之，缺課仍可能影響「參與」與「作業」等成績。 ✓ If you skip class for more than 8 hours, your course withdrawal may NOT be approved, and you will get 0 credits for this course. 無故不到課逾 8 小時者，將不予同意其停修申請，亦無 法取得本課程學分。 ✓ A student will fail to get the 2 credits for missing 5 classes, including the ones due to any kinds of leaves. 缺課達五次（含各類請假缺課）者，將無法從本課程獲取任何學分。 2. Absence from a class is no excuse for failing to complete in-class practices, to submit assignments in time, or to get informed of assignments or the class you have missed. It is your responsibility to hand in the assignments within 5 days (weekends & holidays included) and to reach your classmates or the instructor and refer to the course platform (eeclass) for the relevant information concerning what has been covered in the class. You may ask a classmate of yours to help with assignment submission and collection of assignment worksheets, if any. You may make an appointment with the instructor for assignment worksheets. 缺席與請假不得作為未 能完成當日上課練習、無法及時繳交作業或不知道該次課後作業之藉口。缺席與請假者負有及時 （五日內）繳交作業，並透過同學、課程平台，或親自聯繫老師了解該次上課內容與課後作業之 責。（可委託同學代為繳交作業或拿取作業單，或自行前來教師研究室繳交或領取。） 3. ✓ Assignments are expected to be completed and submitted by the due date. No late submission will be accepted or graded unless the instructor approves or grants your application for extension of submission. 作業請按時繳交（或上傳）。未獲教師同意可延遲繳 交者或超過寬限期，其遲交作業不批改、不計分。 ✓ Your absence CANNOT be an assumption that you are entitled to hand in the late assignments far later (more than 5 days) or until your next presence. 請勿自以為逾期的作業可以自行延遲超過五 日，或下次出現時才繳交。 ✓ NO full credit for late submission/Penalty for late submission: 10% of the total mark awarded will be deducted for each working day after the submission date. 每遲交一日。扣 10%成績。 Late Submission Mark Awarded After Penalty 6 Number of days late Penalty Original grade 90 Original grade 60 1 10% 81 54 2 20% 72 48 3 30% 63 42 4 40% 54 36 5 50% 45 30 More than 5 days Grade of zero awarded 遲交逾 5 日，不計分 ✓ Frequent late submissions with no valid excuses or under controllable circumstances will NOT be accepted or graded since the third late assignment. 無合理原因或非為不可抗力情形 的慣性遲交作業，第三份起將不予批改與計分。 4. Plagiarism on assignments and cheating on the exam is absolutely unacceptable. If someone is found plagiarizing or cheating, it means he/she will get a zero point for that assignment or exam. 嚴禁抄襲與作弊。抄襲與作弊者，學期成績以不及格處理。情節重大時，將提報至相關單 位依校規處理。 5. AI-assisted reports and assignments are allowed in limited instances: AI can be used to prepare for reports and assignments by brainstorming and tentative revision, but students must show how AI helps them reach the result. 僅限使用生成式 AI 於作業或報告之準備（如腦力激盪與初步 修訂等），學生須註明 AI 如何用於協作其作業或報告。 6. Penalty for no or poor participation in pair or group work Students are expected to take part in pair or group activities. Failure to engage in these activities (due to you absence or lateness) will lead to reductions in grades awarded. Sometimes the reduction may be suggested by other group members; in other circumstances, the instructor may reduce the grade awarded without reference to other group members. 學生負有參與雙人 或小組活動之義務。如因個人遲到或缺席導致小組活動無法順利進行，請假或缺席者該次活動成 績將以扣分或甚至 0 分計算。 7. ✓ Mobile devices are only used for educational purposes relevant to the subject or tasks in the classroom setting with the permission of or at the request of the instructor. Using mobile devices for studying other subjects or entertaining purposes is absolutely prohibited. Students who violate the regulation will be considered absent from the class or asked to leave the classroom. 行動裝置僅限於學習活動，使用須獲得老師同意或遵照老師指示。嚴禁 使用行動裝置研習其他課程或娛樂使用。違反規定者，以「未到課」處置，亦得請違規者離開 教室。 ✓ During class students are not to be seen with a cell phone in hand or on the desk. Mobile phones are expected to be turned off or switched to a silent mode. 課程進行時，請關閉行動 電話或轉為靜音模式。未獲教師指示或許可，不得於上課時間使用或放置於桌上。 8. The syllabus, handouts, and returned assignments should be kept at least until the end of this semester for later reference or the final exam. 課程相關各項文件請妥為保存至學期結束。 7 Teaching Activities  Lectures 口頭講授  Pair/Group discussion 配對／分組討論  Assignments 作業  Student presentations 學生報告  Quizzes 小考  Projects 專題 Classroom Languages English 70 % Mandarin 30 % Detailed Syllabus: WE EK DAT E Textbook unit/topic/t heme Class Activities / Assignments Skill/Strategies Academic Language Skills 1 9/7 Orientatio n, File 2A Doctor, doctor! It integrates a four-skill coursebook and related extensive learning materials to engage students in rigorous practice sessions focused on listening, reading, speaking, vocabulary, and grammar. Provided with intensive learning tasks on various topics, students should have been able to effectively apply the language strategies and knowledge acquired during the course to their daily English comprehension and communication in authentic settings. Subsidiary aim In this course students will have opportunities to 1. expand both general and academic words and expressions relevant to various topics through targeted exercises and activities. 2. review grammar structures and apply grammatical concepts in context to refine accuracy. 3. improve their listening skills such as anticipating, listening for opinions, and note- taking to extract essential information and connect main ideas with the use of a variety of audio/video materials including conversations, announcements, interviews, lectures, and etc. 2 4. learn to read a wide range of texts with comprehension skills such as scanning for specific information, comparing and contrasting ideas, skimming for main ideas and summarizing. 5. engage in interactive discussions through which they practice precise and fluent expression of their observations, experiences, opinions, and feedbacks on different general or academic topics. CEFR Can-do Statements (B2) Reception Listening OVERALL LISTENING COMPREHENSION B2 Can follow extended speech and complex lines of argument provided the topic is reasonably familiar, and the direction of the talk is sign-posted by explicit markers. [overall listening comprehension] B2+ Can understand standard spoken language, live or broadcast, on both familiar and unfamiliar topics normally encountered in personal, social, academic or vocational life. Only extreme background noise, inadequate discourse structure and/or idiomatic usage influence the ability to understand. [overall listening comprehension] EAP EOP UNDERSTANDING INTERACTION BETWEEN NATIVE SPEAKERS B2 Can with some effort catch much of what is said around him/her, but may find it difficult to participate effectively in discussion with several native speakers who do not modify their language in any way. [understanding interaction between native speakers] LISTENING TO ANNOUNCEMENTS & INSTRUCTIONS B2 Can understand announcements and messages on concrete and abstract topics spoken in standard dialect at normal speed. [listening to announcements & instructions] LISTENING TO RADIO, AUDIO & RECORDINGS B2+ Can understand recordings in standard dialect likely to be encountered in social, professional or academic life and identify speaker viewpoints and attitudes as well as the information content. [listening to radio, audio & recordings] EAP EOP Reception Reading OVERALL READING COMPREHENSION B2 Can read with a large degree of independence, adapting style and speed of reading to different texts and purposes, and using appropriate reference sources selectively. Has a broad active reading vocabulary, but may experience some difficulty with low- frequency vocabulary. [overall reading comprehension] READING FOR ORIENTATION B2 Can scan quickly through long and complex texts, locating relevant details. [reading for orientation] EAP Intera ction Spoke n Speaking OVERALL SPOKEN INTERACTION B2 Can interact with a degree of fluency and spontaneity that makes regular interaction, and sustained relationships with native speakers 3 quite possible without imposing strain on either party. [overall spoken interaction] CONVERSATION B2 Can engage in extended conversation on most general topics in a clearly participatory fashion, even in a noisy environment. [conversation] INFORMAL DISCUSSION (WITH FRIENDS) B2 Can take an active part in informal discussion in familiar contexts, commenting, putting point of view clearly, evaluating alternative proposals and making and responding to hypotheses. [informal discussion (with friends)] B2 Can with some effort catch much of what is said around him/her in discussion, but may find it difficult to participate effectively in discussion with several native speakers who do not modify their language in any way. [informal discussion (with friends)] B2 Can account for and sustain his/her opinions in discussion by providing relevant explanation, arguments and comments. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP EOP Production SpokenSpeaking OVERALL SPOKEN PRODUCTION B2 Can give clear, detailed description and presentations on a wide range of subjects related to his/her field of interest, expanding and supporting ideas with subsidiary points and relevant examples. [overall spoken production] EAP EOP Receptio n Communi cation Strategies IDENTIFYING CUES & INFERRING (SPOKEN & WRITTEN) B2 Can use a variety of strategies to achieve comprehension, including listening for main points, checking comprehension by using contextual clues. [identifying cues & inferring (spoken & written)] EAP Working with Text Communicative Language Competence NOTE-TAKING (LECTURES, SEMINARS, ETC.) B2 Can understand a clearly structured lecture on a familiar subject, and can take notes on points which strike him/her as important, even though he/she tends to concentrate on the words themselves and therefore to miss some information. [note-taking (lectures, seminars, etc.) EAP PROCESSING TEXT B2 Can summarize a wide range of factual and imaginative texts, commenting on and discussing contrasting points of view and the main themes. [processing text] EAP B2 Can summarize extracts from news items, interviews or documentaries containing opinions, argument and discussion. [processing text] EAP VOCABULARY RANGE B2 Has a good range of vocabulary for matters connected to his/her field and most general topics. [grammatical accuracy] VOCABULARY CONTROL B2 Lexical accuracy is generally high, though some confusion and incorrect word choice does occur without hindering communication. docs.text: 1 National Tsing Hua University Upper-Intermediate English I 中高級英文一 Fall 2026 Course Information Course Number LANG 1010 16 Credits 2 Classroom 綜二館 105 教室 Class hours □ Monday □ Tuesday ■ Wednesday □ Thursday □ Friday □ 8:00A.M. – 9:50A.M. ■ 10:10A.M. – 12:00P.M. 可選課學生 身分別  前標生 □ 中級生 □ 初級生 Language Level □ A2－A2+（初級） □ B1-B1+（中級）  B2（中高級） Prerequisites 加簽說明 □ 不開放人工加簽。所有學生須由選課系統亂數選課。 ■ 開放人工加簽 3 位學生。學生符合以下條件，得於第 1 週上課 時，向老師提出加簽申請。老師簽署申請表後，申請表送英語教育中心 辦公室。由老師進行線上簽核（校務資訊系統）。 ■ 條件 1：必須於第一週到課 Requirement #1: Attend the first class ■ 條件 2：須有其他時段【中高級英文一】衝堂無法選課之證明（如 選課紀錄或本學期所有科目課程表） Requirement #2: Offer a proof of time conflict with the other courses of the same title so that you MUST be taking this course. ■ 條件 3：自所屬選課階段（大一生：新生選課與第 3 次選課，點選 自己所屬「學院別」班級；所有大學部學生：第 1-3 次選課亂數選 課皆未選上；各次選課，已選上任一【中高級英文一】但自行退選 者，不予人工加簽再次選課） Requirement #3: Offer the history or record of course registration in the previous sessions that you were NOT selected for any class of Upper- Intermediate English I or that you are not qualified for course registration ■ 條件 4：應屆畢業生 Requirement #4: You are supposed to graduate this semester or this school year 提醒：學生修讀英文領域課程，請依本校規劃選課之修業年級選課。如因個人考 量，未對應年級而逕自改於其他修業年級選課之英文領域課程，或指定加簽某特 定課程，英語教育中心與任課教師將礙難配合或處理。 Reminder: Please take the required English courses in accordance with the scheduled 2 curriculum offered by our school. Your personal scheduling or preference of taking courses during your college stay will NOT be a valid excuse for the teacher to take your request for extra course registration into account. Instructor & Contact Information Name Email Office & Tel Office Hour 吳聖鵬 hank.spwu@gmail.com N/A N/A Course Aims / Description Primary aim This year-long course is designed to enhance students’ overall English proficiency by integrating listening, speaking, reading and writing activities with targeted grammar review and vocabulary development. Utilizing a four-skill coursebook plus a self‐ access learning project, the curriculum provides opportunities for students to apply language learning strategies, synthesize complex arguments, and build communicative confidence both inside and outside the classroom. Upon completion of the course, students are expected to have consolidated their linguistic foundation, enabling them to engage fluently and confidently in authentic everyday communication. Furthermore, students will master academic vocabulary and word- formation principles, including the use of prefixes, suffixes and roots. Subsidiary aim In this course students will have opportunities to 1. review and practice grammar points and sentence structures to describe and discuss a variety of topics and issues related to their life 2. build up theme-based vocabulary and even academic words for and through reading and listening to conversations, interviews, talks, and lectures 3. practice academic skills such as outlining, summarizing, critical thinking while listening, reading, speaking and writing 4. manage and present information, perspectives, or problem-solving in speaking and writing tasks or activities Corresponding CEFR Can-do statements 1. Can understand the main ideas of propositionally and linguistically complex speech of both concrete and abstract topics in a standard dialect, including technical discussions in his/her field of specialization. [overall listening comprehension] 2. Can follow the essentials of lectures, talks and reports and other forms of academic/professional presentations which are propositionally and linguistically complex. [listening as a member of a live audience] 3. Can read with a large degree of independence, adapting style and speed of 3 reading to different texts and purposes, and using appropriate reference sources selectively. Has a broad active reading vocabulary, but may experience some difficulty with low-frequency vocabulary. [overall reading comprehension] 4. Can interact with a degree of fluency and spontaneity that makes regular interaction, and sustained relationships with native speakers quite possible without imposing strain on either party. [overall spoken interaction] 5. Can give clear, detailed description and presentations on a wide range of subjects related to his/her field of interest, expanding and supporting ideas with subsidiary points and relevant examples. [overall spoken production] 6. Can write clear, detailed texts on a variety of subjects related to his/her field of interest, synthesizing and evaluating information and arguments from a number of sources. [overall written production] 7. Can pass on detailed information reliably. [propositional precision] 英文核心能力指標 University Student Core Competency Indicators 1. 英語溝通與表達能力 (ability to communicate and express oneself in English) [30%] 2. 深度分析與組織思考的能力 (ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English) [10%] 3. 英語學習策略與技巧 (knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques) [30%] 4. 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 (global views of English and multicultural diversity) [15%] 5. 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣與能力 (ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit) [15%] Teaching Materials and References Textbook(s) Christina Latham-Koenig, Clive Oxenden, and Kate Chomacki. Class attendance, lesson preparation and active class participation are required. ✓ As you are all present whenever the instructor takes the roll, you will get 60% in this category Attendance and Participation. 經常性點名，全勤者可得「出席與參與」項目中的 60%成績。 ✓ Each skip will cost 2 points from the category Attendance and Participation (up to 15 points in the final grade). 未假不到課（翹課），每 次從「出席與參與」成績（占學期成績 15 分）扣 2 分。 ✓ If you are absent in case of UNCONTROLLABLE situations (e.g. illness, emergency, important occasions, etc.), please apply for a leave on the Student Leave System on Academic Information System of National Tsing Hua University or on the iNTHU app (from the Office of Student Affair website), with clear leave information, including leave type, leave period, and reasons (must be clear and valid enough for the teacher’s approval). As the reasons or the documents are not clear, valid or sufficient enough, the teacher may deny the application. 遇不可抗力情形需請假者，請於本校校務資 訊系統上的學生請假系統或下載 iNTHU APP，填寫資料（請假類別、請假日期、請假事由）。請假 事由須合理並敘述清楚，提供老師是否准假之參考。請假單上的理由或所附證明文件不清楚 或不充分時，該次請假申請得不予核准。 ✓ Please observe the information you are expected to offer for each of the following leave types: ◼ For sick leave, please describe severe symptoms and medical treatments you have been taking in the box “Reason.” 請病假時，請於理由欄位說明影響上課之顯著症狀，就醫或服 藥等處理。 ◼ For personal leave, please describe the uncontrollable event and how it makes you absent from the class. 請事假時，請於理由欄位敘明事件，並說明該事件如何致使你無法前來上 課。 ◼ No leave application will be approved on the dates of presentations, peer evaluations, and midterm/final exams. Please care for your health and reserve the time for these important class activities. 報告、同儕互評、期中／期末考當日不得請假。請注意身心健康 並為這些重要課程活動預留時間。 NTHU 學生請假 Q&A 5 ◼ There will be NO make-up exams or presentations unless you apply for leave with valid and official reasons for your absence beforehand. 無合理且正式的缺課原因，將不予補考 或補行報告。 ✓ You are expected to apply for leave before the class you are absent from. Any overdue leave application must be made within 7 days from the last day of absence. 請假已事先申請為原 則。逾期請假申請必須於 7 日內補請。未能於規定期間申請者，均以曠課論。 ✓ Being late for more than 10 minutes (with no valid excuses) is treated as absence from that hour. Being late for more than 30 minutes is treated as absence from the whole class. 無故 遲到逾 10 分鐘，以該小時未到課紀錄。遲到逾 30 分鐘，視為該次上課未到課。 ✓ No points will be deducted for your ATTENDANCE as long as your approved leave is no more than 6 hours. However, you may lose points for your PARTICIPATION or in-class practices scheduled on the date of your absence. 核准的請假時數未逾 6 小時，不扣出席成績。惟當日 如有上課練習或小組活動，請假者無法參與或完成，將無法獲得該次練習或該項評量成績。換 言之，缺課仍可能影響「參與」與「作業」等成績。 ✓ If you skip class for more than 8 hours, your course withdrawal may NOT be approved, and you will get 0 credits for this course. 無故不到課逾 8 小時者，將不予同意其停修申請，亦無 法取得本課程學分。 ✓ A student will fail to get the 2 credits for missing 5 classes, including the ones due to any kinds of leaves. 缺課達五次（含各類請假缺課）者，將無法從本課程獲取任何學分。 2. Absence from a class is no excuse for failing to complete in-class practices, to submit assignments in time, or to get informed of assignments or the class you have missed. It is your responsibility to hand in the assignments within 5 days (weekends & holidays included) and to reach your classmates or the instructor and refer to the course platform (eeclass) for the relevant information concerning what has been covered in the class. You may ask a classmate of yours to help with assignment submission and collection of assignment worksheets, if any. You may make an appointment with the instructor for assignment worksheets. 缺席與請假不得作為未 能完成當日上課練習、無法及時繳交作業或不知道該次課後作業之藉口。缺席與請假者負有及時 （五日內）繳交作業，並透過同學、課程平台，或親自聯繫老師了解該次上課內容與課後作業之 責。（可委託同學代為繳交作業或拿取作業單，或自行前來教師研究室繳交或領取。） 3. ✓ Assignments are expected to be completed and submitted by the due date. No late submission will be accepted or graded unless the instructor approves or grants your application for extension of submission. 作業請按時繳交（或上傳）。未獲教師同意可延遲繳 交者或超過寬限期，其遲交作業不批改、不計分。 ✓ Your absence CANNOT be an assumption that you are entitled to hand in the late assignments far later (more than 5 days) or until your next presence. 請勿自以為逾期的作業可以自行延遲超過五 日，或下次出現時才繳交。 ✓ NO full credit for late submission/Penalty for late submission: 10% of the total mark awarded will be deducted for each working day after the submission date. 每遲交一日。扣 10%成績。 Late Submission Mark Awarded After Penalty 6 Number of days late Penalty Original grade 90 Original grade 60 1 10% 81 54 2 20% 72 48 3 30% 63 42 4 40% 54 36 5 50% 45 30 More than 5 days Grade of zero awarded 遲交逾 5 日，不計分 ✓ Frequent late submissions with no valid excuses or under controllable circumstances will NOT be accepted or graded since the third late assignment. 無合理原因或非為不可抗力情形 的慣性遲交作業，第三份起將不予批改與計分。 4. Plagiarism on assignments and cheating on the exam is absolutely unacceptable. If someone is found plagiarizing or cheating, it means he/she will get a zero point for that assignment or exam. 嚴禁抄襲與作弊。抄襲與作弊者，學期成績以不及格處理。情節重大時，將提報至相關單 位依校規處理。 5. AI-assisted reports and assignments are allowed in limited instances: AI can be used to prepare for reports and assignments by brainstorming and tentative revision, but students must show how AI helps them reach the result. 僅限使用生成式 AI 於作業或報告之準備（如腦力激盪與初步 修訂等），學生須註明 AI 如何用於協作其作業或報告。 6. Penalty for no or poor participation in pair or group work Students are expected to take part in pair or group activities. Failure to engage in these activities (due to you absence or lateness) will lead to reductions in grades awarded. Sometimes the reduction may be suggested by other group members; in other circumstances, the instructor may reduce the grade awarded without reference to other group members. 學生負有參與雙人 或小組活動之義務。如因個人遲到或缺席導致小組活動無法順利進行，請假或缺席者該次活動成 績將以扣分或甚至 0 分計算。 7. ✓ Mobile devices are only used for educational purposes relevant to the subject or tasks in the classroom setting with the permission of or at the request of the instructor. Using mobile devices for studying other subjects or entertaining purposes is absolutely prohibited. Students who violate the regulation will be considered absent from the class or asked to leave the classroom. 行動裝置僅限於學習活動，使用須獲得老師同意或遵照老師指示。嚴禁 使用行動裝置研習其他課程或娛樂使用。違反規定者，以「未到課」處置，亦得請違規者離開 教室。 ✓ During class students are not to be seen with a cell phone in hand or on the desk. Mobile phones are expected to be turned off or switched to a silent mode. 課程進行時，請關閉行動 電話或轉為靜音模式。未獲教師指示或許可，不得於上課時間使用或放置於桌上。 8. The syllabus, handouts, and returned assignments should be kept at least until the end of this semester for later reference or the final exam. 課程相關各項文件請妥為保存至學期結束。 7 Teaching Activities  Lectures 口頭講授  Pair/Group discussion 配對／分組討論  Assignments 作業  Student presentations 學生報告  Quizzes 小考  Projects 專題 Classroom Languages English 70 % Mandarin 30 % Detailed Syllabus: WE EK DAT E Textbook unit/topic/t heme Class Activities / Assignments Skill/Strategies Academic Language Skills 1 9/9 Orientatio n, File 2A Doctor, doctor! Liu liumeitzu@gapp.nthu.edu.tw N/A N/A 2 Course Aims / Description Primary aim This one-year course aims to enhance students’ overall English competence by developing their listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills. Through interactive activities, grammar review, and vocabulary expansion, students will strengthen their ability to communicate effectively in both everyday and academic contexts. The course incorporates a four-skill coursebook and a self-access learning project to provide structured learning tasks and opportunities for independent practice. Students will also be introduced to essential academic English skills, such as summarizing texts and writing structured essays, as well as practicing note-taking and understanding lectures to improve their ability to engage with academic materials. By the end of the course, students are expected to demonstrate greater confidence and fluency in authentic communication, whether in daily interactions or academic discussions. Subsidiary aim In this class, students will have opportunities to 1. review and practice grammar points and sentence structures to describe and discuss a variety of topics and issues related to their life 2. build up theme-based vocabulary and even academic words for and through reading and listening to conversations, interviews, talks, and lectures 3. practice academic skills such as outlining, summarizing, and critical thinking while listening, reading, speaking, and writing 4. present information, perspectives, or problem-solving in speaking and writing tasks or activities Corresponding CEFR Can-do statements 1. [LISTENING]: Can understand the main ideas of propositionally and linguistically complex speech of both concrete and abstract topics in a standard dialect, including technical discussions in his/her field of specialization. 2. [READING]: Can quickly identify the content and relevance off news items, articles and reports on a wide range of professional topics, deciding whether closer study is worthwhile. 3. [SPOKEN INTERACTION]: Can use the language fluently, accurately and effectively on a wide range of general, academic, vocational or leisure topics, marking clearly the relationships between ideas. 4. [WRITTEN PRODUCTION]: Can write letters conveying degrees of emotion and highlighting the personal significance of events and experiences and commenting on the correspondent’s news and views. 5. [SOCIOLINGUISTIC APPROPRIATENESS]: Can express him/herself confidently, clearly and politely in a formal or informal register, appropriate to the situation and the person(s) concerned. 3 英文核心能力指標 University Student Core Competency Indicators 1. 英語溝通與表達能力 (ability to communicate and express oneself in English) 30% 2. 深度分析與組織思考的能力 (ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English) 20% 3. 英語學習策略與技巧 (knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques) 20% 4. 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 (global views of English and multicultural diversity) 20% 5. 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣與能力 (ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit) 10% Teaching Materials and References Textbook(s) Christina Latham-koenig, Clive Oxenden, and Kate Chomachi.(2021) American English File 4, 3rd Edition. VoiceTube / YouTube / Podcast 4. Online news stories Requirements & Rules: 1.Class attendance and class participation:  Attendance is taken every session throughout the semester. You have a total of three opportunities for leave without penalty. Sick leave, official leave, personal leave, mental health leave (activated on the third time with school-parent concern), and menstrual leave no proof is required. All leave requests should be submitted through the school’s online System。  Four absences (with approved requests) or two absences (without requests) will result in a failing grade.  Through school system: 3 chances.  Without school system: 1 chance Official school competition leave — we’ll discuss this separately. 4  Lateness: Unless an unavoidable reason is provided, a 20% deduction will be applied.  Class Participation: In-class assignments (pair work) and answering questions. 請特別留意，這門課很注重出席率，因此如果經批准的請假累計達到4次以上 (包含4次)， 或是有 2 次沒有來也沒有請假（包含 2 次），這門課程就會不及格。 2. Assignment: No make-up submissions.  In the first week, I’ll open the assignment submission period, which will last until the deadline. You’ll have time to submit. Therefore, no excuses for absence will be accepted for late submissions.  Absence from a class is no excuse for submitting assignments in time or ignoring assignments or the class you have missed. It is your responsibility to ask your classmates what has been covered in the class. 3. No make-up exams or presentation: The group presentation and the midterm role-play are essential team-based performance assignments. Your participation is crucial. If you are late, absent, or fail to complete your assigned part—and this negatively impacts your group—you will receive a zero for the assignment and fail the course. 4. Mobile phone/ tablets: make sure to mute or turn off your mobile phone before class begins. During the class, no access to mobile devices is allowed unless permission is given for a specific learning task or activity. 5. Plagiarism / Cheating : plagiarism on assignments and cheating on the exam is absolutely unacceptable. 6. AI-assisted reports and assignments  It is allowed in limited instances: AI can be used to prepare for reports and assignments by brainstorming, but students must show how it helped them reach the result. Grading: 1. Attendance and participation 15% 2. Midterm exam 20% 3. Final Exam 25% 4. Assignments / quizzes 20% 5. Self-access learning 10% 6. The student never attends class nor submits assignments. 2. The student is absent or asks for leave with NO valid excuses for more than 4 classes. 3. The student never explains to or discusses with the teacher his/her difficulty in taking care of this subject. 4. The student neither offers valid excuses on his application for course withdrawal nor notifies the teacher beforehand. 學生如遇有以下情形，其停修申請將不予「同意」 1. 學生未曾到課或繳交任何作業。 2. 學生無故缺席或未有證明之請假超過四次 3. 學生從未向老師解釋、或與之討論，修讀本課程時的困難 4. 學生未在停修申請上敘明或以其他通訊方式告知老師停修本課程之原因 避免學生規避「低修」學分數而選課，或以其他理由選課但不上課等情事 提醒：請於選課前參考課程大綱，了解評分方式、各週進度。並於第一堂課進一步了 解作業、報告、考試的規劃與所需處理時間。評估自已的學習量能，避免修課失衡。 Instructor & Contact Information Name Email Office & Tel Office Hour 徐桂平 Vicky Hsu personal messaging on eeclass1 綜二館 B 側 209 ( 34417) Tuesday 10:00 A.M.-12:00 P.M. 綜二館 B 側 209 1 No email via eeclass will be replied to, for the sender’s email address does not belong to the student. Please leave messages on eeclass, using the “personal messages” function. eeclass eeclass 2 prepared by Vicky Hsu Course Aims / Description 1. Primary aim This one-year course is designed to enhance students’ overall English competence through listening, speaking, and reading activities plus grammar review and vocabulary development. A four-skill coursebook plus a self-access learning project will be integrated to design learning tasks and provide opportunities for students to practice language learning strategies, get exposed to English in any form, and develop their confidence and fluency in the classroom and outside the classroom. After having taken this course, students are expected to consolidate their knowledge of English language and engage themselves more confidently and fluently in authentic communication in everyday settings and even in school settings. 2. Subsidiary aim In this class, students will have the opportunity to 1. review and practice grammar points and sentence structures, especially concerning verb tenses, to describe and discuss a variety of topics and issues related to their life 2. build up theme-based vocabulary and also academic words for and through reading and listening to conversations, interviews, talks, and lectures 3. practice academic skills such as outlining, summarizing, paraphrasing, and critical thinking while listening, reading, speaking and writing 4. manage and present information, perspectives, or problem-solving/decision-making in speaking and writing tasks or activities 3. Corresponding CEFR Can-do statements (B2) Reception Listening LISTENING TO RADIO, AUDIO & RECORDINGS B2 Can understand most radio documentaries and most other recorded or broadcast audio material delivered in standard dialect and can identify the speaker’s mood, tone, etc. [listening to radio, audio & recordings] Reception Reading OVERALL READING COMPREHENSION B2 Can read with a large degree of independence, adapting style and speed of reading to different texts and purposes, and using appropriate reference sources selectively. Has a broad active reading vocabulary, but may experience some difficulty with low- frequency vocabulary. [overall reading comprehension] READING FOR INFORMATION & ARGUMENT B2 Can understand articles and reports concerned with contemporary problems in which the writer adopts particular stances or viewpoints. [reading for information & argument] In tSpeaking INFORMAL DISCUSSION (WITH FRIENDS) 3 prepared by Vicky Hsu B2 Can account for and sustain his/her opinions in discussion by providing relevant explanation, arguments and comments. [informal discussion (with friends)] INFORMATION EXCHANGE B2 Can pass on detailed information reliably. [information exchange] Production Spoken Speaking OVERALL SPOKEN PRODUCTION B2 Can give clear, detailed description and presentations on a wide range of subjects related to his/her field of interest, expanding and supporting ideas with subsidiary points and relevant examples. [overall spoken production] ADDRESSING AUDIENCES B2 Can give a clear, prepared presentation, giving reasons in support of or against a particular point of view and giving the advantages and disadvantages of various options. [addressing audiences] Reception Communi cation Strategies IDENTIFYING CUES & INFERRING (SPOKEN & WRITTEN) B2 Can use a variety of strategies to achieve comprehension, including listening for main points, checking comprehension by using contextual clues. [identifying cues & inferring (spoken & written)] EAP Interaction Communi cation Strategies COOPERATING B2 Can give feedback on and follow up statements and inferences and so help the development of the discussion. [cooperating] EAP ASKING FOR CLARIFICATION B2 Can ask follow-up questions to check that he/she has understood what a speaker intended to say, and get clarification of ambiguous points. [asking for clarification] Working with Text NOTE-TAKING (LECTURES, SEMINARS, ETC.) B2 Can understand a clearly structured lecture on a familiar subject, and can take notes on points which strike him/her as important, even though he/she tends to concentrate on the words themselves and therefore to miss some information. [note-taking (lectures, seminars, etc.) EAP PROCESSING TEXT B2 Can summarize a wide range of factual and imaginative texts, commenting on and discussing contrasting points of view and the main themes. [processing text] EAP 4 prepared by Vicky Hsu Communicative Language Competence Range GENERAL LINGUISTIC RANGE B2+ Can express him/herself clearly and without much sign of having to restrict what he/she wants to say. [processing text] VOCABULARY RANGE B2 Has a good range of vocabulary for matters connected to his/her field and most general topics. [vocabulary range] Control GRAMMATICAL ACCURACY B2+ Good grammatical control. Occasional “slips” or non-systematic errors and minor flaws in sentence structure may still occur, but they are rare and can often be corrected in retrospect. [grammatical accuracy] VOCABULARY CONTROL B2 Lexical accuracy is generally high, though some confusion and incorrect word choice does occur without hindering communication. [vocabulary control] ORTHOGRAPHIC CONTROL B2 Can produce clearly intelligible continuous writing, which follows standard layout and paragraphing conventions. [orthographic control] EAP B2 Spelling, punctuation and layout are accurate but may show signs of mother tongue influence. [orthographic control] Sociolinguistic SOCIOLINGUISTIC APPROPRIATENESS B2 Can with some effort keep up with and contribute to group discussions even when speech is fast and colloquial. [sociolinguistic appropriateness] Pragmatic FLEXIBILITY B2 Can adjust to the changes of direction, style and emphasis normally found in conversation. [flexibility] COHERENCE B2 Can use a limited number of cohesive devices to link his/her utterance into clear, coherent discourse, though there may be some “jumpiness” in a long contribution. [coherence] EAP 英文核心能力指標 University Student Core Competency Indicators 1. 英語溝通與表達能力 (ability to communicate and express oneself in English) 30% 2. 深度分析與組織思考的能力 (ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in 20% 5 prepared by Vicky Hsu English) 3. 英語學習策略與技巧 (knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques) 30% 4. 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 (global views of English and multicultural diversity) 10% 5. 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣與能力 (ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit) 10% Teaching Materials and References Uniform textbook Christina Latham-Koenig, Clive Oxenden, and Kate Chomacki. (2021) American English File 4, 3rd Edition. New York: Oxford University Press. ISBN: 978-0-19- 490685-2 Reminder: Students are required to use the PHYSICAL COPY of the textbook for in-class practices and assignments. E-books or any unauthorized format of this textbook is not used in class due to any excuses. 修讀本課程之學生，需使用此教材的「實體書」，進行上課練習與作業。 上課時，不使用電子書或任何未經授權的教材。 CEFR Scale □ B2+ ■ B2 □ B1 □ A2+ □ A2 Platforms and accounts for course materials and learning resources 1. 清華大學 eeclass 數位學習系統 https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw/ 2. MS Forms (for assignments & quizzes) 3. Office365 account issued by the Center of Computer and Communication of National Tsing Hua University Grading Scheme 1. Attendance and participation (cf. Requirements and rules 1, 2, 6, and 7) 15% 2. Assignments (& quizzes) (cf. Requirements and rules 3-5) 25% 3. Final exam (File 2A, File 3A & File 4A) (cf. Requirements and rules 4) 30% 4. Presentation (A video to the future self) 10% 5. Academic English Skills practices (AI-assisted or TEEMI platform) 10% 6. Self-access learning project (6-8 tasks related to grammar, public speaking, & topics in AEF 4) 10% Note: The percentage of this grading scheme is subject to possible adjustments. To be announced. Requirements & Rules 1. Class attendance, lesson preparation and active class participation are required.  As you are all present whenever the instructor takes attendance, you will get 60% (9 points) in this category Attendance and Participation. 經常性點名，全勤者可得「出席與參與」項目 中的 60%（9 分）成績。  Each skip will cost 2 points from the category Attendance and Participation (up to 15 points in the final grade). 未假不到課（翹課），每次從「出席與參與」成績（占學期成績 15 分）扣 6 prepared by Vicky Hsu 2 分。  If you are absent in case of UNCONTROLLABLE situations (e.g. illness, emergency, important occasions, etc.), please apply for a leave on the Student Leave System on Academic Information System of National Tsing Hua University or on the iNTHU app (from the Office of Student Affair website), with clear leave information, including leave type, leave period, and reasons (must be clear and valid enough for the teacher’s approval). As the reasons or the documents are not clear, valid or sufficient enough, the teacher may deny the application. 遇不可抗力情形需請假者，請於本校校務資訊系統上的學 生請假系統或下載 iNTHU APP，填寫資料（請假類別、請假日期、請假事由）。請假事由須合理並 敘述清楚，提供老師是否准假之參考。請假單上的理由或所附證明文件不清楚或不充分時， 該次請假申請得不予核准。  Please observe the information you are expected to offer for each of the following leave types:  For sick leave, please describe severe symptoms and medical treatments you have been taking in the box “Reason.” 請病假時，請於理由欄位說明影響上課之顯著症狀，就醫或服 藥等處理。  For personal leave, please describe the uncontrollable incident and how it makes you absent from the class. 請事假時，請於理由欄位敘明該不可抗力事件，並說明該事件如何 致使你無法前來上課。  Please observe the school calendar and avoid arranging any (family or personal) vacations or trips during the semester. No scheduled arrangements for pleasure or personal convenience will be considered uncontrollable incidents. 請依本校行事曆，避免於學期間 以個人或家庭為由安排度假、旅遊活動。任何與玩樂或個人方便之安排，皆無法歸類為不可 抗力事件。  No leave application will be approved on the dates of presentations, peer evaluations, and midterm/final exams. Please care for your health and reserve the time for these important class activities. 報告、同儕互評、期中／期末考當日不得請假。請注意身心健康 並為這些重要課程活動預留時間。  There will be NO make-up exams or presentations unless you apply for leave with valid and official reasons for your absence beforehand. 無合理且正式的缺課原因，將不予補考 或補行報告。  You are expected to apply for leave before the class you are absent from. Any overdue leave application must be made within 7 days from the last day of absence. 請假以事先申請為原 則。逾期請假申請必須於 7 日內補請。未能於規定期間申請者，均以曠課論。  Being late for more than 10 minutes (with no valid excuses) is treated as absence from that hour (1 point deducted). Being late for more than 30 minutes is treated as absence from the whole class (2-points deducted). 無故遲到逾 10 分鐘，以該小時未到課紀錄（扣 1 分）。遲 到逾 30 分鐘，視為該次上課未到課（扣 2 分）。  No points will be deducted for your ATTENDANCE as long as your approved leave is no more NTHU Q&A 7 prepared by Vicky Hsu than 6 hours. However, you may lose points for your PARTICIPATION or in-class practices scheduled on the date of your absence. 核准的請假時數未逾 6 小時，不扣出席成績。惟當日 如有上課練習或小組活動，請假者無法參與或完成，將無法獲得該次練習或該項評量成績。換 言之，缺課仍可能影響「參與」與「作業」等成績。  If you skip class for more than 8 hours, your course withdrawal may NOT be approved, and you will get 0 credits for this course. 無故不到課逾 8 小時者，將不予同意其停修申請，亦無 法取得本課程學分。  A student will fail to get the 2 credits for missing 5 classes, including the ones due to any kinds of leaves. 缺課達五次（含各類請假缺課）者，將無法從本課程獲取任何學分。 2. Absence from a class is no excuse for failing to complete in-class practices, to submit assignments in time, or to get informed of assignments or the class you have missed. It is your responsibility to hand in the assignments within 5 days (weekends & holidays included) and to reach your classmates or the instructor and refer to the course platform (EECLASS) for the relevant information concerning what has been covered in the class. You may ask a classmate of yours to help with assignment submission and collection of assignment worksheets, if any. You may make an appointment with the instructor for assignment worksheets. 缺席與請假不得作為未 能完成當日上課練習、無法及時繳交作業或不知道該次課後作業之藉口。缺席與請假者負有及時 （五日內）繳交作業，並透過同學、課程平台，或親自聯繫老師了解該次上課內容與課後作業之 責。（可委託同學代為繳交作業或拿取作業單，或自行前來教師研究室繳交或領取。） 3.  Assignments are expected to be completed and submitted by the due date. No late submission will be accepted or graded unless the instructor approves or grants your application for extension of submission. 作業請按時繳交（或上傳）。未獲教師同意可延遲繳 交者或超過寬限期，其遲交作業不批改、不計分。  Your absence CANNOT be an assumption that you are entitled to hand in the late assignments far later (more than 5 days) or until your next presence. 請勿自以為逾期的作業 可以自行延遲超過五日，或下次出現時才繳交。  NO full credit for late submission/Penalty for late submission: 10% of the total mark awarded will be deducted for each working day after the submission date. 每遲交一日。扣 10%成績。 Late Submission Mark Awarded After Penalty Number of days late Penalty Original grade 90 Original grade 60 1 10% 81 54 2 20% 72 48 3 30% 63 42 4 40% 54 36 5 50% 45 30 More than 5 days Grade of zero awarded 遲交逾 5 日，不計分  Frequent late submissions with no valid excuses or under controllable circumstances will 8 prepared by Vicky Hsu NOT be accepted or graded since the third late assignment. 無合理原因或非為不可抗力情形 的慣性遲交作業，第三份起將不予批改與計分。 4. Plagiarism on assignments and cheating on the exam is absolutely unacceptable. If someone is found plagiarizing or cheating, it means he/she will get a zero point for that assignment or exam. 嚴禁抄襲與作弊。抄襲與作弊者，學期成績以不及格處理。情節重大時，將提報至相關單 位依校規處理。 5. AI regulations for assignments, reports, and projects AI-assisted reports and assignments are allowed in limited instances: AI can be used to prepare for reports and assignments by brainstorming, grammar checks, or tentative revision, but students must show how AI helps them reach the result. 僅限使用生成式 AI 於作業或報告之準 備（如腦力激盪、文法檢查與初步修訂等），學生須註明 AI 如何用於協作其作業或報告。  Moderate Brainstorming: GenAI is allowed for helping you generate ideas (via your conversation with GenAI), outline the thoughts, or explore concepts, but the core information and arguments must be original, not contributed entirely by AI. AI 可用於協助 擬進行適度的腦力激盪，如協助生成想法（與 AI 進行對話討論）、將想法撰寫成提綱、或探 索相關概念等，但核心資訊與論點必須是學生原創，而非由 AI 提供或生成所有資訊或資料。  Limited Editing: Students write their own work first, then use GenAI tools exclusively for spelling, grammar, and structural polish. No AI-generated content will be added to students’ original work. 學生必須先自行寫出，再使用 AI 工具，僅用於拼字、文法、句構的 修正與修飾。學生作品仍只能有學生原創的想法，不得加入 AI 生成的內容。  AI Transparency (Full use with citation): If it is permissible to complete specified tasks with GenAI in an assignment or project, any AI- generated content must be cited or provided in an appendix for its critical engagement in the output. 即使作業容許 AI 協作某些特定任 務、也必須在作業或報告中清楚標示所引用的 AI 生成內容 (How to cite Gen AI 如何引用 AI 文字: https://tamu.libguides.com/c.php?g=1289555&p=9679433)  Plagiarism/Academic dishonesty/Ethical misconduct: Using AI-generated content is not always traditional plagiarism, but submitting or publishing it as your own original work is widely considered academic dishonesty or ethical misconduct. If your work contains verbatim AI-generated text or lacks proper source attribution, it will result in a severe point deduction. 使用 AI 生成之內容並不一定構成傳統認定的抄襲，但以 AI 生成內容做為 自己的作品逕行繳交或發表，仍廣義地視為缺乏學術誠信或有道德瑕疵。如果您的作 品包含逐字 AI 生成文本，或缺乏適當的來源標註，將會導致嚴重扣分。 6. Penalty for no or poor participation in pair or group work Students are expected to take part in pair or group activities. Failure to engage in these activities (due to you absence or lateness) will lead to reductions in grades awarded. Sometimes the reduction may be suggested by other group members; in other circumstances, the instructor may reduce the grade awarded without reference to other group members. 學生負有參與雙人 How to cite Gen AI 9 prepared by Vicky Hsu 或小組活動之義務。如因個人遲到或缺席導致小組活動無法順利進行，請假或缺席者該次活動成 績將以扣分或甚至 0 分計算。 7.  Mobile devices are only used for educational purposes relevant to the subject or tasks in the classroom setting with the permission of or at the request of the instructor. Using mobile devices for studying other subjects or for entertaining purposes is absolutely prohibited. Students who violate the regulation will be considered absent from the class or asked to leave the classroom. 行動裝置僅限於學習活動，使用須獲得老師同意或遵照老師指示。嚴禁 使用行動裝置研習其他課程或娛樂使用。違反規定者，以「未到課」處置，亦得請違規者離開 教室。  During class students are not to be seen with a cell phone in hand or on the desk.
