_____________ Date ____ The 10-Year Video Letter Project SECTION 1: PROJECT GUIDELINES & SPECIFICATIONS ᇤᇥᇦᇧᇨ Project Overview Welcome to your first major college project! You will record a 3-minute video addressed to yourself 10 years in the future. This project serves a dual purpose: 1. Personal ReflecƟon: To map out your ambiƟons, personal growth, and acƟon plan for your college years. 2. Language Mastery: To demonstrate your pracƟcal understanding and usage of various English verb tenses (Past, Present, and Future forms). ᢇᢈᢉᢊ Technical & PresentaƟon Guidelines  Video Length: Exactly 2:45 to 3:15 minutes. Videos under or over this limit will receive a point deducƟon.  Recording Format: MP4 or MOV. Landscape orientaƟon (horizontal) is highly recommended.  Audio & Video Quality: Record in a quiet, well-lit room. Your voice must be clearly audible.  Eye Contact: Do not simply read from a script. Look directly into the camera lens to speak to your future self. ។៕៖ៗ៘៙ Important Deadlines  Phase 1: WriƩen Script Submission – Due on [Insert Date] via Moodle/Google Classroom.  Phase 2: Final Video Link Submission – Due on [Insert Date]. Upload your video to YouTube as an "Unlisted" video and submit the link. SECTION 2: THE 3-MINUTE SCRIPT FRAMEWORK Use this framework to organize your thoughts. Each secƟon must take roughly 1 minute of your speaking Ɵme. ഹഺ഻഼ഽാ Grammar Checklist To get full points for grammar, you must include and highlight these 5 essenƟal tenses: * [ ] Past Simple (e.g., I chose, I started) * [ ] Present Perfect (e.g., I have lived, I have met) * [ ] Present ConƟnuous / Plans (e.g., I am taking, I am going to) * [ ] Future ConƟnuous (e.g., I will be working) * [ ] Future Perfect (e.g., I will have graduated) МНОП Script Template 15 prepared by Vicky Hsu  Minute 1: Past & Present Self (The "How I Got Here" Phase)  Target Tenses: Past Simple, Present Perfect.  Prompt: What significant event brought you to this university? How has your life changed since orientaƟon?  Example: "Hello, Future Me! Today is [Month, Day, Year], and I am recording this from my freshman dorm room. Looking back, I chose this university because I fell in love with the campus during my high school tour. Since my classes started last month, I have met so many people from diƯerent cities. I have already joined two clubs, and honestly, I have been a little overwhelmed, but I am adjusting well."  Minute 2: College AcƟon Plan (The "Making the Most of It" Phase)  Target Tenses: Present ConƟnuous (for arranged plans), Future with will / be going to.  Prompt: What are you acƟvely doing this semester to grow? What specific milestones will you achieve?  Example: "Right now, I am studying incredibly hard for my first economics midterm. To make the most of my time here, I am planning a study abroad trip for my junior year. Next semester, I am going to apply for an internship at a local tech startup. I will not waste my college years; instead, I am going to push myself out of my comfort zone every single day."  Minute 3: 10-Year Visions (The "Dreaming Big" Phase)  Target Tenses: Future ConƟnuous, Future Perfect.  Prompt: What will you be doing daily at age 28? What major goals will you have achieved by then?  Example: "Ten years from now, I imagine you will be working as a senior consultant at a global firm. I hope that by 2036, you will have graduated top of our class and will have traveled to at least five diƯerent countries. By the time you watch this video, I hope you will have built a career you love. Don't forget where you started!" SECTION 3: YOUTUBE UPLOAD TUTORIAL ("UNLISTED" MODE) To protect your privacy while allowing your classmates and professor to review your project, you MUST upload your video as an "Unlisted" video. ❚❛❜ Important Privacy DefiniƟons: ᤶᤷ Public: Anyone on the internet can search for and find your video. ᤶᤷ Private: No one can see the video except you. Classmates and professors cannot open the link. 16 prepared by Vicky Hsu ࠱࠲࠳࠴ Unlisted (Required): The video will not appear in search results or on your channel. Your personal scheduling or preference of taking courses during your college stay will NOT be a valid excuse for the teacher to take your request for extra course registration into account. Course Description Primary Aim This one-year course is designed to enhance students’ overall English competence through listening, 2 prepared by Kevin Chiang speaking, and reading activities plus grammar review and vocabulary development. A four-skill coursebook plus a self-access learning project will be integrated to design learning tasks and provide opportunities for students to practice language learning strategies, get exposed to English in any form, and develop their confidence and fluency in the classroom and outside the classroom. After having taken this course, students are expected to consolidate their knowledge of English language and engage themselves more confidently and fluently in authentic communication in everyday settings and even in school settings. In this class, students will have opportunities to 1. review and practice grammar points and sentence structures to describe and discuss a variety of topics and issues related to their lives, 2. build up theme-based vocabulary and even academic words for and through reading and listening to conversations, interviews, talks, and lectures, 3. present and explain information, perspectives, or problem-solving in speaking and writing tasks or activities. Secondary Aim 1. Students are required to practice their speaking skill, including daily conversation and formal presentation, by practicing at class and get feedback from their classmates. 2. They should be able use and review the grammar they learned before college in oral and written form. 3. Each of the student needs to write a self-studying plan for the semester at the beginning and review how well he/she has completed at the end of semester. 4. Students are required to learn how to write formal essays in various genres and review their peers’. Also, they will get their peers feedback and revise their own accordingly. 5. They should practice listening skill both in the classroom and outside the classroom and show their result in self-learning review sheet. Through interactive activities, grammar review, and vocabulary expansion, students will strengthen their ability to communicate effectively in both everyday and academic contexts. The course incorporates a four-skill coursebook and a self-access learning project to provide structured learning tasks and opportunities for independent practice. Students will also be introduced to essential academic English skills, such as summarizing texts and writing structured essays, as well as practicing note-taking and understanding lectures to improve their ability to engage with academic materials. By the end of the course, students are expected to demonstrate greater confidence and fluency in authentic communication, whether in daily interactions or academic discussions. Subsidiary aim In this class, students will have opportunities to 1. review and practice grammar points and sentence structures to describe and discuss a variety of topics and issues related to their life 2. build up theme-based vocabulary and even academic words for and through reading and listening to conversations, interviews, talks, and lectures 3. practice academic skills such as outlining, summarizing, and critical thinking while listening, reading, speaking, and writing 4. present information, perspectives, or problem-solving in speaking and writing tasks or activities Corresponding CEFR Can-do statements 1. docs.text: 1 revised by KWONG National Tsing Hua University Upper-intermediate English I 中高級英文一 Fall 2026 Course Number 11510LANG101027 Credits 2 Classroom 綜二 203 Class hours □Monday □ Tuesday □ Wednesday □ Thursday □Friday □ 10:10A.M. – 12:00P.M. 學生身分別 □ 頂 標生 ■ 前 標生 □ 中 級生 □ 初級生 □ 不開放人工加簽。所有學生須由選課系統亂數選課。 Instructor & Contact Information: Name Email Office Hour Miss Kwong ymkwong@gapp.nthu.edu.tw By appointment Course Aims / Description 1. Primary aim Upper-intermediate English I is an integrated course designed to develop students' four English skills (i.e., listening, speaking, reading, & writing) with an emphasis on speaking and listening. In this course, students will: -Identify listening problems and develop listening strategies and skills, -Gain confidence in speaking and improve speaking fluency, pronunciation, and conversation strategies, -Develop general reading skills, including word skills and comprehension strategies. 2. Subsidiary aim In this class, students will have opportunity to 1. listen to authentic English-speaking topics such as English news reports, daily life conversations or English documentary video clips and personal presentation. 2. review and practice grammar points and sentence structures to describe and discuss a variety of topics and issues related to their life 3. build up theme-based vocabulary and even academic words for and through reading and listening to conversations, interviews, talks, and lectures 4. practice academic skills such as outlining, summarizing, critical thinking while listening, reading, speaking and writing 2 revised by KWONG 5. manage and present information, perspectives, or problem-solving in speaking and writing tasks or activities 3. Corresponding CEFR Can-do statements LISTENING AS A MEMBER OF A LIVE AUDIENCE B2 Can follow the essentials of lectures, talks and reports and other forms of academic/professional presentations which are propositionally and linguistically complex. [listening as a member of a live audience] EAP EOP LISTENING TO ANNOUNCEMENTS & INSTRUCTIONS B2 Can understand announcements and messages on concrete and abstract topics spoken in standard dialect at normal speed. [listening to announcements & instructions] LISTENING TO RADIO, AUDIO & RECORDINGS B2 Can understand most radio documentaries and most other recorded or broadcast audio material delivered in standard dialect and can identify the speaker’s mood, tone, etc. [listening to radio, audio & recordings] WATCHING TV & FILM B2 Can understand most TV news and current affairs programs. [watching TV & film] Reception Reading OVERALL READING COMPREHENSION B2 Can read with a large degree of independence, adapting style and speed of reading to different texts and purposes, and using appropriate reference sources selectively. Has a broad active reading vocabulary, but may experience some difficulty with low- frequency vocabulary. [overall reading comprehension] READING CORRESPONDENCE B2 Can read correspondence relating to his/her field of interest and readily grasp the essential meaning. [reading correspondence] EOP READING FOR INFORMATION & ARGUMENT B2 Can understand articles and reports concerned with contemporary problems in which the writer adopts particular stances or viewpoints. [reading for information & argument] Interaction Spoken Speaking OVERALL SPOKEN INTERACTION B2 Can interact with a degree of fluency and spontaneity that makes regular interaction, and sustained relationships with native speakers quite possible without imposing strain on either party. [overall spoken interaction] 3 revised by KWONG B2 Can highlight the personal significance of events and experiences, account for and sustain views clearly by providing relevant explanations and arguments. [overall spoken interaction] CONVERSATION B2 Can engage in extended conversation on most general topics in a clearly participatory fashion, even in a noisy environment. [conversation] B2 Can convey degrees of emotion and highlight the personal significance of events and experiences. [conversation] INFORMAL DISCUSSION (WITH FRIENDS) B2 Can account for and sustain his/her opinions in discussion by providing relevant explanation, arguments and comments. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP EOP Produc tion Spoken Speaking SUSTAINED MONOLOGUE: DESCRIBING EXPERIENCE B2 Can give clear, detailed description on a wide range of subjects to his/her field of interest. [sustained monologue: describing experience] Reception Communic ation Strategies IDENTIFYING CUES & INFERRING (SPOKEN & WRITTEN) B2 Can use a variety of strategies to achieve comprehension, including listening for main points, checking comprehension by using contextual clues. [identifying cues & inferring (spoken & written)] EAP Interactio n Communic ation Strategies ASKING FOR CLARIFICATION B2 Can ask follow-up questions to check that he/she has understood what a speaker intended to say, and get clarification of ambiguous points. [asking for clarification] Working with Text Communicative Language Competence NOTE-TAKING (LECTURES, SEMINARS, ETC.) B2 Can understand a clearly structured lecture on a familiar subject, and can take notes on points which strike him/her as important, even though he/she tends to concentrate on the words themselves and therefore to miss some information. [note-taking (lectures, seminars, etc.) EAP VOCABULARY RANGE B2 Has a good range of vocabulary for matters connected to his/her field and most general topics. [vocabulary range] Control GRAMMATICAL ACCURACY B2 Shows a relatively high degree of grammatical control. Does not make mistakes which lead to misunderstanding. [grammatical accuracy] 4 revised by KWONG 英文核心能力指標 University Student Core Competency Indicators 1. 英語溝通與表達能力 (ability to communicate and express oneself in English) 30% 2. 深度分析與組織思考的能力 (ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English) 10% 3. 英語學習策略與技巧 (knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques) 20% 4. 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 (global views of English and multicultural diversity) 20% 5. 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣與能力 (ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit) 20% Teaching materials and References Uniform Textbook Ken Beatty, Series Consultant, Startup 6, Peason, ISBN: 978-0-13468420-8 CEFR Scale □ B2+ ■ B2 □ B1 □ A2+ □ A2 Online Learning Platform Eeclass 數位學習平台 http://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw Requirements & Rules: Class rules: ** Respect each other mutually. ** No make-up exams will be given and no late work will be accepted unless there is an official reason with prior approval. ** Tentative Syllabus and grading scheme maybe changed to meet the students‘ need and will be announced either in class or via emails/ ilms system. ** Plagiarism / cheating is not tolerated. After having taken this course, they are expected to consolidate their knowledge of English language, build up a learning routine, and acquire more access to learning recourses. 2. Subsidiary aim In this class, students will have the opportunity to 1. review and practice grammar points and sentence structures, especially concerning verb tenses, to describe and discuss a variety of topics and issues related to their life. 2. build up theme-based vocabulary and also academic words for and through reading and listening to conversations, interviews, talks, and lectures. 3. practice academic skills such as outlining, summarizing, paraphrasing, and critical thinking while listening, reading, speaking and writing. 4. manage and present information, perspectives, or problem-solving/decision-making in speaking and writing tasks or activities. 2 3. Corresponding CEFR Can-do statements (B2) Reception Listening LISTENING TO RADIO, AUDIO & RECORDINGS B2 Can understand most radio documentaries and most other recorded or broadcast audio material delivered in standard dialect and can identify the speaker’s mood, tone, etc. [listening to radio, audio & recordings] Reception Reading OVERALL READING COMPREHENSION B2 Can read with a large degree of independence, adapting style and speed of reading to different texts and purposes, and using appropriate reference sources selectively. Has a broad active reading vocabulary, but may experience some difficulty with low-frequency vocabulary. [overall reading comprehension] READING FOR INFORMATION & ARGUMENT B2 Can understand articles and reports concerned with contemporary problems in which the writer adopts particular stances or viewpoints. [reading for information & argument] Interaction Spoken Speaking INFORMAL DISCUSSION (WITH FRIENDS) B2 Can account for and sustain his/her opinions in discussion by providing relevant explanation, arguments and comments. [informal discussion (with friends)] INFORMATION EXCHANGE B2 Can pass on detailed information reliably. [information exchange] Production Spoken Speaking OVERALL SPOKEN PRODUCTION B2 Can give clear, detailed description and presentations on a wide range of subjects related to his/her field of interest, expanding and supporting ideas with subsidiary points and relevant examples. [overall spoken production] ADDRESSING AUDIENCES B2 Can give a clear, prepared presentation, giving reasons in support of or against a particular point of view and giving the advantages and disadvantages of various options. [addressing audiences] Rece ption Communi cation IDENTIFYING CUES & INFERRING (SPOKEN & WRITTEN) B2 Can use a variety of strategies to achieve comprehension, including EAP 3 Strategies listening for main points, checking comprehension by using contextual clues. [identifying cues & inferring (spoken & written)] Interaction Communi cation Strategies COOPERATING B2 Can give feedback on and follow up statements and inferences and so help the development of the discussion. [cooperating] EAP ASKING FOR CLARIFICATION B2 Can ask follow-up questions to check that he/she has understood what a speaker intended to say, and get clarification of ambiguous points. [asking for clarification] Working with Text Communicative Language Competence NOTE-TAKING (LECTURES, SEMINARS, ETC.) B2 Can understand a clearly structured lecture on a familiar subject, and can take notes on points which strike him/her as important, even though he/she tends to concentrate on the words themselves and therefore to miss some information. [note-taking (lectures, seminars, etc.) EAP PROCESSING TEXT B2 Can summarize a wide range of factual and imaginative texts, commenting on and discussing contrasting points of view and the main themes. [processing text] EAP Communicative Language Competence Range GENERAL LINGUISTIC RANGE B2+ Can express him/herself clearly and without much sign of having to restrict what he/she wants to say. [processing text] VOCABULARY RANGE B2 Has a good range of vocabulary for matters connected to his/her field and most general topics. [vocabulary range] Control GRAMMATICAL ACCURACY B2+ Good grammatical control. Occasional “slips” or non-systematic errors and minor flaws in sentence structure may still occur, but they are rare and can often be corrected in retrospect. [grammatical accuracy] VOCABULARY CONTROL B2 Lexical accuracy is generally high, though some confusion and incorrect word choice does occur without hindering communication. [vocabulary control] ORTHOGRAPHIC CONTROL 4 B2 Can produce clearly intelligible continuous writing, which follows standard layout and paragraphing conventions. [orthographic control] EAP B2 Spelling, punctuation and layout are accurate but may show signs of mother tongue influence. [orthographic control] Sociolinguisti c SOCIOLINGUISTIC APPROPRIATENESS B2 Can with some effort keep up with and contribute to group discussions even when speech is fast and colloquial. [sociolinguistic appropriateness] Pragmatic FLEXIBILITY B2 Can adjust to the changes of direction, style and emphasis normally found in conversation. [flexibility] COHERENCE B2 Can use a limited number of cohesive devices to link his/her utterance into clear, coherent discourse, though there may be some “jumpiness” in a long contribution. [coherence] EAP Teaching Materials and References -Uniform textbook: Christina Latham-Koenig, Clive Oxenden, and Kate Chomacki. (2021) American English File 4 , 3rd Edition. Kakga ehsu@mx.nthu.edu.tw Upon request Course Aims / Description Primary aim This year-long course is designed to strengthen students’ overall academic English proficiency through integrated listening, speaking, and reading activities, complemented by grammar review and vocabulary expansion. The curriculum incorporates a four-skill coursebook alongside a self-access learning project, fostering active engagement in language learning both inside and outside the classroom. Through carefully designed tasks, students will develop effective learning strategies, gain exposure to authentic English in various contexts, and build confidence in their communication skills. By the end of the course, students are expected to consolidate their language knowledge and communicate more fluently and confidently in both everyday interactions and academic settings. 2 Subsidiary aim This course provides students with the opportunity to: 1. Review and apply essential grammar structures and sentence patterns to effectively describe and discuss a range of topics and issues relevant to their lives. 2. Develop theme-based academic vocabulary, including high-frequency academic terms, through engagement with various reading and listening materials such as conversations, interviews, lectures, and talks. 3. Enhance academic skills, including outlining, summarizing, note-taking, and critical thinking, while integrating listening, reading, speaking, and writing activities. 4. Present and articulate information, perspectives, and problem-solving approaches through structured speaking and writing tasks. 5. Foster academic English proficiency in alignment with Taiwan’s Bilingual Nation 2030 policy, equipping students with the necessary language skills to engage confidently in academic and professional settings in an increasingly bilingual environment. 3. Corresponding CEFR Can-do statements Can-do statement #1 [LISTENING] can with some effort catch much of what is said around me, but may find it difficult to understand a discussion between several speakers who do not modify their language in any way. Can-do statement #2 [READING] can understand articles, reports and reviews in which the writers express specific points of view. Can-do statement #3 [SPEAKING INTERACTION] can take an active part in conversation, expressing clearly my points of view, ideas or feelings naturally with effective turn-taking. Can-do statement #4 [SPEAKING PRODUCTION] can present a topical issue in a critical manner and weigh up the advantages and disadvantages of various options. Can-do statement #5 [WRITTEN PRODUCTION] can write at length about topical issues, even though complex concepts may be oversimplified, and can correct many of my mistakes in the process. Can-do statement #6 [STRATEGIES] can generally correct slips and errors if I become aware of them or if they have led to misunderstandings. Can-do statement #7 [QUALITY OF LANGUAGE] can link what I say or write into clear, well-organized text, though I may not always do this smoothly so there may be some “jumps.” 4. Corresponding EAP Can-do statements Listening ＊Recognising lecture structure: understanding relationships in the lecture understanding relations within the sentence/complex sentences importance markers, signposts. 3 ＊Deducing the meaning of unfamiliar words and word groups. ＊Recognizing implications: information not explicitly stated recognising the speaker's attitude. Evaluating the importance of information - selecting information. Speaking ＊Making a presentation: the structure of presentations making and using notes to speak from. ＊Introducing the topic giving the information in detail sequencing, describing similarities and differences comparing and contrasting illustrating a point - giving examples and referring to research emphasising a point summarising and concluding. ＊Controlling the discussion: leading the discussion changing the subject - moving on speeding up things coming to a conclusion. Reading ＊Understanding meaning: deducing the meaning of unfamiliar words and word groups relations within the sentence/complex sentences implications - information not explicitly stated, conceptual meaning, e.g. comparison, purpose, cause, effect. ＊Understanding relationships in the text: - text structure the communicative value of sentences relations between the parts of a text through lexical and grammatical cohesion devices and indicators in discourse. Writing ＊Using sources: making notes and writing up notes - paraphrasing, summarising, quoting & referring to sources, writing a bibliography. ＊Writing descriptions of places, objects etc classifying and categorising comparing and contrasting reporting and narrating. ＊Describing processes and developments: expressing purpose, means and method, degrees of certainty, reasons and explanations/cause and effect describing developments and changes describing a sequence of events/time relations. 英文核心能力指標 University Student Core Competency Indicators 1. 英語溝通與表達能力 20% (ability to communicate and express oneself in English) 2. 深度分析與組織思考的能力 20% (ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English) 3. 英語學習策略與技巧 20% (knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques) 4. 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 20% (global views of English and multicultural diversity) 5. 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣與能力 20% (ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit) 4 Teaching materials and References Uniform textbook Christina Latham-Koenig, Clive Oxenden, and Kate Chomacki. Attendance and participation 20% 2. Midterm exam 20% 3. Final Exam 20% 4. Assignments & quizzes 20% 5. Presentations/Role plays/Show-n-Tell 20% Note: The percentage of this grading scheme is subject to possible adjustments. To be announced. Requirements & Rules 1. Class attendance, lesson preparation and active class participation are required.  As you are all present whenever the instructor takes the roll, you will get 60% in this category Attendance and Participation. 經常性點名，全勤者可得「出席與參與」項目中的 60%成績。  Each skip will cost 2 points from the category Attendance and Participation (up to 15 points in the final grade). 未假不到課（翹課），每 次從「出席與參與」成績（占學期成績 15 分）扣 2 分。  If you are absent in case of UNCONTROLLABLE situations (e.g. illness, emergency, important occasions, etc.), please apply for a leave on the Student Leave System on Academic Information System of National Tsing Hua University or on the iNTHU app (from the Office of Student Affair website), with clear leave information, including leave type, leave period, and reasons (must be clear and valid enough for the teacher’s approval). As the reasons or the documents are not clear, valid or sufficient enough, the teacher may deny the application. 遇不可抗力情形需請假者，請於本校校務資 訊系統上的學生請假系統或下載 iNTHU APP，填寫資料（請假類別、請假日期、請假事由）。請假 事由須合理並敘述清楚，提供老師是否准假之參考。請假單上的理由或所附證明文件不清楚 或不充分時，該次請假申請得不予核准。  Please observe the information you are expected to offer for each of the following leave NTHU 學生請假 Q&A 5 types:  When requesting sick leave, please specify in the reason column the significant symptoms affecting your ability to attend class, as well as any medical consultation or medication taken. Only those who provide a doctor's certificate of diagnosis are eligible to submit makeup assignments. Medical receipts or prescription slips are not considered official proof of sick leave. 請病假時，請於理由欄位說明影響上課之顯著症狀，就醫或服藥等處 置。只有提出請假當日的醫生診斷證明者才能補交作業，就醫收據或藥單都不算病假正式證 明。  For personal leave, please describe the uncontrollable event and how it makes you absent from the class. 請事假時，請於理由欄位敘明事件，並說明該事件如何致使你無法前來上 課。  No leave application will be approved on the dates of presentations, peer evaluations, and midterm/final exams. Please care for your health and reserve the time for these important class activities. 報告、同儕互評、期中／期末考當日不得請假。請注意身心健康 並為這些重要課程活動預留時間。  There will be NO make-up exams or presentations unless you apply for leave with valid and official reasons for your absence beforehand. 無合理且正式的缺課原因，將不予補考 或補行報告。  You are expected to apply for leave before the class you are absent from. Any overdue leave application must be made within 7 days from the last day of absence. 請假已事先申請為原 則。逾期請假申請必須於 7 日內補請。未能於規定期間申請者，均以曠課論。  Being late for more than 10 minutes (with no valid excuses) is treated as absence from that hour. Being late for more than 30 minutes is treated as absence from the whole class. 無故 遲到逾 10 分鐘，以該小時未到課紀錄。遲到逾 30 分鐘，視為該次上課未到課。  No points will be deducted for your ATTENDANCE as long as your approved leave is no more than 6 hours. No late submission will be accepted or graded unless the instructor approves or grants your application for extension of submission. 作業請按時繳交（或上傳）。未獲教師同意可延遲繳 交者或超過寬限期，其遲交作業不批改、不計分。  Frequent late submissions with no valid excuses or under controllable circumstances will 6 NOT be accepted or graded since the third late assignment. 無合理原因或非為不可抗力情形 的慣性遲交作業，第三份起將不予批改與計分。 4. Plagiarism on assignments and cheating on the exam is absolutely unacceptable. If someone is found plagiarizing or cheating, it means he/she will get a zero point for that assignment or exam. 嚴禁抄襲與作弊。抄襲與作弊者，學期成績以不及格處理。情節重大時，將提報至相關單 位依校規處理。 5. AI-assisted reports and assignments are allowed in limited instances: AI can be used to prepare for reports and assignments by brainstorming and tentative revision, but students must show how AI helps them reach the result. 僅限使用生成式 AI 於作業或報告之準備（如腦力激盪與初步 修訂等），學生須註明 AI 如何用於協作其作業或報告。 6. Penalty for no or poor participation in pair or group work Students are expected to take part in pair or group activities. Failure to engage in these activities (due to you absence or lateness) will lead to reductions in grades awarded. Sometimes the reduction may be suggested by other group members; in other circumstances, the instructor may reduce the grade awarded without reference to other group members. 學生負有參與雙人 或小組活動之義務。如因個人遲到或缺席導致小組活動無法順利進行，請假或缺席者該次活動成 績將以扣分或甚至 0 分計算。 7.  Mobile devices are only used for educational purposes relevant to the subject or tasks in the classroom setting with the permission of or at the request of the instructor. Using mobile devices for studying other subjects or entertaining purposes is absolutely prohibited. Students who violate the regulation will be considered absent from the class or asked to leave the classroom. 行動裝置僅限於學習活動，使用須獲得老師同意或遵照老師指示。嚴禁 使用行動裝置研習其他課程或娛樂使用。違反規定者，以「未到課」處置，亦得請違規者離開 教室。  During class students are not to be seen with a cell phone in hand or on the desk. of persuasive, argumentative, and informative texts)  Developing sentence structures and discourse patterns for academic competence (comparing, classifying, synthesizing, evaluating, and inferring)

Students will have opportunities to learn the key components of English (pronunciation, vocabulary, and grammar) and practice language learning strategies, get exposed to English in any form (listening, reading, speaking, and even writing), and develop their confidence and fluency while they are practicing and performing various language tasks in the classroom and outside the classroom. After having taken this course, students are expected to consolidate their essential knowledge of English language and engage themselves in everyday and even authentic communication. Requirements—Students are required to prepare the designated learning activities BEFOREHAND, REGULARLY attend the class, ACTIVELY participate in classroom activities, and complete each assignment ON TIME. Aside from class participation and practices based on the textbook, students are encouraged to work on a self‐access learning project based on designated videos, reading texts, and online English-learning materials. 2 Subsidiary aim In this class, students will have opportunity to 1. develop accuracy and fluency in using key grammar structures such as question forms, Present Simple vs. Present Continuous, and Present Perfect vs. Past Simple. 2. strengthen listening and reading comprehension skills by identifying main ideas, specific information, and speakers’ attitudes in various contexts. 3. expand topic-based vocabulary and use of modifiers to describe people, routines, feelings, and life experiences more vividly. 4. build speaking fluency and interactional strategies through pair discussions, interviews, and opinion-sharing activities that simulate real-life communication. 5. enhance writing skills by composing short texts such as opinion paragraphs, routine descriptions, and personal reflections. 6. improve communicative competence by practicing follow-up questions, active listening, turn-taking, and emotional expression. 7. enhance learner autonomy and reflection through personalized speaking and writing tasks linked to students’ real lives. CEFR Can-do Statements (B1 & B1+) Reception Listening OVERALL LISTENING COMPREHENSION B1 Can understand the main points of clear standard speech on familiar matters regularly encountered in work, articulated. [overall listening comprehension] EOP B1 Can understand straightforward factual information about common everyday or job-related topics, identifying both general messages and specific details, provided speech is clearly articulated in a generally familiar accent. [overall listening comprehension] EAP/ EOP LISTENING AS A MEMBER OF A LIVE AUDIENCE B1 Can follow in outline straightforward short talks on familiar topics provided these are delivered in clearly articulated standard dialect. [listening as a member of a live audience] EAP/ EOP LISTENING TO ANNOUNCEMENTS & INSTRUCTIONS B1 Can understand simple technical information, such as operating instructions for every equipment. [listening to announcements & instructions] EAP/ EOP B1 Can follow detailed directions. [listening to announcements & instructions] LISTENING TO RADIO, AUDIO & RECORDINGS B1 Can understand the main points of radio news bulletins and simpler recorded material about familiar subjects delivered relatively slowly and clearly. [listening to radio, audio & recordings] 3 Reception Reading OVERALL READING COMPREHENSION B1 Can read straightforward factual texts on subjects related to his/her field and interest with a satisfactory level of comprehension. [overall reading comprehension] EAP/ EOP B1+ Can scan longer texts in order to locate desired information, and gather information from different parts of a text, or from different texts in order to fulfil a specific task. [reading for orientation] EAP/ EOP READING FOR INFORMATION & ARGUMENT B1 Can recognize significant points in straightforward newspaper articles on familiar subjects. [reading for information & argument] B1+ Can identify the main conclusions in clearly signaled argumentative texts. [reading for information & argument] EAP B1+ Can recognize the line of argument in the treatment of the issue presented, though not necessarily in detail. [reading for information & argument] EAP READING INSTRUCTIONS B1 Can understand clearly written, straightforward instructions for a piece of equipment. [reading instructions] EOP Interaction Spoken Speaking CONVERSATION B1 Can enter unprepared into conversations on familiar topics. [conversation] B1 Can follow clearly articulated speech directed at him/her in everyday conversation, though will sometimes have to ask for repetition of particular words and phrases. [conversation] INFORMAL DISCUSSION (WITH FRIENDS) B1 Can generally follow the main points in an informal discussion with friends provided speech is clearly articulated in standard dialect. [informal discussion (with friends)] B1 Can give or seek personal views and opinions in discussing topics of interest. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP/ EOP B1 Can make his/her opinions and reactions understood as regards solutions to problems or practical questions of where to go, what to do, how to organize an event (e.g., an outing). [informal discussion (with friends)] B1 Can express belief, opinion, agreement, and disagreement politely. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP/ EOP B1+ Can follow much of what is said around him/her on general topics provided interlocutors avoid every 4 idiomatic usage and articulate clearly. [informal discussion (with friends)] B1+ Can express his/her thoughts about abstract or cultural topics such as music, films. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP/ EOP B1+ Can explain why something is a problem. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP/ EOP B1+ Can give brief comments on the views of others. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP/ EOP B1+ Can compare and contrast alternatives, discussing what to do, where to go, who or which to choose, etc. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP/ EOP FORMAL DISCUSSION (MEETINGS) B1 Can take part in routine formal discussion of familiar subjects which is conducted in clearly articulated speech in the standard dialect and which involves the exchange of factual information, receiving instructions or the discussion of solutions to practical problems. [formal discussion (meetings)] EAP/ EOP B1+ Can follow much of what is said that is related to his/her field, provided interlocutors avoid very idiomatic usage and articulated clearly. [formal discussion (meetings)] EAP/ EOP GOAL-ORIENTED COOPERATION (E.G., REPAIRING A CAR, DISCUSSING A DOCUMENT, ORGANIZING AN EVENT) B1 Can make his/her opinions and reactions understood as regards possible solutions or the question of what to do next, giving brief reasons and explanations. [goal-oriented cooperation (e.g., repairing a car, discussing a document, organizing an event)] EAP/ EOP B1+ Can follow what is said, though he/she may occasionally has to ask for repetition or clarification if the other people’s talk is rapid or extended. [goal- oriented cooperation (e.g., repairing a car, discussing a document, organizing an event)] B1+ Can explain why something is a problem, discuss what to do next, compare and contrast alternatives. [goal-oriented cooperation (e.g., repairing a car, discussing a document, organizing an event)] EAP/ EOP B1+ Can give brief comments on the views of others. [goal-oriented cooperation (e.g., repairing a car, discussing a document, organizing an event)] INFORMATION EXCHANGE B1 Can find out and pass on straightforward factual information. [information exchange] B1+ Can exchange, check out and confirm accumulated factual information on familiar routine and non-routine matters within his/her field with some confidence. [information exchange] EAP/ EOP 5 B1+ Can describe how to do something, giving detailed instructions. B1+ Can synthesize and report information and arguments from a number of sources. [information exchange] EAP/ EOP Interaction Written Writing OVERALL WRITTEN INTERACTION B1+ Can convey information and ideas on abstract as well as concrete topics, check information and ask about or explain problems with reasonable precision. [overall written interaction] EAP/ EOP CORRESPONDENCE B1+ Can write personal letters giving news and expressing thoughts about abstract or cultural topics such as music, films. [correspondence] NOTES, MESSAGES& FORMS B1+ Can take messages communicating inquiries, explaining problems. [notes, messages & forms] Production Spoken Speaking OVERALL SPOKEN PRODUCTION B1 Can reasonably fluently sustain a straightforward description of one of a variety of subjects within his/her field of interest, presenting it as a linear sequence of points. [overall spoken production] EAP/ EOP SUSTAINED MONOLOGUE: DESCRIBING EXPERIENCE B1 Can narrate a story. [sustained monologue: describing experience] EAP SUSTAINED MONOLOGUE: PUTTING A CASE (E.G., IN A DEBATE) B1 Can briefly give reasons and explanations for opinions, plans and actions. [sustained monologue: putting a case (e.g., in a debate)] B1+ Can develop an argument well enough to be followed without difficulty most of the time. [sustained monologue: putting a case (e.g., in a debate)] EAP/ EOP PUBLIC ANNOUNCEMENTS B1 Can deliver short, rehearsed announcements on a topic pertinent to everyday occurrences in his/her field which, despite possibly very foreign stress and intonation, are nevertheless clearly intelligible. [public announcements] ADDRESSING AUDIENCES B1 Can give a prepared straightforward presentation on a familiar topic within his/her everyday life, briefly give reasons and explanations for opinions, plans and actions. [addressing audiences] P r o d u c t i o n W r i t t e n OVERALL WRITTEN PRODUCTION 6 B1 Can write straightforward connected texts on a range of familiar subjects within his field of interest, by linking a series of shorter discrete elements into a linear sequence. [overall written production] CREATIVE WRITING B1 Can write straightforward, detailed descriptions on a range of familiar subjects within his/her field of interest. [creative writing] EAP/ EOP B1 Can write a description of an event, a recent trip – real or imagined. [creative writing] B1 Can narrate a story. [creative writing] REPORTS & ESSAYS B1+ Can write short, simple essays on topics of interest. [reports & essays] EAP B1+ Can summarize, report and give his/her opinion about accumulated factual information on familiar routine and non-routine matters within his/her field with some confidence. [reports & essays] EAP Reception Communication Strategies IDENTIFYING CUES & INFERRING (SPOKEN & WRITTEN) B1 Can identify unfamiliar words from the context on topics related to his/her field and interests. [identifying cues & inferring (spoken & written)] EAP/ EOP B1 Can extrapolate the meaning of occasional unknown words from the context and deduce sentence meaning provided the topic discussed is familiar. [identifying cues & inferring (spoken & written)] Interaction Communication Strategies TAKING THE FLOOR (TURNTAKING) B1 Can initiate, maintain and close simple face-to-face conversation on topics that are familiar or of personal interest. [taking the floor (turntaking)] B1+ Can intervene in a discussion on a familiar topic, using a suitable phrase to get the floor. [taking the floor (turntaking)] COOPERATING B1+ Can summarize the point reached in a discussion and so help focus the talk. [cooperating] EAP/ EOP ASKING FOR CLARIFICATION B1+ Can ask someone to clarify or elaborate what he/she has just said. [asking for clarification] PLANNING B1 Can work out how to communicate the main point(s) he/she wants to get across, exploiting any resources available and limiting the message to what he/she can recall or find the means to express. [planning] B1+ Can rehearse and try out new combinations and expressions, inviting feedback. [planning] 7 Working with Text Communicative Language Competence NOTE-TAKING (LECTURES, SEMINARS, ETC.) B1+ Can take notes during a lecture, which are precise enough for his/her own use at a later date, provided the topic is within his/her field of interest and the talk is clear and well-structured. [note-taking (lectures, seminars, etc.) EAP PROCESSING TEXT B1 Can paraphrase short written passages in a simple fashion, using the original text wording and ordering. [processing text] EAP B1+ Can collate short pieces of information from several sources and summarize them for somebody else. [processing text] Communicative Language Competence Range GENERAL LINGUISTIC RANGE B1 Has enough language to get by, with sufficient vocabulary to express him/herself with some hesitation and circumlocutions on topics such as family, hobbies and interests, work, travel, and current events, but lexical limitations cause repetition and even difficulty with formulation at times. [processing text] VOCABULARY RANGE B1 Has a sufficient vocabulary to express him/herself with some circumlocutions on most topics pertinent to his/her everyday life such as family, hobbies and interests, work, travel, and current events. [vocabulary range] Pragmatic FLEXIBILITY B1 Can exploit a wide range of simple language flexibly to express much of what he/she wants. [flexibility] B1+ Can adapt his/her expressions to deal with less routine, even difficult situations. [flexibility] TAKING THE FLOOR (TURNTAKING) B1+ Can intervene in a discussion on a familiar topic, using a suitable phrase to get the floor. [taking the floor (turntaking)] COHERENCE B1 Can link a series of shorter, discrete simple elements into a connected, linear sequence of points. [coherence] PROPOSITIONAL PRECISION B1 Can express the main point he/she wants to make comprehensibly. [propositional precision] SPOKEN FLUENCY B1 Can keep going comprehensibly, even though pausing for grammatical and lexical planning and repair is very 8 evident, especially in longer stretches of free production. [spoken fluency] B1+ Can express him/herself with relative ease. Despite some problems with formulation resulting in pauses and “culde-sacs”, he/she is able to keep going effectively without help. [listening as a member of a live audience] EAP/ EOP LISTENING TO ANNOUNCEMENTS & INSTRUCTIONS B1 Can understand simple technical information, such as operating instructions for every equipment. [listening to announcements & instructions] EAP/ EOP B1 Can follow detailed directions. [listening to announcements & instructions] LISTENING TO RADIO, AUDIO & RECORDINGS B1 Can understand the main points of radio news bulletins and simpler recorded material about familiar subjects delivered relatively slowly and clearly. [listening to radio, audio & recordings] 3 Reception Reading OVERALL READING COMPREHENSION B1 Can read straightforward factual texts on subjects related to his/her field and interest with a satisfactory level of comprehension. [overall reading comprehension] EAP/ EOP B1+ Can scan longer texts in order to locate desired information, and gather information from different parts of a text, or from different texts in order to fulfil a specific task. [reading for orientation] EAP/ EOP READING FOR INFORMATION & ARGUMENT B1 Can recognize significant points in straightforward newspaper articles on familiar subjects. [reading for information & argument] B1+ Can identify the main conclusions in clearly signaled argumentative texts. [reading for information & argument] EAP B1+ Can recognize the line of argument in the treatment of the issue presented, though not necessarily in detail. [reading for information & argument] EAP READING INSTRUCTIONS B1 Can understand clearly written, straightforward instructions for a piece of equipment. [reading instructions] EOP Interaction Spoken Speaking CONVERSATION B1 Can enter unprepared into conversations on familiar topics. [conversation] B1 Can follow clearly articulated speech directed at him/her in everyday conversation, though will sometimes have to ask for repetition of particular words and phrases. [conversation] INFORMAL DISCUSSION (WITH FRIENDS) B1 Can generally follow the main points in an informal discussion with friends provided speech is clearly articulated in standard dialect. [informal discussion (with friends)] B1 Can give or seek personal views and opinions in discussing topics of interest. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP/ EOP B1 Can make his/her opinions and reactions understood as regards solutions to problems or practical questions of where to go, what to do, how to organize an event (e.g., an outing). [informal discussion (with friends)] B1 Can express belief, opinion, agreement, and disagreement politely. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP/ EOP B1+ Can follow much of what is said around him/her on general topics provided interlocutors avoid every 4 idiomatic usage and articulate clearly. [informal discussion (with friends)] B1+ Can express his/her thoughts about abstract or cultural topics such as music, films. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP/ EOP B1+ Can explain why something is a problem. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP/ EOP B1+ Can give brief comments on the views of others. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP/ EOP B1+ Can compare and contrast alternatives, discussing what to do, where to go, who or which to choose, etc. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP/ EOP FORMAL DISCUSSION (MEETINGS) B1 Can take part in routine formal discussion of familiar subjects which is conducted in clearly articulated speech in the standard dialect and which involves the exchange of factual information, receiving instructions or the discussion of solutions to practical problems. [formal discussion (meetings)] EAP/ EOP B1+ Can follow much of what is said that is related to his/her field, provided interlocutors avoid very idiomatic usage and articulated clearly. [formal discussion (meetings)] EAP/ EOP GOAL-ORIENTED COOPERATION (E.G., REPAIRING A CAR, DISCUSSING A DOCUMENT, ORGANIZING AN EVENT) B1 Can make his/her opinions and reactions understood as regards possible solutions or the question of what to do next, giving brief reasons and explanations. [goal-oriented cooperation (e.g., repairing a car, discussing a document, organizing an event)] EAP/ EOP B1+ Can follow what is said, though he/she may occasionally has to ask for repetition or clarification if the other people’s talk is rapid or extended. [goal- oriented cooperation (e.g., repairing a car, discussing a document, organizing an event)] B1+ Can explain why something is a problem, discuss what to do next, compare and contrast alternatives. [goal-oriented cooperation (e.g., repairing a car, discussing a document, organizing an event)] EAP/ EOP B1+ Can give brief comments on the views of others. [goal-oriented cooperation (e.g., repairing a car, discussing a document, organizing an event)] INFORMATION EXCHANGE B1 Can find out and pass on straightforward factual information. [information exchange] B1+ Can exchange, check out and confirm accumulated factual information on familiar routine and non-routine matters within his/her field with some confidence. [information exchange] EAP/ EOP 5 B1+ Can describe how to do something, giving detailed instructions. B1+ Can synthesize and report information and arguments from a number of sources. [information exchange] EAP/ EOP Interaction Written Writing OVERALL WRITTEN INTERACTION B1+ Can convey information and ideas on abstract as well as concrete topics, check information and ask about or explain problems with reasonable precision. [overall written interaction] EAP/ EOP CORRESPONDENCE B1+ Can write personal letters giving news and expressing thoughts about abstract or cultural topics such as music, films. [correspondence] NOTES, MESSAGES& FORMS B1+ Can take messages communicating inquiries, explaining problems. [notes, messages & forms] Production Spoken Speaking OVERALL SPOKEN PRODUCTION B1 Can reasonably fluently sustain a straightforward description of one of a variety of subjects within his/her field of interest, presenting it as a linear sequence of points. [overall spoken production] EAP/ EOP SUSTAINED MONOLOGUE: DESCRIBING EXPERIENCE B1 Can narrate a story. [sustained monologue: describing experience] EAP SUSTAINED MONOLOGUE: PUTTING A CASE (E.G., IN A DEBATE) B1 Can briefly give reasons and explanations for opinions, plans and actions. [sustained monologue: putting a case (e.g., in a debate)] B1+ Can develop an argument well enough to be followed without difficulty most of the time. [sustained monologue: putting a case (e.g., in a debate)] EAP/ EOP PUBLIC ANNOUNCEMENTS B1 Can deliver short, rehearsed announcements on a topic pertinent to everyday occurrences in his/her field which, despite possibly very foreign stress and intonation, are nevertheless clearly intelligible. [public announcements] ADDRESSING AUDIENCES B1 Can give a prepared straightforward presentation on a familiar topic within his/her everyday life, briefly give reasons and explanations for opinions, plans and actions. [addressing audiences] P r o d u c t i o n W r i t t e n OVERALL WRITTEN PRODUCTION 6 B1 Can write straightforward connected texts on a range of familiar subjects within his field of interest, by linking a series of shorter discrete elements into a linear sequence. [overall written production] CREATIVE WRITING B1 Can write straightforward, detailed descriptions on a range of familiar subjects within his/her field of interest. [creative writing] EAP/ EOP B1 Can write a description of an event, a recent trip – real or imagined. [creative writing] B1 Can narrate a story. [creative writing] REPORTS & ESSAYS B1+ Can write short, simple essays on topics of interest. [processing text] EAP B1+ Can collate short pieces of information from several sources and summarize them for somebody else. [processing text] VOCABULARY RANGE B1 Has a sufficient vocabulary to express him/herself with some circumlocutions on most topics pertinent to his/her everyday life such as family, hobbies and interests, work, travel, and current events. A four-skill coursebook plus a self‐access learning project will be integrated to design learning tasks and provide opportunities for students to practice language learning strategies, get exposed to English in any form, and develop their confidence and fluency in the classroom and outside the classroom. After having taken this course, students are expected to consolidate their knowledge of English language and engage themselves more confidently and fluently in authentic communication in everyday settings and even in academic settings. Subsidiary aim In this class, students will have opportunities to 1. review and practice grammar points and sentence structures to describe and discuss a variety of topics and issues related to their life. 2. build up theme-based vocabulary and even academic words for and through reading and listening to conversations, interviews, talks, and lectures. 3. practice academic skills such as outlining, summarizing, note-taking, and critical thinking while listening, reading, speaking, and writing. 2 4. present and explain information, perspectives, or problem-solving in speaking and writing tasks or activities. A four-skill coursebook plus a self‐access learning project will be integrated to design learning tasks and provide opportunities for students to practice language learning strategies, get exposed to English in any form, and develop their confidence and fluency in the classroom and outside the classroom. After having taken this course, students are expected to consolidate their knowledge of English language and engage themselves more confidently and fluently in authentic communication in everyday settings and even in academic settings. Subsidiary aim In this class, students will have opportunities to 1. review and practice grammar points and sentence structures to describe and discuss a variety of topics and issues related to their life. 2. build up theme-based vocabulary and even academic words for and through reading and listening to conversations, interviews, talks, and lectures. 3. practice academic skills such as outlining, summarizing, note-taking, and critical thinking while listening, reading, speaking, and writing. 2 4. present and explain information, perspectives, or problem-solving in speaking and writing tasks or activities. Your personal scheduling or preference of taking courses during your college stay will NOT be a valid excuse for the teacher to take your request for extra course registration into account. 停修條件 The student’s application for course withdrawal will NOT be approved if 1. The student never attends class nor submits assignments. 2. The student is absent or asks for leave with NO valid excuses for more than 6 classes. 3. The student never explains to or discusses with the teacher his/her difficulty in taking care of this subject. 4. The student neither offers valid excuses on his application for course withdrawal nor notifies the teacher beforehand. 學生如遇有以下情形，其停修申請將不予「同意」 1. 學生未曾到課或繳交任何作業。 2 2. 學生無故缺席或未有證明之請假超過六次 3. 學生從未向老師解釋、或與之討論，修讀本課程時的困難 4. 學生未在停修申請上敘明或以其他通訊方式告知老師停修本課程之原 因 避免學生規避「低修」學分數而選課，或以其他理由選課但不上課等情事 提醒：請於選課前參考課程大綱，了解評分方式、各週進度。並於第一堂課進一 步了解作業、報告、考試的規劃與所需處理時間。評估自已的學習量能，避免修 課失衡。 Instructor & Contact Information: Name Email 林鈺凢 yufanlin@gapp.nthu.edu.tw Course Aims / Description3 Primary aim This one-year course is designed to enhance students’ overall English competence through listening, speaking, reading and writing. The course will be conducted mainly based on the designated textbook; diverse activities will also be integrated into class to build students’ vocabulary bank, strengthen the knowledge of grammar patterns and English learning strategies. Students are given the opportunity to use English in a friendly learning context for developing their confidence and fluency in and outside the classroom. Besides, group discussions and presentations are held to help students gain practical knowledge of daily English, such as organizing travel plan, giving a small talk about specific topic, and express opinions clearly while having group discussions. After taking this course, students are expected to be equipped with the knowledge of English language and engage themselves more actively and confidently in authentic conversations and activities at school and even in everyday settings. Subsidiary aim In this class, students will be given the opportunity to 1. Identify and apply the vocabulary words in certain contexts through reading essays, listening to short dialogues and discussions in class. 2. Review and practice the grammar patterns, sentence structures, and language skills to have conversations in a variety of topics with peers and instructors. 3. Use problem-solving skills and independent thinking skills to answer and ask questions raised by the instructors and peers in class. 4. Build up a learning networking with peers with different expertise in order to get them exposed to different possibilities of English applications. 3 Corresponding CEFR Can-do statements 1. [Listening] Can understand phrases and expressions related to areas of most immediate priority (e.g., very basic personal and family information, shopping, local geography, employment) provided speech is clearly and slowly articulated. [overall listening comprehension] 2. [Listening] Can generally identify the topic of discussion around him/her that is conducted slowly and clearly. [understanding interaction between native speakers] 3. [Speaking] Can agree and disagree with others. 4. [Writing] Can write short, simple notes and messages relating to matters in areas of immediate need. [notes, messages & forms] 5. [Speaking] Can describe everyday aspects of his/her environment e.g., people, places, a job or study experience. [sustained monologue: describing experience] 6. [Interaction] Can ask very simply for repetition when he/she does not understand. [asking for clarification] 7. [Sociolinguistic] Can handle very short social exchanges, using everyday polite forms of greeting and address. [sociolinguistic appropriateness] 英文核心能力指標 University Student Core Competency Indicators 1. 英語溝通與表達能力 (ability to communicate and express oneself in English) 2. 深度分析與組織思考的能力 (ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English) 3. 英語學習策略與技巧 (knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques) 4. 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 (global views of English and multicultural diversity) 5. 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣與能力 (ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit) 4 Teaching Materials and References Textbook(s) Christina Latham-Koenig, Clive Oxenden, and Jerry Lambert. (2021). American English File 2, 3rd Edition. New York: Oxford University Press. ISBN: 978-0-19- 490639-5 CEFR Scale A2 A2+ □ B1 □ B1-B2 □ B2 □ B2+ □ C1 Learning/Resource Platform Techers may upload the teaching materials such as audio files, lecture slides, assignments, quizzes, and supplementary materials to NTHU designated learning platforms (eeclass). Textbook(s) CEFR Scale g A2 □ A2-B1 □ B1 □ B1-B2 □ B2 □ B2+ Grading Scheme 1. Attendance and participation 出席及參與 15% 2. Midterm exam (Role-play) 期中考 20% 3. Final Exam 期末考 20% 4. Quizzes (in-class or online quizzes) 小考 10% 5. Assignments & Tasks (Learning Portfolio, In-class note-taking, peer assessment, in- class group or individual demonstration, preview or review assignments) 各項作業及任務 15% 6. Group Presentation 小組口頭報告 20% Requirements & Rules: 1. Class attendance, lesson preparation and active class participation are required. ü The instructor takes attendance every week at 08:10 throughout the semester. If you are all present whenever the instructor takes the roll, you will get 40 points(i.e. the primitive score) in this category (i.e. attendance & participation). *The other 60 points will be given based on how passionate, active and interactive you are in class and the contributions you make to the class. 每次上課 08:10 點名，皆無缺席可於第一類別原始分數得到 40 分，另 60 分為課堂活動參與，依 是否積極於課堂與同學互動並參與討論且完成交派任務而定，兩項目合計佔總成績 20％。(見下 方星號標記處) ü If you are absent for one class hour (2 class hour a week), 5 points from the primitive score will be deducted, 10 points deducted for 2 class hour. 缺席一節課扣原始成績 5 分（一週共兩節），意指兩節課共扣原始成績 10 分。 5 About Participation: ü Missing a 2-hour session means missing essential interactive assessments, which will result in a deduction of up to 15 points of your total participation grade (i.e. 60 points). 缺席則意味著：當日無法參與課堂討論及活動，缺乏實際使用英文的練習，影響學習目標的達 成，將直接影響參與分數。如：缺席兩堂課 (一週以兩堂計)，*參與項目的原始分數將最高扣至 15 分（參與滿分 60 分）。 ü Second language proficiency is acquired through live participation and spontaneous interaction. Please be advised that missed in-class evaluations are non-reproducible and cannot be made up through written work. 英語學習各方面訓練必須透過持續的課堂實踐來驗證，無法單純以書面作業或其他報告方式替 代。請同學選課前務必評估本學期之時間規劃，及各方面狀態（事假/公假等可事先規劃或避開 的部分）確保能完整參與課堂活動。若選擇加入這門課，請務必確保本學期能夠分配足夠的學 習時間予本課程。 ü This course features various in-class activities, in which you need to be present and actively collaborate with your teammates. Therefore, if you are unfortunately unable to attend for 6 class hours, please discuss it with your instructor, Candy, in advance. Otherwise,you cannot get the points of “attendance and participation” for six hours or more of absence. 本課程強調高度參與。若累積請假或缺席達 6 小時(總上課時數的 1/4)，由於錯過核心教學環節 過多，將無法取得出席及參與之分數。同時，建議學生考慮辦理停修，以免影響最終成績評 定。 Being late for the class: ü Being late than 08:10 is treated as absence from that class hour (5 points will be deducted). 08:10 後進教室，當節課視同缺席，扣 5 分， -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 2. Students Leave System ü If you are absent in case of uncontrollable situations (e.g. illness, emergency, important occasions, etc.), please apply for a leave on the Student Leave System on Academic Information System of National Tsing Hua University or on the iNTHU app (from the Office of Student Affair website), with clear leave information, including leave type, leave period, and reasons (must be clear and valid enough for the teacher’s approval). As the reasons or the documents are not clear, valid or sufficient enough, the teacher may deny the application. 遇不可抗力情形需請假者，請於本校校務資訊系統上的學生請假系統或下載 iNTHU APP，填寫資 料（請假類別、請假日期、請假事由）。請假事由須合理並敘述清楚，提供老師是否准假之參 考。請假單上的理由或所附證明文件不清楚或不充分時，該次請假申請得不予核准。 ü Please observe the information you are expected to offer for each of the following leave type: n For sick leave, please describe severe symptoms and medical treatments you have been taking in the box “Reason.” 請病假時，於理由欄位說明影響上課之顯著症狀，就醫或服藥等處 6 理。 n For personal leave, please describe the uncontrollable event and how it makes you absent from the class. 請事假時，請於理由欄位敘明事件，並說明該事件如何致使你無法前來上課。 n No leave application will be approved on the dates of presentations, peer evaluations, and midterm/final exams. Please care for your health and reserve the time for these important class activities. 報告、同儕互評、期中／期末考當日不得請假。請注意身心健康並為這些重要 課程活動預留時間。 n There will be NO make-up exams or presentations unless you apply for leave with valid and official reasons for your absence beforehand. 無事先提出合理且正式的請假原因，將不予補 考或補行報告。 ü The instructor values the attitude toward English learning far more than the result of each assignment and presentation. The result alone does not necessarily contribute to your growth in language learning. Please do not take advantage of those who are generous in your life, your instructor included. 這門課程更重視大家於課堂中的積極參與及整個學期的學習態度，儘管作業及報告很重要，拿 到好的成果並不代表你獲得了所需具備的技能。要怎麼收穫，先怎麼栽。學校是一個可以讓你 不害怕犯錯的地方，但也請愛惜這些願意與時俱進，寬容調整規定的師長。為自己的選擇負起 責任並尊重與你一起上課的同學及老師，讓我們一起努力建立良好的學習環境。 2. Absence from a class is no excuse for not submitting assignments by the deadline or ignoring assignments or the class you have missed. You need to practice taking the responsibility to ask your classmates or the instructor what has been covered in the class. (No email permitted) 缺席或請假不可作為遲交作業及不了解課堂相關宣布事項的理由，主動詢問同儕或是親自於課堂時 間詢問授課老師相關細節是學生應負起的責任。(不受理 email 詢問課堂內容，課程相關資訊請上 eeclass 查詢) ² As for your assigned midterm, final exam, and important presentations, there is no repetitive reminder from your instructor, it is the student who must take the responsibility for remembering all the scheduled assignments. (When there’s a rescheduled assignment, ensure that you mark it on your calendar). 於期初預排的行程(包含期中、期末考時間以及各項課堂活動及作業繳交時間)請務必自行記 錄，老師不再反覆提醒，學生負起紀錄課堂重要事宜的責任。學期間若有時間的更動，請務必 於課堂中仔細留意並更改自己的行事曆。 4. There will be NO make-up exams or presentations unless you notify the instructor valid and official reasons for your absence beforehand. If a group presentation is “crippled” due to your lateness or absence, you will receive no grade on the presentation. 不接受補考或補報告，除非提早與老師討論所遇困難，若為合理的緣由，必須提出相關證明並以不 違反課堂評分要求的方式與老師擬定出可行的解決方式。若小組報告因為你遲到或是缺席而表現不 佳，你個人將無法獲得該項目的分數。 5. Assignments are expected to be completed and submitted by the deadline. No late submission 7 will be accepted or graded unless the instructor approves your application of late submission. NO full credit for late submission/Penalty for late submission: 10% of the total mark awarded will be deducted for each working day after the submission date. 作業一旦缺交，將依照下方表格扣分處置，超過表格規定時間繳交不予受理，以零分計。 ＊ AI is only allowed in limited instances: AI is only accepted when you see it as a reference but not an assignment generator. You can use it for brainstorming, but your reports at the end should be organized with your own effort. If you copy and paste the ideas directly from AI without specification, your submission of assignment will be considered invalid. ü Plagiarism on assignments and cheating on the exam are unacceptable. If someone is found plagiarizing or cheating, it means he/she will get zero point for that assignment or exam. 一旦發現抄襲或是作弊行為，該項作業或是考試以零分計。 Late Submission Mark Awarded After Penalty Number of days late Penalty Original grade 90 Original grade 60 1 10% 81 54 2 20% 72 48 3 30% 63 42 4 40% 54 36 5 50% 45 30 More than 5 days Not completed and grade of zero awarded 6. Penalty for no or poor participation in group work Students are expected to take part in various group work activities. Failure to engage with these activities may lead to reductions in grades awarded. Sometimes the reduction may be suggested by other group members, in other circumstances the academic in charge may reduce the grade awarded without reference to other group members. 7. Mobile devices are only used for educational purposes relevant to the subject or tasks in the classroom setting with the permission of or at the request of the instructor. During class, students are not to be seen with a cell phone in hand. Mobile phones are expected to be turned off or switched to a silent mode. 8. The syllabus, handouts, returned assignments should be kept at least to the end of this semester for later reference or the final exam. Besides, group discussions and presentations are held to help students gain practical knowledge of daily English, such as organizing travel plan, giving a small talk about specific topic, and express opinions clearly while having group discussions. After taking this course, students are expected to be equipped with the knowledge of English language and engage themselves more actively and confidently in authentic conversations and activities at school and even in everyday settings. Subsidiary aim In this class, students will be given the opportunity to 1. Identify and apply the vocabulary words in certain contexts through reading essays, listening to short dialogues and discussions in class. 2. Review and practice the grammar patterns, sentence structures, and language skills to have conversations in a variety of topics with peers and instructors. 3. Use problem-solving skills and independent thinking skills to answer and ask questions raised by the instructors and peers in class. 4. Build up a learning networking with peers with different expertise in order to get them exposed to different possibilities of English applications. 3 Corresponding CEFR Can-do statements 1. [Listening] Can understand phrases and expressions related to areas of most immediate priority (e.g., very basic personal and family information, shopping, local geography, employment) provided speech is clearly and slowly articulated. [overall listening comprehension] 2. [Listening] Can generally identify the topic of discussion around him/her that is conducted slowly and clearly. [understanding interaction between native speakers] 3. [Speaking] Can agree and disagree with others. 4. [Interaction] Can ask very simply for repetition when he/she does not understand. [asking for clarification] 7. [Sociolinguistic] Can handle very short social exchanges, using everyday polite forms of greeting and address. This subject will cover a series of skills: a. review the fundamental notions of English grammar; b. to understand situational English about different topics; c. to use appropriate lexeme and essential collocations in context to express idea and communicate with each other naturally. Learners will be guided by the instructor to build up English fluency in the uses of words and expressions as well as the application of grammar. Audio and visual learning materials that relate to the theme of each unit will also be provided to diversify learning resources. Through the course, learners will be able to see improvements in the four skills - listening, reading, speaking and writing.. Subsidiary aim In this course students will have opportunities to 1. comprehend exact meanings of vocabulary in written and spoken contexts as well as enlarge its storage by working on skills of prefixes, suffixes roots and word families. 2. Develop proficiency in academic English by exploring synonyms, antonyms, theme-based words and phrases and collocation in assigned readings. 3. Facilitate students with grammatical notions by highlighting its applications in spoken and written texts. 4. Assign speaking and listening tasks to students to practice conversation or dialogue, listening dictation, pair discussion and everyday talk. 5. Enhance students’ reading efficiency and speed by featuring the identification of main ideas, topic sentences and supporting details. Corresponding CEFR Can-do 1. Students are required to prepare the designated passages BEFORE class, ACTIVELY participate in class discussions and complete exercise sections ON TIME. Listening input: A variety of authentic English-speaking contexts, including university lectures, interviews, podcasts, and classroom discussions not only activate students’ background knowledge of the topic, prime them for the authentic and inspirational content they will meet in the thought-provoking TED Talks, but also guide them systematically through strategies and activities to meet future academic, personal or professional goals. Specific and key academic skills are focused in each theme-based unit, where students effectively learn to predict, identify main ideas/details/inferences, take notes and manage lengthy input. Pronunciation is also highlighted as an aid to improving both listening comprehension & speaking fluency. Speaking output: Presentation skills inspired by the TED speakers give students the techniques & authentic language they need to successfully deliver their own presentations, help them gain the opportunity to personalize the language they learn, and build their confidence in expressing ideas and opinions. Visual/digital literacy will be promoted through lots of infographics and speaking activities designed to involve students working with a partner or in a group. With connected ideas and integrated language skills, students will give individual, pair and group projects/presentation regularly throughout the semester. The ultimate goals of the course are to encourage students to take charge of their learning and to facilitate their essential 21st century skills—collaboration, communication and critical thinking. Through extensive reading, students will develop the ability to quickly and accurately grasp the main ideas and key points of texts, while expanding their vocabulary and reading techniques across various fields. Intensive reading activities will further enable students to understand both concrete and abstract meanings 2 Prepared by Man-Ting Huang (黃滿庭) in texts, discuss and analyze the author’s intent, engage in critical thinking, and connect topics to real-world contexts.  Upon completing the course, students will be able to:  Read and comprehend texts at a high-intermediate level, using strategies for both extensive and intensive reading. (EAP)  Identify and understand the main ideas and specific details of various texts efficiently and accurately. (EAP)  Expand and retain knowledge of content-specific vocabulary, collocations, synonyms, antonyms, and phrasal verbs for academic and professional contexts. (EAP)  Develop critical thinking skills by evaluating an author's purpose, tone, and bias, and forming well- supported opinions about the text. (EAP)  Utilize effective study skills, such as note-taking and summarizing, to support academic success. (EAP)  Interpret and integrate information from charts, illustrations, and photographs, alongside textual content. (EAP)  Engage with texts beyond surface-level understanding by forming independent ideas and opinions about key topics. (EAP)  Develop foundational academic writing skills, such as crafting clear, concise paragraphs and organizing ideals logically for academic assignments. Through extensive reading, students will develop the ability to quickly and accurately grasp the main ideas and key points of texts, while expanding their vocabulary and reading techniques across various fields. Intensive reading activities will further enable students to understand both concrete and abstract meanings in texts, discuss and analyze the author’s intent, engage in critical thinking, and connect topics to real-world contexts. Upon completing the course, students will be able to: ✓ Read and comprehend texts at a high-intermediate level, using strategies for both extensive and intensive reading. (EAP) ✓ Identify and understand the main ideas and specific details of various texts efficiently and accurately. (EAP) Prepared by Jennifer Liu 2 ✓ Expand and retain knowledge of content-specific vocabulary, collocations, synonyms, antonyms, and phrasal verbs for academic and professional contexts. (EAP) ✓ Develop critical thinking skills by evaluating an author’s purpose, tone, and bias, and forming well-supported opinions about the text. (EAP) ✓ Utilize effective study skills, such as note-taking and summarizing, to support academic success. (EAP) ✓ Interpret and integrate information from charts, illustrations, and photographs, alongside textual content. (EAP) ✓ Engage with texts beyond surface-level understanding by forming independent ideas and opinions about key topics. (EAP) ✓ Develop foundational academic writing skills, such as crafting clear, concise paragraphs and organizing ideals logically for academic assignments. (EAP) Course Goals: ⚫ This course aims to enhance students’ academic reading ability with useful reading strategies. The designated textbook provides academic readings materials to consolidate comprehension across different fields. Students are guided from a great variety of reading passages so as to be familiar with contextualized vocabulary and various aspects toward issues. After input from all types of reading materials, students are encouraged to express opinions on related issues with the practice on presentation skills. Course Descriptions: ⚫ Lecture, as well as group discussion, presentation, and language activities will help students get prepared for daily and academic reading tasks. Note-taking skills, vocabulary, and reading skills are designed to improve students’ reading ability, while discussion, debate, and presentation would train student’s academic communication.
