Liu) wenchenl2013@gmail.com 綜二 210 Friday 1:30 pm-3:30 pm (By Appointment) COURSE GOALS & DESCRIPTION This two-credit semester course, High-Intermediate English Reading III, is designed to help first-year college students at a high-intermediate level strengthen and enhance their English reading skills. Through extensive reading, students will develop the ability to quickly and accurately grasp the main ideas and key points of texts, while expanding their vocabulary and reading techniques across various fields. Intensive reading activities will further enable students to understand both concrete and abstract meanings in texts, discuss and analyze the author’s intent, engage in critical thinking, and connect topics to real-world contexts. Class activities include lectures, group discussions, pair practice, and presentations. Upon completing the course, students will be able to: ✓ Read and comprehend texts at a high-intermediate level, using strategies for both extensive and intensive reading. (EAP) ✓ Identify and understand the main ideas and specific details of various texts efficiently and accurately. (EAP) ✓ Expand and retain knowledge of content-specific vocabulary, collocations, synonyms, antonyms, and phrasal verbs for academic and professional contexts. (EAP) ✓ Develop critical thinking skills by evaluating an author’s purpose, tone, and bias, and forming well- supported opinions about the text. (EAP) ✓ Utilize effective study skills, such as note-taking and summarizing, to support academic success. (EAP) ✓ Interpret and integrate information from charts, illustrations, and photographs, alongside textual content. (EAP) ✓ Engage with texts beyond surface-level understanding by forming independent ideas and opinions about key topics. (EAP) 2 UNIVERSITY STUDENT CORE COMPETENCY INDICATORS 課程核心能力 1. The ability to communicate and express oneself in English 英語溝通與表達能力 25% 2. The ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English 深度分析與組織思考能力 25% 3. The knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques 英語學習策略與技巧 25% 4. Global views of English and multicultural diversity 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 10% 5. The ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣能力 15% UNIFORM TEXTBOOK Vargo, M., Blass, L. & Sherman K. (2025). Pathways: Reading, Writing, and Critical Thinking 4 (3rd Edition). National Geographic Learning. ISBN: 9780357980101 CEFR Scale ■ C1 □ B2 □ B1 □ A2+ □ A2 E-LEARN PLATFORM https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw RECOMMENDED ONLINE DICTIONARIES 1. Longman Dictionary of Contemporary English Online https://www.ldoceonline.com/ 2. Cambridge Dictionary https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/ 3. The Free Dictionary http://www.thefreedictionary.com/ REGULATIONS FOR USING AI (AI 使用原則) Students are not allowed to use AI or machine-translation tools, including Google Translate, to generate or translate answers or assignments. This prohibition applies to questions and answers about the presentation article titles, presentation transcripts, and in-class worksheets. However, students may use AI to proofread or revise work that they have written independently in English. When using AI for proofreading or revision, students must submit their original version, the AI revised version, and a list of lessons or insights they gained by comparing the two versions. GRADING 1. Attendance and Participation – 15% 2. Pair Article Presentation – 15 % 3. Quizzes – 20 % 4. In-Class Tasks/ Worksheets – 15 % 5. Assignments – 5% 6. Uniform Final Exam – 30% 3 Class Participation/ Attendance Students are expected to attend each class punctually and actively participate in pair, group, and class discussions. If you cannot attend, you must (1) email the teacher and (2) apply for leave through the university’s online system. For further information, please refer to the following: • Student Leave Policies: https://sa.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/406-1480-264831,r7918.php?Lang=zh-tw • Student Leave Guidelines: https://sa.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/406-1480-269011,r7918.php?Lang=zh-tw • Related Document Downloads: https://sa.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/412-1480-21552.php?Lang=zh-tw Important rules for this course: 1. For sick or personal leave, you must provide valid supporting documentation. ▪ For sick leave, a medical receipt or certificate is required. 2. To arrange a make-up quiz, presentation, or final examination, you must provide official supporting documentation. ▪ Traveling or taking a driver’s license test is not considered an acceptable reason. 3. If your leave request is not approved, it will be counted as an absence. 4. An absence from class is not an excuse for being unaware of assignments, announcements, or material covered in class. It is your responsibility to ask your classmates what you missed and find out what assignments or preparation are required for the next class. Attendance, punctuality, and class participation will be recorded and included in your course evaluation. Attendance will be recording beginning in the first week, so please make sure that you attend the first class and arrive on time. Attendance Policy ➢ Starting score: 9 (起始點: 9 分) ➢ Late arrival: -2 (遲到: 2 分) ➢ Absence: -10 (缺席: 10 分) ➢ Irrelevant activities in class: -2 (做課堂不相關的事: 2 分) The starting attendance score is 9 points. Each late arrival deducts 2 points. Each absence deducts 10 points. Engaging in irrelevant activities in class deducts 2 points. (This includes using a phone for non-class- related activities or working on assignments for other courses.) The score has no lower limit but a maximum of 20 points. In other words, a negative attendance score will lower your semester grade, while a high attendance score can earn you up to 5 extra points towards your semester grade. 出席成績從 9 分開始計算，並依以下規則增減：每次遲到扣 2 分，缺席扣 10 分。若在課堂上從事無關活動 （如使用手機處理與課程無關的事務或做其他課程作業），則扣 2 分。分數累積上限為 20 分，無下限。換 言之，若出席成績為負分，將併入學期成績計算；若累積達 20 分，則學期成績額外加 5 分。 All these seemingly complicated and trivial calculations for attendance and class participation are designed to encourage you to speak more English and participate more actively in class. The more you engage in each class, the more harvest you’ll reap from this course. 4 PAIR ARTICLE PRESENTATION Students will choose an article from the course packet and deliver a 10-minute pair presentation in class. Sign-ups must be completed by the third week, and the presentation schedule will be announced afterward. To fulfill this course requirement, students must: • Begin preparation at least two weeks in advance • Meet all deadlines • Memorize their speeches • Rehearse thoroughly (For further details, see Appendices I & II) IN-CLASS TASKS/WORKSHEETS Each class includes pair or group tasks and discussions, and all students are required to participate actively. At the end of each session, the instructor will collect the worksheets. Four or five will be randomly selected for grading. A group-member evaluation may occasionally be administered after a group task. Students will evaluate each member’s contribution to the task. If a student receives an average peer-evaluation score below 6 out of 10, the instructor will review the student’s contribution to the group task based on the peer evaluations, written comments, completed work, and classroom observations. If insufficient participation is confirmed, the student’s individual worksheet score may be reduced or, in cases of non-participation, recorded as 0. • If you are absent, the worksheet score will be 0. • Late submissions will not be accepted. ASSIGNMENTS All assignments must be typed and turned in on time. Late assignments will not be graded. QUIZZES Two quizzes, as scheduled in the course outline, will test students on both vocabulary and the content of the textbook articles as well as articles presented by classmates. Pop quizzes may also be given before student presentations; these will count for 1/4 of the total 20 % quiz grade. UNIFORM FINAL EXAM The uniform final exam (30% of the semester grade) will take place in the regular classroom at the usual class meeting time in Week 16. It will cover four units of the textbook: Units 1, 4, 6, and 8. Units 1, 4, and 8 will be taught in class, while Unit 6 must be studied independently by students. COPY FEE A copy fee of NT$70-100 will be collected once during the semester to cover the course packet, test sheets and handouts. 5 SUGGESTIONS FOR SUCCESS IN THIS COURSE To get the most out of this course, you are advised to: 1. Attend every class and arrive on time. 2. Volunteer to speak and participate actively in pair, group, and whole-class discussions. 3. Preview the course materials before class. 4. Learn and review new vocabulary every day, and apply what you have learned. 5. Submit assignments, worksheets, and presentation materials by the stated deadlines. Upload electronic files to eeclass and submit printed copies in class when required. o Electronic files allow the instructor to review your work for compliance with the course AI policy. o Printed copies will be used for reading, grading, and providing feedback in order to reduce the instructor’s screen time and eye strain. 6. Please feel free to ask questions whenever you have them. 7. If you have been putting considerable time and effort into the course but still feel that you are falling behind, please reach out to Jennifer for assistance. COURSE SCHEDULE Week Date Main Topic Reading Strategies Critical Thinking 1. 9/7 Course Introduction & Orientation Introduction to the BEST Test of English Proficiency* 2. 9/14 Unit 1 The Changing Workplace Introduction to the BEST Reading Test* ✓ Identifying main ideas and key details (EAP) 3. 9/21 Unit 1 The Changing Workplace Introduction to the BEST Writing Test*  Recognizing claims and counterclaims (EAP) 4. 9/28 No Class (Teacher’s Day) Watch a video lesson on Unit 1 The Changing Workplace ✓ Understanding cohesion (EAP) 5. 10/5 Unit 1 The Changing Workplace  Summarizing a text (EAP) 6. 10/12 Unit 4 Rethinking Transport Recognizing and evaluating different viewpoints (EAP) 7. 10/19 Quiz#1 8. 10/26 No Class (Taiwan Restoration Day) Watch a video lesson on Unit 4 Rethinking Transport ✓ Using a concept map (EAP) 6 9. 11/2 Unit 4 Rethinking Transport ✓ Understanding complex sentences (EAP)  Inferring meaning (EAP) 10. 11/9 Unit 4 Rethinking Transport  Comparing and contrasting two perspectives (EAP) 11. 11/16 Unit 8 Living Longer ✓ Reading extended texts (EAP) 12. 11/23 Unit 8 Living Longer ✓ Asking questions as you read (EAP) 13. 11/30 Quiz#2 14. 12/7 Unit 8 Living Longer ✓ Understanding supporting examples (EAP)  Interpreting visual data (EAP) 15. 12/14 Unit 8 Living Longer  Synthesizing (EAP) 16. 12/21 Uniform Final Exam (原班級教室與上課時間考試) Note: Unit 6, “Why Language Matters,” is designated as a self-learning unit for students. 7 Appendix I: Pair Article Presentation Guidelines Students will choose an article from the course packet and deliver a 10-minute pair presentation in class without using PowerPoint slides. Sign-ups must be completed by Week 3, and the presentation schedule will be announced afterward. To fulfill this requirement, begin preparing at least two weeks in advance, meet all deadlines, memorize your speech, and rehearse thoroughly. I. Two Weeks Before the Presentation Day a) Confirm the article you will present. b) Meet with your partner and divide the work evenly. c) Read the article carefully at least once. d) Post your questions about the article’s title, together with your answers, on eeclass. II. One Week Before the Presentation Day a) Post your subheadings of the article on eeclass. 1. Number all paragraphs first. 2. Group paragraphs logically and give each group a subheading. 3. Use short phrases, not full sentences. b) Post your vocabulary list on eeclass. c) Vocabulary List Guidelines i. This list is different from the “Vocabulary Sharing” portion of your presentation. It should contain at least 15 words; longer or more difficult articles may require additional words. ii. Number the words and list them in the order in which they appear in the article. iii. For each word, include: 1. The word and its part of speech (e.g., noun, verb, or adjective) 2. Its English definition as used in the article 3. A dictionary example sentence illustrating the same meaning iv. If you cannot find an example in dictionaries, use the sentence from your article. Do not invent your own example sentence. v. Recommended dictionaries: 1. Longman Dictionary of Contemporary English http://www.ldoceonline.com/dictionary/epidemic 2. Cambridge Dictionary https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/ 3. TheFreeDictionary http://www.thefreedictionary.com/innumerable ◼ Note: Use Longman first, as definitions in class are usually drawn from it. If not suitable, consult Cambridge, then The Free Dictionary. vi. Do not email me your vocabulary list. Proofreading is your responsibility. However, if you have difficulty finding a definition, you may ask Jennifer. d) Compose your speech as early as possible. e) Memorize your speech and rehearse it thoroughly before presentation day. III. One Day Prior to the Presentation a) Upload your written report to eeclass. b) Print one copy of your written report. 8 IV. On the Day of the Presentation a) Materials • Distribute copies of your vocabulary list to your classmates. • Before presenting, submit one copy of your vocabulary list and one copy of your written report to the instructor. b) Content of the Presentation Your presentation should include: 1. Summary (3 minutes) • Tip: List key words first, and then organize them into main ideas logically in your own words. • Do not copy sentences directly from the article. 2. Vocabulary or Sentence Sharing (2 minutes) • Choose 2 or3 words or phrases that impressed you most. • Explain why you selected them and how they can be used. • You may also share a sentence that you find interesting from the article instead of words or phrases 3. Personal Responses (2 minutes each speaker) • Each presenter must share their own thoughts and reflections on the article. c) Time Limit • Total time: 10 minutes • Article summary: 3 mins. • Vocabulary/ sentence sharing: 2 mins. • Personal responses: 2 mins. per speaker ◼ You must stop immediately when time is up, even if your presentation is unfinished. d) Q&A • After your talk, classmates and the instructor will ask questions about the article or your presentation. • Both presenters must take turns answering. • Students who ask questions will earn extra class participation point for that day. e) Written Report 1. Type a written report that includes your article summary, vocabulary or sentence sharing, and personal responses. 2. Indicate how you and your partner divided the work. 3. Upload your written report to eeclass one day before your presentation. 4. Submit one printed copy to the instructor before presenting. 5. AI Usage Policy: You must not use AI or machine-translation tools, including Google Translate to generate or translate your speech or written report. However, you may use AI to proofread or revise work that you have written independently in English. If you use AI for proofreading or revision, you must also submit: • Your original version; • The AI’s revised version; and • A sort list of lessons or insights you gained by comparing the two versions. 9 Appendix II: Rubric for the Pair Article Presentation Category Description Point Value Volume, Articulation, & Pronunciation • speaks loudly and clearly • articulates words clearly • uses accurate pronunciation 20 Preparation • posts questions about the article title and their answers two weeks prior to the presentation • posts the finalized version of article subheadings and word list on eeclass one week before the presentation • uploads the written report to eeclass one day before the presentation • distributes the copies the vocabulary list on time • submits the written report on time • responds effectively to questions from the instructor and classmates 20 Delivery • delivers a well-organized presentation • avoids unnecessary long pauses • uses an appropriate pace, effective intonation, and natural pauses • maintains sufficient eye contact • presents without reading from notes • manages the allotted time effectively 20 Content Summary: • includes the key points • does not copy sentences from the article • organized Word sharing: • explains the reasons for choosing the words • explains the meanings of the words used in the article • suggests how the words/phrases can be used Response: • meaningful reflection 20 Vocabulary List & Written Report Vocabulary list: • includes all important new words • chooses correct meanings used in the article • few errors • a complete list • numbers and lists the words according to their order of appearance in the article Written report: • typed • few grammatical errors • organized • includes work allocations 20 Total 100

Students are required to prepare the designated passages BEFORE class, ACTIVELY participate in class discussions and complete exercise sections ON TIME. Listening input: A variety of authentic English-speaking contexts, including university lectures, interviews, podcasts, and classroom discussions not only activate students’ background knowledge of the topic, prime them for the authentic and inspirational content they will meet in the thought-provoking TED Talks, but also guide them systematically through strategies and activities to meet future academic, personal or professional goals. Specific and key academic skills are focused in each theme-based unit, where students effectively learn to predict, identify main ideas/details/inferences, take notes and manage lengthy input. Pronunciation is also highlighted as an aid to improving both listening comprehension & speaking fluency. Speaking output: Presentation skills inspired by the TED speakers give students the techniques & authentic language they need to successfully deliver their own presentations, help them gain the opportunity to personalize the language they learn, and build their confidence in expressing ideas and opinions. Visual/digital literacy will be promoted through lots of infographics and speaking activities designed to involve students working with a partner or in a group. With connected ideas and integrated language skills, students will give individual, pair and group projects/presentation regularly throughout the semester. The ultimate goals of the course are to encourage students to take charge of their learning and to facilitate their essential 21st century skills—collaboration, communication and critical thinking. Through extensive reading, students will develop the ability to quickly and accurately grasp the main ideas and key points of texts, while expanding their vocabulary and reading techniques across various fields. Intensive reading activities will further enable students to understand both concrete and abstract meanings 2 Prepared by Man-Ting Huang (黃滿庭) in texts, discuss and analyze the author’s intent, engage in critical thinking, and connect topics to real-world contexts.  Upon completing the course, students will be able to:  Read and comprehend texts at a high-intermediate level, using strategies for both extensive and intensive reading. (EAP)  Identify and understand the main ideas and specific details of various texts efficiently and accurately. (EAP)  Expand and retain knowledge of content-specific vocabulary, collocations, synonyms, antonyms, and phrasal verbs for academic and professional contexts. (EAP)  Develop critical thinking skills by evaluating an author's purpose, tone, and bias, and forming well- supported opinions about the text. (EAP)  Utilize effective study skills, such as note-taking and summarizing, to support academic success. (EAP)  Interpret and integrate information from charts, illustrations, and photographs, alongside textual content. (EAP)  Engage with texts beyond surface-level understanding by forming independent ideas and opinions about key topics. (EAP)  Develop foundational academic writing skills, such as crafting clear, concise paragraphs and organizing ideals logically for academic assignments. (EAP) UNIVERSITY STUDENT CORE COMPETENCY INDICATORS 課程核心能力 1. The ability to comm unicate and express oneself in English 英語溝通與表達能力 25% 2. The ability to thin k critically and organize ideas lo gically in English 深度分析與組織思考能力 25% 3. The knowledge of En glish learnin g strategies and techniques 英語學習策略與技巧 25% 4. (2025). Pathways: Reading, Writing, and Critical Thinking Level 4 (3rd Edition). National Geographic Learning. ISBN: 9780357980101 Online Learning SPARK PLATFORM at learn.eltngl.com Teacher-led or Self-Study CEFR Scale ■ C1 □ B2 □ B1 □ A2 □ A1 3 Prepared by Man-Ting Huang (黃滿庭) GRADING 1. Attendance and participation – 15% 2. Quizzes – 30% 3. Midterm reading project + Presentation in 3 to 5-minute talk – 25% 4. Uniform Final Exam – 30% UNIFORM FINAL EXAM This uniform final exam will take place, in the classrooms where the class usually meet and in regular class meeting hours, in Week 16. (統一期末考訂於第十六週，原班級教室與上課時間考試。) Note: Pathways Units 1, 4, 6 to be taught during class sessions, Unit 8 designated for student self- study, and all these four units covered in final exam. (註: 課堂教授 Pathways 第 1, 4, 6 單元，學生自學第 8 單元，期末考範圍 1, 4, 6, 8 全部四單元。) CLASSROOM LANGUAGE ■ English 70 % ■ Mandarin 30% SUGGESTED CLASS ACTIVITIES  Group or individual presentations █ Research, prepare, and deliver presentations on assigned topics, developing communication skills, confidence, and the ability to organize and share ideas effectively.  Jigsaw reading █ Divide an article or text into sections. Students read their section, summarize it, and share it with peers to complete the full picture.  Critical analysis discussions █ Choose articles or essays and have students discuss the author’s purpose, tone, and main arguments.  Discussion Circles □ Provide prompts related to course content or current events. Students take turns sharing opinions and supporting their ideas with examples.  Vocabulary building activities □ Expand and apply vocabulary through tasks such as word maps, matching synonyms, and writing stories, enhancing understanding and usage in context.  Interpretation projects █ Analyze and interpret information from texts, charts, graphs and illustrations. Present findings clearly and connect them to real-world applications. CLASS RULES 1. Students are required to attend each class session and conscientiously participate in classroom learning 4 Prepared by Man-Ting Huang (黃滿庭) activities in order to be regarded as full attendance and granted a score of 90 in the grading category of Attendance & Participation. (上課全勤，且認真參與課堂學習， 出勤參與成績得 90 分。） 2. Occasional absences up to three times will lead to a zero in the score for Attendance & Participation category, and five absences will result in a failure in this course. （三次無故缺席，無法獲得任何出勤參與成績; 五次無故缺席，學期總成績不及格。） 3. Authorized absence under exceptional circumstances can be granted, if evidence for justifiable cause can be produced. （有正當理由並可提出證明的特殊狀況，方可准假。） REGULATIONS FOR USING AI (課程使用 AI 的原則) □ 完全開放使用且無須註明 □ 有條件開放，依課程規定使用生成式 AI。 ■ 禁止使用，作業或報告必須由學生本人產出。 (AI-assisted assignments are NOT allowed; only content generated by the student can be accepted.) □ 本課程無涉及 AI 使用 生成式 人工智慧 倫理聲明 根據本校公布之「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採取禁止使 用，相關監管機制如下:  修讀本門課程之學生應注意本門課不得繳交使用生成式人工智慧所產出的作業、報 告或個人心得。若經查核發現，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重 新評分或不予計分。  修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。 依據上述指引，本課程對於 AI 使用策略之考量與決議: 利用人工智慧生成書寫文字已是一般人輕易可得的事，不須依賴他人代工，幾個按 鍵就可產出有內容的文字，切要主旨前後一致，敘事說理文意貫串，字詞句法精準。利 用機器瞬間數百萬次改寫改說，重新置換字詞字句，可輕易躲過剽竊偵測軟體，達到 100% Unique 獨特原創性，輕鬆取得及格以上滿意的分數。我們若想逆向溯源找出機器 撰寫改說的證據，或是查驗文字內容是否由人類或機器創作，其難度相對高，畢竟人類 語文表達，就本質來說，雖有語法約定俗成的限制，但也容許相當大的自由程度，同樣 意思可以不同字詞句法表達，容許使用不同旨趣細微差別的文字，這也是人工智慧文字 內容生成系統建構所利用的語言特性。 然而，若是不需付出任何努力學習，就可取得一篇精緻完美的報告或論述文章，這 對於學校作為建構知識學習場域實質構成欺瞞，對於社會公益公平負面影響尤其鉅大。 畢竟，學習者工作本質就是學習，抄襲造假不但無助於學習，適足以鼓勵欺瞞造假負面 價值，更是扼殺學習工作建構知識技能本質的意義。因此，學術工作由他人或機器代工 都是違背學術倫理的行為。學習者選擇誠實努力工作或是欺瞞他人找代工，這是倫理善 惡的分野，直接相關學習探索進程。本課程任課教師經審慎考量，本課程授課教師認為 本課程不宜使用生成式人工智慧作為課堂活動內容或學習輔助工具。 學 生 使 用 AI 條件 ▓ 禁止使用，作業或報告必須由學生本人產出。(AI-assisted assignments are NOT allowed: only content generated by the student personally can be accepted.) Through extensive reading, students will develop the ability to quickly and accurately grasp the main ideas and key points of texts, while expanding their vocabulary and reading techniques across various fields. Intensive reading activities will further enable students to understand both concrete and abstract meanings in texts, discuss and analyze the author’s intent, engage in critical thinking, and connect topics to real-world contexts. Upon completing the course, students will be able to: ✓ Read and comprehend texts at a high-intermediate level, using strategies for both extensive and intensive reading. (EAP) ✓ Identify and understand the main ideas and specific details of various texts efficiently and accurately. (EAP) ✓ Expand and retain knowledge of content-specific vocabulary, collocations, synonyms, antonyms, and phrasal verbs for academic and professional contexts. (EAP) 2 ✓ Develop critical thinking skills by evaluating an author’s purpose, tone, and bias, and forming well-supported opinions about the text. (EAP) ✓ Utilize effective study skills, such as note-taking and summarizing, to support academic success. (EAP) ✓ Interpret and integrate information from charts, illustrations, and photographs, alongside textual content. (EAP) ✓ Engage with texts beyond surface-level understanding by forming independent ideas and opinions about key topics. (EAP) ✓ Develop foundational academic writing skills, such as crafting clear, concise paragraphs and organizing ideals logically for academic assignments. (EAP) UNIVERSITY STUDENT CORE COMPETENCY INDICATORS 課程核心能力 1. The ability to communicate and express oneself in English 英語溝通與表達能力 20% 2. The ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English 深度分析與組織思考能力 25% 3. The knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques 英語學習策略與技巧 25% 4. Global views of English and multicultural diversity 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 20% 5. The ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣能力 10% UNIFORM TEXTBOOK ⚫ Vargo, M., Blass, L. & Sherman K. (2025). Pathways: Reading, Writing, and Critical Thinking (3rd Edition). National Geographic Learning. ISBN: 9780357980101 CEFR Scale ■ B2+ □ B2 □ B1 □ A2+ □ A2 GRADING 1. Attendance and participation – 15% 2. Midterm Group Presentation – 20% 3. Assignments (Outline + Summary) – 20% 4. Quizzes – 15% 5. Uniform Final Exam – 30% UNIFORM FINAL EXAM The uniform final exam, accounting for 30% of the semester grade, will take place in the usual classrooms and at the regular class meeting times in Week 16. Four units* of the textbook will be covered in the uniform exam. ⚫ Pathways: Units 1, 4, 6, & 8 [Unit 6 for Self-Learning] 3 ⚫ Question Types: Vocabulary, Comprehension, Essay Questions, Reading Charts & Graphs, Summarizing, etc. CLASSROOM LANGUAGE  English 70 %  Mandarin 30 % SUGGESTED CLASS ACTIVITIES ⚫ Group presentations □ Research, prepare, and deliver presentations on assigned topics, developing communication skills, confidence, and the ability to organize and share ideas effectively. ⚫ Jigsaw reading □ Divide an article or text into sections. Students read their section, summarize it, and share it with peers to complete the full picture. ⚫ Critical analysis discussions □ Choose articles or essays and have students discuss the author’s purpose, tone, and main arguments. ⚫ Discussion Circles □ Provide prompts related to course content or current events. Students take turns sharing opinions and supporting their ideas with examples. ⚫ Vocabulary building activities □ Expand and apply vocabulary through tasks such as word maps, matching synonyms, and writing stories, enhancing understanding and usage in context. ⚫ Interpretation projects □ Analyze and interpret information from texts, charts, graphs and illustrations. Present findings clearly and connect them to real-world applications. REGULATIONS FOR USING AI □ 有條件開放生成式 AI 於課程產出 本課程鼓勵學生在透明與負責任的原則下，適度使用 AI 工具進行課業協作。學生應在課堂作業 或報告的標題頁註腳或引用文獻後，簡要說明如何使用生成式 AI 進行議題發想、文句潤飾或結 構參考等內容。然而，在「個人反思報告」和「小組採訪作業」中，禁止使用生成式 AI 工具進 行撰寫。如經查核未標註 AI 工具的使用情況，教師或學校有權重新評分或不予計分。 [source: https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248357.php?Lang=zh-tw#example] CLASS RULES 1. docs.text: Tentative Syllabus for “Upper-Intermediate English: Listening and Speaking” in fall, 2025 Classroom: 綜二 103 Class Hours: Wednesday 8:00 ~ 9:50 (W12) and 10:10 ~ 12:00 (W34) Credits: 2 Instructor: 馬紹芸 (Shao-Yun Ma) E-mail: elisama1112@gmail.com 課程概述與目標 This course aims at enhancing students' listening comprehension and speaking ability by exposing them to various intriguing materials suitable to the high-intermediate levels. With broad range of listening materials and academic vocabulary assembled from the Academic Word List (Coxhead, 2000) and CEFR (Common European Framework of Reference for Languages), students are expected to learn and acquire high-intermediate to advanced level of listening and speaking skills. The activities in the textbook include lecture-based listening exercises to facilitate students' listening comprehension skills as well as to inspire students’ language use and relate to themes through thought-provoking TED talks. Classroom activities are designed with the intention of meeting their needs and arousing interests to improve their English vocabulary and listening as well as speaking skills for future uses such as reading images, communicating clearly and collaborate, work independently, and think critically. University Student Core Competency Indicators 25% 1. The ability to communicate and express oneself in English 英語溝通與表達能力 25% 2. The ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English 深度分析與組織思考能力 20% 3. The knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques 英語學習策略與技巧 15% 4. Global views of English and multicultural diversity 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 15% 5. The ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語 的習慣能力 Declaration for Student Use of AI: Conditionally Open, Please Specify the Usage of Generative AI in Course Output: Example 1: Students are allowed to use generative AI tools, but they should specify the use of AI in their course output and provide relevant citations or links. Example 2: Students are permitted to use generative AI tools, and they should explain the usage of AI tools and relevant parameter settings in their course output. Class Rules 1. Class attendance, lesson preparation and active class participation are required. 2. Absence from a class is NO excuse for not knowing the assignment and what has been discussed in that class. It is YOUR responsibility to ask your fellow classmates what has been covered and what will be doing in the class. 3. Plagiarism and cheating on the exam is absolutely not permitted. If someone is found plagiarizing or cheating on an exam, it means he/she will get a zero point for that exam. 4. There will be NO make-up exams/presentations unless valid and official reasons for absence are presented beforehand. 5. The handouts given in the class should be kept at least till the end of the semester for later reference or final exam. 6. Cellular phones should be turned off during the two-hour class period. Textbook & Supplementary Material 1. Lee, C. (2023). 21st Century Communication: Listening, Speaking and Critical Thinking, 2nd Ed. Boston, MA: National Geographic Learning. ISBN: 978-0-357-85600-0 2. Other resources and supplementary materials will be distributed in class or online. Grading 1. final exam (listening and vocabulary): 20% 2. final presentation, project, or exam (speaking): 10% 3. attendance and in-class participation: 15% 4. quizzes and presentations: 15% 5. portfolio: 20% 6. online recording and listening exercises: 20% EAP Skills of the three Units Unit 1: - Recognizing the repetition of important details - Asking rhetorical questions - Synthesizing and evaluating ideas - Starting presentations with questions Unit 6: - Noticing questions - Recognizing a speaker’s purpose - Describing time, frequency, and duration - Analyzing infographics - Synthesizing and evaluating ideas - Providing context in presentations Unit 7: - Matching speakers with their ideas - Recognizing perspectives - Responding to people opinions - Comparing concerns of people from different generations - Synthesizing and evaluating ideas - Delivering a dynamic presentation Tentative Schedule Weeks Date Tentative Contents week 1 9/3 orientation and overview of the course basic listening and note-taking skills Introduction to the BEST Test of English Proficiency week 2 9/10 Unit 1 Lessons A-C: vocabulary and collocations, note-taking of numerical information, listening of repetition, and asking rhetorical questions Introduction to the BEST Test of English Proficiency week 3 9/17 Unit 1 Lesson D: a conversation about news headlines week 4 9/24 Unit 1 Lessons E-F: vocabulary and TED talk of “Fake Videos of Real People—and How to Spot Them” week 5 10/1 Unit 1 Lessons G-H: critical thinking and presentation skills week 6 10/8 Unit 6 Lessons A-C: vocabulary and collocations, note-taking of noticing questions, recognizing a speaker’s purpose, and describing time, frequency, and duration in speaking week 7 10/15 Unit 6 Lesson D: lectures of people sharing their phone usage week 8 10/22 Unit 6 Lessons E-F: words and collocations, pronunciation of “that”, and a TED talk of “Does Photographing a Moment Steal the Experience from You?” week 9 10/29 Unit 6 Lessons G-H: critical thinking and presentation skills week 10 11/5 Unit 7 Lessons A-C: words and collocations, note-taking of matching speakers with their ideas, recognizing perspectives in listening, and responding to people’s opinions week 11 11/12 No class due to Sports Day week 12 11/19 Unit 7 Lesson D: lectures of concerns of people from different generations Lessons E-F: words and collocations, TED talk of “How Generational Stereotypes Hold Us Back at Work” week 13 11/26 Unit 7 Lessons G-H: critical thinking and presentation skills week 14 12/3 review for the final exam and follow up of the three units week 15 12/10 final presentations week 16 12/17 final exam of listening and vocabulary

Mandarin 30% Upper-­‐intermediate English III Listening & Speaking 2 prepared by Iris Chang Course Goals / Description 中 高 級 英 文 三 聽 講 為 一 門 2 學 分 學 期 課 程，為 訓 練 中 高 級 程 度 之 大 一 學 生 習 得 進 階 主 題 式 英 語 溝 通 與 表 達 ， 強 化 學 生 思 考 、 組 織 及 表 達 的 整 合 技 能 ； 並 培 養 學 生 發 現 問 題 、 以 英 語 提 問 並 表 達 意 見 的 能 力，經 由 實 境 口 說 與 演 講 訓 練，增 進 學 生 英 語 聽 力 及 訓 練 演 說 技 巧 。 This semester-based English III course is specifically designed to enhance Freshman students’ listening & speaking competency at the intermediate to high-intermediate level. Students are required to prepare the designated passages BEFORE class, ACTIVELY participate in class discussions and complete exercise sections ON TIME. Listening input: A variety of authentic English contexts, including talks, discussions, and conversations not only help expand students’ existing knowledge about interesting and contemporary topics, but also guide them systematically through strategies and activities to meet future academic, personal or professional goals. Specific learning points are focused in each theme-based chapter, where students effectively learn to manage lengthy listening input by predicting, identifying main ideas/details, and taking notes. Pronunciation is also highlighted to improve students’ listening comprehension and speaking fluency. Speaking output: Presentation skills inspired by the Ted talks give students the techniques and authentic language they need to deliver their own presentations. Accuracy-based and fluency-based activities for specific communicative functions will help students gain the opportunity to personalize the language they learn, and to build their confidence in expressing their ideas and opinions. Communicative speaking activities including games, role-plays, and conversation practice are designed to reinforce the chapter content and to allow students to practice integrated language skills. Individual and group projects/presentations will also be given throughout the semester. The ultimate goal of this course is the encourage students to take charge of their own learning and to facilitate the essential l 21st century skills – collaboration, communication and critical thinking. Students will have opportunities to learn the key academic skills through thought-provoking TED talks (signposting with questions, personalizing a presentation, closing a presentation, numbering key points, using your voice effectively, etc.) and get exposed to collaboration, communication, and critical thinking. After having taken this course, students are expected to consolidate their essential knowledge of listening input and speaking output. Requirements—Students are required to prepare the designated learning activities BEFOREHAND, REGULARLY attend the class, ACTIVELY participate in classroom activities, and complete each assignment ON TIME. Aside from class participation and practices based on the textbook, students are encouraged to work on a self‐access learning project based on designated videos, reading texts, and online English-learning materials (VOA News). Bring my expertise into the classroom. For example, many years of my study, professional experience Upper-intermediate English III Listening & Speaking 4 revised by Yuan-yang Wang (well, I work as a translator), and stories from real life. I believe that we can learn through stories. (You, too, are encouraged to bring stories to class to stimulate discussion.) 4. Regard struggling with ideas as a process of learning. 5. Be open about different ideas. 6. Treat you with respect since you are adult learners. HERE IS WHAT I EXPECT FROM YOU: 1. Class attendance, lesson preparation and active class participation are required. If you are absent for more than 6 hours with no valid excuses, you will fail this course. 2. Absence from a class is NO excuse for not knowing the assignment and what has been discussed in that class. It is YOUR responsibility to ask your fellow classmates what has been covered and what will be doing in the class. 3. Effort to make this class your own. Always ask yourself: What will I do to promote my learning? 4. Plagiarism and cheating on the exam are absolutely not permitted. If someone is found plagiarizing or cheating on an exam, it means he/she will get a zero point for that exam. If you have any questions regarding the expectations for a specific assignment or exam, please do not hesitate to ask. 5. Honesty. I will ask you many questions throughout the semester. “I don’t know,” “I need to think about it for a while,” or “I need to pass on that question” are acceptable answers. 6. There will be NO make-up exams/presentations unless valid and official reasons for absence are presented beforehand. 7. docs.text: 1 National Tsing Hua University Fall 2026 Upper-Intermediate English III_Reading Class W3W4 COURSE INFORMATION Course Number LANG 103025 Credits 2 Classroom 綜二 204 Class hours □ Monday □ Tuesday ■ Wednesday □ Thursday □ Friday □ 8:00A.M. – 9:50A.M. ■ 10:10A.M. – 12:00P.M. 學生身分別 ■ 頂標生 □ 前標生 □ 中級生 □ 初級生 Extra Enrollments: Not Available 本課程不提供加簽 INSTRUCTOR Name Email Office Office Hour 劉文貞 (Jennifer W. Liu) wenchenl2013@gmail.com 綜二 210 Friday 1:30 pm-3:30 pm (By Appointment) COURSE GOALS & DESCRIPTION This two-credit semester course, High-Intermediate English Reading III, is designed to help first-year college students at a high-intermediate level strengthen and enhance their English reading skills. Through extensive reading, students will develop the ability to quickly and accurately grasp the main ideas and key points of texts, while expanding their vocabulary and reading techniques across various fields. Intensive reading activities will further enable students to understand both concrete and abstract meanings in texts, discuss and analyze the author’s intent, engage in critical thinking, and connect topics to real-world contexts. Class activities include lectures, group discussions, pair practice, and presentations. Upon completing the course, students will be able to: ✓ Read and comprehend texts at a high-intermediate level, using strategies for both extensive and intensive reading. (EAP) ✓ Identify and understand the main ideas and specific details of various texts efficiently and accurately. (EAP) ✓ Expand and retain knowledge of content-specific vocabulary, collocations, synonyms, antonyms, and phrasal verbs for academic and professional contexts. (EAP) ✓ Develop critical thinking skills by evaluating an author’s purpose, tone, and bias, and forming well- supported opinions about the text. (EAP) ✓ Utilize effective study skills, such as note-taking and summarizing, to support academic success. (EAP) ✓ Interpret and integrate information from charts, illustrations, and photographs, alongside textual content. (EAP) ✓ Engage with texts beyond surface-level understanding by forming independent ideas and opinions about key topics. (EAP) 2 UNIVERSITY STUDENT CORE COMPETENCY INDICATORS 課程核心能力 1. The ability to communicate and express oneself in English 英語溝通與表達能力 25% 2. The ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English 深度分析與組織思考能力 25% 3. The knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques 英語學習策略與技巧 25% 4. Global views of English and multicultural diversity 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 10% 5. The ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣能力 15% UNIFORM TEXTBOOK Vargo, M., Blass, L. & Sherman K. (2025). Pathways: Reading, Writing, and Critical Thinking 4 (3rd Edition). National Geographic Learning. ISBN: 9780357980101 CEFR Scale ■ C1 □ B2 □ B1 □ A2+ □ A2 E-LEARN PLATFORM https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw RECOMMENDED ONLINE DICTIONARIES 1. Longman Dictionary of Contemporary English Online https://www.ldoceonline.com/ 2. Cambridge Dictionary https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/ 3. The Free Dictionary http://www.thefreedictionary.com/ REGULATIONS FOR USING AI (AI 使用原則) Students are not allowed to use AI or machine-translation tools, including Google Translate, to generate or translate answers or assignments. This prohibition applies to questions and answers about the presentation article titles, presentation transcripts, and in-class worksheets. However, students may use AI to proofread or revise work that they have written independently in English. When using AI for proofreading or revision, students must submit their original version, the AI revised version, and a list of lessons or insights they gained by comparing the two versions. GRADING 1. Attendance and Participation – 15% 2. Pair Article Presentation – 15 % 3. Quizzes – 20 % 4. In-Class Tasks/ Worksheets – 15 % 5. Assignments – 5% 6. Uniform Final Exam – 30% 3 Class Participation/ Attendance Students are expected to attend each class punctually and actively participate in pair, group, and class discussions. If you cannot attend, you must (1) email the teacher and (2) apply for leave through the university’s online system. For further information, please refer to the following: • Student Leave Policies: https://sa.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/406-1480-264831,r7918.php?Lang=zh-tw • Student Leave Guidelines: https://sa.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/406-1480-269011,r7918.php?Lang=zh-tw • Related Document Downloads: https://sa.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/412-1480-21552.php?Lang=zh-tw Important rules for this course: 1. For sick or personal leave, you must provide valid supporting documentation. ▪ For sick leave, a medical receipt or certificate is required. 2. To arrange a make-up quiz, presentation, or final examination, you must provide official supporting documentation. ▪ Traveling or taking a driver’s license test is not considered an acceptable reason. 3. If your leave request is not approved, it will be counted as an absence. 4. An absence from class is not an excuse for being unaware of assignments, announcements, or material covered in class. It is your responsibility to ask your classmates what you missed and find out what assignments or preparation are required for the next class. Attendance, punctuality, and class participation will be recorded and included in your course evaluation. Attendance will be recording beginning in the first week, so please make sure that you attend the first class and arrive on time. Attendance Policy ➢ Starting score: 9 (起始點: 9 分) ➢ Late arrival: -2 (遲到: 2 分) ➢ Absence: -10 (缺席: 10 分) ➢ Irrelevant activities in class: -2 (做課堂不相關的事: 2 分) The starting attendance score is 9 points. Each late arrival deducts 2 points. Each absence deducts 10 points. Engaging in irrelevant activities in class deducts 2 points. (This includes using a phone for non-class- related activities or working on assignments for other courses.) The score has no lower limit but a maximum of 20 points. In other words, a negative attendance score will lower your semester grade, while a high attendance score can earn you up to 5 extra points towards your semester grade. 出席成績從 9 分開始計算，並依以下規則增減：每次遲到扣 2 分，缺席扣 10 分。若在課堂上從事無關活動 （如使用手機處理與課程無關的事務或做其他課程作業），則扣 2 分。分數累積上限為 20 分，無下限。換 言之，若出席成績為負分，將併入學期成績計算；若累積達 20 分，則學期成績額外加 5 分。 All these seemingly complicated and trivial calculations for attendance and class participation are designed to encourage you to speak more English and participate more actively in class. The more you engage in each class, the more harvest you’ll reap from this course. 4 PAIR ARTICLE PRESENTATION Students will choose an article from the course packet and deliver a 10-minute pair presentation in class. Sign-ups must be completed by the third week, and the presentation schedule will be announced afterward. To fulfill this course requirement, students must: • Begin preparation at least two weeks in advance • Meet all deadlines • Memorize their speeches • Rehearse thoroughly (For further details, see Appendices I & II) IN-CLASS TASKS/WORKSHEETS Each class includes pair or group tasks and discussions, and all students are required to participate actively. At the end of each session, the instructor will collect the worksheets. Four or five will be randomly selected for grading. A group-member evaluation may occasionally be administered after a group task. Students will evaluate each member’s contribution to the task. If a student receives an average peer-evaluation score below 6 out of 10, the instructor will review the student’s contribution to the group task based on the peer evaluations, written comments, completed work, and classroom observations. If insufficient participation is confirmed, the student’s individual worksheet score may be reduced or, in cases of non-participation, recorded as 0. • If you are absent, the worksheet score will be 0. • Late submissions will not be accepted. ASSIGNMENTS All assignments must be typed and turned in on time. Late assignments will not be graded. QUIZZES Two quizzes, as scheduled in the course outline, will test students on both vocabulary and the content of the textbook articles as well as articles presented by classmates. Pop quizzes may also be given before student presentations; these will count for 1/4 of the total 20 % quiz grade. UNIFORM FINAL EXAM The uniform final exam (30% of the semester grade) will take place in the regular classroom at the usual class meeting time in Week 16. It will cover four units of the textbook: Units 1, 4, 6, and 8. Units 1, 4, and 8 will be taught in class, while Unit 6 must be studied independently by students. COPY FEE A copy fee of NT$70-100 will be collected once during the semester to cover the course packet, test sheets and handouts. 5 SUGGESTIONS FOR SUCCESS IN THIS COURSE To get the most out of this course, you are advised to: 1. Attend every class and arrive on time. 2. Volunteer to speak and participate actively in pair, group, and whole-class discussions. 3. Preview the course materials before class. 4. Learn and review new vocabulary every day, and apply what you have learned. 5. Submit assignments, worksheets, and presentation materials by the stated deadlines. Upload electronic files to eeclass and submit printed copies in class when required. o Electronic files allow the instructor to review your work for compliance with the course AI policy. o Printed copies will be used for reading, grading, and providing feedback in order to reduce the instructor’s screen time and eye strain. 6. Please feel free to ask questions whenever you have them. 7. If you have been putting considerable time and effort into the course but still feel that you are falling behind, please reach out to Jennifer for assistance. COURSE SCHEDULE Week Date Main Topic Reading Strategies Critical Thinking 1. 9/9 Course Introduction & Orientation Introduction to the BEST Test of English Proficiency* 2. 9/16 Unit 1 The Changing Workplace Introduction to the BEST Reading Test* ✓ Identifying main ideas and key details (EAP) 3. 9/23 Unit 1 The Changing Workplace Introduction to the BEST Writing Test*  Recognizing claims and counterclaims (EAP) 4. 9/30 Unit 1 The Changing Workplace ✓ Understanding cohesion (EAP) 5. 10/7 Unit 1 The Changing Workplace  Summarizing a text (EAP) 6. 10/14 Unit 4 Rethinking Transport ✓ Recognizing and evaluating different viewpoints (EAP) 7. 10/21 Quiz#1 8. 10/28 Unit 4 Rethinking Transport ✓ Using a concept map (EAP) 6 9. 11/4 Unit 4 Rethinking Transport ✓ Understanding complex sentences (EAP)  Inferring meaning (EAP) 10. 11/11 No Class (Sports Day) Watch a video lesson on Unit 4 Rethinking Transport  Comparing and contrasting two perspectives (EAP) 11. 11/18 Unit 8 Living Longer ✓ Reading extended texts (EAP) 12. 11/25 Unit 8 Living Longer ✓ Asking questions as you read (EAP) 13. 12/2 Quiz#2 14. 12/9 Unit 8 Living Longer ✓ Understanding supporting examples (EAP)  Interpreting visual data (EAP) 15. 12/16 Unit 8 Living Longer  Synthesizing (EAP) 16. 12/23 Uniform Final Exam (原班級教室與上課時間 考試) Note: Unit 6, “Why Language Matters,” is designated as a self-learning unit for students. 7 Appendix I: Pair Article Presentation Guidelines Students will choose an article from the course packet and deliver a 10-minute pair presentation in class without using PowerPoint slides. Sign-ups must be completed by Week 3, and the presentation schedule will be announced afterward. To fulfill this requirement, begin preparing at least two weeks in advance, meet all deadlines, memorize your speech, and rehearse thoroughly. I. Two Weeks Before the Presentation Day a) Confirm the article you will present. b) Meet with your partner and divide the work evenly. c) Read the article carefully at least once. d) Post your questions about the article’s title, together with your answers, on eeclass. II. One Week Before the Presentation Day a) Post your subheadings of the article on eeclass. 1. Number all paragraphs first. 2. Group paragraphs logically and give each group a subheading. 3. Use short phrases, not full sentences. b) Post your vocabulary list on eeclass. c) Vocabulary List Guidelines i. This list is different from the “Vocabulary Sharing” portion of your presentation. It should contain at least 15 words; longer or more difficult articles may require additional words. ii. Number the words and list them in the order in which they appear in the article. iii. For each word, include: 1. The word and its part of speech (e.g., noun, verb, or adjective) 2. Its English definition as used in the article 3. A dictionary example sentence illustrating the same meaning iv. If you cannot find an example in dictionaries, use the sentence from your article. Do not invent your own example sentence. v. Recommended dictionaries: 1. Longman Dictionary of Contemporary English http://www.ldoceonline.com/dictionary/epidemic 2. Cambridge Dictionary https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/ 3. TheFreeDictionary http://www.thefreedictionary.com/innumerable ◼ Note: Use Longman first, as definitions in class are usually drawn from it. If not suitable, consult Cambridge, then The Free Dictionary. vi. Do not email me your vocabulary list. Proofreading is your responsibility. However, if you have difficulty finding a definition, you may ask Jennifer. d) Compose your speech as early as possible. e) Memorize your speech and rehearse it thoroughly before presentation day. III. One Day Prior to the Presentation a) Upload your written report to eeclass. b) Print one copy of your written report. 8 IV. On the Day of the Presentation a) Materials • Distribute copies of your vocabulary list to your classmates. • Before presenting, submit one copy of your vocabulary list and one copy of your written report to the instructor. b) Content of the Presentation Your presentation should include: 1. Summary (3 minutes) • Tip: List key words first, and then organize them into main ideas logically in your own words. • Do not copy sentences directly from the article. 2. Vocabulary or Sentence Sharing (2 minutes) • Choose 2 or3 words or phrases that impressed you most. • Explain why you selected them and how they can be used. • You may also share a sentence that you find interesting from the article instead of words or phrases 3. Personal Responses (2 minutes each speaker) • Each presenter must share their own thoughts and reflections on the article. c) Time Limit • Total time: 10 minutes • Article summary: 3 mins. • Vocabulary/ sentence sharing: 2 mins. • Personal responses: 2 mins. per speaker ◼ You must stop immediately when time is up, even if your presentation is unfinished. d) Q&A • After your talk, classmates and the instructor will ask questions about the article or your presentation. • Both presenters must take turns answering. • Students who ask questions will earn extra class participation point for that day. e) Written Report 1. Type a written report that includes your article summary, vocabulary or sentence sharing, and personal responses. 2. Indicate how you and your partner divided the work. 3. Upload your written report to eeclass one day before your presentation. 4. Submit one printed copy to the instructor before presenting. 5. AI Usage Policy: You must not use AI or machine-translation tools, including Google Translate to generate or translate your speech or written report. However, you may use AI to proofread or revise work that you have written independently in English. If you use AI for proofreading or revision, you must also submit: • Your original version; • The AI’s revised version; and • A sort list of lessons or insights you gained by comparing the two versions. 9 Appendix II: Rubric for the Pair Article Presentation Category Description Point Value Volume, Articulation, & Pronunciation • speaks loudly and clearly • articulates words clearly • uses accurate pronunciation 20 Preparation • posts questions about the article title and their answers two weeks prior to the presentation • posts the finalized version of article subheadings and word list on eeclass one week before the presentation • uploads the written report to eeclass one day before the presentation • distributes the copies the vocabulary list on time • submits the written report on time • responds effectively to questions from the instructor and classmates 20 Delivery • delivers a well-organized presentation • avoids unnecessary long pauses • uses an appropriate pace, effective intonation, and natural pauses • maintains sufficient eye contact • presents without reading from notes • manages the allotted time effectively 20 Content Summary: • includes the key points • does not copy sentences from the article • organized Word sharing: • explains the reasons for choosing the words • explains the meanings of the words used in the article • suggests how the words/phrases can be used Response: • meaningful reflection 20 Vocabulary List & Written Report Vocabulary list: • includes all important new words • chooses correct meanings used in the article • few errors • a complete list • numbers and lists the words according to their order of appearance in the article Written report: • typed • few grammatical errors • organized • includes work allocations 20 Total 100

docs.text: 1 Prepared by Man-Ting Huang (黃滿庭) National Tsing Hua University Fall 2025 Upper-Intermediate English III_Reading Tentative Syllabus_W3W4 COURSE INFORMATION Course Number LANG 103026 Credits 2 Classroom Education #102 (教育館) Class hours □ Monday □ Tuesday ■ Wednesday □ Thursday □ Friday □ 8:00A.M. – 9:50A.M. ■ 10:10A.M. – 12:00P.M. 學生身分別 ■ 頂標生 □ 前標生 □ 中級生 □ 初級生 Extra Selection: 開放加簽之條件 加簽說明 □ 不開放人工加簽。所有學生須由選課系統亂數選課。 ■ 人數上限後，開放人工加簽，學生必須符合以下條件，於第一週上課時，備妥 加簽申請表，請老師同意並簽署加簽，申請送達英語教育中心辦公室，再由老師 線上簽核完成。 ■ 條件 1：第一週必須到課。 □ 條件 2：須有其他時段【選讀英語文】衝堂無法選課之證明（如選課紀錄或本 學期所有科目課程表） □ 條件 3：自所屬選課階段（大二生：第 1-2 次選課；大三、大四學生：第 3 次 選課）起，亂數選課皆未選上（選上但退選者，不得以人工加簽再次選課） ■ 條件 4：應屆畢業生 □ 條件 5：__________ 提醒：學生修讀英文領域課程，請依本校規劃選課之修業年級選課。如因個人考量，未對 應年級而逕自改於其他修業年級選課之英文領域課程，或指定加簽某特定課程，英語教育 中心與任課教師將礙難配合或處理。 INSTRUCTOR Name Email Office & Tel Office Hour Man-Ting Huang (黃滿庭) mthwang14@hotmail.com (full-time teachers only) (full-time teachers only) COURSE GOALS & DESCRIPTION 中高級英文三閱讀為一門兩學分的學期課程，幫助中高級程度之大一新生鞏固並精進英文閱讀能力。 透過廣泛閱讀，學習在短時間內快速正確精準把握文章大意與重點，拓展不同領域的字彙及閱讀技巧。 透過精讀，學習深度了解文章具體及抽象意涵，討論分析文本內涵與外延，評估作者立意觀點與語氣， 批判思辨議題，與實際世界互動。 This high-intermediate level English course is designed to help students develop extensive and intensive reading skills to grasp the point and support in the text, to explore vocabulary and reading skills by studying discipline-specific rhetoric of language patterns, and further to analyze and discuss issues that can be inferred or implied by what is presented in the text. Students will have training on academic reading 2 Prepared by Man-Ting Huang (黃滿庭) skills and strategies and critical thinking skills, working to apply the skills and language being learned in task-based collaborative activities that extend each reading chapter. By the end of this course, students will learn to develop the ability to understand and deliver academic arguments and to gain proficiency in using the language in academic contexts. Upon completing the course, students will be able to:  Read and comprehend texts at a high-intermediate level, using strategies for both extensive and intensive reading. (EAP)  Identify and understand the main ideas and specific details of various texts efficiently and accurately. (EAP)  Expand and retain knowledge of content-specific vocabulary, collocations, synonyms, antonyms, and phrasal verbs for academic and professional contexts. (EAP)  Develop critical thinking skills by evaluating an author’s purpose, tone, and bias, and forming well- supported opinions about the text. (EAP)  Utilize effective study skills, such as note-taking and summarizing, to support academic success. (EAP)  Interpret and integrate information from charts, illustrations, and photographs, alongside textual content. (EAP)  Engage with texts beyond surface-level understanding by forming independent ideas and opinions about key topics. (EAP)  Develop foundational academic writing skills, such as crafting clear, concise paragraphs and organizing ideals logically for academic assignments. (EAP) UNIVERSITY STUDENT CORE COMPETENCY INDICATORS 課程核心能力 1. The ability to comm unicate and express oneself in English 英語溝通與表達能力 30% 2. The ability to thin k critically and organize ideas lo gically in English 深度分析與組織思考能力 30% 3. The knowledge of En glish learnin g strategies and techniques 英語學習策略與技巧 20% 4. Global views of English and multicultural diversity 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 10% 5. The ability to use existing English le arning resour ces and development of independent self-learning habit 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣能力 10% UNIFORM TEXTBOOK Textbook Vargo, M., Blass, L. & Sherman K. (2025). Pathways: Reading, Writing, and Critical Thinking Level 4 (3rd Edition). National Geographic Learning. ISBN: 9780357980101 Online Learning SPARK PLATFORM at learn.eltngl.com Teacher-led or Self-Study 3 Prepared by Man-Ting Huang (黃滿庭) CEFR Scale ■ C1 □ B2 □ B1 □ A2 □ A1 GRADING 1. Attendance and participation – 15% 2. Quizzes – 30% 3. Midterm reading project + 5-minute talk – 25% 4. Uniform Final Exam – 30% UNIFORM FINAL EXAM The uniform final exam, accounting for 35% of the semester grade, will take place in the usual classrooms and at the regular class meeting times in Week 16. Four units* of the textbook will be covered in the uniform exam.  Pathways: Units 1, 4, 6, & 8 *Note: Units 1, 4, 6 to be taught during class sessions, Unit 8 designated for self-study, and all of these four units to be covered in the final exam. (註: 課堂教授第 1, 4, 6 單元，學生自學第 8 單元，期末考就這四單元。) CLASSROOM LANGUAGE ■ English 80 % ■ Mandarin 20% CLASS ACTIVITIES Group or individual presentations ◆ Research, prepare, and deliver presentations on assigned topics, developing communication skills, confidence, and the ability to organize and share ideas effectively. Jigsaw reading ◆ Divide an article or text into sections. Students read their section, summarize it, and share it with peers to complete the full picture. Critical analysis discussions ◆ Choose articles or essays and have students discuss the author’s purpose, tone, and main arguments. Discussion Circles ◆ Provide prompts related to course content or current events. Students take turns sharing opinions and supporting their ideas with examples. Vocabulary building activities ◆ Expand and apply vocabulary through tasks such as word maps, matching synonyms, and writing stories, enhancing understanding and usage in context. Interpretation projects ◆ Analyze and interpret information from texts, charts, graphs and illustrations. Present findings clearly and connect them to real-world applications. 4 Prepared by Man-Ting Huang (黃滿庭) CLASS RULES 1. Students are required to attend each class session and conscientiously participate in classroom learning activities in order to be regarded as full attendance and granted a score of 90 in the grading category of Attendance & Participation. (上課全勤，且認真參與課堂學習， 出勤參與成績得 90 分。） 2. Occasional absences up to three times will lead to a zero in the score for Attendance & Participation category, and five absences will result in a failure in this course. （三次無故缺席，無法獲得任何出勤參與成績; 五次無故缺席，學期總成績不及格。） 3. Authorized absence under exceptional circumstances can be granted, if evidence for justifiable cause can be produced. （有正當理由並可提出證明的特殊狀況，方可准假。） REGULATIONS FOR USING AI (課程使用 AI 的原則) □ 完全開放使用且無須註明 □ 有條件開放，依課程規定使用生成式 AI。 ■ 禁止使用，作業或報告必須由學生本人產出。 (AI-assisted assignments are NOT allowed; only content generated by the student can be accepted.) □ 本課程無涉及 AI 使用 生成式 人工智慧 倫理聲明 根據本校公布之「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採取禁止使 用，相關監管機制如下:  修讀本門課程之學生應注意本門課不得繳交使用生成式人工智慧所產出的作業、報 告或個人心得。若經查核發現，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重 新評分或不予計分。  修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。 依據上述指引，本課程對於 AI 使用策略之考量與決議: 利用人工智慧生成書寫文字已是一般人輕易可得的事，不須依賴他人代工，幾個按 鍵就可產出有內容的文字，切要主旨前後一致，敘事說理文意貫串，字詞句法精準修 飾。利用機器瞬間數百萬次改寫改說，重新置換字詞字句，可輕易躲過剽竊偵測軟體， 達到 100% Unique 獨特原創性，輕鬆取得及格以上滿意的分數。我們若想逆向溯源找 出機器撰寫改說的證據，或是查驗文字內容是否由人類或機器創作，其難度相對高，畢 竟人類語文表達，就本質來說，雖有語法約定俗成的限制，但也容許相當大的自由程 度，同樣意思可以不同字詞句法表達，容許使用不同旨趣細微差別的文字，這也是人工 智慧文字內容生成系統建構所利用的語言特性。 然而，若是不需付出任何努力學習，就可取得一篇精緻完美的報告或論述文章，這 對於學校作為建構知識學習場域實質構成欺瞞，對於社會公益公平負面影響尤其鉅大。 畢竟，學習者工作本質就是學習，抄襲造假不但無助於學習，適足以鼓勵欺瞞負面價 值，更是扼殺學術工作在建構知識本質的意義。因此，學術工作由他人或機器代工都是 違背學術倫理的行為。學習者選擇誠實努力工作或是欺瞞他人找代工，這是倫理善惡的 分野，直接相關學習探索進程。本課程任課教師經審慎考量，本課程授課教師認為本課 程不宜使用生成式人工智慧作為課堂活動內容或學習輔助工具。 5 Prepared by Man-Ting Huang (黃滿庭) 學 生 使 用 AI 條件 ▓ 禁止使用，作業或報告必須由學生本人產出。 (AI-assisted assignments are NOT allowed: only content generated by the student personally can be accepted.) The ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit 善 用 英 語 學 習 資 源 ， 培 養 獨 立 學 習 英 語 的 習 慣 能 力 Classroom Language ■ English 80 % ■ Mandarin 20 % Course Goals / Description 中 高 級 英 文 三 聽 講 為 一 門 2 學 分 學 期 課 程，為 訓 練 中 高 級 程 度 之 大 一 學 生 習 得 進 階 主 題 式 英 語 溝 通 與 表 達 ， 強 化 學 生 思 考 、 組 織 及 表 達 的 整 合 技 能 ； 並 培 養 學 生 發 現 問 題 、 以 英 語 提 問 並 表 達 意 見 的 能 力，經 由 實 境 口 說 與 演 講 訓 練，增 進 學 生 英 語 聽 力 及 訓 練 演 說 技 巧 。 Objective—This semester-based course is aimed at equipping students with listening and speaking competency at the upper-intermediate level. Students will have opportunities to learn the key academic skills through thought-provoking TED talks (signposting with questions, personalizing a presentation, closing a presentation, numbering key points, using your voice effectively, etc.) and get exposed to collaboration, communication, and critical thinking. After having taken this course, students are expected to consolidate their essential knowledge of listening input and speaking output. Requirements—Students are required to prepare the designated learning activities BEFOREHAND, REGULARLY attend the class, ACTIVELY participate in classroom activities, and complete each assignment ON TIME. Aside from class participation and practices based on the textbook, students are encouraged to work on a self‐access learning project based on designated videos, reading texts, and online English-learning materials (VOA News). (You, too, are encouraged to bring stories to class to stimulate discussion.) 4. Regard struggling with ideas as a process of learning. 5. Be open about different ideas. 6. Treat you with respect since you are adult learners. HERE IS WHAT I EXPECT FROM YOU: 1. Class attendance, lesson preparation and active class participation are required. Absence from a class is NO excuse for not knowing the assignment and what has been discussed in that class. Students are required to prepare the designated passages BEFORE class, ACTIVELY participate in class discussions and complete exercise sections ON TIME. Listening input: A variety of authentic English-speaking contexts, including university lectures, interviews, podcasts, and classroom discussions not only activate students’ background knowledge of the topic, prime them for the authentic and inspirational content they will meet in the thought-provoking TED Talks, but also guide them systematically through strategies and activities to meet future academic, personal or professional goals. Specific and key academic skills are focused in each theme-based unit, where students effectively learn to predict, identify main ideas/details/inferences, take notes and manage lengthy input. Pronunciation is also highlighted as an aid to improving both listening comprehension & speaking fluency. Speaking output: Presentation skills inspired by the TED speakers give students the techniques & authentic language they need to successfully deliver their own presentations, help them gain the opportunity to personalize the language they learn, and build their confidence in expressing ideas and opinions. Visual/digital literacy will be promoted through lots of infographics and speaking activities designed to involve students working with a partner or in a group. With connected ideas and integrated language skills, students will give individual, pair and group projects/presentation regularly throughout the semester. The ultimate goals of the course are to encourage students to take charge of their learning and to facilitate their essential 21st century skills—collaboration, communication and critical thinking.
