docs.text: 1 National Tsing Hua University Fall 2026 Upper-Intermediate English III_Reading Class R1R2 COURSE INFORMATION Course Number LANG 103033 Credits 2 Classroom 綜二 204 Class hours □ Monday □ Tuesday □ Wednesday ■ Thursday □ Friday ■ 8:00A.M. – 9:50A.M. □ 10:10A.M. – 12:00P.M. 學生身分別 ■ 頂標生 □ 前標生 □ 中級生 □ 初級生 Extra Enrollments: Not Available 本課程不提供加簽 INSTRUCTOR Name Email Office Office Hour 劉文貞 (Jennifer W. Liu) wenchenl2013@gmail.com 綜二 210 Friday 1:30 pm-3:30 pm (By Appointment) COURSE GOALS & DESCRIPTION This two-credit semester course, High-Intermediate English Reading III, is designed to help first-year college students at a high-intermediate level strengthen and enhance their English reading skills. Through extensive reading, students will develop the ability to quickly and accurately grasp the main ideas and key points of texts, while expanding their vocabulary and reading techniques across various fields. Intensive reading activities will further enable students to understand both concrete and abstract meanings in texts, discuss and analyze the author’s intent, engage in critical thinking, and connect topics to real-world contexts. Class activities include lectures, group discussions, pair practice, and presentations. Upon completing the course, students will be able to: ✓ Read and comprehend texts at a high-intermediate level, using strategies for both extensive and intensive reading. (EAP) ✓ Identify and understand the main ideas and specific details of various texts efficiently and accurately. (EAP) ✓ Expand and retain knowledge of content-specific vocabulary, collocations, synonyms, antonyms, and phrasal verbs for academic and professional contexts. (EAP) ✓ Develop critical thinking skills by evaluating an author’s purpose, tone, and bias, and forming well- supported opinions about the text. (EAP) ✓ Utilize effective study skills, such as note-taking and summarizing, to support academic success. (EAP) ✓ Interpret and integrate information from charts, illustrations, and photographs, alongside textual content. (EAP) ✓ Engage with texts beyond surface-level understanding by forming independent ideas and opinions about key topics. (EAP) 2 UNIVERSITY STUDENT CORE COMPETENCY INDICATORS 課程核心能力 1. The ability to communicate and express oneself in English 英語溝通與表達能力 25% 2. The ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English 深度分析與組織思考能力 25% 3. The knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques 英語學習策略與技巧 25% 4. Global views of English and multicultural diversity 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 10% 5. The ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣能力 15% UNIFORM TEXTBOOK Vargo, M., Blass, L. & Sherman K. (2025). Pathways: Reading, Writing, and Critical Thinking 4 (3rd Edition). National Geographic Learning. ISBN: 9780357980101 CEFR Scale ■ C1 □ B2 □ B1 □ A2+ □ A2 E-LEARN PLATFORM https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw RECOMMENDED ONLINE DICTIONARIES 1. Longman Dictionary of Contemporary English Online https://www.ldoceonline.com/ 2. Cambridge Dictionary https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/ 3. The Free Dictionary http://www.thefreedictionary.com/ REGULATIONS FOR USING AI (AI 使用原則) Students are not allowed to use AI or machine-translation tools, including Google Translate, to generate or translate answers or assignments. This prohibition applies to questions and answers about the presentation article titles, presentation transcripts, and in-class worksheets. However, students may use AI to proofread or revise work that they have written independently in English. When using AI for proofreading or revision, students must submit their original version, the AI revised version, and a list of lessons or insights they gained by comparing the two versions. GRADING 1. Attendance and Participation – 15% 2. Pair Article Presentation – 15 % 3. Quizzes – 20 % 4. In-Class Tasks/ Worksheets – 15 % 5. Assignments – 5% 6. Uniform Final Exam – 30% 3 Class Participation/ Attendance Students are expected to attend each class punctually and actively participate in pair, group, and class discussions. If you cannot attend, you must (1) email the teacher and (2) apply for leave through the university’s online system. For further information, please refer to the following: • Student Leave Policies: https://sa.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/406-1480-264831,r7918.php?Lang=zh-tw • Student Leave Guidelines: https://sa.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/406-1480-269011,r7918.php?Lang=zh-tw • Related Document Downloads: https://sa.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/412-1480-21552.php?Lang=zh-tw Important rules for this course: 1. For sick or personal leave, you must provide valid supporting documentation. ▪ For sick leave, a medical receipt or certificate is required. 2. To arrange a make-up quiz, presentation, or final examination, you must provide official supporting documentation. ▪ Traveling or taking a driver’s license test is not considered an acceptable reason. 3. If your leave request is not approved, it will be counted as an absence. 4. An absence from class is not an excuse for being unaware of assignments, announcements, or material covered in class. It is your responsibility to ask your classmates what you missed and find out what assignments or preparation are required for the next class. Attendance, punctuality, and class participation will be recorded and included in your course evaluation. Attendance will be recording beginning in the first week, so please make sure that you attend the first class and arrive on time. Attendance Policy ➢ Starting score: 9 (起始點: 9 分) ➢ Late arrival: -2 (遲到: 2 分) ➢ Absence: -10 (缺席: 10 分) ➢ Irrelevant activities in class: -2 (做課堂不相關的事: 2 分) The starting attendance score is 9 points. Each late arrival deducts 2 points. Each absence deducts 10 points. Engaging in irrelevant activities in class deducts 2 points. (This includes using a phone for non-class- related activities or working on assignments for other courses.) The score has no lower limit but a maximum of 20 points. In other words, a negative attendance score will lower your semester grade, while a high attendance score can earn you up to 5 extra points towards your semester grade. 出席成績從 9 分開始計算，並依以下規則增減：每次遲到扣 2 分，缺席扣 10 分。若在課堂上從事無關活動 （如使用手機處理與課程無關的事務或做其他課程作業），則扣 2 分。分數累積上限為 20 分，無下限。換 言之，若出席成績為負分，將併入學期成績計算；若累積達 20 分，則學期成績額外加 5 分。 All these seemingly complicated and trivial calculations for attendance and class participation are designed to encourage you to speak more English and participate more actively in class. The more you engage in each class, the more harvest you’ll reap from this course. 4 PAIR ARTICLE PRESENTATION Students will choose an article from the course packet and deliver a 10-minute pair presentation in class. Sign-ups must be completed by the third week, and the presentation schedule will be announced afterward. To fulfill this course requirement, students must: • Begin preparation at least two weeks in advance • Meet all deadlines • Memorize their speeches • Rehearse thoroughly (For further details, see Appendices I & II) IN-CLASS TASKS/WORKSHEETS Each class includes pair or group tasks and discussions, and all students are required to participate actively. At the end of each session, the instructor will collect the worksheets. Four or five will be randomly selected for grading. A group-member evaluation may occasionally be administered after a group task. Students will evaluate each member’s contribution to the task. If a student receives an average peer-evaluation score below 6 out of 10, the instructor will review the student’s contribution to the group task based on the peer evaluations, written comments, completed work, and classroom observations. If insufficient participation is confirmed, the student’s individual worksheet score may be reduced or, in cases of non-participation, recorded as 0. • If you are absent, the worksheet score will be 0. • Late submissions will not be accepted. ASSIGNMENTS All assignments must be typed and turned in on time. Late assignments will not be graded. QUIZZES Two quizzes, as scheduled in the course outline, will test students on both vocabulary and the content of the textbook articles as well as articles presented by classmates. Pop quizzes may also be given before student presentations; these will count for 1/4 of the total 20 % quiz grade. UNIFORM FINAL EXAM The uniform final exam (30% of the semester grade) will take place in the regular classroom at the usual class meeting time in Week 16. It will cover four units of the textbook: Units 1, 4, 6, and 8. Units 1, 4, and 8 will be taught in class, while Unit 6 must be studied independently by students. COPY FEE A copy fee of NT$70-100 will be collected once during the semester to cover the course packet, test sheets and handouts. 5 SUGGESTIONS FOR SUCCESS IN THIS COURSE To get the most out of this course, you are advised to: 1. Attend every class and arrive on time. 2. Volunteer to speak and participate actively in pair, group, and whole-class discussions. 3. Preview the course materials before class. 4. Learn and review new vocabulary every day, and apply what you have learned. 5. Submit assignments, worksheets, and presentation materials by the stated deadlines. Upload electronic files to eeclass and submit printed copies in class when required. o Electronic files allow the instructor to review your work for compliance with the course AI policy. o Printed copies will be used for reading, grading, and providing feedback in order to reduce the instructor’s screen time and eye strain. 6. Please feel free to ask questions whenever you have them. 7. If you have been putting considerable time and effort into the course but still feel that you are falling behind, please reach out to Jennifer for assistance. COURSE SCHEDULE Week Date Main Topic Reading Strategies Critical Thinking 1. 9/10 Course Introduction & Orientation Introduction to the BEST Test of English Proficiency* 2. 9/17 Unit 1 The Changing Workplace Introduction to the BEST Reading Test* ✓ Identifying main ideas and key details (EAP) 3. 9/24 Unit 1 The Changing Workplace Introduction to the BEST Writing Test*  Recognizing claims and counterclaims (EAP) 4. 10/1 Unit 1 The Changing Workplace ✓ Understanding cohesion (EAP) 5. 10/8 Unit 1 The Changing Workplace  Summarizing a text (EAP) 6. 10/15 Unit 4 Rethinking Transport ✓ Recognizing and evaluating different viewpoints (EAP) 7. 10/22 Quiz#1 8. 10/29 Unit 4 Rethinking Transport ✓ Using a concept map (EAP) 6 9. 11/5 Unit 4 Rethinking Transport ✓ Understanding complex sentences (EAP)  Inferring meaning (EAP) 10. 11/12 Unit 4 Rethinking Transport  Comparing and contrasting two perspectives (EAP) 11. 11/19 Unit 8 Living Longer ✓ Reading extended texts (EAP) 12. 11/26 Unit 8 Living Longer ✓ Asking questions as you read (EAP) 13. 12/3 Quiz#2 14. 12/10 Unit 8 Living Longer ✓ Understanding supporting examples (EAP)  Interpreting visual data (EAP) 15. 12/17 Unit 8 Living Longer  Synthesizing (EAP) 16. 12/24 Uniform Final Exam (原班級教室與上課時間 考試) Note: Unit 6, “Why Language Matters,” is designated as a self-learning unit for students. 7 Appendix I: Pair Article Presentation Guidelines Students will choose an article from the course packet and deliver a 10-minute pair presentation in class without using PowerPoint slides. Sign-ups must be completed by Week 3, and the presentation schedule will be announced afterward. To fulfill this requirement, begin preparing at least two weeks in advance, meet all deadlines, memorize your speech, and rehearse thoroughly. I. Two Weeks Before the Presentation Day a) Confirm the article you will present. b) Meet with your partner and divide the work evenly. c) Read the article carefully at least once. d) Post your questions about the article’s title, together with your answers, on eeclass. II. One Week Before the Presentation Day a) Post your subheadings of the article on eeclass. 1. Number all paragraphs first. 2. Group paragraphs logically and give each group a subheading. 3. Use short phrases, not full sentences. b) Post your vocabulary list on eeclass. c) Vocabulary List Guidelines i. This list is different from the “Vocabulary Sharing” portion of your presentation. It should contain at least 15 words; longer or more difficult articles may require additional words. ii. Number the words and list them in the order in which they appear in the article. iii. For each word, include: 1. The word and its part of speech (e.g., noun, verb, or adjective) 2. Its English definition as used in the article 3. A dictionary example sentence illustrating the same meaning iv. If you cannot find an example in dictionaries, use the sentence from your article. Do not invent your own example sentence. v. Recommended dictionaries: 1. Longman Dictionary of Contemporary English http://www.ldoceonline.com/dictionary/epidemic 2. Cambridge Dictionary https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/ 3. TheFreeDictionary http://www.thefreedictionary.com/innumerable ◼ Note: Use Longman first, as definitions in class are usually drawn from it. If not suitable, consult Cambridge, then The Free Dictionary. vi. Do not email me your vocabulary list. Proofreading is your responsibility. However, if you have difficulty finding a definition, you may ask Jennifer. d) Compose your speech as early as possible. e) Memorize your speech and rehearse it thoroughly before presentation day. III. One Day Prior to the Presentation a) Upload your written report to eeclass. b) Print one copy of your written report. 8 IV. On the Day of the Presentation a) Materials • Distribute copies of your vocabulary list to your classmates. • Before presenting, submit one copy of your vocabulary list and one copy of your written report to the instructor. b) Content of the Presentation Your presentation should include: 1. Summary (3 minutes) • Tip: List key words first, and then organize them into main ideas logically in your own words. • Do not copy sentences directly from the article. 2. Vocabulary or Sentence Sharing (2 minutes) • Choose 2 or3 words or phrases that impressed you most. • Explain why you selected them and how they can be used. • You may also share a sentence that you find interesting from the article instead of words or phrases 3. Personal Responses (2 minutes each speaker) • Each presenter must share their own thoughts and reflections on the article. c) Time Limit • Total time: 10 minutes • Article summary: 3 mins. • Vocabulary/ sentence sharing: 2 mins. • Personal responses: 2 mins. per speaker ◼ You must stop immediately when time is up, even if your presentation is unfinished. d) Q&A • After your talk, classmates and the instructor will ask questions about the article or your presentation. • Both presenters must take turns answering. • Students who ask questions will earn extra class participation point for that day. e) Written Report 1. Type a written report that includes your article summary, vocabulary or sentence sharing, and personal responses. 2. Indicate how you and your partner divided the work. 3. Upload your written report to eeclass one day before your presentation. 4. Submit one printed copy to the instructor before presenting. 5. AI Usage Policy: You must not use AI or machine-translation tools, including Google Translate to generate or translate your speech or written report. However, you may use AI to proofread or revise work that you have written independently in English. If you use AI for proofreading or revision, you must also submit: • Your original version; • The AI’s revised version; and • A sort list of lessons or insights you gained by comparing the two versions. 9 Appendix II: Rubric for the Pair Article Presentation Category Description Point Value Volume, Articulation, & Pronunciation • speaks loudly and clearly • articulates words clearly • uses accurate pronunciation 20 Preparation • posts questions about the article title and their answers two weeks prior to the presentation • posts the finalized version of article subheadings and word list on eeclass one week before the presentation • uploads the written report to eeclass one day before the presentation • distributes the copies the vocabulary list on time • submits the written report on time • responds effectively to questions from the instructor and classmates 20 Delivery • delivers a well-organized presentation • avoids unnecessary long pauses • uses an appropriate pace, effective intonation, and natural pauses • maintains sufficient eye contact • presents without reading from notes • manages the allotted time effectively 20 Content Summary: • includes the key points • does not copy sentences from the article • organized Word sharing: • explains the reasons for choosing the words • explains the meanings of the words used in the article • suggests how the words/phrases can be used Response: • meaningful reflection 20 Vocabulary List & Written Report Vocabulary list: • includes all important new words • chooses correct meanings used in the article • few errors • a complete list • numbers and lists the words according to their order of appearance in the article Written report: • typed • few grammatical errors • organized • includes work allocations 20 Total 100

Students are required to prepare the designated passages BEFORE class, ACTIVELY participate in class discussions and complete exercise sections ON TIME. Listening input: A variety of authentic English contexts, including talks, discussions, and conversations not only help expand students’ existing knowledge about interesting and contemporary topics, but also guide them systematically through strategies and activities to meet future academic, personal or professional goals. Specific learning points are focused in each theme-based chapter, where students effectively learn to manage lengthy listening input by predicting, identifying main ideas/details, and taking notes. Pronunciation is also highlighted to improve students’ listening comprehension and speaking fluency. Communicative speaking activities including games, role-plays, and conversation practice are designed to reinforce the chapter content and to allow students to practice integrated language skills. Individual and group projects/presentations will also be given throughout the semester. The ultimate goal of this course is the encourage students to take charge of their own learning and to facilitate the essential l 21st century skills – collaboration, communication and critical thinking. Through extensive reading, students will develop the ability to quickly and accurately grasp the main ideas and key points of texts, while expanding their vocabulary and reading techniques across various fields. Intensive reading activities will further enable students to understand both concrete and abstract meanings in texts, discuss and analyze the author’s intent, engage in critical thinking, and connect topics to real-world contexts. Upon completing the course, students will be able to: ✓ Read and comprehend texts at a high-intermediate level, using strategies for both extensive and intensive reading. (EAP) ✓ Identify and understand the main ideas and specific details of various texts efficiently and accurately. (EAP) ✓ Expand and retain knowledge of content-specific vocabulary, collocations, synonyms, antonyms, and phrasal verbs for academic and professional contexts. (EAP) ✓ Develop critical thinking skills by evaluating an author’s purpose, tone, and bias, and forming well-supported opinions about the text. (EAP) ✓ Utilize effective study skills, such as note-taking and summarizing, to support academic success. (EAP) ✓ Interpret and integrate information from charts, illustrations, and photographs, alongside textual content. (EAP) ✓ Engage with texts beyond surface-level understanding by forming independent ideas and opinions about key topics. (EAP) ✓ Develop foundational academic writing skills, such as crafting clear, concise paragraphs and organizing ideals logically for academic assignments. (EAP) UNIVERSITY STUDENT CORE COMPETENCY INDICATORS 課程核心能力 1. The ability to communicate and express oneself in English 英語溝通與表達能力 25% 2. The ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English 深度分析與組織思考能力 25% 3. The knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques 英語學習策略與技巧 25% 4. Global views of English and multicultural diversity 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 10% 5. The ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣能力 15% UNIFORM TEXTBOOK Vargo, M., Blass, L. & Sherman K. (2025). Pathways: Reading, Writing, and Critical Thinking Book 4 (3rd Edition). National Geographic Learning. ISBN: 9780357980101 CEFR Scale ■ C1 □ B2+ □ B2 □ B1 □ A2+ □ A2 GRADING 1. Attendance and participation – 15% Please refer to the following websites: 國立清華大學學生請假辦法 https://sa.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/406-1480-264831,r7887.php?Lang=zh-tw 學生請假簡介 https://sa.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1480-269011.php?Lang=zh-tw a. Sick leave: Students should ask for sick leave by emailing the teacher or through NTHU’s Academic Information Systems prior to the class One hour of sick leave will lead to 0.5 point-deduction from the final grade. b. Personal leave: Students should notify the teacher with documentary proof ONE week prior to the leave. One hour of personal leave will lead to 0.5 point-deduction from the final grade. c. Absence without valid proof will cost the student 1 point from the final grade for one period of absence. d. Being late for class for more than 10 minutes will lead to 0.5 point-deduction from the final grade. e. Students will get flunked for absence for more than 6 hours with no valid reasons. f. Absence from a class is no excuse for not knowing the assignment and what has been discussed in that class. 2. Assignments – 20% Assignments will mostly be uploaded to Eeclass. Once students finish the assignments, they should upload them to Eeclass. Occasionally hard copies are required, too. Plagiarizing is forbidden and will result in a zero grade. One-week late submission will still be accepted but will lead to loss in grade points. All assignments should be kept till the end of the semester for later reference. 3. Quizzes – 20% If a student is absent on the day when a quiz is given, he/she will have to take a make-up quiz the next week. All quiz papers should be kept till the end of the semester for later reference. 4. Midterm project –15% It includes a quiz on Unit 6 and an assignment. (Unit 6 is a self-study unit.) 5. Uniform Final Exam – 30% The final exam will take place in the usual classrooms and in the regular class meeting hours in Week 15(Dec. 18). Four units( Units 1, 4, 6, & 8) will be covered. Three units (Units 1, 4 and 8) will be taught in class, while students will need to study Unit 6 by themselves. CLASSROOM LANGUAGE  English _70_%  Mandarin _30_% SUGGESTED CLASS ACTIVITIES ⚫ Jigsaw reading □ This cooperative learning strategy has students fully engaged in class. And while taking turns teaching their home group about their section of the text, they also practice how to express themselves clearly. A group assignment follows the reading. ⚫ Writing practice □ Students practice writing short answers or essays on questions/topics related to the text in the textbook. All practices call for critical thinking. ⚫ Group discussion □ Students discuss topics provided at the beginning of each unit and share conclusion reached in their group. ⚫ Vocabulary building activities □ Expand and apply vocabulary through tasks such as word maps, matching synonyms, and writing stories, enhancing understanding and usage in context. ⚫ Reading comprehension practice □ Students practice paraphrasing, identifying main-idea sentences, and writing outlines and summaries. REGULATIONS FOR USING AI Students are not allowed to use AI to generate any assignments. However, they are allowed to use AI to revise their assignments. When doing so, students need to provide their original version, the revised version by the AI, and a list of lessons or insights they have gained from the AI’s revised version. CLASSROOM RULES 1. Class attendance, lesson preparation and active class participation are required. 2. Plagiarism and cheating on the exam are forbidden. If someone is found plagiarizing or cheating on an exam, it means he/she will get a zero point for that assignment/exam. 3. In-class practices should be kept at least till the end of the semester for later reference or final exam. 4. Cellular phones should be turned off during the two-hour class period. COURSE SCHEDULE Week Date Main Topic Reading Strategies Critical Thinking 1. 9/11 Course Introduction & Orientation Introduction to the BEST Test of English Proficiency* 2. 9/18 Unit 1 The Changing Workplace Introduction to the BEST Reading Test* Identifying main ideas and key details (EAP) 3. 9/25 No Class (Mid-Autumn Festival) 4. 10/2 Unit 1 The Changing Workplace Introduction to the BEST Writing Test* Recognizing claims and counterclaims (EAP) 5. 10/9 No Class (Double Tenth Day) 6. 10/16 Unit 1 The Changing Workplace Quiz on Unit 1 Understanding cohesion (EAP) Summarizing a text (EAP) 7. 10/23 Unit 4 Rethinking Transport Recognizing and evaluating different viewpoints (EAP) 8. 10/30 Unit 4 Rethinking Transport Using a concept map (EAP) 9. 11/6 Unit 4 Rethinking Transport Understanding complex sentences (EAP) Inferring meaning (EAP) 10. 11/13 Unit 4 Rethinking Transport Quiz on Unit 4 Comparing and contrasting two perspectives (EAP) 11. 11/20 Unit 8 Living Longer Reading extended texts (EAP) 12. 11/27 Unit 8 Living Longer Asking questions as you read (EAP) 13. 12/4 Unit 8 Living Longer Understanding supporting examples (EAP) Interpreting visual data (EAP) 14. 12/11 Quiz on Unit 8 Unit 6 outline & summary Synthesizing (EAP) 15. 12/18 Uniform Final Exam 16. 12/25 No Class (Constitution Day)

Through extensive reading, students will develop the ability to accurately grasp the main ideas and key points of the text, while expanding their vocabulary and acquiring various reading techniques each week through sufficient demonstration and practice. Intensive reading activities will enable students to understand both concrete and abstract meanings of the text, analyze the author’s intentions, and engage in critical thinking. Weekly assignments will allow students to apply their academic skills in writing that trains their research ability in composing short essays for academic or test purposes. 1 Through individual presentation or as a group, students will learn to connect topics with language use in real-world contexts and broaden their horizons, while collaborating with classmates to propose solutions to the task as required. (EAP)  Develop critical thinking skills by evaluating an author’s purpose, tone, and bias, and forming well- supported opinions about the text. (EAP)  Utilize effective study skills, such as note-taking and summarizing, to support academic success. (EAP)  Interpret and integrate information from charts, illustrations, and photographs, alongside textual content. (EAP)  Engage with texts beyond surface-level understanding by forming independent ideas and opinions about key topics. (EAP)  Develop foundational academic writing skills, such as crafting clear, concise paragraphs and organizing ideals logically for academic assignments. (EAP) UNIVERSITY STUDENT CORE COMPETENCY INDICATORS 課程核心能力 1. The ability to communicate and express oneself in English 英語溝通與表達能力 20% 2. The ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English 深度分析與組織思考能力 25% 3. The knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques 英語學習策略與技巧 20% 4. Pathways: Reading, Writing, and Critical Thinking (3rd Edition). CEFR Scale ■ B2+ □ B2 □ B1 □ A2+ □ A2 2 GRADING 1. Attendance and participation – 15% 2. Assignments – 30% 3. Presentations – 10% 4. Midterm exam – 15% 5. Uniform Final Exam – 30% UNIFORM FINAL EXAM The uniform final exam, accounting for 30% of the semester grade, will take place in the usual classrooms and at the regular class meeting times in Week 16.  Pathways: Units 1, 4, 6, & 8 *Note: Among the 4 units, unit 6 is designated as a self-learning unit for students. *All 4 units of the textbook will be included in the final exam. CLASSROOM LANGUAGE ■ English ___85____% ■ Mandarin ____15_____% CLASS ACTIVITIES  Group or individual presentations ■ Research, prepare, and deliver presentations on assigned topics, developing communication skills, confidence, and the ability to organize and share ideas effectively.  Jigsaw reading ■ Divide an article or text into sections. Students read their section, summarize it, and share it with peers to complete the full picture.  Critical analysis discussions ■ Choose articles or essays and have students discuss the author’s purpose, tone, and main arguments.  Discussion Circles ■ Provide prompts related to course content or current events. Students take turns sharing opinions and supporting their ideas with examples.  Vocabulary building activities ■ Expand and apply vocabulary through tasks such as word maps, matching synonyms, and writing stories, enhancing understanding and usage in context.  Interpretation projects ■ Analyze and interpret information from texts, charts, graphs and illustrations. Present findings clearly and connect them to real-world applications. REGULATIONS FOR USING AI ■ Conditionally open: students may use generative AI in assignments for finding data or facts only. CLASS RULES 1. Class attendance, lesson preparation, and active class participation are required. 3 2. Absence from a class is NO excuse for not knowing the assignment and what has been discussed in that class missed. Absentees should ask for fellow classmates’ help to catch up with what has been and will be covered in the classes. 3. Plagiarism or cheating on the exam is absolutely prohibited. If anyone is found plagiarizing or cheating on an exam, a zero point will be given to that exam. 4. There will be NO make-up exams/presentations unless valid and official reasons for absence are presented beforehand. 5. Cellular phones should be muted or turned off during the two-hour class period. COURSE SCHEDULE (Syllabus) *Note: During the first 3 weeks, instructors introduce the BESTEP test, an academically oriented English proficiency assessment developed specifically for college students in Taiwan. Instructors focus on the Reading and Writing sections and explain that the required academic reading and writing skills will be covered throughout the course. docs.text: i National Tsing Hua University 中高級選讀英文 時事英文 Readings on Current Affairs Fall 2026_M56 COURSE INFORMATION LANG 2000 _01_ Credits 2 Classroom GEN II R204 (綜二 204) Class Hours ■ Monday □ Tuesday □ Wednesday □ Thursday □ Friday ■ 1:20P.M. – 3:10P.M. □ 3:30P.M. – 5:20P.M. □ _____ P.M. – _____P.M. Course Type □ EGP (English for general purposes) ■ EAP (English for academic purposes) □ EOP (English for occupational purposes) Language Level □ B1（中級） □ B1-B2 ■ B2（中高級） □ B2+ □ C1 Core Ability ■ comprehension/reception □ communication/interaction □ production 可選課學生 身分別 ■ 頂標生 ■ 前標生 □ 中級生 □ 初級生 Prerequisites 本校必修英語課程 INSTRUCTOR Name Email Office & Tel Office Hour 劉文貞 wenchenl2013@gmail.com 綜二 210 Friday 1:30-3:30 pm (By Appointment Only) EXTRA ENTROLMMENTS: Not Available 本課程不開放加簽 This course does not accept additional enrollments. If you are interested, you may attend the first class and continue checking the course registration system. Because of the strict attendance and participation policy, some seats may become available during the first three weeks. COURSE GOALS & DESCRIPTION 1. Primary aim This course equips students with the ability to read English news articles and express opinions on news and current issues, preparing them for future academic studies. It seeks to stimulate interest, expand vocabulary in journalistic English, and build background knowledge of diverse topics—politics, society, finance, technology, medicine, environment, humanities, arts, leisure, and sports—through extensive exposure to authentic news articles. 2. Subsidiary aim By completing the course, students will be able to: ⚫ understand the structure and characteristics of news writing ⚫ extend and consolidate vocabulary and reading skills across fields ⚫ appreciate satire, humor, and metaphor in news reports ⚫ gain familiarity with historical and cultural contexts of current affairs ⚫ develop critical thinking, participate in discussions, and express opinions ⚫ build habits of reading, listening to, and watching news reports ii UNIVERSITY STUDENT CORE COMPETENCY INDICATORS 英文核心能力指標 No. Core Competency Indicators % 1. 英語溝通與表達能力 (ability to communicate and express oneself in English) 20 2. 深度分析與組織思考的能力 (ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English) 25 3. 英語學習策略與技巧 (knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques) 20 4. 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 (global views of English and multicultural diversity) 25 5. 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣與能力 (ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit) 10 TEACHING MATERIALS AND REFERENCES Textbook(s) 自編教材 News articles from The New York Times, The Washington Post, The Guardian, Taipei Times, and Taiwan News etc. News broadcasts from CNN, BBC, FOX News, ICRT and FTV English edition, etc. CEFR Scale □ B1 □ B1-B2 ■ B2 ■ B2+ □ C1 E-LEARN PLATFORM https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw RECOMMENDED ONLINE DICTIONARIES 1. Longman Dictionary of Contemporary English Online https://www.ldoceonline.com/ 2. Cambridge Dictionary https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/ 3. The Free Dictionary http://www.thefreedictionary.com/ REGULATIONS FOR USING AI (AI 使用原則) Students are not allowed to use AI or machine-translation tools, including Google Translate, to generate or translate answers or assignments. This prohibition applies to questions and answers about the presentation article titles, presentation transcripts, and in-class worksheets. However, students may use AI to proofread or revise work that they have written independently in English. When using AI for proofreading or revision, students must submit their original version, the AI revised version, and a list of lessons or insights they gained by comparing the two versions. iii COURSE REQUIREMENTS 1) Attendance and Participation 15 % 2) Quizzes 30 % 3) News Presentation 20 % 4) In-Class Tasks/ Worksheets 10 % 5) Take-Home Assignments 15 % 6) FutureLearn Videos 10 % Class Participation/ Attendance Students are expected to attend each class punctually and actively participate in pair, group, and class discussions. If you cannot attend, you must (1) email the teacher and (2) apply for leave through the university’s online system. For further information, please refer to the following: • Student Leave Policies: https://sa.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/406-1480-264831,r7918.php?Lang=zh-tw • Student Leave Guidelines: https://sa.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/406-1480-269011,r7918.php?Lang=zh-tw • Related Document Downloads: https://sa.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/412-1480-21552.php?Lang=zh-tw Important rules for this course: 1. For sick or personal leave, you must provide valid supporting documentation. ▪ For sick leave, a medical receipt or certificate is required. 2. To arrange a make-up quiz, presentation, or final examination, you must provide official supporting documentation. ▪ Traveling or taking a driver’s license test is not considered an acceptable reason. 3. If your leave request is not approved, it will be counted as an absence. 4. An absence from class is not an excuse for being unaware of assignments, announcements, or material covered in class. It is your responsibility to ask your classmates what you missed and find out what assignments or preparation are required for the next class. Attendance, punctuality, and class participation will be recorded and included in your course evaluation. Attendance will be recording beginning in the first week, so please make sure that you attend the first class and arrive on time. Attendance Policy ➢ Starting score: 9 (起始點: 9 分) ➢ Late arrival: -2 (遲到: 2 分) ➢ Absence: -10 (缺席: 10 分) ➢ Irrelevant activities in class: -2 (做課堂不相關的事: 2 分) The starting attendance score is 9 points. Each late arrival deducts 2 points. Each absence deducts 10 points. Engaging in irrelevant activities in class deducts 2 points. (This includes using a phone for non-class-related activities or working on assignments for other courses.) The score has no lower limit but a maximum of 20 points. In other words, a negative attendance score will lower your semester grade, while a high attendance score can earn you up to 5 extra points towards your semester grade. 出席成績從 9 分開始計算，並依以下規則增減：每次遲到扣 2 分，缺席扣 10 分。若在課堂上從事 無關活動（如使用手機處理與課程無關的事務或做其他課程作業），則扣 2 分。分數累積上限為 20 iv 分，無下限。換言之，若出席成績為負分，將併入學期成績計算；若累積達 20 分，則學期成績額外 加 5 分。 All these seemingly complicated and trivial calculations for attendance and class participation are designed to encourage you to speak more English and participate more actively in class. The more you engage in each class, the more harvest you’ll reap from this course. QUIZZES Two scheduled quizzes (see course outline) will test students on: • Vocabulary • Content of the news articles discussed in class and presented by peers • News reading strategies and writing conventions In addition, pop quizzes may be given before student news presentations. Pop quizzes will account for one-third of the quiz grade (10% of the final grade). NEWS PRESENTATION Students must select a news section (e.g. international news, national news, or opinion, etc.) and give EITHER a group OR an individual presentation. The chosen article must be printed and distributed to all classmates at least one week prior to the presentation day. To succeed, students should begin preparing at least 3 weeks in advance, meet all deadlines, memorize their speeches, and rehearse thoroughly so that they can deliver their presentation confidently without reading from a script. (See Appendices I and II for details.) IN-CLASS TASKS/WORKSHEETS Every class will include individual, pair or group tasks and discussions. Each student is expected to participate actively and contribute meaningfully. At the end of the class, worksheets will be collected. 3 or 4 will be randomly selected for grading. A group-member evaluation may occasionally be administered after a group task. Students will evaluate each member’s contribution to the task. If a student receives an average peer-evaluation score below 6 out of 10, the instructor will review the student’s contribution to the group task based on the peer evaluations, written comments, completed work, and classroom observations. If insufficient participation is confirmed, the student’s individual worksheet score may be reduced or, in cases of non-participation, recorded as 0. • If you are absent, the worksheet score will be 0. • Late submissions will not be accepted TAKE-HOME ASSIGNMENTS All take-home assignments must be typed and turned in on time. These assignments are designed to build on class progress, so late work cannot be graded. FUTURELEARN VIDEOS Students are required to watch the assigned Future Learn videos (https://www.futurelearn.com/ ) and complete the related discussions, exercises, or tests. Since there is not enough class time to introduce all of v the essential materials, these videos provide explanations of news English conventions and news reading strategies. They are an important supplement to the course and ensure that students come to class prepared to apply these concepts in discussions and assignments. COPY FEE A copy fee of NT$100-120 will be collected once during the semester to cover the course packet, test sheets and handouts. INSTRUCTOR’S GUIDELINES FOR SUCCESS To get the most of this course, you are advised to: 1. Attend all classes regularly and on time. 2. Contribute actively to pair, group, and class discussions. 3. PREVIEW EACH NEWS ARTICLE (including the PRESENTATION ARTICLE) BEFORE CLASS. Use the news reading strategies we practice in class, and come with subheadings and annotations prepared. 4. Ask questions whenever you don’t understand—your curiosity helps everyone learn. 5. Submit assignments, worksheets, and presentation materials by the stated deadlines. Upload electronic files to eeclass and submit printed copies in class when required.  Electronic files allow the instructor to review your work for compliance with the course AI policy.  Printed copies will be used for reading, grading, and providing feedback in order to reduce the instructor’s screen time and eye strain. 6. Browse news headlines and stories and listen to or watch English news broadcasts regularly to stay familiar with current affairs. 7. Review and build your vocabulary every day—it’s the key to understanding more. 8. If you have been putting considerable time and effort into the course but still feel that you are falling behind, please reach out to Jennifer for assistance. To succeed, students should begin preparation about 3 weeks in advance, meet all deadlines, and rehearse carefully. Three Weeks Before the Presentation Day a) Begin browsing news headlines to find a topic that interests you. (Make sure it belongs to the news section you have signed up for the presentation.) b) Email Jennifer the link (URL) to the article instead of attaching a file. In your email, include your presentation date, the news section you’ve signed up for, and the correct word count of the article. c) How to choose an article Please choose your news article from the following sources: i. Newspapers: ◼ English newspapers in Taiwan: Taipei Times, Taiwan News ◼ U.S. newspapers: The New York Times, Washington Post, Los Angeles Times, etc. ◼ UK newspapers: The Times, The Guardian, etc. ii. News agencies: AP, Reuters, CNA (https://focustaiwan.tw/) , etc. If you wish to use another source, please discuss it with me in advance. d) The article must be published after the first day of this semester, __Sep. 7 __. e) Make sure the article belongs to the news section you signed up for. f) The article length should be between 470 and 1200 words. This ensure it is substantial enough for analysis but still manageable within the presentation time. g) Please email me your article early to allow time for approval and preparation. (Do not wait until the last minute.) h) Once your article has been finalized, please keep it. This will give you enough time to focus on preparation and practice. II. Two Weeks Before the Presentation Day a) You should have finalized your article choice with Jennifer by now. b) Post your article link on eeclass. c) Post your questions on the headline as well as their answers on eeclass. d) For Group Presentations Only: ✓ Show Jennifer a printed outline of your presentation. ✓ Make an appointment with Jennifer to present in her office. III. One Week Before the Presentation Day a)Distribute copies of your presentation article to your classmates in class. (**Week 16 presenters must distribute the article copies on Dec. 7th (for M56 Class) and Dec. 10th (For R56 Class) 1. When preparing the original copy, include the date, and the name of the newspaper, the ix news agency, and the journalist(s). The font size should be at least 12 pt, and leave 1-inch margin space for classmates to take notes. 2. DO NOT CHANGE THE ARTICLE’S LAYOUT, INCLUDING NUMBERING THE PARAGRAPHS OR HIGHLIGHING THE VOCAB WORDS. 3. Before making copies, please email Jennifer the original file for approval. b) Post your subheadings of the article on eeclass. 1. Number the paragraphs first. 2. Group the paragraphs and give each group a subheading. 3. Subheadings should be phrases not full sentences. c) Post your vocab list of the article on eeclass. 1. The vocabulary list is different from ‘word sharing.’ It should contain around 15 or more words, depending on the length and difficulty level of the article. 2. How to make the vocabulary list i. Create a list of words you don't know from this article. Each entry must include the word, its part of speech, (e.g. noun, verb, or adjective, etc.), the English definition used this article, and an example sentence. ii. Number the words in the order they appear in the article. iii. If you cannot find an example sentence from dictionaries, you may use the sentence from the article. Do not create your own sentence. iv. Use the following dictionaries to look up definitions and examples: 1. Longman Dictionary of Contemporary English http://www.ldoceonline.com/dictionary/epidemic 2. Cambridge Dictionary https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/ 3. TheFreeDictionary http://www.thefreedictionary.com/innumerable Note: Please consult Longman or Cambridge first. The definitions I provide in class are mostly from these two dictionaries because they are easier to understand and remember. If you cannot find a suitable definition there, then use TheFreeDictionary. d) Do not email me your vocab list. You are responsible for proofreading it. However, if you have trouble finding a suitable definition for a word, you are welcome to ask Jennifer. e)Compose your speech as early as possible. f) Memorize and rehearse your speech well before your presentation day. g) For Group Presentations Only: 1. Have your ppt slides 100% ready for the 2nd meeting. 2. Bring your own laptop, the article you will present, and a hard copy of your vocabulary list. 3. Before 2nd meeting, download all the files you will need, including your PowerPoint slides, Kahoot questions and answers, and any videos you plan to use during your presentation. Note: Internet access in my office is unreliable. Waiting for files to download during the meeting wastes valuable time. Failure to download all necessary files in advance will result in a deduction from your preparation score. 4. Arrive at Jennifer’s office on time and deliver your entire presentation. 5. Take notes on Jennifer’s feedback during the meeting and revise your presentation accordingly. x IV. On the Presentation Day a) Distribute copies of the vocabulary list to your classmates, and submit one copy of the vocabulary list to the teacher during the class recess. b) [For Individual Presentations Only] Turn in your written report to the teacher before you step up to the podium to present. c) Content of the Presentation & Time Limit ◼ Individual News Presentation (7 mins.) (With NO ppt slides) 1) News summary (3 mins.) : Summarize the news story. Tip: List some key words first. Then, organize the key words/main ideas in your own logic and in your own words. 2) Vocabulary word sharing (2 mins.) : Choose one or two new words you learned from the article and explain why the words made a strong impression on you. If time allows, you may also share a sentence from the article that you find interesting. 3) Your response to the news story (2 mins.) : Share your personal thoughts or reactions after reading the article. Q&A: After your presentation, your classmates and the teacher will ask you questions about the article or your presentation. (Students who ask questions can earn extra class participation points that day.) ◼ Group News Presentation (25 mins.) (WITH ppt slides) 1) Warm-Up Activity (5 mins.) 2) Vocabulary (3 mins.) 3) Comprehension of the News Article (10 mins.) • Comprehension Questions • Subheadings 4) Extended Discussion (6 mins.) 5) Conclusion (1 min.) Please complete your speech within the time limit. When the time is up, you must stop immediately, even if you have not finished. d) Written Report (For Individual Presentations Only) 1. docs.text: 1 National Tsing Hua University 中高級選讀英文 (中英文筆譯 English-Chinese Translation) Fall 2026 Course Number LANG 2000 __06___ Credits 2 Classroom 綜二館 105 Class hours ■ Monday □ Tuesday □ Wednesday □ Thursday □ Friday ■ 1:20P.M. – 3:10P.M. □ 3:30P.M. – 5:20P.M. □ _____ P.M. – 5_____P.M. Course Type □ EGP (English for general purposes) ■ EAP (English for academic purposes) □ EOP (English for occupational purposes) Language Level □ B1（中級） □ B1-B2 ■ B2（中高級） ■ B2+ □ C1 Core Ability ■ comprehension/reception □ communication/interaction ■ production 可選課學生 身分別 ■ 頂標生 ■ 前標生 □ 中級生 □ 初級生 Prerequisites 中高級英文一／二 Instructor & Contact Information: Name Email Office & Tel Office Hour Emily Zhang yatsun.chang@gmail.com - email for appointment Course Aims / Description Primary aim After taking the course, students will have learnt basic translation techniques needed in translation from English to Chinese, and practiced translating various sentence patterns and texts. Students are also expected to apply acquired skills in translating texts from their field of studies, short essays of their interests and news reports. Subsidiary aim Students will be guided to analyze and translate different texts. Throughout the process, students will become more aware of the linguistic differences between Chinese and English. Skills of sight translation will also be introduced and practiced to facilitate class activities. Corresponding CEFR Can-do statements Can-do statement #1: I can understand articles, reports and reviews in which the writers express specific points of views. (reading) Can-do statement #2: I can understand the main points in formal and informal letters relating to my personal and professional interests, with occasional use of a dictionary. (reading) Can-do statement #3: I can write clear, detailed descriptions on a variety of subjects related to my field of interest. (written production) Can-do statement #4: I can generally cover gaps in vocabulary and structure with paraphrases. (written production) 2 Can-do statement #5: I can use a variety of strategies to achieve comprehension, including checking comprehension by using contextual clues. docs.text: prepared by Vicky Hsu1 National Tsing Hua University 中高級選讀英文－AI 輔助學術寫作 AI-assisted English Writing for Academic Purposes Fall 2026 Course Information Course Number LANG 2000 04 Credits 2 Classroom 綜二館 201 教室 Class Hours ■ Monday □ Tuesday □ Wednesday □ Thursday □ Friday □ 1:20P.M. – 3:10P.M. ■ 3:30P.M. – 5:20P.M. Course Type □ EGP (English for general purposes) ■ EAP (English for academic purposes) □ EOP (English for occupational purposes) Language Level □ B1（中級） □ B1-B2 ■ B2（中高級） □ B2+ □ C1 Core Ability ■ comprehension/reception □ communication/interaction ■ production 可選課學生 身分別 ■ 頂標生 ■ 前標生 □ 中級生 □ 初級生 Prerequisites • Students have taken up Upper-Intermediate English I/II or III. • Students are familiar with English sentence patterns and the most frequent 3000 words in English. • Students aim to write and publish their own ideas, opinions, and evaluations for academic purposes. 加簽說明  不開放加簽。所有學生須由選課系統亂數選課。 Instructor & Contact Information Name Email Office & Tel Office Hour 徐桂平 Vicky Hsu personal messaging on eeclass1 綜二館 B 側 209 ( 34417) Tuesday 10:00 A.M.-12:00 P.M. 綜二館 B 側 209 Course Aims / Description 1. Primary aim This writing course is designed for students who are novice writers for academic purposes. It aims to prepare students for developing basic writing strategies and skills and organizing their ideas within PARAGRAPHs, along with AI integration and collaboration. Sentence-building, analysis of common academic writing models, and paragraph-writing practices engage students in designing and expressing the flow of ideas. Collaboration with AI helps provide quick reviews, diagnoses, feedback, and 1 No email will be replied to, especially when the sender’s email address does not belong to the student. Please leave messages on eeclass, using the “personal messages” function. eeclass email prepared by Vicky Hsu2 suggestions to help students revise ideas and structures in paragraphs, edit with a sophisticated use of language (syntax, lexicon, transitions, and punctuation), and even improve the writing style for academic purposes. After completing this subject, students are expected to write more skillfully and independently to express and communicate their ideas more effectively in PARAGRAPHs for academic purposes. Note: This course focuses mainly on writing, not using AI tools or applications to write for a human being. Students are expected to practice their own writing before working with AI to receive feedback and suggestions for polishing their writing. 2. Subsidiary aim In this class, students will have opportunities to 1. Reviewing writing basics—syntax and lexicon • Review parts of speech and basic sentence patterns • Practice sentence-building skills and strategies (expanding, combining, reducing, & relocating) 2. Analyzing writing models • Identify paragraph structure and develop the fundamental types of sentences in a paragraph (the topic sentence, supporting sentences, and the concluding sentence) • Analyze the model writing examples to build and organize a paragraph structure 3. Collaborative & independent writing practices • Practice writing 2-3 types of common academic writing models collaboratively and independently • Revise and edit their writing for clarity (cohesion & coherence) and appropriate use of vocabulary, grammar, and transitional devices (with the help of AI) 4. AI-Human Collaboration • Create prompts and rubrics for AI to diagnose and evaluate the writing tasks • Identify and correct common mistakes in word choice and grammar points (with the help of AI) • Polish language use with precise lexicon and concise sentence structure • Detect the flaw and the logical fallacy in the flow of ideas. 3. Corresponding CEFR Can-do statements Reception Reading OVERALL READING COMPREHENSION B2 Can read with a large degree of independence, adapting style and speed of reading to different texts and purposes, and using appropriate reference sources selectively. Has a broad active reading vocabulary, but may experience some difficulty with low- frequency vocabulary. [overall reading comprehension] READING FOR INFORMATION & ARGUMENT B2 Can understand articles and reports concerned with contemporary problems in which the writer adopts particular stances or viewpoints. [reading for information & argument] prepared by Vicky Hsu3 B2+ Can obtain information, ideas and opinions from highly specialized sources within his/her field. [reading for information & argument] EAP EOP Interact ionWriting OVERALL WRITTEN INTERACTION B2 Can express news and views effectively in writing, and relate to those of others. [overall written interaction] Production Written OVERALL WRITTEN PRODUCTION B2 Can write clear, detailed texts on a variety of subjects related to his/her field of interest, synthesizing and evaluating information and arguments from a number of sources. [overall written production] EAP EOP CREATIVE WRITING B2 Can write clear, detailed descriptions on a variety of subjects related to his/her field of interest. [creative writing] REPORTS & ESSAYS B2 Can write an essay or report which develops an argument, giving reasons in support of or against a particular point of view and explaining the advantages and disadvantages of various options. [reports & essays] EAP EOP B2+ Can write an essay or report that develops an argument systematically with appropriate highlighting of significant points and relevant supporting detail. [reports & essays] EAP EOP Reception Communi cation Strategies IDENTIFYING CUES & INFERRING (SPOKEN & WRITTEN) B2 Can use a variety of strategies to achieve comprehension, including listening for main points, checking comprehension by using contextual clues. [identifying cues & inferring (spoken & written)] EAP Working with Text Communicative Language NOTE-TAKING (LECTURES, SEMINARS, ETC.) B2 Can understand a clearly structured lecture on a familiar subject, and can take notes on points which strike him/her as important, even though he/she tends to concentrate on the words themselves and therefore to miss some information. [note-taking (lectures, seminars, etc.) EAP PROCESSING TEXT B2 Can summarize extracts from news items, interviews or documentaries containing opinions, argument and discussion. [processing text] EAP Communicative LanguageRange GENERAL LINGUISTIC RANGE B2 Has a sufficient range of language to be able to give clear descriptions, express viewpoints and develop arguments without much conspicuous searching for words, using some complex sentence forms to do so. [general linguistic range] EAP VOCABULARY RANGE prepared by Vicky Hsu4 B2 Has a good range of vocabulary for matters connected to his/her field and most general topics. [vocabulary range] Control GRAMMATICAL ACCURACY B2 Shows a relatively high degree of grammatical control. Does not make mistakes which lead to misunderstanding. [grammatical accuracy] VOCABULARY CONTROL B2 Lexical accuracy is generally high, though some confusion and incorrect word choice does occur without hindering communication. [vocabulary control] ORTHOGRAPHIC CONTROL B2 Spelling, punctuation and layout are accurate but may show signs of mother tongue influence. [orthographic control] Pragmatic THEMATIC DEVELOPMENT B2 Can develop a clear description or narrative, expanding and supporting his/her main points with relevant supporting detail and examples. [thematic development] EAP COHERENCE B2 Can use a limited number of cohesive devices to link his/her utterance into clear, coherent discourse, though there may be some “jumpiness” in a long contribution. [coherence] EAP B2+ Can use a variety of linking words efficiently to mark clearly the relationships between ideas. [coherence] EAP EOP 英文核心能力指標 University Student Core Competency Indicators No. Core Competency Indicators 1. 英語溝通與表達能力 (ability to communicate and express oneself in English) 30% 2. 深度分析與組織思考的能力 (ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English) 20% 3. 英語學習策略與技巧 (knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques) 30% 4. 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 (global views of English and multicultural diversity) 10% 5. 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣與能力 (ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit) 10% Teaching Materials and References Textbook(s) 1. Gemini https://gemini.google.com/ 4. NotebookLM https://notebooklm.google/ 5. Grammarly https://app.grammarly.com/ 6. Quillbot https://quillbot.com/ prepared by Vicky Hsu6 Grading Scheme 1. Attendance and participation (cf. Requirements and rules 1, 2, 6, and 7) 15% 2. Paragraph Writing & Revision (3 rough drafts plus 2-3 revised drafts, 2 personal reflections on collaboration with AI) (cf. Requirements and rules 3-5) 50% 3. Self-access learning project on Microsoft Forms (grammar/syntax and writing basics) 10% 4. Grammar / Vocabulary exercises (cf. Requirements and rules 3-5) 15% 5. Pair presentation (grammar points and sentence structures) (cf. Requirements and rules 6) 5% 6. Teacher-student conferences (one-on-one discussions about rough drafts) 5% Note: The percentage of this grading scheme is subject to possible adjustments. To be announced. Requirements & Rules 1. Class attendance, lesson preparation and active class participation are required.  As you are all present whenever the instructor takes attendance, you will get 60% (9 points) in this category Attendance and Participation. 經常性點名，全勤者可得「出席與參與」項目 中的 60%（9 分）成績。  Each skip will cost 2 points from the category Attendance and Participation (up to 15 points in the final grade). 未假不到課（翹課），每次從「出席與參與」成績（占學期成績 15 分）扣 2 分。  If you are absent in case of UNCONTROLLABLE situations (e.g. illness, emergency, important occasions, etc.), please apply for a leave on the Student Leave System on Academic Information System of National Tsing Hua University or on the iNTHU app (from the Office of Student Affair website), with clear leave information, including leave type, leave period, and reasons (must be clear and valid enough for the teacher’s approval). As the reasons or the documents are not clear, valid or sufficient enough, the teacher may deny the application. 遇不可抗力情形需請假者，請於本校校務資訊系統上的學 生請假系統或下載 iNTHU APP，填寫資料（請假類別、請假日期、請假事由）。請假事由須合理並 敘述清楚，提供老師是否准假之參考。請假單上的理由或所附證明文件不清楚或不充分時， 該次請假申請得不予核准。  Please observe the information you are expected to offer for each of the following leave types:  For sick leave, please describe severe symptoms and medical treatments you have been taking in the box “Reason.” 請病假時，請於理由欄位說明影響上課之顯著症狀，就醫或服 藥等處理。  For personal leave, please describe the uncontrollable incident and how it makes you absent from the class. 請事假時，請於理由欄位敘明該不可抗力事件，並說明該事件如何 致使你無法前來上課。  Please observe the school calendar and avoid arranging any (family or personal) vacations or trips during the semester. No scheduled arrangements for pleasure or personal NTHU Q&A prepared by Vicky Hsu7 convenience will be considered uncontrollable incidents. 請依本校行事曆，避免於學期間 以個人或家庭為由安排度假、旅遊活動。任何與玩樂或個人方便之安排，皆無法歸類為不可 抗力事件。  No leave application will be approved on the dates of presentations, peer evaluations, and midterm/final exams. Please care for your health and reserve the time for these important class activities. 報告、同儕互評、期中／期末考當日不得請假。請注意身心健康 並為這些重要課程活動預留時間。  There will be NO make-up exams or presentations unless you apply for leave with valid and official reasons for your absence beforehand. 無合理且正式的缺課原因，將不予補考 或補行報告。  You are expected to apply for leave before the class you are absent from. Any overdue leave application must be made within 7 days from the last day of absence. 請假以事先申請為原 則。逾期請假申請必須於 7 日內補請。未能於規定期間申請者，均以曠課論。  Being late for more than 10 minutes (with no valid excuses) is treated as absence from that hour (1 point deducted). Being late for more than 30 minutes is treated as absence from the whole class (2-points deducted). 無故遲到逾 10 分鐘，以該小時未到課紀錄（扣 1 分）。遲 到逾 30 分鐘，視為該次上課未到課（扣 2 分）。  No points will be deducted for your ATTENDANCE as long as your approved leave is no more than 6 hours. However, you may lose points for your PARTICIPATION or in-class practices scheduled on the date of your absence. 核准的請假時數未逾 6 小時，不扣出席成績。惟當日 如有上課練習或小組活動，請假者無法參與或完成，將無法獲得該次練習或該項評量成績。換 言之，缺課仍可能影響「參與」與「作業」等成績。  If you skip class for more than 8 hours, your course withdrawal may NOT be approved, and you will get 0 credits for this course. 無故不到課逾 8 小時者，將不予同意其停修申請，亦無 法取得本課程學分。  A student will fail to get the 2 credits for missing 5 classes, including the ones due to any kinds of leaves. 缺課達五次（含各類請假缺課）者，將無法從本課程獲取任何學分。 2. Absence from a class is no excuse for failing to complete in-class practices, to submit assignments in time, or to get informed of assignments or the class you have missed. It is your responsibility to hand in the assignments within 5 days (weekends & holidays included) and to reach your classmates or the instructor and refer to the course platform (EECLASS) for the relevant information concerning what has been covered in the class. You may ask a classmate of yours to help with assignment submission and collection of assignment worksheets, if any. You may make an appointment with the instructor for assignment worksheets. 缺席與請假不得作為未 能完成當日上課練習、無法及時繳交作業或不知道該次課後作業之藉口。缺席與請假者負有及時 （五日內）繳交作業，並透過同學、課程平台，或親自聯繫老師了解該次上課內容與課後作業之 責。（可委託同學代為繳交作業或拿取作業單，或自行前來教師研究室繳交或領取。） 3.  Assignments are expected to be completed and submitted by the due date. No late submission will be accepted or graded unless the instructor approves or grants your application for extension of submission. 作業請按時繳交（或上傳）。未獲教師同意可延遲繳 交者或超過寬限期，其遲交作業不批改、不計分。 prepared by Vicky Hsu8  Your absence CANNOT be an assumption that you are entitled to hand in the late assignments far later (more than 5 days) or until your next presence. 請勿自以為逾期的作業 可以自行延遲超過五日，或下次出現時才繳交。  NO full credit for late submission/Penalty for late submission: 10% of the total mark awarded will be deducted for each working day after the submission date. 每遲交一日。扣 10%成績。 Late Submission Mark Awarded After Penalty Number of days late Penalty Original grade 90 Original grade 60 1 10% 81 54 2 20% 72 48 3 30% 63 42 4 40% 54 36 5 50% 45 30 More than 5 days Grade of zero awarded 遲交逾 5 日，不計分  Frequent late submissions with no valid excuses or under controllable circumstances will NOT be accepted or graded since the third late assignment. 無合理原因或非為不可抗力情形 的慣性遲交作業，第三份起將不予批改與計分。 4. Plagiarism on assignments and cheating on the exam is absolutely unacceptable. If someone is found plagiarizing or cheating, it means he/she will get a zero point for that assignment or exam. 嚴禁抄襲與作弊。抄襲與作弊者，學期成績以不及格處理。情節重大時，將提報至相關單 位依校規處理。 5. AI regulations for assignments, reports, and projects AI-assisted reports and assignments are allowed in limited instances: AI can be used to prepare for reports and assignments by brainstorming, grammar checks, or tentative revision, but students must show how AI helps them reach the result. 僅限使用生成式 AI 於作業或報告之準 備（如腦力激盪、文法檢查與初步修訂等），學生須註明 AI 如何用於協作其作業或報告。  Moderate Brainstorming: GenAI is allowed for helping you generate ideas (via your conversation with GenAI), outline the thoughts, or explore concepts, but the core information and arguments must be original, not contributed entirely by AI. AI 可用於協助 擬進行適度的腦力激盪，如協助生成想法（與 AI 進行對話討論）、將想法撰寫成提綱、或探 索相關概念等，但核心資訊與論點必須是學生原創，而非由 AI 提供或生成所有資訊或資料。  Limited Editing: Students write their own work first, then use GenAI tools exclusively for spelling, grammar, and structural polish. No AI-generated content will be added to students’ original work. 學生必須先自行寫出，再使用 AI 工具，僅用於拼字、文法、句構的 修正與修飾。學生作品仍只能有學生原創的想法，不得加入 AI 生成的內容。 prepared by Vicky Hsu9  AI Transparency (Full use with citation): If it is permissible to complete specified tasks with GenAI in an assignment or project, any AI- generated content must be cited or provided in an appendix for its critical engagement in the output. 即使作業容許 AI 協作某些特定任 務、也必須在作業或報告中清楚標示所引用的 AI 生成內容 (How to cite Gen AI 如何引用 AI 文字: https://tamu.libguides.com/c.php?g=1289555&p=9679433)  Plagiarism/Academic dishonesty/Ethical misconduct: Using AI-generated content is not always traditional plagiarism, but submitting or publishing it as your own original work is widely considered academic dishonesty or ethical misconduct. If your work contains verbatim AI-generated text or lacks proper source attribution, it will result in a severe point deduction. 使用 AI 生成之內容並不一定構成傳統認定的抄襲，但以 AI 生成內容做為 自己的作品逕行繳交或發表，仍廣義地視為缺乏學術誠信或有道德瑕疵。如果您的作 品包含逐字 AI 生成文本，或缺乏適當的來源標註，將會導致嚴重扣分。 6. Penalty for no or poor participation in pair or group work Students are expected to take part in pair or group activities. Failure to engage in these activities (due to you absence or lateness) will lead to reductions in grades awarded. The ability to communicate and express oneself in English 英 語 溝 通 與 表 達 能 力 10% 2. The ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English 深 度 分 析 與 組 織 思 考 能 力 20% 3. Primary aim This course is designed to introduce students to the interpretation world and its real practice. Consecutive interpretation will be covered starting from a very general aspect gradually into the professional domain. Students will not only gain the knowledge on the interpretation as a whole, but also learn and develop the most basic technique to interpret accurately and fluently from English into Chinese and vice versa chunks of articles or speeches (usually 2-3 minutes long). 2. Subsidiary aims 1. to enhance confidence in oral communication and in getting message across 2. to develop interests in building the bridge between two cultures 3. to enhance English listening and speaking ability 4. to improve the skills of summarizing and grasping main ideas/key messages 5. to explore both general and professional areas of studies Course Methodology The main focus of the course will be on the practice of basic techniques and interpretation itself. In the first half of the semester and before the actual interpretation practices begin, students will receive training and learn some basic skills including: 1. shadowing 2. short-term memory recall 3. summarizing & paraphrasing 4. BIG numbers 5. sight interpretation 6. word choice 7. note-taking In the second half of the semester, workshops and mock conferences will be held, where students will have numerous interpretation practices on interested topics and speeches. If students are absent due to uncontrollable circumstances (e.g., illness, emergency, important occasions, etc.), a valid proof must be provided within two weeks. All leave requests should be submitted through the school’s online system. Five absences with approved requests or three absences without requests will result in a failing grade. 2. Course Description: This course is designed to transition ESL students from general English proficiency to academic competence by equipping them with critical thinking and reading skills. Through the lens of critical thinking, students will engage with 14 selected academic texts of diverse topics to broaden their global horizons as well as sharpen their analytical abilities. Aside from lecturing and discussions conducted based on the criteria of critical thinking, weekly assignments will be given in the form of presentation individually or as a group or writing a summary or report of the course materials, to enable students to apply their knowledge and analytical skills acquired in and outside the classroom. By the end of this course, students will be able to evaluate the credibility 1 of sources, comprehend different viewpoints, analyze the structure of an article, and synthesize information to propose their own argument in speech and writing, as well as collaborate with group members in completing course assignments. Subsidiary aim To enhance students' academic English proficiency through: 1. Critical inquiry into the concepts and structures of academic articles; and 2. Applying effective reading strategies to in-depth understanding of the text; 3. Rendering individual viewpoints/responses through speaking and writing; & 4. Exploring issues with the assistance of AI in research and learning. 英文核心能力指標 University Student Core Competency Indicators 1. 英語溝通與表達能力 (ability to communicate and express oneself in English) 20% 2. 深度分析與組織思考的能力 (ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English) 25% 3. 英語學習策略與技巧 (knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques) 20% 4. 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 (global views of English and multicultural diversity) 20% 5. 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣與能力 (ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit) 15% Teaching Materials and References Textbook(s) Online articles from academia and major news platforms, such as Times, university journals, etc. (as per syllabus) CEFR Scale □ B1 □ B1-B2 □ B2 ■ B2+ ■ C1 Learning/Resource Prestigious online media, Big Think, Scientific American, etc. Grading: 1. docs.text: 1 National Tsing Hua University 中級／中高級選讀英文 ［職場英語口語表達/ Oral Communication for Professional Contexts］ Fall 2026 Course Number 11510LANG200021 Credits 2 Classroom 綜二 108 Class hours □ Monday Tuesday □ Wednesday □ Thursday □ Friday 1:20 P.M. – 3:10P.M. □ 3:30 P.M. – 5:20P.M. 10:10 a.m.-12:00 p.m. Course Type □ EGP (English for general purposes) □ EAP (English for academic purposes) EOP (English for occupational purposes) Language Level □ B1（中級） □ B1-B2 B2（中高級） □ B2+ □ C1 Core Ability □ comprehension/reception √ communication/interaction □ production 可選課學生 身分別 頂標生 前標生 □ 中級生 □ 初級生 Prerequisites 修畢中高級英文一/二，中高級英文聽講或閱讀 加選說明 不開放人工加簽。所有學生須由選課系統亂數選課。 停修條件 The student’s application for course withdrawal will NOT be approved if 1. The student never attends class nor submits assignments. 2. The student is absent or asks for leave with NO valid excuses for more than 6 classes. 3. The student never explains to or discusses with the teacher his/her difficulty in taking care of this subject. 4. The student neither offers valid excuses on his application for course withdrawal nor notifies the teacher beforehand. 學生如遇有以下情形，其停修申請將不予「同意」 1. 學生未曾到課或繳交任何作業。 2. 學生無故缺席或未有證明之請假超過六次 3. 學生從未向老師解釋、或與之討論，修讀本課程時的困難 4. 學生未在停修申請上敘明或以其他通訊方式告知老師停修本課程之原因 避免學生規避「低修」學分數而選課，或以其他理由選課但不上課等情事 提醒：請於選課前參考課程大綱，了解評分方式、各週進度。並於第一堂課進一步了 解作業、報告、考試的規劃與所需處理時間。評估自已的學習量能，避免修課失衡。 2 Instructor & Contact Information: Name Email 林鈺凢 yufanlin@gapp.nthu.edu.tw Course Aims / Description Primary aim The course “Oral Communication for Professional Contexts” mainly aims to help students acquire the required knowledge for transitioning from college to the target workplace. Students will also become familiar with specific English occupational terms, phrases, and expressions for work and obtain knowledge of business etiquette and cultural differences at different workplaces. Throughout the semester, students will be given the chance to be exposed to the English oral learning environment, which focuses especially on occupation-related topics. Furthermore, job interview techniques, presentation skills, and international etiquette at work are also the key components that will be touched upon throughout the semester. In addition to occupational oral training, this course also briefly introduces the writing techniques of résumé and cover letter, which are basic job-hunting elements for students’ future careers. More importantly, students must engage in a variety of in-class activities and are encouraged to apply English to occupation-related situations as frequently as possible to strengthen their English speaking, and writing skills as well as their confidence in using the language. Subsidiary aim In this class, students will be given the opportunity to: 1. Be aware of the knowledge that they should acquire prior to entering workplaces through reading, and doing the role-play of occupation-related dialogues and group discussions. 2. Engage in an interview scenario by doing mock interview with their peers, and they will also be rated and commented on by their instructor and peers for further improvement. 3. Promote themselves and show their strengths as an interviewee through giving individual presentation. 4. Build up a learning networking with peers with different expertise to get them exposed to different possibilities of English applications. 5. Apply the techniques of writing resume and cover letter for future careers and practice their critical thinking skill by providing suggestions and commenting on peers’ performances. 3 Corresponding CEFR Can-do statements Notes [Listening] 1. Can understand announcements and messages on concrete and abstract topics spoken in standard dialect at normal speed. [listening to announcements & instructions] 2. Can keep up with an animated conversation between native speakers. [understanding interaction between native speakers] [Speaking] 3. Can account for and sustain his/her opinions in discussion by providing relevant explanation, arguments and comments. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP EOP 4. Can give a clear, prepared presentation, giving reasons in support of or against a particular point of view and giving the advantages and disadvantages of various options. [addressing audiences] EAP [Communicatio n strategies] 5. Can give feedback on and follow up statements and inferences and so help the development of the discussion. [cooperating] EAP EOP 6. Can use stock phrases (e.g., “That’s a difficult question to answer”) to gain time and keep the turn whilst formulating what to say. [taking the floor (turntaking)] [Sociolinguistic] 7. docs.text: Fall 2026 1/3 Reading on Pop Science 科普閱讀 Discover science. Discover fun! Course #: LANG200022 Class hours: 13:20 – 15:10 (T56) on Tuesday Professor: Yun-yin Huang 黃芸茵 (yyhuang@gapp.nthu.edu.tw) Office hours: By appointment only @ R207, General Building II. (Make appointments at http://140.114.119.46:8080/consultation/ ) Course Description Dive into the fascinating world of science through narratives from various sources in this engaging undergraduate course. We will explore how scientific knowledge can be used to solve real-world problems in various intriguing questions. Through guided readings and discussions, we will analyze how scientific concepts are communicated, evaluate the accuracy and clarity of scientific information presented, and consider the impact of storytelling techniques on public understanding of science. Course Objectives This course aims to enhance students’ scientific literacy, develop their critical thinking skills, and foster a deeper appreciation for the intersection of science and society through reading and discussion. Additionally, students will have the opportunity to communicate their insights and reflections in mini-presentations, further honing their ability to convey complex scientific ideas to diverse audiences. Specific learning objectives include: ⚫ Recall and describe the main ideas in the reading ⚫ Explain and illustrate the main ideas with relevant examples ⚫ Evaluate the quality of the reported study with textual evidences. ⚫ Enhance scientific literacy in both written and spoken English. Course Requirements 1. Actively engage and participate in all class activities. 2. Complete all assignments on time. No late submission will be accepted. 3. Adhere to RCR guidelines. You are accountable for the integrity of your work. Conditionally open to AI tools. 4. [Leave request] Inform your absence by email to BOTH Professor Huang and the TA. The student never attends class nor submits assignments. 2. The student is absent or asks for leave with NO valid excuses for more than 6 classes. 3.
