The student neither offers valid excuses on his application for course withdrawal nor notifies the teacher beforehand. 學生如遇有以下情形，其停修申請將不予「同意」 1. 學生未曾到課或繳交任何作業。 2. 學生無故缺席或未有證明之請假超過四次 3. 學生從未向老師解釋、或與之討論，修讀本課程時的困難 4. 學生未在停修申請上敘明或以其他通訊方式告知老師停修本課程之原因 避免學生規避「低修」學分數而選課，或以其他理由選課但不上課等情事 提醒：請於選課前參考課程大綱，了解評分方式、各週進度。並於第一堂課進一步了 解作業、報告、考試的規劃與所需處理時間。評估自已的學習量能，避免修課失衡。 Instructor & Contact Information Name Contact Information Office & Tel Office Hour 徐桂平 Vicky Hsu personal messaging on eeclass1 綜二館 B 側 209 ( 34417) Tuesday 10:00 A.M.-12:00 P.M. 綜二館 B 側 209 1 No email will be replied to, especially when the sender’s email address does not belong to the student. Please leave 2 prepared by Vicky Hsu Course Aims / Description 1. Primary aim This novel course is designed for students who hope to read English novels for pleasure and for improvement of reading comprehension and skills. Through reading the novel and discussing the issues presented in the plot, students are expected to engage in a close reading of the language used in a specific section of the novel and make connections between the novel and any or all of the following: the personal world, aspects of human nature, society and the wider world. 2. Subsidiary aim The activities related to reading a novel will be divided into six phases: (1) understanding and examining the literary elements and structures of a novel (2) developing the habit of reading through chapter-by-chapter reading (3) enhancing reading comprehension skills and reading strategies (4) interacting with classmates in the discussion of the situations, confrontations, and challenges faced by the main characters (5) exploring and sharing context clues, perspectives, and cultural information (6) investigating authentic language use and rhetorical devices such as form, tone, word use, and imagery 3. Corresponding CEFR Can-do statements Reception Reading OVERALL READING COMPREHENSION B2 Can read with a large degree of independence, adapting style and speed of reading to different texts and purposes, and using appropriate reference sources selectively. Has a broad active reading vocabulary, but may experience some difficulty with low- frequency vocabulary. [overall reading comprehension] READING FOR ORIENTATION B2 Can scan quickly through long and complex texts, locating relevant details. [reading for orientation] EAP Interaction Spoken Speaking INFORMAL DISCUSSION (WITH FRIENDS) B2 Can take an active part in informal discussion in familiar contexts, commenting, putting point of view clearly, evaluating alternative proposals and making and responding to hypotheses. [informal discussion (with friends)] B2 Can account for and sustain his/her opinions in discussion by providing relevant explanation, arguments and comments. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP EOP INFORMATION EXCHANGE B2 Can pass on detailed information reliably. [information exchange] INTERVIEWING AND BEING INTERVIEWED messages on eeclass, using the “personal messages” function. eeclass email 3 prepared by Vicky Hsu B2+ Can carry out an effective, fluent interview, departing spontaneously from prepared questions, following up and probing interesting replies. [interviewing and being interviewed] EAP EOP Production Spoken Speaking OVERALL SPOKEN PRODUCTION B2+ Can give clear, systematically developed descriptions and presentations, with appropriate highlighting of significant points, and relevant supporting detail. [overall spoken production] SUSTAINED MONOLOGUE: DESCRIBING EXPERIENCE C1 Can give elaborate descriptions and narratives, integrating sub themes, developing particular points and rounding off with an appropriate conclusion. [sustained monologue: describing experience] ADDRESSING AUDIENCES B2 Can give a clear, prepared presentation, giving reasons in support of or against a particular point of view and giving the advantages and disadvantages of various options. [addressing audiences] EAP B2+ Can give a clear, systematically developed presentation, with highlighting of significant points, and relevant supporting details. [addressing audiences] EAP Production Written CREATIVE WRITING B2 Can write a review of a film, book, or play. [creative writing] EAP B2+ Can write clear, detailed descriptions of real or imaginary events and experiences marking the relationship between ideas in clear connected text, and following established conventions of the genre concerned. [creative writing] EAP REPORTS & ESSAYS B2 Can write an essay or report which develops an argument, giving reasons in support of or against a particular point of view and explaining the advantages and disadvantages of various options. [reports & essays] EAP EOP B2 Can synthesize information and arguments from a number of sources. [reports & essays] EAP Reception Communi cation Strategies IDENTIFYING CUES & INFERRING (SPOKEN & WRITTEN) B2 Can use a variety of strategies to achieve comprehension, including listening for main points, checking comprehension by using contextual clues. [identifying cues & inferring (spoken & written)] EAP Interaction Communi cation Strategies TAKING THE FLOOR (TURNTAKING) B2 Can intervene appropriately in discussion, exploiting appropriate language to do so. [taking the floor (turntaking)] EAP EOP B2 Can initiate, maintain, and end discourse appropriately with effective turntaking. [taking the floor (turntaking)] COOPERATING 4 prepared by Vicky Hsu B2 Can help the discussion along on familiar ground, confirming comprehension, inviting others in, etc. [cooperating] B2+ Can give feedback on and follow up statements and inferences and so help the development of the discussion. [cooperating] EAP EOP ASKING FOR CLARIFICATION B2 Can ask follow-up questions to check that he/she has understood what a speaker intended to say, and get clarification of ambiguous points. [asking for clarification] Working with Text Communicative Language NOTE-TAKING (LECTURES, SEMINARS, ETC.) B2 Can understand a clearly structured lecture on a familiar subject, and can take notes on points which strike him/her as important, even though he/she tends to concentrate on the words themselves and therefore to miss some information. [note-taking (lectures, seminars, etc.) EAP PROCESSING TEXT B2 Can summarize the plot and sequence of events in a film or play. [processing text] EAP Communicative Language Competence Range GENERAL LINGUISTIC RANGE B2 Has a sufficient range of language to be able to give clear descriptions, express viewpoints and develop arguments without much conspicuous searching for words, using some complex sentence forms to do so. [general linguistic range] EAP VOCABULARY RANGE B2 Has a good range of vocabulary for matters connected to his/her field and most general topics. [vocabulary range] Control GRAMMATICAL ACCURACY B2 Shows a relatively high degree of grammatical control. Does not make mistakes which lead to misunderstanding. [grammatical accuracy] B2+ Good grammatical control. Occasional “slips” or non-systematic errors and minor flaws in sentence structure may still occur, but they are rare and can often be corrected in retrospect. [grammatical accuracy] VOCABULARY CONTROL B2 Lexical accuracy is generally high, though some confusion and incorrect word choice does occur without hindering communication. [vocabulary control] Sociolinguistic SOCIOLINGUISTIC APPROPRIATENESS B2 Can express him/herself appropriately in situations and avoid crass errors of formulation. [sociolinguistic appropriateness] B2+ Can express him/herself confidently, clearly and politely in a formal or informal register, appropriate to the situation and the person(s) concerned. [sociolinguistic appropriateness] EAP EOP 5 prepared by Vicky Hsu Pragmatic FLEXIBILITY B2 Can adjust to the changes of direction, style and emphasis normally found in conversation. [flexibility] B2+ Can adjust what he/she says and the means of expressing it to the situation and the recipient(s) and adopt a level of formality appropriate to the circumstances. [flexibility] EAP EOP THEMATIC DEVELOPMENT B2 Can develop a clear description or narrative, expanding and supporting his/her main points with relevant supporting detail and examples. [thematic development] EAP COHERENCE B2 Can use a limited number of cohesive devices to link his/her utterance into clear, coherent discourse, though there may be some “jumpiness” in a long contribution. [coherence] EAP 英文核心能力指標 University Student Core Competency Indicators No. Core Competency Indicators 1. 英語溝通與表達能力 (ability to communicate and express oneself in English) 30% 2. 深度分析與組織思考的能力 (ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English) 30% 3. 英語學習策略與技巧 (knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques) 20% 4. 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 (global views of English and multicultural diversity) 10% 5. 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣與能力 (ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit) 10% Teaching Materials and References Textbook(s) Lisa Genova. Requirements and rules 1, 2, 6, and 7) A student will fail to get the 2 credits for missing 5 classes, including the ones due to any kind of leave. 缺課達五次（含各類請假缺課）者，將無法從本課程獲取任何學分。 15% 2. Class attendance, lesson preparation and active class participation are required.  As you are all present whenever the instructor takes attendance, you will get 60% (9 points) in this category Attendance and Participation. 經常性點名，全勤者可得「出席與參與」項目 中的 60%（9 分）成績。  Each skip will cost 2 points from the category Attendance and Participation (up to 15 points in the final grade). 未假不到課（翹課），每次從「出席與參與」成績（占學期成績 15 分）扣 2 分。  If you are absent in case of UNCONTROLLABLE situations (e.g. illness, emergency, important occasions, etc.), please apply for a leave on the Student Leave System on Academic Information System of National Tsing Hua University or on the iNTHU app (from the Office of Student Affair website), with clear leave information, including leave type, leave period, and reasons (must be clear and valid enough for the teacher’s approval). As the reasons or the documents are not clear, valid or sufficient enough, the teacher may deny the application. 遇不可抗力情形需請假者，請於本校校務資訊系統上的學 生請假系統或下載 iNTHU APP，填寫資料（請假類別、請假日期、請假事由）。請假事由須合理並 敘述清楚，提供老師是否准假之參考。請假單上的理由或所附證明文件不清楚或不充分時， 該次請假申請得不予核准。  Please observe the information you are expected to offer for each of the following leave types:  For sick leave, please describe severe symptoms and medical treatments you have been taking in the box “Reason.” 請病假時，請於理由欄位說明影響上課之顯著症狀，就醫或服 藥等處理。  For personal leave, please describe the uncontrollable incident and how it makes you absent from the class. 請事假時，請於理由欄位敘明該不可抗力事件，並說明該事件如何 致使你無法前來上課。  Please observe the school calendar and avoid arranging any (family or personal) vacations or trips during the semester. No scheduled arrangements for pleasure or personal convenience will be considered uncontrollable incidents. 請依本校行事曆，避免於學期間 以個人或家庭為由安排度假、旅遊活動。任何與玩樂或個人方便之安排，皆無法歸類為不可 抗力事件。  No leave application will be approved on the dates of presentations, peer evaluations, and midterm/final exams. Please care for your health and reserve the time for these NTHU Q&A 7 prepared by Vicky Hsu important class activities. 報告、同儕互評、期中／期末考當日不得請假。請注意身心健康 並為這些重要課程活動預留時間。  There will be NO make-up exams or presentations unless you apply for leave with valid and official reasons for your absence beforehand. 無合理且正式的缺課原因，將不予補考 或補行報告。  You are expected to apply for leave before the class you are absent from. Any overdue leave application must be made within 7 days from the last day of absence. 請假以事先申請為原 則。逾期請假申請必須於 7 日內補請。未能於規定期間申請者，均以曠課論。  Being late for more than 10 minutes (with no valid excuses) is treated as absence from that hour (1 point deducted). Being late for more than 30 minutes is treated as absence from the whole class (2-points deducted). 無故遲到逾 10 分鐘，以該小時未到課紀錄（扣 1 分）。遲 到逾 30 分鐘，視為該次上課未到課（扣 2 分）。  No points will be deducted for your ATTENDANCE as long as your approved leave is no more than 6 hours. However, you may lose points for your PARTICIPATION or in-class practices scheduled on the date of your absence. 核准的請假時數未逾 6 小時，不扣出席成績。惟當日 如有上課練習或小組活動，請假者無法參與或完成，將無法獲得該次練習或該項評量成績。換 言之，缺課仍可能影響「參與」與「作業」等成績。  If you skip class for more than 8 hours, your course withdrawal may NOT be approved, and you will get 0 credits for this course. 無故不到課逾 8 小時者，將不予同意其停修申請，亦無 法取得本課程學分。  A student will fail to get the 2 credits for missing 5 classes, including the ones due to any kinds of leaves. 缺課達五次（含各類請假缺課）者，將無法從本課程獲取任何學分。 2. Absence from a class is no excuse for failing to complete in-class practices, to submit assignments in time, or to get informed of assignments or the class you have missed. It is your responsibility to hand in the assignments within 5 days (weekends & holidays included) and to reach your classmates or the instructor and refer to the course platform (EECLASS) for the relevant information concerning what has been covered in the class. You may ask a classmate of yours to help with assignment submission and collection of assignment worksheets, if any. You may make an appointment with the instructor for assignment worksheets. 缺席與請假不得作為未 能完成當日上課練習、無法及時繳交作業或不知道該次課後作業之藉口。缺席與請假者負有及時 （五日內）繳交作業，並透過同學、課程平台，或親自聯繫老師了解該次上課內容與課後作業之 責。（可委託同學代為繳交作業或拿取作業單，或自行前來教師研究室繳交或領取。） 3.  Assignments are expected to be completed and submitted by the due date. No late submission will be accepted or graded unless the instructor approves or grants your application for extension of submission. 作業請按時繳交（或上傳）。未獲教師同意可延遲繳 交者或超過寬限期，其遲交作業不批改、不計分。  Your absence CANNOT be an assumption that you are entitled to hand in the late assignments far later (more than 5 days) or until your next presence. 請勿自以為逾期的作業 可以自行延遲超過五日，或下次出現時才繳交。  NO full credit for late submission/Penalty for late submission: 10% of the total mark awarded will be deducted for each working day after the submission date. 每遲交一日。扣 8 prepared by Vicky Hsu 10%成績。 Late Submission Mark Awarded After Penalty Number of days late Penalty Original grade 90 Original grade 60 1 10% 81 54 2 20% 72 48 3 30% 63 42 4 40% 54 36 5 50% 45 30 More than 5 days Grade of zero awarded 遲交逾 5 日，不計分  Frequent late submissions with no valid excuses or under controllable circumstances will NOT be accepted or graded since the third late assignment. 無合理原因或非為不可抗力情形 的慣性遲交作業，第三份起將不予批改與計分。 4. Plagiarism on assignments and cheating on the exam is absolutely unacceptable. If someone is found plagiarizing or cheating, it means he/she will get a zero point for that assignment or exam. 嚴禁抄襲與作弊。抄襲與作弊者，學期成績以不及格處理。情節重大時，將提報至相關單 位依校規處理。 5. AI regulations for assignments, reports, and projects AI-assisted reports and assignments are allowed in limited instances: AI can be used to prepare for reports and assignments by brainstorming, grammar checks, or tentative revision, but students must show how AI helps them reach the result. 僅限使用生成式 AI 於作業或報告之準 備（如腦力激盪、文法檢查與初步修訂等），學生須註明 AI 如何用於協作其作業或報告。  Moderate Brainstorming: GenAI is allowed for helping you generate ideas (via your conversation with GenAI), outline the thoughts, or explore concepts, but the core information and arguments must be original, not contributed entirely by AI. AI 可用於協助 擬進行適度的腦力激盪，如協助生成想法（與 AI 進行對話討論）、將想法撰寫成提綱、或探 索相關概念等，但核心資訊與論點必須是學生原創，而非由 AI 提供或生成所有資訊或資料。  Limited Editing: Students write their own work first, then use GenAI tools exclusively for spelling, grammar, and structural polish. No AI-generated content will be added to students’ original work. 學生必須先自行寫出，再使用 AI 工具，僅用於拼字、文法、句構的 修正與修飾。學生作品仍只能有學生原創的想法，不得加入 AI 生成的內容。  AI Transparency (Full use with citation): If it is permissible to complete specified tasks with GenAI in an assignment or project, any AI- generated content must be cited or provided in an appendix for its critical engagement in the output. 即使作業容許 AI 協作某些特定任 務、也必須在作業或報告中清楚標示所引用的 AI 生成內容 (How to cite Gen AI 如何引用 AI 文字: https://tamu.libguides.com/c.php?g=1289555&p=9679433)  Plagiarism/Academic dishonesty/Ethical misconduct: Using AI-generated content is not How to cite Gen AI 9 prepared by Vicky Hsu always traditional plagiarism, but submitting or publishing it as your own original work is widely considered academic dishonesty or ethical misconduct. If your work contains verbatim AI-generated text or lacks proper source attribution, it will result in a severe point deduction. 使用 AI 生成之內容並不一定構成傳統認定的抄襲，但以 AI 生成內容做為 自己的作品逕行繳交或發表，仍廣義地視為缺乏學術誠信或有道德瑕疵。如果您的作 品包含逐字 AI 生成文本，或缺乏適當的來源標註，將會導致嚴重扣分。 6. Penalty for no or poor participation in pair or group work Students are expected to take part in pair or group activities. Failure to engage in these activities (due to you absence or lateness) will lead to reductions in grades awarded. Sometimes the reduction may be suggested by other group members; in other circumstances, the instructor may reduce the grade awarded without reference to other group members. 學生負有參與雙人 或小組活動之義務。如因個人遲到或缺席導致小組活動無法順利進行，請假或缺席者該次活動成 績將以扣分或甚至 0 分計算。 7.  Mobile devices are only used for educational purposes relevant to the subject or tasks in the classroom setting with the permission of or at the request of the instructor. Using mobile devices for studying other subjects or for entertaining purposes is absolutely prohibited. Students who violate the regulation will be considered absent from the class or asked to leave the classroom. 行動裝置僅限於學習活動，使用須獲得老師同意或遵照老師指示。嚴禁 使用行動裝置研習其他課程或娛樂使用。違反規定者，以「未到課」處置，亦得請違規者離開 教室。  During class students are not to be seen with a cell phone in hand or on the desk. Mobile phones are expected to be turned off or switched to a silent mode. 課程進行時，請關閉行動 電話或轉為靜音模式。未獲教師指示或許可，不得於上課時間使用或放置於桌上。 8. The syllabus, handouts, and returned assignments should be kept at least until the end of this semester for later reference or the final exam. 課程相關各項文件請妥為保存至學期結束。 Teaching Activities  Lectures 口頭講授  (pre-recorded video on YouTube) Peer Evaluation • Creating a presentation to report results 12 prepared by Vicky Hsu Academic Linguistic Skills Indicators Reading  Identifying appropriate reading techniques  Following descriptions of processes and sequences  Taking notes Writin g Using narrative and descriptive language (clearly describing a series of events)  Creating a poster to report results Speaking/Discu ssion  Exchanging and challenging ideas appropriately (in academic discussion)  Expressing and defending opinions  Explaining the possible implications of events  Creating a presentation to report results 13 prepared by Vicky Hsu Guideline for a Reading Log for Still Alice In addition to reading and discussing Still Alice (written by Lisa Genova) throughout the semester, you are required to create a READING LOG as a final/term project. Deadline: December 30 (Wednesday), 2026 (Winter Week 1) Submission: upload to eeclass (a PDF file) Your READING LOG is supposed to include the following: 1. Book Information  Book’s title, author(s), genre  Main characters or a character map or web for their relationships  A summary of the novel Still Alice (important events in the novel)  Readers’ likes and dislikes  Book reviews/Recommendation on the Internet (optional)  Websites (e.g., official site or bookstore websites) that provide information about the author, the novel, the subject matter, and/or reviews. Note: The information above is mainly the result of an Internet search, not your personal ideas. In other words, the book information you find may have motivated or helped you read the novel Still Alice. 2. Reflection Write a reflection about 500 words in length. You can’t be wrong with your emotions and responses, as these reflect your personal reactions to the novel. Take some risks and be honest. Use the sample prompts to help you get started with expressing your likes/dislikes, confusion, observations, and even enlightenment. Relate your personal experiences to the plot or the subject matter. Specify the page number(s) if you refer to a specific scene or chapter in your reflection. Sample Prompts:  I really don't understand the part where . . .  I really like/dislike this idea because . . .  This character reminds me of somebody I know because . . .  This character reminds me of myself because . . .  I think this setting is important because . . .  This scene reminds me of a similar scene in (title of book/movie/T.V. show) because . . . Book Information的部份是這本書的基 本資料，只要做網路資料的蒐集就可 以（但需註明資料來源） 在書的內頁、博客來、或 Amazon.com 都 可 以 找 到 這 些 book title, author, genre, 出版社、出版年份。 有些小說，在網路上還可以找到人物 的關係圖 , plot summary，讀者喜歡或 不喜歡這本書的理由。或是這本書的 優缺點（例如文字的難易度、情節的安 排合理或鬆散等）與推薦的理由。某些 作者或暢銷書甚至還有自己的網頁。 Reflection的部分是要自己寫的唷。不可以抄 網路上的文字。 這部份是根據你自己已經閱讀的部分，以英 文寫一篇感想。 Guideline上所列的 Prompts 不需要全部使用，你可以挑選你想回應的幾 個重點來回答。但是不要像回答簡答題一 樣，一題一題答。請寫成一篇有頭有尾有邏 14 prepared by Vicky Hsu  I like/dislike this writing because . . .  This part is very realistic/unrealistic because . . .  I think the relationship between ______and ______ is interesting because . . .  This section makes me think about . . .  I like/dislike (name of character) because . . .  This situation reminds me of a similar situation in my own life. What happened was . . .  If I were (name of character) at this point, I would . . .  I began to think of . . .  I love the way . . .  I can't believe . . .  I wonder why . . .  I noticed . . .  I'm not sure . . .  My favorite character is ___ . . .  I like the way the author . . .  I felt sad when . . .  I wish that . . .  I was surprised . . . 3. I want to know more about . . My Favorite chapters and discussions Our weekly discussions provide plenty of information and ideas for you to write the summary of SOME of your favorite 3-4 chapters. You are also expected to share the results of our weekly group discussions. You are encouraged to write your responses to 4-5 questions listed on the weekly handouts of discussion questions. 4. Glossary  Creating a glossary is an important part of English learning. A glossary helps a reader understand the words in the story and facilitates the reading process. A glossary can be helpful, especially a lot of terminology (e.g, medical or legal terms) used for the story or the subject matter.  Go through the pages you have read in the book and create your own glossary. The glossary must contain two sections: VOCABULARY and EXPRESSIONS. In the VOCABULARY section, you are required to list at least 30 words. For each item, you list 1. Word entry 2. Part of speech 詞性 3. Definition (in English; you are welcome to add a Chinese translation to the word); the definition should be carefully selected to meet the context. 英文定義（可以附加中文 定義） 4. TWO example sentences: One example sentence from the dictionary or any other text and the other should be the sentence in the novel that contains the word, along Glossary的部分重點是查字典的工作。選出 30-50個你覺得應該要懂的新單字（不要隨 便列出 Vicky覺得你國中或高中就應該懂得 的 單 字 ） ， 利 用 網 路 上 的 英 英 字 典 （ Longman, MacMillan, Oxford, Cambridge 等），查出英文的 definition，如果可以加 上詞性與中文定義更好。記得要列至少二 句例句 ，其中一句從你閱讀的文本裡選 出，句末加上頁碼），另加一句從字典或其 他來源上選出的例句。 15-20 idiomatic expressions也是同樣的格式 （英文定義、詞類、中文定義、例句）。 Idiomatic expressions是指字詞的搭配與組 合是固定用法，某些 idiomatic expressions 從字面上可能是不容易猜出語意的。 15 prepared by Vicky Hsu with the page number in the parentheses. 附上單字出現在小說中的句子，並註明頁碼，加上一句其他來源（字典、網路文章等）的例句。 Sample: 1. paradigm (n.) a model or example that shows how something works or is produced Frankly, pure pleasure is not my cultural paradigm. [Eat Pray Love, p. 79] the basic paradigm of the family tree 2. sheer (adj.) luck, happiness etc with no other feeling or quality mixed with it [= pure] Generally speaking, though, Americans have an inability to relax into sheer pleasure. [Eat Pray Love, p. 80] I'll never forget the look of sheer joy on her face. In the EXPRESSION section, you are required to list at least 15 fixed or idiomatic expressions. For each expression, you list: 1. Expression entry 2. Definition (in English; you are welcome to add a Chinese translation to the word); the definition should be carefully selected to meet the context 3. 2 example sentences: One example sentence from the dictionary or any other text and the other should be the sentence in the novel that contains the word, along with the page number in the parentheses. Note: You may use online English-English dictionaries to facilitate creating the glossary. Longman English Dictionary Online http://www.ldoceonline.com/ Cambridge Dictionaries Online http://dictionary.cambridge.org/ Oxford Dictionaries Online http://oxforddictionaries.com/ 5. Memorable Quotes Copy at least ONE sentence in each chapter (page numbers included) in your reading log and explain why these lines caught your attention and/or how the quotes move or inspire you. Your explanation can be in English or Chinese. Reminder: Avoid relating the quote to the story/event around it only or explaining what happens in the novel. The key point should be how you PERSONALLY get connected to the quote Sample: “People think a soul mate is your perfect fit, and that’s what everyone wants. But a true soul mate is a mirror, the person who shows you everything that’s holding you back, the person who brings you to your own attention so you can change your life. A true soul mate is probably the most important person you’ll ever meet, because they tear down your walls and smack you awake.” [Eat Pray Love, p. 198] Memorable quotes 是希望你列出在閱讀這 本小說時，喜歡或有特別感受的句子。請 勿解釋這個句子所在的小說情節（這我們 都讀過，不需要重述）。重點在於這些文 句與你個人所產生的連結、衝擊、反思 等。你所選出的句子不一定要很優美或很 艱澀。可以是英文用得很棒的句子，是你 心有戚戚焉的句子，請列出這些句子、標 示頁數，並加上自己的註解、對應的心 情、感想等（中英文皆可）。 16 prepared by Vicky Hsu 6. Culture Notes A "culture note” originally refers to a small "pop-up" text that explains a cultural element on a TV program or film that the target audience is not expected to understand. Examples can be:  Cultural artifacts and symbols  Definitions for specific terms  Puns and jokes that are hard or impossible to explain with just subtitles. Learning English through reading also means learning about the culture. These notes aim to provide insight into the people, places, customs, and history of English-speaking countries. In the CULTURE NOTES section, you are required to create at least 8 notes. Each note includes the following: (In order to explain the cultural element better, you may explain it in English or Mandarin.) 1. the cultural element 2. explanation or information in English plus photos. (You may also add information in Mandarin.) 3. information source or at least one website that provides information for the cultural element Sample: 1. sweet ‘n’ Lo: a brand of artificial sweetener made primarily from granulated saccharin. It also contains dextrose and cream of tartar, and is distributed primarily in packets. There have been over 500 billion Sweet'N Low packets produced. 最有名的代糖品牌，現在在英文中可直接用 Sweet ‘N Low 表示代糖。 http://www.sweetnlow.com/ http://www2.mmh.org.tw/nutrition/chao/sweetner.htm 2. gravy boat: Could you bring me a gravy boat? 能不能請你幫我帶一個滷汁皿? a long, low container with a handle, used for serving gravy at the table gravy 是一種褐色的稠汁，通常老美在吃 mashed potato 時都會加上一點 gravy 調味。那這個 gravy boat 就是用來裝 gravy 的一種器皿. (utensil)。這樣講也許太抽象，大家有沒有吃過牛排？拿來裝 黑胡椒醬那種像船一樣的器皿就是 gravy boat。話說第一次老美跟我說，"Could you bring me a gravy boat?"我的直覺反應就是"boat?"帶什麼樣的船啊？原來此船非彼船，指的是盛裝東西用的 器皿。(Source: http://www.amazon.com/exec/obidos/tg/browse/-/13413561/102-0857506-0383315) 7. Others You may create an extension edition of the assignments we have done (plot maps, culture notes, the timeline, storyboard for the book trailer, etc.) throughout the semester and your notes or reflections on some issues we have discussed. You may place them in your reading log. Culture Notes的範圍十分廣泛，可以是書中提到 的某種食物、藥品、品牌、書籍、建築或是歌 手、企業家等。甚至歷史上的事件、醫學常識或 是某種科技產品或概念。只要是你覺得對我們這 些英語學習者值得多知道一些的事物或概念，都 可以列在 Culture Notes。這 10個 Culture Notes 也是查資料的工作。請把基本的資訊列出（不要 只列網址），除了英文資訊（必要），附加中文 資料也歡迎。有圖片也不錯。記得要列出資料 17 prepared by Vicky Hsu Final Oral Report (pre-recorded YouTube video)—My Next Read Task Prompts & PowerPoint Slide Guide Sheet You are going to make a video report to share with your teacher and classmates a novel you may read after having read Still Alice in our class. Your report is supposed to be 4-5 minutes. Reports that are shorter than 3.5 minutes or longer than 6 minutes cannot get a better grade than a “C-”. (Reminder: Preparedness is a must; rehearsals may help.) Still Alice 4-5 3.5 6 C- The book in this report MUST be a NOVEL. Please check the handout “Introducing the novel” for a clear definition of a novel, concerning the content, length, and story types. Please confirm the genre of the book you choose for the report carefully. Avoid reporting on nonfiction, biographies, autobiographies, memoirs, diaries, collections of short stories or comics, or you will get 0 points in this category. Introducing the novel Deadline & Schedule:  December 20, 2026 : Video Upload to YouTube and the YouTube link to eeclass  December 21-23, 2026 : Peer Evaluation This “My Next Read” presentation is not equal to a book report. Instead, it is more like a sharing that focuses on how you find out and why you decide to read the novel after having read the novel Still Alice. Still Alice Your “My Next Read” presentation may include at least five out of these aspects: • an appealing opening as a hook or an attention-getter • factors or reasons for your choice (Note: It would be better if your ideas are related to this course or the novel Still Alice.) • brief book information (e.g., author, subject matters, synopsis, social/cultural background, memorable quotes, level of language difficulty, …) (Note: the book information is used for your choice, not for knowing the whole story. Remember that you haven’t read it yet, at least the English version of the novel.) • your expectations (fun reading, language learning, culture, history, figurative language, ...) • Any other appeal related to the novel (impressive sentences, reader’s review, a friend’s or celebrity’s recommendation, film adaptations, etc.) • An impressive concluding remark to remind your teacher and classmates that you are looking forward to reading the novel you choose (Note: it would be great if you relate your next read to this course or the novel Still Alice) 18 prepared by Vicky Hsu   Still Alice     Reminder of the content and organization  Greetings & overview of the oral report (Note: The opening of an oral presentation is a key moment to grab your audience’s attention and make them wonder and anticipate what will be going on like the opening chapter of a novel.)  Book information (Note: Remember that you haven’t read this novel yet, and it’s illogical that you know the detailed development of the novel and even the ending. Please keep the book information short but clear enough for you and your classmates to consider the novel a worthy read. It’s enough.)  Factors/reasons for your choice (Note: It’s the highlight and the essence of the oral report. Please make the audience feel your genuine desire to read the novel.)  Your expectation of reading the novel (Note: Remember that you haven’t read or finished this novel; it’s impossible to talk as if you were familiar with the plot. Instead, you are expected to talk like a reader who gets ready to remove the wrapping off the novel and turn to the first page. You may secretly turn to the last page to read the ending, but you are supposed to expect what you will get after reading the whole novel.)  Inspirational quotes for reading the novel (optional) (Note: You may google the novel, especially those bestsellers, and you may find some sentences on the Internet that inspire or move readers. If you read some, you may feel moved or inspired immediately without knowing too much about the plot. Or, you may imagine what would be in the novel while reading these sentences selected from the novel. It’s great to share with your audience how you feel reading these inspirational quotes.  An impressive or aspirational conclusion  Please avoid spoilers in the presentation The following is a tentative structure of the final oral report and the slide design. 19 prepared by Vicky Hsu Guidelines for Making a Cultural Infographic DirecƟons: You will create your own infographic about a specific item, place, or person from SƟll Alice to help you and your classmates beƩer understand the world Alice lives in. Task: Create an infographic as a culture note 1. What is an Infographic? An infographic is considered a visual story or a poster that delivers and teaches a specific type of informaƟon. It uses a mix of pictures, icons, charts, and a small amount of text to explain a topic quickly and clearly. The goal is to make informaƟon easy to understand and remember. 2. EssenƟal InformaƟon to Include Your infographic must answer these four key quesƟons about your chosen topic:  The "What": A Clear DefiniƟon  What is this item? Describe it in simple terms.  What does it look like? What is it made of?  The "Where": Origin and Context  Where does it come from (a country, a company)?  Where in the story do we see it? (e.g., in Alice's home, at Harvard).  The "Why": ConnecƟon to SƟll Alice (This is the most important part.)  Why is this item important in the novel?  What does it tell us about a character (Alice, John, her children)?  Does it represent a theme, like memory, idenƟty, or loss?  "Fun Facts" or "Did You Know?"  Include 1-2 interesƟng facts that your classmates might not know. This could be about its history, its use, or a surprising detail. 3. Suggested Steps to Make Your Infographic Step 1: Choose Your Topic Select one item from the category “Culture Notes” at the end of the vocabulary lists (available on EECLASS). For example:  Food: enchilada, ravioli, mulled cider, lasagna, fortune cookie (Note: No recipes, please!!!)  Technology: Blackberry  Places: Harvard University, Stanford University, The Charles River, CITGO, “T”  Culture-specific items: blue ribbon, blue book, tarot cards  Medical care/concept: menopause, estrogen replacement, Prozac, MRI, jet lag, The "Mini- Mental State Exam", Lipitor,  Product brands: Neutrogena, Starbucks, Kodak, Ben & Jerry’s  Holiday: Easter, Halloween  AcƟviƟes: yard sale, Yankee swap,  Famous people: Jennifer Aniston, Ansel Adams Step 2: Define your target audience  Who will need the infographic?  What do you want your infographic to achieve? Step 3: Research Your Topic & gather data & informaƟon  Find the essenƟal informaƟon. Use simple search terms like: "What is a BlackBerry 20 prepared by Vicky Hsu phone?", "History of Harvard University," "Social/Culture issues of Ben & Jerry’s."  Remember to find out how it connects to the novel if possible! Reread the chapter where the item appears. Step 3: Plan & Design Your Layout Before you use a computer, sketch a simple plan on paper. Where will your Ɵtle go? Where will the pictures be? This saves you Ɵme later. Step 4: Create Your Infographic Use a free online tool to create your infographic. They have templates that make it easy! Recommended Tools: Canva, Piktochart, Venngage, Infogram, Adobe Express (Some have free versions). What to do:  Choose a simple, clean template.  Write clear Ɵtles and headings for each secƟon.  Use simple sentences. Remember, you are teaching your classmates.  Add images or icons that relate to your topic.  Include a small note at the boƩom with your sources (e.g., "Sources: Wikipedia, Britannica.com"). 4. Tips for a Great Infographic ࿨࿩࿪ Less is More: Don't write long paragraphs. Use short sentences and bullet points. ᗟᗠᗡᗢ Be Visual: Use at least 2-3 images or icons.် ျြွှဿ၀ Use Color Wisely: SƟck to 2-3 main colors that look good together. ဓနပ Choose a Readable Font: Use a clear, simple font like Arial, HelveƟca, or Lato. ᗒᗓᗔᗕᗖᗗᗘ Proofread! Check your spelling and grammar carefully before you submit. 5. Checklist Before You Submit Ask yourself these quesƟons before you finish:  Does my infographic have a clear Ɵtle?  Does it include all four "EssenƟal InformaƟon" secƟons (What, Where, Why, Fun Facts)?  Is the "ConnecƟon to SƟll Alice" secƟon clear and well-explained?  Is the language simple and easy for my classmates to understand?  Does it look organized and visually appealing (not too crowded)? Have I checked for spelling and grammar mistakes?

docs.text: 1 National Tsing Hua University 中高級選讀英文［英文批判閱讀與寫作］English Critical Reading and Writing Fall 2026 Course Information Course Number LANG 2000 __ Credits 2 Classroom 綜二 202 Class Hours □ Monday □ Tuesday □ Wednesday ■ Thursday □ Friday □ 1:20P.M. – 3:10P.M. □ 3:30P.M. – 5:20P.M. ■ __10___ A.M. – __12___P.M. Course Type □ EGP (English for general purposes) ■ EAP (English for academic purposes) □ EOP (English for occupational purposes) Language Level □ B1（中級） □ B1-B2 ■ B2（中高級） ■ B2+ □ C1 Core Ability ■ comprehension/reception □ communication/interaction ■ production 可選課學生 身分別 ■ 頂標生 ■ 前標生 □ 中級生 □ 初級生 Prerequisites 修畢中高級英文一、二或中高級英文三 加簽說明 ☑ 不開放人工加簽。所有學生須由選課系統亂數選課。 提醒：學生修讀英文領域課程，請依本校規劃選課之修業年級選課。如因個 人考量，未對應年級而逕自改於其他修業年級選課之英文領域課程，或指定 加簽某特定課程，英語教育中心與任課教師將礙難配合或處理。 Instructor & Contact Information Name Email Office & Tel Office Hour 林嘉瑜 joylin.nthu@gmail.com 綜二 209 34417 Monday 13:00-15:00 Course Aims / Description 1. Primary aim This course aims to develop students’ source-based writing skills on academic reading texts. In this class, students are introduced with the skills to recognize and respond to specific points in the materials they read, to synthesize ideas from several reading selections, as well as to evaluate and to argue about the ideas they have found in those reading materials. Class activities include lectures, writing exercises, small-group and whole-class discussion, as well as individual and group presentations. Supplementary course materials can be found on eeclass course website (https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw/). Participation in class discussion and activities is required and will contribute to the final grade. Homework may be given daily and will be due in the following week. Students are expected to come to 2 class prepared to discuss designated chapters and assignments. Quizzes will be designed to test students’ learning on sentence skills. Source-based writing will focus specifically on the summary and response on the academic texts. The final report will be designed to incorporate all the source-based writing skills covered in this semester. 2. Subsidiary aim In this class, students will utilize academic reading ability to strengthen comprehension, note- taking, and outlining skills. This will enable students to practice paraphrasing, summarizing, and synthesizing information from various texts. Additionally, students will cultivate the ability to formulate their own viewpoints based on different sources and relevant supporting points, facilitating the creation of comprehensive source-based writing. 3. Corresponding CEFR Can-do statements Reception Reading READING FOR ORIENTATION B2 Can scan quickly through long and complex texts, locating relevant details. [reading for orientation] EAP B2 Can quickly identify the content and relevance off news items, articles and reports on a wide range of professional topics, deciding whether closer study is worthwhile. [reading for orientation] EAP EOP READING FOR INFORMATION & ARGUMENT B2 Can understand articles and reports concerned with contemporary problems in which the writer adopts particular stances or viewpoints. [reading for information & argument] B2+ Can obtain information, ideas and opinions from highly specialized sources within his/her field. [reading for information & argument] EAP EOP B2+ Can understand specialized articles outside his/her field, provided he/she can use a dictionary occasionally to confirm his/her interpretation of terminology. [reading for information & argument] EAP EOP C1 Can understand in detail a wide range of lengthy, complex taxts likely to be encountered in social, professional or academic life, identifying finer points of detail including attitudes and implied as well as stated opinions. [reading for information & argument] EAP EOP Interaction WrittenWriting OVERALL WRITTEN INTERACTION B2 Can express news and views effectively in writing, and relate to those of others. [overall written interaction] C1 Can express him/herself with clarity and precision, relating to the addressee flexibly and effectively. [overall written interaction] Production Written Writing OVERALL WRITTEN PRODUCTION B2 Can write clear, detailed texts on a variety of subjects related to his/her field of interest, synthesizing and evaluating information and arguments from a number of sources. [overall written production] EAP EOP C1 Can write clear, well-structured texts of complex subjects, underlining the relevant salient issues, expanding and supporting points of view at some length with subsidiary points, reasons and relevant examples, and rounding off with an appropriate conclusion. [overall written production] EAP EOP 3 REPORTS & ESSAYS B2 Can write an essay or report which develops an argument, giving reasons in support of or against a particular point of view and explaining the advantages and disadvantages of various options. [reports & essays] EAP EOP B2 Can synthesize information and arguments from a number of sources. [reports & essays] EAP B2+ Can write an essay or report that develops an argument systematically with appropriate highlighting of significant points and relevant supporting detail. [reports & essays] EAP EOP B2+ Can evaluate different ideas or solutions to a problem. [reports & essays] EAP C1 Can write clear, well-structured expositions of complex subjects, underlining the relevant salient issues. [reports & essays] EAP C1 Can expand and support points of view at some length with subsidiary points, reasons and relevant examples. If you are interested, you may attend the first class and continue checking the course registration system. Because of the strict attendance and participation policy, some seats may become available during the first three weeks. Course Aims / Description 1. Primary aim This course equips students with the ability to read English news articles and express opinions on news and current issues, preparing them for future academic studies. It seeks to stimulate interest, expand vocabulary in journalistic English, and build background knowledge of diverse topics—politics, society, finance, technology, medicine, environment, humanities, arts, leisure, and sports—through extensive exposure to authentic news articles. 2. Subsidiary aim By completing the course, students will be able to: ⚫ understand the structure and characteristics of news writing ⚫ extend and consolidate vocabulary and reading skills across fields ⚫ appreciate satire, humor, and metaphor in news reports ⚫ gain familiarity with historical and cultural contexts of current affairs ⚫ develop critical thinking, participate in discussions, and express opinions ⚫ build habits of reading, listening to, and watching news reports ii University Student Core Competency Indicators 英文核心能力指標 No. Core Competency Indicators % 1. 英語溝通與表達能力 (ability to communicate and express oneself in English) 20 2. 深度分析與組織思考的能力 (ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English) 25 3. 英語學習策略與技巧 (knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques) 20 4. 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 (global views of English and multicultural diversity) 25 5. 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣與能力 (ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit) 10 Corresponding CEFR Can-do Statements 1. Can-do Statement #1 Overall Reading Comprehension Can read with a large degree of independence, adapting style and speed of reading to different texts and purposes, and using appropriate reference sources selectively. Has a broad active reading vocabulary, but may experience some difficulty with low-frequency idioms. 2. Can-do Statement #2 Reading for Orientation Can scan quickly through long and complex texts, locating relevant details. (EAP) Can quickly identify the content and relevance of news items, articles and reports on a wide range of professional topics, deciding whether closer study is worthwhile. (EAP/EOP) 3. Can-do Statement #3 Reading for Information & Agreement Can understand articles and reports concerned with contemporary problems in which the writer adopts particular stances or viewpoints 4. Can-do Statement #4 Overall Spoken Interaction Can interact with a degree of fluency and spontaneity that makes regular interaction with native speakers quite possible. Can use the language fluently, accurately and effectively on a wide range of general, academic, vocational or leisure topics, marking clearly the relationships between ideas (EAP/EOP) 5. Can-do Statement #5 Formal Discussion (Meetings) Can participate actively in routine and non-routine formal discussion (EAP/EOP) Can follow the discussion on matters related to his/her field, understand in detail the points given prominence by the speaker (EAP/EOP) 6. Can-do Statement #6 Addressing Audiences Can give a clear, prepared presentation, giving reasons in support of or against a particular point of view and giving the advantages and disadvantages of various options. (EAP) Can give a clear, systematically developed presentation, with highlighting of significant points, and relevant supporting details. (EAP) 7. Can-do Statement #7 General Linguistic Range Can express him/herself clearly and without much sign of having to restrict what he/she wants to say. Has a sufficient range of language to be able to give clear descriptions, express viewpoints and develop arguments without much conspicuous searching for words, using some complex sentence forms to do so. (EAP) iii Teaching materials and References Textbook(s) 自編教材 News articles from The New York Times, The Washington Post, Taipei Times, and Taiwan News etc. News broadcasts from CNN, BBC, FOX News, ICRT and FTV English edition, etc. CEFR Scale □ B1 □ B1-B2 ■ B2 ■ B2+ □ C1 E-Learn Platform https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw RECOMMENDED ONLINE DICTIONARIES 1. Longman Dictionary of Contemporary English Online https://www.ldoceonline.com/ 2. Cambridge Dictionary https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/ 3. The Free Dictionary http://www.thefreedictionary.com/ Regulations for Using AI (AI 使用原則) Students are not allowed to use AI or machine-translation tools, including Google Translate, to generate or translate answers or assignments. This prohibition applies to questions and answers about the presentation article titles, presentation transcripts, and in-class worksheets. However, students may use AI to proofread or revise work that they have written independently in English. When using AI for proofreading or revision, students must submit their original version, the AI revised version, and a list of lessons or insights they gained by comparing the two versions. Course Requirements 1) Attendance and Participation 15 % 2) Quizzes 30 % 3) News Presentation 20 % 4) In-Class Tasks/ Worksheets 10 % 5) Take-Home Assignments 15 % 6) FutureLearn Videos 10 % iv Class Participation/ Attendance Students are expected to attend each class punctually and actively participate in pair, group, and class discussions. If you cannot attend, you must (1) email the teacher and (2) apply for leave through the school’s online system. Some details here: • Student Leave Policies: https://sa.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/406-1480-264831,r7918.php?Lang=zh-tw • Student Leave Guidelines: https://sa.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/406-1480-269011,r7918.php?Lang=zh-tw • Related Document Downloads: https://sa.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/412-1480-21552.php?Lang=zh-tw Important rules for this course: 1. For sick or personal leave, you must provide valid supporting documentation. ▪ For sick leave, a medical receipt or certificate is required. 2. To arrange a make-up quiz, presentation, or final examination, you must provide official supporting documentation. ▪ Traveling or taking a driver’s license test is not considered an acceptable reason. 3. If your leave request is not approved, it will be counted as an absence. 4. An absence from class is not an excuse for being unaware of assignments, announcements, or material covered in class. It is your responsibility to ask your classmates what you missed and find out what assignments or preparation are required for the next class. Attendance, punctuality, and class participation will be recorded and included in your course evaluation. Attendance will be recording beginning in the first week, so please make sure that you attend the first class and arrive on time. Attendance Policy ➢ Starting score: 9 (起始點: 9 分) ➢ Late arrival: -2 (遲到: 2 分) ➢ Absence: -10 (缺席: 10 分) ➢ Irrelevant activities in class: -2 (做課堂不相關的事: 2 分) The starting attendance score is 9 points. Each late arrival deducts 2 points. Each absence deducts 10 points. Engaging in irrelevant activities in class deducts 2 points. (This includes using a phone for non-class-related activities or working on assignments for other courses.) The score has no lower limit but a maximum of 20 points. In other words, a negative attendance score will lower your semester grade, while a high attendance score can earn you up to 5 extra points towards your semester grade. 出席成績從 9 分開始計算，並依以下規則增減：每次遲到扣 2 分，缺席扣 10 分。若在課堂上從事 無關活動（如使用手機處理與課程無關的事務或做其他課程作業），則扣 2 分。分數累積上限為 20 分，無下限。換言之，若出席成績為負分，將併入學期成績計算；若累積達 20 分，則學期成績額外 加 5 分。 All these seemingly complicated and trivial calculations for attendance and class participation are designed to encourage you to speak more English and participate more actively in class. The more you engage in each class, the more harvest you’ll reap from this course. v Quizzes Two scheduled quizzes (see course outline) will test students on: • Vocabulary • Content of the news articles discussed in class and presented by peers • News reading strategies and writing conventions In addition, pop quizzes may be given before student news presentations. Pop quizzes will account for one-third of the quiz grade (10% of the final grade). News Presentation Students must select a news section (e.g. international news, national news, or opinion, etc.) and give EITHER a group OR an individual presentation. The chosen article must be printed and distributed to all classmates at least one week prior to the presentation day. To succeed, students should begin preparing at least 3 weeks in advance, meet all deadlines, memorize their speeches, and rehearse thoroughly so that they can deliver their presentation confidently without reading from a script. (See Appendices I and II for details.) In-Class Tasks and Worksheets Every class will include individual, pair or group tasks and discussions. Each student is expected to participate actively and contribute meaningfully. At the end of the class, worksheets will be collected. 3 or 4 will be randomly selected for grading. A group-member evaluation may occasionally be administered after a group task. Students will evaluate each member’s contribution to the task. If a student receives an average peer-evaluation score below 6 out of 10, the instructor will review the student’s contribution to the group task based on the peer evaluations, written comments, completed work, and classroom observations. If insufficient participation is confirmed, the student’s individual worksheet score may be reduced or, in cases of non-participation, recorded as 0. • If you are absent, the worksheet score will be 0. • Late submissions will not be accepted Take-Home Assignments All take-home assignments must be typed and turned in on time. These assignments are designed to build on class progress, so late work cannot be graded. Future Learn Videos Students are required to watch the assigned Future Learn videos (https://www.futurelearn.com/ ) and complete the related discussions, exercises, or tests. Since there is not enough class time to introduce all of the essential materials, these videos provide explanations of news English conventions and news reading strategies. They are an important supplement to the course and ensure that students come to class prepared to apply these concepts in discussions and assignments. vi Copy Fee A copy fee of NT$100-120 will be collected once during the semester to cover the course packet, test sheets and handouts. Instructor’s Guidelines for Success To get the most of this course, you are advised to: 1. Attend all classes regularly and on time. 2. Contribute actively to pair, group, and class discussions. 3. PREVIEW EACH NEWS ARTICLE (including the PRESENTATION ARTICLE) BEFORE CLASS. Use the news reading strategies we practice in class, and come with subheadings and annotations prepared. 4. Ask questions whenever you don’t understand—your curiosity helps everyone learn. 5. Submit assignments, worksheets, and presentation materials by the stated deadlines. Upload electronic files to eeclass and submit printed copies in class when required.  Electronic files allow the instructor to review your work for compliance with the course AI policy.  Printed copies will be used for reading, grading, and providing feedback in order to reduce the instructor’s screen time and eye strain. 6. Browse news headlines and stories and listen to or watch English news broadcasts regularly to stay familiar with current affairs. 7. Review and build your vocabulary every day—it’s the key to understanding more. 8. If you have been putting considerable time and effort into the course but still feel that you are falling behind, please reach out to Jennifer for assistance. Guidelines for the News Article Presentation Students will choose a news section (e.g., international news, national news, or opinion, etc.) and give either a group or an individual presentation in class. The sign-up will be completed in Week 3, and the presentation list will be announced then. To succeed, students should begin preparation about 3 weeks in advance, meet all deadlines, and rehearse carefully. Because the evaluation process begins 3 weeks before the presentation, please read the following guidelines closely. I. Three Weeks Before the Presentation Day a) Begin browsing news headlines to find a topic that interests you. (Make sure it belongs to the news section you have signed up for the presentation.) b) Email Jennifer the link (URL) to the article instead of attaching a file. In your email, include your presentation date, the news section you’ve signed up for, and the correct word count of the article. c) How to choose an article Please choose your news article from the following sources: i. Newspapers: ◼ English newspapers in Taiwan: Taipei Times, Taiwan News ◼ U.S. newspapers: The New York Times, Washington Post, Los Angeles Times, etc. ◼ UK newspapers: The Times, The Guardian, etc. ii. News agencies: AP, Reuters, CNA (https://focustaiwan.tw/) , etc. If you wish to use another source, please discuss it with me in advance. d) The article must be published after the first day of this semester, __Sep. 7 __. e) Make sure the article belongs to the news section you signed up for. f) The article length should be between 470 and 1200 words. This ensure it is substantial enough for analysis but still manageable within the presentation time. g) Please email me your article early to allow time for approval and preparation. (Do not wait until the last minute.) h) Once your article has been finalized, please keep it. This will give you enough time to focus on preparation and practice. II. Two Weeks Before the Presentation Day a) You should have finalized your article choice with Jennifer by now. b) Post your article link on eeclass. c) Post your questions on the headline as well as their answers on eeclass. d) For Group Presentations Only:  Show Jennifer a printed outline of your presentation.  Make an appointment with Jennifer to present in her office. III. One Week Before the Presentation Day a) Distribute copies of your presentation article to your classmates in class. (**Week 16 presenters must distribute the article copies on Dec. 7 (for M56 Class) and Dec. 10 (For R56 Class) 1. When preparing the original copy, include the date, and the name of the newspaper, the xii news agency, and the journalist(s). The font size should be at least 12 pt, and leave enough margin space for classmates to take notes. 2. DO NOT CHANGE THE ARTICLE’S LAYOUT, INCLUDING NUMBERING THE PARAGRAPHS OR HIGHLIGHING THE VOCAB WORDS. 3. Before making copies, please email Jennifer the original file for approval. b) Post your subheadings of the article on eeclass. 1. Number the paragraphs first. 2. Group the paragraphs and give each group a subheading. 3. Subheadings should be phrases not full sentences. c) Post your vocab list of the article on eeclass. 1. The vocabulary list is different from ‘word sharing.’ It should contain around 15 or more words, depending on the length and difficulty level of the article. 2. How to make the vocabulary list i. Create a list of words you don't know from this article. Each entry must include the word, its part of speech, (e.g. noun, verb, or adjective, etc.), the English definition used this article, and an example sentence. ii. Number the words in the order they appear in the article. iii. If you cannot find an example sentence from dictionaries, you may use the sentence from the article. Do not create your own sentence. iv. Use the following dictionaries to look up definitions and examples: 1. Longman Dictionary of Contemporary English http://www.ldoceonline.com/dictionary/epidemic 2. Cambridge Dictionary https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/ 3. TheFreeDictionary http://www.thefreedictionary.com/innumerable Note: Please consult Longman or Cambridge first. The definitions I provide in class are mostly from these two dictionaries because they are easier to understand and remember. If you cannot find a suitable definition there, then use TheFreeDictionary. d) Do not email me your vocab list. You are responsible for proofreading it. However, if you have trouble finding a suitable definition for a word, you are welcome to ask Jennifer. e) Compose your speech as early as possible. f) Memorize and rehearse your speech well before your presentation day. g) For Group Presentations Only: 1. Have your ppt slides 100% ready for the 2nd meeting. 2. Bring your own laptop, presentation article and vocablary list. 3. Come to Jennifer’s office on time and present your entire presentation. 4. Revise your presentation based on Jennifer’s feedback. xiii IV. On the Presentation Day a) Distribute copies of the vocabulary list to your classmates, and submit one copy of the vocabulary list to the teacher during the class recess. b) [For Individual Presentations Only] Turn in your written report to the teacher before you step up to the podium to present. c) Content of the Presentation & Time Limit  Individual News Presentation (7 mins.) (With NO ppt slides) 1) News summary (3 mins.) : Summarize the news story. Tip: List some key words first. Then, organize the key words/main ideas in your own logic and in your own words. 2) Vocabulary word sharing (2 mins.) : Choose one or two new words you learned from the article and explain why the words made a strong impression on you. If time allows, you may also share a sentence from the article that you find interesting. 3) Your response to the news story (2 mins.) : Share your personal thoughts or reactions after reading the article. Q&A: After your presentation, your classmates and the teacher will ask you questions about the article or your presentation. (Students who ask questions can earn extra class participation points that day.)  Group News Presentation (25 mins.) (WITH ppt slides) 1) Warm-Up Activity (5 mins.) 2) Vocabulary (3 mins.) 3) Comprehension of the News Article (10 mins.) • Comprehension Questions • Subheadings 4) Extended Discussion (6 mins.) 5) Conclusion (1 min.) Please complete your speech within the time limit. When the time is up, you must stop immediately, even if you have not finished. d) Written Report (For Individual Presentations Only) 1. Type a written report of your presentation and give it to the teacher before you present on the presentation day. 2. The report should include: summary, word sharing and personal response/ thoughts after reading the article. 3. Post your written report on eeclass no later than the presentation day. 4. AI Usage Policy: You must not use AI to generate your speech. However, you are encouraged to use AI to proofread or revise your speech. If you do so, you must submit: • Your original version, • AI’s revised version, and • A sort list of lessons you learned from the AI’s feedback. e) PPT Slides (For Group Presentations Only) 1. Post your ppt slides on eeclass instead of submitting a written report. 2. Your last slide must include the detailed work allocation of all group members, both for preparation and for the in-class presentation. xiv Appendix II Rubric for Individual News Article Participants will delve into texts, actively engaging with the material to achieve a deeper understanding. Through this process, they will develop the ability to navigate complex narratives and expository texts with ease, while also honing their critical thinking abilities to analyze and interpret the content effectively. Subsidiary aim Throughout the duration of the course, students will actively participate in the following steps, which are strategically devised to enhance their critical thinking and reading proficiency: (1) Developing the ability to discern between factual information and subjective opinions presented in texts. (2) Evaluating the credibility of sources used in academic contexts. (3) Recognizing and understanding various perspectives presented in texts. (4) Engaging in whole-class discussions on current issues to practice critical thinking and analysis. (5) Collaborating in group problem-solving activities to deepen comprehension and analytical skills. (6) Enhancing public speaking abilities through individual presentations, thereby applying learned vocabulary and sentence structures effectively. Grading: 1. Attendance and participation 15% 2. Midterm Exam 25% 3. Final Exam 25% 4. Quizzes 15% 5. Presentations 20% Requirements & Rules: 1. Class attendance, lesson preparation and active class participation are required. ✔ The instructor takes attendance almost every class throughout the semester. ✔ If you are absent from a class meeting, 1 point will be deducted from semester grade. ✔ If you are absent in case of uncontrollable situations (e.g. illness, emergency, important occasions, etc.), please email the instructor as you decide to take a leave and give the instructor the valid proof WITHIN TWO WEEKS. A receipt or a medicine prescription with correct stamp of date by accredited hospitals can be seen as a valid proof. ✔ Being late for more than 20 minutes is treated as absence from that hour (0.5 point will be deducted). 2. Active Participation Incentive To encourage and reward active participation, students will receive 5 extra points every time they raise their hand to answer questions or volunteer to come to the stage to make a sentence. Accumulating 100 extra points through active participation will result in gaining one additional point atop your semester grade. Students will be introduced to commonly used vocabulary, phrases, and idioms specific to various office scenarios. To enhance language acquisition and output, the course will feature role-play exercises and group projects. These activities, particularly role-play and presentations, will serve as key opportunities for students to actively use and practice the language. Students will also be expected to present their findings and articulate their opinions in a structured and professional manner, further reinforcing their language skills. Subsidiary aim This course is designed to build students' professional manners, ethics, and English proficiency for effective workplace communication. (1) Students can understand and use professional vocabulary, phrases, and idioms common in office settings. (2) Students can apply interviewing techniques to enhance communication and assessment skills. (3) Students can understand the significance of positive teamwork dynamics. (4) Students can be familiar with technological advancements in office. (5) Students can create and deliver clear and effective presentations. (6) Students can develop strategies for understanding and navigating office politics. (7) Students can analyze sales strategies and apply them in real-world selling scenarios. Can take some initiatives in an interview/consultation (e.g., to bring up a new subject) but is very dependent on interviewer in the interaction. [interviewing and being interviewed] 6. Can paraphrase short written passages in a simple fashion, using the original text wording and ordering. docs.text: 1 National Tsing Hua University 中級選讀英文［學術生活英語聽講］ Academic Living English-Listening and Speaking Fall 2026 楊幸瑜 (Jane Yang) Course Number 11510LANG200064 Credits 2 Classroom 綜二 103 Class hours □ Monday □ Tuesday ■ Wednesday □ Thursday □ Friday ■ 10:10 A.M. – 12:00 P.M. Course Type ■ EGP (English for general purposes) ■ EAP (English for academic purposes) □ EOP (English for occupational purposes) Language Level ■ A2 (初級) ■ B1（中級） ■ B1-B2 □ B2（中高級） □ B2+ □ C1 Core Ability ■ comprehension/reception ■ communication/interaction ■ production 可選課學生 身分別 □ 頂標生 □ 前標生 ■ 中級生 ■ 初級生 Prerequisites 「修畢初級英語一、二」 或 「修畢中級英語一、二」的學生/對各國文化有 興趣且期待訓練口語聽力能力的同學 加簽說明 ■ 不開放加簽 提醒：學生修讀英文領域課程，請依本校規劃選課之修業年級選課。如因個人 考量，未對應年級與學院分配時段而逕自改於其他修業年級選課或改選其他時 段之英文領域課程，或指定加簽某特定課程，英語教育中心與任課教師將礙難 配合或處理。 Instructor & Contact Information: Name Email Office & Tel Office Hour 楊幸瑜 Jane Yang janeyang1129@gmail.com N/A By Appointment Course Aims / Description1 Primary aim This course is designed to help students enhance their listening and speaking skills in English, with a focus on developing their ability to communicate effectively in both academic and real-world contexts. Through 2 engaging in diverse communicative tasks, students will strengthen their interpersonal communication abilities, build confidence in expressing ideas, and develop strategies for understanding and responding appropriately in a variety of multicultural situations. Class activities will include pair and group discussions, role plays, interviews, and class presentations, all of which will help students improve their listening comprehension and speaking fluency. At the same time, these tasks will also prepare students to participate actively in academic discussions, collaborate on group projects, and deliver well-structured presentations, fostering skills essential for success in both academic and professional environments. By the end of the course, students will become more confident and versatile communicators in English, capable of navigating both academic and everyday interactions with clarity, cultural awareness, and effective communicative strategies. They will be better equipped to process information from diverse sources, express their ideas persuasively, and adapt their language use appropriately to different contexts and audiences. Subsidiary aim In this class, students will have opportunity to 1. Improve listening comprehension and academic listening skills: Students will engage with diverse audio materials, including stories, lectures, and selected BBC Learning English Course: 6 Minute English episodes. They will practice identifying main ideas, understanding speaker opinions, inferring meaning, and following both conversational and academic discussions across accents and contexts. 2. Develop speaking fluency and presentation skills: Students will express opinions, share experiences, and participate in structured discussions and presentations based on topics from the textbook and the selected BBC Learning English Course episodes. They will practice storytelling, descriptive speech, and academic presentation techniques to improve clarity, organization, and use of appropriate vocabulary. 3. Enhance communicative competence and academic strategies: Through role plays, interviews, and discussions, students will develop practical and academic communication strategies, including clarifying, summarizing, negotiating meaning, and adapting language for different contexts and purposes. 4. Develop critical thinking and analytical discussion skills: Students will analyze global issues and cultural topics from the textbook, developing their ability to evaluate viewpoints, support opinions with reasoning, and participate in academic discussions with confidence. [overall listening comprehension] EOP B1 Can understand straightforward factual information about common everyday or job-related topics, identifying both general messages and specific details, provided speech is clearly articulated in a generally familiar accent. [understanding interaction between native speakers] LISTENING AS A MEMBER OF A LIVE AUDIENCE B1 Can follow in outline straightforward short talks on familiar topics provided these are delivered in clearly articulated standard dialect. [listening as a member of a live audience] EOP EAP LISTENING TO ANNOUNCEMENTS & INSTRUCTIONS B1 Can follow detailed directions. [understanding native speaker interlocutor] CONVERSATION B1 Can enter unprepared into conversations on familiar topics. [conversation] B1 Can follow clearly articulated speech directed at him/her in everyday conversation, though will sometimes have to ask for repetition of particular words and phrases. [conversation] B1 Can maintain a conversation or discussion but may sometimes be difficult to follow when trying to say exactly what he/she would like to. [informal discussion (with friends)] B1 + Can explain why something is a problem. [informal discussion (with friends)] B1 + Can give brief comments on the views of others. [informal discussion (with friends)] B1 + Can compare and contrast alternatives, discussing what to do, where to go, who or which to choose, etc. [informal discussion (with friends)] B2 Can account for and sustain his/her opinions in discussion by providing relevant explanation, arguments and comments. [formal discussion (meetings)] B1 + Can follow much of what is said that is related to his/her field, provided interlocutors avoid very idiomatic usage and articulated clearly. [formal discussion (meetings)] EAP EOP GOAL-ORIENTED COOPERATION (E.G., REPAIRING A CAR, DISCUSSING A DOCUMENT, ORGANIZING AN EVENT) B1 Can generally follow what is said and, when necessary, can repeat back part of what someone has said to confirm mutual understanding. docs.text: 1 National Tsing Hua University 中級選讀英文［學術情境閱讀 Academic Situational Reading］ Fall 2026 Course Number LANG 200066 Credits 2 Classroom 綜二館 202 Class hours □ Monday □ Tuesday □ Wednesday □ Thursday  Friday  1:20P.M. – 3:10P.M. □ 3:30P.M. – 5:20P.M. □ _____ P.M. – 5_____P.M. Course Type □ EGP (English for general purposes)  EAP (English for academic purposes) □ EOP (English for occupational purposes) Language Level  B1（中級） □ B1-B2 □ B2（中高級） □ B2+ □ C1 Core Ability  comprehension/reception  communication/interaction □ production 可選課學生 身分別 □ 頂標生 □ 前標生  中級生  初級生 Prerequisites 修畢中級英文一二／初級英文一二課程且成績及格 加簽說明 □ 不開放人工加簽。所有學生須由選課系統亂數選課。  開放人工加簽__2__位學生。學生符合以下條件，得於第__1__週上課時， 向老師提出加簽申請。老師簽署申請表後，申請表送英語教育中心辦公 室。由老師進行線上簽核。  條件 1：必須於第一週到課  條件 2：須有其他時段【選讀英語文】衝堂無法選課之證明（如選課紀錄 或本學期所有科目課程表）  條件 3：自所屬選課階段（大二生：第 1-2 次選課；大三、大四學生：第 3 次選課）起，亂數選課皆未選上（選上但退選者，不得以人工加簽再次選 課）  條件 4：應屆畢業生 備註：符合以上條件者若超過 2 位，則依優先順序加簽前 2 名。 提醒：學生修讀英文領域課程，請依本校規劃選課之修業年級選課。如因個 人考量，未對應年級而逕自改於其他修業年級選課之英文領域課程，或指定 加簽某特定課程，英語教育中心與任課教師將礙難配合或處理。 Instructor & Contact Information: Name Email 汪友于 lucywang2012th@gmail.com 2 Course Aims / Description1 Primary aim This course aims to equip intermediate students with the essential reading skills, strategies, and academic literacy competencies required for success in English- medium academic contexts. The course adopts a situational approach, exposing students to authentic academic reading scenarios across various disciplines while progressively building their capacity to comprehend, analyze, and critically evaluate academic texts. Subsidiary aim Subsidiary aims describe the enabling language skills, strategies, and competencies that students must develop to achieve the primary objectives of this course. These aims are organized to progressively build academic situational reading proficiency. Students will practice the following in this course: (1) Developing reading skills and strategies Students develop pre-reading and text preview competencies. Students identify main Ideas and supporting details. Students identify author's purpose and perspective. (2) Applying language knowledge to reading comprehension Students build core academic vocabulary recognition and usage. Students decode complex grammatical structures in academic texts. Students build expanded academic and discipline-specific vocabulary. (3) Practicing higher-order thinking Students make inferences and interpret implicit meanings. Students evaluate arguments, evidence, and source credibility. Students synthesize information from multiple sources. (4) Enhancing academic reading proficiency Students recognize and analyze academic text structures and rhetorical patterns. Students develop active annotation skills through extensive reading. Students use critical thinking to understand the underlying academic concepts. Students will be invited to complete a reading profile questionnaire individually and discuss their responses with a partner in order to activate their metacognitive awareness, help instructor understand their backgrounds, and build classroom community. Later, students will work in groups to categorize words by displaying 10 words from readings (mix of general, academic, and specialized) to enhance their academic word awareness. Students will be also asked to discuss why recognizing academic vocabulary like analyze, theory, examine, hypothesis, research, comprehension, cognitive is important. Students will maintain a vocabulary notebook, record 5-10 new academic words per week which include: word, definition, example 1 請參閱 Bloom’s Taxonomy of Measurable Verbs。 3 sentence, word family members, and collocations. Since academic English has many fixed phrases (collocations) that appear frequently, the game “Words That Go Together” will be played to improve academic reading fluency. Students will build up academic vocabulary as well as synonyms and antonyms through collaborative learning such as brain storming. Prefixes, suffixes, root words, and collocations will be also focused. They will be also encouraged to analyze context clues for the words by finding some unfamiliar words in the text to identify context clues involving definition clue (direct explanation), synonym clue, and example/explanation clue. After being familiar with the new words and reading skills involving making inferences in context, students will improve reading comprehension. As for real academic situations, Students will receive some different academic scenarios and must choose appropriate reading strategy such as skimming or scanning. By the way, listening skills help reinforce letter-sound relationships to correctly pronounce written words. Video teaching helps review words to enhance word recognition and reading comprehension via academic situations in videos. After mid-term, in order for students to read extensively, they will vote for three topics out of six to read and they will be encouraged to get other reading materials, such as the China Post, Taiwan News, CNN, related to the topics they vote for, as their reading assignments. Students have to highlight the key points and take notes on their outside reading materials to share the main ideas and their reading comprehension with their group members. Academic Language Proficiency? "Academic language proficiency is knowing and being able to use general and content-specific vocabulary, specialized or complex grammatical structures – all for the purpose of acquiring new knowledge and skills, interacting about a topic, or imparting information to others," (Bailey, 2007). In sum, students who are proficient AL users are well-equipped to learn new knowledge through reading or listening, and to express their knowledge and ideas through oral discussions and writing. Source: https://www.serpinstitute.org/wordgen-weekly/academic-language When we refer When we refer to “academic language”, we’re talking about the language students need in order to understand the content that is being taught across the curriculum; the language needed to process learning; and the language students need in order to understand what they are learning, how and why; as well as to self-monitor this. … Dr Robin Scarcella, in 2003, told us that this “academic language” also includes the language of higher- order thinking such as inventing, inferring and conceptualising, and includes both oral and written communication skills too. … Echevarria, Short and Powers also identified that students must have an in-depth knowledge of words in context, in order to achieve fluency; something that is crucial for students’ academic success. It's been identified that there are three dimensions of academic language which are: 15  Linguistic  Cognitive  Sociocultural/ Psychological These three dimensions work together to achieve academic English fluency and were first identified by Kern in 2003, who argued that all three dimensions must be addressed by schools in order for EAL students to reach their potential. Summarised briefly, linguistic fluency includes:  an understanding how language functions (grammar rules, intonation, parts of words parts);  where and when to use certain genres and forms of writing;  writing organisation and structure (discourse markers etc); and  academic vocabulary, including words that are used across subject areas, for example: analyse, explain. Cognitive fluency includes:  critical thinking skills;  higher-order thinking skills;  identifying fact from opinion;  reading texts critically;  writing and speaking persuasively using evidence; and  students thinking about their own language acquisition, and evaluating/monitoring their own learning. Sociocultural/Psychological fluency includes:  “social and cultural norms, values, beliefs, attitudes, motivations, interests, behaviours, practices, and habits” (Scarcella 2003); and  “the particular conventions and norms that characterise the people who use it” (Scarcella, 2003); Source: https://www.ealinclusive.com/overview-of-academic-language 16

By integrating pronunciation training with academic logic, students are expected to achieve the following visions: 1. Metacognition: Develop the ability to self-monitor and self-correct speech, moving beyond rote imitation to understanding the mechanics of sound. 2. Intelligibility: Shift the focus from a "standard accent" to effective communication, ensuring clarity and precision in academic contexts. 3. Integration of Sound and Logic: Utilize suprasegmental features (stress, rhythm, intonation) as high-order thinking tools to organize arguments and highlight information hierarchy. Subsidiary aim To achieve the main goals, this course targets the following milestones: 1. Diagnosis & Correction: Identify and correct common segmental errors (vowels/consonants) that impede understanding. 2. Mastering Rhythm: Internalize the "stress-timed" nature of English to improve the flow and naturalness of speech. 3. Academic Pragmatics: Learn to use vocal cues to perform academic functions (e.g., signaling transitions, contrasting ideas, hedging). 4. Confidence Building: Reduce speaking anxiety through consistent practice and constructive peer feedback.
