Introduction to English as a Lingua Franca (ELF). Materials: Recording a 1- minute "Research Interest Statement" (Baseline recording). Activity: Peer Blind Listening. Students identify "points of confusion" without seeing the text. Analysis: Is it a segmental error or a lack of prosody? Assignments: In-class self-intro. Prepare for “Research Interest Statement” and upload to eeclass. Building Metacognitive Awareness. Understanding that oral expression requires "editing" and "design," just like academic writing. 2 Wk2: 9/8 Intelligibility Focus – Key Consonants & Vowels: Prioritizing clarity over a "standard" accent. Addressing common confusion points for L1 Mandarin speakers. Materials: The Academic Word List (AWL). Activity: Minimal Pairs with Academic Context (e.g., low/law, thinking/sinking, collect/correct). Assignments: Phonetic symbols of vowels and their pronunciation. Get ready for group presentation (1). Precision & Professionalism. In technical fields, mispronouncing a variable or term can lead to a misunderstanding of the entire formula or theory. 3 Wk3: 9/15 Word Stress & Morphology: Stress determines part of speech and meaning. Materials: Word Families (e.g., PHOtograph, phoTOgraphy, photoGRAPHic). Activity: Rubber Band Strategy (physically stretching a band to match stress duration). Assignments: Phonetic symbols of consonants and their pronunciation. Vocabulary Acquisition. Academic terminology is often polysyllabic. Mastering stress rules helps students quickly acquire new terms and identify keywords in listening. 4 Wk4: 9/22 The Soul of the Sentence – Content vs. Function Words: The "Stress- Materials: A short academic abstract. Activity: Telegraphic Information Hierarchy. Deciding which word to stress is a higher-order 9 Timed" nature of English rhythm. Speech: Removing prepositions/articles to isolate the "core message", Schwa sound /ə/ reduction practice. Assignments: Phonetic symbols and their practices (1). Get ready for group presentation (2). thinking process—it forces the student to determine what information is essential versus peripheral. 5 Wk5: 9/29 Thought Groups & Pausing: Speaking with commas and periods. Reducing cognitive load for the listener. Materials: Complex/Compound sentences from journal articles. Activity: "Chunking" Practice. Students receive unpunctuated text and must mark logical breathing points. Comparing how different chunks alter meaning. Assignments: Phonetic symbols and their practices (2). Syntactic Processing. Proper pausing allows the audience to digest complex information. It demonstrates logical clarity and consideration for the listener. 6 Wk6: 10/6 Words & Prominence: New Information vs. Old Information. Materials: Text containing "Problem to Solution" structures. Activity: Contrastive Stress drills (e.g., "I didn’t say HE stole the data" – shifting focus changes meaning). Assignments: Phonetic symbols and their practices (3). Get ready for group presentation (3). Literature Review Strategy. Using stress to clearly distinguish between "what previous researchers did" (Old) and "what this study contributes" (New). 7 Wk7: 10/13 Intonation & Pragmatics: Falling (Certainty), Rising (Inquiry), Fall-Rise (Reservation/Contrast). Materials: Audio clips of academic discussions/roundtables. Activity: Simulation of Hedging & Stance. Intonation is key to expressing academic humility and rigor, 10 academic disagreement. Using the Fall-Rise tone to express polite dissent ("I see your point, but..."). Assignments: Phonetic symbols and their practices (4). Get ready for Midterm. preventing statements from sounding overly dogmatic or aggressive. 8 Wk8: 10/20 Midterm – Mini-3MT (Three Minute Thesis) Activity: Students select a paper abstract and present it. Assessment: Focus on Thought Groups, Prominence of keywords, and the distinction between old/new information. 9 Wk9: 10/27 Connected Speech & Fluency: Smoothing the stream of speech (Linking, Elision). Materials: Academic transition phrases (e.g., First of all, In addition to). Activity: Shadowing Technique. Mimicking a TED Talk speaker to internalize flow and speed. Assignments: Phonetic symbols and their practices (5). Get ready for group presentation (4). Credibility. Fluency reduces the listener's processing effort. Familiarity with linking allows the speaker to allocate brainpower to content rather than pronunciation mechanics. 10 Wk10: 11/3 Signposting in Presentations: Using sound to guide the audience through structure. Materials: Presentation scripts. Activity: "Pitch Reset" practice. Using a higher pitch to signal the start of a new section (e.g., "Turning now to the methodology..."). Assignments: Phonetic symbols and their practices (6). Macro-Structure Control. A pitch reset acts as an auditory header, re- engaging the audience's attention at critical transition points. 11 Wk11: 11/10 Voicing Data & Visuals: Pronouncing numbers, trends, and graph Materials: Various statistical charts and graphs. Results Interpretation. Accurate vocal representation of data 11 descriptions. Activity: Number stress differentiation (e.g., 15 vs. 50), Sound Iconicity: Matching voice pitch to the trend line (voice goes up as the graph goes up). Assignments: Phonetic symbols and their practices (7). Get ready for group presentation (5). ensures the audience "hears" the trends, reinforcing the visual evidence. 12 Wk12: 11/17 Strategies for Q&A and Defense: Listening for stress in questions and responding with stability. Materials: Videos of conference Q&A sessions. Activity: Paraphrasing: Restating the question to confirm understanding, Buy-Time Strategies: Using fillers (e.g., "That is a crucial point...") to think while maintaining vocal control. Assignments: Phonetic symbols and their practices (8). Get ready for the Elevator Pitch. Critical Defense. A steady tempo and controlled intonation during Q&A demonstrate confidence and mastery, even when facing challenging inquiries. 13 Wk13: 11/24 The Elevator Pitch: Persuasion and condensation. Activity: 90-second research pitch. Requirement: Every sentence must have a clear Focus Word. Assignments: Phonetic symbols and their practices (9). Get ready for group presentation (6). Synthesis & Value Proposition. Condensing complex research implies high-level understanding. Using sound to highlight the "So What?" (significance) of the study. 14 Wk14: 12/1 Paralinguistics & Non- Verbal Communication: Synchronizing eye contact and gestures with stress and intonation. Materials: Analysis of top-tier speakers (watching silent first, then with sound). Activity: Video recording and playback to check for Embodied Cognition. Effective communication is multimodal. Coordinating gestures with speech rhythm reinforces the speaker's 12 Synchrony between hand gestures and vocal stress. Assignments: Phonetic symbols and their practices (10). Get ready for final presentation. argument. 15 Wk15: 12/8 Final Simulation – Mock International Conference Format: A simulated symposium. 5-8 minute presentation + 2 minute Q&A per student. Requirement: Mandatory use of signposting, contrastive intonation, and proper thought grouping. Assignments: Get ready for self-analysis. Feedback: Peer review using a rubric based on the course concepts. 16 Wk16: 12/15 Reflection & Future Roadmap: Progress review (Week 1 vs. Week 15). Activity: Self-analysis of the "before and after" recordings, Building a personal "Audio Corpus" (collecting recordings of experts in their specific field). Lifelong Learning. Course Type □ EGP (English for general purposes)  EAP (English for academic purposes) □ EOP (English for occupational purposes) Language Level  B1（中級） □ B1-B2 □ B2（中高級） □ B2+ □ C1 Core Ability  comprehension/reception  communication/interaction □ production 可選課學生 身分別 □ 頂標生 □ 前標生  中級生  初級生 Prerequisites 修畢中級英文一二／初級英文一二課程且成績及格 加簽說明 □ 不開放人工加簽。所有學生須由選課系統亂數選課。  開放人工加簽__2__位學生。學生符合以下條件，得於第__1__週上課時， 向老師提出加簽申請。老師簽署申請表後，申請表送英語教育中心辦公 室。由老師進行線上簽核。  條件 1：必須於第一週到課  條件 2：須有其他時段【選讀英語文】衝堂無法選課之證明（如選課紀錄 或本學期所有科目課程表）  條件 3：自所屬選課階段（大二生：第 1-2 次選課；大三、大四學生：第 3 次選課）起，亂數選課皆未選上（選上但退選者，不得以人工加簽再次選 課）  條件 4：應屆畢業生 備註：符合以上條件者若超過 2 位，則依優先順序加簽前 2 名。 提醒：學生修讀英文領域課程，請依本校規劃選課之修業年級選課。如因個 人考量，未對應年級而逕自改於其他修業年級選課之英文領域課程，或指定 加簽某特定課程，英語教育中心與任課教師將礙難配合或處理。 Instructor & Contact Information: Name Email 汪友于 lucywang2012th@gmail.com 2 Course Aims / Description1 Primary aim This course aims to equip intermediate students with the essential reading skills, strategies, and academic literacy competencies required for success in English- medium academic contexts. The course adopts a situational approach, exposing students to authentic academic reading scenarios across various disciplines while progressively building their capacity to comprehend, analyze, and critically evaluate academic texts. Subsidiary aim Subsidiary aims describe the enabling language skills, strategies, and competencies that students must develop to achieve the primary objectives of this course. These aims are organized to progressively build academic situational reading proficiency. Students will practice the following in this course: (1) Developing reading skills and strategies Students develop pre-reading and text preview competencies. Students identify main Ideas and supporting details. Students identify author's purpose and perspective. (2) Applying language knowledge to reading comprehension Students build core academic vocabulary recognition and usage. Students decode complex grammatical structures in academic texts. Students build expanded academic and discipline-specific vocabulary. (3) Practicing higher-order thinking Students make inferences and interpret implicit meanings. Students evaluate arguments, evidence, and source credibility. Students synthesize information from multiple sources. (4) Enhancing academic reading proficiency Students recognize and analyze academic text structures and rhetorical patterns. Students develop active annotation skills through extensive reading. Students use critical thinking to understand the underlying academic concepts. Students will be invited to complete a reading profile questionnaire individually and discuss their responses with a partner in order to activate their metacognitive awareness, help instructor understand their backgrounds, and build classroom community. Later, students will work in groups to categorize words by displaying 10 words from readings (mix of general, academic, and specialized) to enhance their academic word awareness. Students will be also asked to discuss why recognizing academic vocabulary like analyze, theory, examine, hypothesis, research, comprehension, cognitive is important. Students will maintain a vocabulary notebook, record 5-10 new academic words per week which include: word, definition, example 1 請參閱 Bloom’s Taxonomy of Measurable Verbs。 3 sentence, word family members, and collocations. Since academic English has many fixed phrases (collocations) that appear frequently, the game “Words That Go Together” will be played to improve academic reading fluency. Students will build up academic vocabulary as well as synonyms and antonyms through collaborative learning such as brain storming. Prefixes, suffixes, root words, and collocations will be also focused. They will be also encouraged to analyze context clues for the words by finding some unfamiliar words in the text to identify context clues involving definition clue (direct explanation), synonym clue, and example/explanation clue. After being familiar with the new words and reading skills involving making inferences in context, students will improve reading comprehension. As for real academic situations, Students will receive some different academic scenarios and must choose appropriate reading strategy such as skimming or scanning. By the way, listening skills help reinforce letter-sound relationships to correctly pronounce written words. Video teaching helps review words to enhance word recognition and reading comprehension via academic situations in videos. After mid-term, in order for students to read extensively, they will vote for three topics out of six to read and they will be encouraged to get other reading materials, such as the China Post, Taiwan News, CNN, related to the topics they vote for, as their reading assignments. Students have to highlight the key points and take notes on their outside reading materials to share the main ideas and their reading comprehension with their group members. [processing text] EAP B1+ Can collate short pieces of information from several sources and summarize them for somebody else. structures and discourse patterns for academic competence (comparing, classifying, synthesizing, evaluating, and inferring) 14 What is Academic Language Proficiency? "Academic language proficiency is knowing and being able to use general and content-specific vocabulary, specialized or complex grammatical structures – all for the purpose of acquiring new knowledge and skills, interacting about a topic, or imparting information to others," (Bailey, 2007). In sum, students who are proficient AL users are well-equipped to learn new knowledge through reading or listening, and to express their knowledge and ideas through oral discussions and writing. Source: https://www.serpinstitute.org/wordgen-weekly/academic-language When we refer When we refer to “academic language”, we’re talking about the language students need in order to understand the content that is being taught across the curriculum; the language needed to process learning; and the language students need in order to understand what they are learning, how and why; as well as to self-monitor this. … Dr Robin Scarcella, in 2003, told us that this “academic language” also includes the language of higher- order thinking such as inventing, inferring and conceptualising, and includes both oral and written communication skills too. … Echevarria, Short and Powers also identified that students must have an in-depth knowledge of words in context, in order to achieve fluency; something that is crucial for students’ academic success. It's been identified that there are three dimensions of academic language which are: 15  Linguistic  Cognitive  Sociocultural/ Psychological These three dimensions work together to achieve academic English fluency and were first identified by Kern in 2003, who argued that all three dimensions must be addressed by schools in order for EAL students to reach their potential. Summarised briefly, linguistic fluency includes:  an understanding how language functions (grammar rules, intonation, parts of words parts);  where and when to use certain genres and forms of writing;  writing organisation and structure (discourse markers etc); and  academic vocabulary, including words that are used across subject areas, for example: analyse, explain. Cognitive fluency includes:  critical thinking skills;  higher-order thinking skills;  identifying fact from opinion;  reading texts critically;  writing and speaking persuasively using evidence; and  students thinking about their own language acquisition, and evaluating/monitoring their own learning. Sociocultural/Psychological fluency includes:  “social and cultural norms, values, beliefs, attitudes, motivations, interests, behaviours, practices, and habits” (Scarcella 2003); and  “the particular conventions and norms that characterise the people who use it” (Scarcella, 2003); Source: https://www.ealinclusive.com/overview-of-academic-language 16

After immersing in facts and figures pertaining to an interesting contemporary topic, students are encouraged to engage in critical thinking and communicate with fellow students on related issues in their own field of study. Subsidiary aim After completing this course, students should be able to • understand the main points of discussion on topics that are familiar, of personal interest or involving everyday college life • give descriptions on a variety of topics and subjects that are likely to be encountered in academic life 1 請參閱 Bloom’s Taxonomy of Measurable Verbs。 2 • follow essentials of lectures, talks, and other forms of academic presentations • make their opinions and reactions understood in academic settings • take notes during a lecture on topics that is within their field of interest • develop and present a short talk on subject related to students’ field of study • initiate and maintain simple face-to-face conversation on general, academic, or leisure topics CEFR Can-do Statements (B2, B2+ and C1) Reception eception Listening UNDERSTANDING INTERACTION BETWEEN NATIVE SPEAKERS B1 Can generally follow the main points of extended discussion around him/her, provided speech is clearly articulated in standard dialect. Can give detailed accounts of experiences, describing feelings and reactions. [sustained monologue: describing experience] B1 Can describe dreams, hope, and ambitions. [sustained monologue: describing experience] ADDRESSING AUDIENCES B1 Can give a prepared straightforward presentation on a familiar topic within his/her everyday life, briefly give reasons and explanations for opinions, plans and actions. [addressing audiences] Reception Communi cation Strategies IDENTIFYING CUES & INFERRING (SPOKEN & WRITTEN) B1 Can identify unfamiliar words from the context on topics related to his/her field and interests. docs.text: 1 National Tsing Hua University 中級選讀英文［學術生活英語聽講］ English for Academic Communication: Listening & Speaking Fall 2026 Course Number 11510LANG 200072 Credits 2 Classroom 請查閱校務資訊系統的課 程資訊後填入 Class hours □ Monday □ Tuesday □ Wednesday □ Thursday  Friday  1:20P.M. – 3:10P.M. □ 3:30P.M. – 5:20P.M. □ _____ P.M. – 5_____P.M. Course Type □ EGP (English for general purposes)  EAP (English for academic purposes) □ EOP (English for occupational purposes) Language Level  B1-B1+（中級） □ B1-B2 □ B2（中高級） □ B2+ □ C1 Core Ability  comprehension/reception  communication/interaction  production 可選課學生 身分別 □ 頂標生 □ 前標生  中級生  初級生 Prerequisites 初級／中級英文一／二 加簽說明 不開放人工加簽，所有學生須由選課系統亂數選課。 Instructor & Contact Information: Name Email Office & Tel Office Hour 蔡佩蓉 (Katherine Tsai) k_tsai@gapp.nthu.edu.tw N/A N/A Course Aims / Description1 Primary aim This intermediate English course is designed to provide students with an authentic English-speaking environment to practice language for every aspect of academic life, from social networking to relationships, and from money issues to discussions of changing fads. After immersing in facts and figures pertaining to an interesting contemporary topic, students are encouraged to engage in critical thinking and communicate with fellow students on related issues in their own field of study. Subsidiary aim After completing this course, students should be able to • understand the main points of discussion on topics that are familiar, of personal interest or involving everyday college life • give descriptions on a variety of topics and subjects that are likely to be 1 請參閱 Bloom’s Taxonomy of Measurable Verbs。 2 encountered in academic life • follow essentials of lectures, talks, and other forms of academic presentations • make their opinions and reactions understood in academic settings • take notes during a lecture on topics that is within their field of interest • develop and present a short talk on subject related to students’ field of study • initiate and maintain simple face-to-face conversation on general, academic, or leisure topics CEFR Can-do Statements (B2, B2+ and C1) Reception eception Listening UNDERSTANDING INTERACTION BETWEEN NATIVE SPEAKERS B1 Can generally follow the main points of extended discussion around him/her, provided speech is clearly articulated in standard dialect. [understanding interaction between native speakers] LISTENING AS A MEMBER OF A LIVE AUDIENCE B1 Can follow in outline straightforward short talks on familiar topics provided these are delivered in clearly articulated standard dialect. [listening as a member of a live audience] B1+ Can follow a lecture or a talk within his/her own field, provided the subject matter is familiar and the presentation straightforward and clearly structured. [listening as a member of a live audience] EOP EAP LISTENING TO ANNOUNCEMENTS & INSTRUCTIONS B1 Can follow detailed directions. [listening to announcements & instructions] LISTENING TO RADIO, AUDIO & RECORDINGS B1 Can understand the main points of radio news bulletins and simpler recorded material about familiar subjects delivered relatively slowly and clearly. [listening to radio, audio & recordings] WATCHING TV & FILM B1 Can catch the main points in TV programs on familiar topics when the delivery is relatively slow and clear. [watching TV & film] B1 Can follow many films in which visuals and action carry much of the storyline, and which are delivered clearly in straightforward language. [watching TV & film] Receptio n Reading OVERALL READING COMPREHENSION B1 Can read straightforward factual texts on subjects related to his/her field and interest with a satisfactory level of comprehension. [overall reading comprehension] EAP EOP I n t e r a c t i o n S p o k e n Speaking OVERALL SPOKEN INTERACTION 3 B1 Can enter unprepared into conversation of familiar topics, express personal opinions and exchange information on topics that are familiar, of personal interest or pertinent to every life (e.g., family, hobbies, work, travel, and current events). [overall spoken interaction] UNDERSTANDING NATIVE SPEAKER INTERLOCUTOR B1 Can follow clearly articulated speech directed at him/her in everyday conversation, though will sometimes have to ask for repetition of particular words and phrases. [understanding native speaker interlocutor] CONVERSATION B1 Can maintain a conversation or discussion but may sometimes be difficult to follow when trying to say exactly what he/she would like to. [conversation] B1 Can express and respond to feelings such as surprise, happiness, sadness, interest and indifference. [conversation] INFORMAL DISCUSSION (WITH FRIENDS) B1 Can generally follow the main points in an informal discussion with friends provided speech is clearly articulated in standard dialect. [informal discussion (with friends)] B1 Can make his/her opinions and reactions understood as regards solutions to problems or practical questions of where to go, what to do, how to organize an event (e.g., an outing). [informal discussion (with friends)] B1 Can express belief, opinion, agreement, and disagreement politely. [informal discussion (with friends)] FORMAL DISCUSSION (MEETINGS) B1+ Can follow much of what is said that is related to his/her field, provided interlocutors avoid very idiomatic usage and articulated clearly. [formal discussion (meetings)] EAP EOP INFORMATION EXCHANGE B1+ Can synthesize and report information and arguments from a number of sources. [information exchange] EAP EOP Production Spoken Speaking SUSTAINED MONOLOGUE: DESCRIBING EXPERIENCE B1 Can reasonably fluently relate a straightforward narrative or description as a linear sequence of points. Can give detailed accounts of experiences, describing feelings and reactions. [sustained monologue: describing experience] B1 Can describe dreams, hope, and ambitions. [sustained monologue: describing experience] ADDRESSING AUDIENCES B1 Can give a prepared straightforward presentation on a familiar topic within his/her everyday life, briefly give reasons and explanations for opinions, plans and actions. [addressing audiences] R e c e p t i o n Communi IDENTIFYING CUES & INFERRING (SPOKEN & WRITTEN) 4 cation Strategies B1 Can identify unfamiliar words from the context on topics related to his/her field and interests. [identifying cues & inferring (spoken & written)] EAP EOP Working with Text Communi cation Strategies NOTE-TAKING (LECTURES, SEMINARS, ETC.) B1+ Can take notes during a lecture, which are precise enough for his/her own use at a later date, provided the topic is within his/her field of interest and the talk is clear and well-structured. [note- taking (lectures, seminars, etc.) EAP PROCESSING TEXT B1 Can paraphrase short written passages in a simple fashion, using the original text wording and ordering. [processing text] EAP B1+ Can collate short pieces of information from several sources and summarize them for somebody else. [processing text] EAP 英文核心能力指標 University Student Core Competency Indicators 1. 英語溝通與表達能力 (ability to communicate and express oneself in English) 40% 2. 深度分析與組織思考的能力 (ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English) 20% 3. 英語學習策略與技巧 (knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques) 20% 4. 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 (global views of English and multicultural diversity) 10% 5. 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣與能力 (ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit) 10% Teaching Materials and References Textbook(s) New Interactions 2: Listening/Speaking, by Judith Tanka and Paul Most. This course aims at providing graduate students with the essential skills in academic written communications, meaning both the reading and writing of scholarly articles. Topics of this course include the common structure (IMRD/IPTC), concerns & moves of different sections, two distinct approaches to Abstracts, strategies to maintain the flow of the writing, as well as when/how to write descriptively (data commentary) and analytically (CARS model). ✎ Writing is thinking and this course is designed to help you writer better, and also think more logically and critically. [Suggested total learning time: 24 hours +] Course Objectives This course starts an analysis of purposes and audience of research articles, then move on to sample texts from various disciplines. By the end of the course, learners will be able to: ✎ Improve research writing skills for clarity and coherence. ✎ Develop discipline-specific vocabulary and genre knowledge for research writing. ✎ Enhance critical thinking skills for evaluating academic texts. Course Requirements 1. Watch 9-hour of self-paced online lectures on 清華雲 platform. 2. Take 8 quizzes and the final exam on 清華雲 platform. 3. Active participation in all 4 synchronous sessions (google meet attendance to be recorded) 4. Complete and submit all tasks (8 quizzes, final exam, analysis report) on time. 5. Use of AI: Conditionally open. Regarding transparency and responsibility, you can choose to use AI for collaboration and mutual learning to enhance the quality of your work. If you do, you must briefly explain how generative AI was used. - Watch Unit 6 lectures; take Quiz 6 . - Identify the moves in Discussion/Conclusion in your model article. 10 11/9 (1) Introducing your study: CARS model (2) Group discussion (SS III) - Watch Unit 7 lectures; take Quiz 7. - Identify the 3 obligatory moves of CARS model in your model article. 11 11/16 (1) RA abstract (1) Review - Watch Unit 8 & 9 lectures; take Quiz 8 . - Identify the moves in the abstract of your Fall 2026 3/3 model article. 12 11/23 (1) Comment on analysis reports (2) Feedback and wrap-up (SS IV) - Review Unit 1- 9 lectures; take the final exam. - Submit an analysis report of the model article 24 hours before synchronous session IV. ⚫ Synchronous sessions (SS), the live sessions, are conducted online at https://meet.google.com/ecb-nsso-prp on designated Monday, 13:20 - 14:10 pm (T5), during the course period between, Fall 2026 (GMT+8) on Oct 5, Oct 19, Nov 9, and Nov 23 respectively. EXTRA TIPS FOR LIVE SESSIONS 1. Prepare in Advance: Before each live session, review the relevant materials, readings, or assignments. This preparation will help you follow the discussion more easily and participate more effectively. 2. Test Your Technology: Ensure your internet connection is stable and your audio and video settings are working properly. Join the session a few minutes early to troubleshoot any potential technical issues. You’re supposed to turn on your camera at all time. 3. Create a Quiet Environment: Find a quiet, distraction-free space to join the live session. This helps you stay focused and actively participate in discussions without interruptions. 4. Participate Actively: Use the chat function to ask questions, share comments, or respond to peers. Raise your hand virtually if you want to speak or contribute to the discussion verbally. If the session includes breakout room activities, actively participate and collaborate with your group. This is a great way to deepen your understanding of the material and engage with your peers. 5. Take Notes: Keep a notebook or digital document open to jot down key points, ideas, or questions that arise during the session. This will help you retain information and formulate questions or comments. 6. Ask Questions: Don’t hesitate to ask questions if you need clarification on any topic. Live sessions are an excellent opportunity to get immediate feedback and guidance from the instructor. 7. Be Respectful and Courteous: Follow online etiquette by being respectful to the instructor and peers. Listen actively when others are speaking, and avoid interrupting. Use a respectful tone in both verbal and written communications. 8. Use the Mute Button Wisely: Mute your microphone when you’re not speaking to minimize background noise and enhance the session's audio quality for everyone. Be prepared. Be active. Be critical. Be respectful. And have fun! 😊

Most leaders today are often evaluated by their ability to speak effectively. If you listen to effective leaders, you'll notice one of their skills is public speaking. In this three-credit English course, students will develop skills to become more confident, effective public speakers and, therefore, leaders. Students will be able to utilize the power of storytelling to communicate effectively. We will demystify the process of writing, rehearsing, and delivering a meaningful and engaging speech. By the end of the course, students will be able to organize speeches clearly, write them effectively, and deliver them confidently. Course Objectives 1. Understand how leaders use different genres of speeches to communicate powerfully. 2. Write and deliver engaging speeches; speak confidently with appropriate visuals, body language, and voice. 3. docs.text: National Tsing Hua University Public Speaking and Presentation 演說與簡報 Tentative Syllabus, Fall 2026 Course Code Number: 11510LANG500011 Class hours: Friday 3:30 pm~6:20 pm (F7F8F9) Classroom: 綜二 204 Credits: 3 Instructor: 陳佳伶 Chia-ling Chen Email: chialing.c@mx.nthu.edu.tw Core competency indicators * The ability to communicate and express oneself in English (40%) * The ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English (20%) * Knowing English learning strategies and techniques (15%) * Having the global views of English and multicultural diversity (15%) * Ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit (10%) Course description This course aims to equip students with an essential skill set for delivering speeches and academic presentations through weekly training and assignments and monitor their learning progress. By exploring noted speeches, lectures, and an effective guide on presentation skills, students will be able to learn from various speakers' presenting styles and develop their own. The course is designed for those with an aim to deliver a presentation in a conference or speak in a professional occasion in the near future. During the term, an English-speaking toolkit will be acquired through weekly/daily exercises inside and outside the classroom. By the end of the term, the students shall be able to deliver their speech/presentation of a chosen topic with confidence, fluency, and accuracy. Course objectives The students will receive sufficient training on academic English and speaking skills, and be able to deliver a presentation/speech on a topic in their special field and demonstrate competency for this purpose. Students are also expected to strengthen and exhibit their critical thinking abilities in preparing materials for short talks, classroom activities, and a term project of delivering a 15 min speech/presentation. Teaching Methods Lectures and classroom activities, including speaking and listening practice, pair discussion, answering short questions, show-and-tell exercise, and presentations. Weekly assignment related to a chosen subject, in-class demonstration of ability to apply the skills taught in each session, topical demos, and a 15-minute final presentation will be the basis for evaluating students’ learning outcome. Course rules 1. Active participation. 2. Punctual delivery of weekly assignment. (No more than 2 late deliveries)* 3. Engaging in the use of online learning system and other digital resources. 4. Requests for leave of absence must be submitted prior to the class date. 5. Utilization of AI technology is encouraged. *Make-up assignment should be submitted within a week after the due date. Weekly sessions Week Date Main Topic Pages of Ref. 1 1 9/11 Course overview & introduction Chapter 1 Four Perspectives on Presentations pp.1-11 2 9/18 Chapter 2 Speech: The Words You Say pp.12-32 3 9/25 Targeting the Audience; Speaking from Points pp.32-47 4 10/2 Chapter 3 Structure: The Strategy You Choose pp.49-67 5 10/9 Holiday 6 10/16 Anticipating the Audience’s Initial Questions; Losing the Audience at Sea pp.69-103 7 10/23 Chapter 4 Visual Aids: Your Supporting Cast pp.105-128 8 10/30 Following the Defaults of PowerPoint pp.129-153 9 11/6 Guidelines for Typography, Color, and Layout pp.154-170 10 11/13 Mid-term Presentations 11 11/20 Following the Common Practices pp.171-201 12 11/27 Not Accounting Murphy’s Law -- Preparing Visual Aids pp.203-227 13 12/4 Chapter 5 Delivery: You, the Room, and the Audience pp.228-258 14 12/11 Chapter 6: Conclusion-- Composure and Handling Questions pp.259-275 15 12/18 Final Presentations 16 12/25 Holiday Assessment Students will be scored based on class participation and the assignment completed weekly, and the mid-term and final presentations. The points will be totaled as the final score composing the following items: • 10% Attendance • 10% Classroom activities and exercises • 15% Mid-term presentation • 35% Weekly assignment • 30% Term project: a 15 min presentation Regulations for Using AI: Permit using AI for research purposes and speaking & listening practice. docs.name: 基礎泰語一
docs.text: 1 國立清華大學課程教學大綱 課程簡介 Course Description 介紹泰國數字單位及筆劃練習，介紹數字單位運用，介紹泰文聲韻母及韻母。 能夠使用基礎會話與泰國人溝通。 自住旅遊專用語，問候語篇，你電話號碼幾號？，買東西篇，能給我一個折扣嗎？， 量詞，顏色，在路邊攤點菜及泰語文法。 課程目標與學習成效 Course Objectives & Learning Outcomes 1.能了解曼谷話，曼谷話是泰語的標準語。 วัตถุประสงค์ 2.在短期內能聽、說、讀、寫常用泰語、自我介紹、打招呼、問路、買東西。 3.在此學期，若按照教師的學法，保證到泰國觀光必能以泰語跟泰國人溝通，買東西不 受騙，不迷路。 4. 認識泰國的觀光勝地,泰國人的思想、文化、泰國人的基本禮貌（合掌,說話,送禮、 禁忌）。 5.將來能進修，而到泰國發展，例如：推廣中華文化、作生意、傳道、作研究、工作、 當中文教師、編中文課本等的重要基楚技能。 6.目前在泰國華語人才的需求量甚大，泰國正掀起了華文熱，很歡迎華文母語者到泰 國任教教中文，若懂泰文是將來的優勢。 7.為了提高學泰文的效率，教師建議錄音回家復習，有行線的筆記本。 8.泰國人個性溫和好客，從來不排華，沒有種族歧視，是個值得居住的地方，若懂泰 文就沒有溝通障礙。 9.學泰文不是件很難的事，只要有信心與恆心，不早放棄，保證會成功。 每週課程進度與作業要求 Course Schedule & Requirements 【請詳述：課程內容與指定閱讀／教學活動與課前、課後作業/學生學習投入時間（含 課堂教學時數）】 教材:新版大家來學泰語 400 元，泰文第㇐步 320 元與基礎泰文字(二)150 元(教科 書可以使用整個學年) docs.text: 1 國立清華大學課程教學大綱 課程簡介 Course Description 介紹泰國數字單位及筆劃練習，介紹數字單位運用，介紹泰文聲韻母及韻母。 能夠使用基礎會話與泰國人溝通。 自住旅遊專用語，問候語篇，你電話號碼幾號？，買東西篇，能給我一個折扣嗎？， 量詞，顏色，在路邊攤點菜及泰語文法。 課程目標與學習成效 Course Objectives & Learning Outcomes 1.能了解曼谷話，曼谷話是泰語的標準語。 วัตถุประสงค์ 2.在短期內能聽、說、讀、寫常用泰語、自我介紹、打招呼、問路、買東西。 3.在此學期，若按照教師的學法，保證到泰國觀光必能以泰語跟泰國人溝通，買東西不 受騙，不迷路。 4. 認識泰國的觀光勝地,泰國人的思想、文化、泰國人的基本禮貌（合掌,說話,送禮、 禁忌）。 5.將來能進修，而到泰國發展，例如：推廣中華文化、作生意、傳道、作研究、工作、 當中文教師、編中文課本等的重要基楚技能。 6.目前在泰國華語人才的需求量甚大，泰國正掀起了華文熱，很歡迎華文母語者到泰 國任教教中文，若懂泰文是將來的優勢。 7.為了提高學泰文的效率，教師建議錄音回家復習，有行線的筆記本。 8.泰國人個性溫和好客，從來不排華，沒有種族歧視，是個值得居住的地方，若懂泰 文就沒有溝通障礙。 9.學泰文不是件很難的事，只要有信心與恆心，不早放棄，保證會成功。 每週課程進度與作業要求 Course Schedule & Requirements 【請詳述：課程內容與指定閱讀／教學活動與課前、課後作業/學生學習投入時間（含 課堂教學時數）】 教材:新版大家來學泰語 400 元，泰文第㇐步 320 元與基礎泰文字(二)150 元(教科 書可以使用整個學年) (請各位同學在第㇐週要準備剛好的錢購買書 870 元) 2 週次 課程內容 1 泰語課程簡介，學習泰文的目標，介紹泰國文化， 第一節：介紹泰國數字單位及筆劃練習。（第 7-10 頁） 2 介紹泰文聲韻母：（ก- ฆ）6 個聲母及（สระอะ-สระอือ）8 個韻母， 第一節：介紹數字單位運用。（第 11-19 頁） 3 介紹泰文聲韻母：（ง- ฌ）6 個聲母及再（สระอุ – สระแอ）6 個韻母 第一課：問候語篇（生詞介紹）。（第 114-119 頁），(會話)。（第 120-121 頁） 4 介紹泰文聲韻母：（ญ- ฑ） 6 個聲母及（สระโอะ – สระเออ） 6 個韻母 第一課：句型練習：疑問句文法、修飾詞文法。（第 121-125 頁） 5 介紹泰文聲韻母：（ฒ- ท）6 個聲母及（สระเอียะ – สระอัว） 6 個韻母， 第二課：基礎會話：你電話號碼幾號？(生詞介紹) 。（第 127-129 頁），(會話) （第 130-131 頁）。 6 介紹泰文聲韻母：（ธ- ฝ） 6 個聲母及（สระอํา – สระฤๅ） 8 個韻母， 第二課：句型練習：疑問句文法、修飾詞文法。（第 132-134 頁） 7 介紹泰文聲韻母：（พ- ร） 6 個聲母及溫習全部的韻母， 第三課：買東西篇（生詞介紹）（第 135-136 docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 11510LE 140100 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 35 中文名稱 Course Title 基礎印尼語一 英文名稱 Course English Title Bahasa Indonesia Basic I 任課教師 Instructor 尤溫柔 (Juli Joe) 教師連絡方式： 手機：0932-299191 EMAIL：jou.joe@gmail.com Line：julijoe0117 課程 Line 群組： 上課時間 Time 週四 15:30 – 18:20 上課教室 Room 綜二 103 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) 1.本課程希望學生: a.除了能辨認字母的發音，還可以掌握印尼語在日常生活中所使用的詞彙與基本語法，並能以印尼 語進行簡單的交際。 b.透過學習印尼語的過程中學到了印尼文化風俗。 2.內容涵蓋： 打招呼，自我介紹，日常生活 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 印尼語初學，basic Indonesian，基礎，打招呼，自我介紹，生活用語 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程適合零基礎的印尼語初學者。通過朗讀課文（以會話形式）、扮演 角色、對話練習、簡單的口頭報告(對話內容)等教學手段培養學習著聽， 說，讀，寫的言語技能和運用印尼語進行社會交際的能力。 ● 指定用書(Text Books) 帶你學印尼語，零基礎也 OK！ https://reurl.cc/paAa8Z ● 參考書籍 (References) 我的第一本印尼語文法 ：用最科學的方法，聰明記住印 尼語文法！ ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 以交際為主要原則、精講多練、師生互動、講練結合的活動練習、 任務型教學。 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 會依照教學/考試需要而做調 整 週 進度 1 2026/9/10 印尼語的字母發音(A~Z) 複合子音，複合母音(p.8~18) 2 2026/9/17 打招呼(p.20~31) 第一課 3 2026/9/24 認識彼此(p.32~47) 第二課 4 2026/10/1 拜訪(p.48~63) 第三課 5 2026/10/8 這是什麼(p.64~77) 第四課 6 2026/10/15 最喜歡的(p.78~97) 第五課 7 2026/10/22 最喜歡的(p.98~111) 第六課 期中考前複習 8 2026/10/29 期中考(筆試) 9 2026/11/5 這個多少錢? docs.name: 中級泰語一
docs.text: 教學目標： 1.能更了解深入進階泰國話，並提升泰語的溝通能力。 2.認識泰國的觀光勝地,泰國人的思想、文化、泰國人的基本禮貌（合掌,說話,送禮、禁忌）。 跨文化與語言的角度廣大的視野 3.為了提升泰文的拼音能力、與閱讀能力，使學習者能拼出泰文詞彙。 4.在此學期能聽與說進階的飛機上用語、問方向與位置、訂房間、餐廳可以學到如何點餐、 認識泰國的菜單、旅遊同學可以學到觀光景點、購買東西與殺價、泰國同學交流上課用語等。 5.在此學期能讀與寫泰文中的字母、韻母的拼音法。 6.在此學期能了解中、高、低子音與長韻母和短韻母之拼音法。在文法方面，認識泰語未來式、 完成式，並能夠應用疑問句、肯定句，以及否定句在溝通語交談上。 ***第一週請務必出席,缺席者等於放棄本課程*** (準備購物 12 堂泰語實用會話原價 500 元 打 8 折 400 元)(教科書可以使用整個學年) 1 在飛機上可以學到搭飛機的用語(第一段)，例如:點餐，點飲料，選座位，劃位， 艙等的類別。 2 在飛機上可以學到搭飛機的用語(第二段) 3 問路可以學到方向(第一段)，例如:左轉，右轉，前面，後面。這樣同學去泰國 不會迷路錄。 4 問路可以學到方向(第二段) 5 飯店(第一段) 同學學到訂房間用語，認識房間的類型。 6 飯店(第二段) 同學學到訂房間用語，認識房間的類型。 7 期中考 8 在餐廳可以學到如何點餐(第一段)，特別注意不吃辣或不加辣椒。 9 在餐廳可以學到如何點餐(第二段) 。 10 同學可以學到如何跟老闆談價錢(第一段) ，商品的名稱，鈔票的種類。 11 同學可以學到如何跟老闆談價錢(第二段) ，商品的名稱，鈔票的種類。 12 旅遊同學可以學到觀光景點(第一段)，例如: 玉佛寺，臥佛寺，鄭王廟，等等。 13 旅遊同學可以學到觀光景點(第二段)，例如: 玉佛寺，臥佛寺，鄭王廟，等等。 14 期末考 15 線上上課聽歌學泰語跟欣賞廣告學泰語。 16 線上上課聽歌學泰語跟欣賞廣告學泰語。 17 線上上課聽歌學泰語跟欣賞廣告學泰語。 18 線上上課聽歌學泰語跟欣賞廣告學泰語。 評量工具與策略、評分標準成效 Evaluation Criteria 1. 每週作業 20 分（準時交作業） 2. 課堂表現 20 分（準時上課無故缺席、遲到、學習態度、聽從教授、為教師 或同學服務、幫助同學） 3. 每週小考 20 分（考試只是一種鼓勵同學進步，別擔憂） 4. 其中考試 20 分 5. 期末考 20 分 總共 100 分 實施方法： 1.按照課本的進度進行受課 2.利用投影片進行補助教學 3.利用作習本補助同學練習寫泰文字 4.利用泰文歌教學增加學泰文的樂趣 閱讀資料與參考書籍（หนังสืออ้างอิง）： 1. 《如何增進泰文字彙能力》文翔圖書公司。 2. 鄧欣然《泰語入門 อักษรภาษาไทยเบืÊองต้น》三思堂文化事業有限公司，台北縣新店市，台灣。 (02)89902588。 3. 李錫強《標準泰國語 ภาษาไทยมาตรฐาน》冠唐國際圖書股份有限公司 1998.(02)2298-1127。 4. 傅增有《泰語三百句 ภาษาไทย》三思堂文化事業有限公司。 5. ผศ.ดร.เรืองอุไรอินทรประเสริฐ,มโนรมย์พิพิธกุล《แบบหัดอ่านภาษาไทย๑ - docs.text: Fall, 2024 1 Syllabus: 11310LING500100 Phonology (I) Spatiotemporal: Lecture: T 9:10 a.m.~ 12:00 p.m., HSS Building, C519 Recitation: T.B.A. (one hour per week) Instructor: Feng-fan Hsieh siahonghoan@faculty.hss.nthu.edu.tw HSS Building, A430, x3-4633/PhonLab@C514, x3-4513 TA: T.B.A. Office hours: by appt. Class website: http://moodle.nthu.edu.tw (Email me for access to the course website if you are not a registered student) Required texts: Hayes, Bruce P. (2008) Introductory Phonology. Malden, MA: Blackwell. Kenstowicz, Michael J. (1994) Phonology in Generative Grammar. Malden, MA: Blackwell. Course description: This course is an introduction to the description and analysis of sound patterns that are found in the world’s languages. It is designed to provide you with: a. An overview of the basic phenomena that the field of phonology concerns itself with: the types of patterns that are found in human languages; ways languages may differ from one another; how speakers represent sound patterns mentally b. Analytical tools (under the framework of rule-based phonology) to describe the sound patterns that are found in a language c. Practice developing linguistic analysis: describing the data, presenting the analysis, developing the argument of one analysis over another. Course requirements: a. Assigned readings b. Class participation and class attendance (10%) c. Problem sets (40%) d. Final exam (50%) Written assignments: There will be five (5) homework assignments, generally handed out on Tuesdays and due on the following Tuesday. Late homework will not be accepted except for compelling reasons (e.g. in documented cases of emergency) and with prior permission of the instructor. Submission via email won’t be accepted, either. Fall, 2024 2 Collaboration policy: You are strongly encouraged to work together, and to discuss readings and your solutions to the written assignments with each other. You must write up your assignments individually, however. If you are having problems with any assignments, please do not hesitate to get in touch with the instructor or TA – in person or by email. We are more than happy to help. Ethical guidelines for the use of Generative AI: Not applicable Schedule of topics (subject to revision) • Readings and assignments (*) are due the day they are listed. MK 9.6~9.8 Week 13 Nov 26 Underspecification & Constraints MK 9.9, 9.11~9.15 Week 14 Dec 3 Prosodic Morphology McCarthy and Prince (1995) Week 15 Dec 10* Productivity, Diachrony and Synchrony, and abstractness BH chaps. 9, 11, 12 Week 16 Dec 17 Final exam

docs.name: 句法學一
docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number LING5003 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 中文名稱 Course Title 句法學一 英文名稱 Course English Title Syntax I 任課教師 Instructor 蔡維天 上課時間 Time W6W7W8 上課教室 Room 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 本課程的主旨在於介紹句法學的基礎原則與研究方法，同時也逐步引介當代句法理論的重要 發現和中心議題。我們從語句的解析著手，讓同學們熟悉科學研究的理念與方法；並從比較 句法(comparative syntax)的角度來探討語言之間的類同與歧異，進而引領同學一窺語法做為 人類本能的性質與結構。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 句法學，語法理論，比較句法，普遍語法，語言類型學 Syntax, Grammatical Theory, Comparative Syntax, Universal Grammar, Linguistic Typology 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程的主旨在於介紹句法學的基礎原則與研究方法，同時也逐步引介當代句法理論的重要 發現和中心議題。 ● 指定用書(Text Books) Roberts, Ian. 2023. Beginning Syntax. Cambridge University Press. Haegeman, Liliane. 1994. Introduction to Government and Binding Theory, 2nd edition, Blackwell, Cambridge, US. ● 參考書籍(References) Haegeman, Liliane. 2006. Thinking Syntactically: A Guide to Argumentation and Analysis. Oxford: Blackwell. Soames, Scott and David Perlmutter. 1979. Syntactic Argumentation and the Structure of English. University of California Press. ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 我們從語句的解析著手，讓同學們熟悉科學研究的理念與方法；並從比較句法(comparative syntax)的角度來探討語言之間的類同與歧異，進而引領同學一窺語法做為人類本能的性質 與結構。 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 第 1~2 週 The Biological Basis of Language: Universal Grammar 第 3~4 週 Syntactic Analysis & Methodology 第 5~6 週 Argument Structure 第 7~8 週 X-Bar Theory, C-selection & S-selection 第 9~10 週 Transformation & Movement 第 11~12 週 Syntactic Islands & Locality Principles 第 13~14 週 Binding Theory & C-command 第 15~16 週 Raising Structure & Control Structure ● 成績考核(Evaluation) 一﹑作業 (50%) 二﹑期末考 (50%) ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 本課程無涉及 AI 使用 Not applicable

docs.name: 腦神經語言學
docs.text: Neurolinguistics Instructor: Yi-ching Josephine Su (蘇宜青) Course Description The goal of this course is to provide students with a state-of-the-art survey of the neuroscience of language, a multidisciplinary field that has seen significant advances in the past few decades. Lectures and discussion will cover the central aspects of language processing in the brain such as auditory perception, lexical access and syntax/semantic processing from a range of studies of neurological and developmental language disorders, as well as functional neuroimaging. Textbooks Brennan, Jonathan R. (2022) Language and the Brain: A Slim Guide to Neurolinguistics. Oxford University Press. Selected readings from the two books below and other journals or books will be provided in class. 1. De Zubicaray, Greig I., & Schiller, Niels O. (2019) The Oxford Handbook of Neurolinguistics. docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 學分 Credit 人數限制 Class Size 中文名稱 Course Title 台灣南島語言語態與動詞的句法和語意研究 英文名稱 Course English Title Syntax and Semantics of Voice and Verbs in Formosan Languages 任課教師 Instructor 張永利 上課時間 Time 星期五 (3-n) Fri(10:10-13:00) 上課教室 Room 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) This course offers a systematic examination of voice morphology and verbal semantics in Formosan languages, a typologically significant subgroup of Austronesian. Building on contemporary work in formal syntax and semantics, we will investigate how the Formosan voice system interacts with argument structure, case licensing, verb classification, and event structure. Central topics include the alignment properties of Formosan voice (accusative vs. ergative patterns), the status of voice as a locus of case/wh/topic agreement or transitivity, the nature of LV/IV and the inventory of voice distinctions, and the role of voice in structuring stative, interrogative, and perception predicates. We will also explore how voice-sensitive restructuring and degrees of event integration inform the syntax– semantics interface in these languages. The course combines instructor-led lectures with student-led seminar discussions. Assessment is based on regular attendance, preparation and participation, an in- class presentation, and a final term project. 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) Austronesian Voice, Verb Classification, Formosan Languages, Morphosyntax, Grammaticalization, Ergativity, Event Structure 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) This course addresses core theoretical questions about voice and verb semantics in Formosan languages. It focuses on how voice interacts with alignment, argument structure, case, and event structure, framed within contemporary formal syntax and semantics. The course is organized around the following guiding questions: (1) Is Formosan voice best analyzed as accusative or ergative (Aldridge 2013; Chen 2025)? (2) Does Formosan voice encode case/wh/topic agreement, or is it primarily a reflex of transitivity (Chen 2025; Aldridge 2026)? (3) Does the system instantiate a four-way or a two-way opposition in syntax, and what do the labels Locative Voice (LV) and Instrumental Voice (IV) actually capture (J. Wu 2007; Chang 2015)? (4) In what ways does voice morphology shape verb classification (I. Wu 2006; Chang & Svensson 2026)? (5) How do the cardinality and scalarity properties of stative verbs constrain their syntactic behavior (Chang 2023, 2024)? (6) What is the categorial status of Formosan interrogative verbs—auxiliary, light, or fully lexical? (7) How does the grammaticalization of perception verbs determine their structural position (Chang & Yeh 2026)? (8) What factors govern degrees of event integration and restructuring, and what role does Formosan voice play in restructuring configurations (I. Wu 2013; Chang 2025)? ● 指定用書(Text Books) Please refer to References ● 參考書籍(References) Aldridge, Edith. 2021. docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 待定 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 無限制 中文名稱 Course Title 語言中的情感表達 英文名稱 Course English Title Expressivity in Linguistic Expression 任課教師 Instructor 連金發 上課時間 Time 周一: 2.20-5.20 上課教室 Room C519 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) 十九世紀末、二十世紀初葉，德國哲學家佛雷格(Frege 1918)除了意義和指稱之區分之外， 還對德語的助詞(如 doc, aber)的語意提出洞見，即助詞所表現的語意不會影響句子的真假值。 這預示了二十世紀下半葉 Grice (1975) 的定規含意說(conventional implicature)。Potts (2005)將 定規含意這樣的理念加以擴充，專注直示(at issue)意外暗示意的研究，暗示意存在於情緒用語 (如 that jerk 那個怪胎)，包含輕蔑語(slur)及詈詞(epithets)等。 定規含意不同於會話含意(conversational implicature)，前者的含意不可以取消 (not defeasible)，而後者可以。Potts (2005)將定規含意這樣的理念加以擴充，專注語詞直示意之上 的額外含意的研究。傳統上語意學的論述，以真值條件(truth condition)為依據來解析語意，但 還需要考慮定規語意之存否。若以真值條件和定規性的正負值來劃分，可得四類的語意詮釋: (1) 描述意、(2)使用條件意 (use-conditional meaning) (簡稱暗示意)、(3) 語用增強、(4) 會話含 意。比如，dog(狗)屬描述意，但 cur(雜種狗)帶負面的暗示意，即涉真值但定規，和 dog 都有相 同真值，然而 damn(該死)只表負面意，沒有真值。詈語或輕蔑語不具真值條件，但具定規性， 可以表達使用條件語意(暗示意)，與真假值無關。 本課程以上述理論為基礎，探討情感表現與語言體系各部門的互動關係, 並探索各種情感 表現所引發的理論議題。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 情感詞，直示意，暗示意，定規含意，語言行為，輕蔑語，呼喚語 expressives, at-issue meaning, use-conditional meaning, conventional Implicature, speech act, slur, vocatives 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) 依下列單元進行教學: 1. 理論背景 2. 情感表現和詞彙 3. 情感表現和詞法 4. 情感表現和句法 5. 情感表現和多重語意 6. 情感表現和語言變遷 7. 情感表現和語言行為 8. 情感表現和輕蔑語 9. 情感表現和客套語 10. 情感表現和呼喚語 ● 指定用書(Text Books) 無指定用書 以參考論文代之 ● 參考書籍(References) Brown, Roger & Albert Gilman. 1960. Syllabus Week Date Teacher Topic Content 1 9/9 張慧雲 陳韋靜 實驗安全與設備介紹 顯微鏡介紹 (a) 課程說明 (b) 維護實驗環境整潔 (c) 實驗室安全規則講解與儀器設備介紹 (d) 顯微鏡原理與操作 2 9/16 陳韋靜 顯微操作技術(一) 魚類解剖觀察、耳石取樣及標本包埋 3 9/23 陳韋靜 顯微操作技術(二) 研磨、顯微鏡觀察及照相 4 (c)清點使用器具與整理實驗環境 評分方式： 項目 比例 評分標準 平時表現 25% (a) 出席狀況 (b) 實驗儀容：實驗衣及服裝穿著(ex 包鞋) (c) 實驗過程表現與實驗態度 (d) 實驗器材完善度：打破或毀損將酌量扣分 實驗報告 42% 12 份預報 + 6 份報告 期末考 33% (a) 筆試：70% (b) 操作考：30% 實驗記錄與報告（Laboratory report and note) 學習和養成書寫實驗報告是這門生物實驗課重要的一環，實驗報告可依個人實驗需要稍加增減 和修改。每一新單元開始前請同學繳交上一單元實驗成果報告給助教審查，希望這門實驗課能提供良好 的機會，可以啟發同學們在實驗研究上的興趣並重視研究精神。本學期需繳 6 份完整報告，實驗成果記 錄報告注重原創性和應用性，資料分析和實驗報告撰寫，均為必須。實驗報告撰寫規格如下 : I. 實驗名稱（heading) : 包括組別和姓名。 II. 目的（purpose) : 簡短清晰的寫 1-5 個句子。描述實驗目的，探討有趣和重要的生物問題。 III. 方法 （method) : 讓同學有多方了解實驗儀器的機會，培養實際操作之能力，並鼓勵創造新方法。 IV. 結果和討論 （results and discussion) : (a). 有系統的呈現實驗當中所觀察到的現象和記錄下來的 data。 (b). 實驗後所做的計算和圖表。圖表要排序並標示計量單位，如此 ，在寫結果和討論時，才容 易引用 (The information found in Figure 1….) 。 (c). 對 data 的分析和比較及從中所做的推論 (interpretation and unknown identification) 。 (d). 整個實驗的結論。 如果結果未達成目標或不如預期，也請說明可能的原因，及重做時可改進之處。 問題回答（Answers and Questions) : 講義上的問題和老師與助教詢問的問題回答。 實驗規則補充： 1. 上課務必注意時間，請勿喧鬧。 2. 實驗課服裝： 實驗衣、長褲、包腳的鞋子，長髮者必須將頭髮紮起。 3. 預報一單元每人一份，於每次上課時將紙本帶給助教檢查， 參考實驗講義內容整理，亦可另外加自己查到的參考資料，務必註明參考書目。 4. 結報一單元一組一份： a. 繳交日期：該單元結束後、下一次上課日課程開始前統一繳交給助教。 遲交一天扣報告成績 5 分，遲交時間未滿一天者，以一天計。 b. 繳交形式：紙本(列印或手寫均可)，同一組結報裝訂一起繳交。 c. 結報內容：封面— 實驗單元、班別、組別、成員名單與學號、註明分工 實驗目的 實驗方法與流程 實驗結果與分析 結果討論 參考資料及問題回答 （其他可參考科學論文寫作相關書籍） 如有任何疑問，請聯絡助教。

docs.name: 書報討論
docs.text: 1 Seminar (書報討論) Instructor: Chun-Chao Wang (王群超) Email: ccwang@life.nthu.edu.tw Phone: +886-3-516-2589 (office) http://chunchaowang.wix.com/wanglab Office Location: Life Science Building I, Room 527 Office Hours: By appointment Course Description: The Seminar allows students a chance to meet every week to discuss journal articles. The primary goals of this course are to help students keep up with the scientific literature, and help students argue logically, and present newest research in a way that others can follow. We hope everyone takes advantage of this opportunity, as it is a great way to practice speaking in front of a group, critically analyze papers, and be aware of the state-of-the-art advances in the fields of quantitative cell biology and cancer biology. Course Requirements and Expectations: • Each student must select a paper that they consider to be either important or controversial from a pre-approved list of articles. They should make a case for why it is significant, controversial, etc. and what they find interesting. • Students are required to read all papers. If you read the paper(s) before each class, discussions will be more meaningful, and learning will increase. Expect to spend a minimum of 90–120 minutes reading per paper. • Students are expected to construct a lightning talk (3 minutes) and an oral presentation (30 minutes). • When in the audience, you are expected to 1) submit 1 question, 2) present one slide made by the speaker after the oral presentation, in your own word (“Audience presentation”), and 3) ask questions (optional). • You are expected to host a presentation. • Be respectful and professional: remember that your responses are public, so always maintain a respectful and professional tone, even when handling criticism or negative feedback. As a presenter: • Rehearse your presentation out loud several times, if possible, in front of friends or family members, or in front of the mirror. Use your mobile device to record rehearsal. Ask your audience for feedback after you finish your rehearsal. • You will record a lightning talk and upload your YouTube file. • Responding to YouTube comments. Submit a screenshot or PDF of your YouTube comment and its response in eeclass. Keep a record of who submits their comments/questions late. 2 • You are welcome to discuss your oral presentation with me. Please email me to make an appointment at least 10 days in advance of your oral presentation. • Slides should be submitted 3 days before the oral presentation. • Mark slides that you would like to have presented by the audience. • The oral presentation order will be decided at the first class. • Example Lightning Talks https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLd8bBKy1dyo2Z52CGlZl58gt6q4p7QD X-&si=0E8Jf8HYHY8zVGq3 As an audience: • Every student is required to submit a written comment on YouTube, including at least one question about each paper, no later than 24 hours before the oral presentation day. Submit a screenshot or PDF of your YouTube comment in eeclass. • Presenters do not have to submit questions about the paper they present. • Present one slide made by the speaker in your own word. • Ask questions in class (optional). As a host: • Introduce the speaker. • Run the "Audience Presentation" using the random name picker: https://tw.piliapp.com/random/wheel/ • Run Q&A session. Grading: • Presentation (total 60%): Lightning talk (10%) Oral presentation (40%) Responding to YouTube comments (10%). • Participation (total 45%): Submit questions (15%) “Audience presentation” (15%) host a presentation (10%) ask questions in class (5%)

docs.text: 當代認知神經科學：腦與心智 Contemporary Cognitive Neuroscience: Brain and Mind (通識課程, LS114300, Fall 2026) 加簽者請務必出席第一堂課（9/9，實體或線上都可）以填 寫加簽表單及參與課堂小考。 加簽表單填寫時間僅開放 9/9 第一節課程開始後一小時 (15:30~16:30)。 未達上述條件者不予加簽。 第一堂課直播網址 https://www.youtube.com/live/0Hb5laOEUVs 課程規定: 請另詳閱「2026 課程規定」之投影片（清華數位學習 平台 eeclass）。 Instructor: 焦傳金 Contact info: 生科二館 646, 03-574-2464, ccchiao@life.nthu.edu.tw Classroom: 生科二館華生廳 (Watson Hall)＋YouTube 同步直播 Class time: W7W8W9 (15:30-18:20 pm) Course materials : 清華數位學習平台 eeclass（https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw/） 即時互動系統 slido（https://www.slido.com/index-b?experience_id=2） 課程信箱: brain7mind@gmail.com Course TAs: 黃品睿 ray614h@gmail.com Reference: Cognitive Neuroscience: The Biology of the Mind (Sixth Edition), Michael Gazzaniga, Elizabeth A. Phelps, Dani S. Bassett, George R. Mangun, Richard B. Ivry (2025) Course description: 認知神經科學（Cognitive Neuroscience）是一門新興 的研究領域，主要是探索腦與心智（Brain and Mind）的關連性。從感覺與知 覺（Sensation and Perception）、學習與記憶（Learning and Memory）、注 意力與情緒（Attention and Emotion）、同理與厭惡（Empathy and Disguise）、決策與執行（Decision-making and Execution）、乃至意識 （Consciousness）的產生，都是認知神經科學的範疇。瞭解這些認知行為背 後的神經科學不僅是本世紀最重要的一項科學探索，也與每個人的有密切的關 係。例如：神經經濟學（Neuroeconomics）與消費者行為及市場調查有關， 退化性神經疾病（Neurodegenerative disorders）與老年失智症有關。在本 課程中，我們將依序探討認知神經科學中的主要課題，重點在於介紹最新的研 究發展，並討論這些科學發現對個人及社會的衝擊。本課程將以腦與心智相關 的科普書籍與科學人雜誌過去所發表有關認知神經科學的文章為主，並以影片 及近期發表的期刊論文為輔，搭配課程中互動討論，讓沒有生物學背景的學生 也可輕鬆地學習本課程。 Course schedule: Week Topic Note 1 腦與心智簡介 簡介各週內容，暴力行為在腦中的運作模式 第一週上課使用直播方式，不需前往教室 (加簽規定如上) 2 感覺&知覺 I 視覺的錯視、視覺訊息的處理 3 感覺&知覺 II 奧妙的色彩如何影響大腦認知 4 感覺&知覺 III 原來我們聽到的可能不一樣、基因影響嗅覺辨識! 5 學習&記憶 感官、短期、長期，原來有不同的記憶形式 6 睡眠&夢 我可以都不睡覺嗎? 我為何需要睡覺? 7 報償&成癮 為何毒品這麼難戒除，成癮對腦造成的傷害 8 理性&感性 動物也會難過，不同情緒由不同腦區控制 9 選擇&決策 如何做出選擇，究竟你在選什麼? 10 全校運動會 11 同理心 網路和面對面的霸凌有何不同，你懂我的痛嗎? 12 智力&創造力 天才從何而來? 創意如何產生? 13 發育&可塑性 嬰兒天生會做哪些事?學前教育可以如何進行 14 老化&疾病 如何優雅的老化，能阻止大腦變老嗎? 15 腦科學&科技&社會 男、女頭腦大不同? 16 意識&自由意志 植物人有意識嗎? 繳交期末報告 #本課程同時採用實體上課與同步遠距教學（同學可自由選擇學習方式） Grading policy: 課堂參與：40% (每堂課結束後需將課程心得與自我經驗分享上傳至社群軟體 fb、ig) 課堂小考：30% (每個段落皆有課堂小考，以 slido 進行) 期末報告：30% (個人書面報告或團體影片報告擇一) 課堂參與（加分）：0-5% 課程要求： 1. 攜帶行動載具（手機、平版、筆電）來上課，並確定自己在良好的網路空間 中上課 2. 下載 slido 3. 擁有任一社群軟體 加簽規定： 1. 欲加簽者請參與第一堂線上直播課程，並於課程中填寫加簽表單，表單關閉 後不再開放加簽 2. 直播連結: https://www.youtube.com/live/wOssI06rW-g 學生使用 AI 規則： 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出

docs.name: 計算神經科學導論
docs.text: 國立清華大學 115 學年第 1 學期新開課程課程大綱 科號 Course Number 11510LS 314500 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Class Size 20 中文名稱 Course Title 計算神經科學導論 英文名稱 Course English Title Introduction to Computational Neuroscience 任課教師 Instructor 羅中泉 上課時間 Time T7T8 上課教室 Room 生二 220 一、課程說明 本課程以“理解大腦與神經系統的計算原理”以及“實際動 手操作神經網計算模型”為兩大主軸。希望在目前腦科學與 人工智慧最熱門的時代，提供學生一個跨領域學習的機會。 本課程將概略性介紹計算神經的理論，尺度從認神經網路到 神經細胞乃至於相關的腦功能與認知行為。以實用性角度出 發，讓學生理解日常生活的認知行為背後牽涉到的複雜大腦 計算問題。本課程盡量減少深奧的數學公式，每一個主題皆 佐以神經網路模擬軟體教學以讓學生實際動手與體驗。 本課適合理工與生命科學等科系大三大四同學修讀，並特別 設計給有下列需求的學生： 1. 正在學習認知與心理學，希望能進一步理解相關大腦神 經網路理論，或 2. 正在修讀神經科學與生命科學，希望能學習大腦系統性 的行為及其理論，或 3. 對機器學習與人工智慧有涉略，但希望能更理解相關生 物基礎與理論。 二、指定用書 以授課老師的公開線上課程網站為主要授課內容 https://sites.google.com/view/brain-and- computation/home 三、參考書籍 1. Computational Cognitive Neuroscience. by Michael Frank, Yuko Munakata, Thomas Hazy, Randall O'Reilly. http://a.co/bkNI2Mf (Amazon Kindle edition) https://grey.colorado.edu/CompCogNeuro/index.php/CCNBook /Main (Free online edition) 2. Peter Dayan & L. F. Abbott. Theoretical Neuroscience: Computational and Mathematical Modeling of Neural Systems. The MIT Press (2005) 四、教學方式 本課程以部分線上課程搭配實體課堂講解與電腦上機實作。 本課程分成四個主題，每一主題有2-4個單元。上課的部分 強調與學生的討論與互動，實機操作部分鼓勵學生發揮創 意。實機操作僅需操作軟體，不需要撰寫程式，但若有 Python程式語言的基本能力可增進學習效果。 五、教學進度 教學大綱 L3-1. Networks 1. Network structures 2. Feedforward networks and perceptron * 3. Recurrent network and working memory * 4. Recurrent network and navigation* L3-2. Connections 1. Synapse models: firing rate based & spike based 2. Synapse physiology L3-3. Neurons 1. Leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) model 2. Synaptic inputs in LIF model * 3. The Hodgkin-Huxley model 4. Other neuron models L3-4. Learning and memory 1. Hebbian learning & spike-timing dependent plasticity (STDP)* 2. Conditioning* 3. Reinforcement learning* *為附有電腦實作之單元 教學進度 9/8 Lecture L3-1-1, L3-1-2 9/15 Hands-on L3-1-2-h1, L3-1-2-h2 9/22 (Online) Lecture L3-1-3 9/29 hands-on L3-1-3-h1, L3-1-3-h2 10/6 (Online) Lecture L3-1-4 10/13 Hands-on L3-1-4-h1 10/20 Mid-term exam 10/27 (Online) Lecture L3-2-1, L3-2-2 11/3 (Online) Lecture L3-3-1, L3-3-2 11/10 Hands-on L3-3-1-h1 L3-3-1-h2 11/17 (Online) Lecture L3-3-3, L3-3-4 11/24 (Online) Lecture L3-4-1, 12/1 Hands-on L3-4-1-h1, L3-4-1-h2 12/8 (Online) Lecture L3-4-2, L3-4-3 12/15 Hands-on L3-4-2-h1, L3-4-3-h1 12/22 Final exam 標示 (Online) 者為線上課程，學生須自行觀看指定影片並作線 上測驗。無實體課程。若對於影片內容有疑問，可於課程網站之 留言區詢問、跟老師約時間討論、或於下次實體上課時討論。 六、成績考核 1. 每單元線上評量 13 次 x 3% = 39% 2. 課堂互動、討論與電腦實作 6 次 x 4% = 24% 3. 期中考 17% 4. 期末考 20% 七、可連結之網頁 位址(相關網頁) 本課程使用學校的 eeclass 平台為課程網站 另外可參考授課老師的線上課程網站 https://sites.google.com/view/brain-and- computation/home 八、AI 使用規則 學生在撰寫程式、報告與課堂測驗時可使用生成式 AI 或相 關工具。期中考與期末考不得使用任何 AI 工具。

docs.text: 1 Molecular and Cellular Biology II, LS340100 Fall, 2026 Lecture: Tuesdays 13:20-14:10, Fridays 13:20-15:10, Life Science Building II, Rm109 Instructors: Dr. Jui-Chou Hsu (徐瑞洲), jchsu@life.nthu.edu.tw LS-I 523, ext. 42768 Dr. Mou-Chieh Kao (高茂傑), mckao@life.nthu.edu.tw LS-I 307, ext. 42472 Dr. Chung-Yu Lan (藍忠昱), cylan@life.nthu.edu.tw LS-I 405, ext. 42473 Teaching assistant: 稍後宣布 Course Description: The first one-third of the course will discuss protein targeting and sorting, signal transduction, growth control, and cancer. The rest of the time will be devoted to various aspects of transcription in prokaryotes and eukaryotes. Many experimental results are presented to illustrate the control and regulation of these topics.  Students are urged to read the basic methodology section in chapters 1-5 of the molecular biology textbook before attending the molecular biology portion of the class. Text Books: The world of cell, 7th ed., Becker, Benjamin Cummings Molecular Biology, 5th ed., Robert F. Weaver. McGraw Hill（偉明圖書代理） References: The cell, 4th ed., Albert, 2002 Molecular Biology of the Gene, 5th ed., Watson et al., Pearson Benjamin Cummings Teaching Methods: The lectures will be aided by PowerPoint slides and closely follow the textbook. Students are encouraged to ask questions and discuss the areas they have difficulties with the lecturers. Syllabus:  In the cell biology part, lectures will cover chapters 14, 18, 19, 22, and 24 of the book “The world of cell, 7th ed.”.  In the molecular biology part, lectures will cover chapters 6 to 12 in the book “Molecular Biology, 5th ed.”. Please refer to the following syllabus for a detailed schedule. 2 Week date Topics (chapter) Instructor 1 9/08 9/11 Protein targeting and sorting (18,22) Hsu 2 9/15 9/18 Protein targeting and sorting (18,22) Hsu 3 9/22 9/25 Signaling transduction mechanism: II (14) 中秋節(停課一天) Hsu 4 9/29 10/02 Signaling transduction mechanism: II (14) Regulation of the cell cycle and cancer (19,24) Hsu 5 10/06 10/09 Regulation of the cell cycle and cancer (19,24) 國慶日補假 Hsu 6 10/13 10/16 Regulation of the cell cycle and cancer (19,24) Examination I (lecture 9/08 ~10/13) Hsu 7 10/20 10/23 The mechanism of transcription in bacteria (6) Kao 8 10/27 10/30 The mechanism of transcription in bacteria (6) Kao 9 11/03 11/06 Operons: fine control of bacterial transcription (7) Kao 10 11/10 11/13 Operons: fine control of bacterial transcription (7) Major shifts in bacterial transcription (8) Kao 11 11/17 11/20 Eukaryotic RNA polymerases and their promoters (10) Examination II (lecture 10/20 ~11/13) Lan Kao 12 11/24 11/27 Eukaryotic RNA polymerases and their promoters (10) Lan 13 12/01 12/04 General transcription factors in eukaryotes (11) Lan 14 12/08 12/11 General transcription factors in eukaryotes (11) Transcription activators in eukaryotes (12) Lan 15 12/15 12/18 Transcription activators in eukaryotes (12) Final examination (lecture 11/17 ~12/15) Lan 16 12/22 12/25 考試週(停課一天) 行憲紀念日(停課一天)  本課程無涉及 AI 使用

docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 11510LS 390104 學分 Credit 1 人數限制 Class Size 11 中文名稱 Course Title 書報討論 英文名稱 Course English Title Seminar 任課教師 Instructor 李政昇 上課時間 Time R2 上課教室 Room 生二 107 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) 本課程旨在培養學生研讀高影響力科學期刊的習慣與學術素養。透過深入拆解論文邏輯與數據 詮釋，學生將掌握生命科學前沿趨勢，並接受完整的學術溝通訓練，包括：製作專業投影片、 進行簡潔扼要的口頭報告，以及磨練答辯與提問技巧。期能藉此引導學生發掘研究興趣，為未 來的學術或職涯發展奠定紮實基礎。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) Seminar、Journal Article、Literature Reading、Oral Presentation、Discussion 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) The goal of this course is to develop students' academic literacy and their ability to engage with high- impact scientific literature. By breaking down the logic of scientific papers and interpreting complex data, students will stay abreast of cutting-edge trends in life sciences. Students will also undergo rigorous training in academic communication—specifically in designing professional slides, delivering concise presentations, and navigating Q&A sessions. This course serves as a stepping stone for students to discover their research passions and establish a solid groundwork for their future careers. ● 指定用書(Text Books): N/A ● 參考書籍(References): 兩年內（2024 以後）發表的生物科學期刊（推薦 Cell, Nature, Science, Nature Communications, PNAS, Nucleic Acids Research, EMBO Journal, Science Advances, Cell Reports 等）的文章，建議 （但不局限於）DNA repair、chromatin dynamics 的相關主題。 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 每周由一位學生進行口頭報告，針對不同的文獻做報告與討論。 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 前兩週為課程規範介紹與報告順序安排、教師講解報告要點並示範。同學需於第二週上課前提 供兩篇欲報告之論文的 DOI 上傳至 eeclass 作業區，由老師擇一。之後每週一位同學報告。 報告當週的星期二中午以前須將投影片上傳至 eeclass 作業區。報告時間 30-35 分鐘，提問與討 論 10 分鐘，老師講解 5 分鐘。每次課堂結束後，聽眾每人須繳交互評分數及建議。 報告完後兩週內，根據獲得的反饋，重新錄製，繳交檔案。 若期末有多餘時間將進行三分鐘演講活動。 ● 成績考核(Evaluation) 報告整體表現（80%）：老師評分（針對課堂上的報告表現以及之後的重新錄製）60%、準時 完成論文選定、投影片上傳、重製影片上傳 5%、同學互評成績 15%。 聽眾於課堂發問、參與討論、提供互評分數及建議（20%）。 Bonus：三分鐘演講（若有時間進行的話，5%）。 出席為必要條件，無故缺席一次扣 10 分。請假須依正常程序辦理，若超過兩次，須完成額外指 定作業，否則超過兩次後每次扣 5 分。遲到將累計總時數，每 5 分鐘扣 1 分。 當週報告同學因私人因素無法報告者，扣總成績 20 分。 ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output 基於透明與負責任的原則，本課程鼓勵學生利用 AI 進行協作或互學，以提升本門課產出品 質。根據本校公布之佈的「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採取 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於作業或報告，說明如下: • 學生可於課堂作業或報告中的「標題頁註腳」或「引用文獻後」簡要說明如何使用生成 式 AI 進行議題發想、文句潤飾或結構參考等使用方式。然而，在本課程的「個人反思 報告」、「小組採訪作業」中，學生不得使用生成式 AI 工具撰寫作業。若經查核使用 卻無在作業或報告中標明，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或 不予計分。 • 本門課授課教材或學習資料若有引用自生成式 AI，教師也將在投影片或口頭標注。 • 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。 ● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website) https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw/

docs.name: 生物多樣性概論
docs.text: 國立清華大學 課程大綱 📌 課程基本資訊 • 科號： 11510LS 414600 • 科目名稱： 生物多樣性概論 (Introduction of Biodiversity) • 學分： 3 學分 • 人數限制： 120 人 • 上課時間： 每週三 W7、W8、W9 • 教室： 生科二館 秉乾講堂 • 授課教師： 黃貞祥老師、郭立園老師（共同主持） 🎯 課程核心能力培養 (Core Capabilities) 本課程設計緊密結合系所核心能力指標，各佔 20% 權重： 1. 主動學習與團隊合作： 培養高度的學習意願、彈性適應力與良好的團隊協 作精神。 2. 職場綜合軟實力： 鍛鍊穩重抗壓的工作態度，並提升口語表達與人際溝通 能力。 3. 科學邏輯與通識素養： 奠定紮實的理學邏輯訓練，兼蓄人文社會與科技管 理之跨領域視野。 4. 社會關懷與實踐力： 引導學生善用學術理論，將知識轉化為關懷環境與承 擔社會責任的行動。 5. 生科專業與跨界挑戰： 扎根生命科學專業知識，建立勇於接受跨領域挑戰 的創新精神。 📝 一、課程說明 (Course Description) 本課程旨在帶領學生系統性地探索地球上豐富的生物多樣性。課程不僅講述不同物 種、基因與生態系的特性，更著重於觀念的啟發。我們將引導以現代生命科學為核 心的同學們，在各自的專業領域中，學習運用生物多樣性的經驗思維與邏輯，並結 合現代生物學的前沿技術。 透過本課程，期許學生能打破單一學科的框架，為未來的科學研究催生出更大的突 破，並對全球生態脈絡擁有更宏觀的理解與實務應用能力。 📚 二、指定用書 (Required textbooks) 1. E. O. Wilson (1992). The Diversity of Life. Harvard Univ. Press.（中譯本：《繽 紛的生命》，金恆鑣譯，天下文化） 2. E. O. Wilson (2016). Half Earth: Our Planet’s Fight for Life. Liveright Publishing Corporation.（中譯本：《半個地球：探尋生物多樣性及其保存之 道》，金恒鑣、王益真譯，商周出版） 3. 行政院農委會林務局 出版。《上課了，生物多樣性》(I、II、III、IV)。 📖 三、參考書籍 (Reference Books) 課程內容涵蓋臺灣本土與全球生態，建議延伸閱讀以下分類書籍： • 動物與昆蟲領域： o 《台灣哺乳動物》(2008) 祈偉廉／天下文化 o 《台灣鳥類誌》(2012) 劉小如等／農委會林務局 o 《台灣蛙類與蝌蚪圖鑑》(2019) 楊懿如／貓頭鷹出版社 o 《蛇類大驚奇》(2013) 杜銘章／遠流文化 o 《昆蟲觀察入門》(2022) 張永仁／遠流文化 o 《台灣蝴蝶圖鑑》(2021) 李俊延、王效岳／貓頭鷹出版社 • 植物與真菌領域： o 《台灣民族植物圖鑑》(2012) 鍾明哲、楊智凱／晨星出版社 o 《台灣水生植物圖鑑》(2007) 李松柏／晨星出版社 o 《真菌微宇宙：看生態煉金師如何驅動世界》(2021) Merlin Sheldrake ／果力文化 • 海洋與生態保育： o 《臺灣百種海洋動物 II：無脊椎動物》(2021) 陳國勤等／海委會海 保署 o 《黑潮洶湧：關於人、海洋、鯨豚的故事》(2016) 張卉君／網路與 書出版社 o 《菜市場魚圖鑑》(2006) 賴春福、吳佳瑞／天下文化 o 👥 四、教學方式 (Teaching Methods) 本課程採「專家特邀演講為主，任課教師授課為輔」的模式。每週邀請海內外各領 域頂尖學者前來分享第一手研究與保育實務，提供學生最前沿的視野。 📅 五、教學進度表 (Course Schedule) 本課程安排多位跨校與跨總研院單位的權威學者，進度規劃如下： 週 次 日期 課程主題 授課／演講專家 01 9/9 認識生物多樣性 郭立園老師、黃貞祥老師 02 9/16 蕨類的多樣性與演化 郭立園老師（國立清華大學） 03 9/23 開花植物的多樣性與演化 王俊能老師（國立台灣大學） 04 9/30 走訪校園生態（實地考 察） 郭立園老師、黃貞祥老師 週 次 日期 課程主題 授課／演講專家 05 10/7 鳥類的多樣性與演化 黃貞祥老師（國立清華大學） 06 10/14 昆蟲的多樣性與保育 吳士緯老師（國立臺灣博物 館） 07 10/21 生物多樣性國際公約 鍾國芳老師（中央研究院） 08 10/28 土壤裡的生物多樣性 張智涵老師（國立台灣大學） 09 11/4 哺乳類的多樣性與保育 顏士清老師（國立清華大學） 10 11/11 🎒 校運會（停課一次） - 11 11/18 病原體多樣性 張筱涵老師（國立清華大學） 12 11/25 微生物多樣性及人類健康 蕭尊先老師（國立清華大學） 13 12/2 真菌多樣性及保育 蔡怡陞老師（中央研究院） 14 12/9 兩棲爬行類的多樣性與保 育 林思民老師（國立台灣師範大 學） 15 12/16 海洋生物的多樣性與永續 利用 柯佳吟老師（國立台灣大學） 16 12/23 📊 期末成果報告 全體師生 💯 六、成績考核 (Grading Policy) • 每週課後小考 (26%)： 針對當週專家演講內容進行考核（皆為單選題）。 • 心得報告 (44%)： 自選其中一週的課程主題撰寫深度心得。 • 課程作業 (20%)： 校園生物紀錄實作。 • 課堂出席 (10%)： 課堂參與度與出席率。 ⚠ 重要學術倫理規範： 「心得報告」必須由學生親自撰寫，切勿使用任何生成式 AI 工具（如 ChatGPT、Gemini 等）生成報告。 經查獲者將依校規與課程規範嚴格議處。

docs.name: 生命科學之模式生物
docs.text: 國立清華大學 115 學年第ㄧ學期課程大綱 科號 Course No. 11010LS 545700 組別 group 學分 credit 2 人數限制 Size limit 30 修課年級 For grade ■ 大學部 年級以上 (undergraduate) ■ 碩士班一年級以上(含博士班) graduate ■ 碩士班二年級以上(含博士班) 上課時間 Time T7T8 教室 Room TBA 科目中文名稱 Course title in Chinese 生命科學之模式生物 Model organisms in life sciences 科目英文名稱 Course title in English Model Organisms in Life Sciences 任課教師 Teacher 李以如, 劉姿吟, 王歐力, 王翊青, 江運金, 桑自剛 擋修科目 Prerequisite 擋修分數 credit ※下列各欄由任課教師提供※ 一、課程說明 Course Description 人類基因體定序的完成，方便讓我們更了解所有人類的蛋白 質，但基因體的定序並無法提供足夠的信息來了解蛋白質的 功能、結構以其生物體內的訊號傳遞。現在，研究人員需要 的是，可以了解基因的作用，以及其編碼蛋白在細胞過程中 所扮演的角色。為了回答這些問題，研究員需要依靠一些小 型生物來了解生物體的奧妙，其條件是：容易培養，基因體 定序已完成，已具備突變株，容易被改造，適合顯微鏡觀 察，能快速而精準的篩選突變株，生命週期短，以及遵守人 道精神。 儘管大多數的微小模式生物體與人類毫無共同之處，但是大 部分生物的基因相似性卻是極高的。在許多情況下，某些模 式生物的基因已被成功地被人類基因取代，卻沒有影響其細 胞功能。模式生物，現在被廣泛地用來研究人類的疾病，並 且在較簡單的生物研究疾病，也減少了受爭議的倫理問題。 在這一學期的課程中，我們將介紹常用的一些在世界廣泛被 使用的模式生物，包括：老鼠，斑馬魚，阿拉伯芥，果蠅， 線蟲，酵母菌和大腸桿菌。課堂上，我們將選定一些主題進 行討論，像是解剖，發展（胚胎學），神經生物學（神經解 剖學，行為，mechanosensation，電生理學），遺傳（基因 體計畫），操作和維護這些模式生物，改造與基因的表達， 交配和性別鑑定，突變實驗（顯微注射，基因槍，和化學藥 物EMS），基因定位（SNP定位），RNAi干擾和利用轉位 子(transposons)的基因操作，顯微鏡使用，疾病模式，毒理 學和藥理學，演化和生態學，研究的方法和搜尋網站等等。 更有趣的，學生將有機會參加特定實驗室的操作或是觀摩。 並可學習如何處理和維護選定的模式生物，以及利用顯微鏡 來篩選綠色螢光蛋白的表達和其他變異之間的差異。 Course Description: The completion of the Human Genome Project has improved our understanding of human proteins. However, simply sequencing the genome is not enough to fully understand protein functions, structures, and their roles in cellular signaling. Researchers need methods to understand gene functions and the roles of encoded proteins in cellular processes. To address these questions, researchers rely on model organisms that meet specific criteria: ease of cultivation, completed genome sequencing, available mutants, modifiability, suitability for microscopic observation, rapid and precise mutant screening, short life cycles, and adherence to ethical principles. While it's true that most model organisms don't share direct commonality with humans, many species do exhibit a significant genetic similarity. This similarity has allowed human genes to be successfully replaced in model organisms without disrupting cellular function. As a result, model organisms have become invaluable tools in the study of human diseases, offering a way to investigate simpler biological systems and thereby reducing ethical controversies. Course Objectives: • Introduce commonly used model organisms in biomedical research. • Discuss various biological disciplines using model organisms, including anatomy, embryology, neurobiology, genetics, and more. • Provide hands-on experience and observational opportunities in laboratory settings. • Teach maintenance and handling of model organisms, microscopic screening techniques, and identification of protein expression variations. Model Organisms Covered: • Yeast • Arabidopsis • Nematode • Mouse • Zebrafish • Fruit fly Key Topics: 1. Anatomy and Developmental Biology (Embryology) 2. Neurobiology o Neuroanatomy o Behavior o Mechanosensation o Electrophysiology 3. Genetics o Genome projects o Manipulation and maintenance of model organisms o Gene expression and modification o Mating and sex determination 4. Mutation Experiments o Microinjection o Gene gun technology o Chemical mutagenesis (e.g., EMS) 5. Gene Localization o SNP mapping 6. RNA Interference (RNAi) 7. Transposon-based Gene Manipulation 8. Microscopy Techniques 9. Disease Models 10. Toxicology and Pharmacology 11. Evolution and Ecology 12. Research Methodologies and Database Searching Practical Experience: Students may be able to participate in laboratory work or observations, learning to handle and maintain selected model organisms. Practical sessions will include using microscopes to screen for green fluorescent protein expression and identifying differences among various mutants. docs.text: 國立清華大學 115 學年度第 1 學期課程大綱 科號 Course Number 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Class Size 10 中文名稱 Course Title 證據產生與整合特論一 英文名稱 Course English Title Evidence generation and synthesis I 任課教師 Instructor 施銘杰 上課時間 Time TaTb 上課教室 Room 清華實驗室 617 課程簡述(必填) （最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) In medical research, evidence generation and synthesis are crucial in the practice of evidence- based medicine. In evidence generation, we strive to identify statistical methods that correctly produce answers for our clinical question of interest, with special care to the data generation mechanism and the assumptions required to validify the estimation methods. In evidence synthesis, we aim to combine multiple pieces of data that provide evidence to our clinical question of interest, with the aim of producing a coherent conclusion with efficient estimation and minimized bias. With a focus on current research projects in Dr. MC Shih's lab, this special topic course begins with a systematic review of current methods in (1) causal inference under the high dimensional data setting (2) evidence synthesis from heterogeneous sources, followed by general and then focused discussion of potential novel methods that are of interest. 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 因果推論；證據整合；統合分析；機器學習；高維度資料分析 Causal inference; Evidence synthesis; meta-analysis; machine learning; high-dimensional data analysis 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus @@@ Discuss with the course instructor before enrolling in the course @@ ● 課程說明(Course Description) In medical research, evidence generation and synthesis are crucial in the practice of evidence- based medicine. Students are required to submit two reports, midterm and final, and each counts for 30%. The content of the final report is limited to the content of the speech after the midterm report. PhD students must write in English, and the master students can write in English or Chinese. Plagiarism (including from online source, machine translation software or someone else's work) or improper reference are prohibited. Deadline for midterm report: 23:59, November 4, 2026 Deadline for final report: 23:59, December 23, 2026 The late submission: -2 points /day toward final score ii. docs.text: 科號 Course Number 11510LSBS790101 學分 Credit 1 人數限制 Class Size 10 中文名稱 Course Title 書報討論 英文名稱 Course English Title Seminar 任課教師 Instructor 劉懿璇 Yi-Shiuan Liu 上課時間 Time F5 上課教室 Room LS II 生二 107 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters 本課程目的在於深化同學對專業領域最新研究文獻的掌握與批判性解析能力， 並提升口頭表達與科學討論的技巧。學生將輪流選擇與課程主題相關的研究論 文進行報告，並與全班進行深入討論。透過課堂互動與導師引導，學生將學習 分析研究方法、解讀數據、以及科學論證與回應質疑的技巧。本課程同時鼓勵 學生從文獻中發掘研究動機、建立跨領域連結，進一步提出原創性研究問題的 能力。 請輸入課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」至少 5 個, 每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文, 以半形逗點分隔 (必填) Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 生物醫學 (Biomedicine), 期刊論文(Journal article), 口頭報告(Oral presentation), 科學方法(Scientific methods), 批判性思維(Critical thinking) 一、課程說明 本課程旨在訓練學生閱讀、理解、分析同儕審查文獻。透過 每週指定文獻的報告與討論，學生將培養學術溝通、邏輯表 達、問題提出與論證能力，並加強對研究方法與學術寫作的 掌握。 This course aims to train students in reading, understanding, and analyzing peer-reviewed journal articles. Through weekly oral presentations and discussions of assigned readings, students will develop skills in academic communication and critical thinking, while also deepening their understanding of scientific methods and academic writing. 二、指定用書 無 N/A 三、參考書籍 生命科學領域具代表性的學術期刊 四、教學方式 1. 上課方式以文獻討論為主。學生於課前預習文獻，並於 課堂中輪流提出問題討論。 2. 演講同學於演講前兩週將擬報告之研究論文寄給老師以 徵得老師同意；演講前一週將該論文全文以 PDF 電子檔發 給全班同學，以利預先閱讀與討論準備。 3. 每位同學報告 30 ~ 40 分鐘，10 ~ 20分鐘問題回答。 4. 口頭報告後兩周內繳交書面報告(約 2頁A4)，針對報告 與提問內容做出討論與心得總結。 5. 學期末每位同學另進行 10 分鐘研究自述，分享研究方 法與經驗。 1. The course is primarily conducted through literature presentations and discussions. 2. The presenting student must send the proposed research article to the instructor two weeks before the presentation for approval. One week prior to the presentation, the full article in PDF format should be shared with all classmates. 3. Each student will give a 30–40 minute presentation, followed by 10–20 minutes of Q&A. 4. A written report (approximately 2 A4 pages) should be submitted within two weeks after the oral presentation. 5. At the end of the semester, each student will give a 10- minute research talk, sharing their research experiences. 五、教學進度 每週以 1 位同學進行報告為原則。 In principle, one student will give a presentation each week. 六、成績考核 報告內容與簡報品質 presentation 40% 批判性分析能力 critical thinking 10% 討論互動與提問 participation in discussion 25% 書面摘要 written report 15% 課堂出席 attendance 10% 可使用 AI 相關工具，但需揭露使用範圍與方法。 ※請假規定依清華大學學則辦理。遲到 15 分鐘視為缺席。 七、可連結之網頁 位址(相關網頁)

docs.text: 國立清華大學 115 學年度第 1 學期課程大綱 科號 Course Number 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Class Size 需與授課教師討論 後加簽選課 Requiring application in order to enroll in the course. 中文名稱 Course Title 離子通道、代謝調控與發炎機制特論一 英文名稱 Course English Title Special Topics in Ion Channels, Metabolism, and Inflammation (I) 任課教師 Instructor 邱于芯 上課時間 Time F7F8 上課教室 Room LS2, Rm 218 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) 本課程探討離子通道與細胞代謝在發炎與疾病中的交互作用，重點放在心血管疾病與神經系統疾 病（如 TBI、heart failure、AD）。課程將介紹：離子通道與膜蛋白生物學、免疫與神經發炎的 分子機制、細胞代謝重塑與免疫調控、心血管與神經疾病的發炎機制、離子通道作為藥物標靶、 新藥開發策略、轉譯醫學與臨床應用。課程形式包含講授、文獻討論、小組討論及個人研究報告。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 離子通道、細胞代謝、發炎、心血管疾病、神經系統疾病、新藥開發 Ion channel, cell metabolism, inflammation, cardiovascular disease, neurological disease, drug development 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程探討離子通道與細胞代謝在發炎與疾病中的交互作用，重點放在心血管疾病與神經系統疾病（如 TBI、heart failure、Alzheimer’s disease）。課程將介紹：離子通道與膜蛋白生物學、免疫與神經發炎的 分子機制、細胞代謝重塑與免疫調控、心血管與神經疾病的發炎機制、離子通道作為藥物標靶、新藥開發策略、 轉譯醫學與臨床應用。課程形式包含: 課堂講授、文獻閱讀與討論、小組討論及個人研究報告。完成本課程後， 學生應能：理解離子通道在細胞訊號傳遞與發炎反應中的角色，包括 ATP release、Ca²⁺ signaling、膜電位 調控等；分析細胞代謝重塑（metabolic reprogramming）如何影響免疫與發炎反應，如 glycolysis、 mitochondrial metabolism、Warburg effect；說明心血管疾病、腦損傷與神經退化性疾病中的發炎與代謝 機制；批判性閱讀並分析相關領域的研究文獻；了解從分子機制到藥物開發的轉譯研究流程，包括 target identification、drug screening、animal models、clinical translation；培養研究設計與科學報告能力， 能夠提出可行的研究假說。 ● 指定用書(Text Books) 1. Hille B. Ion Channels of Excitable Membranes (3rd ed.) 2. Janeway’s Immunobiology (10th ed.) ● 參考書籍(References) 1. Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (7th ed.) 2. Molecular Biology of the Cell – Alberts (7th ed.) ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 課程採用研究導向教學模式，透過課堂講授、文獻閱讀與討論、小組討論與學生個人報告，培養學生分析科 學文獻與設計研究計畫的能力。 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 週次 主題 內容簡述 1 課程介紹與疾病背景 介紹課程內容、評量方式，以及發炎與代謝在疾病中的重要性 2 離子通道基本概念 離子通道結構、分類與生理功能 3 離子通道與細胞訊號 Ca²⁺ signaling、ATP release channels、膜電位調控 4 發炎與免疫反應 Innate immunity、cytokines、inflammasome 5 免疫代謝 免疫細胞的代謝調控 6 發炎中的代謝重組 Glycolysis、mitochondrial metabolism 7 神經發炎機制 Microglia、astrocytes、neuron-glia interactions 8 文獻討論 學生文獻導讀與討論 9 心血管疾病中的離子通道 Arrhythmia、vascular inflammation、heart failure 10 腦損傷與神經退化疾病 Traumatic brain injury & neurodegenerative disease 11 腦部中代謝的細胞交互作用 Brain metabolism, focusing on neuron-glia crosstalk 12 離子通道作為藥物標靶 Ion channel-targeted therapeutics 13 新藥開發策略 Drug screening、small molecule、peptide or biologics 14 轉譯醫學 Animal model development & biomarker identification 15 學生研究提案報告 Proposal presentation 16 未來研究方向 AI 藥物設計與未來發展 ● 成績考核(Evaluation) 評量方式 (比例): 文獻討論參與 (20%)、小組討論與問題提出 (20%)、個人文獻報告 (30%)、期末研究構想 proposal (30%) ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output 可參考下列網頁範例 See the following web page for examples. https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248357.php?Lang=zh-tw ● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website)

Various nuclear factors are essential for immune organogenesis, leukocyte lineage development, differentiation, effector functions and immune tolerance.
