docs.text: Updated on July 19, 2025. 1 PME400500: Numerical Analysis (in English conditionally; X-class) Fall 2025 Department of Power Mechanical Engineering, National Tsing Hua University I. Course Description (課程說明) Error analysis (Chap. 1), solutions of equations in one variable (Chap. 2), interpolation and polynomial approximation (Chap. 3), numerical differentiation and integrating (Chap. 4), initial-value problems for ordinary differential equations (Chap. 5), direct methods for solving linear systems (Chap. 6), and iterative technique in matrix algebra (Chap. 7). The approximation theory (Chap. 8) might be delivered provided we have sufficient time. Other chapters in the textbook will NOT be covered. II. Prerequisite (預修課程) Engineering Mathematics (I) III. Textbooks (指定用書) 1. R.L. Burden, and J.D. Faires, Numerical Analysis, 10th ed., Thomson Brooks/Cole, Belmont, CA, USA, 2016. (for theory) IV. References (參考書籍) 1. G.R. Lindfield, and J.E.T. Penny, Numerical Methods: Using MATLAB, 4th ed., Academic Press, Cambridge, MA, USA, 2019. (for coding) 2. T. Sauer, Numerical Analysis, 3rd ed., Pearson Education Inc., Edinburgh Gate, United Kingdom, 2023. (for examples and homework) V. Time and Location (教學時間與地點) 1. Lectures (in English) / Lectures review (in Mandarin) / Coding exercises 2. Written exams (9:00 – 12:00 on Tuesday at Room 209, ENG_I) 3. NTHU MOOCs https://mooc.nthu.edu.tw/ (https://mooc.nthu.edu.tw/course/info/339) 4. Videos of last year are provided on eLearn https://elearn.nthu.edu.tw/ by permitted request VI. Instructor (授課教師) Dr. Yu-Bin Chen (陳玉彬 教授); ybchen@pme.nthu.edu.tw Updated on July 19, 2025. 2 Room 512 in Engineering Building I 03-5715131 (ext. 33767) Office hour: Wednesday 13:10 – 13:30 or reserved via e-mail VII. Teaching Assistants (助教) 1. Mr. Chang-Li Zheng (鄭長力) l6509eo@gmail.com 2. Mr. Shang-Wei Liu (劉上偉) sean910830@gmail.com Office hour: Tuesday 14:10 – 16:00 or reserved via e-mail Room 430 in Engineering Building I 03-5715131 (ext. 33743) VIII. Evaluation (成績考核) Homework: 150 (sum of 5 assignments) Tests: 240 (1.4  higher + 1.0  lower) Bonus: 80 (attendance, answering to in-class questions) Grade guidelines are given according to the rules described in the following. Assume student A gets the highest score x in the class. Student B gets the score y, which is higher than 280. Student C gets the score z, which is lower than 280. Then, student A will get 97 in Numerical Analysis as the final grade. Student B will get the score “60 + 37(y  280)/(x  280).” Student C will get the score “55  z/280.” For example, we assume that student A gets the highest original score 430, student B gets 400, and student C gets the score 260. The final grade of student A, B, and C will be 97, 60 + 37(400  280)/(430  280) = 89.6 = 90, and 55260/280 =51.07 = 51, respectively. Note: A student will fail in this course even he or she gets the original score 279, unless more than 15% of students are flunked. The criteria 279 can only be slightly adjusted till less than 15% of students are flunked and the average score of whole class can be curved to 70 -79. Note: The average score of whole class will be curved to 70 – 79, which is requested by PME. Homework: Please read the relevant sections of the references before each lecture. Read the book examples carefully before doing homework also. There will be five homework assignments, due before the class as indicated on the schedule page. Solutions will be announced after the due date. The steps Score Range  280 < 280 Actual Grade  60  55 Updated on July 19, 2025. 3 of solution should be detail enough and clear; otherwise you will not receive full credit even if your answers are correct. Discussion among classmates is encouraged; however, you are expected to solve problems independently. Homework grading will be largely based on efforts and whether you have used the procedures correctly, rather than the numbers. You will receive a penalty for each unsolved problem. All assignments will be counted. Examination: There will be two exams in the semester. See the tentative schedule for examination dates. Please see the instructor immediately if a conflict arises. The first exam will contain 4 problems and last about 120 minutes. Complete solution of all problems will receive more than 100 points and the total points gained will be counted as the grades. Hence, you are encouraged to attack all problems in each exam. After the first exam, a vote will be held to decide if the final test is on-line or in-class. If an on-line test is conducted, more than 5 problems will be given while a student will be specifically asked to solve one problem within the given time (24 hours usually). Students can use any computer and his/her favorite software for this test. Before the time is up, he/she needs to upload answers on the course website and sends e-mails to the TA. TA’s Help: To help you on programming, the following time slots before mid-term exam are available for discussion and questions: - 10/24 (Thu.), from 2:00 PM to 4:00 PM - 10/25 (Fri.), from 2:00 PM to 4:00 PM - 10/28 (Mon.), from 2:00 PM to 4:00 PM You can choose a time that best fits for your schedule. Academic Honesty: Academic integrity and honesty is essential to achieve high-quality education and to keep the prestige of the institution. We will not tolerate any academic misconduct, such as cheating. Cheating includes, but is not limited to: copying directly from unauthorized source, such as friends, classmates or a solutions manual; allowing another person to copy your work; signing another person's name or having another person sign your name on an attendance sheet; taking a test or quiz in someone else's name, or having someone else take a test or quiz in your name; or asking for regrade of a paper that has been altered. docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 11510PME 500000 學分 Credit 1 人數限制 Class Size 中文名稱 Course Title 書報討論 英文名稱 Course English Title Seminar 任課教師 Instructor 陳嘉元 Chia-Yuan Chen 上課時間 Time R7R8 上課教室 Room ENG I 工一 107 課程簡述 本課程為動力機械工程學系研究所同學的必修課程，每週舉行一次，每次約 2 小時，邀請國內 外各相關領域的專家或產業不 同領域的實踐者至本系演講。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」 書報討論 Seminar 課程大綱 Detailed Course Syllabus 一、課程說明 本課程為動力機械工程學系研究所同學的必修課程，每週舉行一次，每次約 2 小時，邀請國內 外各 相關領域的專家或產業不同領域的實踐者至本系演講。 二、指定用書 無 三、參考書籍 無 四、教學方式 課程參與及演講心得 五、教學進度 TBA 六、成績考核 - Attendance 48%, Notes 36%, Q&A 16% Attendance and notes are capped at 84%. Each attendance counts for 4%, and each note of the speech counts for 3%. Attending 12 seminars will result in full attendance points. Scores from classroom Q&A are capped at 16%. The final grade will be capped at 99%. 出席成績佔 48%，演講重點摘要佔 36%，課堂提問佔 16%。 簽到+重點摘要至多計算至 84 分 (出席 12 次可拿滿分)。每次出席佔 4 分，每一份演講重點摘要佔 3 分。課堂提問至多計算至 16 分。期末成績至多給至 99 分。 - Please write your notes on a white A4 paper (with the back side blank) during the seminar and submit it to the TA before leaving the classroom. Notes must be submitted on time and in the required format; late submissions or use of the wrong format will not be accepted. It is recommended to use bullet points and list at least five key points covering the beginning, middle, and end of the seminar. 演講重點摘要請在課堂內書寫，下課時繳交 (限以 A4 白色紙張撰寫，背面需空白) 予助 教。摘要請於下課離開教室時繳交，不接受事後補交或以其他格式紙張撰寫。建議摘要以條列 式撰寫重點，至少列舉超過五項重點，並涵蓋演講前中後的內容為佳。 - If you need to be absent from class for any reason, including sick leave, personal leave, or participation in events such as international conferences, prior approval is not required. Students are allowed up to three absences without penalty. However, a fourth absence (or any additional absence) will result in a failing grade (F) for the course. 如果你需要請包含病假、事假，或其他事 由不能到課(例如參加國際會議)，不須事先請假。本課程每人可缺席三次演講 (即本學期至少出 席 11 場)。缺席合計超過四次以上，學期成績逕以不及格論。 - Asking meaningful questions during the Q&A session can contribute up to 16% of your final grade. For each seminar, you may earn up to 8% from Q&A participation, with each valid question worth 4%. To receive these points, you must record the question you asked and the speaker’s response in your class notes. Copying or claiming credit for questions asked by other students will be considered academic dishonesty, and the final grade will be recorded as F. 在課堂中提問可以獲得最多 16 分的分數，但無法超過這個上限。每提出一個問題可以得到 4 分，同一堂課提出複數問題最多得 8 分。請在你的重點摘要內寫下你所問的問題並標註演講者 的回答 (不須另紙書寫)。若你未提問，請勿寫下其他同學提出的問題並偽裝成自己提問，違規 者學期成績以不及格論。 - If any of the following situations occur, the student’s final semester grade will be considered as F: (a) Forging attendance records (including signing inor others or having someone sign in for you); (b) Clearly plagiarizing another student’s summary notes; (c) Recording Q&A from other students without asking any questions themselves, in order to receive points; (d) Being absent from more than three seminars. Individual students involved in the above situations will be notified to explain their situation and reasons to the teaching assistants and course instructors. 若有以下狀況，學期總成績將計為不及格： (a) 假造點名結果 (包含代替他人點名、被他人代 點名)。 (b) 演講重點摘要明確抄襲其他同學。 (c) 沒有進行課堂發問但寫下其他人的 Q&A 企 圖獲得額外分數。 (d) 缺席合計達四次以上。以上情事將會通知個別同學找助教與任課教師說 明狀況與緣由。

docs.name: 流體不穩定性控制理論
docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number PME 511400 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 無 中文名稱 Course Title 流體不穩定性控制理論 英文名稱 Course English Title Flow Instability Control Theory 任課教師 Instructor 胡相宸 上課時間 Time F6F7F8 上課教室 Room 工一 209 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Fluid instability, particularly the transition from laminar to turbulent flow, plays a fundamental role in fluid dynamics and is especially critical in electronic cooling and semiconductor processing. In recent years, the rising demand for high-performance immersion liquid cooling, driven by the increasing power density of advanced chips and the rapid evolution of semiconductor fabrication technologies, has intensified the need to better understand and actively control the resulting thermo-flow effects. These effects directly impact the quality of epitaxial thin films as well as the performance of high- performance computing (HPC) and artificial intelligence (AI) chips. One of the most urgent challenges in the metal-organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) epitaxial process is how to achieve the uniformity and stability of reactive gas flows. Addressing this challenge is essential for improving thin film quality and ensuring reliable device operation. This course integrates the fundamentals of flow instability and thermal convection with an active flow-field stabilization strategy known as the Kelly-Hu Mechanism. Within this framework, students will explore innovative approaches to stabilizing flow behavior in the MOCVD process and to overcoming thermal management challenges posed by next-generation high-power chips. The course is designed formaster’s and doctoral students, as well as advanced undergraduates (junior or senior level), who have completed an introductory course in fluid mechanics. 流體穩定性與不穩定性是流體動力學中最核心且廣泛被探討和研究的課題，尤其在電子冷却與半導體製程中更顯 關鍵。流場從穩定層流(Laminar Flow)發展成不穩定紊流（Turbulence）的物理現象廣泛存在於各種應用科學領 域。近年來，隨著高耗能晶片對高效能浸沒式液體冷卻技術需求的迅速攀升，以及半導體製程設備因應高階運算 與人工智慧（AI）晶片爆炸性需求而快速成長，晶片製程中的熱流效應已成為影響薄膜磊晶層品質與晶片效能的 關鍵挑戰。因此，在有機金屬化學氣相沉積（MOCVD）磊晶過程中，如何有效控制反應氣體的均勻性與穩定性， 已成為半導體產業亟待克服的重要議題。本課程將系統講解流體穩定與不穩定的理論基礎，並結合熱流擾動特性 與 Kelly-Hu 主動控制機制，探討如何有效調控 MOCVD 製程中的流場穩定性，並因應高效能晶片的散熱挑 戰。課程兼具理論與實務，協助學員建立先進熱流管理與半導體精密製程控制的新視野，全面掌握次世代熱流控 制的核心技術。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) Flow Instability, Floquet Theory, Galerkin Method, Boussinesq Approximation, Rayleigh-Taylor Instability, Kelvin-Helmholtz Instability, Orr-Sommerfeld Equation, Rayleigh-Bénard Convection, Rotating flow and Centrifugal Instabilities, Finite Amplitude, Thermal Convection, Taylor Vortex Flow, Modulated Fluid Motions, MOCVD Flow 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) 流體穩定性與不穩定性的控制，是流體力學中的核心課題，對電子冷卻與半導體製程尤為重要。流體受到外力擾 動或邊界變化時，層流（Laminar Flow）可能轉變為高度不穩定的紊流（Turbulence），影響化工製程、熱流系 統及半導體設備的性能。深入理解穩定（Steady）與不穩定（Unsteady）流場的物理機制，有助於精準控制流體 擾動並提升工程效能。隨著高階晶片與半導體技術的發展，此研究對提高晶片良率與運行效能具有直接意義。 流體動力學與半導體製程的融合，是一項高度跨領域的前瞻性研究，涵蓋工程力學、材料科學與物理化學等領 域。有效掌握流體不穩定性的控制理論與方法，並結合人工智慧技術進行流場擾動的預測與主動控制，將是推動 高效能晶片製程與散熱技術發展的關鍵。隨著高耗能晶片對高效能浸沒式液體冷卻技術需求的快速增長，以及高 階運算與人工智慧（AI）晶片市場的蓬勃發展，半導體製程中熱流效應已成為影響薄膜磊晶層品質與晶片效能的 主要挑戰。在有機金屬化學氣相沉積（MOCVD, Metal-Organic Chemical Vapor Deposition）磊晶過程中，如 何穩定並均勻地控制反應氣體的流場，已成為半導體產業亟需克服的技術瓶頸。本課程將聚焦於熱流擾動特性與 穩定流場之主動控制機制，並結合 Kelly-Hu 機制（Kelly-Hu Mechanism），提出創新且高效的控制方法，應對 MOCVD 製程中流場的不穩定性，同時滿足高耗能晶片所引起的散熱挑戰。 本課程內容設計將系統性介紹穩定與不穩定流場的基本特性與關鍵物理機制，深入探討引發流體擾動的成因與控 制方法，特別強調 Kelly-Hu 機制在流場控制中的應用。此外，課程亦將探討多種調控流場穩定性的方法，提供 學生解決實際工程問題的理論基礎與技術工具。本課程適合碩士與博士研究生研習，亦歡迎已完成基礎流體力學 課程的大三或大四學生選修。 課程內容包括：  Stability problems and the dynamic control of modulated systems based on Floquet theory and the Kelly-Hu Mechanism  Instabilities involving interfaces and disturbance energy equations  The Orr–Sommerfeld and vorticity equations  Rayleigh–Bénard convection and centrifugal instabilities  Finite-amplitude thermal convection and rotating flows  Active control strategies for modulated fluid motions  Thermal management in cooling systems and MOCVD (Metal-Organic Chemical Vapor Deposition) flow control The control of fluid stability and instability is a central challenge in fluid mechanics, with critical applications in electronic cooling and semiconductor processing. Fluid flows are highly sensitive to disturbances and sudden boundary changes, which can trigger transitions from laminar to turbulent regimes, affecting both engineered systems and natural phenomena. Understanding these mechanisms is essential for precise flow control and for enhancing the performance and reliability of advanced integrated circuits (ICs) and semiconductor manufacturing processes. The rapid growth of high-power chips and advanced semiconductor technologies has made thermo- flow effects in chip manufacturing a critical challenge, directly impacting thin-film quality and device performance. Achieving uniform and stable reactive gas flows in the MOCVD epitaxial process is now a top priority for the semiconductor industry. This course combines fluid dynamics with active flow-field stabilization using the Kelly-Hu Mechanism, giving students the tools to understand and control flow instabilities. Through theory and practical applications, students will explore innovative solutions for thermal management and next-generation chip fabrication. This course is suitable for master's and doctoral students, as well as advanced undergraduates (junior or senior year) who have completed an introductory course in fluid mechanics. ● 指定用書(Text Books) None ● 參考書籍(References) 1. R. E. Kelly, “The Onset and Development of Thermal Convection in Fully Developed Shear Flows,” Advances in Applied Mechanics, Vol. 31, pp. 35-112, 1994. 2. S. Chandrasekhar, “Hydrodynamics and Hydromagnetic Stability”(1961) 3. P. G. Drazin and W. H. Reid, “Hydrodynamic Stability”(1981) 4. R. E. Kelly and H.-C. Hu, "The Onset of Rayleigh-Bénard Convection in Non-Planar Oscillatory Flows," Journal of Fluid Mechanics, Vol. 249, pp. 373-390, 1993. 5. H.-C. Hu and R. E. Kelly, "The Effect of a Time-Periodic Axial Shear Flow upon the Onset of Taylor Vortices," Physical Review E, Vol. 51, pp. 3242-3251, 1995. 6. Philip Hall, "Finite-Amplitude Convection in the Presence of an Unsteady Shear Flow," Journal of Fluid Mechanics, Vol. 287, pp. 225-249, 1995. 7. Trudi A. Shortis and Philip Hall, “On the Effect of Feedback Control on Bénard Convection in a Boussinesq Fluid,” ICASE Report No. 96-9, NASA Langley Research Center, 1996. 8. H.-C. Hu and R. E. Kelly, “Stabilization of Longitudinal Vortex Instabilities by Means of Transverse Flow Oscillations,” Physics of Fluids, Vol. 9, pp. 648-654, 1997. 9. A. Weisberg, I. Kevrekidis and A. J. Smits, "Delaying transition in Taylor-Couette flow with axial motion of the inner cylinder," Journal of Fluid Mechanics, Vol. 348, pp. 141-151, 1997. 10. F. Marques and J. M. Lopez, "Taylor–Couette flow with axial oscillations of the inner cylinder: Floquet analysis of the basic flow," Journal of Fluid Mechanics, Vol. 348, pp. 153-175, 1997. 11. J. M. Lopez and F. Marques, "Modulated Taylor–Couette flow: Onset of Spiral Modes," Theoretical and Computational Fluid Dynamics, Vol. 19, pp. 59-69, 2002. ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) Lecture Notes & Class ppt ● 教學進度(Syllabus) Syllabus 課程大綱 Lecture Contents I Introduction to Flow Stability I.1. A Brief Historical Survey I.2. General Concepts Concerning Stability II The Formulation of Stability Problems II.1. Models of Physical Processes II.2. Models of Stability Problems III Dynamic Control to Modulated Flow Systems III.1. Galerkin Method Introduction III.2. Floquet Theory III.3. Kelly-Hu Mechanism IV Instability Involving an Interface IV.1. Rayleigh-Taylor Instability IV.2. Kelvin-Helmholtz Instability V Disturbance Energy Equation for Shear Flow Instability VI Orr-Sommerfeld Equation and Vorticity Equation VII Onset of Rayleigh-Bénard Convection VII.1. The Fundamental Problem VII.2. Effects of Different Boundary Conditions VIII Rotating Flows and Centrifugal Instabilities IX Finite Amplitude Thermal Convection and Rotating Flow X Instability Control of Modulated Fluid Motions X.1. Thermal Convection Control Methodology X.2. Rotating Flow Control Methodology XI Innovations to Manage Cooling and MOCVD Flows XI.1. Thermo-Flow Management for IC cluster Modules XI.2. Flow Stability in MOCVD Reactors ● 成績考核(Evaluation) Grading Policy Mid-term 20% Final 20% Homework 20% Term-paper, and Presentation 40% ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) (1) 完全開放使用且無須註明 Unrestricted use with no disclosure required (2) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output 本課程鼓勵學生在透明與負責的原則下，適度使用 AI 工具進行課業協作。學生應在作業或報告的標題頁註腳 或引用文獻部分簡要說明 AI 工具的使用情況，並遵循學校的相關指引。如未明確標註，教師有權重新評分或 不予計分。 (3) 禁止使用，請註明相關的監管機制 Prohibited use; please specify relevant oversight (4) 本課程無涉及 AI 使用 Not applicable 可參考下列網頁範例 See the following web page for examples. https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248357.php?Lang=zh-tw ● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website) 

docs.name: 高等振動學
docs.text: Prof. Jen-Yuan (James) Chang Telephone: +886-03-574-2498  Office: Engineering Building I – R509  Email: jychang@pme.nthu.edu.tw Page 1/2 PME 534200 Advanced Mechanical Vibrations 高等振動學 Fall Semester, 2026 Instructor: NTHU Chair Professor Jen-Yuan (James) Chang 張禎元 清華講座教授 Credits: 3 credits. Language: This course will be offered in English Class meetings: M5M6M7 Engineering Building I – R216 Office hours: Monday 18:30-19:00 PM in Prof. Chang’s office Course description: The subject area for this course is mechanical vibration, at a level appropriate for master and doctoral graduate students. Classical techniques in mechanical vibration are developed for the modeling and analysis of discrete and continuous linear dynamic systems. Continuous systems are described within the broader context of operator theory to emphasize the physical and mathematical analogies with discrete systems. Specific topics include: Discrete systems. Equations of motion for multiple degree of freedom systems through Lagrange’s method; linearization about equilibrium; symmetry and definiteness properties; free vibration; matrix eigenvalue problems; orthogonality; Rayleigh quotient; generalized coordinates; transient and forced response through modal analysis. Continuous systems. Classical rod, shaft, string, beam, membrane and plate models; Hamilton’s principle; equations of motion and boundary conditions through variational methods; essentials of functional analysis; exact solution of eigenvalue problems; Galerkin’s method; essential and suppressible boundary conditions; Kamke quotient; introduction to elastic wave propagation and vibrations of rotors. Prerequisites: PME 332000 “Mechanical Vibrations,” or its equivalent. Textbooks: L. Meirovitch, Analytical Methods in Vibrations, Macmillan Lecture notes/materials provided by Professor Chang. References: S.S. Rao, Vibration of Continuous Systems, Wiley. L.A. Pars, A Treatise on Analytical Dynamics, Oxbow. F.S. Tse, I.E. Morse, and R.T. Hinkle, Mechanical Vibrations, Prentice-Hall. D. Newland, Mechanical Vibration Analysis and Computation, Longman. Teaching Method: Classroom lectures in English with teaching materials posted in Moodle. Assessments: Homework & Labs 30% Term Project 10% Midterm Exams 30% Final Exam 30% Homework Policy: Problem sets will be assigned regularly and will usually be due one week later. Usually combination of analytical, computational, and graphical approaches will be expected in homework. Copy of homework is not allowed. However, you are allowed to discuss homework problems with one another in order to teach each other how to solve problems. You are NOT allowed to copy work from someone else OR to work step-by-step through a problem with someone else. The work you hand in with your name on it must be your attempt to work through the problem. As a general guideline, oral communication regarding the homework is allowed, whereas written communication is not allowed. Because of the fast pace of the class, please avoid handing in late homework. If homework is submitted after solution set is distributed, 50% of the grade will be taken off. Prof. Jen-Yuan (James) Chang Telephone: +886-03-574-2498  Office: Engineering Building I – R509  Email: jychang@pme.nthu.edu.tw Page 2/2 Course Outline and Reading Schedule Discrete Systems: 1. Review of Single Degree of Freedom Systems (Meirovitch, Chapter 1) a. Free vibrations b. Response through transform methods c. Frequency response function 2. Equations of Motion for Multi-Degree of Freedom Systems (Chapter 2, 3) a. Definitions and concepts b. Derivation of Lagrange’s equation c. Small oscillations around equilibrium 3. Free Vibration (Chapter 4) a. Matrix eigenvalue problems b. Properties of the eigenvalue problem c. Solution methods d. Expansion techniques e. Rayleigh’s quotient 4. Modal Analysis (Chapter 7.1-7.6 and 9.1-9.5) a. Response problems b. General solutions c. Steady State Harmonic Response d. Damped system response Mechanism of dissipation; Viscous damping; Rayleigh proportional damping; Modal damping Continuous Systems: 5. Equations of Motion for Continuous Systems (Course notes and Chapters 5, and 10.1-10.5) a. Transition from discrete system to continuous system b. Infinitesimal element approach Torsional Rod, longitudinal rod, and string models; Euler-Bernoulli, Rayleigh, and Timoshenko Models; Membranes c. Variational approach Hamilton’s principle for a conservative discrete system; Extended Hamilton’s principle; Extension to continuous systems; Applications 6. Eigenvalue Problems of Continuous Systems (Course notes and Chapter 5) a. Formulation and solution of eigenvalue problems One-dimensional, 2nd-order problems; One-dimensional, 4th order problems; Two-dimensional, 2nd-order problems; Two-dimensional, 4th-order problems. b. Structure of the eigenvalue problem Essentials of functional analysis; Properties of linear operators, symmetric, and positive- definiteness. 7. Modal Analysis (Course notes and Chapter 7.7-7.17) a. General development b. Steady state harmonic response c. Static response d. Transformations for inhomogeneous boundary conditions 8. Special topics a. Introduction to global discretization (Course notes and Chapter 6.1-6.6) b. Introduction to constrained systems (Course notes) c. Introduction to elastic wave propagation (Course notes and Chapter 8.1-8.8) d. Vibrations of rotors (Course notes)

docs.name: 彈性波元件與應用
docs.text: PME 5371 Elastic Wave Devices and Applications Instructor: Ming-Huang Li Objectives: The goal of this course is to discuss the fundamentals of elastic waves in solids and their engineering applications. This is a theoretical course focused on the development of equivalent circuit models for various elastic wave devices. The course begins with the theoretical background of ultrasonic wave propagation in solids and crystals. This is followed by an exploration of the design methodologies of RF microdevices (such as FBAR and Lamb wave resonators), as well as various micromachined ultrasonic transducers (CMUT and PMUT). The final part of the course covers circuit and subsystem design based on these devices. Students are expected to gain general knowledge of integrated ultrasonic microsystems. Commercial software tools (COMSOL Multiphysics, MATLAB, and Keysight ADS) will be used for homework assignments. Prerequisites: Mechanics of Materials, General Physics Language: This course is offered in English, but some important concepts will be repeated in Mandarin. Grading: Assignments + Experiments (35%) Final Exam (45%) Final Project Presentation and Report (20%) Textbook: No textbook. Lecture notes will be distributed weekly. Key References: 1. J. F. Rosenbaum, Bulk Acoustic Wave Theory and Devices, Artech House, 1988. 2. B. A. Auld, Acoustic Fields and Waves in Solids, vol. 1, Wiley, New York, 1973. 3. D. Royer, E. Dieulesaint, and D. P. Morgan, Elastic Waves in Solids I - Free and Guided Propagation, Springer-Verlag Berlin Heidelberg, 2000. 4. S. Senturia, Microsystem Design, Kluwer Academic Publishers, 2001. Course Outline: (1) Introduction of vibrations and waves (2) Bulk waves in solids and crystals (3) Film bulk acoustic wave resonators (FBAR) (4) Plate wave resonators (PWR) (5) RF filters and oscillators based on elastic wave devices (6) Micromachined ultrasonic transducers: CMUT and PMUT (Optional) (7) Electronic circuit design for MUTs (Optional) 生成式人工智慧倫理聲明：禁止使用 經仔細考量後，本課程授課教師認為不宜於此門課程當中使用生成式人工智慧於課堂學習當中。因本 課程的內容於生成式 AI 中尚有諸多錯誤，且容易影響學生對基礎核心知識之判讀。 根據本校公布之「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採取禁止使用，以下為相 關的監管機制。 修讀本門課程之學生應注意本門課不得繳交使用生成式人工智慧所產出的作業、報告或個人心得。若 經查核發現，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。 Ethical Statement on Generative Artificial Intelligence: Prohibition on Use After careful consideration, the course instructor believes that it is not appropriate to use generative AI in learning for this course. Students taking this course should be aware that assignments, reports, or personal reflections generated using AI models are strictly prohibited. If such use is detected, the course instructor, university, or relevant authority reserves the right to re-evaluate or not score the assignment or report. Students who enroll in this course are deemed to have agreed to the above ethical statement at the time of course selection.

You will lose points by skipping classes while gain points by asking good questions or initiating discussion. Because this class is expected to be taught in English, students are expected to participate in English as well. Note: The average score of whole class will be curved to 80 – 85, which is requested by PME. Updated: 08/24/2024 2 Quizzes: There will be 4 quizzes. See the tentative schedule for examination dates. Please see the instructor immediately if a conflict arises. Quizzes will be CLOSE BOOK, while the final exam will be OPEN BOOK ONLY. You can bring English textbooks and other textbooks in English. Conversely, lecture notes, Chinese textbook and materials not in the book form are NOT permitted. You will need a calculator for both exams. Field trips: Because the source for our professional knowledge can be seminars and conferences, we will have two field trips during the semester. It is required to attend at least 2 talks and write a report for each. A report should introduce the subject, methodology, and authors’ contributions, and your feelings. Items should be addressed in the report are suggested below: – What is the subject? Why is it related to radiation/light/electromagnetic waves? – Why is the subject/work important? Why do authors dig into the problem? – What is the main contribution of this work, such as the difficulty they overcome? – What methodology/algorithm did authors employ? Could you do the same now in your LAB? – What could be its next step or anything else you would like to share? Term project: The subject will be announced in the first week of semester. Every student is asked to do a term project independently by the end of semester. The term project includes an oral presentation, a written report, and hands-on results (artworks). An A4 page of abstract is ought to be delivered in the middle of semester for instructor’s review. The presentation and PPT file must be in English because the official language of course is English. 5 points will be deducted for students who either present not in English or use non-English PPT file. All topics related to radiative heat transfer are welcomed. The presentation will be held at the end of the semester and each presentation will take about 15 minutes with 3 minutes Q&A. The presentation will be graded based on following items: the fitness of title and length of presentation, the organization and fluency, clarity of figures and tables, completeness of contents, and time management as well as gestures. Project deliverables include terms in the following: – Abstract and revised one – Progress briefs – Classroom presentation – Written report at the end of semester – Hands-on results For the report, the page limit and format are not restricted if the instructor can appreciate your works. However, you may want to refer a conference or journal template to make the report look professional. Contents should include review of the literature/state-of-the-art in the field. One should formulate the problem (state the problem, make and justify assumptions/idealizations, formulate governing equations, approach for evaluation of radiative properties, and boundary conditions. The report also needs to identify/describe a suitable solution technique and obtain representative results (only if time permits). Moreover, it is expected to propose experiments for theory validation, including design of experimental setup and discussion of anticipated difficulties in performing experiments and/or interpreting results. Academic Honesty: Academic integrity and honesty is essential to achieve high-quality education and to keep the prestige of the institution. We will not tolerate any academic misconduct, such as cheating. Cheating includes, but is not limited to: copying directly from unauthorized source, such as friends, classmates or a solutions manual; allowing another person to copy your work; signing another person's assignment or having another person finish your own work; taking a test or quiz in someone else's name, or having someone else take a test or quiz in your name; or asking for regrade of a paper that has been altered from its original form. docs.text: 精準醫學概論 INTRODUCTION TO PRECISION MEDICINE PMED 7001 | FALL, 2026 SYLLABUS LAST UPDATED ON 9/6/2026 PAGE 1 OF 5 課程資訊 精準醫學概論 INTRODUCTION TO PRECISION MEDICINE 精準醫療博士學位學程 | PMED 7001 115 學年度上學期 週三 | 14:20 – 17:30 生科一館 1 樓 112 室 腦科學 VR 教室 開課教師 黃至正 chihchenghuang@mx.nthu.edu.tw (03)571-5131 #42685 生科二館 212 室 曾大千 tc.tseng@mx.nthu.edu.tw (03)571-5131 #42756 生科二館 414 室 課程助教 陳奕璇 maggiechen@gapp.nthu.edu.tw 邱梓怡 anny.zyq@gapp.nthu.edu.tw (03)571-5131 #33492 生科二館 101B 室 評分標準 ▪ 出缺席 | 10% ▪ 課堂參與 | 10% ▪ 上課心得報告 | 25% ▪ 台灣醫療科技展參訪報告 | 25% ▪ 精準醫療團隊新創競賽 | 30% 課程概述 精準醫學（precision medicine）結合基因體學、分子診斷、生物資訊、 人工智慧、醫療器材及創新治療技術，已成為現代醫學與生技產業的 重要發展方向。隨著次世代定序 (next-generation sequencing, NGS）、液 態 活 檢 、 多 體 學 分 析 （multi-omics）、 伴 隨 式 診 斷 （companion diagnostics）及人工智慧技術的快速進展，疾病診斷、藥物開發與治療 決策正逐步朝向個人化與精準化發展。 本課程涵蓋三大主軸： ▪ 精準腫瘤醫學（precision oncology） 包括伴隨式診斷、次世代定序、液態活檢、癌症標靶治療及免疫 治療等內容。 ▪ 先進診斷與醫療科技 包括生醫感測器、生物晶片、生醫電子、人工智慧醫療及數位病 理等新興技術。 ▪ 創新治療與產業轉譯 包括硼中子捕獲治療（boron neutron capture therapy, BNCT）、精準 藥物開發、生技創業及智慧醫療產業應用等主題。 本課程邀請國內精準醫學領域之學術專家、臨床醫師及產業領袖共同 授課，透過專題演講、產業案例分享、台灣醫療科技展參訪及團隊競 賽，培養學生跨領域整合能力、創新思維與產學合作視野，協助學生 掌握精準醫療與大健康產業之最新發展趨勢。 擋修或建議先修 無。 參考教材 講者之演講內容與投影片。 考試 無。 作業繳交規定 ▪ 上傳至 eeclass 系統。 ▪ 不接受作業遲交。 ▪ 人工智慧（artificial intelligence, AI）使用原則：條件式使用。 - 若使用 AI 協助完成報告，則需揭露使用 AI 之方式與涵蓋範圍， 並提供原始指令(prompt)。 - 如未特別說明，學生之報告將上傳至 Turnitin。若經 Turnitin 判 定內容超過 33%為 AI 生成，需當面向教師說明；否則教師將從 嚴評分。 精準醫學概論 INTRODUCTION TO PRECISION MEDICINE PMED 7001 | FALL, 2026 SYLLABUS LAST UPDATED ON 9/6/2026 PAGE 2 OF 5 預計進度與講題 週次 日期 講者資訊與講題 課程事項 01 09/09 課程簡介 黃至正 博士 國立清華大學 | 精準醫療博士學位學程 | 助理教授 02 09/16 精準檢測: 生物晶片與生醫電子在精準醫療中的角色 黃至正 博士 國立清華大學 | 精準醫療博士學位學程 | 助理教授 03 09/23 講題待定 于松桓 博士 國立中山大學 | 精準醫學研究所 | 助理教授 04 09/30 器官晶片 李孟學 博士 國立陽明交通大學 | 生物科技學系 | 助理教授 05 10/07 硼中子捕獲治療 陳韋霖 博士 禾榮科技 | 研發工程中心 | 副總經理 06 10/14 腫瘤微環境 精準醫療團隊新創競賽分組名單 郭育倫 博士 圖爾思生物科技 | 副總經理 07 10/21 講題待定 林之儀 博士 國立中興大學 | 生命科學系 | 助理教授 08 10/28 腫瘤微環境 傅勝雍 博士 國立清華大學 | 分析與環境科學所 | 博士後研究員 09 11/04 製藥產業現況 梁子豪 A.R.Z CHEMICALS TAIWAN LTD. | 總經理 10 11/11 停課 (全校運動大會) 11 11/18 智慧醫療 郭志峰 博士 柏瑞醫股份有限公司 | 策略長 12 11/25 循環腫瘤細胞類器官於精準醫療之應用 陳柏翰 精拓生技 | 創辦人暨執行長 吳詩培 精拓生技 | 共同創辦人暨營運長 13 12/04 台灣醫療科技展 星期五 曾大千 / 黃至正 台北南港展覽館 14 12/09 基因檢測在大健康產業的應用 江淑華 先見基因科技股份有限公司 | 總經理 15 12/16 淺談製藥 GMP 品質系統 林俊毅 盛鈉生物科技 | 經理 16 12/23 精準醫療新創團隊競賽 曾大千 / 黃至正 期末團隊口頭報告 12/27 繳交報告 報告上傳截止日 星期日 上課心得報告 醫療科技展參訪報告 精準醫療團隊新創競賽報告 精準醫學概論 INTRODUCTION TO PRECISION MEDICINE PMED 7001 | FALL, 2026 SYLLABUS LAST UPDATED ON 9/6/2026 PAGE 3 OF 5 出缺席 [10 分] 助教將同時提供紙本簽到與線上簽到，遲到 10 分鐘以上者，以「無故缺席」記。預設出缺席分數為 10 分，第 二次無故缺席開始扣分，每次扣 3 分。無故缺席達 5 次以上，學期成績不及格。可參照下表。 無故缺席堂數 獲得分數 1 堂 10 分 2 堂 07 分 3 堂 04 分 4 堂 01 分 ≥5 堂 學期成績不及格 ▪ 請假不扣分，但需 email 通知助教並附上證明。 ▪ 同學可在 eeclass 的「出缺席」頁面查閱自己的出缺席紀錄。 ▪ 遠距上課：在職生若因工作場所距離因素，可向開課教師申請遠距上課。一般生若臨時有特殊情況無 法到課，亦可遠距上課，惟須事先通知老師與助教。視訊連結：https://meet.google.com/tqu-vobz-cnz。 課堂參與 [10 分] 為了鼓勵學生積極參與課程並與講者互動，課堂提問將獲得分數。相關細節如下： ▪ 發問可獲得 1 分 (同堂課發問多次仍計 1 分)。 ▪ 最高獲分上限為 10 分。 ▪ 可在 eeclass「成績計算」頁面查閱課堂提問加分紀錄。 ▪ 若發現提問加分未計入，請主動與助教聯繫確認。 上課心得報告 [25 分] 請從本課程所有講題中，選擇一場最具啟發性、最有收穫的主題。 格式與篇幅： ▪ 內容須包含演講摘要以及個人心得。 ▪ 至多 2 頁。紙張尺寸可為 A4 (297mm × 210mm) 或美國信紙 (279.4 mm × 216 mm) 。 ▪ 正文(body text)需超過 800 個字。 ▪ 檔案格式需為.docx 或.pdf。 內容： ▪ 演講摘要（Summary） 說明該主題的核心概念、研究重點或演講者的重要觀點。 ▪ 個人心得與反思（Reflection） 必須為全文至少一半以上的篇幅，可包含： - 你從此講題得到的啟發或新觀點 - 你認為此講題對精準醫學、生醫研究或臨床應用的貢獻 - 此內容與你的學習、研究或未來生涯目標的連結 - 個人疑問、批判性思考或延伸想法 - 鼓勵深入分析，不限個人經驗亦可談學術面與社會面。 台灣醫療科技展參訪報告 [25 分] 格式與篇幅： ▪ 至多 2 頁。紙張尺寸可為 A4 (297mm × 210mm) 或美國信紙 (279.4 mm × 216 mm) 。 ▪ 本文(body text)需超過 800 個字。 ▪ 檔案格式需為.docx 或.pdf。 內容： ▪ 報告須描述本次參訪中所觀察到的重點攤位或展區內容。 ▪ 必須包含「參訪心得與反思」，此部分須佔全文一半以上篇幅。 ▪ 可適度加入參訪時拍攝之相關照片（非必須）。 精準醫學概論 INTRODUCTION TO PRECISION MEDICINE PMED 7001 | FALL, 2026 SYLLABUS LAST UPDATED ON 9/6/2026 PAGE 4 OF 5 精準醫療團隊新創競賽 [30 分] 為呈現各組於團隊創新競賽中的構想與成果，請各組依以下格式準備並繳交報告文件。 團隊口頭報告規範 ▪ 每組報告時間：約 30 分鐘 ▪ 簡報內容建議包含（但不限於）： - 創新問題定義 - 構想核心理念 - 技術/市場可行性 - 預期效益與未來發展 文件繳交 ▪ 上台報告之簡報檔 PPT（必繳文件） 作為正式簡報使用，內容需清楚呈現團隊構想、資料分析與論證。請注意格式、圖文整合與邏輯性。 ▪ 團隊創新競賽構想書（補充文件） 作為簡報之外之補充資料。請依附件提供之「空白構想書格式」完成填寫。包含構想背景、創新點、 技術可行性、預期成果、團隊分工等內容。 精準醫學概論 INTRODUCTION TO PRECISION MEDICINE PMED 7001 | FALL, 2026 SYLLABUS LAST UPDATED ON 9/6/2026 PAGE 5 OF 5 常見問與答 作業可以遲交嗎? 不可以。遲交一律以零分計算。 如何確認心得報告為原創? 同意選修本門課程的同學，其個人報告（例如：上課心得報告、台灣醫療科技展參訪報告）將由助教或老師上 傳至 Turnitin.com ，進行文字內容相似度及 AI 生成內容檢測，以協助確認報告是否符合課程對於生成式 AI 使用 之相關規範。所有提交的文件將作為 Turnitin.com 數據庫的來源，且將遵守 Turnitin.com 的使用條款協議。 如果個人報告由 AI 協助完成，我該如何說明使用 AI 之方式與涵蓋範圍並提供原始指令(prompt)？ 請另外提供文件（.docx 或.pdf 檔）簡略說明，原始指令可以藉由提供連結或截圖貼上該文件。報告與說明文件 需同時上傳至該次作業繳交區。 如果個人報告由 AI 協助完成，但我忘記說明使用 AI 之方式與涵蓋範圍怎麼辦？ 教師將從嚴評分。 如果個人報告由 AI 協助完成，但我忘記附上供原始指令(prompt)怎麼辦？ 教師將從嚴評分。

docs.text: National Tsing Hua University QF2141 Financial Management Course Syllabus Instructor: Tak-Yuen Wong Email: etywong110@gmail.com Office: TSMC Building Room 755 Office Hours: by appointment Course Description This course provides an introduction to finance, covering the basic concepts and tools necessary to understand how capital markets work and how financial instruments are used for investments. The course explores core concepts for the financial aspects of decision-making, including the principles of valuation, arbitrage, costs of capital, diversification, risk-return trade-off, and market efficiency. Building on these concepts, we will develop analytical frameworks for the valuation of real and financial assets, portfolio selection, and costs of capital estimation. This knowledge is essential for navigating the uncertainty and financial innovations in current times. Learning Objectives Upon completion of the course, you should be able to understand  The basic financial instruments: bonds, mortgages, and stocks.  The fundamental approach for valuation: the time value of money and its relation to the discount rate (cost of capital) and the risk premium of a real or financial asset.  The main model of asset pricing: the Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM), and its applica- tion to estimate costs of capital.  The structure of capital markets, market efficiency, and predictability of prices. Textbook Brealey, Richard, Stewart Myers, and Franklin Allen, 2020, Principles of Corporate Finance, Mc- Graw Hill, 13th Edition. - A thorough introduction to the theory and practice of finance. One of the most popular finance textbooks. - Lecture notes are mostly based on the textbook. Grading Policy Grades are based on 4 assignments (30%), a midterm exam (30%) and a final exam (40%). Assignments are individual and should be type or written legibly. You must submit in hard copy in class on the scheduled date. No late submissions will be accepted. Both exams are closed-book and closed notes. A (financial) calculator is allowed but no other electronic device (e.g., calculator on a smart phone is not permitted). Extra practice problems will be provided before exams. Schedule for exams will announced on the first day of the class. In case you cannot attend any of the exams, you must apply for a makeup beforehand with valid proof. 1 Tentative Class Schedule This is an approximate schedule of topics that will be covered. You are recommended to read the corresponding book chapter prior to the lecture. Topic Textbook 1. Introduction to finance Ch. 1 2. Principles of valuation Ch. 2 3. Bond pricing Ch. 3 4. The value of common stocks Ch. 4 5. Investment decisions Ch. 5-6 6. Risk, return, and Portfolio theory Ch. 7-8 7. The Capital Asset Pricing Model Ch. 8 8. Risk and costs of capital Ch. 9 9. Market efficiency Ch. 13 10. Practices in capital budgeting Ch. 10-12 Recommended Readings I strongly encourage you to devote time outside of class to sharpen your understanding of the financial markets. Besides leading business publications such as Financial Times and the Wall Street Journal, I highly recommend the following books. Malkiel, Burton, A Random Walk Down Wall Street, 2020. - Best-selling introduction to practical investing. A great way to ease into financial markets. Lewis, Michael, The Big Short: Inside the Doomsday Machine, 2011. - A non-fiction book on the story of the 2007-09 subprime mortgage crisis and the people who profited from it. It provides an informative look at the world of finance. Bernstein, Peter, Capital Ideas: The Improbable Origins of Modern Wall Street, 2005. - An entertaining historical account of the origins and evolution of modern finance and the people who contributed to its development. 2

docs.text: Course Syllabus QF314800: Mathematical Statistics I Instructor: Chung-Han Hsieh (ch.hsieh@mx.nthu.edu.tw) Course Description & Audience: This course concentrates on theoretical statistics using the first principles of probability theory. Our aim is to introduce many fundamentals and lay a solid foundation for students to explore various areas such as data science, quantitative finance, statis- tical signal processing, machine learning, financial mathematics, and econometrics in the future. Many of the results will be delivered in a definition-theorem-proof manner. The prerequisite is one year of calculus. To succeed in this course, some mathematical maturity is expected. • Introduction to Statistics • Probability Theory • Transformation and Expectations • Common Families of Distributions • Sampling Distributions • Limiting Behaviors of Random Sequences • Elementary Statistical Inferences Prerequisites: A student planning to take this course should have a fair familiarity with mul- tivariate calculus. Time and Place: Lectures are at T7T8T9, in Room 204 TSMC Building. Office Hours: Office hours for the instructor are at 12:00–13:00 Monday, in Room 608 TSMC Building. Meetings are also possible at other times by appointment. Course Materials: Students will be provided with handout material to support the lectures. The material will be mainly drawn from some recommended textbooks/references listed below. 1. G. Casella and R. L. Berger, Statistical Inference, Cengage Learning, 2001. 2. R. Hogg, J. McKean, and A. Craig, Introduction to Mathematical Statistics, Pearson, 2018. 3. J. A. Rice, Mathematical Statistics and Data Analysis, Cengage Learning, 2006. 4. D. Wackerly, W. Mendenhall, and R. L. Scheaffer, Mathematical Statistics with Applica- tions, Thomoson Brooks/Cole, 2008. Teaching Method: Lecture Homework: Approximately weekly. You are encouraged to join with other students in dis- cussing the course work, including homework. However, work that you hand in must have been prepared by you alone. 1 Grading: The grade will be based on homework (20%), a midterm (30%), and a final (50%). The instructor may exercise discretion up to 5% in each of the grading categories. Ethics Statement on Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI): This course adopts condi- tionally open policy. Students are required to disclose the use of generative AI in their assign- ments, specifically detailing its role in idea generation, sentence refinement, or structure. Failure to disclose will result in academic penalties, including potential reevaluation of the work. The instructor will also transparently indicate any use of AI in course materials. Students enrolled in this course agree to the above ethics statement if registering for the class. 2

docs.text: ðÞ4À¢ Ò 2025 年秋季 鍾經樊教授 cfchung@mx.nthu.edu.tw 本課程的目標是訓練學生未來能在金融工程領域 (金融商品設計, 投資銀行業務與資本市場操作, 衍生性金融商品 投信與投顧, 市場、 信用、 與流動性風險管理, 資產價格建模與應用) 就業, 本課程因而極為計算導向 (也因此與其 他衍生性金融商品相關課程有很大的差異) 。 整年課程的教程中有超過千條的數學式, 學生必須很快的適應並學會 從數學式的推導與演算中獲得金融直覺, 之前沒有一年以上的微積分以及一年以上的統計學準備的同學不太可能 跟得上本課程的進度。 本課程是一整學年課程的上學期部分, 只修一學期的學生將完全不懂選擇權的操作以及避險分析, 因而強烈建議只 擬修習一學期衍生金融商品的學生轉修其他相關課程。 本課程涵蓋的內容包括如下四個部份: 1. 金融體系: ï 金融商品與金融市場 ï 金融機構 ï 中央銀行與金融基礎設施 ï 金融商品會計 2. 基本金融商品的價格: ï 複利與折現 ï 利率與零息債券的價格 ï 利率期限結構 ï 付息債券的無套利價格 ï 殖利率與平價殖利率 ï 存續期間與凸率 ï 股票與股價 ï 外匯與匯率 3. 遠期契約: ï 遠期契約的交易 ï 跨期無套利原則 ï 遠期價格 ï 遠期外匯契約 ï 遠期利率 ï 遠期利率協定 ï 證券的附條件交易 ï 證券的信用交易 4. 期貨: ï 期貨的交易 ï 保證金制度與逐日結算 ï 期貨價格 ï 股價指數期貨 ï 利率期貨 ï 債券期貨 本課程將以任課老師的中文教程為主, 兩本不錯的英文參考書是 ï Hull, J. docs.text: National Tsing Hua University QF322700 Macro-Finance Course Syllabus Instructor: Tak-Yuen Wong Email: etywong110@gmail.com Office: TSMC Building Room 755 Office Hours: by appointment Course Description Macro-Finance is an emerging field after the 2007-08 Great Financial Crisis. Traditional macroe- conomic analysis, both the classical and the Keynesian schools, has ignored the role of the financial system in channeling resources across the economy, leading to failure in foreseeing and under- standing financial crises and modern global economic issues. The subject bridges the gap between the macroeconomy (GDP, employment, consumption, etc.) and the financial sector (asset prices, credit supply, etc.). It takes the view that financial activity is at the heart of economic fluctuations, and not only during times of severe crisis. The purpose of this course is to understand the two- way interactions between the real economy and the financial sector by digging into the following mechanisms. 1. Amplification and financial acceleration: shocks arising in the real economy can propagate through financial markets and amplify business cycles. 2. Bank runs: banks can be the source of shocks, which lead to instability in the real economy. 3. Intermediary capital constraint: the capacity for financial intermediaries to take leverage drives asset prices and risk premia. 4. Safe premium: global investors are always seeking “safe assets”, which the U.S. government bonds are viewed as the most important class. The financial sector has implications on public debt sustainability and fiscal policy. The course is designed for upper-level undergraduate students who are interested in modern topics in macroeconomics and finance. We learn from insights developed by a number of Nobel laureates in Economic Sciences, including Tirole (2014), Holmstrom (2016), Bernanke, Diamond, and Dybvig (2022) as well many young and influential scholars. Prerequisites You should have basic understanding of microeconomics, macroeconomics, financial management. Familiarity with analytical tools, e.g., differentiation, constrained optimization, etc., is expected. In addition, the course is designed for students who are not averse to mental exercises. Grading Policy Grades are based on assignments (30%), a midterm exam (30%) and a final exam (40%). Assignments are individual and should be type or written legibly. You must submit in hard copy in class on the scheduled date. No late submissions will be accepted. 1 Both exams are closed-book and closed notes. A (financial) calculator is allowed but no other electronic device (e.g., calculator on a smart phone is not permitted). Extra practice problems will be provided before exams. Schedule for exams will announced on the first day of the class. In case you cannot attend any of the exams, you must apply for a makeup beforehand with valid proof. Detailed Topics 1. The fundamentals of decision-making in macro-finance (a) Intertemporal choices; Permanent Income Hypothesis (PIH) (b) The effects of borrowing constraint 2. The 2008 Financial Crisis (a) Asset pricing bubbles; housing market; collateral value (b) Amplification mechanism: Kiyotaki-Moore (1997)’s credit cycles (c) Financial accelerator: Bernanke-Gertler (1989) 3. The role of financial intermediaries (a) Banking with Holmstrom-Tirole (1997) and Diamond-Dybvig (1983): monitoring, liq- uidity transformation, maturity mismatch, bank runs (b) Intermediary asset pricing with Brunnermeier-Sannikov (2014) and He-Krishnamurthy (2012): financial leverage of investment funds, implications on endogenous risk and risk premium 4. Public debt as safe assets (a) Government budget constraint, Ricardian equivalence (b) What is safety premium? Public debt sustainability; global shortage of safe assets (c) Fiscal policy with household indebted demand and income inequality (Straub-Mian-Sufi 2021) 5. Additional Topics (if time permitted): Automation, AI, and growth, Climate Finance Recommended Readings There are no required textbooks for the course. Some readings will be drawn from the following sources. 1. New articles and commentaries from the Financial Times, the Wall Street Journal, and the Economists. 2. Accessible survey articles from academic journals, e.g., Journal of Economic Perspectives, Annual Review of Financial Economics. 3. Carlin, Wendy and David Soskice, David, 2024, Macroeconomics: Institutions, Instability, and Inequality. Freely available at Stone Econ Center at UCL. - The most updated textbook that relates financial markets and institutions to the macroeconomy, with difficulty set in between intermediate and advanced courses. We only read a few chapters in the book. 2

This is to build the wide range of view of students to understand specific company from supply chain point of view and cultivate students’ capability to analyze a hidden champion companies through the annual reports and be able to objectively review the performance of the business. 課程說明 Course Description 【隱型冠軍】八週課程：介紹隱型冠軍的基礎理論，說明隱形冠軍的定義，研究方法 論，並介紹一些有名的隱型冠軍公司。同時說明隱型冠軍公司的客戶經營，產品發展， 以及服務提供的策略，介紹它們如何利用創新來面對競爭，常用的財務策略，公司組 織，以及對員工的管理方式。 [Hidden Champion] 8 weeks courses Introduce the definition of the Hidden Champion and introducing successful cases. Dr. Hermann Simon’s research methodology will be introduced. The course will include both lecture and discussion, covers the market and focus, globalization, customers, products, services, and innovation. The competition and financing, employees and leaders will also be discussed. 【職業參訪】三週：實地參觀隱型冠軍型態的公司。 [Innovative tours] 3 weeks courses Visit hidden champion types of the companies 【外部講座】兩週：邀請隱型冠軍經營者分享。 [Guest Speakers] 2 weeks courses. docs.text: National Tsing Hua University Department of Quantitative Finance Spring 2026 graduate course: 3 credits Instructor: Pei-Fang Hsieh Phone: 03-5715131 ext. 62163 Email: pfhsieh@mx.nthu.edu.tw Empirical Research of Derivative Markets Course Overview Students who are taking this course should have already taken courses of option and future markets (derivative markets) and financial econometrics. This course is an introduction to empirical researches of derivative markets, with focus on a particular topic. This course will focus on the implied information of option markets and introduce several important findings of this topic. The two sections of the course are: ⚫ The implied information of the theoretical option prices and the option trading volumes of market participators. The references of the first section will mainly introduce the information content of option volume and option implied volatility calculated by various option pricing models. ⚫ The second section will introduce the most recently popular empirical workings about the implied information of underlying asset from option trading volume (or trading strategies) of investors. The discussion of information content in derivative markets will refer to market efficiency and behavioral finance. Course Requirements ⚫ Lectures and discussion in weekly course. Students should read the selected paper of corresponding week topic in advance. ⚫ We have two assignments in this course. Students should select two papers in each of those two sections to write referee letters (try to find some problems or something that can be extended). ⚫ No midterm and final examination. However, every student should prepare final oral presentation about one of those papers. The papers will be assigned in the second week after beginning this course. ⚫ The course grade will be determined according to the following weighting scheme: - 20% Class participation - 40% Assignments - 40% Final oral presentation. Course Material 1. Text book: Beyond Greed and Fear: Understanding Behavioral Finance and the Psychology of Investing, Shefrin, Oxford University Press (2002). 2. Research papers: you should download the required reading papers from e-journal search system or SSRN website. Course Outline and Required Reading Topic One: The information content of option volume. Week 5 (3/23): The estimated methods of implied volatility. 1. Garman, M.B. and Klass, M.J., 1980. The model-free implied volatility and its information content, Review of Financial Studies 18, 1305-1342.*** 4. Martens, M. and Dijk, D., 2007. The information content of implied volatilities and model-free volatility expectations: evidence from options written on individual stocks, Journal of Banking and Finance 34, 871-881. Week 7 (4/6): Prediction of the underlying asset 1. Harvey, C.R. and Whaley, R.E., 1991. S&P 100 index option volatility, Journal of Finance 46, 1551-1561.*** 2. Jorion, P., 1995. Option spread and combination trading, Journal of derivative 10, 70-88.*** 3. Chaput, J.S. and Ederington, L.H., 2005. Volatility trade design, Journal of Futures Markets 25, 243-279.*** 4. Chaput, J.S. and Ederington, L.H., 2005. Vertical spread design, Journal of derivative 12, 28-46. Week 9 (4/20): First round of final oral presentation. Topic Three: Who is the informed trader? Week 10 (4/27): The standpoint that particular traders may be informed I. 1. Chan, K.C. and Lakonishok, J., 1995. docs.text: Course Syllabus QF527200: Robust and Stochastic Portfolio Optimization Instructor: Chung-Han Hsieh (ch.hsieh@mx.nthu.edu.tw) Course Description & Audience: This course concentrates on studying several problems in stochastic portfolio optimization. We aim to make optimal portfolio management robust with respect to various modeling risks. Coverage of the material will be suitable for graduate students interested in quantitative finance, stochastic optimization, and theoretical portfolio management. The intended topics of the course to cover are listed as follows. Part 1: Review: Convex Optimization • Convex Sets • Convex Functions • Convex Optimization Problems • Optimization under Uncertainty (SOCP and SDP) Part 2: Robust and Stochastic Portfolio Optimization • Sensitivity of Mean-Variance Model & Factor Model • Black-Litterman Model • Unconstrained Optimization Theory • Duality Theory • On Risk-Averse Optimization • On Multi-Period Portfolio Optimization Part 3: Some Special Topics (if time permitted) • Special Topic: Stochastic Optimal Control Theory • Special Topic: Distributionally Robust Optimization • Special Topic: Chance Constrained Optimization Prerequisites: A student planning to take this course should have a fair familiarity with math- ematical analysis, linear algebra, optimization, probability theory, statistics, and investment theory. Familiarity with some numerical software such as Matlab or Python is also required. If in doubt about the background, the student should consult with the instructor. Textbooks & References: Students will be provided with handout material to support the lectures. The material will be mainly drawn from some recommended textbooks/references listed below. 1. A. Shapiro, D. Dentcheva, A. Ruszcy´nski, Lectures on Stochastic Programming: Modeling and Theory, SIAM, 2014. 2. A. Beck, Introduction to Nonlinear Optimization, SIAM, 2020. 1 3. R. Xie and W. Wei, Distributionally Robust Optimization and its Applications, Springer, 2024. 4. S. Boyd and L. Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization, Cambridge University Press, 2004. 5. F. J. Fabozzi, P. N. Kolm, D. Pachamanova, S. M. Focardi, Robust Portfolio Optimization and Management, Wiley, 2007. 6. D. G. Luenberger, Optimization by Vector Space Methods, Wiley, 1976. 7. A. Ben-Tal, L. El. Ghaoui, and A. Nemirovski, Robust Optimization, Princeton university press, 2009. 8. G. Cornuejols, J. Pena, R. T¨ut¨unc¨u, Optimization Methods in Finance, Cambridge Uni- versity Press, 2018. Time: Lectures are at R5R6R7. Teaching Method: Lecture Homework: Approximately bi-weekly. You are encouraged to join with other students in discussing the course work, including homework. However, work that you hand in must have been prepared by you alone. Grading: The grade will be based on final exam (40%), homework (20%) and a special project (40%). The instructor may exercise discretion up to 10% in each of the grading categories. Course Website: https://sites.google.com/view/chung-han-hsieh-website/home/teaching/robust- and-stochastic-portfolio-optimization Ethics Statement on Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI): This course adopts con- ditionally open policy. Students are required to disclose the use of generative AI in their as- signments and projects, specifically detailing its role in idea generation, sentence refinement, or structure. Failure to disclose will result in academic penalties, including potential reevaluation of the work. The instructor will also transparently indicate any use of AI in course materials. Students enrolled in this course agree to the above ethics statement if registering for the class. 2

docs.text: National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 科號 Course Number 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Size of Limit 30 中文名稱 Course Title 人工智慧與財務實證研究 (英文授課) 英文名稱 Course English Title Artificial Intelligence in Finance Research 任課教師 Instructor 邱婉茜 教師聯絡方式 Contact Information wan-chien.chiu@mx.nthu.edu.tw 上課時間 Time M5M6M7 上課教室 Room 先修科目 Prerequisite(s) 無 本課程對應之學習目標與核心能力 Aligned Learning Goals and Learning Objectives此科目對應之系所課程規畫所欲培養之核心能力 Core capability to be cultivated by this course 權重（百分比） Percentage 以堅實理論為基礎，理解財金體系運作機制，應用財金分析技術，實際 解決財金問題。 To understand the mechanism of the finance system through solid theoretical foundation and to apply quantitative financial analysis to solve real-world financial issues. 具備厚實財金基礎知識，包括財務管理與公司理財、衍生性商品訂價與 風險管理 To learn the knowledge of financial management, corporate finance, financial derivatives, and risk management. 具備創新管理，開發新領域的能力 To acquire the ability to innovate, integrate, and develop new research areas. 培養跨領域工作的能力 To develop the ability to work across different disciplines. 具備團隊合作的精神，有效溝通的能力，以及人文素養與國際觀。 To develop teamwork spirit, to acquire the ability to communicate effectively, and to have broad knowledge across humanities, social science and natural science with international perspective. 20% 20% 40% 10% 10% 課程目標 Course Objectives This course equips students with the ability to understand and apply artificial intelligence, machine learning, and Large Language Models (LLMs) techniques in modern finance research. Students will learn how AI methods can be used to analyze financial markets, corporate behavior, innovation, and textual disclosure. 課程說明 Course Description National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus This course introduces the use of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and Large Language Models (LLMs) in modern finance research. With the rapid expansion of financial big data — including market data, firm disclosures, innovation records, and alternative textual sources — AI methods have become increasingly important tools for empirical analysis and academic research in finance. The course covers both methodological foundations and research applications. Students will learn core machine learning techniques such as regularization methods, tree-based models, and neural networks, as well as natural language processing and representation learning approaches used to analyze financial texts, corporate disclosures, and innovation activities. The course also introduces recent developments in causal machine learning, emphasizing how predictive models can be integrated with economic theory and identification strategies to address research questions in asset pricing, corporate finance, and financial intermediation. Through hands-on coding exercises and empirical research projects, students will develop the ability to construct research datasets, implement AI-based models, interpret empirical results, and critically evaluate model validity and economic significance. The course places strong emphasis on research design, interpretability, and robustness, preparing students to conduct independent research using modern data science tools in finance. 指定用書 Textbooks There is no assigned textbook. Please see References section for the relevant teaching materials. 參考書籍 References Academic Papers: Babina, T., Fedyk, A., He, A., Hodson, J., 2024. Artificial intelligence, firm growth, and product innovation. Journal of Financial Economics, 151, 103745. Bekamiri, Hamid, Daniel S Hain, and Roman Jurowetzki, “Patentsberta: A deep nlp based hybrid model for patent distance and classification using augmented sbert,” Technological Forecasting and Social Change, 2024, 206, 123536. Bergeaud, A., Jaffe, A.B. Papanikolaou, D., 2025. Natural Language Processing and Innovation Research (No. w33821). National Bureau of Economic Research. Bergeaud, A., Potiron, Y. and Raimbault, J., 2017. Classifying patents based on their semantic content. PloS one, 12(4), p.e0176310. Caskurlu, Tolga and Hoberg, Gerard and Phillips, Gordon M., 2025. New Technology Sectoral Disruptions. Working Paper. Chiu, W.-C., Tseng, K., 2026. The Value of Transparency: Evidence from Federal Trade Commission’s Green Guides. Working Paper. Ghosh, Mainak, Sebastian Erhardt, Michael E Rose, Erik Buunk, and Dietmar Harhoff, National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus “PaECTER: Patent-level Representation Learning using Citation-informed Transformers,” arXiv preprint arXiv:2402.19411, 2024. Lu, S., Serafeim, G., Xu, S., Awada, M., 2025. Tracking business opportunities for climate solutions using AI in regulated accounting reports. Nature Communications, 16(1), 9769. Qiu, L., Sha, F., Allen, K., Kim, Y., Linzen, T. and van Steenkiste, S., 2026. Bayesian teaching enables probabilistic reasoning in large language models. Nature Communications. Schütt, H.H., 2023. What Can Bayesian Inference Do for Accounting Research?. Journal of Financial Reporting, 8(2), pp.157-174. 教學方式 Teaching Approach This course adopts a research-oriented and interactive teaching approach. The primary course materials consist of selected academic journal articles and empirical research papers on artificial intelligence and machine learning applications in finance. Students are expected to complete assigned readings prior to each class. Class sessions will combine lectures, guided discussions, and methodological demonstrations, with an emphasis on understanding research design, empirical strategies, and the economic interpretation of AI-based findings. The instructor will facilitate in-depth classroom discussions to encourage critical thinking about the strengths and limitations of AI methods in finance research. Students will complete several individual assignments and empirical coding exercises aimed at developing their ability to construct research datasets, implement AI techniques, and interpret empirical results. These assignments are designed to strengthen both conceptual understanding and technical skills relevant to conducting independent finance research using modern data science tools. 評分標準 Grading • Class Participation & Discussions: 50% • Individual Assignment: 50% 教學進度 Course Schedule • Module 1 — Role of AI in Finance Research — prediction vs causal inference, big data in finance. • Module 2 — Natural Language Processing in Finance — sentiment analysis, topic modeling, 10‑K analysis. • Module 3 — Large Language Models in Finance Research — LLM classification and validation. • Module 4 — Patent and Innovation AI Methods — embeddings and technology similarity. • Module 5 — Causal Machine Learning and Bayesian

To maximize the availability to Ph.D. students (for the goals set up by National Chair Professorship and 跨校博士生聯合培育計畫), Prof. Hsu plans to give lectures in both Hsinchu (NTHU) and Taipei (NTU or NCCU). To reduce the transportation time and costs for students, Prof. Hsu plans to give two sessions (say 3 + 3 = 6 hours) on each lecture day. 2. This is a lecture-based course and will be taught in English. 3. Students will need to use English in their in-class reports. 4. Students will need to attend online or in-person conferences hosted by Prof. Hsu, including “Taiwan Symposium on Innovation Economics and Entrepreneurship” ( https://oir.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1487-164855.php), “ NTHU-UNSW-SMU Symposium on Sustainable Finance and Economics” ( https://oir.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1487-225483.php), and AIEA monthly seminar ( https://www.aiea.org/0504) A sample list of weekly teaching schedule (and my related papers) 1. Green innovations: - “Green Entrepreneurship” with Wan-Chien Chiu, Shenje Hshieh, and Geoffery Zheng. - “Grow in the Sun: Valuation and Development of Green Innovation under Mandatory Carbon Disclosure”, with Jianqiang Chen and Pei-Fang Hsieh. - “Green Products”, with Wan-Chien Chiu, Kai Li, and Joy Tianjiao Tong. - “Corporate philanthropy and innovation: The case of the pharmaceutical industry,” with Frederick Bereskin, Journal of Applied Corporate Finance 28 (2), 80-86, 2016. - “Corporate philanthropy, research networks, and collaborative innovation,” with Frederick Bereskin and Terry L. Campbell, Financial Management, 45 (1), 175-206, 2016. 2. Emissions and pollutions: - “The pollution premium,” with Kai Li (PKU) and Chi-Yang Tsou, Journal of Finance 78(3), 1343-1392, June 2023. - National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus - “Carbon Emissions Under Exchange Rate Risk”, with Yan Li, Mark P. Taylor, and Zigan Wang. - “Financial Frictions and Pollution Abatement Over the Life Cycle of Firms”, with Min Fang and Chi-Yang Tsou 3. Stakeholders’ roles: - “The eco-gender gap in boardrooms,” with Kai Li and Yihui Pan, Management Science (Sustainability Department). - “Leviathan Inc. and corporate environmental engagement,” with Hao Liang and Pedro Matos, Management Science (Finance Department), 69(12), 7719-7758, December 2023. - “Environmental liabilities, borrowing costs, and pollution prevention activities: the nationwide impact of the Apex Oil ruling,” with Jianqiang Chen, Pei-Fang Hsieh, and Ross Levine, Journal of Corporate Finance, 91, 102739, April, 2025. - “Corporate social responsibility and external disruptions,” with Hsiao-Hui Lee and Long Yi, Journal of Corporate Finance, 89, 102675, December 2024. - “In the mood for creativity: Sunshine-induced mood, inventor performance, and firm value,” with Yangyang Chen, Madhu Veeraraghavan, and Edward Podolski, Journal of Empirical Finance, 78, 101527, Sept. 2024. - “Stakeholder Disciplining from Benefit Corporation Laws: Evidence from Stock Returns around Product Controversies”, with Hsiao-Hui Lee, Qingyu Meng, and Hong Wu. 4. Regulation and policies: - “Information disclosure and peer innovation: Evidence from mandatory reporting of clinical trials,” with Kyungran Lee, S. Katie Moon, and Seungjoon Oh, Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis, 60(7), 3267-3310, November 2025. - “Pay transparency and inventor productivity: Evidence from state-level pay secrecy laws,” with Huasheng Gao and Jin Zhang, forthcoming, RAND Journal of Economics, 56(4), 389-418, Winter 2025 - “Gender gap in the ownership of promising land,” with Cyrus C. Y. Chu and Yi- Ting Wang, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS), 120 (24) e2300189120, June 2023. - “Freedom of Information and Regulatory Enforcement with Respect to Corporate Pollution”, with Adriana Cordis, Hunghua Pan, and Jin Zhang. 指定用書 Textbooks No textbook 參考書籍 References No references 教學方式 Teaching Approach National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 1. Lectures 2. Student/colleague presentations 3. Guess speaker presentations (online or in-person symposium and seminars) 評分標準 Grading 1. Attendance: 20% 2. Assignments: 80% (2 in-class presentations) 教學進度 Course Schedule Prof. Hsu will host 3-4 online or in-person symposiums (all online: https://oir.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1487-164855.php & https://oir.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1487-225483.php) in this semester. Each symposium often runs from 9am to 4pm (5 to 7 hour long). Prof. Hsu will also host monthly online AIEA seminar (https://www.aiea.org/0504) that runs at 9PM-10PM on Friday or 9AM-10AM on Saturday. These symposiums and seminars are part of the lectures. In special occasions, the instructor will give online lecture instead of in-person meeting Tentative weekly schedules (this is based on 2024 calendar and will be updated): • Sept. 5: 2pm-5pm, 6pm-9pm • Sept. 19: 2pm-5pm, 6pm-9pm • Oct. 3: 2pm-5pm, 6pm-9pm • Oct. 17: 2pm-5pm, 6pm-9pm • Oct. 31: 2pm-5pm, 6pm-9pm • Nov. 14: 2pm-5pm, 6pm-9pm • Nov. 28 : 2pm-5pm, 6pm-9pm • Dec. 12: 2pm-5pm, 6pm-9pm 課程相關連接 Course Related Links For papers, please visit my SSRN link: https://scholar.google.com.tw/citations?user=Txx- kokAAAAJ&hl=zh-TW&oi=ao

docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 暫不填寫 學分 Credit 1 人數限制 Class Size 30 中文名稱 Course Title 專題演講 英文名稱 Course English Title Colloquium 任課教師 Instructor 林佳妏、薛光隆 上課時間 Time Sa 上課教室 Room 南大校區 N201 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) 本專題匯聚產官學研專家，以「法規科學」為核心，貫穿生醫產業價值鏈。課程涵蓋 ICH 國際 指南、新藥、建廠與醫材、研發策略、專利迴避設計與 CDE 審查實務，並延伸至產品商業上 市與論文寫作。期能透過實戰經驗分享，建構學生從創新研發、法規取證到市場佈局的完整宏 觀視野。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 學術演講,實務分享,專業養成,思考邏輯訓練,問答對應培養,法規科學、藥品、醫材、GMP、論文 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) 邀請知名專家或校內教師或畢業學生到學程上演講。 課程時程表 (9 月 19 日 – 12 月 19 日，注意只有 10/31-11/21 是連續的) 日期 主題 / 核心 講師 9/19 專題導論與法規科學前沿/品質源於設計 （QbD）：學名藥藥證申請實務 林佳妏／薛光隆 教授 10/17 產業動態與資訊洞察 環球生技雜誌 林明定 總編 10/24 停課（小組討論） 無 10/31 PIC/S GMP 藥廠建廠與確效實戰精要 暢鴻生技 巫鴻章 副總 （前莎多 利斯總監） 11/07 人工智慧與論文寫作 郭孟倫 教授 11/14 數位病理, 小分子藥品開發與論文準備經 驗分享（畢業學長姐分享） 李秉謙 Ping-Chien Lee (羅氏) /郭 佳蓉（台灣微脂體） 11/21 藥品法規審查, AI 健康醫療與論文準備經 驗分享（畢業學長姐分享） 陳佳沛 (前 CDE 審查員，現任工 研院) / 李美蕙（DCB） 12/19 新藥之查驗登記實務 沛爾首席顧問 厲文海 （前諾華資 深品保處長） ( 註：講者安排期間僅限 10/17 至 11/21 之間，12/19 保留為已畢業學長姐之期末評分專用。) ● 指定用書(Text Books) 無 ● 參考書籍(References) 無 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 1.本學程主辦的演講(每周邀請人員不同)形式，依學程公告為準。 2.期末繳交心得報告。 ● 成績考核(Evaluation) 本課程成績將由「出席與參與」及「期末心得報告」綜合評量： 1. 出席與課堂提問：本門課極重視實體互動，缺席上限為半堂課（事先請假㇐堂視為半堂課）。若缺 席達㇐堂，總成績將為 A 以下；缺席兩堂為 A- 等級。此外，每位學生須於全學期任㇐場次中至 少提出㇐個問題，與講者進行交流。 2. 期末心得報告： 請以你課堂提問的那場演講為核心，撰寫㇐份期末心得。報告格式不拘， 但內容須以「職能增加」或「職涯成⾧」為導向，具體論述該專題對您專業發展的實質啟 發。 ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) (1) (2) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output 可參考下列網頁範例 See the following web page for examples. https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248357.php?Lang=zh-tw ● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website)

docs.name: 研究方法
docs.text: 1 115-1「研 究 方 法 」課 程 大 綱 授課教師：華文所．林佳儀（研究室在文學館 201） 電子信箱：chiayi@gapp.nthu.edu.tw 一、課程說明(Course Description) 「研究方法」這門課，希望能夠帶領學生認識華文文學研究現況、入門相關研究方法、 熟悉文獻資料，並引領寫作論文的實際過程，祈使學生順利開展研究生涯。課堂實作內容， 包括研究發想、轉譯書寫、文獻回顧、研究計畫發表，由小組到個人，希望能夠循序漸進， 引導學生先根據作品／文獻，有組織地書寫相關主題，再進入研究計畫的規範架構之中，展 現思考問題與鋪敘論述的能力。 二、教學方式(Teaching Method) 教師講述、師生討論、小組作業、個人作業、口頭發表 三、教學進度(Syllabus) （將依實際上課情形調整） 週次 日期 課 程 進 度 一 9/9 課程說明、研究資源選介、書目及註腳寫作格式（自備筆電）、分組 ◎作業：書目 10 筆，依姓氏筆畫排序（包括專書、期刊論文、學位論文、 報紙等），文史或 APA 7 格式，週二下午 17:00 前，上傳 eeclass 作業區 二 9/16 竹塹城區踏查及餐敘 三 9/23 華文文學研究範式、論文組織、摘要寫作 ◎閱讀論文：黃美娥〈清代竹塹地區文學的發展與特色〉、陳室如〈晚清 海外旅人的倫敦印象──張祖翼《倫敦竹枝詞》與晚清海外遊記的對照〉 四 9/30 圖書館及資料庫運用、研究取徑、文獻回顧 五 10/7 【預計安排專題演講】 六 10/14 【預計安排專題演講】 七 10/21 小組報告｜華人文化田野願望（建議 2 人一組）（口頭及文字） 八 10/28 華文文學作品討論 九 11/4 研究計畫撰寫：問題意識、文獻回顧、研究方法、結構安排、圖表附錄 十 11/11 （全校運動會，停課一天）｜請上傳學術倫理認證 可約個別討論（實體或線上） 十一 11/18 （停課，改至週五晚上，線上上課）｜可約個別討論（實體或線上） 11/20 文獻解讀、議題發想 週五 19:00，與馬來西亞拉曼大學中文系碩士班線上上課（林佳儀主講） 十二 11/25 （停課，改至週五晚上，線上上課）｜可約個別討論（實體或線上） 11/27 週五 19:00，與馬來西亞拉曼大學中文系碩士班線上上課（黃麗麗主講） 馬華文學及馬來文學、馬英文學（比較文學視野） 十三 12/2 個人報告（1）｜文獻回顧 A（口頭及文字） 2 十四 12/9 個人報告（1）｜文獻回顧 B（口頭及文字） 十五 12/16 個人報告（2）｜研究計畫發表 A（口頭及文字） 十六 12/23 個人報告（2）｜研究計畫發表 B（口頭及文字） ＊（補充說明） 各週課程除上述主題之外，亦將涵蓋下列各面向： 1. 圖書館及研究中心的簡介與利用。 2. 電子資源與檢索工具的使用與檢索。 3. 讀書報告寫作指引與如何閱讀學術專書、論文。 4. 研究議題的選擇與資料的搜集、揀擇。 5. 研究大綱的擬定及參考書目的編纂。 四、成績考核(Evaluation) 課堂參與 20%：包括出席及討論。 小組作業 15%：口頭報告+2000 字左右書面報告，需配圖。 平時作業 30%：歷次小作業，週二 17:00 前上傳 eeclass 作業區。 期末報告 35%：請完成結構完整的研究計畫（包括參考書目）。 ※如使用生成式 AI 完成作業，需正確引註，並說明使用歷程。 五、參考書籍(References) 周春塘：《撰寫論文必讀的第 1 本書》（五版），臺北：五南圖書出版，2024 年。 docs.name: 現代散文的藝術美學與創作專題
docs.nameEn: Art Aesthetics and Creation of Modern Prose
docs.text: 現代散文的藝術美學與創作專題 授課老師：黃雅莉 教室：文學館 303 時間：星期一早上 234 節 mail： yali@mx.nthu.edu.tw , huangyali1966@gmail.com 老師研究室：文學館 202 聯絡電話：0911073247 一、 課程簡介 本課程是現代文學專業中一門理論與實踐、閱讀與創作相互結合的課程。在豐富學 生散文知識的同時，也培養學生基礎的創作能力。課程以閱讀、研究、創作並行之方式， 引領學生共同思索散文文體的規範、破體的邊界及其生命與哲思，並在創作的實踐中， 透過文本或視聽等媒界的激發，促使學生有能力開創自己的書寫風格，將個人的個性和 語境轉化於文字之中，形成一種個性化書寫。 課程有三重點：第一，對散文文體美學進行學理的剖析與辯證的論述，開掘散文藝 術獨到的藝術表現方式，藉由散文文本，向學生分析各種散文的創作技巧和藝術實踐。 第二，讓學生閱讀關於現代散文研究的相關論文，透過前行研究者學術論文的分析，深 化學生對於散文創作美學的理論建構能力。第三，請學生根據本課程講授的各式散文創 作類型中各選一種進行創作。通過以上三方面培養學生文本分析、獨立思辯、主題闡釋、 文學創作的能力。 授課內容乃以主題單元的方式，對現代散文的創作實踐經驗進行總結，概括散文的 文體美學特徵，並從表現手法、形象刻劃和結構經營等各方面，論述了散文創作表現真 摯與平淡的典型美、深邃美與哲理美、傳神美與簡約美、波瀾美與曲折美等各式審美的 創造規律和藝術手法進行說明，透過這些主題的探討，有助學生對散文藝術美學理論的 建構和散文創作能力的提高。 二、教學目標 (一)教學理念 長久以來，在我們心目中的散文，是一種具有主觀色彩、必然是有作者「我」 的文體，然而，隨著高科技時代的來臨與人心漸趨複雜，在瞬息萬變的時代中， 為因應社會發展的需要，為了增加散文藝術的創新性，有些作家在創作時，不甘 心拘守在傳統散文原有的模式，散文開始有了很不一樣的發展。在這種變化當 中，有幾個重點是不容被忽略。那就是「文體的破體與混血」、「身份的變身與越 界」、「類型化的趨勢」。歷史上的每一種書寫風氣的變化，都意味著時代的變遷。 它的意義不僅在於對一段已經逝去時光的回顧和總結，更為重要的是一個新時代 文學思潮的引領。二十一世紀以來的散文創作進入了一個多元審美的時代，隨著 市場經濟、傳播媒介和新興文化觀念的雜糅與融合，使得散文文體的疆域發生了 很大變化，散文的創作也隨之進入一個新階段，有所謂的越界變體、魔幻寫實、 存在主義等創作觀念或流派的出現，也在驗證著當下散文寫作新的格局和改變。 本課程向學生梳理分析現代散文創作的多元格局和新變，在具體分析作家作品的 基礎上審視當下散文寫作的探索和嘗試。 其次，散文是人學，是情學，更是心靈學與性格學，也是一種藝術美學。一 個作家在進行藝術構思時，必然自覺或不自覺地在作品中傾注自己的美學理想， 體現自身的審美觀念。作家的審美情趣和審美標準，往往是受作家的世界觀、文 化和藝術修養所制約，同時又要受歷史發展進程中特定的時代精神的感召和影 響，這些都會促使作家努力進行新的藝術探索，積極地創造出更具有歷史價值和 美學價值的力作。本課程主要是針對散文藝術營構的創作實際向學生進行散文學 的剖析與辯證，進而得出散文的情感性、審美性對人們的生命活動提供最充分的 形象化的解釋，以及作品審美價值所體現出來的客觀的、歷史的詩性特徵。 其三，本課程也期許學生可以流暢的書寫一篇散文成品。在經歷了前半段列 舉的各式散文書寫的講授後，已讓學生理解散文創作的藝術美學。學生透過前面 對各種不同類型散文書寫的鑑賞，吸收前人創作智慧，進而幫助自己也能反思自 己的人生。學生透過本課程，寫出一篇屬於自己的散文成品，那是更為有意義的 事情。創作教學是一種綜合訓練，是練學生將自己看到的，聽到的，想到的，及 親手做過的事情，運用遣詞造句、布局謀篇、運用富個性化的文字風格表達出來。 它不僅是字、詞、句、段、篇和標點符號的綜合訓練，也不僅是觀察、思維等智 加活動的綜合訓練，更是立場、觀點、思想、感情和思想方法的綜合訓練。期望 學生能在不斷地探索中而尋找到散文創作中更高的美學境界。 綜合上述，以下說明本課程的教學目標。 (二)本課程的教學目標 1、學生能理解當代散文的文體特質，確立散文的文體界限與破體的分寸。 2、學生能嫻熟探索散文文體的創作奧秘，確立散文的身份越界、虛構現象的程 度掌握。 3‧學生能確立散文吸收各種文體藝術後的表現手法和創作意義，能掌握當代散 文的審美鑑賞方法、理解散文文本的各種表現技巧。 4‧培養學生能確立散文創作變化的趨勢和文學史意義。 5‧學生能掌握散文鑑賞的方法：能嫻熟地感受、品味鑑賞、評價批評散文，深 入探討它的審美特徵和文學性，揭示其深層次的文學律動，以此豐富和發展 對現代散文的理解與接受。 6‧透過散文文本研究文化現象，透過作家的心態、人格、話語方式剖析知識份 子的心路歷程，並探討文化精神與審美選擇之間的關係。 7‧訓練學生更好的掌握散文創作的規律，把學習散文審美藝術實際運用到自己 作品中。 8‧引導學生了解現代散文的文體特質與內在精神後更能透過散文解讀人生，進 而透過散文來發現自己，尋找自己，解讀自己，思考自己的人生。 9、期許學生除了透過散文來反思自我，提高心靈的敏感和性靈的深度，也能以 這種反思來理解自我和他人的互動、與自然互動、與世界共存的緊密關係， 同時能以心會心，將心比心，讓自己更具有包容力與對現實世界的關懷和熱 情。 三、課程大綱 本課程一學期共 16 週，由 18 週濃縮為 16 週，是因為要讓學生利用自主學 習的時間和空間去構思一篇散文或論文。散文易寫而難工，而且散文創作的選材 和思考需要一段時間去醞釀，屬於個人化的情感抒發。沒有情感也就不存在真正 的藝術。情感在散文創作中占有舉足輕重的地位。更重要的是思考因素，哲思是 感情發展的高級層次。對主題的思考、對藝術表現的選擇、對自然景物的描寫， 都必須給學生更多的空間和時間，是以本課程以 16 週來設計，以下按照 16 週的 週次說明上課的主題和論述文本。 第一週：課程介紹與評量方式說明 從散文的邊界與跨越談起——後現代主義視野下的現代散文創作概 況、九十年代至今散文文體之變遷、散文的研究路徑與創作規律 第二週 現代散文的辨體論：散文的文體特質和藝術精神 現代散文的文體本色、現代散文和其他文體的差異 散文和小說的比較(兼談散文借用小說虛構的分寸) 散文與詩的比較(兼談散文借用詩歌意象的分際) 第三週 散文的破體與越界論 散文的審美藝術對現實的超越：談散文的真實與虛構、散文創作者身份 的變身與越界、散文如何對其他文體借鑑，散文創作的混血與破體，詩的 語境、小說架構、戲劇性張力的滲入，於是造成了幾種游離在兩種或多種文 體之間的散文類型，也就是散文有向其他文體借用、移植於散文的「破體」 嘗試。 第四週 小說化散文的敘述化與虛構性：散文如何借鑑小說而創作小說體散文： 以王鼎鈞《碎琉璃》中〈敵人的朋友〉、〈哭屋〉為論 (9/28 日教師節停課，以非同步線上教學進行) 第五週 詩化散文的詩情與畫境：散文如何借鑑詩歌而創作詩化散文─ 以王鼎鈞〈驚生〉、〈腳印〉、余光中、楊牧早期散文為論 第六週 寓言體散文的解構性與變型化：散文如何借鑑寓言而創作寓言體散文— 以顏崑陽〈不知終站的列車〉、王鼎鈞〈那樹〉、〈最美與最醜〉為論 第七週 交會時互放的光亮：談人物的摹寫與人間情緣的觸動 以琦君、廖玉蕙、阿盛散文中的人物形象為論 第八週 意識流散文結構的跳躍性與脈絡的潛隱化、朦朧美─ 以曾麗華〈旅途冰涼〉為論 (10/26 光復節補假日停課，以非同步線上教學進行) 第九週 感官與記憶的寫作：談飲食散文中的經驗與表現 以韓良露、蔡珠兒為論 第十週 寫物與體物：散文的自然書寫與詠物抒懷、身體書寫： 以凌拂、劉克襄、周芬伶為論 第十一週 散文的紀錄與片斷經營： 手記式散文的語錄化與札記性─以隱地為論 日記體散文的絮語性與生命片段—以林文義、王幼華為論 第十二週 極短篇化散文的諷喻化和哲理性─以簡媜、林燿德為論 第十三週 行走中的療癒：旅行書寫中的空間書寫與生命記錄： 以舒國治、張讓、蔣勳為論 第十四週 同學選題報告—散文創作成果或論文發表 第十五週 同學選題報告—散文創作成果或論文發表 第十六週 同學選題報告—散文創作成果或論文發表 四、參考書目 講義位址(Web Links) 清大 鄭明娳《文學創作與欣賞》，台北：學海書局，民國一九七三年三月。 亮軒《從散文解讀人生》，台灣新生報，民國一九九四年六月。 李光連《散文技巧》，台北洪葉文化事業有限公司，一九九六年五月。 楊昌年《現代散文新風貌》，台北：東大圖書公司，民國一九八八年二月。 楊松年、林明昌主編《多元的交響：世華散文評析》(唐山) 何寄澎主編《散文批評》(正中) 張瑞芬《五十年來台灣女性散文．評論篇》(麥田) 張瑞芬《台灣當代女性散文史論》(麥田) 黃雅莉《漂泊與尋找—王鼎鈞散文自傳書寫的詩心與文境》，秀威出版，2019 五、教學方式(Teaching Method) 本課程主題是現代散文的藝術美學與創作實踐，在豐富學生散文專業知識的 同時，也培養學生基礎的寫作能力。創作教學是學生和教師一起進行積極思維活 動的過程，它的課堂形式是由學生和教師共同互動方能形成，把作家作品和講義 作為知識傳授的工具，學生通過作品接受進行寫作實踐，由學生的研究表現和創 作成果來檢驗教師的教學效果。 現今，大家所樂於採用的創作指導，有的偏向於「概念式」，從寫作原理入 手，解說一般的寫作步驟及技巧；有的偏於題目式，針對固定的命題，提示具體 的寫作方法。概念式的指導，重視基本的寫作理論，能收到觸類旁通的功效，但 容易流於空泛，不切實際；題目式的指導，重視單一題目的引導，雖較能指引學 生下筆成文，但是作文題目多如牛毛，往往掛一漏萬，顧此失彼。為了兼取以上 兩種作文指導的優點，並避免可能產生的缺點，本課程導向本源，引導學生從創 作的發生論、過程論來介紹散文的思考和表現，訓練學生思維的靈活、培養觀察 能力、善於充實與體驗生活的經驗。使抽象的理論和實際的作品，互相印證，相 得益彰。 教學方式採用課堂講授、同學提問、專題討論、同學報告與創作、老師講評 與同學交流，詳細說明如下： 1‧本課程前半部以教師講授為主，並根據不同的探討議題，設計相關主題， 提供學生反思與辯證。 2‧課堂最後 3-4 週排定同學報告，修課同學可以依個人對散文的藝術偏好選 擇撰寫一篇分析散文的論文，或創作篇一篇散文。(論文篇幅至少 8000 字，創作 篇幅至少 2500 字，另外還必須附上創作理念與設計之說明)。 六、成績考核： 1、出席狀況與課堂的參與度：30% (說明：出缺席佔 10%，未能來上課請向老師請假，否則會影響本項成績、 課堂討論參與度佔 20%) 2、課堂中個人選題報告 (佔 30%) 每位同學可以依自己能力與喜好選擇報告類型，二者擇一進行之： (1)創作一篇散文，並且要附上創作理念或創作心得。在學期最後三週分享自己 的創作成品，並接受老師同學的提問交流。 (2)寫一篇關於現代散文的論文，除了帶領同學導讀作品，也要自行設計研究主 題來表達你閱讀的體悟與感受，報告中師生進行討論及意見交流。 3、期末作業：40% 就上述第二項選題報告之後，根據老師同學給予的建議，把它修訂成為一篇 散文成品或小論文，於本學期第 18 週的週四交出。(40%) 七、生成式人工智慧倫理聲明 依據 112/5/1 本校發佈的「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」： 校方尊重教師對於課程使用 AI 工具的策略，教師應於課程大綱中敘明學生使用 AI 的聲明，尤其是正確引註 AI 並揭露使用的歷程。 經仔細考量後，本課程性質與內容不宜使用生成式人工智慧於課堂學習當 中。因生成式 AI 中尚有諸多錯誤，且容易影響學生對生命情感教育與基礎知識 之判讀。本課程採取禁止使用生成式人工智慧，相關監管機制如下： 修讀本門課程之學生應注意本門課不得繳交使用生成式人工智慧所產出的 作業、報告或個人心得。若經查核發現，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作 業或報告重新評分或不予計分。 修讀本課程之學生，於選課時視為同意以上的倫理聲明。

docs.text: 1 國立清華大學華文文學所課程大綱 科 號 學 分 3 學分 人數限制 10 人 任 課 教 師 林保全 時 間 教 室 科目中文名稱 中國文獻載體專題 科目英文名稱 Topics on Documentary Carriers In Chinese Literature 一、課程說明 參見次頁所附。 二、指定用書 參見次頁所附。 三、參考書籍 參見次頁所附。 四、教學方式 參見次頁所附。 五、教學進度 參見次頁所附。 六、成績考核 參見次頁所附。 七、講義位址 h t t p : / / 2 一、課程說明 1. 本課程設計是以國際生、僑生或大學非文史相關科系畢業的學生為主，在缺乏古 籍、文獻、版本等相關知識之下，提供其理解與認識中國傳統文獻載體的文化及 內涵。 2. 本課程旨在研習中國文獻所呈現的載體，其性質、特質，及其所呈現的字體與反 映的文化內涵。 3. 中國文字與載體自殷墟甲骨文以來，歷經了青銅器的吉金文字、簡牘帛書的戰國 文字、大小篆、古今隸，以及紙張出現後的抄本卷軸、刊本雕版、木活字、鉛活 字，及其所對應的行書、楷書等等，源遠流長變化多端，藉由本課程之研習，進 而得以掌握各時代載體與文字的特質，並具體與系統的獲得相關的知識。 4. 本課程將透過具體實作，在不同的載體上刻寫不同的文字，並且在不同的載體中 進行各式各樣的裝幀，以體驗各種載體與文字及其形制的特質與文化內涵。 二、指定用書 1. 教師自編教材。 三、參考書籍 1. 趙海麗等：《中國文獻載體演變史》，濟南：齊魯，2017。 2. 于省吾《雙劍誃吉金文選》，北京：中華，2009 年。 3. 王國維《生霸死霸考》，台北：藝文出版社，1971 年。 4. 王國維《觀堂集林》，台北：河洛圖書，1975 年。 5. 王國維《古史新證》，收入《王國維全集》第 11 冊，杭州：浙江教育；廣州：廣 東教育，2009 年。 6. 王國維《觀堂古金文考釋》，收入《王國維全集》第 11 冊，杭州：浙江教育；廣 州：廣東教育，2009 年。 7. 宋鎮豪等主編《甲骨文獻集成》，成都：四川大學出版社，2001 年。 8. 李零〈郭店楚簡校讀記〉，《道家文化研究》，第十七輯，「郭店楚簡」專號，香港： 三聯書店，1999 年 8 月 。 9. 李零《郭店楚簡校讀記(增訂本)》，北京：北京大學出版社，2002 年 3 月 。 10. 李學勤〈先秦儒家著作的重大發現〉，《中國哲學》，第 20 輯，1999 年 1 月 。 11. 李學勤〈帛書五行與尚書洪範〉，《學術月刊》，第 11 期，1986 年 11 月 。 12. 李學勤〈荊門郭店楚簡中的子思子〉，《中國哲學》，第 20 輯，1999 年 1 月 。 13. 李學勤〈從簡帛佚籍《五行》談到《大學》〉，《中國哲學》，1999 年 2 月。 14. 周鳳五〈讀郭店竹簡《成之聞之》劄記〉，《古文字與古文獻》，試刊號，1999 年 10 月 。 15. 周鳳五〈郭店竹簡的形式特徵與分類意義〉，《郭店楚簡國際學術研討會論文集》， 美國哈佛大學、武漢大學主辦，湖北人民出版社，2000 年 5 月。 16. 周鳳五〈傳統漢學經典的再生──以《清華簡・保訓》「中」字為例〉，臺北：《漢 學研究通訊》，2012 年 5 月號。 17. 周鳳五主編：《先秦文本及思想之形成、發展與轉化（上）（下）》 ，台北：國立 臺灣大學出版社，2013 年。 18. 胡厚宣《殷墟發掘》，上海：學習出版社，1955 年。 19. 荊門市博物館編《郭店楚墓竹簡》，北京：文物，1998 年 5 月。 20. 涂宗流《郭店楚簡先秦儒家佚書校釋》，臺北：萬卷樓圖書有限公司，2001 年 2 月。 21. 馬王堆漢墓帛書整理小組：《馬王堆漢墓帛書》，北京 : 文物出版社, 1978 年。 22. 清華大學出土文獻硏究與保護中心編 ; 李學勤主編《清華大學藏戰國竹簡》，上 3 海 : 中西書局, 2010。 23. 郭沫若《卜辭通纂》，北京：科學出版社，1983 年。 24. 陳夢家《殷墟卜辭綜述》，台北：大通，1971 年。 25. 陳夢家《西周銅器斷代》，北京：中華，2004 年。 26. 湖北省荊門市博物館：〈荊門郭店一號楚墓〉，《文物》，第 7 期，1997 年 。 27. 湖北省荊沙路考古隊：〈包山楚簡〉，《文物》，1991 年。 28. 勞榦：《居延漢簡》，台北市 : 中央硏究院歷史語言硏究所,1957-1960 年。裘錫圭 《古代文史研究新探》，南京，江蘇古籍，1992 年。 29. 董作賓《殷曆譜》，四川南溪：中央研究院歷史語言研究所，1945 年。 30. 劉信芳《簡帛五行解詁》，臺北：藝文印書館，2000 年 12 月 。 31. 劉信芳《包山楚簡解詁》，臺北：藝文印書館，2003 年 12 月 。 32. 韓仲民〈長沙馬王堆漢墓帛書概述〉，《文物》，1974 年第 9 期， 33. 顧史考（ Scott Cook）：《郭店楚簡先秦儒書宏微觀》，上海：上海古籍出版社， 2012 年。 34. 羅振玉《殷商貞卜文字考》，收入宋鎮豪等主編《甲骨文獻集成》第 7 冊，成都： 四川大學出版社，2001 年。 四、教學方式 1. 本課程教學方式以講授與討論並行，講授佔 60％，討論佔 40％。課程期間必須 預先研讀指定之原典或相關論文，並於課堂中針對原典、論文進行理解、分析與 討論。 五、教學進度（各週教學進度依國定假日或實際上課進度之故，保留彈性調整空間，謹供參考） 主題（一）：龜卜、腹甲與甲骨卜辭（第 1、2 週） 1. 殷墟甲骨的發現。 2. 甲骨的製作與形制特色。 3. 甲骨文的功能與文字特色。 4. 甲骨文刻寫實作、周易古法實作。 主題（二）青銅器與吉金文字（第 3、4 週） 1. 青銅器的製作、形制與功能。 2. 鍾鼎文、吉金文字的功能與文字特色。 3. 重要青銅器、鍾鼎文、吉金文字導論。 主題（三）簡牘、帛書與戰國文字、秦漢古今隸（第 5、6、7 週） 1. 簡牘、帛書的製作、形制與功能。 2. 簡牘、帛書文字的功能與文字特色。 3. 重要簡牘、帛書及戰國文字、大小篆、古今隸導論。 4. 竹簡書寫與編繩實作 主題（四）石刻（第 8、9 週） 1. 石刻的形制、類型與功能。 4 2. 歷代重要石刻文獻導論。 3. 石刻常見的文字類型與特色。 4. 拓碑實作。 主題（五）紙張與卷軸、抄本、敦煌寫本（第 10、11 週） 1. 紙的製作、形制與流傳過程。 2. 卷軸、抄本、敦煌寫本的文獻特質。 3. 卷軸、抄本、敦煌寫本的形制與裝幀及其文字類型。 4. 手工抄紙實作、卷軸製作實作。 主題（六）雕版印刷、木活字、鉛活字與刊本（第 12、13 週） 1. 雕版、活字印刷的製作、形制與流傳過程。 2. 雕版、活字印刷的文獻特質。 3. 刊本形制與各種常見的裝幀類型及其文字型態。 4. 宋元明清時期各種重要刊本的介紹。 5. 雕版印刷實作、鉛活字印刷、各式刊物裝幀實作。 期末報告（第 14、15 週） 期末考週（第 16 週） 自主學習 1. 課後可參考影視資料： ①. 《甲骨文朝》（CCTV 製作） ②. 《二十世紀重大考古紀錄：馬王堆大發現（上）、（下）》（CCTV 紀錄製作） ③. 《荊門戰國楚墓（上）、（下）》（中華國寶製作） ④. 《揭秘睡虎地（一）、（二）、（三）》（中華國寶製作） ⑤. 《雲夢秦墓（上）、（下）》（中華國寶製作） ⑥. 李零《簡帛古書與學術源流（修訂本）》（北京：三聯，2020 年）。 六、成績考核 1. 出席率佔 40%。 2. 課堂報告佔 20%。 3. 期末報告佔 40%。 七、其他 1. 09/25 第三週 中秋節放假。 2. 10/09 第五週 國慶日補假。 3. 12/25 第十六週 行憲紀念日放假。
